Family Name: Regulation for the National Mandatory Registry of Programs and/or Projects [Reglamento de Funcionamiento del Registro Nacional Obligatorio de Programas y/o Proyectos (RENAPP)]
Family Summary:
The regulation outlines the procedures for the functioning of the National Mandatory Registry of Programs and/or Projects (RENAPP), aimed at reducing emissions or increasing greenhouse gas (GHG) removals, in alignment with international commitments.

Institutional Roles and Responsibilities

Ministry of Environment and Water [Ministerio de Medio Ambiente y Agua (MMAyA)]: Through the Directorate General for Mitigation and Adaptation of Climate Change [Dirección General de Medio Ambiente y Cambios Climáticos (DGMACC)] oversees the RENAPP, ensuring the implementation of related processes and responsibilities, which are as follows:

- Approve GHG emission reduction/removal methodologies and certification standards.

- Register programs/projects for GHG reductions/removals, including carbon markets.

- Include Bolivia’s NDC mitigation measures and related emission reductions [Unidades de Reducción de Emisiones o Incremento de Remociones de Gases de Efecto Invernadero (UREs)].

- Integrate monitoring data from registered programs/projects.

- Authorise international URE transfers in line with international standards.

- Accredit validation/verification entities for compliance.

- Support national GHG balances and UNFCCC reporting.

- Approve mitigation measure design, monitoring, and methodology.

- Provide technical assistance and seek funding for RENAPP operations.

Other Institutional Participants

- Participating entities: Individuals or organizations (public or private, national or international) that initiate the registration process for mitigation programs/projects.

- Sectoral priority entities: Ministries that head sectors are responsible for the technical criteria related to program/project registration.

- Ministry of Economy and Public Finance: Approves international treaties related to carbon markets as per Article 6 of the Paris Agreement.

Registration and Certifcation Process

- Registration Process: The RENAPP requires the registration of programs and projects that contribute to GHG reductions or removals.

- Monitoring and Reporting: Ongoing monitoring of the registered programs is essential to provide transparent, reliable information on their progress. This data will be integrated into Bolivia’s national GHG inventory and reported under the UNFCCC guidelines.

Categories of Mitigation Measures

- NDC-aligned measures: Actions designed by competent sector authorities aimed at reducing emissions or increasing removals, aligned with the NDC.

- Mitigation measures:

• Cooperative approaches and other compliance markets: Measures implemented in cooperation with other countries or entities under international agreements, generating tradable URE.

• Voluntary Measures: Measures targeting emission reductions or removals for use in voluntary carbon markets, potentially contributing to the NDC but not necessarily.

Certification Standards and Methodologies

- Certification procedures:

• Recognition of external certification standards: DGMACC can recognise certification standards that issue certificates for emission reductions or removals, provided they meet specified criteria.

• Application process: Any individual or entity can apply to DGMACC for recognition, and DGMACC will review and provide a decision within set timeframes.

• Validity: Recognition is valid for 10 years, after which the applicant can reapply.

- Requirements for certification standards:

• Information for recognition: Includes details such as the applicant’s name, legal representative, and registration mechanisms for URE.

• Main business focus: The certification standard should focus on operating a registry for voluntary or regulatory programs that contribute to GHG reductions and removals.

• Transparency: Standards must ensure clear traceability and prevent double counting of emission reduction certificates.

Methodologies

- Approval process: The DGMACC may approve methodologies aligned with recognised Certification Standards for calculating emission reductions or GHG removal increases.

- Key Criteria for methodology approval:

• Additionality: The methodology must demonstrate additionality of emissions reductions/removals per the regulations.

• Data alignment: Must align with the National GHG Inventory System and include relevant parameters, considering carbon leakage, policies, and social, environmental, and economic circumstances at local, regional, and national levels.

• Baseline methodology: Should incorporate publicly available data supporting assumptions

• Compatibility with National Reference Emission Levels (NRE): Must be compatible with Bolivia’s existing NRE across sectors such as industry, energy, waste, and forestry.

• REDD+ safeguards: Methodologies must comply with REDD+ safeguards and Bolivia’s corresponding regulations.

- Publication of methodologies: Approved methodologies will be listed on the MMAyA website.

Registration procedure

- General criteria

• Any participating entity must register in the RENAPP.

• Each entity can register only one account in the RENAPP and must designate a primary account representative.

• The DGMACC will approve the entity registration within 30 working days after submission of complete information.

- Requirements for the registration of participating entities in RENAPP

• Required information: Entity name, contact details, legal constitution details, directors and decision-makers. Commercial number (if assigned) and tax identification number.

• Foreign entities: Must have a branch or permanent representation in Bolivia or partner with a local institution.

• Legal representation: Non-individual entities must designate a primary or alternate account representative residing in Bolivia.

• Declaration: A sworn declaration from the primary account representative is required.

- Requirements for the registration of users in RENAPP

• User Registration: Individuals acting as representatives for participating entities must submit: Personal identification information and relevant documents. Proof of the relationship with the entity and, if applicable, the entity’s legal representative accreditation.

• Exclusions: Individuals with criminal records are not eligible for registration.

• Approval: The DGMACC will approve user registration within 30 working days of receiving complete information.

Recognition of Validation and Verification Bodies (VVB)

- Accreditation: The DGMACC may recognise VVBs accredited by recognised Certification Standards.

- Validation and Verification Services: VVBs provide external evaluations of the Design Document for Mitigation Measures (DDMM) and periodic evaluations of monitoring reports, ensuring compliance with REDD+ safeguards and other relevant standards.

- Public List: The DGMACC maintains and publicly shares a list of recognized VVBs.

Mitigation Measure Owners

- Program/Project ownership: designated participating entity is responsible for managing the project and its registration.

- The Entity is accountable for:

• Requesting authorization and registering the mitigation activity.

• Reporting the start of the activity to the DGMACC.

• Hiring and overseeing the performance of the VVB.

• Requesting international transfer of URE for cooperative approaches.

Administrative Procedures for Registration

• The participating entity submits a request for the registration of mitigation programs and projects, providing the necessary documentation for evaluation.

• The DGMACC evaluates the application for admissibility within 10 working days.

• If the application is deemed acceptable, the DGMACC has 30 working days to make a decision, with the possibility for the entity to address any observations within 10 working days.

• The DGMACC generated a final report, indicating whether it approves or rejects the participating entity’s registration in the RENAPP.

• The validity of registration is based on the credit period requested.

Requirements for Registration and Enrollment of Mitigation Measures in RENAPP

- Documentation needed for registration:

• Completed registration application

• Environmental license (if applicable).

• Documented methodology for calculating emission reductions or removals.

• Proof of validation of the methodology by an VVB.

• Evidence of community consent for projects in indigenous or campesino communities.

• Proof of payment for the administrative procedure.

- Registration application should include:

• Name of the individual or legal entity presenting as the holder of the mitigation activity.

• Name of the legal representative or proxy, if applicable.

• Identification document number.

• Registration number where the legal representation is recorded, if applicable.

• Contact details (legal address, email, and phone number).

• Name of the program and/or project, and the corresponding carbon mitigation measure under cooperative approaches or voluntary carbon market.

• For measures under cooperative approaches, the name of the international agreement Bolivia has signed under Paragraph 2 of Article 6 of the Paris Agreement.

• For voluntary carbon market measures, the mitigation measure ID number granted by the certification standard.

- Additional documentation for REDD+ projects:

• Georeferenced project area.

• Prevention and Mitigation Program and the Environmental Implementation and Monitoring Plan and its approved administrative act.

• Compliance with REDD+ safeguards.

Modification of the Mitigation Measures Registration in RENAPP

- Communication of modifications: Any changes to a registered program/project in RENAPP must be communicated by the program/project holder to the DGMACC within 30 business days of the modification.

- Modification Request: The program/project holder must submit a modification request to DGMACC, including:

• The validated DDMM by an VVB.

• Documents supporting the modification request, including calculation of emission reductions or removals.

• Validation report of the modified DDMM issued by an VVB.

• Documentation showing approval from all stakeholders involved in the program/project.

- Evaluation by DGMACC:

• DGMACC will evaluate whether the proposed changes affect initially assessed criteria.

• The procedure follows the same process as new registrations, with observation and correction periods.

- Approval and Legal Effect:

• The modification will take effect upon formal notification of approval by DGMACC, within 10 business days from a favorable resolution.

• RENAPP registration will be updated immediately to reflect authorised changes.

URE Generation from Mitigation Measures

- Procedure for URE registration:

• Participants' request: Entities may request the registration of UREs generated from the mitigation measures of their registered programs/projects in RENAPP. These UREs must correspond to certified emission reduction or absorption certificates recognized by DGMACC.

• DGMACC evaluation: DGMACC will evaluate the registration request within 30 business days of receiving a complete request. If there are observations, the entity will have 10 business days to correct them.

• Results notification: DGMACC will notify the entity and the Certification Standard of the results, including the amount of UREs to be registered.

• Certification standard's role: Before UREs can be registered, the Certification Standard must notify DGMACC that the emission reduction or absorption certificates have been canceled or withdrawn. This cancellation or withdrawal must be published on the Certification Standard’s website.

• URE registration: DGMACC will register UREs in RENAPP within 5 business days after receiving confirmation of certificate cancellation or withdrawal from the Certification Standard. Each URE will be assigned a unique serial number and can be traced from issuance to cancellation or withdrawal.

• Eligibility for registration: Only UREs generated within the relevant credit period (annually) can be registered. The registration acknowledges the entity's ownership of the UREs but does not grant ownership of natural resources in Bolivia, if affected by the mitigation measures.

Requirements for URE Registration in RENAPP

- Entities must submit documentation demonstrating monitoring and verification by an VVB.

- Additional documentation is required for REDD+ programs to ensure safeguards compliance.

Suspension of RENAPP Registration

- Grounds for suspension:

• Discretion of authorities: As per competent authorities' instructions.

• Entity’s request: Upon the request of the entity.

• Errors in monitoring reports: If monitoring reports overestimate reductions or removals by more than 5%.

• Non-compliance with Laws: If the program/project fails to comply with applicable environmental, health, or safety laws.

• Double Counting of UREs: If UREs have been issued under another voluntary or mandatory program for the same period and program.

- Effect of Suspension:

• During suspension, UREs cannot be registered or used.

• Suspension does not affect the credit period.

- Suspension in Carbon Markets:

• If UREs are suspended for carbon market use under cooperative or compliance frameworks, Bolivia’s international agreements under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement will apply.

Revocation of RENAPP Registration

- Grounds for revocation:

• If the suspension results from certain grounds (e.g., authorities' orders), UREs cannot be registered or used.

• If revocation results from an entity’s request, UREs generated before the revocation can be registered for the relevant credit period.

- Notification of revocation: DGMACC will notify the external certification program of the revocation for appropriate actions to be taken.
Document Title: Regulation for the National Mandatory Registry of Programs and/or Projects [Reglamento de Funcionamiento del Registro Nacional Obligatorio de Programas y/o Proyectos (RENAPP)]

Family Name: 11th Basic Energy Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand
Family Summary: This policy document outlines plans for the development of the Republic of Korea's power sector until 2038. It plans to reach 21.7% of renewables by 2030, and 33% by 2038.
Document Title: 11th Basic Energy Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand (2024-2038)

Family Name: Energy Policy and Strategy 2024–2029
Family Summary:
The Energy Policy and Strategy 2024–2029 outlines a series of innovative initiatives, bold targets, and strategic investments that will propel Maldives towards a more sustainable future. By harnessing renewable energy sources such as solar, wind, and ocean energies, Maldives will reduce its dependence on fossil fuels, lower its greenhouse gas emissions, and create a more sustainable and resilient energy infrastructure. This document serves as guidance for stakeholders across government, industry, and civil society to collaborate in driving the transition to a cleaner and more sustainable energy future.

Key objectives of the Maldives Energy Policy include:

  1. Diversifying the energy mix: Promoting the development and utilization of renewable energy sources, such as solar, wind, biomass and ocean energies, to reduce the country's dependence on imported fossil fuels and enhance energy security;
  2. Improving energy efficiency: Implementing measures to enhance energy efficiency across all sectors to reduce energy consumption and lower greenhouse gas emissions;
  3. Enhancing access to energy services: Ensuring universal access to affordable, reliable, and modern energy services for all citizens;
  4. Strengthening energy governance: Enhancing institutional capacity, regulatory frameworks, and governance structures to facilitate the effective implementation of energy policies and programs; and
  5. Promoting public awareness and engagement: Raising awareness about the importance of sustainable energy practices and promoting community participation in energy conservation and renewable energy initiatives.

The policies are:

  • Policy 1: Increase the Share of Renewable Energy in the National Energy Mix;
  • Policy 2: Promote Energy Efficiency and Conservation;
  • Policy 3: Improve Energy Security and Affordability;
  • Policy 4: Strengthen Institutional Capacity and Regulatory Framework of the Energy Sector; and
  • Policy 5: Promote Energy Research and Development.
Document Title: Energy Policy and Strategy 2024–2029 * indicates required fields

Family Name: Action Plan for the Development of Carbon Dioxide Capture Utilization and Storage (CCUS)
Family Summary:
The plan responds both to requests of the Czech industry and to EU legislation, particularly Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 – the Net-Zero Industry Act, which aims at ensuring an annual geological storage of at least 50 Mt CO2 by 2030 across the EU. It is reflected that existing strategic documents on the national level lack the required level of detail and concrete measures as regards CCUS development.

The main objective of the action plan for the development of CCUS is to describe these technologies, their potential and limitations in the Czech Republic, including the introduction of methods of support and enabling development in all parts of the value chain (capture, transport, use/storage). The Action Plan can thus become the basis for possible subsequent management decisions in the area of decarbonization.
Document Title: The Government approved the Action Plan for the Development of CO2 Capture, Utilization and Storage Technologies in the Czech Republic (“CCUS Action Plan”)

Family Name: National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) 2025
Family Summary: National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) from 2025 aims to provide a comprehensive and proactive long-term framework to promote effective disaster responses by national and subnational authorities. The plan acknowledges climate change as one of the dominant threats to Pakistan's economy and society, and underscores the need for better disaster preparation as these risks increase. It contains objectives for general capacity building, alongside media engagement, risk prioritisation, hazard analysis, provincial co-ordination and academic knowledge-sharing. The plan also contains specific interventions including the formation of a National Drainage Plan, to reduce flood risk, and climate-smart vegetation choices for crops and erosion-reduction plantings.
Document Title: National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) 2025

Family Name: National Strategy for Food Security in Remote Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Communities 2025-2035
Family Summary:
This Strategy aims to coordinate action across Australia to address the unique and specific food security needs of First Nations people living in remote communities, including to improve the preparedness and resilience of First Nations communities to the impact of climate change.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people have sustained vast and varied food systems that maintained collective healthand wellbeing for tens of thousands of years. The disruption of traditional ways of gathering and preparing food has had a significant impact on food security and health outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. Many remote communities now experience food insecurity at a much higher rate than Australians as a whole.
Document Title: National Strategy for Food Security in Remote Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Communities 2025-2035

Family Name: Clean Mobility Development Strategy
Family Summary:
This Clean Mobility Development Strategy (SDMP) defines measures for mitigating climate change in the transport sector. The third version (SDMP 3) sets out the actions planned for 2030 and 2035 for passenger and logistics and freight transport, with the aim of meeting France's targets and commitments to combat global warming and control energy consumption. The SDMP 3 also takes account of social and economic issues linked to the mobility of people and goods, by proposing measures that are economically efficient and compatible with social justice.

The SDMP is provided for in Article 40 of Law No. 2015-992 of 17 August 2015 on the energy transition for green growth (LTECV). It also falls within the framework of the Law of 24 December 2019 on the Orientation of Mobilities (LOM), in particular Article 73, which states: "France sets itself the objective of achieving, by 2050, the complete decarbonisation of the land transport sector, understood in terms of the carbon cycle of the energy used".
Document Title: Clean Mobility Development Strategy (SDMP 3)

Family Name: Digitisation strategy for the climate and environment sector 2025-2030
Family Summary:
This Strategy provides businesses in the climate and environment sector with predictability and the opportunity to unite around prioritised areas that will ensure efficient, secure and future-oriented digitalisation in a multi-year perspective, this time towards 2030. In the strategy, the government identifies the following priority areas of focus :

  • Exploiting the opportunities of artificial intelligence;
  • Harnessing the opportunities in data and data-driven innovation;
  • Accelerating the green and digital transition;
  • Promoting an adaptable and innovative business sector;
  • Renew and simplify public services; and
  • Preserving a society based on trust and inclusion.
Document Title: Digitisation strategy for the climate and environment sector 2025-2030

Family Name: Decree No. 57/2025/ND-CP for regulations on the purchase and sale of renewable energy
Family Summary:
This Decree regulates the mechanism for direct electricity trading between renewable energy power generators and large electricity consumers, via dedicated power transmission lines and under fixed-term electricity supply contracts.

Electricity companies may not exceed 20% of the total electricity generated. The purchase and sale price of solar power shall be the average market price of electricity for the preceding consecutive month, as published by the Electricity Regulatory Authority and the Electricity Exchange, and shall not exceed the maximum price of the prescribed price range.
Document Title: Decree No. 57/2025/ND-CP for regulations on the purchase and sale of renewable energy

Family Name: Coastal Communities Program against Climate Change and Pollution (C5) [(Programa Comunidades Costeras ante el Cambio Climático y la Contaminación (C5)]
Family Summary: The "Coastal Communities Facing Climate Change and Pollution" (C5) programme, initiated by the National Institute of Ecology and Climate Change (INECC), addresses the critical environmental challenges affecting coastal communities in the Gulf of Mexico. These communities, located in Tamaulipas, Veracruz, Tabasco, Campeche, Yucatán, and Quintana Roo, face significant impacts from hydrocarbon pollution, wetland degradation, and climate change effects such as rising temperatures, sea-level rise, coastal erosion, and declining fish stocks. The programme focuses on empowering fishing communities through capacity building, diversification of economic activities, and sustainable practices, with the goal of restoring and conserving coastal ecosystems. Central to this is a collaborative approach that includes participatory diagnostics, knowledge sharing, and the joint identification of problems and solutions.The C5 programme operates through 92 Learning Centres (CAPs) across the Gulf, fostering community organisation and promoting sustainable practices to combat climate change and pollution. Activities include waste management initiatives, with a focus on plastic collection, and strengthening knowledge of climate change adaptation and sustainable resource management. Challenges include limited infrastructure, security concerns hindering access to some communities, and a need for greater collaboration with local authorities, businesses, and academia. According to the programme, future steps involve strengthening inter-agency collaboration, forming regional working groups, and seeking funding to support community-led action plans for climate change adaptation and mitigation.
Document Title: Coastal Communities Program against Climate Change and Pollution (Programa Comunidades Costeras ante el Cambio Climático y la Contaminación)

Family Name: Fourth National Development Plan (NDPI) 2025/26 - 2029/30
Family Summary: The plan aims to promote sustainable socioeconomic development nationally, building on the aims and achievements of the previous three National Development Plan cycles. It acknowledges climate as a major threat to sustainable development, and among its solutions emphasises appropriate land administration, forest and wetland restoration, wide-ranging rural and urban adaptation, improving capacity to access climate finance, and promoting clean cooking fuels to replace wood biomass. For climate adaptation, which receives particular emphasis, key measures include enhanced irrigation and increasing water storage capacity by around 20% over the 2025-2029 period.
Document Title: Fourth National Development Plan (NDPI) 2025/26 - 2029/30

Family Name: National Development Program (PND) 2025-2030 [Programa Nacional de Desarrollo (PND) 2025-2030]
Family Summary: The 2025–2030 Mexican National Development Plan (PND) articulates the government’s vision for consolidating the country’s ongoing transformation through a model rooted in Mexican Humanism (Humanismo Mexicano). This framework prioritises social justice, democratic governance, and environmental sustainability, seeking to decouple political power from private and foreign interests while restoring the State’s leadership in economic, energy, and social policy. The Plan reaffirms commitments to universal social rights, the expansion of public infrastructure, and a transition from economic growth to holistic development that centres human wellbeing, dignity, and environmental stewardship.The PND integrates sustainability and climate resilience across policy areas. Key strategies include the promotion of clean energy through public investment and energy sovereignty via strengthened state enterprises (PEMEX and CFE); the sustainable use of natural resources; and robust adaptation and mitigation actions in response to climate change. Emphasis is placed on climate justice, rural equity, and the protection of vulnerable populations. The Plan also outlines the expansion of renewable energy capacity, the right to water, and the transition to agroecological practices.
Document Title: National Development Program 2025-2029 (Programa Nacional de Desarrollo 2025-2030)

Family Name: 2025 Operating Rules of the Sustainable Forest Development Program for Well-being
Family Summary: The Programa Desarrollo Forestal Sustentable para el Bienestar (2025) is a federal initiative designed to promote sustainable forest management while addressing climate change through mitigation and adaptation strategies. The program aims to integrate Mexico’s forested and forest-priority lands into competitive, participatory, and sustainable practices, ensuring environmental health and carbon sequestration. Key strategies include community-based forest management, reducing emissions from deforestation (REDD+), restoring degraded ecosystems, and active conservation through payment for ecosystem services. It also prioritizes wildfire prevention, pest control, and reforestation to enhance resilience against climate-driven threats like droughts and forest degradation.The program is structured into five components. (1) Community forest management and value chains; (2) Commercial and agroforestry plantations; (3) Forest restoration; (4) Ecosystem services; (5) Forest protection.
Document Title: 2025 Operating Rules of the Sustainable Forest Development Program for Well-being (Reglas de Operación 2025 del Programa Desarrollo Forestal Sustentable para el Bienestar)

Family Name: Moldova Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2025-2030
Family Summary: Moldova's Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) for 2025-2030 is based on existing national policies and strategies, and addresses five overarching dimensions of progress for the country's energy system: decarbonisation; energy efficiency; energy security; internal energy markets; research, innovation and competitiveness. The NECP aims to highlight existing, planned and potential policies/investments over the 2025-2030 period. Targets in the plan include a 27% renewable share of gross final energy consumption by 2030, and secondarily a maximum final energy consumption of 2.8 million tonnes of oil equivalent (Mtoe), which is to be achieved by energy efficiency measures. The decarbonisation measures in this plan include financial instruments (ie. integration into EU cross-border emissions trading), biological measures (ie. afforestation, low-carbon cattle feed), renewable energy installations, electrification of public transport, promotion of biogas and biofuels.
Document Title: Moldova Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2025-2030

Family Name: Sowing Life Program (Programa Sembrando Vida)
Family Summary: This policy sets out a target to plant 1 billion trees and pays farmers to plant fruit or timber trees on small plots of land to encourage industry in deprived rural areas. mexicoThe impact is still unclear as planting big swaths of commercial species, sometimes on land that held native forests, can potentially end up increasing deforestation rates.
Document Title: Acuerdo por el que se Emiten las Reglas de Operación del Programa Sembrando Vida, para el Ejercicio Fiscal 2025

Family Name: Regulation of the Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources Number 4/2025 concerning the Business and Utilization of Biofuels
Family Summary:
MEMR Regulation No. 4/2025 is a regulation issued by Indonesia’s Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (MEMR) in 2025. This regulation introduces several key advancements compared to previous biofuel regulations (2008 and 2015), which primarily focused on biodiesel (B100) and bioethanol (E100).

The regulation includes:

  • Biodiesel (B35): 35% palm oil-based biodiesel blend for diesel fuel.
  • Bioethanol (E10): 10% ethanol blend for gasoline.
  • Diesel Biohydrocarbon (D100): 100% hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) for diesel replacement.
  • Bioavtur (J100): 100% bio-jet fuel for aviation.
Document Title: Regulation of the Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources Number 4/2025 concerning the Business and Utilization of Biofuels

Family Name: Decree No. 3369 regulating Law 7190/23 on Carbon Credits
Family Summary:
Decree No. 3369 establishes Paraguay’s first formal legal framework for carbon market activities by implementing and regulating Law 7190/23,, as mandated in Chapter V, Article 25 of the law.

The Decree aligns Paraguay’s carbon market regulations with the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 6, which encourages international co-operation to support the achievement of nationally determined contributions (NDCs) through mitigation and adaptation measures. It also aligns with constitutional principles set out in Article 7, which recognises the right of every person “to live in a healthy and ecologically balanced environment”, and Article 8, which establishes that “activities likely to cause environmental alteration shall be regulated by law”.

The Decree creates the Carbon Markets Directorate (DMC), responsible for implementing, supervising, and regulating the carbon market system in Paraguay. It also outlines the foundational rules for the Carbon Credit Registry (created by Law 7190/23), ensuring transparency and traceability through measurable and verifiable data related to carbon credits, Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs), and NDC compliance projections.
Document Title: Decree No. 3369 regulating Law 7190/23 on Carbon Credits

Family Name: Fuel Quality Standards (Paraffinic Diesel) Determination 2025 (Renewable Diesel Standard)
Family Summary:
This fuel quality standard, read with the Fuel Quality Standards Act 2000, enables the supply of renewable diesel (neat and at all blend rates) without the need to apply for time-limited approvals. This ensures that sales of such diesel can happen without burdensome administrative processes and that consumers are provided with fuel that enables efficient engine operability, and provides a market signal that could increase the uptake of renewable diesel in Australia.

Renewable diesel, a type of paraffinic diesel produced exclusively from renewable sources, reduces greenhouse gas emissions while maintaining similar chemical properties to mineral diesel (made from crude oil). The similar properties allow renewable diesel to potentially be used as a drop-in fuel in diesel engines used in heavy vehicles and machinery, and some light vehicles. The emissions reduction is dependent on the feedstock and production method.
Document Title: Fuel Quality Standards (Paraffinic Diesel) Determination 2025

Family Name: Future Made in Australia (Production Tax Credit and Other Measures) Act 2025
Family Summary:
This legislation implements production tax incentives for renewable hydrogen and critical minerals.

The incentives are:

  1. Hydrogen Production Tax Incentive worth $2 per kilogram of renewable hydrogen produced between 2027–2028 and 2039–40 for up to ten years per project.
  2. Critical Minerals Production Tax Incentive worth ten per cent of relevant processing and refining costs for Australia’s 31 critical minerals, for critical minerals processed and refined between 2027–28 and 2039–40, for up to ten years per project.

The incentives will support Australia’s efforts to decarbonise our industries, and produce and process more of the minerals needed for the energy transition.
Document Title: Future Made in Australia (Production Tax Credit and Other Measures) Act 2025

Family Name: Power Development Plan 2023-2050
Family Summary: In alignment with the Philippine Energy Plan (PEP) which prioritises the aggressive deployment of renewable energy, this the Power Development Plan (PDP) 2023-2050 coordinates adjustments across the power industry’s sub-sectors - generation, transmission, distribution, and supply - to align with the nation’s medium- to long-term energy goals. The PDP adopts the national renewable energy power generation mix targets of 35% by 2030 and 50% by 2040, while providing a roadmap for stakeholders in the electric power industry. The PDP is also aligned with the PEP's goal to create a resilient, climate-proof energy infrastructure.
Document Title: Power Development Plan 2023-2050

Family Name: Strategic Plan for the Ministry of Housing and Urban Development 2025-2030
Family Summary: The Strategic Plan for the Ministry of Housing and Urban Development 2025-2030 provides a five-year vision to guide urban development efforts in Eswatini. The plan aims to modernise housing systems, urban governance and emergency preparedness while promoting sustainability and inclusivity. Family Summary: This policy, which succeeds the 2012 Energy Management Regulations, informs energy management requirements for all facilities (e.g. commercial, industrial, institutional) whose energy consumption exceeds 180,000 kWh/year. Family Summary: Rwanda's 2025 Energy Policy sets out a long term vision for the development of the sector, focusing on electricity supply, transport and rural cooking fuel. The policy contains provisions for clean cooking fuel, renewables expansion (including off-grid solar), increased climate-resilience of hydropower, electromobility infrastructure, use of crop biofuels, and ensuring efficiency and low air pollution in any fossil fuel growth that takes place.
Document Title: Rwanda Energy Policy

Family Name: The 7th Strategic Energy Plan
Family Summary: This plan, established under Japan's Basic Act on Energy Policy, outlines the overall directions for Japan’s energy policies. In conjunction with the GX2040 Vision and the Plan for Global Warming Countermeasures, both of which were also approved by Cabinet on February 18, 2025, the Japanese government will strive to achieve stable energy supply, economic growth, and decarbonization simultaneously.
Document Title: 7th Strategic Energy Plan

Family Name: The National Biodiversity Action Plan (2023-2027)
Family Summary: The National Biodiversity Action Plan (2023-2027) in Thailand, adopted by the Cabinet on October 29, 2024, is implemented from 2023 to 2027 and sets out three main strategies and twelve national targets focused on strengthening conservation, promoting sustainable and equitable use of biodiversity, and mainstreaming biodiversity into national policies. Key targets include expanding protected areas, halting species extinction, supporting sustainable agriculture and tourism, and integrating biodiversity values into all sectors to align with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.
Document Title: The National Biodiversity Action Plan (2023-2027)

Family Name: Internal Regulations of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development
Family Summary: The Internal Regulations of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (SADER) establishes a structured framework for advancing sustainable agricultural development in Mexico, emphasising climate resilience, biodiversity conservation, and resource efficiency. Organised into specialised coordinations and directorates (including the Coordinación General de Sustentabilidad y Resiliencia Climática and Dirección General de Sustentabilidad), the policy mandates inter-institutional collaboration to integrate climate adaptation into agricultural planning. Key responsibilities include designing public policies to mitigate climate risks (e.g., droughts, floods), promoting sustainable production systems, and aligning national efforts with international agreements (e.g., Paris Agreement). The policy explicitly addresses climate change. The Coordinación General de Sustentabilidad y Resiliencia Climática oversees initiatives such as promoting agroecological practices, restoring degraded soils, optimising water use, and reducing pesticide reliance. It also emphasises deforestation prevention and the adoption of regenerative livestock systems to curb greenhouse gas emissions. The Dirección General de Sustentabilidad further mandates the development of climate-resilient strategies, including early-warning systems for extreme weather, land-use planning to avoid deforestation, and biodiversity integration into agriculture. Similarly, financing mechanisms under the Dirección General de Financiamiento Verde seek international partnerships to fund sustainable projects, aligning with global climate goals.
Document Title: Decree issuing the Internal Regulations of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (Decreto por el que se expide el Reglamento Interior de la Secretaría de Agricultura y Desarrollo Rural)

Document Title: National Sustainable Development Strategy

Family Name: The National Climate Change (Climate Change Mechanisms) Regulations, 2025
Family Summary: The National Climate Change (Climate Change Mechanisms) Regulations, 2025 provide an administrative framework to operationalise national and international climate commitments in Uganda, following the legal framework given in the National Climate Change Act 2021. These regulations define the roles and sequential protocol for verifiers of emissions reduction units, as well as mechanisms projects and the operation of emissions trading.
Document Title: The National Climate Change (Climate Change Mechanisms) Regulations, 2025

Family Name: Decision No. 232/QD-TTg
Family Summary:
Decree No. 232/QD-TTg establishes Vietnam’s national carbon market, with a pilot phase from 2025 to 2028 and full operations starting in 2029. The decree aims to support the country’s greenhouse gas reduction targets while promoting financial flows to carbon projects and enhancing corporate competitiveness.

The market will operate under a centralised model, with trading on the Hanoi Stock Exchange and oversight by the Vietnam Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation. Two types of carbon credits are defined: (1) credits from Japan’s Joint Crediting Mechanism, the voluntary market, and Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, and (2) carbon quotas under the national emissions trading system, allocated freely or via auctions.

Five intergovernmental groups will manage key aspects of implementation, ensuring structured market development and preventing unregulated trading.
Document Title: Decision No. 232/QD-TTg

Family Name: Comprehensive Carbon Reduction Action Plan
Family Summary:
Taiwan’s Comprehensive Carbon Reduction Action Plan focuses on six major sectors through flagship carbon reduction projects to intensify reduction efforts. The Plan also proposes sectoral self-driven carbon reduction plans, continuously adjusting strategies as needed. The Plan incorporates six mechanisms—technological innovation, financial support, carbon pricing, regulatory adaptation, green collar talent, and community-driven initiatives—to integrate carbon reduction efforts across sectors.

The goal is to achieve four major transition visions: a more diversified energy transition, a more innovative industrial transition, a lower-carbon lifestyle transition, and a more resilient social transition. The Plan also aims to reduce air pollution, enhance energy independence, drive private investment, and cultivate green-collar talent, further accelerating green growth and improving societal well-being.
Document Title: Comprehensive Carbon Reduction Action Plan

Family Name: Rail Investment Plan
Family Summary: In early 2025, Morocco's Minister of Transport and Logistics presented a MAD 96 billion investment plan to modernize the country's rail system by 2030. MAD 53 billion is earmarked for the construction of a high-speed rail line between Marrakech and Kenitra, MAD 29 billion to aquire 18 high-speed trains and 150 multi-service trains, and MAD 14 billion to build or renovate railway stations.
Document Title: Rail Investment Plan

Family Name: Rwanda Energy Group (REG) Strategic Plan 2024-2034
Family Summary: The Strategic Plan guides Rwanda Energy Group's (REG) long-term operations in promoting the development of the energy sector and electricity generation, on behalf of the Rwandan government. It aims to meet or surpass 60% renewables in the energy mix by 2034, achieve 100% grid access for the population, and provide substantial physical and research infrastructure to support these targets. It notes the importance of climate-specific green financing, as mechanisms to achieve these targets.
Document Title: Rwanda Energy Group (REG) Strategic Plan 2024-2034

Family Name: Royal Decree on the Establishment of the Center for Climate Change Risk Analysis
Family Summary: The Royal Decree formalizes the creation of the Centre for Climate Change Risk Analysis (CeRAC) in Belgium. Based within the Federal Public Service for Health and Environment, this independent center's mission is to assess medium- and long-term climate and environmental risks. It focuses on improving the country's resilience by conducting complex risk analyses and publishing recommendations for policymakers.
Document Title: Royal Decree on the Establishment of the Center for Climate Change Risk Analysis

Family Name: Society's Security Strategy
Family Summary:
The Societal Security Strategy describes a comprehensive security operating model. The goal of the strategy, which was approved as a government decision-in-principle, is to provide everyone with a common framework for implementing comprehensive security from their own starting points.

The chapter 37 of the strategy covers environmental and climate change monitoring and preparedness in Finland, with the Ministry of the Environment (YM) and Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (MMM) as lead agencies. Its goal is to maintain Finland's capacity to detect, monitor, and forecast environmental and climate change emergencies, and to prepare society to adapt to them. Given that cross-border environmental impacts require broad Finnish participation in international environmental, climate, and biodiversity agreements. Concretely, this involves maintaining and developing environmental monitoring systems, data registers, and weather observation networks (increasingly using satellite and AI methods), and using weather data and climate models to track and assess future climate change, with research institutes generally contributing knowledge on climate mitigation and adaptation.
Document Title: Society's Security Strategy

Family Name: Bulgaria Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030.

The measures of the plan aim: 1) to strengthen policy response and ensure that climate change adaptation is included in the legal framework; 2) to build adaptation capacity and develop financial, social and political guidelines on risk management; 3) to improve knowledge management, research, education and communication with stakeholders. In the context of decarbonisation. The plan aims to increase the use of renewable sources in key sectors such as electric power, transport and heating/cooling. The NECP set several measures to ensure energy efficiency and security : 1) the diversification of the supply of energy resources; 2) increasing the flexibility of the national energy system; 3) addressing constrained or disrupted supply of energy sources for the purpose of enhancing the resilience of regional and national energy systems; 4) improving interconnectivity and information security (cybersecurity). Quantified targets include a 34.96% renewable share of gross final energy consumption by 2030, and an overall 10% decrease in non-ETS greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 relative to 2005.
Document Title: Bulgaria Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030

Family Name: National Development Plan 2025-2030 (Plan Nacional de Desarrollo -PND- 2025-2030)
Family Summary: The National Development Plan PND 2025–2030 (Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2025-2030) outlines the strategic framework for Mexico’s federal policy planning, in accordance with Article 26 of the Constitution, which mandates that the state must guide national development through a democratic and deliberative planning system. The Plan functions as a mandatory reference point for all sectoral, institutional, regional, and special programmes of the Federal Public Administration, requiring alignment in both programming and budgetary processes. In line with the Ley de Planeación, the PND includes a diagnostic overview of national priorities, general policy axes, implementation strategies, performance indicators, and a long-term vision.The 2025–2030 Plan introduces four general policy axes: governance with justice and citizen participation; development with well-being and humanism; moral economy and dignified work; and, sustainable development. The PND 2025-2030 additionally includes transversal priorities such as gender equality, public innovation, and the rights of Indigenous and Afro-Mexican peoples. Environmental and climate-related goals are woven into various policy strands, including commitments to strengthen state control over the energy sector, promote renewable energy, expand access to solar panels. Climate change is also indirectly included in the goals related to securing the right to water through irrigation modernisation and water recycling, and the advance of environmental protection through circular economy initiatives, reforestation, and air quality improvement in major urban areas.
Document Title: National Development Plan 2025-2030 (Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2025-2030)

Family Name: Regulation on the Management of Industrial Emissions
Family Summary: The purpose of this Regulation is to regulate the administrative and technical procedures and principles for green transformation, circular economy and decarbonisation in industry to prevent and minimize the formation of industrial emissions and waste accumulation that cause air, water, soil, noise and odour pollution, and to use resources efficiently, with a control approach, in order to integrate the zero pollution target for the holistic protection of the environment and human health.
Document Title: Regulation on the Management of Industrial Emissions

Family Name: Pakistan Policy Guidelines for Trading in Carbon Markets 2025
Family Summary: The Pakistan Policy Guidelines for Trading in Carbon Markets (2025) aim to set the stage for the establishment of carbon markets, and provide a roadmap for their early development and operation. The document is underpinned by commitment to the Paris Agreement, and adherence to international best practice in carbon trading. It emphasises the importance of nature-based carbon projects, for their social and environmental synergies. These guidelines include an implementation mechanism which calls for the establishment of a national carbon registry, a carbon market working group and a national monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) system.
Document Title: Pakistan Policy Guidelines for Trading in Carbon Markets 2025

Family Name: Agreement on the Operating Rules of the Fertilizer Program for Fiscal Year 2025
Family Summary: This policy establishes the operational rules for Mexico's 2025 Fertilizer Programme, a national initiative designed to enhance agricultural productivity and support food security. Rooted in constitutional mandates for rural development, food sovereignty, and equitable resource distribution, the programme targets small and medium-scale producers of designated staple crops. It operates under broader frameworks including the Law of Sustainable Rural Development and aligns with specific Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 2.3 (doubling small-scale agricultural productivity) and SDG 1.5 (building resilience in vulnerable communities). The programme prioritises direct support to marginalised regions and indigenous communities, emphasising unconditioned aid delivery without intermediaries to foster inclusive rural transformation.The policy integrates climate and energy transition considerations through environmental safeguards and resilience-building measures. Explicitly prohibits fertiliser distribution in protected natural areas (e.g., core zones of biosphere reserves) and lands with unauthorised land-use changes, thereby preventing ecological degradation linked to intensive agriculture. It further supports climate adaptation by targeting vulnerable zones to strengthen food self-sufficiency systems and promote sustainable production practices.
Document Title: Agreement announcing the Operating Rules of the Fertilizer Program for fiscal year 2025 (Acuerdo por el que se dan a conocer las Reglas de Operación del Programa de Fertilizantes para el ejercicio fiscal 2025)

Family Name: Government Decree 2/2025 on a grant to promote the decarbonisation and energy efficiency of industrial production processes and the transition to a climate-neutral economy
Family Summary:
This decree provides for such a provision in the State Aid Act (688/2001) granted as a special grant pursuant to Section 5 Subsection 3 for investment projects related to the promotion of low-carbon and energy efficiency in industrial production processes and the transition to a climate-neutral economy.

A grant may be granted for an investment project to be implemented in Finland, excluding the Åland Islands, whose impacts are estimated, based on an overall assessment, to be significant in terms of Finland's climate and economic policy objectives. A grant may be granted if the eligible costs of the investment are at least EUR 30,000,000.
Document Title: State Aid Act (688/2001)

Family Name: Greece Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030.

The specific objectives of the plan include: Implementing climate adaptation measures at national, regional, and local levels, focusing on sustainable land use and promoting sustainable urban mobility; Introducing waste management strategies that align with the principles of the circular economy and adhere to public procurement requirements; and increasing the share of renewable energy sources in gross final energy consumption and improving energy efficiency measures. This includes enhancing the use of biofuels and completely phasing out lignite for power generation in Greece by 2028 to address environmental protection concerns. The plan aims to achieve at least a 42.5% renewables share of gross final energy consumption by 2030, some some more ambitious sectoral sub-targets.

The National Plan outlines specific priorities and corresponding measures across various core sectors to achieve these objectives. These include: utilising resources within the emissions trading system; preserving biodiversity; ensuring the efficient use of water resources; maintaining and enhancing forest services and management; developing aquaculture and water management plans; implementing flood risk management strategies and managing coastal zones; preventing and responding to forest fires; and promoting sustainable food production and farm management, optimising agricultural land use
Document Title: Greece Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030

Family Name: Malta National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030. The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness.

Malta’s strategy under the Decarbonisation dimension is to ensure a transition to a low-carbon economy by a reduction of GHG emissions and an increase in renewable energy sources. In terms of Energy Security, Malta will follow its commitment to achieve a greater security of supply through the diversification of energy sources and suppliers. To ensure Malta's energy integration, the plan establishes policies and measures to increase the flexibility of the energy system. Malta will boost research, innovation and competitiveness, exploring enhanced biofuel usage and deploying an offshore renewable energy farms. The plan aims for a 25% renewable energy share by 2030.
Document Title: Malta - Final updated NECP 2021-2030 - Annex

Family Name: Slovenia Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030. The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness.

The plan establishes the following key objectives : 1) to reduce GHG emissions in transport, agriculture, general consumption, waste management, indutry, energy sectors, to reduce the use of fossil energy sources (phasing out consumption of coal as well as support for the implementation of pilot projects for the production of synthetic methane and hydrogen), to increase the share of renewables in energy end-use; 2) to improve energy and material efficiency in all sectors; 3) to provide additional financial, human and technical resources to expedite the integrated development of the electricity distribution network to reinforce resistance to disruption and boost connectivity; 4) to invest in human resources and new knowledge, to support businesses for a competitive transition to a climate-neutral and circular economy, and to promote new RD programmes. Key quantified targets for 2030 include a 35-45% reduction in total greenhouse gas emissions compared to 2005 (the exact value depends on an unfinalised timeline of nuclear power decommissioning), and a renewable share of energy production of at least 55%. Coal will be fully phased out by 2033.

The plan establishes the following key objectives : 1) to reduce GHG emissions in transport, agriculture, general consumption, waste management, indutry, energy sectors, to reduce the use of fossil energy sources (phasing out consumption of coal as well as support for the implementation of pilot projects for the production of synthetic methane and hydrogen), to increase the share of renewables in energy end-use; 2) to improve energy and material efficiency in all sectors; 3) to provide additional financial, human and technical resources to expedite the integrated development of the electricity distribution network to reinforce resistance to disruption and boost connectivity; 4) to invest in human resources and new knowledge, to support businesses for a competitive transition to a climate-neutral and circular economy, and to promote new RD programmes. Key quantified targets for 2030 include a 35-45% reduction in total greenhouse gas emissions compared to 2005 (the exact value depends on an unfinalised timeline of nuclear power decommissioning), and a renewable share of energy production of at least 55%. Coal will be fully phased out by 2033.
Document Title: Slovenia Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030

Family Name: MMAF Regulation No. 1/2025 on the Procedures for Implementing Carbon Economic Value in the Marine Sector
Family Summary: Regulation of the Minister of Marine Affairs and Fisheries No. 1 of 2025 sets the rules for implementing a marine-sector carbon economy in Indonesia. It defines how monitoring, reporting, and verification must be done in line with national emission-reduction targets.
Document Title: MMAF Regulation No. 1/2025 on the Procedures for Implementing Carbon Economic Value in the Marine Sector

Family Name: National Climate Smart Agriculture Food Security and Action Plan (2016-2020)
Family Summary: This Action Plan provides the implementation framework for an effective development of climate-smart agriculture in the ground. It formulates specific strategies that will contribute developing climate-resilient agriculture and food systems for all agro-ecological zones, as well as the human resource capacity required for a climate-resilient agriculture promotion in Ghana.
Document Title: National Climate Smart Agriculture Food Security and Action Plan (2016-2020)

Family Name: National Forest Integrated Strategic Plan (2025-2043)
Family Summary:
This Plan ensures sutainable forest management and biodiversity conservation, and is provided for under the Forest Act. The integrated strategic plan will guide the provincial governments to sustainably manage national forests and to face the challenges seen in forest management in inter-provincial coordination and cooperation, and to increase the production and productivity of forest products. This will contribute to promoting a clean environment, self-reliance in forest products, export promotion, and green economy development.

Climate-related actions include:

  • Mapping climate change vulnerability and poverty analysis in the forest sector;
  • Formulating forest management action plans at all levels and ecosystem risk analysis;
  • Recognition and priorisation of climate change options in the forestry sector;
  • Climate change adaptation capacity development;
  • Plantation and promotion of forest vegetation adapted to climate change for the provision of goods and services from forests;
  • Diversification of income generation to increase the resilience of the poor, women, Dalits, indigenous peoples, and marginalised groups and forest management groups at risk of climate change;
  • Climate change and natural disaster risk analysis, risk reduction plan preparation and calculation.
Document Title: National Forest Integrated Strategic Plan (2025-2043)

Family Name: Vanuatu Loss and Damage Policy
Family Summary: Vanuatu's Loss and Damage Policy, published by the Department of Climate Change in 2025, provides a broad overview and an implementation roadmap for measures to improve loss and damage management under climate change. It establishes a taxonomy of loss and damage events; provides theoretical links to climate change mitigation, adaptation and disaster risk management; highlights priority research areas, particularly around quantifying impact projections; incorporates local action and traditional knowledge; and aims to center its country programme into the future around a single Loss and Damage Fund.
Document Title: Vanuatu Loss and Damage Policy

Family Name: Strategic Plan of the National System of Protected Wild Areas of Paraguay (SINASIP) 2020-2030
Family Summary:
It is Paraguay’s strategic roadmap for the National System of Protected Wild Areas (SINASIP) for the years 2025-2030. It aims to strengthen conservation, improve management and governance of protected areas, and ensure their sustainability.

The document acknowledges the fundamental role of natural ecosystems in mitigation and adaptation to climate change.

The document highlights as essential to develop and implement these plans with an emphasis on the conservation and adaptive measures to climate change, enabling strategic management that guarantees the protection of biodiversity and the resilience of ecosystems.
Document Title: Strategic Plan of the National System of Protected Wild Areas of Paraguay (SINASIP) 2020-2030

Family Name: National Energy Pact of the Republic of Côte d’Ivoire
Family Summary:
The National Energy Pact of the Republic of Côte d’Ivoire, aligned with its National Development Plan 2021-2025 and Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) No. 7 of the United Nations, constitutes a roadmap aimed at guaranteeing access to affordable, reliable, inclusive, sustainable, and clean energy for the entire Ivorian population. It aims to accelerate access to electricity and clean cooking to 100% and 50%, respectively, by 2030 and to significantly increase electricity generation capacity from renewable sources (45% by 2030).

The private sector will play a key role in achieving these objectives, with the ambition of mobilising approximately US$2 billion in private investment in energy production, transmission, distribution, and decentralised renewable energy (DRE) and clean cooking solutions.

This plan details the reforms to be implemented around five main pillars: (i) Rehabilitating and expanding energy production, transmission, and distribution infrastructure at competitive costs; (ii) Leveraging the benefits of increased regional integration; (iii) Adopting DRE and clean cooking solutions for affordable last-mile access as essential elements of the energy access agenda; (iv) Encourage private sector participation to mobilize additional resources; and (v) Ensure the financial viability and improve the operational efficiency of the electricity sector. This approach will mobilise the resources necessary to guarantee reliable, affordable, inclusive, sustainable, and clean energy, while contributing to the economic growth and development of the country and the region.
Document Title: National Energy Pact of the Republic of Côte d’Ivoire

Family Name: National Circular Economy Strategy and Action Plan
Family Summary: The National Circular Economy Strategy and Action Plan, which contributes towards combating climate change, strengthens the understanding of circular economy in Turkey and to implement environmentally friendly production and consumption models. Circular economy is not only a concept but also our responsibility for the future. With this strategy, Turkey will maximise resource efficiency, ensure the reuse of waste, and create new business and investment opportunities while protecting our environment. The objective is to increase the use of circular materials by minimising waste generation in our production and consumption processes, while achieving the net-zero emissions target by 2053. The action plan will encourage the adoption of environmentally friendly practices at every stage from industrial production to consumption and will instill circular economy awareness in all segments of society. In many sectors, from packaging to textiles, from electronic products to construction, sustainable and environmentally friendly solutions will be developed and these solutions will be integrated into production and consumption processes.
Document Title: National Circular Economy Strategy and Action Plan

Collection Name: Singapore's Green Data Centre Roadmap Implementation
Collection Summary: This Roadmap charts a sustainable pathway for the continued growth of data centres in Singapore to support its ambitions for the digital economy.
Family Name: Singapore Standard SS 715:2025 - Energy Efficiency of Data Centre IT Equipment
Family Summary:
Derived from the Green Data Centre Roadmap, the new Singapore Standard “SS 715:2025: Energy Efficiency of Data Centre IT Equipment” is a Singapore standard that sets energy efficiency requirements for data center IT equipment, aiming to cut energy use by at least 30%. It is targeted at data centre operators, consultants, customers, and sustainability officers looking to optimise IT equipment procurement and operations for energy efficiency.

In its fact sheet, the standard aims to help users achieve at least 30% energy savings by:

  • Setting the Minimum energy efficiency performance level of IT equipment in data centres;
  • Establishing best practices and guidelines for selection and operation of IT equipment in data centres;
  • Support for higher temperature data centre operations.
Document Title: Singapore Standard SS 715:2025 - Energy Efficiency of Data Centre IT Equipment

Family Name: Sectoral Adaptation Plan - Agriculture, Forestry and Seafood
Family Summary:
The 2024 National Adaptation Framework (NAF) requires the development of Sectoral Adaptation Plans (SAPs) for 13 key sectors. The SAPs were developed applying a six-step adaptation planning process described in Sectoral Planning Guidelines for Climate Change Adaptation to prepare the ground, conduct a climate impact screening, prioritise impacts, conduct a detailed climate risk assessment, develop goals, objectives and actions, and establish governance and implementation frameworks.

The goals of the Agriculture, Forestry and Seafood Climate Change Sectoral Adaptation Plan are to:

  • Establish a cohesive framework for governance, collaboration and cross sector resilience in agriculture, forestry, and seafood;
  • Promote sustainable agricultural practices that enhance resilience and safeguard the natural environment;
  • Promote sustainable forest management that enhances resilience and safeguards the natural environment; and
  • Maintain sustainable fishing and aquaculture practices, and enhance resilience of the seafood sector.

Examples of actions include:

  • Strategically investing in and facilitating targeted climate adaptation research and innovation across agriculture, forestry, and seafood sectors, leveraging the expertise of key national research bodies;
  • Encouraging farm diversification to improve the resilience of the agri-food sector;
  • Developing a facility for forest research and innovation with a strong focus on sustainability, circular economy and value creation; and
  • Supporting a resilient, climate smart, environmentally sustainable and profitable Irish seafood sector in order to maximise its contribution to jobs and growth and maintaining the economic and social activities of our most vibrant and sustainable coastal communities.
Document Title: Sectoral Adaptation Plan - Agriculture, Forestry and Seafood

Family Name: Reimaanlok Conservation Area Management Planning Framework
Family Summary:
This Framework uses community-based tools and approaches to establish and manage protected/conservation areas. It provides for the establishment and management of protected/conservation areas, including ecosystem-based adaptation methods such as conserving reefs, coasts and terrestrial ecosystems that buffer atolls against sea-level rise and climate impacts.

A Local Resource Committee (LRC) is first established by the municipal government to oversee the development of the resource management plan in that atoll. The LRC consists of representatives from the local government, traditional leadership, church leadership, men and women’s groups, youth, elderly and persons with disabilities. The plan is then developed with the community. The Coastal Management Advisory Council (CMAC) provides counsel, reviews project proposals and carries out relevant activities based on the Reimaanlok process.
Document Title: Reimaanlok Conservation Area Management Planning Framework

Family Name: National Energy Policy 2025 – 2034
Family Summary:
This Policy sets the strategic direction for Kenya's energy sector, to provide affordable, reliable, and sustainable energy that drives national development, economic growth, and climate resilience. It promotes distributed and decentralised energy solutions including mini-grids, standalone photovoltaic (PV) systems, productive use of energy, electric mobility and energy storage systems to ensure a just and equitable energy transition.

The Policy covers many areas of energy policy, from liquefield petroleum gas to electric cooking solutions to energy efficiency. There is also a framework for implementation, including coordination, regulation, reporting and funding, and a section on monitoring and evaluation.
Document Title: National Energy Policy 2025 – 2034

Family Name: National Gender and Climate Change Action Plan (2025-2027)
Family Summary: This Plan was developed to complement and build on the National Climate Change Action Plan (2023-2027) to effectively mainstream gender across eight priority areas, targets and implementatino mechanisms. The five strategic objectives of this Gender and Climate Change Action Plan are: (i) to mainstream gender in climate change laws, policies, action plans and strategies at both national and county levels; (ii) to increase access to climate finance through simplified, gender-responsive funding mechanisms; (iii) to create awareness of the gendered impacts of climate change; (iv) to increase access and adoption of gender responsive technology to accelerate adaptation and mitigation interventions; and (v) to track impacts of gender and climate change interventions.
Document Title: National Gender and Climate Change Action Plan (2025-2027)

Family Name: Green Transition Guarantee Project
Family Summary: This policy provides guarantees totaling KRW 1.5 trillion to small climate technology companies with excellent green technologies, as well as to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) promoting greenhouse gas reductions. The goal is to support smooth funding procurement for these enterprises, and to spur investment in facilities for carbon neutrality and low-carbon transition.
Document Title: Green Transition Guarantee Project

Family Name: Transport Sector Mitigation and Adaptation Plan
Family Summary: Sectoral mitigation strategy and adaptation plan focused on reducing emissions from transport through electrification and modal shift. Key measures include expanding electric bus fleets in Santiago and other regions, electrifying taxis and shared taxis (“colectivos”), expanding metro and rail networks, and developing cycling infrastructure. Implementation of these measures is expected to deliver at least 3.43 MtCO₂e in emissions reductions by 2030.
Document Title: Transport Sector Mitigation and Adaptation Plan (Plan Sectorial de Mitigación y Adaptación al Cambio Climático del Sector Transportes )

Family Name: Plan Mexico
Family Summary: Plan Mexico is an ambitious economic strategy that aims to position Mexico among the world's ten largest economies by 2030. The plan emphasizes the goal of producing 50% of domestic consumption in strategic sectors, such as energy, petrochemicals, and mobility, by that year. Measures affecting the energy sector include commitments to increase oil production and expand investment in clean energy sources.
Document Title: Plan Mexico

Family Name: Minerals Strategy
Family Summary: In 2025, the government launched the Minerals Strategy for New Zealand, and a Critical Minerals List that includes 37 minerals to guide the development of New Zealand's minerals sector until 2040.
Document Title: A Minerals Strategy for New Zealand to 2040

Family Name: 4th Basic Plan for the K-ETS
Family Summary: The basic plan sets out the plan to achieve the total greenhouse gas reduction target for greenhouse gas emitting businesses in accordance with Article 4 of the Act On The Allocation And Trading Of Greenhouse-Gas Emission Permits. It also sets out the issues with the K-ETS thus far, such as oversupply of allowances.
Document Title: 4th Basic Plan for the K-ETS

Family Name: Environmental Regulations RE2020
Family Summary:
The RE 2020 is the new energy and environmental regulations for all new construction. It introduces environmental performance in new construction via life cycle analysis.

The RE2020 applies in several stages:

  • initially, it concerns: individual houses and collective housing;
  • secondly, it concerns: primary and secondary education offices and buildings;
  • in a third step, it concerns specific tertiary buildings: hotels, shops, gymnasiums.

RE is broken down broadly into three areas: energy; comfort and carbon. ‘Energy’ relates mainly to the energy consumption required while the building is in operation, which is now based on CO2 emissions rather than kilowatt hours. This is referred to as ‘energy carbon impact’ in RE2020. ‘Comfort’ refers to the amount of discomfort permitted in hot weather. The regulations limit the maximum indoor temperature a building can reach during five consecutive hot summer days. ‘Carbon’ measurements are the climate-change impact of the construction itself, including the building materials and the construction process. This is known as the construction carbon impact, which will reduce significantly over the years, by 2025, 2028 and 2031.
Document Title: Consolidated regulatory texts

Family Name: Executive Order on Reduction of Greenhouse Gases from the Transport Sector and Sustainability of Biofuels
Family Summary:
This Order mandates biofuel blending requirements in transport fuels for aviation, shipping and road transport and implements the EU Renewable Energy Directive II (EU RED II), setting out the sustainability criteria for biofuels which apply regardless of their geographical origin. Enterprises shall report to the Danish Energy Agency on how they have complied with their obligations.

The Danish Energy Agency shall charge an annual fee to companies to cover the cost of administration in relation to the reduction of greenhoue gases from the aviation and maritime transport sectors.
Document Title: Danish energy ministry - Fuel displacement requirements
