Family Name: General Scheme for the Placement of Electric Power Facilities in the Russian Federation up to 2042
Family Summary: This strategy establishes the strategic framework for the development of power generation capacity and grid infrastructure from 2031 to 2042, focus on future electricity demand and system adequacy. According to the plans, fossil fuels will account for around 57% of electricity generation, nuclear power 24% (up from 18% in 2024), hydropower 15%, and wind and solar 3%.
Document Title: General Scheme for the Placement of Electric Power Facilities in the Russian Federation up to 2042

Family Name: Master Plan of the National System of Protected Natural Areas (SINANPE) [Plan Director del Sistema Nacional de Áreas Naturales Protegidas (SINANPE)]
Family Summary: Peru’s updated Director Plan for Protected Areas serves as the country’s ten-year national strategy for the management of the National System of Natural Protected Areas (SINANPE) and projects a vision to 2050. Structured around a renewed conceptual framework, strategic plan and set of policy guidelines, the document identifies 75 terrestrial and 36 marine priority sites to complete a representative, ecologically connected network that supports biodiversity conservation, climate-change mitigation and ecosystem-based adaptation. It aligns with the National Environment Policy (2030), the National Biodiversity Strategy (2050) and the National Climate Change Strategy (2050), embedding commitments to Peru’s NDCs through measures such as REDD⁺ projects, landscape-scale restoration, water-regulation initiatives and community-led nature-based solutions.Operationally, the Plan promotes integrated landscape governance that extends beyond protected-area boundaries, emphasising intercultural, gender and rights-based approaches and requiring collaboration among national agencies, regional and local governments, Indigenous peoples, civil society and the private sector. Key objectives for the 2025-2035 period include: reducing land- and water-use change, curbing deforestation, improving the status of threatened ecosystems and species, lessening pollution pressures, and strengthening institutional capacity and financing (including climate funds and the Fondo Verde). By coupling effective protection with climate resilience and sustainable livelihood opportunities, the Plan positions SINANPE as a cornerstone of Peru’s strategy to confront biodiversity loss, contribute measurable GHG reductions and safeguard ecosystem services critical to local and national development.
Document Title: Master Plan for Protected Natural Areas (Plan Director de las Áreas Naturales Protegidas)

Family Name: Ordinance GM/MMA 1.256 of December 26, 2024 on the AdaptaCidades Initiative
Family Summary: This Ordinance from the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (MMA) establishes the initiative to support the development of Municipal Climate Change Adaptation Plans (AdaptaCidades), to support states and municipalities in the development of local or regional climate change adaptation strategies and plans, as part of the Resilient Green Cities Programme. The programme allows states and municipalities to join, by signing the Adhesion Agreement, to promote integration and coordination between municipal, state and federal governments to strengthen climate adaptation and resilience policies. It establishes that resources from the National Climate Change Fund may be used to implement the AdaptaCidades initiative.
Document Title: Ordinance GM/MMA 1.256 of December 26, 2024

Family Name: Ordinance MF 2.046 of December 26, 2024
Family Summary: This Ordinance from the Ministry of Finance (MF) Authorises the Federal Government to pay up quotas, in local currency, in the Infrastructure Support Fund for Recovery and Adaptation to Extreme Climate Events (FIRECE).
Document Title: Ordinance MF 2.046

Family Name: Guiding Opinion on the Comprehensive Greening of Agricultural Development for Rural Ecological Revitalisation
Family Summary: This Opinion sets the target of 2030 for the preliminary establishment of green low-carbon agricultural systems. It sets out the aims to reduce the use of resources and inputs; the use of waste; the promotion of stable and diversified agricultural systems; and low-carbon supply chains. The implementation of these aims is to promote value transformation, recognising the ecological value of green agriculture products, and improve the carbon sequestration function of the agircultural sector. There is a focus on reducing methane emissions from rice fields, nitrogen dioxide emissions from agricultural land, methane emissions from enteric fermentation, and methane and nitrogen dioxide emissions from manure management.
Document Title: Guiding Opinion on the Comprehensive Greening of Agricultural Development for Rural Ecological Revitalisation

Family Name: Maldives Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy 2024–2030
Family Summary:
The Maldives faces a growing threat from natural hazards due to climate change and anthropogenic hazards. This Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) Strategy outlines a comprehensive and collaborative approach, aligned with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (SFDRR), to build a more resilient nation. The seven key priorities of this Strategy are: -

  1. Strengthen governance and legal frameworks;
  2. Enhanced multi-hazard risk assessment;
  3. Building resilience through infrastructure and nature;
  4. Empowering communities for effective response;
  5. Strengthening early warning systems and preparedness;
  6. Promoting comprehensive recovery and livelihood resilience; and
  7. Cultivating a culture of safety and climate resilience.
Document Title: Maldives Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy 2024–2030

Family Name: State planning guidelines for climate and energy
Family Summary:
The purpose of the guidelines is to ensure that climate and energy are emphasized in planning according to the Planning and Building Act 2008 and other government exercises and activities in the state, municipalities and county authorities. Climate includes both the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, carbon capture and storage and adaptation to expected climate change. The guidelines clarify the state's expectations of how this should be done, and the state's contribution to the knowledge base and guidance.

The guidelines should contribute to:

a.Norway's national climate goals as set out in the Climate Act;

b.the basis of life and natural diversity for current and future generations;

c.good security of energy supply;

d.society and ecosystems' preparation for and adaptation to climate change; and

e. the work to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, more efficient and flexible energy use, better climate adaptation and other environmental goals;

f. the clarification of roles and responsibilities of state, county authorities and municipalities; and

g. municipalities and county authorities prioritising climate and energy considerations in their exercise of authority, and the municipalities in their activities.
Document Title: State planning guidelines for climate and energy

Collection Name: China's Greenhouse Gas Emissions Accounting, Reporting and Verification Guidelines for Power Generation Facilities
Collection Summary: These guidelines seek to improve the quality of carbon emission data, and the national carbon emission trading system and enhance corresponding technical specifications.
Family Name: Guidelines for Accounting and Reporting of Greenhouse Gas Emissions for Enterprises – Power Generation Facilities
Family Summary: This document provides the guidelines for the accounting of greenhouse gas, fossil fuel combustion, and purchased and used electricity emissions for power generation facilities. It includes provisions for carbon emission data quality management, reporting and other information disclosure requirements. It applies to power generation facilities that participate in the National Carbon Emissions Trading Market and use fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas to generate electricity.
Document Title: Guidelines for Accounting and Reporting of Greenhouse Gas Emissions for Enterprises – Power Generation Facilities

Family Name: Austria Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030.

Austria's plan aims in particular to improve the development of transport, a sector which still needs improvement in Austria, especially in built-up areas and along transit routes. With some emphasis on the transport sector, the general decarbonisation objectives of the plan are as follows: 1) the general reduction of GHG emissions (non-ETS) by 48% compared to 2005, 2) to strengthen and develop public transport, 3) mobility management for businesses, towns and cities, municipalities, regions and tourism, 4) e-mobility in private transport, 5) to green the standard fuel consumption tax and the engine-related insurance tax, 6) to introduce a tax deduction for electric bicycles and motorcycles. Decarbonisation measures are also targeted to buildings, agriculture, forestry, waste management, fluorinated gases and spatial planning. For energy, the main objective is to increase the share of renewable energy in gross final energy consumption of energy to at least 57%, and source 100% of electricity consumption from renewables (nationally/balanced).To achieve this goal, the main instrument remains taxation (tax advantages/exemptions). The plan also aims to ensure measures concerning : 1) energy efficiency, 2) internal energy markets, 3) research/innovation/competitiveness, 4) evaluation and monitoring.
Document Title: Austria - Final Updated NECP (Annex) 2021 - 2030

The plan establishes 'key policy planning priorities' with specific measures: 1) GHG emissions and removals: promotion of natural gas and RES, reduction of emissions in the transport, agricultural and waste sector, increasing carbon sinks and improving energy efficiency in building and infrastructure; 2) Renewable energy sources : promotion of synergies with other sectors (Energy Efficiency, Waste, Security of supply) to promotion RES in all energy sectors, support schemes for RES to participate in the Electricity Market, etc; 3) Energy efficiency: energy efficiency obligation scheme for energy distributors, implementation of information and education measures, etc; 4) Security of supply: increasing the flexibility of the national energy system; 5) Internal Energy market: promotion of electricity interconnectivity of Cyprus via the project of common interest EuroAsia Interconnector, etc. Specific targets include a 32% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030, from a 2005 baseline, and a renewables share by 2030 of at least 29% in the primary energy consumption of the transport sector.
Document Title: Cyprus - Final Updated NECP (Annex 2) 2021 - 2030

Family Name: Action plan for the Swedish Transport Agency's work on climate adaptation 2025-2029
Family Summary:
According to the Ordinance(2018:1428) on the climate adaptation work of authorities, the authorities concerned shall draw up an action plan. This action plan is based on the climate and vulnerability analysis developed by the Swedish Transport Agency.

The measures in the action plan aim to develop work on climate adaptation throughout the authority. The measures that have been decided will be implemented primarily by the Roads and Railways Department and the Maritime and Aviation Department in collaboration with the relevant departments and activities.

The overall objective of transport policy is to ensure a socio-economically efficient and long-term sustainable transport supply for citizens and businesses throughout the country.

The Agency sees a need to inform and cooperate with the people/sections involved in the regulatory process at the Swedish Transport Agency. In the traffic safety supervision of railways, the Agency has a mandate to integrate issues about the actors' management of risks resulting from a changing climate. There is also a need to continue to monitor the impacts of climate on airport accessibility.
Document Title: Action plan for the Swedish Transport Agency's work on climate adaptation 2025-2029

Family Name: National Agreement for the Human Right to Water and Sustainability
Family Summary: This Mexican National Agreement for the Human Right to Water and Sustainability establishes a framework for addressing water scarcity and quality issues across the country. Rooted in the constitutional right to water access, sanitation, and sustainable resource use, the agreement acknowledges the interconnectedness of water security with human rights, environmental preservation, and climate change mitigation. The document highlights the severe challenges facing Mexico's water resources, including limited management of surface and groundwater, pollution from untreated wastewater, and unequal water distribution exacerbated by climate change impacts, particularly droughts affecting agricultural production.The core objective is to guarantee the human right to sufficient and safe water, alongside promoting efficient water use in industrial, agricultural, and livestock sectors. This aims to be achieved through collaborative investments in infrastructure, public-private partnerships for local improvements, effective concession management, and digitising administrative processes. The agreement explicitly addresses climate change by calling for adaptation and mitigation measures, including reforestation and environmental restoration, pollution reduction, and the promotion of water treatment, reuse, and innovative technologies.
Document Title: National Agreement for the Human Right to Water and Sustainability (Acuerdo Nacional por el Derecho Humano al Agua y la Sustentabilidad)

Family Name: Exempt Resolution No.7120/2024 of the MMA [Resolución Exenta N° 7120/2024 del MMA]
Family Summary:
Exempt Resolution No. 7120/2024 recognizes and partially approves the following 'External Certification Programs':

- Cercarbono by Certificadora de Carbono.

- BioCarbon Standard

Key Points for Mitigation Activities

- Renewable energy projects will be excluded from partial recognition if they meet both of the following criteria:

They do not have emission reduction certificates issued by September 29, 2023, for reductions corresponding to 2020, 2021, 2022, or 2023.

The technologies used account for more than 5% of the installed capacity of the National Electric System.

- The exclusion does not apply to renewable energy projects that:

Are for self-consumption, with or without grid injection.

Are connected to an electrical system with a capacity less than 1,500 kW.

Are connected to an electrical system with installed generation capacity under 200 MW and net power equal to or less than 50 MW.

Are hybrid systems with energy storage, with net power equal to or less than 15 MW.

Are linked to generation systems with excess power of no more than 9,000 kW connected to the National Electric System.
Document Title: Exempt Resolution No.7120/2024 of the MMA [Resolución Exenta N° 7120/2024 del MMA]

Family Name: Powering Canada’s Future: A Clean Electricity Strategy
Family Summary:
This Clean Electricity Strategy builds on the vision of providing clean, reliable and affordable energy to support a competitive, net-zero emissions Canadian economy, with growing supply attracting investment and creating good jobs. This Strategy articulates the federal government’s role, focusing on three key areas:

  • Growing the grid and managing demand;
  • Providing policy certainty and smoothing the path; and
  • Collaborating on tailored approaches for every region.

There are six key principles underpinning this Strategy:

  • Principle 1: Provincial and Territorial Jurisdiction Must be Respected and Supported with Policy Certainty;
  • Principle 2: Electricity Must Remain Reliable and Affordable;
  • Principle 3: Electricity Demand and Supply Must be Considered Equally;
  • Principle 4: Canadian Industries, Investors, and Workers Must Have the Power Needed to Build Canada’s Industrial Future;
  • Principle 5: Northern, Indigenous, and Remote Communities Must Benefit from a Flexible Approach that Reflects Their Unique Opportunities and Challenges; and
  • Principle 6: Indigenous Peoples and Communities Must be Recognized as Clean Energy Leaders.
Document Title: Powering Canada’s Future: A Clean Electricity Strategy

Family Name: English Devolution White Paper
Family Summary:
In the area of environment and climate change, the UK government has committed to making Britain a clean energy superpower. So that Strategic Authorities can play their role in this mission, it will make the following changes: 

  • Mayors will be handed control of retrofit funding as part of the Integrated Settlements, providing a strengthened route to local delivery of the Warm Homes Plan.
  • Strategic Authorities will have a strategic role in the delivery of the Great British Energy Local Power Plans, delivering local sustainable energy generation.
  • They will also have a role in the wider energy system, delivering the transition to Net Zero and to a low-cost, clean power energy system by 2030, become the zoning co-ordinators for local heat networks, and with their plans taken into account in the National Energy System operators’ Regional Energy Strategic Plans.
  • Finally, we will expand Strategic Authorities’ role in leading Local Nature Recovery Strategies.

In addition, future opportunities for devolution and partnership working will be explored with Strategic Authorities. These could include issues like water management, the circular economy, pollution, or flood resilience. The UK government will also explore how Strategic Authorities and Mayors can provide greater local leadership in responding to the impacts of climate change, and a better route for rural communities to be considered in local policy decision making.
Document Title: English Devolution White Paper

Family Name: Canada Offshore Renewable Energy Regulations
Family Summary: These Regulations stipulate that in respect of an offshore renewable energy project, information submitted in an application for an authorization must demonstrate that the work or activities will be carried on in a manner that is safe and secure, that protects property and the environment, that is in conformity with all applicable laws in respect of safety, security and environmental protection and that takes into account the potential impacts of climate change.
Document Title: Canada Offshore Renewable Energy Regulations

Family Name: Energy Sector Plan 2023-2028
Family Summary: This plan guides the development of the Samoan energy sector over the medium term, emphasising the need to adapt to climate risk by diversifying the energy supply, and mitigate emissions by switching to renewable energy. It aims to to achieve a 70% renewable share of energy consumption by 2031, and develop solar, wind, biomass and hydroelectric generation infrastructure as well as significant grid improvements. The plan notes the need for development to be inclusive, emphasising the effectiveness of local ownership over off-grid renewable generation systems.
Document Title: Energy Sector Plan 2023-2028

Family Name: Clean Power 2030 Action Plan
Family Summary: The Clean Power 2030 Action Plan sets out how the UK government will work with the clean power sector, including industry, trade unions, investors, policy makers and others, to achieve its clean power goal. The goal is to have clean sources produce at least as much power as consumed in the whole year, and at least 95% of the power generated. Unabated gas supply will be used only when essential. 43-50 GW of offshore wind, 27-29 GW of onshore wind, and 45-47 GW of solar power will be added.The UK will invest around £40 billion per year for six years from 2025 to 2030. Actions to accelerate the delivery of clean power include: reforming grid connections; reforming the planning system; renewal and nuclear project delivery; electricity market reform; short-duration energy storage and flexibility; long-duration flexible capacity; more sustainable supply chains and a skilled workforce.The plan will reduce over-reliance on fossil fuels and exposure to the cost of globally traded oil and gas in the context of recent global insecurity.
Document Title: Clean Power 2030 Action Plan

Family Name: Clean Electricity Regulations: SOR/2024-263
Family Summary:
The purpose of these Regulations is to protect the environment and human health from the threat of climate change by establishing a regime that prohibits excessive carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions from the use of fossil fuel to generate electricity.

The Regulations are meant to: -

  1. enable significant greenhouse gas reductions to ensure a net-zero electricity grid by 2050;
  2. enable provinces and territories to maintain electricity affordability for Canadians and businesses; and
  3. enable provinces and territories to maintain grid reliability as Canada’s electricity needs to grow.

The Regulations adopt an absolute emissions approach expressed as an annual emissions limit (i.e., tonnes of CO2e (t) per year). Before 2050, generating units must adhere to an annual emissions limit of 65 t/GWh. A unit may emit up to 35 t/GWh above the 65 t/GWh limit by remitting an equivalent amount of eligible offset credits. The Regulations also The CER introduces a compliance credit system, rewarding generating units that operate below their emissions intensity limits, and offer operators flexibility through emissions trading and credit pooling mechanisms.
Document Title: Clean Electricity Regulations: SOR/2024-263

Family Name: Strategic Plan of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry 2024-2028
Family Summary:
This Strategic Plan sets out the objectives, targets, and performance indicators for the protection of agriculture, forestry, and water resources, along with natural ecosystems. The objective related to climate change is to enhance adaptation capacity and resilience to climate change. The relevant targets are:

  • Enhancing capacity for adaptation to climate change;
  • Increasing greenhouse gas emission reduction capacity and promoting the use of renewable energy;
  • Enhancing capacity to combat agricultural drought; and
  • Mitigating the adverse effects of floods and waterlogging.

A regulatory analysis was also conducted for the Strategic Plan. The following needs were identified:

  • The preparation of an overarching regulation covering all sectors to harmonise water efficiency policy within the framework of adaptation to climate change;
  • Increasing education and awareness activities on climate change, drought, and desertification were needed; and
  • Planning production in a manner that adapts to water scarcity and climate change.
Document Title: Strategic Plan of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry 2024-2028

Family Name: German Climate Adaptation Strategy 2024
Family Summary:
The strategy defines measurable goals for climate adaptation in Germany, a total of 33 goals and 45 sub-goals. Most goals are to be achieved by 2030, some by 2050. The objectives are assigned indicators to measure the achievement of objectives. The following applies: No additional bureaucratic burdens or reporting obligations will be created for citizens or companies.

The objectives are assigned to seven clusters that reflect the entire range of adaptation and prevention:

  1. Infrastructure
  2. Land and land use
  3. human health and care
  4. Urban development, spatial planning and civil protection
  5. Water
  6. ECONOMICS
  7. Cross-cluster topics

The strategy aims to strengthen the resilience, i.e. the resilience, of the landscape water balance – this means above all, to restore the ability of the landscape to store water. This requires, among other things, as many unsealed surfaces as possible that can absorb water and healthy, loose soils that can store the water for a long time. This is a sub-goal to the goal of "Preserving available water resources in the long term".

The Adaptation Action Plan IV (APA IV) (Annex 2 to the Strategy) implements the Climate Adaptation Strategy 2024 and defines the measures with which the Federal Government is driving forward Germany's adaptation to climate change and how it is supporting responsible stakeholders in the implementation of measures. It presents the federal government's current and future measures for adapting to the climate impacts.
Document Title: Adaptation Action Plan (APAIV)

Family Name: National Plan for Integrated Disaster Risk Reduction Management 2024-2034
Family Summary:
The National Plan for the Comprehensive Management of Disaster Risk Reduction 2024-2034 - Plan GIRRDD - aims to strengthen prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, recovery and rehabilitation in Guatemala; linking institutional actions of the public, academic and scientific sectors, private sector, cooperation and civil society, in the management of disaster risk reduction at different levels, contributing to the protection and achievement of sustainable development.Its specific goals are:

  • Systematically identify and assess risks to achieve the strengthening of institutional and community capacities in risk reduction management.
  • Promote a culture of resilience at all levels of society based on the human rights-based approach at all territorial levels.
  • Determine indicators and monitoring and evaluation mechanisms to ensure the effectiveness of implemented actions, adjusting strategies as necessary.
Document Title: Plan Nacional de Gestión Integral de Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres 2024-2034 (National Plan for Integrated Disaster Risk Reduction Management 2024-2034)

Family Name: Portugal Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030. The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness.

The plan establishes the following objectives: 1) to limit the GHG emissions, to build a strategy based on renewable sources of energy on the path to a carbon neutral economy (electrification of the economy and consumption, promote electric vehicles,introduce of renewable gases); 2) Rehabilitating and making buildings more efficient, to promote active and shared mobility, reinforce public transport and electric mobility; 3) to diversificate energy sources by the development of endogenous renewable energy resources; 4) to promote interconnectivity in energy markets and systems; 5) to invest in public and private research, innovation and competitiveness. This plan increases Portugal's non-ETS net GHG emissions reduction target for 2030 (relative to 2005) from a 17% reduction to 28.7%.
Document Title: Portugal Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030

Family Name: Ordinance MF 964, of June 11, 2024, on the Eco Invest Brasil Programme
Family Summary: This Ordinance from the Ministry of Finance (MF) establishes the criteria for the eligibility of investments to the Eco Invest Brasil Programme, the allocation of resources, the processes for the qualification of financial agents and the rendering of accounts, as well as the governance structure of the External Private Capital Mobilisation and Exchange Protection Line, within the scope of the Programme, establishes the composition and powers of the Programme's Executive Committee and makes other provisions. It defines the economic activities eligible for funding under the Eco Invest Brasil Programme as those that contribute to ecological transformation, decarbonisation and increased resilience to climate change impacts, specifying the priority activities.
Document Title: Ordinance MF 964, of June 11, 2024

Family Name: The First Nations Clean Energy Strategy 2024-2030
Family Summary:
The Strategy’s vision is a sustainable clean energy future for all Australians, with Country and Culture at the Heart. The vision is underpinned by three goals:

  • empower First Nations communities with clean energy
  • achieve economic benefits with First Nations peoples
  • enable equitable partnerships.

A further 11 objectives and 24 priority areas for action support the goals and vision.
Document Title: The First Nations Clean Energy Strategy 2024-2030

Family Name: Guidance on climate and sustainability in planning
Family Summary: This Guide reviews the new possibilities in the Planning Act, which aim to help municipalities, based on local wishes and considerations, raise the climate agenda by planning for a green transition, prioritizing climate considerations in physical planning and using physical planning as an active tool in preventive climate efforts. The guide on climate and sustainability in planning reviews the parts of the aforementioned changes to the Planning Act that relate to climate, green transition and nature. The guide elaborates on the new possibilities for taking climate considerations into account in planning, planning for renewable energy, requiring mitigation measures as a condition for commissioning, planning for parking that supports the green transition and ensuring urban nature.
Document Title: Guidance on climate and sustainability in planning

Family Name: Country Plan for Green Growth and Climate Actions (2024-2028)
Family Summary: The Vietnam-GGGI Country Planning Framework (CPF) 2024-2028, launched on December 6, 2024, aims to support Vietnam's green growth and climate action objectives, including achieving net-zero emissions by 2050. The framework focuses on seven strategic areas: green investments, climate action, green industries, climate-resilient agriculture, waste management, green buildings, and carbon pricing, aligning with national policies such as the updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 2022 and the National Power Development Plan 8 (PDP8).
Document Title: Viet Nam Country Planning Framework 2024-2028

Family Name: National Strategy for Transformation (NST2, 2024-2029)
Family Summary: The strategy provides a short term framework to guide national development priorities, and underscores the need to mainstream climate change adaptation and mitigation across sectors. It contributes to Rwanda's Vision 2050, as well as addressing more immediate issues. The primary axis of climate action in this strategy is in enhancing agri-food systems, improving wellbeing, economic resilience and also international trade balances through exports. It promotes major investments in irrigation technology and deployment, and landscape-level measures such as agroforestry and forest restoration. It aims to mobilise $3 billion USD for nature and climate issues, and create 1.25 million jobs, upskilling the labour force in crucial sectors for sustainability.
Document Title: National Strategy for Transformation (NST2, 2024-2029)

Family Name: Circular No. 19/2024/TT-BNNPTNT on MRV and GHG Inventory for Livestock Sector
Family Summary: This Circular, issued by the Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development, details the technical requirements for the measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) of greenhouse gas emissions reductions and greenhouse gas inventory for livestock. The Department of Livestock is responsible for compiling information to produce an inventory report for livestock. It also has to build a basic emissions baseline for 2026-2020 and develop a plan to monitor and supervise the implementation of the sectoral plan to reduce GHG emissions.
Document Title: Circular No. 19/2024/TT-BNNPTNT on MRV and GHG Inventory for Livestock Sector

Family Name: National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction 2024-2030
Family Summary: Moldova's National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction 2024-2030 recognises an increasing risk of natural disasters due to climate change. The strategy calls for greater co-ordination between sectors, capacity building and greater data integration such as the production of national hazard vulnerability maps. It aims to conform to EU standards on disaster risk reduction, and names government agencies responsible for specific elements of this process.
Document Title: National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction 2024-2030

Family Name: National REDD+ Strategy (SN-REDD+) 2024
Family Summary: Burkina Faso's National REDD+ Strategy (SN-REDD+) from 2024 notes the economic importance of sustainable forest usage for alleviating rural poverty, and aims to promote sustainable management and restoration over the 2024-2033 period, contributing to domestic development goals and international land-based net emissions mitigation efforts. The strategy aims to roughly quadruple the carbon sequestration of forest land in Burkina Faso by 2033, relative to 2022, via substantial and funded reforestation, afforestation and forest restoration projects. Other priority areas in the strategy include promoting increases in agricultural productivity, to prevent the need for encroachment on forest land.
Document Title: National REDD+ Strategy (SN-REDD+) 2024

Family Name: National Strategy of Regional Development (NSRD) 2024-2028
Family Summary:
The National Strategy of Regional Development (NSRD) determines the national priorities in regional development policies and functions as a blueprint for the regional development plans of 26 regional development agencies (DAs), action plans of regional administrations, other national and regional development strategies, the public investment and budgeting process, and specific territorial development programs.

The NSRD (2024-2028)'s vision is "With its globally competitive, prosperous and resilient regions and by using its local dynamics completely developed Türkiye" Within the scope of the new NSRD, nine themes have been determined: urban development, rural development, social policies, industry-logistics-transportation, green growth, RD and innovation, entrepreneurship, digitalization and tourism. Strategies have been developed for the 2024-2028 period under these themes, including on combating climate change.
Document Title: National Strategy of Regional Development (NSRD) 2024-2028

Family Name: Roadmap for Green Fuels in Transport and Industry 2024
Family Summary:
The Roadmap for Green Fuels in Transport and Industry is developed and published by MissionGreenFuels in collaboration with Ramboll. MissionGreenFuels is one of four state-initiated mission-driven green research and innovation partnerships supported by the Innovation Fund Denmark and Next Generation EU. This roadmap is designed to guide Denmark towards Denmark's goals of being a leader in green fuel technology nad helping other nations accelerate their shift to green fuels, aligning with the government's ambitious targets of reducing carbon emissions by 70% by 2030 and reaching full decarbonization by 2050.

This roadmap is a tool for researchers, policymakers, and other central stakeholders. It provides a comprehensive framework to address technical, commercial, regulatory, social, and sustainability challenges that impede the widespread adoption of green fuels. The document identifies critical activities across these domains, with a focus on advancing technology readiness, scaling production capabilities, and improving market competitiveness of green fuels.

This document explores the following dimensions:

  • Technical innovations: Advancing production, storage, distribution, and offtake technologies to enhance efficiency and scalability.
  • Commercial strategies: Lowering costs and improving market competitiveness to ensure economic viability vis-à-vis conventional fossilbased fuels.
  • Regulatory frameworks: Supportive policies that incentivize the growth and integration of green fuels into the broader energy system.
  • Social considerations: Public perception, community engagement, and workforce development to foster broad societal support and a social license to operate. By taking a holistic approach, this roadmap outlines clear priorities and actionable steps for green fuels stakeholders. It aims to drive immediate actions and guide long-term strategies to position Denmark as a leader in green fuels, supporting both national and global climate goals.
Document Title: Roadmap for Green Fuels in Transport and Industry 2024

Family Name: Energy Sector Mitigation and Adaptation Plan
Family Summary: This plan (Plan Sectorial de Mitigación y Adaptación de Energía) outlines the mitigation measures needed for Chile’s energy sector to meet its NDC and other sectoral targets, namely the 80% of electricity generation from renewables by 2030 and 2040 coal phase-out for the energy sector. It identifies policy measures across electricity generation, electrification, and energy efficiency. It estimates energy efficiency measures to contribute to around 7% of Chile’s cumulative emissions reductions by 2050. The plan also emphasises developing Chile’s green hydrogen economy and includes a target for green hydrogen to make up 15% of final non-electric energy consumption by 2035 and 70% by 2050.
Document Title: Energy Sector Mitigation and Adaptation Plan (Plan de Mitigación y Adaptación al Cambio Climático de Energía)

Family Name: Mining Sector Mitigation and Adaptation Plan
Family Summary: This sectoral plan (Plan Sectorial de Cambio Climático: Sector Minería) outlines the mitigation measures needed to align the mining sector with Chile’s climate commitments and 2050 National Mining Policy, including measures related to electrification, green hydrogen adoption, energy efficiency improvements, and renewable energy contracts and distributed generation. It reiterates the targets from the National Mining Policy, including a carbon neutral sector by 2040, a 50% reduction in emissions for large mining operations by 2030, and targeting 90% of renewable energy contracts by 2030 and 100% by 2050.
Document Title: Decreto número 24, de 2024.- Aprueba Plan Sectorial de Mitigación y de Adaptación al Cambio Climático en el Sector Minería

Family Name: Mining Sector Mitigation and Adaptation Plan
Family Summary: This sectoral plan (Plan Sectorial de Cambio Climático: Sector Minería) outlines the mitigation measures needed to align the mining sector with Chile’s climate commitments and 2050 National Mining Policy, including measures related to electrification, green hydrogen adoption, energy efficiency improvements, and renewable energy contracts and distributed generation. It reiterates the targets from the National Mining Policy, including a carbon neutral sector by 2040, a 50% reduction in emissions for large mining operations by 2030, and targeting 90% of renewable energy contracts by 2030 and 100% by 2050.
Document Title: Mining Sector Mitigation and Adaptation Plan 2025-2029 (Plan Sectorial de Cambio Climático: Sector Minería 2025-2029)

Family Name: Housing and Urban Development Sector Mitigation and Adaptation Plan
Family Summary: This sectoral plan outlines the mitigation measures needed for Chile’s housing sector and urban development to meet its NDC and other sectoral targets. The primary mitigation actions include energy efficiency improvements (e.g. new thermal insulation standards, stricter building codes, retrofitting), the electrification of residential energy use, and expanding sustainable urban infrastructure. The plan reiterates Chile’s national energy efficiency targets, established under the Energy Efficiency Law, of reducing final energy consumption in the buildings sector by 10% by 2030 and by 35% by 2050.
Document Title: Sectoral Mitigation Plan of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Development and Update of the Climate Change Adaptation Plan for Cities

Family Name: National electric Cooking Strategy
Family Summary: National policy and framework aiming to accelerate the adoption of electric cooking, with the objective of reaching 10% of Kenyan households in 2028. It provides a roadmap of policy measures including market development, institional coordination, behaviour change, and financing. The strategy is aligned with Kenya's broader goals outlined in the National Cooking Transition Strategy.
Document Title: Kenya National electric Cooking Strategy (KNeCS) 2024

Family Name: New Zealand's second emissions reduction plan 2026-30
Family Summary: The second emission reduction plan was initially published in December 2024 and then amended in January 2026. The plan details how the country will meet the second emissions budget in light of the revised approach to reducing agricultural emissions (i.e. the decision against an on-farm agricultural emissions pricing system). The second emissions budget covers the period of 2026-2030 and has a limit of 249.2 MtCO2e.
Document Title: New Zealand's second emissions reduction plan 2026-2030

Family Name: National Urban Stormwater Plan (PNAPU)
Family Summary:
The National Urban Rainwater Plan (PNAPU) is part of the National Water Plan and focus on urban drainage, drinking water, and sanitation. Its main goal is to ensure universal and sustainable access to these services while promoting efficient, effective, and quality water management.

A key objective is to integrate climate change impacts into the design and management of stormwater drainage systems. This includes incorporating climate risk management into stormwater projects and master plans, considering climate change scenarios, and conducting climate projections for design criteria. The aim is to develop a national methodology for including climate change in scenarios of economic constraints and high uncertainty, with the expectation that these criteria will become mandatory for approving drainage projects. The plan's strategy focuses on providing adequate flood protection, minimising pollution, and promoting the value of water and its services in urban areas, while improving living conditions.
Document Title: National Urban Stormwater Plan (PNAPU)

Family Name: National Strategy for Sustainable Bioeconomy (ENBS)
Family Summary:
Bioeconomy emerges as a development paradigm aimed at replacing fossil resources in the face of global challenges such as population growth, urbanization, climate change, depletion of non-renewable resources, and biodiversity loss. Sustainable bioeconomy plays a key role in transitioning to an economy designed to operate within planetary boundaries.

This approach supports international environmental commitments related to climate change mitigation and adaptation, biodiversity conservation, and combating desertification, as well as the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development adopted by the United Nations.

The goal of the National Strategy for Sustainable Bioeconomy (ENBS) is to position bioeconomy as an opportunity to consolidate productive diversification through the sustainable use of biological resources. The vision is for the country to strengthen its international position by adopting a sustainable, efficient, and innovative approach to using its biological and natural resources.

Bioeconomy development relies on the sustainable use of natural resources to ensure long-term economic growth. It serves as an integrative policy framework adopted by several countries to boost competitiveness, create jobs, promote social inclusion, and address environmental and climate change challenges
Document Title: National Strategy for Sustainable Bioeconomy (ENBS)

Family Name: National Urban Policy
Family Summary: This policy seeks to cover all of Australia’s cities, including Australia's capital cities in which nearly 18 million people reside. It provides a framework and goals that support all cities, large and small—from our central business districts to suburban and peri-urban realms and everything in between. The goals are: liveable and equitable; productive and innovative; and sustainable and resilient. Urban places value and protect Australia’s unique environment and biodiversity for future generations. Planning and development should support Australia's path to net zero and provide opportunities for connection with the environment. Australia's cities, communities and systems should be resilient to the impacts of climate change and other risks.
Document Title: National Urban Policy

Family Name: Action Plan for Transition to a Green Economy (2024–2030)
Family Summary: National medium-term action plan to implement Kazakhstan's 'green economy' concept. Establishes measurable indicators, annual reporting requirements, and clear inter-agency responsibilities, and outlines coordinated sectoral measures, including renewable energy expansion and improved energy efficiency, to support Kazakhstan's long-term carbon neutrality objectives.
Document Title: Resolution 1019/2024 approving the Action Plan for Transition to a Green Economy (2024–2030)

Family Name: Annual Climate Change Statement 2024
Family Summary: This is the Australian Government's annual progress report on climate change and energy initiatives. The Annual Climate Change Statement is a requirement under the Climate Change Act 2022. The statement must consider the Climate Change Authority's advice. It also outlines the government's response to the Authority's recommendations. The 2024 Statement is the third version.

Family Name: Tree Planting Taskforce
Family Summary: The UK's Tree Planting Taskforce was launched on 28 November 2024 to oversee the planting of millions of trees, aiming to meet net zero targets and enhance woodland resilience. Its key objectives include improving cross-nation collaboration, sharing best practices, and addressing barriers to tree planting. The UK is allocating up to £400 million for tree planting and peatland restoration over 2024 - 2026 to support the UK’s broader goal of increasing tree cover, including a legal target of 16.5% in England by 2050.
Document Title: Government Launches Tree Planting Taskforce to Oversee Planting of Millions of Trees Across Our Four Nations

Family Name: Supreme Decree No. 012-2024-MINAM. Approves the National Policy: National Strategy for Climate Change to 2050 (Decreto Supremo N° 012-2024-MINAM. Aprueba la Política Nacional: Estrategia Nacional ante el Cambio Climático al 2050)
Family Summary: This Supreme Decree establishes Peru’s long‑term framework (Política Nacional: Estrategia Nacional ante el Cambio Climático al 2050) for addressing climate change impacts while guiding a transition towards a low‑carbon and climate‑resilient development model. Applicable to all public entities, private stakeholders and civil society, the strategy is coordinated by the Ministry of Environment and implemented through national and sectoral planning systems. It sets out binding measures for adaptation and mitigation, supported by ongoing monitoring and evaluation in alignment with international climate commitments, notably the Paris Agreement.The Strategy seeks to reduce climate‑related damages by at least 20% by 2030 and 30% by 2050, focusing on sectors highly exposed to risks such as health, agriculture, fisheries, forests, water resources, tourism and transport. In mitigation, Peru commits to peak greenhouse gas emissions at 179 MtCO₂e in 2030 and achieve net‑zero emissions by 2050 through energy system decarbonisation, higher efficiency, enhanced forest conservation, circular economy approaches and sustainable agriculture. To deliver these goals, the policy outlines seven priority objectives, including reducing vulnerability among marginalised groups, promoting resilient infrastructure, fostering sustainable land use, expanding renewable energy and clean transport, and advancing governance through scientific research, citizen participation and the creation of “green jobs.” In this way, the strategy envisions a just and inclusive transition that curtails emissions and safeguards livelihoods across the country.
Document Title: National Policy: National Strategy on Climate Change to 2050 (Política Nacional: Estrategia Nacional ante el Cambio Climático al 2050)

Family Name: Climate Protection Ordinance
Family Summary: The Climate Protection Ordinance operationalizes the Climate and Innoavation Act (KlG) by defining specific funding programs, such as subsidies for replacing fossil fuel heating systems with renewable alternatives and energy efficiency measures. It also establishes a network for climate change adaptation, coordinating efforts between federal, cantonal, and local authorities, as well as the private sector. Additionally, it introduces voluntary climate stress tests for the financial sector to align investments with climate goals.
Document Title: Regulation on the Federal Act on the objectives in climate protection, innovation and the strengthening of energy security (Climate Protection Regulation, KlV)

Family Name: Climate Risk Assessment Methodology for Projects in the Public Investment Management System
Family Summary: Climate change poses a major threat to public investments, increasing risks and uncertainties that demand resilient infrastructure. For Niger, which is highly vulnerable—especially to frequent, severe floods—resilient and green public investments are essential to strengthen its adaptive capacity and support its transition to green infrastructure. Hence, the main objective of the strategy document is to gradually develop a "Climate Risk Assessment Methodology for projects in the Public Investment Management system" for Niger. This methodology will be implemented during the design and proposal stages for all Public Investment Program (PIP) projects. It is specifically designed to ensure that projects undertake progressively more sophisticated climate risk assessments as they advance, ultimately guaranteeing the long-term resilience and success of the nation's public investments.
Document Title: Climate Risk Assessment Methodology for Projects in the Public Investment Management System

Family Name: Ministerial Resolution No. 00411-2024-MINAM. Methodological document on the measurement of greenhouse gas emissions, reductions, and removals in the forests of the Amazon biome (Resolución Ministerial N°00411-2024-MINAM. Documento metodológico sobre la medición de las emisiones, reducciones y remociones de Gases de Efecto Invernadero en los bosques del bioma amazónico)
Family Summary: Ministerial Resolution N° 00411-2024-MINAM introduces a comprehensive methodological document for measuring greenhouse gas emissions, reductions, and removals in the Amazonian biome, addressing Peru's critical role in forest carbon accounting. The document establishes a standardized Measurement, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) framework aligned with Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) guidelines, focusing on the country's extensive Amazonian forest ecosystem, which represents over 50% of national territory and 93% of its forest areas. By providing a systematic approach to quantifying forest-related greenhouse gas dynamics, the resolution aims to enhance the reliability and consistency of climate change reporting, particularly in the context of Peru's international commitments under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the Paris Agreement.
Document Title: Methodological document on the measurement of greenhouse gas emissions, reductions, and removals in the forests of the Amazon biome (Documento metodológico sobre la medición de las emisiones, reducciones y remociones de Gases de Efecto Invernadero en los bosques del bioma amazónico)

Family Name: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate
Family Summary:
The Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate secures demand for SAF by obligating the supply of an increasing amount of SAF in the overall UK aviation fuel mix, and incentivising SAF supply through the award of tradeable certificates with a cash value.

The SAF Mandate starts in 2025 at 2% of total UK jet fuel demand, increasing linearly to 10% in 2030 and then to 22% in 2040. From 2040, the obligation will remain at 22% of total UK jet fuel demand until there is greater certainty regarding SAF supply. According to government estimates, the SAF Mandate could deliver up to 6.3 megatonnes of carbon savings per year by 2040.
Document Title: Sustainable Aviation Fuel Mandate: Compliance Guidance

Family Name: Principles for voluntary carbon and nature market integrity
Family Summary:
The UK government principles for voluntary carbon and nature market integrity are:

1. Use credits in addition to ambitious actions within value chains;

2. Use high integrity credits;

3. Measure and disclose the planned use of credits as part of sustainability reporting;

4. Plan ahead;

5. Make accurate green claims using appropriate terminology; and

6. Co-operate with others to support the growth of high integrity markets.
Document Title: Principles for voluntary carbon and nature market integrity

Family Name: Supreme Decree No. 010-2024-MINAM. Supreme Decree on the operation of the National Registry of Mitigation Measures (RENAMI) [Decreto Supremo N° 010-2024-MINAM. Decreto Supremo sobre el funcionamiento del Registro Nacional de Medidas de Mitigación (RENAMI)]
Family Summary: This Peruvian Supreme Decree establishes operational provisions for the National Registry of Mitigation Measures (RENAMI), a measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) tool administered by the Ministry of Environment through its Directorate General of Climate Change and Desertification. The registry comprises three components: mitigation measures forming Peru's Nationally Determined Contribution (declarative nature), carbon market mitigation measures under cooperative approaches and their emission reduction units (constitutive nature), and voluntary carbon market mitigation measures (declarative nature). The instrument delineates institutional responsibilities, with the Ministry managing registrations, recognising certification standards and methodologies, authorising international transfers of emission reduction units as Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs), and maintaining the national GHG emissions balance. Sectoral authorities must report monitoring data for NDC measures under their responsibility and provide technical opinions on carbon market projects. The decree establishes that carbon market measures under cooperative approaches, implemented through Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement, generate emission reduction units eligible for international transfer to meet other countries' NDCs or international mitigation purposes such as CORSIA, whilst voluntary carbon market measures may contribute to Peru's NDC implementation within corresponding emission sectors.
Document Title: Supreme Decree No. 010-2024-MINAM. Supreme Decree approving the provisions for the operation of the National Registry of Mitigation Measures (RENAMI) [Decreto Supremo No. 010-2024-MINAM. Decreto Supremo que aprueba las disposiciones para el funcionamiento del Registro Nacional de Medidas de Mitigación (RENAMI)]

Family Name: Ministerial Resolution No. 00389-2024-MINAM. Guidelines for the process, management, and provision of periodic information on the approach to and compliance with REDD+ safeguards (Resolución Ministerial N°00389-2024-MINAM. Lineamiento para el proceso, gestión y provisión de información periódica sobre el abordaje y respeto de las salvaguardas REDD+)
Family Summary: This Peruvian ministerial resolution establishes guidelines for the processing, management and periodic provision of information on the approach to and respect for REDD+ safeguards. The instrument operationalises the Safeguards Information Module (MIS REDD+) as the mechanism through which the Ministry of Environment, via its Directorate General of Climate Change and Desertification, processes and disseminates information on compliance with the seven UNFCCC-recognised REDD+ safeguards (Cancun Decision 1/CP.16). These safeguards encompass complementarity with national forest programmes and international agreements, transparency in forest governance, respect for indigenous peoples' rights and knowledge, full and effective stakeholder participation, compatibility with forest conservation and biodiversity, actions to address reversal risks, and measures to reduce emissions displacement. The guidelines delineate roles for state actors (competent climate change authorities at all government levels) and non-state actors (private entities and indigenous peoples implementing REDD+ actions), establishing procedures for information collection, analysis, management and culturally appropriate dissemination to ensure transparency and continuous improvement in safeguard implementation whilst reducing social and environmental risks and enhancing co-benefits from REDD+ activities.
Document Title: Guidelines for the process, management, and provision of periodic information on the approach to and respect for REDD+ safeguards (Lineamiento para le proceso, gestión y provisión de información periódica sobre el abordaje y respeto de las salvaguardas REDD+)

Family Name: Methodological Guide for the Consideration of Climate Change in the Environmental Impact Assessment System
Family Summary: Issued by Chile's Environmental Assessment Service (SEA) in November 2024, this document is the third edition of the Methodological Guide for the Consideration of Climate Change in the Environmental Impact Assessment System (SEIA). Its publication was made necessary by Supreme Decree No. 30 of 2023, which amended the SEIA Regulations and formally mandated the incorporation of the climate change variable into the environmental assessment procedure. The Guide requires that project proponents integrate climate change considerations throughout all stages of Environmental Impact Statements and Assessments. For example, baseline descriptions must incorporate the adverse effects of climate change and impact prediction must account for the variability of environmental elements as a result of climate change.
Document Title: Methodological Guide

Family Name: Order No. 13808/2024 (appoints the representatives of the VCM technical monitoring committee)
Family Summary: This Order appoints the representatives of the VCM technical monitoring committee provided for in Decree Law No. 4/2024. The representatives are from various government environmental and energy agencies, and experts in climate change and economics.
Document Title: Order No. 13808/2024 (appoints the representatives of the VCM technical monitoring committee)

Family Name: National guidelines for drought risk management
Family Summary: National Guidelines for Drought Risk Management in Finland provide a framework for proactively managing drought risks, which are expected to increase with climate change. The guidelines promote an integrated approach based on early warning and drought indicators, vulnerability and risk assessments, and regional risk management and preparedness plans.
Document Title: National guidelines for drought risk management

Family Name: Georgia Development Strategy - Vision 2030
Family Summary: The cornerstone of the national strategy vision 2030 is the commitment to creating a sustainable, resilient, and modern energy landscape in Georgia, closely aligned with European standards. The plan specifically targets ensuring the overall sustainability and reliability of the energy sector by prioritizing the development of the domestic energy market and actively supporting energy efficiency across all sectors. A key component of this effort is the expansion of clean power generation through the increased deployment of renewable sources of energy. Complementing these energy goals are critical environmental and climate mandates, which include reducing the population's vulnerability to climate change, implementing an integrated management system of water resources, and protecting the Black Sea environment. Furthermore, systemic improvements are targeted through upgrading air quality monitoring and assessment, and fundamentally improving the entire waste management system by promoting the circular economy.
Document Title: Georgia Development Strategy - Vision 2030

Family Name: Executive Order on Green Investment Support Scheme
Family Summary:
The Executive Order applies to a new green investment support scheme. The investment support scheme is administered by the Danish Export and Investment Fund. Support may be granted to investment projects that fall within the scope of the scheme, with a view to accelerating investments in production facilities for certain types of equipment for the transition to a zero-emission economy in Denmark.

Green investment support schemes shall target investments in Denmark in new production facilities or the expansion of existing production facilities within wind technology and electrolysers, such as wind turbines, windmill blades, nacelles, gearboxes, tanks, anodes, cathodes and compressors, etc. The Danish Export and Investment Fund may grant investment aid in the form of direct subsidies to enterprises. Aid in the form of direct grants may not exceed 15 per cent of the eligible costs.
Document Title: Executive Order on Green Investment Support Scheme

Family Name: Singapore Aquaculture Plan
Family Summary: This Masterplan is intended to ensure Singapore's food security through aquaculture. For instance, Singapore is exploring potential sites in the Southern Waters for further studies on integrating closed containment aquaculture systems (CCAS) with open net cage systems for a new hybrid model for farming. CCAS ensures that fishes are protected from external environmental risks such as harmful algal blooms—an increasing concern due to climate change. There are also selective breeding porgrammes for seabass to improve important traits such as robustness in response to changing water conditions due to climate change. The Masterplan covers the following areas to ensure that Singapore adopts innovative and sustainable methods, while keeping to a mix of production systems that are suited to Singapore’s unique constraints: space and infrastructure planning; enabling regulations; research, innovation and enterprise; ecosystem development and demand offtake and promotion of local produce.
Document Title: Singapore Aquaculture Plan

Family Name: Geological Survey of Sweden - action plan for climate adaptation 2025-2027
Family Summary:
This action plan for climate adaptation applies to 2025–2027, but looks forward to 2030. The action plan is based on the Swedish Geotechnical Institute's (SGI's) mission to reduce the risks of landslides, rock falls and coastal erosion and to contribute to sustainable development in a changing climate. The action goals to achieve this visionary authority goal, which encompasses SGI's entire area of ​​operation, are:

• SGI will develop and disseminate knowledge about climate-driven geotechnical risks within four of the national risk areas,

• SGI will develop and disseminated methods for nature-based solutions to reduce coastal erosion and stabilise slopes,

• SGI will implement advice and recommendations on climate adaptation to support sustainable municipal planning, and

• Physical climate adaptation measures for landslides, avalanches and coastal erosion will be implemented and followed up on.

A changing climate can contribute to an increased spread of PFAS and other pollutants that are already present in the landscape and those that will be added in the future. We see that we have an important role in guiding municipalities in how they can assess and manage these risks. Since SGI is primarily a knowledge-producing authority, continued dialogue and cooperation within the civil engineering sector is essential to achieving our authority goal.
Document Title: Geological Survey of Sweden - action plan for climate adaptation 2025-2027

Family Name: National Water Policy 2024
Family Summary:
The Policy discusses water security in the context of climate change. It states that groundwater resources offer essential livelihood mechanisms and its strategic importance will probably intensify under climate change and human development (population growth, urbanisation) in the future. Groundwater constitutes the most important buffer and reserve of water during surplus periods as well as a source of water for streams and/or direct withdrawals in times of shortage, and thus is expected to play an essential role in climate change adaptation.

The Policy also states that Zambia faces the issues of inadequate climate resilient water harvesting infrastructure; inadequate framework for rainwater harvesting; and inadequate groundwater exploration and aquifer mapping.

To harness water resources and ensure water security for enhanced access and utilisation, the Policy lists the measure of establishing mechanisms that ensure environmental considerations are included in the design for water resources infrastructure and mitigate the effects of climate change.
Document Title: National Water Policy 2024 Implementation Plan

Family Name: Climate Action Roadmap For Buildings and Construction
Family Summary:
This Roadmap transforms the building and construction sector to be resilient and inclusive while emitting less carbon. It covers spatial and urban development; existing buildings; new buildings; and the construction supply chain.

The objectives are as follows:

Embodied and operational carbon

  • Increase low-carbon electricity generation and promote clean rural households lighting leading to acombined emission reduction
  • Promote energy efficiency in homes, industry and commerce leading to emission reduction

Adaptation

  • Achieve city-wide resilient infrastructure planning for climate change adaptation
  • Build well-planned and safe communities, while protecting the natural environment

Well-being and inclusion

  • Identify, develop and promote the use of sustainable local materials in building and construction
  • Create an equitable, healthy and prosperous society
Document Title: Climate Action Roadmap For Buildings and Construction

Family Name: Fiji National Carbon Market Strategy Roadmap
Family Summary:
This Strategy Roadmap provides an important overview of carbon market options, opportunities, risks, and priority actions which will help guide further policy development in Fiji and provides a basis for its interactions with new market-based opportunities. Carbon markets are meant to be an additional means to increase investment in sustainable development.

It is designed for use by policymakers, project developers, investors, land and resource owners, credit buyers, local communities, and other relevant stakeholders to shape their potential interaction with carbon market mechanisms.

It contains five chapters:

  • Chapter 1: A market vision, priorities and principles co-designed with multi- stakeholders.
  • Chapter 2: Fiji’s NDC targets, existing financing options, potential roles for high-integrity carbon markets, and the current state of play of carbon projects.
  • Chapter 3: Opportunities and risks, both general and specific to Fiji’s local contexts.
  • Chapter 4: Strategic considerations and options for engagement with carbon markets.
  • Chapter 5: Key pillar action items to enhance market readiness in Fiji, encompassing legal, governance, community benefits and landowner rights, partnerships, and finance.
Document Title: Fiji National Carbon Market Strategy Roadmap

Family Name: National Waste Plan
Family Summary:
This Plan seeks to tackle illegal waste management, which poses a significant risk of hazardous substances spreading and negatively affecting soil, water and air quality, as well as causing negative impacts on the climate, biodiversity and ecosystem services, some important groundwater. It also seeks to reduce the effects of high consumption in Sweden.

The Plan explores areas such as the environmental and climate impact of a textile product consumed in Sweden, promoting the use of existing textile material as a raw material for remanufacturing new products that has a significantly lower environmental and climate impact compared to fiber-to-fiber recycling.
Document Title: National Waste Plan

Family Name: National Hydrogen Strategy
Family Summary: The National Hydrogen Strategy aims to develop hydrogen as a key energy carrier for Italy’s decarbonisation pathway, supporting the targets of the NECP and climate neutrality by 2050. Its main objectives are to expand the production of renewable and low-carbon hydrogen, stimulate demand in hard-to-electrify sectors such as industry and heavy transport, and develop dedicated infrastructure for hydrogen transport, storage and distribution. The strategy also seeks to build a national hydrogen value chain and industrial ecosystem, supported by investments and regulatory measures, including funding from Italy's RRF Plan.
Document Title: National Hydrogen Strategy (Strategia Nazionale Idrogeno)

Family Name: System Development Strategy 2024
Family Summary: The System Development Strategy 2024 (Systementwicklungsstrategie, SES 2024) provides Germany's first integrated, cross-sectoral framework for planning the transition to a climate-neutral energy system by 2045. Published by the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK), the strategy coordinates the long-term development of the electricity, hydrogen, natural gas, and heat sectors to ensure a coherent and cost-efficient transformation. It identifies the large-scale expansion of renewable energy, widespread electrification of transport, buildings, and industry, the establishment of a nationwide hydrogen infrastructure, and increased system flexibility through energy storage, demand-side management, and sector coupling as the key pillars of the future energy system. The SES also emphasizes integrated infrastructure planning, European energy market integration, and the coordinated development of transmission, distribution, and hydrogen networks. As an adaptive planning framework, the strategy serves as the basis for future network development plans and will be periodically updated to reflect technological, economic, and policy developments.
Document Title: System Development Strategy 2024

Family Name: Hydrogen Action Plan
Family Summary:
This plan outlines the steps the Government is taking to lower regulatory barriers and support private investment in hydrogen. The Plan builds on the analysis and consultation undertaken on the Interim Hydrogen Roadmap published in 2023.

The Hydrogen Action Plan has four key priority areas:

1. Create an enabling regulatory environment

2. Reduce barriers for consenting hydrogen projects

3. Promote a cost-effective and market-led transition to a low-emissions economy

4. Support access to international investment and markets
Document Title: Hydrogen Action Plan

Collection Name: The Mother Earth Law and Integral Development to Live Well, Framework Law No 300
Collection Summary:
The Mother Earth Law is a piece of legislation that epitomises Bolivia's dedication to sustainable development, respecting the balance between human life and the natural environment, and prioritising the rights and knowledge of the country's majority indigenous population. The expressed objective of the law is to 'establish the vision and fundamentals of integral development in harmony and balance with Mother Earth to Live Well, guaranteeing the continued capacity of Mother Earth to regenerate natural systems, recuperating and strengthening local and ancestral practices, within the framework of rights, obligations and responsibilities'.
 
 In relation to climate change the law has many provisions that outline the state's vision, citizens' rights, and responsibilities. It embraces the concept of 'climate justice', defined by the ability of all Bolivian citizens to 'Live Well', especially those who are most vulnerable to climate change. It reinforces the point that some states have more of a global responsibility to respond to climate change.
 
 To encourage sustainable development of natural resources, it states that climate change trajectories should be accounted for when planning and zoning responsible land use.
 
 The law focuses on reducing the risks posed by climate change through six lines of actions:
The permanent incorporation of prevention of and managed response to natural disasters into the System of Integral Planning
Risk management for the agricultural sector to prevent diminished crop yields and food insecurity
The adoption of risk management of disasters as well as adaption to climate change across state development projects; development of informational networks to issue early warnings in times of natural crisis as well as to assist the agricultural industry and indigenous communities plan according to climate conditions
Strengthening territorial management processes of sub-national governments through the incorporation of risk management and adaption to climate change perspectives
Articulation between public and private scientific research sectors to share knowledge and co-ordinate research regarding vulnerabilities related to climate change
 
 The Law defines 'Living Well' in relation to climate change and lays out the state's legal obligations. The state will develop policies, strategies and legal techniques to mitigate the effects of climate change and adapt to them through strengthening institutional capacities for the monitoring of climate with the purpose of long-term planning. The state will also encourage the recuperation of traditional indigenous practices that were historically sustainable and allowed for the natural regeneration of resources.
 
 The law also establishes the Plurinational Authority of Mother Earth, within the Ministry of Environment and Water, as the state entity responsible for much of the development, overseeing and co-ordination of projects, programmes and research as it relates to climate change and the objectives of the Plurinational Plan for Climate Change. It also co-ordinates scientific monitoring of GHG emissions. The entity will operate within the framework of 'climate justice,' following the principles of Bolivia's climate change politics.
 
 The Authority will operate through three mechanisms: (1) Joint Mechanism of Mitigation and Adaptation for the Integral and Sustainable Management of Mother Earth's Forests; (2) Mitigation Mechanism to 'Living Well'; and (3) Adaptation Mechanism to 'Living Well'.
 
 The Authority is also responsible for the management of the Plurinational Fund of Mother Earth. The Fund will be financed with multilateral and bilateral aid, public money from the national government allocated to mitigation or adaptation, funds from private donors, national or international loans, and funds at the disposal of the executive branch.
Family Name: Supreme Decree 5264, establishing guidelines for the management and access to climate finance
Family Summary:
The Supreme Decree 5264 establishes guidelines for managing and accessing climate financing within Bolivia, aligning with the country's commitments to climate action as outlined in the Paris Agreement and its NDC. It is deeply rooted in the principles established by Law No. 300, the Mother Earth and Integral Development Framework for Living Well, emphasising the need to protect the Rights of Mother Earth and indigenous peoples, aligning with Bolivia's commitment to addressing climate change through mitigation, adaptation, and loss and damage management.

It defines climate financing as resources aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions and supporting adaptation efforts. The decree mandates that all climate financing efforts, including mitigation and adaptation projects, be centrally registered and overseen by the state to ensure compliance with national and international obligations.

The decree sets forth principles for climate financing, including sovereignty, transparency, equitable responsibility, and precautionary principle. It also creates the National Registry of Programs and Projects (RENAPP) to systematically track and report on climate initiatives, avoiding duplication and ensuring accountability. The decree assigns specific roles to various ministries for project evaluation, registration, and negotiation of climate financing mechanisms, emphasising the importance of coordinated efforts across sectors to effectively manage and access climate funds
Document Title: Supreme Decree 5264, establishing guidelines for the management and access to climate finance
