Family Name: Supreme Decree 5264, establishing the climate finance management and access guidelines for implementing Bolivia's Nationally Determined Contributions
Family Summary: The Bolivia Supreme Decree 5264 establishes a comprehensive framework for climate finance management and access, supporting the implementation of Bolivia's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). Building upon Law 300 (Framework Law of Mother Earth and Integral Development for Living Well), this Supreme Decree emphasises the Bolivian vision for a development in harmony with Mother Earth for the living-well (Vivir-Bien), protecting both Mother Earth's rights and the rights of indigenous-peasant communities, particularly concerning climate crisis context.The Supreme Decree creates an institutional structure that distributes responsibilities across different ministries and establishes the National Registry of Programs and Projects (RENAPP) for tracking climate initiatives and emission reduction units. The decree assigns specific roles to key ministries: (1) evaluation and prioritisation of projects by the Ministries of Hydrocarbons and Energy, Environment and Water, and Rural Development; (2) management of RENAPP by the Ministry of Environment and Water; (3) oversight of debt-for-nature swaps and carbon credits by the Ministry of Economy and Public Finance; (4) access to climate finance mechanisms by the Ministry of Development Planning.Equally, this Supreme Decree establishes four fundamental guiding principles for climate finance: (1) Sovereignty, ensuring state control over natural resources and emission reduction units; (2) Transparency, requiring mandatory disclosure of climate finance information; (3) Common but Differentiated Responsibilities, aligning with UNFCCC and Paris Agreement principles; (4) Precautionary Principle, emphasising preventive measures for environmental protection.Moreover, the scope of the Supreme Decree encompasses public entities, state-owned enterprises, and private actors (both domestic and foreign), applying to both national and subnational climate change mitigation and adaptation projects.
Document Title: Supreme Decree 5264, establishing the climate finance management and access guidelines for implementing Bolivia's Nationally Determined Contributions

Family Name: Alignment of Mexico's National Biodiversity Strategy and 2030 Action Plan with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework Targets (Alineación de la Estrategia Nacional sobre Biodiversidad de México y Plan de Acción 2030 con las Metas del Marco Mundial de Biodiversidad de Kunming-Montreal)
Family Summary: Mexico began aligning its National Biodiversity Strategy (ENBioMex) with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework through a national process led by CONABIO. As a result, the Alignment of Mexico's National Biodiversity Strategy (ENBioMex) and 2030 Action Plan with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) Targets recognises climate change as a critical driver of biodiversity loss, embedding it explicitly in Target 8, which calls for minimising climate and ocean acidification impacts on biodiversity through mitigation, adaptation, and disaster risk reduction. Other targets promote ecosystem-based approaches and nature-based solutions that bolster biodiversity’s role in climate resilience, reinforcing the interdependence of global climate and biodiversity goals.
Document Title: Alignment of Mexico's National Biodiversity Strategy and 2030 Action Plan with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework Targets (Alineación de la Estrategia Nacional sobre Biodiversidad de México y Plan de Acción 2030 con las Metas del Marco Mundial de Biodiversidad de Kunming-Montreal)

Family Name: Brazilian Technical Accounting Standards for Disclosure of Sustainability Information (NBC TDS 01 and 02)
Family Summary:
These rules, published by the Federal Accounting Council, approve NBC TDS 01 and NBC TDS 02, which guide the elaboration of the Sustainability Information Report for all companies and entities that prepare financial reports.

NBC TDS 01 on General Requirements for the Disclosure of Financial Information Related to Sustainability sets out general requirements for the disclosure of financial information related to sustainability.

NBC TDS 02 on Climate-related disclosures requires the entity to disclose information about the risks and opportunities related to climate change for which there is a reasonable expectation that they could affect the entity's cash flows, access to financing or cost of capital in the short, medium or long term. This standard applies to: (a) climate change-related risks to which the entity is exposed, which are: (i) climate-related physical risks; and (ii) climate-related transition risks; and (b) climate-related opportunities available to the entity.
Document Title: Brazilian Accounting Standard, NBC TDS 2

Family Name: Council of Ministers Resolution n.º 147/2024 - Establishes the National Roadmap for the Decarbonization of Aviation
Family Summary: Embedded in environmental sustainability and the commitment to fight climate change, this resolution aims to decarbonize the air transport sector. This resolution establishes the National Roadmap for the Decarbonization of Aviation (RONDA) and the Alliance for Sustainability in Aviation (ASA).The ASA coalition includes airlines, government bodies, and environmental NGOs, all working towards the common goal of reducing aviation greenhouse gas emissions. Recognizing the growth in air traffic over the coming decades, the ASA seeks to lead the transition to greener practices through collaboration and knowledge sharing, with the goal of developing technological solutions to reduce emissions and improve energy efficiency.
Document Title: Council of Ministers Resolution n.º 147/2024

Family Name: Supreme Decree No. 203-2024-EF, approving the update of the National Competitiveness and Productivity Plan 2019-2030 (Decreto Supremo No. 203-2024-EF, que aprueba la actualización del Plan Nacional de Competitividad y productividad 2019-2030
Family Summary: The Supreme Decree No. 203-2024-EF updates Peru’s National Competitiveness and Productivity Plan (PNCP 2024–2030), embedding climate finance and monitoring mechanisms into its ninth strategic objective, “Promote environmental sustainability in economic activities.” This includes Policy Measure 9.1 (“Climate Finance and Monitoring”), which addresses institutional barriers to accessing international climate funds (e.g., the Green Climate Fund) and integrates climate considerations into financial decision-making. The plan mandates the implementation of a Sistema de Monitoreo to track adaptation/mitigation progress, emissions reductions, and funding flows. This system comprises three components: (i) measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) of greenhouse gas emissions/removals; (ii) monitoring and evaluation (ME) of adaptation measures; and (iii) tracking of climate finance allocation. The policy aligns Peru’s climate action with international obligations under the Paris Agreement and SDG 13, prioritising capacity-building for public and private actors to access climate financing. It recognises the fiscal urgency of adaptation, citing a projected PEN 66 billion cost for 51 adaptation measures by 2030 (per MINAM’s 2021 National Adaptation Plan).
Document Title: Supreme Decree No. 203-2024-EF updates Peru’s National Competitiveness and Productivity Plan (PNCP 2024–2030)

Family Name: National Strategy for Biological Diversity to 2050 (Estrategia Nacional de Diversidad Biológica al 2050)
Family Summary: Peru’s National Strategy for Biological Diversity to 2050 establishes a long-term framework to address biodiversity loss through integrated, participatory governance aligned with climate resilience and sustainable development. Central to the strategy are five strategic objectives targeting land-use change, climate impacts, pollution, invasive species, and institutional weaknesses. These objectives operationalise principles such as the precautionary principle (Rio Declaration, Principle 15), intercultural equity, and human rights-based approaches, ensuring alignment with international obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and the Paris Agreement. The strategy mandates ecosystem-based adaptation, including restoring 10% of degraded ecosystems and species affected by climate change, while integrating traditional ecological knowledge to strengthen adaptive capacity. The strategy’s implementation relies on institutional reforms, such as strengthening multi-level governance and integrating biodiversity metrics (e.g., the Lista Roja de Ecosistemas) into national reporting frameworks, including the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. It addresses climate-biodiversity linkages by prioritising mitigation of climate-driven threats (e.g., deforestation, water pollution) and promoting nature-based solutions, such as community-led water harvesting projects. The "Enfoque Territorial" (territorial approach) ensures localised, context-specific actions, while the Enfoque "Una Salud" (One Health) links ecosystem health to human and animal well-being.
Document Title: National Biological Diversity Strategy to 2050 (Estrategia Nacional de Diversidad Biológica al 2050)

Family Name: Agricultural Sector Mitigation Plan
Family Summary: This plan outlines the mitigation measures needed for Chile’s agriculture, livestock, and forestry sector to meet its NDC and other sectoral targets, particularly supporting the AFOLU sector's role as a net carbon sink contributing to Chile's 2050 climate neutrality goal.
Document Title: Agricultural Sector Mitigation Plan (Plan Sectorial de Mitigación al Cambio Climático - Sector Agricultura)

Family Name: State Programme on the Use of Alternative and Renewable Energy Sources
Family Summary: The State Programme on the Use of Alternative and Renewable Energy Sources is a national programme that promotes power generation from renewable and environmentally sound sources. This programme promotes wind power as the more preferable energy source to solar, hydro, geothermal and biomass energy, but explores the production of these other forms of energy as well.
Document Title: State Programme on the Use of Alternative and Renewable Energy Sources

Family Name: Roadmap for Renewable Energy to 2035
Family Summary: Turkey unveiled its Renewable Energy Roadmap for 2035 on October 21, 2024, outlining ambitious plans to quadruple its wind and solar capacity to 120 GW by 2035. The roadmap includes measures such as annual renewable energy auctions of 2 GW, investments of $108 billion for capacity expansion and grid upgrades, and targets to add at least 7.5-8 GW of new renewable capacity each year.
Document Title: Roadmap for Renewable Energy to 2035

Family Name: Presidential Decree No. 15-2024 -  Regulation Of Law No. 1210, General Tourism Law
Family Summary: This decree aims to establish the regulatory provisions for the application of Law No. 1210, the General Tourism Law. It structures the organisation of the INTUR, the national organism, which, among other things, is the one responsible to plan the country’s tourism development in a coordinated and organized manner, working with local governments, institutions, and sector stakeholders to promote sustainable, responsible, and accessible tourism.

Family Name: Hungary Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030. The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness.

The main objectives of the plan are: 1) to strengthen energy sovereignty and energy security, 2) to maintain the results of reduced overhead costs, 3) to decarbonise energy production with a combination of nuclear energy and renewable energy. The plan states that it is in the interest of Hungary to reduce its demand for energy imports and to ensure its connection to the regional electricity grids and natural gas networks. The reduction of the use of fossil fuels may be achieved through the use of heating/cooling solutions based on renewable resources and the reduction of energy consumption in public institutions, industry and transport. For energy efficiency, the plan establishes green solutions in electromobility, and household-scale energy production for private purposes via the spread of smart meters. Quantified targets for 2030 include a 50% reduction in gross GHG emissions, relative to 1990 levels, and a 30% renewable share of gross final energy consumption.
Document Title: Hungary - final updated NECP 2021 Annex 3 - 2030

The plan states that it is in the interest of Hungary to reduce its demand for energy imports and to ensure its connection to the regional electricity grids and natural gas networks. The reduction of the use of fossil fuels may be achieved through the use of heating/cooling solutions based on renewable resources and the reduction of energy consumption in public institutions, industry and transport. For energy efficiency, the plan establishes green solutions in electromobility, and household-scale energy production for private purposes via the spread of smart meters. Quantified targets for 2030 include a 50% reduction in gross GHG emissions, relative to 1990 levels, and a 30% renewable share of gross final energy consumption.

Family Name: Rwanda's Climate and Nature Finance Strategy (CNFS) 2024-2030
Family Summary: The strategy aims to support Rwanda's Vision 2050, harnessing climate and nature finance for sustainable development and environmental protection in the medium-term. It identifies a range of funding sources, promotes innovative financing mechanisms and partnerships with a range of national and international stakeholders. This strategy functions as a strategic programme for the government's new Climate Finance Department, closely linked to the Rwanda Green Fund and Ministry of Environment.
Document Title: Rwanda's Climate and Nature Finance Strategy (CNFS) 2024-2030

Family Name: Green Skills 2030
Family Summary:
The First National Further Education and Training (FET) Strategy for the Green Transition was launched on 15 October 2024, in collaboration with SOLAS. It builds on the commitment of the current FET strategy to ensure the development of essential climate change and environmental knowledge. This strategy shapes the response and contribution of the sector towards meeting Ireland’s climate action targets by identifying critical skills gaps, and presenting strategic and sector-specific recommendations to support the growing demand for green skills. Its implementation will be overseen by the Green Skills 2030 Implementation Group.

Green Skills 2030 sets out:

  • key skills gaps across critical sectors that are affecting Ireland’s ability to transition to a climate-neutral society
  • strategic and sector-specific recommendations
  • opportunities to respond to skills gaps and build an inclusive workforce as part of the green transition
  • ways in which FET can equip learners with the necessary skills to support the transition to a green economy and society
Document Title: Green Skills 2030

Family Name: National Strategy for the Development of Green Hydrogen and its Derivatives in Tunisia, 2024
Family Summary: The National Strategy for the Development of Green Hydrogen and its Derivatives in Tunisia (2024) aims to promote a green hydrogen industry, beginning with the domestic development of green ammonia for the fertiliser sector. The strategy aims to expand to hydrogen exports and green synthetic fuels in the longer term, exporting 6.3 megatonnes of hydrogen to the EU by 2050.
Document Title: National Strategy for the Development of Green Hydrogen and its Derivatives in Tunisia, 2024

Family Name: National Climate Security Strategy 2024-2028
Family Summary: National Climate Security Strategy 2024-2028 aims to address the significant climate adaptation needs of Burkina Faso, up to 2028 and in the longer term. The strategy operates along four strategic axes: improving climate security governance; sustainable and climate-just management of natural resources; improving human protection against disaster risks and crises; improving Burkina Faso's access to climate finance. It primarily outlines gaps in the existing strategic framework, and broader key areas for increased focus, but promotes some specific interventions such as reforestation and the creation of improved natural disaster early warning systems.
Document Title: National Climate Security Strategy 2024-2028

Family Name: Decree No. 2024-915 of 10 October 2024 on the powers of the Minister of Ecological Transition, Energy, Climate and Risk Prevention
Family Summary:
The Minister of Ecological Transition, Energy, Climate and Risk Prevention prepares and implements the Government's policy in the fields of sustainable development, environment, climate, energy, energy efficiency, the fight against air pollution, the protection of nature and biodiversity, water and the prevention of natural and technological risks and industrial safety as well as the promotion of sustainable management of scarce resources.In the conse of international relations on climate, energy, terrestrial and marine biodiversity, the environment, risk prevention and the circular economy, they represent the Prime Minister, in charge of ecological and energy planning, in European and international negotiations, in consultation with the Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs, and ensure the implementation of the agreements concluded.

In the fight against climate change, in conjunction with interested ministers, they prepare and implement policy on reducing greenhouse gas emissions, energy efficiency and climate change adaptation. As such:

  1. They define and implement, jointly with the Minister of Housing and Urban Renewal, the policy on renovation and energy performance of buildings;
  2. They define and implement, jointly with the Minister of Partnership with the Territories and Decentralization, the policy of decarbonization and electrification of road transport, as well as the tools for financing the ecological transition in the territories;
  3. They define and implement the decarbonisation policy, together with the Minister of Economy, Finance and Industry, with regard to the decarbonisation of industry.
  4. For energy, they define and implement, energy policy, particularly in terms of tariffs, jointly with the Minister of Economy, Finance and Industry, and in terms of energy saving certificates, in order, in particular, to ensure security of supply and access to energy, to combat climate change and to promote the energy transition.
  5. In association with the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industry, they define industrial policy, research and innovation actions concerning the energy sector.
  6. They lead the policy on renewable marine energies, jointly with the Minister of Partnership with Territories and Decentralization.
  7. For raw materials and mines, they define and implement, jointly with the Minister of Economy, Finance and Industry, the policy of raw materials and mines with regard to energy materials and they are associated with the Minister of Partnership with the Territories and Decentralisation with the policy on mines at sea.
Document Title: Decree No. 2024-915 of 10 October 2024 on the powers of the Minister of Ecological Transition, Energy, Climate and Risk Prevention

Family Name: Gender Action Plan 2024-2030
Family Summary: The NDC GAP 2024-2030 sets out strategic actions as guidelines for gender-responsive implementation of the current NDC across all mitigation and adaptation policies and measures, primarily in the agriculture, transport, energy, and waste sectors, and industrial processes and product use. It provides both analytical frameworks and proposed entry points for gender mainstreaming. As a product of interagency collaboration and partnership, it highlights opportunities to mainstream the gender and climate nexus in programs and investments to address vulnerabilities and empower marginalised communities.
Document Title: Gender Action Plan 2024-2030

Family Summary:
One of the national goals is to manage protected and conserved areas (PCAs) to enhance their climate change mitigation and adaptation potential. This Framework also covers marine areas.

Climate-related actions include enahncing ecological resilience (the ability to resist or recover) of marine ecosystems to impacts of climate change and providing corridors for species and habitats that are shifting due to climate change.
Document Title: Maldives National Framework for Management of Protected & Conserved Areas 2024-2029

Family Name: Bill C-49 (Offshore Petroleum)
Family Summary:
Bill C-49 is An Act to amend the Canada–Newfoundland and Labrador Atlantic Accord Implementation Act and the Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Petroleum Resources Accord Implementation Act and to make consequential amendments to other Acts. Amongst other things, it:

  • implements the agreement between the Government of Canada and the Government of Newfoundland and Labrador on offshore petroleum resource management and revenue sharing, to provide for the joint management of offshore renewable energy by those Governments and to make related and consequential amendments;
  • establishes the regulating bodies for offshore renewable energy projects;
  • establishes a land tenure regime for the issuance of submerged land licences to carry out offshore renewable energy projects, as well as the revenues regime associated with those licences and projects;
  • expands the application of the safety and environmental protection regime and its enforcement powers to include offshore renewable energy projects;
  • establish the regulatory and liability regime for abandoned facilities relating to petroleum-related works or activities or offshore renewable energy projects; and
  • allow new methods to demonstrate the existence of significant hydrocarbon accumulations in a geological feature and limit the duration of future significant discovery licences to 25 years.
Document Title: Bill C-49

Family Name: National Water and Energy Demand Management Programme
Family Summary:
The National Water and Energy Demand Management Programme targets 40 per cent efficiency of the three most energy-consuming sectors in the UAE: transport, industry and construction.

The programme includes three main pillars: 

  • Energy;
  • Water; and 
  • Consumption rationalisation. 


Several initiatives will be launched to reduce energy consumption and realise the following targets by 2050:

  • Reduce energy demand by 40 per cent;
  • Increase the renewable energy's contribution to the energy mix to 50 per cent;
  • Expand water re-use by 95 per cent.
Document Title: National Water and Energy Demand Management Programme

Family Name: Offshore Wind Roadmap
Family Summary:
This roadmap provides strategic analysis of the offshore wind development potential in Türkiye, considering the opportunities and challenges under different, hypothetical, growth scenarios. It is intended to provide evidence to support the Government of Türkiye in establishing policy, regulations, processes, and infrastructure to enable successful growth of this new industry.

With energy demand expected to continue increasing, Türkiye needs to expand local energy generation to reduce its reliance on imports and the associated foreign exchange burden on its economy. Türkiye has areas with good natural conditions for offshore wind. This offers a new source of domestic renewable energy generation that could contribute to Türkiye’s transition to net-zero carbon by 2053.

The Roadmap recommends 21 actions that mainly focus on actions to be taken in the short term, but some can span over the entire timeframe up to 2050, across the areas of: vision and volume targets; regulatory and policy framework; financial and economic; health and safety; grid and port infrastructure; and supply chain.
Document Title: Offshore Wind Roadmap

Family Name: Rwanda Green Taxonomy
Family Summary:
Rwanda’s Green Taxonomy is a framework that aims to define sustainability criteria, foster shared understanding and truston what constitutes a green investment, as well as prevent greenwashing.

The development of Rwanda Green Taxonomy is seen as a crucial step in laying a solid foundation for the country's green transformation, developing new industries, and becoming the financial hub of East Africa. It is the second taxonomy in Africa (after South Africa) and the first in Africa to include the agricultural sector. It is also an innovative framework for the inclusion of activities that contribute to climate change adaptation and resilience.

The need for the taxonomy to meet Rwanda's development objectives was first identified in the Rwanda Sustainable Finance Roadmap published in October 2022 for Rwanda’s financial centre (the Kigali International Finance Centre) with support from UNDP. The development of Rwanda Green Taxonomy is supported by the German development agency Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and co-financed by the European Union. A consortium of the Climate Bonds Initiative (CBI) and Ambire Global was commissioned to provide technical assistance for the project, building on their extensive experience in developing national and international taxonomies.
Document Title: Rwanda Green Taxonomy: Annex III - Various Taxonomy Objectives

Family Name: Nature, People and Climate Investment Plan
Family Summary: This Plan is anchored on three (3) programmes, namely: (1) Building Resilience of Food, Livelihoods and Ecosystem Services; (2) Promotion of Climate-Smart Agriculture and Climate Resilience; and (3) Strengthening Community Livelihoods and Resilience through Sustainable Management of Natural Resources. They will be implemented in selected districts of Central, Copperbelt and North-western provinces that are highly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change, such as droughts and floods and whose natural resources, including forests, water catchments and land, have been degraded due to unsustainable practices.
Document Title: Nature, People and Climate Investment Plan

Family Name: Climate Change and Gender Action Plan (Phase II)
Family Summary:
The Ministry for Coordination of Environmental Affairs (MICOA) invited the Global Gender Office of the International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN GGO) on behalf of the Global Gender and Climate Alliance (GGCA) to facilitate a process of revisiting and enhancing the action plan portion of the 2010 Gender, Environment and Climate Change Strategy and Action Plan. The 2010 Plan was a trailblazer as Mozambique was the first country in the world to create such a plan.

MICOA selected six sectors to focus on for this Plan: water, agriculture, health, mitigation (including energy and forests), DRR, and coasts and fisheries.
Document Title: Climate Change and Gender Action Plan (Phase II)

Family Name: Pathways to Sustainable Tourism Growth - National Tourism Strategy 2024-2031
Family Summary: This Strategy sets the direction for the development of Danish tourism towards 2030 with vision, benchmarks and concrete initiatives. The Vision is that tourism must strengthen the Danish economy and Danish society through environmentally, economically and socially sustainable growth that creates value for citizens, tourists and local communities. A cornerstone is green and sustainable solutions with a smaller environmental and climate footprint: All public tourism organizations must be sustainability certified; 70 percent of all accommodations and amusement parks in Denmark must be sustainability certified; and Denmark should be number 1 among the countries in Northern Europe in terms of tourists' assessment of the country as an environmentally friendly travel destination.
Document Title: National Tourism Strategy 2024-2031

Family Name: Guidance for documentation of greenhouse gas emission reduction effects
Family Summary: The guide is intended as a guide for ministries with responsibility for climate initiatives and new technologies that will potentially need to be included in Denmark's national emissions inventory. The guidance is an inter-ministerial working tool prepared by the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities, the Ministry of the Environment, the Ministry of Food, Agriculture and Fisheries and the Ministry of Finance in collaboration with Danish Centre for Environment and Energy, which collects the emission inventory. Requirements and instructions contained in the guidelines will form the basis for the emissions inventory, enabling the assessment of the final fulfilment of the Danish climate targets.
Document Title: Guidance for documentation of greenhouse gas emission reduction effects

Family Name: Malaysia HCFC Phase-out Management Plan (HPMP)
Family Summary:
This plan implements the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer. Malaysia successfully eliminated the use of Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) by 2010. Building on this milestone, Malaysia has implemented the hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFC) Phase Out Management Plan (HPMP) Stage I (2011-2016) and Stage II (2017-2024).

By 2030, Malaysia aims to achieve a full phase-out of HCFCs, accepting a small allowance for the servicing ‘tail’ to 2040. HPMP Stage III will focus to address two subsector plans, the Refrigeration Air Conditioning (RAC) Servicing Sector Plan (HCFC-22) and the Chillers Servicing Sector Plan (HCFC-123). HPMP stage III will further strengthen the regulatory and institutional systems by establishing new bans on the use of HCFCs, and expand customs officers, port authorities and national control and compliance officers’ capacities to control and manage HCFC in trade, use and continue raising awareness to sustain the HCFC phase-out. Implementing HPMP Stage III will reduce Malaysia’s greenhouse gas emissions by up to 8.42 million tonnes CO2-eq.
Document Title: Malaysia HCFC Phase-out Management Plan (HPMP) Stage I (2012)

Document Title: PLANAVEG National Native Vegetation Recovery Plan

Family Name: Revised Biofuels Development and Utilization Strategy of Ethiopia
Family Summary: The strategy paper updates Ethiopia’s biofuels policy framework to expand sustainable biofuel production and use, reduce fossil fuel imports, and support domestic energy production through feedstock development, biodiesel and bioethanol deployment (including transport, aviation SAF and clean cooking fuels), and associated infrastructure and institutional measures.
Document Title: Revised Biofuels Development and Utilization Strategy of Ethiopia

Family Name: National Cooking Transition Strategy
Family Summary: This strategy outlines a roadmap for achieving Kenya’s goal of universal access to clean cooking by 2028. The specific fuel and stove type targets for households consist of 50% LPG stoves, 30% bioethanol, 10% electricity, 3% biogas technology, and 7% of low emission/clean burning sustainable biomass (e.g. briquettes, pellets).
Document Title: Kenya National Cooking Transition Strategy 2024-2028

Family Name: PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement, PM E-DRIVE
Family Summary: In September 2024, the Ministry of Heavy Industry launched the PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Engancement (PM E-DRIVE). The implementation period was set for October 2024 - March 2026, officially launching in 2025. The Electric Mobility Promotion Scheme (EMPS-2024) scheme is being subsumed under the PM E-DRIVE scheme. Eligible categories include electric 2-wheelers, 3-wheelers, ambulances, trucks, buses, and charging infrastructure. The funding, based on a budget of ₹ 10,900 crore, has been extended by two years now set to end in March 2028.
Document Title: PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-DRIVE) Scheme.

Family Name: Regulations of the Federal Budget and Fiscal Responsibility Law
Family Summary: The Federal Budget and Fiscal Responsibility Law Regulation establishes the framework for the planning, allocation, execution, oversight, and evaluation of federal public expenditures in Mexico. It mandates that all federal agencies adhere to mandatory budgetary control systems designed to ensure efficient and transparent management of public resources. These systems are aligned with the principles outlined in the parent law, emphasizing accountability, fiscal responsibility, and strategic resource allocation.
Document Title: Regulations of the Federal Budget and Fiscal Responsibility Law (Reglamento de la Ley Federal de Presupuesto y Responsabilidad Hacendaria)

Family Name: Norwegian Action Plan for Biodiversity (Meld. St. 35 2023-2024)
Family Summary:
This Action Plan shows how the government's policy will contribute to the sustainable use and conservation of natural diversity. The measures are meant to ensure that society's use of nature occurs in a way that makes it possible to use nature and live good lives throughout the country in the future.

The proposals in this action plan will, as far as possible, safeguard the interests of both nature and climate, and measures under all 23 goals (of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework) can contribute to development that both preserves natural diversity, reduces greenhouse gas emissions and strengthens society and nature's ability to withstand climate change. In some cases, however, climate and nature considerations will conflict with each other, for example, to the development of renewable energy and the transmission of such energy through power grids and to the extraction of minerals and the establishment of industry that are important for the green shift, as this requires land. The government addresses these issues but emphasises that trade-offs between climate and nature must be made in the ongoing political work of every government.
Document Title: Norwegian Action Plan for Biodiversity (Meld. St. 35 2023-2024)

Family Name: Concept for the development of hydrogen energy in the Republic of Kazakhstan until 2040
Family Summary: National policy framework for developing Kazakhstan's long-term hydrogen economy vision to 2040 through targeted investments and technology deployment. It sets indicative targets for hydrogen production, including a 10 GW electrolyser target, up to KZT 5 trillion (USD 11.3 billion) in investments, and at least a 20% share of domestic technology supply.
Document Title: Concept for the development of hydrogen energy in the Republic of Kazakhstan until 2030

Family Name: Circular Economy Policy Framework for the Manufacturing Sector in Malaysia
Family Summary: The Circular Economy Policy Framework aims to guide Malaysia in transitioning towards a circular economy, providing support to manufacturers and contribute to the achievement of national climate goals. In alignment with the National Industrial Master Plan 2030, the Framework promotes a restorative industrial model by encouraging closed-loop material flows, minimising raw material consumption, enhancing recyclability, and increasing the availability of secondary feedstocks. It is projected that by 2030, implementing the framework will generate RM16 billion in savings, reduce CO₂ emissions by 6.5 million tonnes, and divert 14 million tonnes of waste annually.
Document Title: Circular Economy Policy Framework for the Manufacturing Sector in Malaysia

Family Name: Spain Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030. The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness.

The plan sets out the following objectives: 1) to become a carbon-neutral country by 2050 by decreasing the gross total GHG emissions in the electricity, transport, industry sectors ; 2) to promote energy efficiency thanks to the penetration of renewable energy in final energy consumption, efficiency measures to the transport, industry and building sectors, energy saving targets; 3) to ensure energy security by the diversification of the national energy mix, the use of domestic sources and an increase in the flexibility of the national energy system; 4) interconnectivity, energy transmission infrastructure, integration of the internal energy market; 5) to strengthen technology transfers, promote public-private partnership and improve business research and innovation. The updated NECP has an enhanced focus on strategic energy independence, with more ambitious targets to reduce external energy dependency from 73% in 2019 to 50% in 2030. Other key aims include a 55% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions in 2030 relative to 2005, and a 81% renewable share of energy production.
Document Title: Spain Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030

Family Name: Guidelines for the Preparation of the 2025-2028 Budget
Family Summary: These Guidelines cover Climate Change/Gender Mainstreaming. Family Name: National Renewable Energy Supply Chain Action Plan
Family Summary:
The National Renewable Energy Supply Chain Action Plan (NRESCAP) aims to identify and reduce risks in Australia’s renewable energy supply chains to help meet the 2030 renewables target. 

The technologies focused on were onshore wind; solar photovoltaics; and batteries. A sample of the actions being delivered to mitigate the identified risks are represented in this document.
Document Title: National Renewable Energy Supply Chain Action Plan

Family Name: Ireland Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030. The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness.

The plan establishes key measures to address the five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: 1) Decarbonisation : to reduce emissions from sectors outside the EU's Emissions Trading System, enhance carbon pricing to create behavioural change and avoid locking in carbon intensive technologies, eliminate non-recyclable plastic and impose higher fees on the production of materials which are difficult to recycle, promote the increased use of domestic harvested wood in longer lived product, mainstream biodiversity across the decision making process in the State, increase electricity generated from renewable sources to 80%, etc; 2) Energy efficiency: to set stricter requirements for new buildings and substantial refurbishment, installing 680,000 heatpumps over the period 2021-2030, and scaling/improving the Sustainable Energy Communities and Better Energy Communities 3) Energy security: to support efforts to increase indigenous renewable sources in the energy mix, including wind, solar and bioenergy, etc; 4) Internal energy market: continue to deepen the integration of IRL’s wholesale electricity market and its regulation with the EU internal energy market (IEM), etc; 5) Research, innovation and competitiveness: to increase investment in knowledge-based capital, to strengthen delivery of public funding for basic and applied research to meet Ireland’s decarbonisation objectives, etc.

Family Name: Australian Sustainability Reporting Standard AASB S2 Climate-related Disclosures
Family Summary:
This Standard requires an entity to disclose information about climate-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect the entity’s cash flows, its access to finance or cost of capital over the short, medium or long term. The main climate-related financial disclosure requirements relate to governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets, including information about scenario analysis and Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions.

This Standard applies to annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2025. Earlier application is permitted. The Corporations Act 2001 sets out which entities are required to comply with this Standard and specifies three

application dates (financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2025, 1 July 2026 and 1 July 2027) for the various classes of entity.
Document Title: Australian Sustainability Reporting Standard AASB S2 Climate-related Disclosures

Family Name: Australian Sustainability Reporting Standard AASB S1 General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability-related Financial Information
Family Summary:
This Standard is a voluntary Standard.  Entities may elect to apply this Standard, which would require an entity to disclose information about all sustainability-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect the entity’s cash flows, its access to finance or cost of capital over the short, medium or long term.

The AASB has also issued a separate, mandatory Standard on climate-related financial disclosures, AASB S2 Climate-related Disclosures. AASB S2 incorporates selected content from this Standard that the AASB considers necessary to make AASB S2 function as the standalone Standard for all climate-related financial disclosures. That content is included in Appendix D to AASB S2. Entities required by the Corporations Act 2001 to comply with AASB S2 are not required to comply with this Standard, but may refer to it for guidance. They may also elect to apply this Standard in preparing their sustainability report.

This Standard is issued as a voluntary Standard consistent with Australian Government policy, which is to mandate only climate-related disclosures at this time. Mandatory disclosure requirements for other sustainability-related topics may be developed in the future, which might result in either revisions to or replacement of this Standard, potentially including removing its voluntary status and making it a mandatory pronouncement.
Document Title: Australian Sustainability Reporting Standard AASB S1 General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability-related Financial Information

Family Name: National Long-Term Development Plan (RPJPN) 2025-2045
Family Summary:
This Plan, approved in Law No. 59 of 2024, outlines efforts to address various aspects of public needs to realise the vision of “Golden Indonesia 2045, a united, sovereign, advanced, and sustainable Indonesia. It serves as a guideline for:

  1. the formulation, monitoring, and review of laws and regulations;
  2. the formulation of the vision, mission, and programs in the candidacy requirements, campaign materials, and debate materials for: a. b. presidential and vice-presidential candidate pairs; and candidate pairs for governor and deputy governor, regent and deputy regent, and mayor and deputy mayor; and
  3. the preparation of master plans, national strategies, roadmaps, or other similar documents related to the elaboration of long-term and medium-term national development planning.

The Plan describes how various regions are affected by climate change, and actions to mitigate and adapt to climate change. Such actions include implementing climate-smart agriculture that is resilient to climate change; rural environmental management, including climate crisis prevention and disaster resilience; and prevention and control of diseases and health issues caused by climate change.

Family Name: Supreme Decree 5224, authorising a loan agreement for the "Contingent Loan for Natural Disasters and Public Health Emergencies" programme
Family Summary: The Supreme Decree 5224, based on constitutional provisions (Article 108, numeral 11) and previous laws (Ley No. 602 on Risk Management), authorises the signing of a loan agreement with the Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) for the programme "Contingent Loan for Natural Disasters and Public Health Emergencies". The programme aims to contribute to reducing the impact that a natural disaster or a severe public health event could have on the country's public finances. The loan was considered to be used supporting the management of risks related to natural disasters and public health emergencies, in line with the objectives of the Economic and Social Plan 2021-2025, which aims to reduce the risk of diseases and improve access to health services, as well as to promote sustainable forest management.

Family Name: Ministerial Resolution No. 00283-2024-MINAM. Guidelines for the reception, administration, and distribution of REDD+ financing in Peru (Resolución Ministerial N°00283-2024-MINAM. Lineamiento para la recepción, administración y distribución del financiamiento REDD+ en el Perú)
Family Summary: This Peruvian ministerial resolution establishes guidelines for the reception, administration and distribution of REDD+ financing across its three phases: preparation, implementation, and results-based payments. The instrument delineates three administrative modalities for managing REDD+ funds: through public entity budgetary allocations subject to the National Public Budget System; via PROFONANPE (the National Fund for State Protected Natural Areas) specifically for funds from the Joint Declaration of Intent with Germany, Norway and the United Kingdom; and through direct donor administration mechanisms such as trusts. The resolution mandates that the Ministry of Environment and donors jointly determine the appropriate modality based on costs, execution timelines and required human resources, with such determination to be formalised in bilateral or multilateral agreements. For results-based payments, the guidelines stipulate that benefit distribution must be equitable, culturally appropriate and participatory, with the Ministry establishing criteria for beneficiary identification in consultation with state and non-state actors, including indigenous peoples, whilst ensuring continued reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from the Land Use, Land-Use Change and Forestry sector.
Document Title: Guidelines for the reception, administration, and distribution of REDD+ financing in Peru (Lineamiento para la recepción, administración y distribución del financimiento REDD+ en el Perú)

Family Summary: The National Health and Climate Strategy (the Strategy) is a whole-of-government plan to address the health and wellbeing impacts of climate change and the contribution the health system make to climate change through the generation of greenhouse gas emissions in care delivery. The 49 actions the Australian Government has committed to under the Strategy will require a range of approaches to deliver successfully. Key to the Strategy’s implementation will be a systematic approach to managing a complex program of work, coordination and leveraging of related policy across all levels of government, a diverse range of portfolios, and the mobilisation of numerous external stakeholders including communication with consumers to increase awareness and promote behaviour change.

Family Name: The list of positive project areas for implementation of Article 6 of the Paris Agreement in Sri Lanka
Family Summary:
In September 2024, the Government of Sri Lanka approved and published a positive list of project areas that are considered for trading under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. The positive list also includes capping the share of emission reductions that can be credited restricted to renewables energy projects. Some types of renewable projects see their emission reductions are capped at 50% and others at 25%. Eligible activities are as follows:

1. Electricity Sector

- Establishment of wind power plants with the assistance of bilateral and multilateral donor agencies and sovereign governments (to the level of 737 MW) - (Maximum 25%)

- Establishment of ground-mounted solar PV with the assistance of bilateral and multilateral donor agencies and sovereign governments (to the level of 1982 MW) - (Maximum 25%)

- Establishment of Offshore Wind Farms (Maximum 50%)

- Establishment of Tidal Energy Farms (Maximum 50%)

- Establishment of Energy Storage Power Facilities such as Hydro Pumped Power Storage (Maximum 50%)

- Establishment of Energy Storage Power Facilities such as Battery Storage in Solar Power Plants (Maximum 50%)

- Electricity Wheeling (50%)

- Demand Side Management programs other than Lighting efficiency improvements (50%)

2. Transport Sector

- Implementation of fuel switch measures focusing on electric mobility and hybrid vehicles (H2)

- Implementation of low-carbon public passenger transport activities, such as Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) and improved rail transportation

- Implementation of rapid transport systems for passenger transport

- Development of new low-carbon transportation infrastructure resulting in fuel savings

3. Industry Sector

- Fuel switch from fossil fuels to renewable energy-based fuels in industrial processes

- Development of Resource-Efficiency Cleaner Production (RECP) practices, including low-carbon technologies and processes

- Introduction of tri-generation* facilities

- Energy efficiency interventions in industries with longer payback periods

4. Forestry Sector

- Restoration and reforestation of terrestrial forests covering various plantations

- Enhancement and expansion of trees outside forests

- Agroforestry on private lands, covering various large and bundled small activities

- Reforestation by the private sector for timber production

- Mangrove restoration subject to the following conditions

a. Restoration of mangroves based on the areas identified by the Department of Forest Conservation and the Department of Wildlife Conservation, which is approximately 2000 ha in extent, will be restored, however, the aforementioned extent would not be considered and allocated for carbon finance and crediting purposes.

b. Apart from the above-mentioned identified areas, any further areas that might be identified based on National Guidelines on Mangrove Restoration in Sri Lanka (2021), and other protocols for blue carbon ecosystem restoration, and approved by the Blue Carbon Task Force, could be considered.

5. Waste Sector

- Deployment of methane abatement technologies in municipal solid waste treatment projects

- Implementation of Waste-to-Energy projects (Incineration, Gasification, Pyrolysis and Plasma)

- Waste dumpsites rehabilitation projects (Avoidance of greenhouse gas emissions in waste dumps/landfills)

- Deployment of Efficient Waste Collection and Transportation Systems and Processes

- Emission Reductions through the Promotion of Recycling Technologies and Process Optimization

6. Agriculture Sector

- Methane emission management from livestock coupled with energy conversion for thermal or electrical generation

- Adoption of innovative technologies in agricultural practices (such as rice cultivation) for GHG emission reductions
Document Title: The list of positive project areas for implementation of Article 6 of the Paris Agreement in Sri Lanka

Family Name: Malaysia Aviation Decarbonisation Blueprint
Family Summary:
The blueprint outlines Malaysia’s strategy to reduce carbon emissions in the aviation sector. It includes strategies like improvements in aircraft technology, operational practices, sustainable aviation fuels, and market-based measures to achieve aviation net-zero targets by 2050. 

The Blueprint aims to achieve the following objectives:

1. Chart a clear path for Malaysia to reach its net-zero targets for international aviation by 2050.

2. Align Malaysia's aviation net-zero pathway for international flights with International Civil Aviation Organization targets.

3. Develop Malaysia’s competitive advantage to become a regional hub for sustainable aviation.

4. Ensure that Malaysian operators are not unfairly burdened and have access to viable solutions for meeting decarbonization targets.

5. Provide measures for the reduction of domestic emissions, as guided by the Nationally Determined Contributions and the Long-Term Low Emissions Development Strategy.
Document Title: Malaysia Aviation Decarbonisation Blueprint

Document Title: National Action Plan for Climate Change Health Adaptation (2024-2030)

Family Name: Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan for the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry until 2027: Risk Management and Competitiveness in a Changing Climate
Family Summary:
Within the administrative branch of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, the Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan functions as a steering and communicative tool to strengthen climate change adaptation. The Action Plan also supports and executes the National Climate Change Adaptation Plan until 2030 (NAP2030).

The plan was compiled as part of official duties of the ministry and its sector organisations. Work on the plan began in 2021 and it was finalised as a publication in late 2023.

The plan is built on several aims, which are specified through targets accompanied by actions. The plan is implemented both as part of official duties of the corresponding actors and through various programmes and projects. Actions are defined until the year 2027 and include the following areas: diversifying crops; water management; reducing weather risks; ensuring health and welfare of farm aniamls; maintaining the vitality of rural areas; ensuring food and nutrition security; and ensuring sustainable forestry. Progress of the plan's implementation and the need for new actions will be assessed in 2025.
Document Title: Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan for the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry until 2027: Risk Management and Competitiveness in a Changing Climate

Family Name: CONPES 4088/2022 - Declaration of strategic importance of investment projects for the implementation of actions that lead to low-carbon and climate-resilient development
Family Summary:
The CONPES 4088 Document of 2022 is an initiative by the Colombian National Government that declares seven investment projects as strategically important to promote low-carbon and climate-resilient development. These projects align with the country's commitments to climate change and aim to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and enhance the resilience of productive sectors and ecosystems in Colombia.

Amidst the projects, there are key points such as the conservation and sustainable use of ecosystems, strengthening of the climate change management in sectoral planning and sustainable agricultural and forestry development.

These projects are set to be developed between 2022 and 2025 and the implementation of these projects is crucial to advancing a sustainable development model that integrates climate change mitigation and the adaptation of the country's productive sectors and ecosystems.
Document Title: CONPES 4088/2022 - Declaration of strategic importance of investment projects for the implementation of actions that lead to low-carbon and climate-resilient development.

Family Summary:

Action 2.2: By 2027, climate-proof action plans will be established, with tailored measures required to maintain or improve the conservation status of the habitats and species

Family Name: Maldives Tourism Climate Action Plan: Strategic Pathways for Climate Resiliency in Tourism
Family Summary: This Plan sets out the Maldives' vision for harnessing the power of tourism to drive positive change. It will help to maximise the positive impacts of tourism while minimising its negative impacts on the environment and communities. By implementing this action plan, the Maldives envisages achieving long-term economic growth, social well-being, and environmental conservation.

The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness.

The plan provides an overview of the country’s energy and climate policy as well as the current status of plans in these areas. Several measures and strategies are implemented to address the five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: 1) Decarbonisation: implementation of the Climate Action Plan 2050 and the Climate Action Programme 2030, better regionalisation of growth of renewable energies, increase the consumption of self-generated electricity, subsidies for electrically powered vehicles (environmental bonus), etc.; 2) Energy efficiency: energy efficiency strategy for buildings, tax incentives for energy-related building renovations, carbon pricing in the heating and transport sectors, etc.; 3) Energy security: Act on the Security of the Electricity and Gas Supply, national preventive action and emergency plans for natural gas, etc; 4) Internal energy market: promote interconnectivity (regional cooperation), etc.; 5) Research, innovation, competitiveness: greater involvement of start-ups, increased technology transfer. Quantified targets in the plan include at least a 65% reduction in net greenhouse gas emissions by 2030, from a 1990 baseline, and a 42.5% renewabe energy share of gross final consumption by 2030. Final energy consumption is to be reduced using energy efficiency measures by at least 26.5% by 2030, from a 2008 baseline.
Document Title: Germany Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030

Family Name: Regulations Governing the Collection of Carbon Fees
Family Summary:
August 2024, Taiwan's Ministry of Environment (MOENV) announced three carbon fee related regulations that establish a carbon pricing system. The first regulation, entitled “Regulations Governing the Collection of Carbon Fees”, outlines how the carbon fees will be collected from entities.

Scope:

Entities subject to carbon fees: Power and gas supply industries, along with manufacturing industries emitting 25,000 metric tons or more of CO2e annually, will be subject to carbon fees.

Payment Timing:

Starting from the year after the fee rate takes effect, entities must pay carbon fees annually by the end of May. Payment is based on the total emissions of the preceding year, calculated using the announced rates. For instance, if the rates become effective on January 1, 2025, then payment for emissions during 2025 would be due by May 2026.

Transitional Adjustment Mechanism:

To ease the transition, a mechanism adjusts chargeable emissions, particularly for industries susceptible to carbon leakage, through an adjustment coefficient that increases over time. The emission adjustment coefficient value for the first period is 0.2, 0.4 for the second, and 0.6 for the third period.

Carbon credits:

Entities can utilize both domestic and carbon credits. Domestic credits can offset up to 10% of chargeable emissions. International credits require MOENV approval and can only be used by industries not considered high risk for carbon leakage.

Implementation Timeline:

Following a trial declaration without payment in 2025, payments based on 2025 emission levels will commence in 2026. The fee rate, to be determined by October 2024 and effective from January 1, 2025, will be reviewed annually.
Document Title: Regulations Governing the Collection of Carbon Fees

Family Name: CNPE Resolution 5 of August 26, 2024, on the National Energy Transition Policy (PNTE)
Family Summary:
This Resolution from the National Energy Policy Council (CNPE) establishes the National Energy Transition Policy (PNTE), the National Energy Transition Plan (Plante), the National Energy Transition Forum (Fonte), and makes other provisions. The Resolution establishes that the aim of the National Energy Transition Policy is to guide national efforts to transform the national energy matrix into a low-carbon economy, contributing to the achievement of net greenhouse gas emission neutrality in the country. The Policy consists of a mechanism to support the integration and coordination of government policies and actions at the federal level, in conjunction with sub-national entities, and for dialogue with civil society and the productive sector, to consolidate national efforts. It must observe the objectives of the national energy policy for the rational use of energy sources in harmony with the international policies and commitments made by the country concerning climate change. It must also consider the other objectives of public policies, including initiatives and strategies to enable the ecological transformation of the Brazilian economy, the increased density of production chains and adding value in the country, and mitigation and adaptation to climate change.

The CEFONTE Resolution from October 1st, 2025 defines the criteria for appointing members to the Plenary of the National Energy Transition Forum - Fonte.

The CEFONTE Resolution from January 13th, 2025 provides for the Regulation of the Public Selection Process for the selection of civil society representatives to make up the Plenary of the National Energy Transition Forum - Source Plenary, for the 2025/2026 biennium.
Document Title: Resolution CEFONTE 1 of January 13, 2025

Family Name: Pact for Ecological Transformation between the three branches of the Brazilian State
Family Summary:
The Pact for Ecological Transformation is a commitment signed by the Executive, Legislative and Judicial branches to act in a harmonious and integrated manner to promote ecological transformation through legislative, administrative and judicial measures.

Its main commitments are:

  • The Legislative Branch will prioritise bills related to the pact's themes, such as the approval of the legal framework for the carbon market, offshore wind energy production and biofuels;
  • The Judiciary will adopt measures to speed up judicial demands involving environmental, land and climate issues, including the definition of targets and protocols by the National Council of Justice (CNJ);
  • The executive branch will expand funding and reduce the cost of credit for sustainable sectors, projects and practices;
  • The executive branch and the judiciary will jointly integrate real estate, environmental, cadastral and tax databases, with georeferenced data, to guarantee legal certainty about the ownership of public and private land in the country, as well as unlock investment.
  • The Legislative, Executive and Judicial branches will adopt management measures to reduce the direct impacts of their activities on the environment, such as sustainable bidding, reducing demand for natural resources, energy efficiency and proper waste disposal.
Document Title: Pact for Ecological Transformation

The program, which aims to provide financial assistance to the General State Budget, will focus on coordinating and implementing actions related to preparedness, response, early recovery, and rehabilitation in the face of adverse hydrometeorological events. The primary objective is to strengthen the country's ability to manage risks associated with climate change-related events by enabling the allocation of resources across different sectors and territories.

Family Name: National Strategy on Adaptation to Climate Change (SNASC) for the period 2024-2030, with a perspective of 2050
Family Summary:
The Strategy aims to improve the adaptive capacity and increase the resilience of socio-economic and natural systems to the impacts of climate variability and change over different areas and time scales, facilitating Romania's transition to a sustainable, low-carbon economy. The SNASC also aims at sectoral development in line with the principles of the EU Strategy for Adaptation to Climate Change, namely smart, rapid, systemic and connected adaptation at the global scale of action.

The Strategy is based on the need to ensure an adequate level of resilience of the Romanian society, economy and environment to the impact of climate change and its associated risks, in the time horizon 2024-2030-2050, by accelerating the introduction of adaptation measures in all sectors of activity. The strategy proposes the picture of Romania's sectoral development in the coming decades in the light of the following scenarios: a) no adaptation measures are taken (baseline scenario) ; b) adaptation measures are adopted, within the framework provided by global climate scenarios. For quantitative assessment of the costs and benefits of adaptation, national sectoral development scenarios are needed to complement the global scenarios used in this document with specific information. The next update cycle of the Adaptation Strategy will need to have such scenarios, built on the integrated assessment models to explore alternative socio-economic conditions in the specific case of Romania.
Document Title: National Strategy on Adaptation to Climate Change (SNASC) for the period 2024-2030, with a perspective of 2050.

Family Summary: These regulations set out the implementation rules for a specific cohesion policy measure under the EU’s 2021–2027 Cohesion Programme, namely Priority 3.1 “Sustainable TEN-T infrastructure” and its Specific Objective 3.1.1.6 “Development of large ports’ public infrastructure”. The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness.

Firstly, the multi-year energy program, which sets the priorities for actions of the public authorities in the field of energy for the next 10 years, divided into two 5-year periods. It deals with all energies and all the pillars of energy policy: control of energy demand, promotion of renewable energies, guarantee of security of supply, control of energy costs, balanced development of networks, etc. Secondly, the national low-carbon strategy, which is France's roadmap for leading the climate change mitigation policy. It provides guidelines for implementing the transition to a low-carbon economy in all sectors of activity. It defines objectives for reducing greenhouse gas emissions at the scale of France in the short and medium term - carbon budgets - and aims to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050. other Quantified goals include a 50% reduction in non-LULUCF GHG emissions by 2030, relative to 1990.

Family Summary:
This Law regulates the cultivation, protection, preservation and improvement of forests, planning, methods and conditions of forest use, construction and maintenance of forest roads, forest monitoring, as well as other issues of importance for forests, forest land and forestry. It also applies to the protection, preservation and use of forest trees located outside forests.

This Law contains provisions on protecting the ecological functions of forests, which include the sequestration of carbon from the air, and on forest monitoring. Forest monitoring is carried out for the purpose of preservation, restoration and sustainable use of forest ecosystems and their services, to increase the resilience of forests and enable the protection of the multifunctionality of forests, with a special emphasis on adaptation and mitigation of climate change.

Family Name: Norway’s strategy for promoting food security in development policy
Family Summary:
This Strategy is aimed at strengthening food systems in developing countries. The vision is to promote, within sustainable frameworks, local production of nutritious food that is processed and sold locally and regionally, thus increasing the incomes of small-scale food producers, stimulating local job creation throughout the value chain, and expanding access to healthy food.

There is an emphasis on increasing local climate-resilient food production, increasing local value creation and income for food producers, reducing malnutrition and malnourishment and reducing the extent of hunger crises, as outlined in the implementation section of the Strategy. The Strategy is guided by the role of women, persons with disabilities, and youth and young adults. The Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation (Norad) actively works on value chain developments through its partners, especially in southern Africa, where bottlenecks have been identified in value chains and targeted initiatives are being implemented. Examples of such bottlenecks may include a lack of storage facilities, credit, local refinement possibilities or market access. Norad collaborates with the private sector to solve these challenges.
Document Title: Norway’s strategy for promoting food security in development policy

Family Summary: The Interministerial Decree of 7 August 2024 (DM n. 294/2024) establishes Italy’s national certification system for the sustainability of biocombustibles, as well as certification schemes for renewable fuels of non-biological origin (RFNBO) and recycled carbon fuels (RCF). The decree implements the framework set out in Legislative Decree No. 199/2021 (transposing the EU Renewable Energy Directive – RED II) and defines the rules for verifying sustainability criteria, including minimum greenhouse-gas emission reductions, traceability along the supply chain through a mass-balance system, and certification procedures carried out by accredited bodies.
Document Title: Ministerial Decree 294/2024 establishing the National System for the Certification of the Sustainability of Biofuels, the Certification of Renewable Fuels of Non-Biological Origin, and that of Fuels from Recycled Carbon

Family Name: Energy Conversion and Efficiency Programme
Family Summary: The main objective of the programme is to reduce building energy consumption and promote energy efficient technology, ranging from appliances to photovoltaic panels and solar water heater. It establishes a credit line for households to purchase household and gas appliances, and material and equipment that improves the building envelope, with a maximum amount up to 25 million pesos, a repayment period of up to 5 years, and a 43% fixed rate. It also provides loans for businesses to purchase equipment and material that reduce energy losses, with up to 10 year terms and a 27% fixed rate in the first year.
Document Title: Resolution 202/2024 - CONVERSION AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY PROGRAM

Family Name: Circular Economy Blueprint for Solid Waste in Malaysia 2025-2035
Family Summary:
This Blueprint is aimed at creating more sustainable solid waste management and will also help the country address the challenges of climate change and achieve net zero carbon emissions as early as 2050.

The Circular Economy Strategy of Refuse, Rethink, Reduce, Reuse, Repair, Refurbish, Remanufacture, Repurpose, Recycle, and Recover will be the basis for every implementation of circular economy initiatives to ensure that resources are used efficiently and waste generation is reduced.

The key initiatives include a mandatory Extended Producer Responsibility policy for manufacturers, Zero Waste to Landfill Certification, a Pay-As-You-Throw scheme, and a proposed Circular Economy Act. The blueprint also proposes the establishment of a National Circular Economy Association to coordinate industry efforts.
Document Title: Circular Economy Blueprint for Solid Waste in Malaysia 2025-2035

Family Name: National Disaster Risk Management Plan 2015-2030 implemented by Decree no. 978/2024
Family Summary:
The Decree 978/2024 adopts the second update of the National Disaster Risk Management Plan 2015-2030 and amends the Decree 308/2016. With this modifications, the Colombian National Disaster Risk Management Plans will have a minimum projection of four constitutional terms of government from the date of its adoption.The main goal of the plan is to guide actions of the National Disaster Risk Management System (SNGRD) to comply with the National Policies on Risk Management and Adaptation to Climate Change. This will contribute to increase the capacity to intervene on the causes of risk, thus contributing to sustainable development and adapted to climate change effects.According to the plan (page 39) the specific goals are:1. Develop knowledge of risk and the effects of climate change to enable effective risk reduction in the territory.

2. Optimise intervention capacity (technical and operational) to reduce existing risks and prevent the generation of new risk conditions, as well as strengthen recovery capacity in the face of materialised risks.

3. Promote incident participation in disaster risk management and adaptation to climate change, taking into account the differentiated needs of the population and society in the territories.

4. Strengthen disaster risk governance for efficient and effective disaster risk management and climate change adaptation.

5. Strengthen preparedness for response to the possible materialization of risk, guaranteeing the integration of the social dynamics of the territory.
Document Title: PLAN NACIONALDE GESTIÓN DEL RIESGO DE DESASTRES "Una estrategia de desarrollo" 2015 -2030 (National Disaster Risk Management Plan "A Development Strategy" 2015-2030)

Family Name: National Strategy for Agricultural Development (SENDA)
Family Summary: This document contains the National Strategy for Agricultural Development (SENDA), which is part of state policies aimed at increasing the productivity of agro-industrial chains, fishing, and aquaculture in a sustainable manner. SENDA thus contributes to the national goal of stimulating long-term economic growth, promoting social inclusion, and improving human well-being. SENDA also seeks to facilitate compliance with environmental commitments, such as the Paris Agreement (United Nations, 2015b) to combat climate change, the Sendai Framework (2015a) for disaster risk reduction, the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (2022), and other multilateral environmental agreementsIn response to the Paris Agreement of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), Uruguay set the goal of reducing absolute emissions (in the Second Nationally Determined Contribution or NDC2) with specific targets for the agricultural sector - for instance stabilizing methane and nitrous oxide emissions to ensure they do not generate additional warming. Following a national and international diagnosis, the document outlines six strategic dimensions identified as key to organizing public policies for sector development, namely: 1) International integration; 2) Infrastructure and logistics; 3) Sustainability of agroecosystems; 4) Productive and social development; 5) Information technologies for agriculture; and 6) Institutional capacities.
Document Title: National Strategy for Agricultural Development (SENDA)

Family Name: Sustainable Finance Taxonomy
Family Summary:
The Sustainable Finance Taxonomy of Costa Rica defines what an environmentally sustainable investment is in a standardised way, establishing a common reference framework that helps actors in the real economy and the financial sector of Costa Rica to identify those investments that contribute to the fulfillment of the environmental and social objectives of the country.

The Taxonomy of Sustainable Finance of Costa Rica has been developed under the leadership of the Ministry of Environment and Energy (MINAE), the Ministry of Finance, the Central Bank of Costa Rica (BCCR), the General Superintendence of Financial Entities (SUGEF), the General Superintendence of Securities (SUGEVAL), the Superintendence of Pensions (SUPEN) and the General Superintendence of Insurance (SUGESE).

The taxonomy identifies eight critical sectors for sustainable investment, including construction, transport, energy, solid waste management, drinking water and sanitation, ICT, manufacturing, and agriculture. Each sector has specified science-based criteria to ensure that activities are not only environmentally sustainable but also contribute to climate mitigation and adaptation efforts.
Document Title: Sustainable Finance Taxonomy

Family Name: Denmark Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030

The plan details key objectives and measures to achieve them: 1) decarbonisation : reduction of GHG emissions, transport green transition with a stop to sales of all new diesel and petrol cars as of 2030, ban on burning of straw residues on fields, public afforestation and a grant scheme for afforestation on private agricultural land and subsidy for conversion of arable land on organic soils to nature, etc; 2) renewable energy: three new offshore wind farms of at least 800 MW each, reduction of the electrical heating tax and of the electricity tax, support of geothermal energy, etc; 3) energy efficiency: to build a competitive subsidy scheme related to private enterprises, efficiency of existing buildings through renovation, etc; 4) energy security: stable energy supply thanks to laws on responsibilities regarding electricity supply, gas supply and emergency plans, prevention of risks in the energy system, increased international cooperation, interconnectivity concerning energy supply. Quantified targets include a 70% reduction of net GHG emissions by 2030, from a 1990 baseline.
Document Title: Denmark Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
