Family Name: Finland Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030. The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness.

The plain aims : 1) to reduce GHG emissions in the non-emissions trading sector; 2) to increase the share of renewable energy in the final energy use of road transport; 3) to promote energy efficiency. The plan outlines the impact of existing policy measures on the projected evolution of greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy and energy efficiency up to 2040. It describes the effects of the planned policy measures on the energy system, greenhouse gas emissions and sinks, economic development, the environment and public health. Specific targets include a 62% renewable share of gross final energy consumption by 2030.
Document Title: Finland Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030

Family Name: Aviation White Paper
Family Summary:
The White Paper and the development of its 56 policy initiatives was informed by extensive consultation on the Aviation Green Paper with the aviation industry, state and territory governments, and the Australian community. These 56 policy initiatives cover 10 key areas including:

  • a better passenger experience
  • a competitive and efficient aviation sector
  • a skilled, secure and productive workforce
  • maximising aviation’s contribution to net zero
  • connecting regional Australia
  • regenerating General Aviation
  • a balanced approach to airport planning and noise
  • world leading safety, security and airspace regulation
  • enabling new aviation technologies
  • connecting Australia to the world 

Climate-related initiatives include providing funding to regional airports to increase climate resilience and requirign additional information in airport master plans to address climate change resilience and decarbonisation.
Document Title: Aviation White Paper

Family Name: Decree No. 2024-658 of 1 August 2024 establishing the Carbon Market Bureau
Family Summary: This Decree establishes the Carbon Market Bureau in charge of setting up carbon credits and a national carbon registry along with institutional arrangements such as a supervisory council and technical secretariat.
Document Title: Decree No. 2024-658 of 1 August 2024 establishing the Carbon Market Bureau

Family Name: Battery Breakthrough Initiative
Family Summary:
This Initiative is part of the Future Made in Australia (FMA) policy agenda of the Australian Government. The program’s objective is to fund projects that enhance Australia’s battery manufacturing capability to improve supply chain resilience and support emissions reduction; or commercialise battery manufacturing processes and technologies that can contribute to emissions reduction.

In the 2024-2025 Federal Budget, the Australian Government announced the Battery Breakthrough Initiative with $500 million of funding to promote the development of battery manufacturing capabilities in Australia. In the 2026 Federal Budget, the Australian Government reduced funding for the Battery Breakthrough Initiative (BBI) to $142 million. ARENA is no longer accepting new applications, subject to further notice.
Document Title: Battery Breakthrough Initiative

Family Name: Agenda 2030: A Pathway for a Resilient and Prosperous Future
Family Summary:
This policy document covers eight thematic areas: climate change; good governance; economic growth and resilience; private sector development; social development; nuclear justice; infrastructure development; and partnership for financing and development. Priority areas and actions are identified under these themes with the aim of providing a resilient and prosperous future for the Republic of the Marshall Islands.

Under climate change, the priority areas are to improve access to climate finance; and adaptation and resilience. Actions include exploring the possibility of accessing global climate finance credit facilities; implementing the National Adaptation Plan; addressing customary land tenure and individual rights to accommodate the protection of some land and the vacating of unprotected land; and addressing early-stage planning to identify protection needs for key islands (or parts of atolls) to provide for safe relocation of populations as reflected in the Marshall Islands' Sea Level Rise Policy.
Document Title: Agenda 2030: A Pathway for a Resilient and Prosperous Future

Family Name: Opinions on Accelerating Comprehensive Green Transformation of Economic and Social Development
Family Summary:
The Opinions of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council on Accelerating Comprehensive Green Transformation of Economic and Social Development was issued in July 2024. The opinions include the following:

  • Promote the green transformation in the urban and rural areas, including the construction of climate-adapted cities and enhance the climate resilience of urban and rural areas;
  • Participate in leading the global green transformation process, including actively participating in the formulation of international rules in dealing with climate change, marine pollution control, biodiversity protection, plastic pollution control and other fields, and promoting the construction of a fair, reasonable and win-win global environmental climate governance system; and
  • Study and formulate special laws to deal with climate change and carbon peaking.
Document Title: Opinions on Accelerating Comprehensive Green Transformation of Economic and Social Development

Family Name: Canada’s 2030 Nature Strategy: Halting and Reversing Biodiversity Loss in Canada
Family Summary:
This national strategy establishes a shared vision and roadmap for halting and reversing biodiversity loss in Canada, laying the groundwork for transformative change. These six pillars ensure that the path to 2030 is inclusive, adaptable, and evidence-based:

  • Recognizing, upholding, and implementing the rights of Indigenous Peoples and advancing reconciliation, as Indigenous Peoples are the original caretakers of the lands, waters, and ice.
  • Ensuring a whole-of-government, whole-of-society approach to create policy coherence and draw on the strengths of every segment of society to build and deliver the solutions we need.
  • Supporting a resilient economy and improving efficiency and certainty, as our prosperity is inherently linked to a healthy environment.
  • Empowering on-the-ground action by reflecting regional differences, supporting communities, and adopting flexible community-based approaches.
  • Using the best available science and knowledge, incorporating new insights, sharing information, and giving equal weight to western science and Indigenous Knowledge.
  • Applying integrated, holistic approaches to ensure our actions are inclusive and transparent.

The strategy addresses all 23 of Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework targets - including Target 8 on minimising the impact of climate change and increasing the climate resilience of biodiversity - and builds on historic recent investments of more than $12B since 2018 in conservation, ecosystem restoration, species protection, and natural climate solutions. In relation to target 8, Canada will mitigate by reducing greenhouse gas emissions economy wide; implementing nature-based solutions; supporting ecosystem-based approaches; and advancing science and knowledge. Canada will adapt by implementing natural climate solutions; advancing science and knowledge; and developing tools and capacity. Canada will also consider cliamte change and biodiversity effects in decision-making, and foster positive impacts of climate action.

The federal government may also explore additional opportunities, including:

  • Advancing new and innovative solutions that address the nexus between climate change and biodiversity loss.
  • Developing an Ocean Climate Action Plan, which could include the use of climate information in decision making.
  • Enhancing our understanding of the impacts of climate change and ocean acidification on biodiversity in Canada's oceans, developing risk management and adaptation approaches, and gaining a better understanding of the carbon sequestration potential of our oceans.
  • Addressing knowledge gaps to support positive biodiversity conservation outcomes from boreal wildfire management response measures and associated forest management practices.
Document Title: Canada’s 2030 Nature Strategy: Halting and Reversing Biodiversity Loss in Canada

Family Name: Strategy of the National Fund for Environmental Protection and Water Management (NFOŚiGW) for 2025–2028
Family Summary:
The Strategy of the National Fund for Environmental Protection and Water Management (NFOŚiGW) for 2025–2028 is a strategic roadmap designed to reinforce the Fund's role as a leader in financing Poland's green transition. The main goal is to drive the green transition and support low-emission transformation, sustainable development, and environmental improvement in Poland through effective pro-environmental initiatives.

The document divides environmental priorities into two categories (i) sectoral: Energy transformation, air quality improvement, circular economy (waste and water management), and biodiversity protection and (ii) horizontal: Climate change adaptation, environmental monitoring, expert research, ecological education, and innovation.

All in all, the strategy is highly climate-centric, aligning with the EU Green Deal and Poland's national energy policies.

The strategy was adopted by Resolution 103/2024 on June 27, 2024.
Document Title: Strategy of the National Fund for Environmental Protection and Water Management (NFOŚiGW) for 2025–2028

Family Name: National Integrated Solid Waste Resource Management Policy (NISWRMP)
Family Summary: The policy aims to sustainably develop and strengthen management of the solid waste sector, noting its contribution to greenhouse gas emissions. It promotes increased climate-resilience from this sector in the long-term, and emissions mitigation actions in the short-term. The policy also promotes stronger regulatory structures and enforcement, expanding the organisational and research capacity of the sector.
Document Title: National Integrated Solid Waste Resource Management Policy (NISWRMP)

Family Name: High Technology Investment Programme (HIT-30)
Family Summary:
President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan launched the High Technology Investment Program (HIT-30), committing USD 30 billion in incentives to establish Türkiye as a global leader in high technology.

The HIT-30 program targets key sectors such as electric vehicles, battery production, semiconductor manufacturing, and energy technology. President Erdoğan reiterated Türkiye's commitment to supporting critical technologies that will strengthen Türkiye's economic and technological independence.

Türkiye's ambition is to become a regional hub for battery production, offering a USD 4.5 billion incentive package to attract international investors.
Document Title: High Technology Investment Programme (HIT-30)

Family Name: Luxembourg Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030. The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness.

The plan establishes the following central objectives: 1) Decarbonisation: reduction of GHG emissions, increase the share of renewable energy in the gross final energy consumption (by cooperating with other EU Member States; 2) Energy efficiency: new fossil-free single-purpose and residential buildings, developing renewable heating networks, preventing traffic through massive expansion of public transport and electromobility; 3) Energy security: reduce dependence on electricity imports by expanding renewable energy, intensify regional cooperation in the field of security of electricity and gas supply; 4) Internal energy market: no further development of national gas infrastructure, combining the sectors of electricity, heat and transport by means of sector coupling; 5) Research, innovation and competitiveness: implementation of a nationwide energy transition 'zero carbon', promote resilient urban and spatial development in conjunction with urban/spatial planning, Luxembourg to become an attractive location for climate solutions providers and start-ups. Other measures include a carbon tax increase. Compared to the 2020 NECP, the renewable energy share (at gross final energy consumption) target for 2030 has been increased from 25% to 37%.
Document Title: Luxembourg Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030

Family Name: Ordinance on State Aid for the Capture, Transport, and Storage of Biogenic CO2 (2024:626)
Family Summary:
The new regulation establishes a framework for state aid through reverse auctions, to incentivise CO2 capture and storage from biofuel combustion.

Through the reverse auction system, the Swedish Energy Agency will award funds to companies offering CO2 capture, transport, and storage at the lowest cost per tonne whilst also fulfilling certain other requirements. The aid is aimed at facilities located in Sweden, both during investment and operations phases. The Energy Agency can allocate 36 billion SEK (3 billion euro) between 2026 and 2046. In the first round, applications for aid under the Regulation can be submitted until 21 November 2024 and there has already been great interest in this. The Energy Agency aims to make a first allocation before the end of this year.

The scheme will run until 31 December 2028. By enabling capture and storage of significant amounts of biogenic CO2, the scheme will contribute to Sweden's efforts to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 85% by 2045 compared to the 1990 level. It will also help Sweden and the EU to meet the objective of achieving climate neutrality by 2050. The European Commission has approved this scheme, under EU State aid rules.
Document Title: Ordinance on State Aid for the Capture, Transport, and Storage of Biogenic CO2 (2024:626)

Family Name: Decree UP-106 On the Establishment of The Climate Council Under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan
Family Summary: Decree UP-106 establishes a national climate council as the highest advisory body to the president on climate adaptation and mitigation, to better co-ordinate and unify national climate policy. The decree and formation of the council initiates the process of developing a national climate mitigation and adaptation strategy. Aside from strategic and legislative efforts, the decree also places emphasis on the expansion and integration of carbon trading systems nationally.
Document Title: Decree UP-106 On the Establishment of The Climate Council Under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan

Family Name: National Delta Programme
Family Summary: The Delta Programme 2025 (DP2025) reports on progress and changes in the Delta Programme and the measures for the years ahead. It protects the Netherlands against high water and flooding, ensures sufficient fresh water, and contributes to climate-resilient and water-robust planning for the Netherlands.
Document Title: National Delta Programme

Family Name: Resolution S/N approving the National Adaptation Plan for Climate Change and Variability in the Energy Sector  (NAP-E)
Family Summary:
The NAP-E's main purpose is to improve the adaptability of the Uruguayan energy system, strengthen its resilience, and reduce its vulnerability to climate threats. This plan acknowledges the high levels of uncertainty associated with climate change, as well as the uncertainty inherent in technological evolution, and adopts an iterative, adaptive, and continuous learning approach. This approach will establish the necessary working processes to integrate climate change adaptation across all sectors, involving all key stakeholders, including the public sector, private sector, and academia.

The overall objective of the NAP-E is to reduce the climate vulnerability of the Uruguayan energy system to ensure it continues to fulfill its essential role of providing quality energy access to the population and contributing to the country’s sustainable development.

To achieve this objective, the NAP-E is structured around five lines of action to be implemented progressively, ensuring continuous and effective adaptation: Governance, Capacity strengthening and awareness, Information management and knowledge generation, Vulnerability reduction, and Monitoring, evaluation, and learning.
Document Title: National Adaptation Plan - Energy

Family Name: Czech Wood Policy
Family Summary:
Czech Wood Policy offers a novel approach insofar that wood is considered a strategic material, a renewable resource and an environmentally-friendly construction material. The key objective is to increase the added value of the wood processed in Czechia and ensure its more efficient use. Concretely, the Policy sets three priorities:

- To ensure sustainable long-term supply for the domestic wood- processing industry.

- To promote the use of wood as a renewable raw material in relevant sectors of the economy and everyday life.

- Continuously increase the production of wood-based products with higher added value and long life cycle, and increase domestic consumption to scale up the use of raw timber and primary processed wood.

In practical terms, meeting the objectives set by this policy document goes hand in hand with the intended increase in the use of wood as a construction material. In fact, by 2035, up to ¼ of all new buildings for family housing buildings by 2035 should use wood as a primary construction material. The other objective is to increase the percentage of wood used in public buildings and refurbishment projects.
Document Title: Czech Wood Policy

Family Name: National Heat Protection Plan (2024)
Family Summary: The national heat protection plan describes measures that are taken at a federal level in cooperation with the federal states and GeoSphere Austria during a extreme heat event, particularly during longer-lasting heat waves. This creates a framework for additional steps at state, regional and local levels in order to best protect the population living in Austria from the health effects of extream heat.The national heat protection plan is therefore a guide for the actions of the ministry responsible for health and other authorities and organizations. These includes health facilities and social organizations at state or municipal level, which will find references to tools and international good practices for further measures. This heat protection plan is regularly evaluated taking into account new scientific findings and adapted if necessary. In this respect, it should be viewed as a living document.
Document Title: National Heat Protection Plan (2024)

Family Name: Seychelles Civil Aviation Authority Act, 2024
Family Summary: The Seychelles Civil Aviation Authority Act, 2024, regulates and provides for the continuation of the Seychelles Civil Aviation Authority. Among the core functions of the authority, the act promotes the establishment and enforcement of environmental sustainability regulations, which it defines such that this includes carbon emissions.
Document Title: Seychelles Civil Aviation Authority Act, 2024

Family Name: Programme for Promoting Green and Circular Economy in the Republic of Moldova 2024-2028
Family Summary: Moldova's Programme for Promoting Green and Circular Economy (2024-2028) aims to mainstream environmental sustainability and circularity across sectors, with emphases on resilient agriculture and decarbonisation of the economy. Other elements of the incorporated action plan include eco-industrial parks for the development and implementation of sustainable technology; institution of new financial instruments such as green bonds; campaigns to influence consumer behaviour; and aims to continue adopting European Union environmental legislation, especially on waste management and energy efficiency.
Document Title: Programme for Promoting Green and Circular Economy in the Republic of Moldova 2024-2028

Family Name: Multiannual Sectoral Strategic Plan (PESEM) for the environmental sector 2024-2030 [Plan Estratégico Sectorial Multianual (PESEM) del sector ambiental 2024 – 2030]
Family Summary: Peru's Ministerial Resolution No. 105-2024-MINAM approves the Multi-Annual Strategic Sectoral Plan for the environmental sector 2024-2030, establishing the strategic framework for environmental governance across national, regional and local government entities within Peru's National Environmental Management System. The Plan articulates six strategic sectoral objectives that directly address climate change mitigation and adaptation whilst advancing the energy transition: reducing biodiversity degradation and ecosystem service loss; controlling environmental pollution across air, water and soil components; strengthening the transition to a circular economy with enhanced solid waste management; reducing climate risks and greenhouse gas emissions in alignment with Peru's Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris Agreement; improving decentralised environmental governance with territorial focus; and enhancing citizens' environmental behaviour. Of particular significance for climate action, Strategic Objective 4 explicitly addresses both adaptation and mitigation dimensions through measures to strengthen climate resilience of populations and ecosystems, implement sectoral GHG reduction strategies, and enhance climate risk monitoring and forecasting systems. The Plan operationalises Peru's commitments under the UNFCCC, the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and broader sustainable development objectives, whilst responding to recommendations from the Environmental Performance Review and supporting Peru's OECD accession process.
Document Title: Multiannual Sectoral Strategic Plan (PESEM) for the environmental sector 2024-2030 [Plan Estratégico Sectorial Multianual (PESEM) del sector ambiental 2024 – 2030]

Family Name: Climate Neutrality Roadmap

Family Name: Italy Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. Following feedback from an EU-wide assessment of draft NECP submissions, EU members are required to submit updated final NECPs for the period 2021-2030. The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness.

The plan establishes key objectives: 1) to accelerate the transition from traditional fuels to renewable sources by promoting the gradual phasing out of coal for electricity generation in favour of an electricity mix based on a growing share of renewables; 2) to implement policies and measures in order to reduce greenhouse gases (phase out of coal, higher CO2 price, acceleration of renewables and energy efficiency in manufacturing); 3) to use a mix of fiscal, economic, regulatory and policy instruments to enhance energy efficiency; 4) to reduce dependence on imports by increasing renewable sources and energy efficiency and to diversify sources of supply through the use of natural gas, including liquefied natural gas (LNG); 5) to ensure a greater degree of market integration and the development of processes, products and knowledge for the use of renewables, energy efficiency and network technology. In the updated final plan, some general targets have been slightly reduced (i.e. the non-ETS emissions reduction target decreased from 30% to a 29.3% reduction) due to the COVID-19 pandemic and energy supply shocks.
Document Title: Italy Updated Final National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030

This Plan represents NDMA's proactive response to the escalating threat of heatwaves.

By addressing meteorological, climatological, and socio-economic dimensions, the plan aims to enhance country's resilience to heat-related disasters while advancing climate adaptation and mitigation objectives. NDMA's Tech team focuses on monitoring and analyzing global and local indicators of potential heatwaves, issues heatwave projections with a lead time of 3-6-month and calculates potential impacts, vulnerabilities and exposure with remarkable accuracy.

Family Name: The Master Plan for Electricity  2023 – 2032
Family Summary: The Master Plan for Electricity 2023–2032 serves as a strategic policy framework to ensure Ecuador's electricity supply meets national demand sustainably and efficiently over the next decade, in a current energetic crisis. Guided by constitutional principles, it prioritises renewable energy expansion, energy efficiency, and infrastructure modernisation to support a transition toward a clean and resilient energy matrix. This plan outlines objectives and strategies for electricity generation, transmission, distribution, public lighting, and regional projects, including a specialised focus on the Galápagos Islands.The plan highlights Ecuador's commitment to diversifying its energy matrix through renewable energy sources like hydropower, green hydrogen, and distributed generation technologies. It incorporates climate resilience measures, integrating risk management for natural, anthropogenic, and climate-related threats. By aligning with the National Development Plan and global sustainability goals, the plan addresses the challenges posed by climate change, emphasising decarbonization and energy security. According to this policy, investment from public and private sectors is integral to achieving its goals, promoting a sustainable energy future while ensuring equitable access to electricity for all citizens, including those in remote regions.
Document Title: Master Plan for Electricity  2023 – 2032

Family Name: 2024 Integrated System Plan
Family Summary:
The Integrated System Plan (ISP) is a 25-year roadmap to transition the National Electricity Market (NEM) to net zero by 2050, released by the Australian Energy Market Operator. The Plan confirms that renewable energy connected with transmission and distribution, firmed with storage and backed up by gas-powered generation, is the lowest-cost way to supply electricity to homes and businesses as Australia transitions to a net zero economy.

The Plan identifies almost 10,000km of new transmission lines are required by 2050 to connect new sources of generation and meet reliability targets at the lowest cost to consumers. Five projects, or 2,500 km, are already underway as committed and anticipated projects. The plan identifies a further 12 projects that are actionable and should continue through planning and delivery.

Crucial technologies factored into the roadmap are domestic rooftop solar panels and associated batteries, smart systems and electric vehicles, also known as consumer energy resources. Home batteries, if well-coordinated, can save consumers around $4.1 billion in avoided costs for additional grid-scale investment.
Document Title: 2024 Integrated System Plan

The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness.

The plan establishes the following objectives: 1) reduction of greenhouse gas emissions with renewable energy and energy saving; 2) combating climate change with a climate-neutral electricity system. The limited availability of renewable sources in the Netherlands is an important point of concern. Since the Netherlands is located along the coast and the wind is relatively strong, and this offers potential for wind energy on land and offshore; 3) a transition to an emission-free mobility system that involves sustainable energy carriers (electricity, biofuels and green hydrogen); 4) homes and other building will be made more energy-efficient in a sustainable transformation of the built-up environment; 5) to promote a robust and sustainable agriculture which adopts a more efficient approach to raw materials and the environment. By 2030 this plan aims for a 60% reduction in net greenhouse gas emissions, as an 'overprogramming' measure to ensure the EU-wide 55% reduction goal is achieved or surpassed nationally.

Family Name: Sustainable Finance Taxonomy
Family Summary:
This Taxonomy is a classification system that defines eligibility criteria and indicators to identify economic activities that contribute to the transition towards a sustainable, resilient and inclusive economy of the country. It is aligned with the 2021 Green Bond Principles, 2021 Social Bond Principles, and the Sustainable Bond Guide, published by the International Capital Market Association (ICMA).

This Taxonomy covers: nine sectors: Agriculture, livestock and forestry; water supply and treatment; manufacturing, waste management and emission capture; supply of electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning; construction; transport; information and communications technology; and financial and insurance activities.

This Taxonomy is the result of a joint effort led by the Panama Sustainable Finance Task Force (GTFS), the Superintendency of Banks of Panama (SBP), the Superintendency of the Securities Market of Panama (SMV), and the Superintendency of Insurance and Reinsurance of Panama (SSRP), in close collaboration with the Ministry of Environment (MiAmbiente) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), and with the technical support of the United Nations Environment Programme Finance Initiative (UNEP FI), and the financial support of the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and the European Union, through its EUROCLIMA program.

Family Name: Agricultural Agreement on a Green Denmark
Family Summary:
The Government and the parties in the Green Tripartite (Agriculture Food, the Danish Nature Conservation Association, the Danish Food Association NNF, Danish Metal, the Confederation of Danish Industry, etc.) have agreed on a long-term basis for the conversion and transformation of Denmark's land and food and agricultural production. The efforts in the agreement will reduce the sector's greenhouse gas emissions and contribute to meeting Denmark's 2030 climate goals, as well as ensuring better conditions for nature, biodiversity, the aquatic environment and drinking water. This will include a historic land conversion and a tax on emissions from livestock. At the same time, the agreement sets the direction for a more sustainable, high-tech and land-efficient agriculture with competitiveness and good jobs throughout the country.

With the agreement, the parties agree that a CO2e tax on emissions from livestock will be introduced. A tax of DKK 300 per ton CO2e will be introduced in 2030, increasing to DKK 750 per ton CO2e in 2035 with a base deduction of 60 percent. The effective tax will therefore amount to DKK 120 per ton CO2e in 2030, increasing to DKK 300 per ton CO2e in 2035. tons of CO2e in 2035. In addition, a good 30 billion kroner will be allocated for the removal of a total of approximately 140,000 ha of carbon-rich lowland soils including marginal areas and the establishment of 250,000 ha of forest. In addition, a subsidy scheme of a total of just over 10 billion kroner will be established towards 2045 for the storage of biochar produced by pyrolysis.

Overall, the efforts in the agreement are estimated to reduce Danish emissions by 1.8 million tons of CO2e in 2030. The agreement thus closes the gap in relation to the 2030 climate target.
Document Title: Agricultural Agreement on a Green Denmark

Family Name: Agreement on a Green Denmark (2024)
Family Summary:
In the summer of 2024, the parties behind the Green Tripartite entered into the historic Agreement on a Green Denmark, which is to ensure more nature, cleaner water and a sustainable transformation of agriculture. Later that year, the SVM government made the political agreement  Implementation of a Green Denmark  with the SF, Liberal Alliance, the Conservative People's Party and the Radical Left, which ensures broad support for the implementation of the tripartite agreement. The agreements are among the most ambitious green agreements in Danish history, and they are agreements that are not only about environmental improvements, but also about ensuring that Denmark can continue to be a pioneer in the green transition.

The agreements have been concluded by the government together with a number of political parties and organizations in the Green Tripartite, including:

  • The government, as well as the SF, the Danish Social Democratic Party, the Liberal Alliance and the Conservative People's Party
  • The National Association of Municipalities (KL)
  • Agriculture Food
  • Danish Nature Conservation Society
  • The Norwegian Food Federation (NNF)
  • Danish Metal
  • Danish Industry

The broad support must ensure that the agreement takes into account nature, the climate and the industries affected by the changes.

The agreements involve a comprehensive restructuring of Denmark's land area and a number of initiatives to protect the environment and reduce climate impact. The most important elements are:

  • 250,000 hectares of new forest, equivalent to the areas of Lolland, Falster and Bornholm combined.
  • Conversion of 140,000 hectares of low-lying agricultural land that emits a lot of CO 2 when cultivated. Some of this land will be converted to nature instead.
  • More biodiversity, including through the creation of 21 new national nature parks, one urban national nature park and improvement of the marine environment in the Little Belt and Øresund.
  • Strengthened efforts for the aquatic environment to reduce oxygen depletion in Danish fjords and coastal areas.
  • CO2 tax on livestock production: Denmark will be the first country in the world to introduce this type of tax. 
  • Forward-looking, competitive and sustainable Danish food production with increased focus on biosolutions, climate technologies and plant-based foods.
  • 43 billion kroner to Danmarks Grønne Arealfond, which will finance green initiatives.
  • 23 local tripartite partnerships, where municipalities, the state and representatives from Agriculture Food and the Danish Nature Conservation Association collaborate to convert agricultural areas to nature.
Document Title: Agreement on the Implementation of a Green Denmark (2024)

Family Summary: The Decree of 19 June 2024 (RES 2 Decree) is a strategic regulatory framework designed to incentivise innovative renewable energy technologies or those with high generation costs that are not yet market-competitive. The decree provides a 20-year support system for offshore wind, floating solar, geothermal, and wave energy through a combination of direct feed-in tariffs and competitive electronic auctions managed by the GSE. Unlike the earlier RES 1 Decree (2019), which focuses on onshore wind and traditional PV, RES 2 Decree is specifically tailored to bridge the industrial gap for next-generation green tech. In the 2026 context, the decree includes a 3% annual reduction in reference tariffs to encourage early adoption and ensure that Italy meets its 2030 decarbonization targets by diversifying its energy mix beyond established renewables.

This collection is made up by documents that relate to Colombia's fair energy transition. 
The Fair Energy Transition is a key process in the fight against climate change, involving the transformation of current energy systems to one based on a low-GHG emitter, having fairer and more sustainable model. 
Colombia's green and fair energy transition strategy seeks to pursue descarbonisation in a way that takes into account paramount elements such as (i) equity and social, environmental and energy justice; (ii) graduality and sovereignty while pursuing the progressive replacement of the current matrix with a cleaner and more efficient one; (iii) social participation; and, (iv) knowledgeable to create economic alternatives.
Family Name: Just Energy Transition Roadmap
Family Summary: The Roadmap for a Just Energy Transition (TEJ in Spanish) provides guidelines for Colombia's transition from an energy matrix based mainly on fossil fuels to one supported mainly by renewable energies, taking into account conditions of binding participation, recognition of multiple knowledge, energy democratisation, and prevention and mitigation of social and environmental damage.The Roadmap firstly presents a full diagnosis of the Fair Energy Transition in Colombia. This diagnosis report is structured into six chapters, covering global energy transition trends, Colombia's current energy system, challenges of its fossil fuel-dependent economy, and the legal framework for the transition. It concludes with key challenges for the transition roadmap, informed by territorial and business dialogues conducted by the Ministry of Mines and Energy across the country. The roadmap is also supported by a bundle of analytical and scenario-based documents: 1 - A central component of this Roadmap consists of the construction of scenarios that incorporate the different Just Energy Transition proposals put forward by the National Government and try to explore potential possible futures in order to make decisions. It presents scenarios of the future development of the different economic sectors, making assumptions about the mechanisms and speeds of implementation of various public policies aimed at reducing GHG emissions, reducing fossil fuel consumption, reindustrialisation, the use of non-conventional renewable energy sources 2- Another document - the Sub-national energy potential and opportunities for decarbonisation in final energy use - aims to identify the production potential of Non-Conventional Renewable Energy Sources (NCRE), (wind, solar, bioenergy, geothermal, hydroelectricity and green hydrogen) and look at the available decarbonisation alternatives.3- The third document named 'Challenge and Opportunities' tries to consider main challenges and develop strategies that favour the implementation of the energy transition with a social, environmental, energy and climate justice perspective 4- The investments assessment presents the costs for the different energy scenarios projected for both energy supply and demand.

This Decree implements the plan provided for in Article 34 of Law No. 2023-973 of October 23, 2023 relating to the green industry.
Document Title: Decree No. 2024-548 of June 15, 2024 on the implementation of the future climate savings plan

Family Name: GD no. 425/2024 on the organization and operation of the National Commission on Climate Change
Family Summary: GD no. 425/2024 defines and regulates the functions of the National Commission on Climate Change. It establishes the main objectives of the commission - to promote cross-sectoral cooperation, mainstream climate considerations in new policy, co-ordinate climate mitigation/adaptation funding streams, and ensure transparent dialogue with the public. This decision also defines the ministerial composition of the commission, and its powers and rights.
Document Title: GD no. 425/2024 on the organization and operation of the National Commission on Climate Change

Family Name: National Family Farming Plan 2024-2028
Family Summary:
The National Family Farming Plan of Uruguay is adopted within the framework of the United Nations’ Decade of Family Farming (2019-2028) and FAO’s and FIDA’s Worldwide Action Plan. This document will guide policies from 2024 to 2028, emphasizing the crucial role that family farming plays in various value chains across the country. After providing the background (legal and institutional framework for family farming) and assessing the current situation and its challenges, the plan outlines strategies for the 2024-2028 period, including implementation strategies such as monitoring, governance, and evaluation.

The National Family Farming Plan (PNAF) is organized around the following key pillars: 1) Legal and institutional framework; 2) Youth; 3) Gender; 4) Organizations; 5) Socioeconomic inclusion and well-being; 6) Sustainability, environment, and climate change; 7) Territory and multidimensionality.

Pillar 6, focusing on Sustainability, Environment, and Climate Change, includes specific actions such as integrating family farming into medium and long-term water sector strategies and addressing its needs; developing risk management tools for family farming; institutionalizing the climate change and family farming perspective in the General Directorate of Rural Development (DGDR); creating methodological guides for systematically including family farming in climate change plans and programs; raising awareness in the family farming sector about biodiversity and related regulations; and coordinating the implementation of both the PNAF and the National Agroecology Plan.
Document Title: National Family Farming Plan 2024-2028

Family Name: Free Electricity Scheme (PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana)
Family Summary: The "PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana" programme aims to provide solar rooftop systems to 10 million households by March 2027. The plan offers subsidies of up to 60% for systems up to 2kW and 40% for 2-3kW systems. The programme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in February 2024. As of January 27, 2025, the scheme has achieved significant progress, with 846,000 households installing rooftop solar systems under the programme.
Document Title: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana - Redefining Solar Power and Energy Access

Family Name: Corporate Average Fuel Economy Standards for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks (CAFE)
Family Summary: This rule by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) establishes Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) standards for passenger cars and light trucks that increase at a rate of 2 percent per year for passenger cars in model years (MYs) 2027-31, 0 percent per year for light trucks in model years 2027-28, and 2 percent per year for light trucks in model years 2029-31. NHTSA is also finalizing fuel efficiency standards for heavy-duty pickup trucks and vans (HDPUVs) for model years 2030-32 that increase at a rate of 10 percent per year and model years 2033-35 that increase at a rate of 8 percent per year.In January 2025, the NHTSA secretary sent a memorandum to NHTSA to review and reconsider this policy, per Trump's executive orders.

Family Name: Decree 12.041/2024 on the Resilient Green Cities Programme
Family Summary: This Decree from the President establishes the Resilient Green Cities Programme (PCVR), to increase the environmental quality and resilience of Brazilian cities in the face of the impacts caused by climate change, by integrating urban, environmental and climate policies, encouraging sustainable practices and valuing the ecosystem services of urban greenery. The PCVR's actions focus on the population of urban areas, observing the criteria of diversity of gender, race, ethnicity, age, disability, income and location in the territory, and will prioritise metropolitan regions and municipalities with high social and climate vulnerability.

Family Name: Magey Saafu Raajje National Waste & Resource Management Policy and Strategy 2024–2028
Family Summary:
This Policy outlines a comprehensive framework for implementing a sustainable solid waste management system in the Maldives, to minimise the negative impact of waste on the environment, climate and public health. lt aims to consolidate existing waste management projects under a unified framework, enhancing efficiency and effectiveness while integrating with other national policies related to protecting human health and environment. Central to the policy is the promotion of a circular economy, encouraging the reuse and recycling of materials to minimise waste generation, including the phasing out of single-use plastics. The policy introduces Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) mechanisms that will establish responsibilities at all levels of the production and consumption chain, including producers, importers, traders, and consumers, and is based on the polluter's pay principle, where the costs of waste management must be borne by the waste producer or by the legal entity managing waste on behalf of others.

To foster consumer behavioural change and community engagement, the policy emphasises increasing sustainable waste management practices through education and awareness campaigns, engaging citizens, communities, schools, NGOs, and other stakeholders in waste management efforts. In addition, by utilising waste as a resource, the policy seeks to drive socio-economic growth and development, creating green jobs and promoting sustainable economic activities. Investments in waste management infrastructure and the adoption of advanced technologies are prioritised. Public-private partnerships are encouraged to enhance collaborative efforts between the government, private sector, and civil society.
Document Title: Magey Saafu Raajje National Waste & Resource Management Policy and Strategy 2024–2028

Family Summary: The resolution aims to enhance Uzbekistan's response to global climate issues by beginning the creation of a national system for monitoring, recording and verification (MRV) of emissions reductions, alongside a national emissions inventory. This includes compiling comprehensive emissions data for the 1990-2023 period.
Document Title: On Measures to Implement a National System of Transparency in the Transition to a Green Economy in the Republic of Uzbekistan PP-213

Family Name: Decree No. 12.044 establishing the National Bioeconomy Strategy
Family Summary: Brazil adopted the "Pathways to a Sustainable Bioeconomy" policy through Decree No. 12,044 on June 5, 2024, establishing the National Bioeconomy Strategy to coordinate and implement public policies for sustainable economic development based on the conservation and regeneration of biodiversity, with the creation of the National Bioeconomy Commission and a National Bioeconomy Development Plan as key instruments.
Document Title: Decree No. 12,044, of June 5, 2024 – Institutes the National Bioeconomy Strategy

Family Name: Green Taxonomy
Family Summary:
The Green Taxonomy of the Dominican Republic (TVRD) is a classification system of economic and asset activities that contribute substantially to the achievement of environmental and/or social objectives, aligning with the commitments, strategies and policies outlined by the country. The TVRD acts as a reference framework that seeks to promote initiatives that support both sustainable development and the transition to a low-carbon economy.

The beginning of taxonomy work began in 2020 with the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MOU) between the International Financial Corporation (IFC) of the World Bank group and the Superintendence of the Securities Market where the action plan was worked to address the taxonomy development project.

The TVRD covers economic ativities that contribute to the environmental objectives of climate change mitigation and adaptation, the sustainable use and protection of water and coastal-marine resources and economic sectors of greater relevance: water and water resources, waste management and emission capture, transport, energy, construction and industry.
Document Title: Green Taxonomy

Family Name: Education Strategic Plan 2024-2028
Family Summary: This Plan includes actions to enhance climate resilience infrastructure, healthcare and safety practices in response to disasters related to climate change and relevant teacher training in schools including in preschools and childcare centres.
Document Title: Education Strategic Plan 2024-2028

Family Name: National Water Sector Strategy (2024-2035)
Family Summary: Lebanon's National Water Sector Strategy (2024-2035) emphasises the importance of enhancing resilience to climate change in the country's water systems. By 2035 he strategy aims to: increase storage capacity; introduce a comprehensive digital monitoring system for national water usage and resources; increase hydropower production capacity by 15%; expand access and public management of water and wastewater systems; achieve a 30% energy cost reduction in the water sector through efficiency measures; and promote stronger governance in the water sector. Further adaptation-related measures include setting up a water resilience research program, and a stormwater management plan due to the increased incidence of extreme rainfall events under climate change.
Document Title: National Water Sector Strategy (2024-2035)

Family Name: Roadmap for energy efficiency
Family Summary:
The energy efficiency efforts contribute to supporting a better balance between the renewable energy that is being produced and the energy that consumers demand. This development will result in great demands for a more digital, efficient and integrated energy system where the energy consumption is electrified - which is more energy efficient compared to fossil fuels. At the same time, the energy must be used flexibly at all stages so that energy consumption can increasingly be managed based on the production of renewable energy. This requires that the energy efficiency efforts are put into a framework based on a systemic understanding of how much, when, and which kind of energy is produced. It is therefore necessary for energy efficiency to be thought of as more than just energy savings - energy efficiency should instead be viewed as a number of supporting measures. The purpose is to support the overall energy system.

Energy efficiency is to be framed as a collective term wherein energy behaviour and energy renovations, electrification, conversions and surplus heat, and flexibility supported by digitalisation and competencies contribute together to ensuring that we get the most out of the overall energy system.
Document Title: Roadmap for energy efficiency

Family Name: Expansion and Modernization Programs for the National Transmission Network and the Elements of the General Distribution Networks of the Wholesale Electricity Market (PAMRNT) 2024-2038 [Programas de Ampliación y Modernización de la Red Nacional de Transmisión y de los elementos de las Redes Generales de Distribución del Mercado Eléctrico Mayorista (PAMRNT) 2024 - 2038]
Family Summary: This policy document details programmes for the expansion and modernisation of Mexico's National Transmission Network (RNT) and General Distribution Networks (RGD) associated with the Wholesale Electricity Market. It operates within the context of the country's Energy Reform, with the Ministry of Energy (SENER) and the National Energy Control Centre (CENACE) coordinating efforts to ensure the efficiency, quality, reliability, continuity, and security of the National Electricity System (SEN). The overarching aim is to strategically plan and develop grid infrastructure, integrating demand forecasts and generation capacity plans. A key objective is to facilitate the increased integration and utilisation of clean energies, thereby modernising the electricity sector to support national development and meet evolving energy policy objectives.The policy significantly emphasises climate change mitigation and adaptation. It supports Mexico's international commitments, such as the Paris Agreement, by promoting the transition to a higher proportion of clean energy in electricity generation, projected to increase to 61.41% by 2038. This involves planning for new capacity from renewable sources and energy storage, alongside measures aimed at reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through fuel substitution and grid efficiency improvements. The policy also incorporates strategies for enhanced resilience, such as ensuring flexible generation to counter the impact of climate events on variable renewable sources. Furthermore, it acknowledges the influence of climate phenomena, like heat waves, on electricity demand patterns and system reliability, and promotes electromobility as a key strategy for reducing transport sector emissions, integrating considerations for the broader energy transition.
Document Title: Programs for the Expansion and Modernization of the National Transmission Network and the elements of the General Distribution Networks that correspond to the Wholesale Electricity Market - PAMRNT 2024 - 2037 (Programas de Ampliación y Modernización de la Red Nacional de Transmisión y de los elementos de las Redes Generales de Distribución que correspondan al Mercado Eléctrico Mayorista - PAMRNT 2024 - 2037)

Family Name: Action Plan for Low-Carbon Transformation and Construction of Coal Power Plants (2024-2027)
Family Summary:
This action plan has been formulated to coordinate the low-carbon transformation of existing coal-fired power units and the low-carbon construction of new coal-fired power units, improve the clean and efficient use of coal, accelerate the construction of a new clean, low-carbon, safe and efficient energy system, and contribute to the achievement of carbon peak and carbon neutrality goals.

By 2025, all of the first batch of low-carbon coal-fired power transformation and construction projects will have commenced, and a number of low-carbon coal-fired power generation technologies will have been converted and applied. The carbon emissions per kilowatt-hour of these projects will be approximately 20% lower than the average carbon emissions of similar coal-fired power units in 2023, significantly lower than the carbon emissions of currently operating advanced coal-fired power units, and thus explore useful experience for the clean and low-carbon transformation of coal-fired power. By 2027, the technology routes for low-carbon coal-fired power generation will be further expanded, and construction and operation costs will be significantly reduced. The carbon emissions per kilowatt-hour of related projects will be reduced by about 50% compared with the average carbon emissions level of similar coal-fired power units in 2023, and close to the carbon emissions level of natural gas power generation units, forming a strong leading and driving role in the clean and low-carbon transformation of coal-fired power. Transformation methods include biomass co-firing, green ammonia co-firing and carbon capture, utilisation and storage.
Document Title: Action Plan for Low-Carbon Transformation and Construction of Coal Power Plants (2024-2027)

Family Name: Government funding for Fuel Cell Vehicles Demonstration projects
Family Summary: The Chinese government earmarked specific funding for fuel cell vehicle (FCV) demonstration projects in 2024, aiming to accelerate the development and commercialization of FCVs in the country. This decision builds upon previous support programs and is designed to encourage city alliances to develop hydrogen and fuel cell value chains, with five regions selected as the first batch of demonstrators: Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong, Hebei, and Henan.
Document Title: Government funding for Fuel Cell Vehicles Demonstration projects

Family Name: Least Cost Power Development Pathway (2024-2043)
Family Summary: Long-term electricity sector planning framework that forecasts electricity demand and determines least-cost expansion of generation, transmission, and distribution capacity. The plan prioritises renewable energy technologies and aims to balance system reliability with affordability and climate considerations. The newest iteration includes additional considerations such as system flexibility measures (e.g. battery storage, pumped hydro), emerging demand from electric cooking and mobility, and assesses modular nuclear as a long-term option.
Document Title: Least Cost Power Development Pathway (2024-2043)

Family Name: White paper on floods and landslides (Meld. St. 27 2023-2024)
Family Summary:
This white paper covers the actions to be taken in relation to floods and landslides, including:

  1. Mapping;
  2. Spatial planning - prevention in new settlements;
  3. Safety measures against floods and landslides;
  4. Monitoring and notification;
  5. Emergency preparedness and crisis management;
  6. Watercourse regulation and flood control;
  7. Stormwater;
  8. Transport and other important infrastructure;
  9. Agriculture; and
  10. Knowledge, research and dissemination.
Document Title: White paper on floods and landslides (Meld. St. 27 2023-2024)

Family Name: Agricultural Agreement 2024 (Prop. 105 S (2023-2024))
Family Summary:
This Agreement was entered into between the state, the Norwegian Farmers' Association and the Norwegian Farmers' and Small Farmers' Association on 16 May 2024, and subsequently approved by Parliament. One of the policy areas is climate, nature and the environment. It was agreed that the agricultural agreement will be turned in a more climate- and environmentally-friendly direction, and will contribute to maintaining the cultural landscape and to reducing the environmental impact from agriculture, including emissions to air and water.

Actions include:

  • Follow-up of the climate agreement between the state and agricultural organizations by strengthening the knowledge base on climate measures, measures that contribute to reduced emissions, increased absorption and better climate adaptation, including increased support for drainage, biogas and other fertilizer measures and hydrotechnical facilities.
  • Follow-up of the Comprehensive Action Plan for the Oslo Fjord with strengthening of grant funds to stimulate the implementation of runoff reduction measures.
  • Follow-up of the government's focus on nature through grazing schemes, pasture subsidies and other schemes that contribute to maintaining and improving the values ​​of the agricultural cultural landscape.
  • A significant investment in fruit and vegetables.
Document Title: Agricultural Agreement 2024 (Prop. 105 S (2023-2024))

Family Name: National Electric System Development Program 2024-2038 (Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional 2024-2038)
Family Summary: The National Electric System Development Program (PRODESEN) 2024-2038 is one of the Mexico’s principal public policy instrument for the annual planning of the National Electric System (SEN) over a fifteen-year horizon, aligned with the National Development Plan (PND) 2019–2024 and embodying the current government’s energy policy objectives in the electricity sector. It integrates key components from related planning frameworks, such as the Indicative Programme for the Installation and Retirement of Power Plants (PIIRCE), and the expansion and modernisation programmes for the National Transmission Network (RNT) and General Distribution Networks (RGD). The PRODESEN prioritises the role of the state-owned Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) in generation, transmission, and distribution, with plans to develop new power plants, rehabilitate and modernise hydroelectric facilities, and enhance system reliability, efficiency, and affordability.In terms of climate change and energy transition, the PRODESEN is underpinned by Mexico’s commitments to international environmental agreements, including the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the Paris Agreement, and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, with a focus on reducing GHG emissions and promoting sustainable energy practices. It outlines a structured approach to increasing clean and renewable energy generation, emphasising the gradual and orderly integration of these sources into the energy mix, supported by necessary grid infrastructure development. The programme also highlights energy efficiency, electromobility, and the expansion of electricity access to rural and marginalised urban areas, aligning energy policy with environmental protection and sustainable development goals, while ensuring system stability and economic viability.
Document Title: Prodesen 2024-2038

Family Name: Urban Green Space Act (Act No. 72 of 1982)
Family Summary: The amendment of 29 May 2024 to the Act establishes a certification system for urban development projects that contributes to urban decarbonisation by creating green spaces, introducing renewable energy, and making efficient use of energy, etc. (Articles 87 to 94). Family Name: Decree 2.553/2024 - Energy Policy of the Republic of Paraguay to 2050
Family Summary:
Decree 2.553/2024 repealed decree 6092/2016 and approved the new Energy Policy of the Republic of Paraguay to 2050.

The vision of this new policy is to consolidate an energy matrix that meets the country's needs, with sustainable use and exploitation of national natural resources and energy, within a framework of regional integration, as an essential element of the comprehensive development of the entire population and the productive and social sectors.

The policy outlines five main goals for the energy sector:

  1. Sustainable and resilient energy supply – Ensure a reliable energy system that supports the population’s well-being and economic development, prioritizing the use of national energy and mining resources.
  2. Leverage energy sector strengths – Use the sector’s competitive advantages to drive socio-economic growth, energy transition, job creation, and global integration.
  3. Regional energy hub – Position the country as a central player in regional energy integration.
  4. Equitable energy access – Guarantee affordable, safe, and sustainable energy for vulnerable groups.
  5. Active participation of stakeholders – Strengthen the role of consumers and other key actors in shaping the energy sector.
Document Title: Decree 2.553/2024 - Energy Policy of the Republic of Paraguay to 2050

Family Name: Methodological Guide For Quantifying Budgetary Risks Related To Natural Disasters
Family Summary: Natural disasters stemming from climate change are an increasingly frequent and costly phenomenon in Niger, significantly undermining the country’s economic performance and putting a heavy strain on its public finances. The purpose of the new methodological guide is to provide detailed instructions for quantifying these climate-related natural disaster fiscal risks. Its goal is to answer a crucial question: What are the potential impacts that future disasters could have on key budgetary aggregates, such as government revenue, expenditure, and even debt, in the coming years?
Document Title: Methodological Guide For Quantifying Budgetary Risks Related To Natural Disasters

Family Name: National Biomethane Strategy
Family Summary:
This Strategy has been developed by the Irish government to meet its commitment to deliver up to 5.7 TWh (which is 10% of the national gas demand) of indigenously produced biomethane by 2030. It envisions that, by 2030, Ireland will have developed a sustainable biomethane industry of scale.

This Strategy covers, amongst other sections, the government funding and policy to support biomethane production, including a Renewable Heat Obligation (RHO) and capital grant support; industry investment in biomethane, including through Gas Purchase Agreements (GPA) and the EU Emissions Trading Schedule; the sustainability of biomethane production; and enhancing alignment between biomethane, biodiversity and the bioeconomy.
Document Title: National Biomethane Strategy

Family Name: Roadmap to a circular economy in water and sanitation by 2030 (Hoja de Ruta hacia una economía circular en agua y saneamiento al 2030)
Family Summary: Peru’s 2030 Roadmap for a Circular Economy in Water and Sanitation (Hoja de Ruta AS), stewarded by the Ministry of Housing, Construction and Sanitation, sets out a sector-wide shift from the prevailing linear model towards closed-loop management of water, energy and residuals. Framed by the National Competitiveness and Productivity Policy and consistent with earlier circular-economy roadmaps for industry, fisheries and agriculture, the document adopts the forthcoming ISO 59004 definition of circularity. It places climate change at the centre of sectoral planning: utilities must draw up mitigation-and-adaptation plans, embed disaster-risk actions in their Optimised Master Plans and tariff reviews, and comply with national risk-management norms, recognising that nine out of ten climate-related disasters are water-borne.
Document Title: Roadmap to a circular economy in water and sanitation by 2030 (Hoja de Ruta hacia una economía circular en agua y saneamiento al 2030)

Family Name: Decree 143/2024
Family Summary: It is established that the creation of the Trust Fund is based on the need and convenience of advancing energy transition, particularly in the implementation of public policies that encourage sustainable mobility to contribute to meeting the commitments to mitigate climate change. It regulates the article 584 of the Law 20212/2023 bringing details about the Trust fund and the payments for the bus fleet operators. The Executive Power, through various ministries (Transport and Public Works, Industry, Energy and Mining, and Economy and Finance), will annually establish reimbursement values for electric buses incorporated into the fleet after the enactment of Law 20212/2023.
Document Title: Decree 143/2024

Family Name: Climate Change Mitigation Strategy and Action Plan 2024-2030
Family Summary:
This document aims to present a roadmap on climate response covering the period until 2030 and includes the relevant strategies and action plans in this regard. Built on a scientific basis, it offers a comprehensive approach by bringing together institutional policies, expert views, and GHG reduction needs. It includes 49 strategies and 260 actions covering GHG reduction policies in energy, industry, buildings, transport, waste, agriculture, and land use, land use change and forestry (LULUCF) sectors as well as in areas of carbon pricing mechanisms and just transition.

The key sectoral strategies in the Action Plan, which comprises 49 strategies and 260 actions for 7 main mitigation sectors and 2 cross-cutting thematic areas, include:

● Promoting energy efficiency across all sectors,

● Maximising the use of renewable energy,

● Reducing product-based carbon footprint and carbon intensity in industry,

● Promoting sustainability reporting,

● Promoting circular economy and resource efficiency across the manufacturing industry,

● Promoting Nearly Zero Energy buildings,

● Promoting the use of district heating and cooling systems,

● Developing electrification systems in the transport sector,

● Developing integrated transport systems,

● Ensuring transition to zero- or low-emission transport systems,

● Protecting and increasing sink areas for effective climate response,

● Ensuring transition of forestry and agricultural enterprises to circular bioeconomy with high added value,

● Extending eco-friendly agricultural practices,

● Ensuring rational fertiliser use,

● Reducing methane emissions originating from livestock,

● Preventing and reducing waste generation,

● Increasing use of waste as raw material/resource in production,

● Establishing an emissions trading system in Türkiye,

● Conducting infrastructure studies on other carbon pricing mechanisms,

● Developing and promoting clean technologies,

● Achieving digitalization in all sectors,

● Developing incentive and support mechanisms for GHG reduction,

● Developing sustainable investment instruments,

● Planning for transition to a low-carbon economy with the principle of just transition,

● Building capacity for just transition and employment transformation, and

● Integrating Türkiye’s net zero emission target into the education system.
Document Title: Climate Change Mitigation Strategy and Action Plan 2024-2030

Family Name: National Ecological Transition Strategy
Family Summary: Tunisia's National Ecological Transition Strategy aims to guide sustainable economic development across a wide range of sectors while preserving and restoring natural capital. The strategy underscores the need to adapt to climate change and reduce the carbon intensity of the economy. Among other measures, it promotes: development of climate-specific policies and the formation of government entities to oversee their implementation; creation of a national climate early warning system; intensification of reforestation efforts; substantial waste reductions across the economy; enhanced flood protection; sustainable urban mobility.
Document Title: National Ecological Transition Strategy

Family Name: Action Plan 2024-2027 of the Strategy for Agriculture and Rural Development of Georgia
Family Summary:
It is the Action Plan 2024-2027 of the Strategy for Agriculture and Rural Development of Georgia 2021-2027. The action plan is composed by 3 main objectives:

  • Competitiveness;
  • Sustainable use of natural resources, preservation of ecosystems, adaptation to climate change;
  • Effective food/feed safety;

In the environmental and climate objectives, the plan highlights as indicator, amongst others, the awareness raised about climate change and adaptation amongst farmers, and the integration of climate change and adaptation preparedness plan into the forest sector.
Document Title: Action Plan 2024-2027 of the Strategy for Agriculture and Rural Development of Georgia

Family Name: Climate Change (Carbon Markets) Regulations 2024
Family Summary: Establishes a formal legal framework for carbon markets in Kenya under the Climate Change Act, organising the certification, verification, and operation of carbon credit programmes, in addition to defining core principles such as additionality, permanence, and double counting. It aims to integrate sustainable development benefits, and enhance the transparency and market oversight of carbon credit activities, while taking environmental and social safeguards into account to support Kenya in meeting its climate commitments. It institutionalises a Designated National Authority responsible for overseeing transactions, compliance, and preventing double counting.
Document Title: Climate Change (Carbon Markets) Regulations 2024

Family Name: Strategy for Expanding Supply and Strengthening Supply Chain for Renewable Energy
Family Summary: The Strategy outlines key financial support programmes providing long-term low-interest loans for renewable energy production facilities and utilisation installations, and deployment support subsidising installation costs for renewable energy facilities in housing, buildings, and regions.
Document Title: Strategy for Expanding Supply and Strengthening Supply Chain for Renewable Energy

Family Name: Presidential Circular 2024/7 on Energy Efficiency
Family Summary:
Presidential Circular 2024/7 contains budget-saving and energy efficiency measures. It contains actions such as:

  • Purchasing electric vehicles when renewing public vehicles,
  • Not exceeding 1.6 lt engine capacity in internal combustion engine vehicles,
  • LED conversion in general lighting,
  • Implementation of energy saving measures specified in the “Public Buildings Savings Target and Implementation Guide”,
  • Implementation of applications (such as insulation) that increase energy efficiency in public buildings,
  • Utilising renewable energy sources (such as generating electricity from solar energy with photovoltaic panels),
  • Preferring energy-efficient projects/products with low energy consumption in public procurements.
Document Title: Presidential Circular 2024/7 on Energy Efficiency

Family Name: Future Made in Australia – National Interest Framework supporting paper
Family Summary:
This paper outlines the National Interest Framework that will guide how the Government will identify priority industries and how policy support will be designed to support the Government’s objectives through its Future Made in Australia agenda. Priority industries under the Future Made in Australia agenda fall into one of two streams:

  • the Net Zero Transformation Stream, which includes industries where Australia will have a comparative advantage as the global economy transitions to net zero
  • the Economic Resilience and Security Stream, which includes industries where some level of domestic capability is necessary to deliver economic resilience and security.
Document Title: Future Made in Australia – National Interest Framework supporting paper

Family Name: Circular of May 14, 2024, no. 22 - Updated Operational Guide for compliance with the principle of not causing significant harm to the environment (DNSH)
Family Summary: Under Article 18 of EU Regulation 241/2021, every reform and investment within a National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP) must strictly adhere to the "Do No Significant Harm" (DNSH) principle. To support government bodies and project leads in navigating these technical requirements, the State General Accounting Office (Ragioneria Generale dello Stato) issued Circular No. 22 of May 14, 2024, which introduces the third edition of the DNSH Operational Guide. The guide brings climate and energy-related requirements and checklists to be fulfilled. Essentially, Circular 22/2024 acts as the definitive technical manual for ensuring that Italy’s green transition investments are legally compliant and eligible for continued EU funding.
Document Title: Operational Guide to respect the DNSH Principle

Family Name: National Energy Policy from 2023 to 2030
Family Summary:
The overall vision of the National Energy Policy (NEP) is a modern, sustainable energy sector focused on energy security, cost minimisation, and local enfranchisement against the global climate change context. This vision will be achieved by transitioning to a more decarbonised economy characterized by affordable, secure, and sustainable energy services, with high levels of local participation, in order to achieve national prosperity. The NEP is intended to help Saint Lucia meet its nationally determined commitment (NDC) under the Paris Agreement.

The following are the NEP’s seven goals for the energy sector by 2030:

  1. Ensure a secure, reliable, affordable, transparent, greener and resilient electricity sector;
  2. Decarbonize thermal applications;
  3. Make reduction in energy intensity a key driver of decarbonisation;
  4. Decarbonize the transport sector;
  5. Ensure a safe, reliable and affordable supply of petroleum products and their efficient and environmentally safe storage, handling and use;
  6. Ensure that human, technical and institutional capacities are aligned with the needs of the energy sector and policy objectives, by integrating social and gender aspects into energy sector development; and
  7. Facilitate access to financing for renewable energy and energy efficiency.
Document Title: NEP Action Plan (October 2023)

Family Name: EPA New Source Performance Standards and Guidelines for Greenhouse Gas Emissions From Fossil Fuel-Fired Electric Generating Units
Family Summary:
This regulation establishes new standards and guidelines under Section 111 of the Clean Air Act to limit greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from fossil fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs). Key provisions include:

  • New Source Performance Standards (NSPS): Sets emission limits for new, modified, and reconstructed fossil fuel-fired EGUs.
  • Emission Guidelines: Provides guidelines for existing fossil fuel-fired EGUs to reduce GHG emissions.
  • Repeal of the Affordable Clean Energy (ACE) Rule: Revokes the previous ACE rule, which had set less stringent standards.

The EPA determined that the best system of emission reduction (BSER) for new coal-fired units is the most efficient demonstrated steam cycle combined with best operating practices, rather than carbon capture and storage, due to cost and feasibility considerations. The BSER is determined based on (i) technological feasibility, (ii) cost-effectiveness, (iii) environmental impact and (iv) energy requirements.The EPA has categorised new and reconstructed combustion turbines into three subcategories based on their operational load (low, intermediate and base) and also set compliance timeline.
Document Title: Correction - EPA New Source Performance Standards and Guidelines for Greenhouse Gas Emissions From Fossil Fuel-Fired Electric Generating Units
