Collection Name: Law 7/2021 on climate change and energy transition [Spain]
Collection Summary:
Enacted in 2021, this law establishes Spain's legal framework for achieving climate neutrality by 2050, aligning with the Paris Agreement and Sustainable Development Goals. It mandates a 23% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 (compared to 1990 levels), alongside ambitious renewable energy targets, including 42% of final energy consumption from renewables and 74% renewable electricity generation by 2030. Energy efficiency measures aim for a 39.5% reduction in primary energy consumption within the same timeframe. The law also prohibits new hydrocarbon and radioactive mineral exploitation, requires emission-free transport systems in cities with populations exceeding 50,000, and emphasises sustainable urban mobility.

The legislation includes a national Just Transition Strategy to ensure equitable economic opportunities, particularly for vulnerable regions, while fostering adaptation and resilience to climate risks across critical sectors such as water, biodiversity, and health. It creates governance mechanisms like the Expert Committee on Climate Change and Energy Transition to monitor progress and updates to Spain's Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC). Projecting investments exceeding €200 billion by 2030, the law is expected to enhance Spain’s GDP by €16.5–25.7 billion annually and generate 250,000–350,000 new jobs. The focus on education, innovation, and public awareness underscores its commitment to a holistic and inclusive transition.

This collection represent a body of policies, strategies, and plans enacted under this law.
Family Name: State Plan for Scientific, Technical, and Innovation Research 2024-2027 (PEICTI)
Family Summary: The State Plan for Scientific, Technical, and Innovation Research 2024-2027 (PEICTI) is a strategic framework developed under Spain’s Law on Science, Technology, and Innovation (Law 14/2011). It serves as the multi-annual instrument for planning and coordinating state-led policies in research, development, and innovation (RDI) within the framework of the Spanish Strategy for Science, Technology, and Innovation 2021-2027 (EECTI). The PEICTI outlines specific objectives derived from the EECTI and includes detailed programmes and actions to be implemented by various government departments and affiliated organisations, including public research institutions. The plan requires strong inter-ministerial collaboration and is classified as a strategic subsidies plan under Spain’s General Subsidies Law.Aligned with the European Green Transition policies, the PEICTI integrates eco-responsibility principles, such as the Do No Significant Harm (DNSH) approach and carbon-neutral infrastructure development. It supports circularity in research projects and aims to enhance public engagement on ecological and climate issues. The plan considered and plays a role in advancing Spain’s National Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC) 2023-2030, contributing to research and innovation for sustainable development.
Document Title: State Plan for Scientific, Technical, and Innovation Research 2021-2023 (PEICTI)

The focus on education, innovation, and public awareness underscores its commitment to a holistic and inclusive transition.

This collection represent a body of policies, strategies, and plans enacted under this law.
Family Name: State Plan for Scientific, Technical, and Innovation Research 2024-2027 (PEICTI)
Family Summary: The State Plan for Scientific, Technical, and Innovation Research 2024-2027 (PEICTI) is a strategic framework developed under Spain’s Law on Science, Technology, and Innovation (Law 14/2011). It serves as the multi-annual instrument for planning and coordinating state-led policies in research, development, and innovation (RDI) within the framework of the Spanish Strategy for Science, Technology, and Innovation 2021-2027 (EECTI). The PEICTI outlines specific objectives derived from the EECTI and includes detailed programmes and actions to be implemented by various government departments and affiliated organisations, including public research institutions. The plan requires strong inter-ministerial collaboration and is classified as a strategic subsidies plan under Spain’s General Subsidies Law.Aligned with the European Green Transition policies, the PEICTI integrates eco-responsibility principles, such as the Do No Significant Harm (DNSH) approach and carbon-neutral infrastructure development. It supports circularity in research projects and aims to enhance public engagement on ecological and climate issues. The plan considered and plays a role in advancing Spain’s National Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC) 2023-2030, contributing to research and innovation for sustainable development.
Document Title: State Plan for Scientific, Technical, and Innovation Research 2024-2027 (PEICTI)

Family Name: Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance
Family Summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority published the Hong one Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (the Taxonomy) to set out guidance on green and sustainable finance and to facilitate financial flows towards green activities, with the objective of contributing to global efforts to combat climate change.
Document Title: Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance

Family Name: Vision 2057: Long-Term National Development Perspective Framework
Family Summary: This framework is a Vision document that reflects the development aspirations of the people of Ghana from which current and future Medium-Term Development Plans will be derived. Strategic directions include: Promote climate-smart agriculture, enhance the resilience of communities, food systems and their associated supply chains, and reduce exposure to climate-, energy- and water-related risks; Enhance climate change resilience; and Incorporate climate-resilient and user-friendly designs as well as sustainable practices in infrastructure development.
Document Title: Vision 2057: Long-Term National Development Perspective Framework

Family Name: National Development Plan 2024-2028
Family Summary:
This plan came as the fourth phase of the national development plans starting in 2010, which represents a state of integration and interconnectedness to achieve Iraq’s vision 2030 in sustainable development, with its targets and programs that overlap and align with the state’s development trends and priorities at this stage, starting with the governance of effective development institutions, through economic reform programs and reforming the business environment for the private sector, digital transformations and reducing development gaps, improving human capital and dealing with the repercussions of climate change.

Amongst the general objectives of the Plan, there are:

  • Diversifying the productive structure of the national economy;
  • Improving the performance efficiency of the infrastructure and community services sector.
  • Implementing climate change mitigation and adaptation policies and strengthening responsive partnerships.
  • Increasing the efficiency of fiscal and monetary policy tools to meet the requirements of economic reform.
Document Title: National Development Plan 2024-2028

Family Name: The Sixteenth Plan (Fiscal Year 2024/25 - 2028/29)
Family Summary:
This Plan has a vision of ensuring good governance, social justice and prosperity. One of the major areas of structural transformation is biological diversity, climate change and green economy. It also identifies climate change as a cross-cutting sector with objectives for mitigation, adaptation, and finance mobilisation, for instance:

  • Develop a resilient public health system that can address climate-related health issues impacting human health., and strengthen public health surveillance to develop health structures that are resilient to climate change.
  • Strengthen the climate resilience of the education system.
  • Adopt climate-resilience in infrastructure planning.
  • Address environmental and climate-related challenges by using climate finance in infrastructure development.
  • Effectively mobilise public and alternative financial resources (public-private partnerships, co-investments, cost sharing, green climate finance), objective allocation, increased spending capacity and maintenance of financial good governance, carry out policy, structural and legal reforms.
Document Title: The Sixteenth Plan (Fiscal Year 2024/25 - 2028/29)

Family Name: National Battery Strategy
Family Summary:
This Strategy focuses on f 5 key priorities:1. Build battery manufacturing capabilities in ways that strengthen economic resilience, leverage Australia’s comparative advantages and add value to Australia's economy.2. Build knowledge and skills to create secure Australian-made jobs.3. Secure Australia’s place in global battery supply chains.4. Lead the world on sustainability, standards and the circular economy.5. Bring all levels of government together.

The outcomes of these Strategy are:

  1. Support Australia’s renewable energy transition through secure and well-paying jobs, value-adding to Australia’s refined minerals, capturing a larger share of the global battery value chain.
  2. Meet Australia's responsibilities to address climate change and transition to renewable energy, leading strong ESG standards in global battery markets.
  3. Diversify global battery supply chains and strengthen Australia’s economic resilience, ensuring reliable energy storage that will support greater use of renewables in Australia’s energy systems.
Document Title: National Battery Strategy

Family Name: Sixth Basic Environment Plan
Family Summary: Through this plan, the Ministry of the Environment seeks to improve the quality of life for citizens by working towards net-zero GHG emissions by 2050, investing in environmental conservation, and promoting public-private colllaborations. This plan presents a broad vision of the government’s environment policy based on the Basic Act on the Environment. The plan lays out strategies for Japan to shift from the linear/standard mass production type of socio-economic system to a circular/high value-added type of socio-economic system that is based on renewable resources, such as recycled resources and biomass resources.
Document Title: Outline of the Sixth Basic Environment Plan

Family Name: Fruit and Vegetable Sovereignty Plan
Family Summary: This Plan addresses the over-reliance on the imports of fruits and plants. To meet the needs and expectations of French consumers, this Plan aims to mitigate and adapt to climate change, preserve biodiversity, use water efficiently and address health issues. The actions focus on the decarbonisation of greenhouse, renewal of orchards, innovative agricultural equipment and research and development. This Plan implements measures identified as part of the Varenne process for agricultural water management and climate change adaptation.
Document Title: Fruit and Vegetable Sovereignty Plan

Family Name: Resolution CMN 5.130 of April 25, 2024, on the Eco Invest Brasil Programme
Family Summary: This Resolution from the National Monetary Council (CMN) provides for financing under the External Private Capital Mobilisation and Exchange Protection Line (the Eco Invest Brasil Line) within the scope of the National Climate Change Fund (FNMC).
Document Title: Resolution CMN 5.130 of April 25, 2024

Family Name: Joint Ordinance from the Inter Institutional Committee on the Brazilian Sustainable Taxonomy no. 3, from April 26, 2024
Family Summary: This Joint Ordinance from the Inter Institutional Committee on the Brazilian Sustainable Taxonomy provides for establishing technical groups for developing the Brazilian Sustainable Taxonomy. It is related to the Federal Decree No. 11.961/2024 on the Brazilian Sustainable Taxonomy Inter Institutional Committee.
Document Title: Joint Ordinance 2nd/ME No. 3

Family Name: Clean Hydrogen Certification System Operation Plan
Family Summary: This plan implements a hydrogen certification system to measure greenhouse gas emissions from hydrogen production and importation. The hydrogen certification system grants the clean hydrogen certification if the processes emit greenhouse gases below a certain threshold as well as providing administrative and financial support. The Korean government has finalized the country’s clean hydrogen certification standard of 4 kg CO2eq/kg H2 by considering international trends and domestic conditions such as technology level and infrastructure. Hydrogen that passes the certification standards is granted one of the four grades of the clean hydrogen certification depending on GHG emission levels.
Document Title: Clean Hydrogen Certification System Operation Plan

Family Name: Coordinated Interagency Transmission Authorizations and Permits Program (CITAP)
Family Summary: This program sets a 2-year timeline for the federal permitting process for transmission infrastructure, making the process more efficient without sacrificing the quality of environmental reviews. This will cut in half the average time to site and permit a transmission project. The program establishes the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) as the lead agency to coordinate and accelerate federal environmental reviews and permitting processes for qualifying electric transmission facilities. The program seeks to spur economic growth and modernize aging electric grid infrastructure by expanding access to clean energy and advanced energy technologies.
Document Title: Coordinated Interagency Transmission Authorizations and Permits Program (CITAP)

Family Name: Hydrogen Development Guidelines for 2024-2050
Family Summary: The Hydrogen Development Guidelines establish a long-term vision for the development of hydrogen fuels in Lithuania, with the goal of creating a green hydrogen ecosystem able to contribute to energy independence and climate change mitigation goals. The vision suggests measures such as a comprehensive and favourable regulatory framework, prioritising locally generated green hydrogen, and a substantial buildout of physical infrastructure to scale up pilot projects. It plans for 129,000 tons of green hydrogen production by 2030.
Document Title: Hydrogen Development Guidelines for 2024-2050

Document Title: Council of Ministers Resolution n.º 63/2024

Family Name: Ratification of the Kigali Amendment on HFCs
Family Summary:
On April 19, 2024, the UAE ratified the Kigali Amendment. On ratification, group II parties commit to peak HFCs consumption by 2024 and to gradually phase down in line with the following schedule:

(i) 2024 to 2028: 100 per cent

(ii) 2029 to 2034: 90 per cent

(iii) 2035 to 2039: 70 per cent

(iv) 2040 to 2044: 50 per cent

(v) 2045 and thereafter: 20 per cent
Document Title: Ratification of the Kigali Amendment on HFCs

Family Name: Decarbonizing the U.S. Economy by 2050: A National Blueprint for the Buildings Sector
Family Summary: This plan by the Department of Energy (DOE) sets a blueprint to reduce U.S. building emissions 65% by 2035 and 90% by 2050 (versus a 2005 baseline). This plan would help enable net-zero emissions economy-wide while centering equity and benefits to communities. The strategic objectives for this plan are: increase building energy efficiency, accelerate on-site emissions reductions, transform the grid edge, and minimize embodied life cycle emissions.
Document Title: Decarbonizing the U.S. Economy by 2050: A National Blueprint for the Buildings Sector

Family Name: Action plan to produce 1 million heat pumps in France
Family Summary:
This Action Plan supports the transitiojn to cleaner energy. Heat accounts for 45% of final energy consumption in France, and only 27% of this heat will come from renewable sources in 2022. Building heating remains a significant source of fossil fuel consumption (oil and especially gas).

The production of air-to-water heat pumps, a dynamic RD ecosystem, a building stock with a well-developed hot water network, and access to affordable, carbon-free electricity, enables French production sites to quickly adapt to growing demand. High-efficiency heat pumps and air conditioners will be adapted to refrigerants with low Global Warming Potential (GWP).
Document Title: Action plan to produce 1 million heat pumps in France

Family Name: Circular Economy National Strategy
Family Summary:
The National Circular Economy Strategy of Uruguay,guides the vision to build a critical mass of stakeholders who will adopt the proposed model by 2050. This includes consumers, producers, businesses, and institutions. Achieving this critical mass will involve a learning process to assimilate system changes at different levels:

  • Optimize resource use and dematerialization at the product, business, and consumer levels.
  • Implement new business models at the meso level (value chains and industrial parks), including shared infrastructure, collaboration, and symbiosis between businesses to improve the efficiency of materials, water, and energy.
  • Contribute at the macro level (cities, regions, and national level) to natural resource conservation, economic prosperity, and social equity.

General Objective: To promote sustainable production and consumption systems focused on the circular use of resources, generating value and regenerating natural systems.

Specific Objectives:

  • Strengthen institutions, public policies, and the environment to promote circular production and consumption systems, including monitoring systems.
  • Encourage RD initiatives for circular models like eco-design, extending product life, material recovery, energy and water recovery, biomass use in cascades, and shared resource use.
  • Foster circular business models and cities.
  • Promote a culture of circular consumption and production.
Document Title: Circular Economy National Strategy

Family Name: Comprehensive Climate Change and Biodiversity Management Plan for the Finance Sector
Family Summary: The Plan Integral de Gestión del Cambio Climático y Biodiversidad del Sector Hacienda (PIGCCSH+B) grounded in Law 1931 of 2018 is the Colombian Ministry of Finance’s framework to integrate climate and biodiversity considerations into fiscal, budgetary, and financial policies, and to mobilize public and private green finance. It defines lines of action for taxation, spending, financial regulation, and risk management so that economic policy supports national climate and biodiversity goals.
Document Title: Comprehensive Climate Change and Biodiversity Management Plan for the Finance Sector (Plan Integral de Gestión del Cambio Climático y Biodiversidad del Sector Hacienda )

Family Summary: This document approves the Regulations of the aid program for the improvement of the national real estate park, the improvement of the energy efficiency of buildings and the use of renewable energies.It establishes the purpose of the RENOVA programme i.e. to regulate access to public aid to rehabilitate buildings located in Andorra to promote improvement of the conditions of habitability, accessibility, industrial safety and general safety of the building, facades, sustainability and energy efficiency, as well as the implementation of renewable energies in the real estate stock.Every year the programme will announce the opening of the call for applications for the Renova program for the improvement of the national real estate stockopen calls via an Edict. The actions that are the subject of aid are selected on a simple competitive basis, so that aid is awarded to applications that meet each and every one of the requirements established in the Renova program's rules.In each year, the applications are open until the budget available in the programme's annual call is exhausted.The available budget for the execution of the Renova program is considered exhausted when the last grant application is submitted that exhausts the amount established in the annual call for applications for the program. Family Name: Decree 145/2024, of 10-4-2024, approving the Regulation of financial aid for electric mobility and for improving the energy efficiency of the national car fleet
Family Summary: The decree aims to promote renovation and improvement of the vehicle fleet to achieve energy savings with positive effects on the environment and road safety. The main goal is to establish and regulate the criteria, requirements and procedures necessary to access financial aid for electric mobility and improve the energy efficiency of the vehicle fleet and  promote a reduction in energy consumption and thus contribute to the energy transition and the fight against climate change.
Document Title: Decree 145/2024, of 10-4-2024, approving the Regulation of financial aid for electric mobility and for improving the energy efficiency of the national car fleet.

The objective is to emphasise climate-friendly solutions without negatively impacting activity levels and operational capability.

Family Name: Norway’s integrated ocean management plans (Meld. St. 21 2023-2024)
Family Summary:
The purpose of the management plans is to provide a framework for value creation through the sustainable use of marine natural resources and ecosystem services and at the same time maintain ecosystem structure, functioning, productivity and diversity. The management plans are thus a tool both for facilitating value creation and food security, and for maintaining the high environmental value of Norway’s seas and oceans.

The plans include the climate and environmental considerations as a basis for marine spatial management; adaptation to climate change and a warmer ocean; and strengthening the knowledge base on oceans and climate change. Norway is considering carbon capture and storage under the seabed, aided by the presence of geological formations suitable for carbon dioxide storage, as an important mitigation measure in climate policy.
Document Title: Norway’s integrated ocean management plans (Meld. St. 21 2023-2024)

Family Name: Transport Adaptation Strategy
Family Summary:
This transport adaptation strategy includes actions and policies to enhance climate adaptation planning across the transport sector, ensure these plans are achieved, and lead to improved climate resilience in the transport system. This strategy will support transport infrastructure operators in recognising the opportunities, including cost savings, that come with adaptation.
As the climate changes, travel disruption from extreme weather could have an increasing impact on day-to-day lives if action is not taken to manage the risk. The Government's 2023 National Risk Register identified risks such as extreme heat, storms and flooding had become more likely due to climate change, with the trend expected to continue over the coming decades.
Document Title: Adapting the UK’s transport system to the impacts of climate change

Family Name: Seychelles National Development Strategy 2024-2028
Family Summary: The Seychelles National Development Strategy 2024-2028 aims to provide an overarching framework to guide sustainable socioeconomic development, and notes climate change mitigation and adaptation as a major risk and practical challenge for the country. The strategy identifies agriculture, digital economy, fisheries and blue economy more generally as key sectors for growth. As balanced outcomes across the economy it prioritises: public service modernisation; general economic transformation; improved public health; law and order; a modernised and forward-looking education system; environmental sustainability and climate change resilience. On climate change the strategy seeks to diversify the export economy to reduce vulnerability to fisheries supply shocks, build capacity for coastal and marine ecosystem/infrastructure protection, and increase the renewables share of energy to 25% by 2030, also increasing energy efficiency to reduce the carbon intensity of the economy.
Document Title: Seychelles National Development Strategy 2024-2028

Family Name: Guidance on Anti-Greenwashing Rule
Family Summary: The FCA’s Anti-Greenwashing Rule, introduced as part of the Sustainability Disclosure Requirements (SDR) package, requires FCA-authorised firms to ensure that sustainability-related references to their products and services are fair, clear, not misleading and consistent with the actual sustainability characteristics of those products or services. FCA guidance (FG24/3) explains that claims should be correct and substantiated, presented clearly, complete and consider the product or service’s full lifecycle, with comparisons being fair and meaningful. Its objective is to reduce greenwashing, improve the credibility of sustainability claims and support informed decision-making and the development of the sustainable finance market.
Document Title: Policy Statement to help consumers navigate the market for sustainable investment products

Family Name: National Energy Performance Strategy
Family Summary: This Strategy coordinates action at the national-level to improve energy performance across Australia. Energy performance includes energy efficiency, demand flexibility and electrification or fuel switching. According to the press release, the Government is investing $15.2 million until 2026 to develop and deliver the strategy.
Document Title: National Energy Performance Strategy

Family Name: National Blue Economy Policy for 2024
Family Summary: The Policy focuses on sustainable use and management of marine and coastal resources to support socio-economic development while ensuring environmental conservation. It emphasises addressing climate change impacts on marine ecosystems through measures like coral reef restoration, establishment of marine protected areas, and promoting sustainable marine spatial planning. It supports activities such as sustainable fisheries, marine tourism, and renewable energy development, aligning with Sustainable Development Goal 14 (Life Below Water) and Tanzania's broader climate commitments, including its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC).
Document Title: National Blue Economy Policy for 2024

Family Name: Ordinance 125/2024/1 - Adopts the Specific Regulation for the Climate Action and Sustainability Thematic Area.
Family Summary:
This regulation sets out the rules for operations related to Climate Action and Sustainability, funded by the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) and the Cohesion Fund (CF), for the programming period 2021-2027. The regulation covers specific objectives related to the Portugal 2030 programs, including:

Energy efficiency and decarbonization in regional and local public administration.
Promotion of self-consumption and renewable energy communities.
Energy storage, better management, and increased digitalization of energy grids.
Climate change adaptation, risk management, and water resource management.
Coastal protection and defence.
Urban water cycle management.
Urban waste management.
Conservation of nature, biodiversity, and natural heritage.
Environmental liabilities, such as abandoned mining sites.
Promoting multimodal sustainable urban mobility as part of the transition to a zero-carbon economy.

Article 11 defines the conditions for funding allocation towards climate goals, prioritising sustainable projects that help to meet climate targets on circular economy, public infrastructure and housing renovation, water supply and contaminated land that becomes a carbon sink.
Document Title: Ordinance 125/2024/1

Family Name: National Green Growth Strategy 2024-2023
Family Summary:
The National Green Growth Strategy is structured in five parts as follows: Chapter One is the introduction which provides the background and context for greening growth in Zambia as well as the National Green Growth Strategy formulation process; Chapter Two provides the sectoral situation analysis and identifies the challenges and opportunities for greening growth in Zambia; Chapter Three gives a scenario analysis and the economic benefits of Green Growth while Chapter Four highlights what it will take to transition Zambia to a green economy and articulates the Vision and the strategic objectives as well as the theory of change for greening growth.

Chapter Five to Chapter Eight breaks down the strategic objectives into development outcomes and interventions while Chapter Nine presents the enabling environment for greening growth in Zambia. Chapter Five is focused on resilient and climate compatible growth in the sectors of agriculture; tourism; energy; water; infrastructure; and climate services and early warning systems.

The implementation and coordination arrangements, including the monitoring and evaluation framework of the Strategy, are discussed in Chapter Ten. The National Green Growth Strategy comes complete with an Implementation Plan which is in Annex One of the document.
Document Title: National Green Growth Strategy 2024-2023

Family Name: Communication Strategy for the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) Process (2023-2030)
Family Summary:
The NAP's climate change communication strategy aims to make adaptation options visible for building a climate-resilient society by 2030. This vision is based on that of the NAP and its main objective is to inform and raise awareness among all stakeholders (civil society, the media, households, women's and youth associations, institutional and community actors, the private sector, research institutes and centers, and parliamentarians) about the NAP's priorities in order to facilitate its ownership, implementation, and monitoring by all stakeholders.

The communication strategy includes three main objectives: (i) to inform and raise awareness among all the aforementioned stakeholders about the NAP's priorities in order to facilitate its ownership, implementation, and monitoring by all stakeholders; (ii) to encourage populations and actors from civil society, research, and the private sector to adopt good climate change adaptation practices; (iii) to collect, document, and share information on climate change adaptation measures and (iv) to coordinate the implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of the communication strategy and to foster exchanges among the stakeholders involved. The communication strategy also defines four strategic areas: (i) ownership of the NAP by policymakers; (ii) raising public awareness of climate change adaptation options; (iii) documenting and sharing information on climate change adaptation measures; and (iv) coordination. The strategy targets all parties affected by climate change at the national level. Communication methods have been identified to disseminate the universal and specific key messages developed in this strategy.
Document Title: Communication Strategy for the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) Process (2023-2030)

Family Name: Methodological guidance for climate and socio-economic calculations
Family Summary: The Guidance describes the framework for calculating the socio-economic consequences of climate policy proposals. The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities continuously prepares analyses of the importance of climate policy for, among other things, greenhouse gas emissions and the economy. The methodological guidance aims to ensure that calculations of the socio-economic consequences of climate policy proposals follow the same overall methods across proposals, and are thus consistent and comparable. The methodological guidance also describes good practice for documenting calculation assumptions and results. Areas of calculatiokn include cost-effectiveness analysis; shadow price for CO2e; cost-benefit analysis; behaviour changes; scaling of cost and effect; and calculation of net socio-economic costs for households, businesses, and the public sector; the value of side effects; caclulation of greenhouse gas reductions; conversion to market prices and the discount rate.
Document Title: Methodological guidance for climate and socio-economic calculations

Family Name: National Reform Programme of the Slovak Republic 2024
Family Summary: The Slovak Republic’s National Reform Programme 2024 frames climate and energy policy as closely intertwined with economic resilience and energy security, particularly in response to the geopolitical impacts of the war in Ukraine. It prioritises reducing dependence on fossil fuel imports, especially from Russia, while accelerating the deployment of renewable energy. A strong emphasis is placed on improving energy efficiency, particularly in buildings, as a cost-effective means of lowering emissions and demand. The programme also highlights the need to modernise electricity grids to accommodate a growing share of renewables and to strengthen system resilience. In the transport sector, efforts focus on decarbonisation through the expansion of low- and zero-emission mobility, although progress is constrained by delays in rail infrastructure projects. Challenges remain, including slow permitting processes, gaps in renewable energy uptake and recycling performance, and the absence of a fully adopted national Climate Act to anchor long-term policy commitments.
Document Title: National Reform Programme of the Slovak Republic

Family Name: Green Hydrogen Action Plan 2023-2030
Family Summary: Chile's Ministry of Energy published the Green Hydrogen Action Plan 2023-2030 on April 25, 2024. The plan outlines 81 actions across 18 categories, focussing on developing standards, streamlining permits, promoting research, advancing incentives, and fostering relationships with potential buyers to establish Chile as a leading producer and exporter of green hydrogen and its derivatives.

Family Name: Infrastructure Sector Mitigation and Adaptation Plan
Family Summary: This plan aims to improve the sustainability of public works, helping Chile to achieve its NDC and carbon neutrality targets. It emphasises measures such as the improved management of construction and demolition waste, and aims to reduce GHG emissions throughout the entire life cycle of public works by measuring its carbon footprint. Overall, the mitigation measures in the plan are expected to contribute to 0.569 MtCO2e in reductions in the 2025-2029 period. Regarding the means of implementation, it highlights strengthening the Sustainable Building Certification and establishing Clean Production Agreements.

Family Name: Low-Carbon and Climate-Resilient Roadmap for the Fertiliser Sector
Family Summary: The Low-Carbon and Climate-Resilient Roadmap for the Fertiliser Sector provides a comprehensive and multifaceted overview of the Turkish fertiliser sector, encompassing its current status, challenges, and potential pathways toward sustainable and low-carbon development. It emphasises the importance of aligning fertiliser investments with the overall objectives of the European Green Deal (GD) strategy, particularly the ambitious target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 within the framework of the Sustainable Development Goals. It also highlights the critical role of implementing measures to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and promote technological transformation in the fertiliser sector in light of Turkey's 2053 net zero targets.

Family Name: Food Waste Strategy 2024-2027
Family Summary: This Strategy aims to prevent and reduce food waste and food loss, thereby benefiting the climate and the economy. The strategy contains 15 initiatives, including the think tank on food waste and food loss, ONE\ THIRD, the voluntary agreement on reducing food waste in the food industry, "Denmark against Food Waste", and research into reducing food waste and food loss.

Family Name: OGA Plan on Emissions Reduction
Family Summary: The Plan is a regulatory instrument issued under the NSTA's overarching OGA Strategy, translating that Central Obligation into concrete, binding requirements, including cutting emissions from flaring, venting, and power generation, and supporting CCUS to help the UK meet net zero by 2050. Rather than setting a single interim target or target year, the Plan lays out binding principles and requirements operators must follow, organised under four headings: investment and efficiency, electrification and low-carbon power, flaring and venting, and inventory. Crucially, emissions offsetting does not count toward meeting these obligations, only actual reductions do.

Family Summary: This Order creates the technical commission to monitor the voluntary carbon market (VCM) provided for in Decree Law No. 4/2024. Family Summary:
This decree establishes the Brazilian Sustainable Taxonomy Interinstitutional Committee (CITSB), of an advisory and deliberative nature, to coordinate the development and implementation of the Brazilian Sustainable Taxonomy (TSB).

The TSB consists of a system for classifying activities, assets or categories of projects that contribute to achieving climate, environmental and social objectives, using specific criteria.

Family Name: Response Strategy for Water Resources Management
Family Summary:
This Strategy adopts the integrated water resources management and river basin approaches and has a vision of attaining economic and ecological prosperity through sustainable management and utilisation of water resources. It contributes towards increasing climate adaptive and resilient capacity of the vulnerable people through climate-friendly water resources management and utilisation.

Under the implementation arrangement, the strategy has specifi ed the role of the government, existing inter-agency committees, public participation private sector, and NGO federations. A National Water Resources Coordination Committee will be established under the chair of the Secretary of Water and Energy Commission Secretariat (WECS) with representation from water-related institutions, associations of local governments and NGOs and private sector. The Water Resources Division (WRD) of WECS will function as its secretariat, and will generate, package and repackage knowledge from strategy implementation and share it using appropriate channels. Activities and sub-activities are also proposed to reduce the capacity-building barriers. Existing training facilities for human resources development have been outlined. Finance, being the critical part of the strategy implementation, is expected from domestic sources, foreign investments, bilateral and multilateral sources, and through access to climate finance. Taking note of increase in climate-induced disasters in recent years, the Loss and Damage Fund, established in 2022 and operationalised in 2023, is considered be an appropriate window to access funding for addressing climate-induced disasters, including sediment disasters.

A response strategy monitoring framework outlines indicators, means of verification, frequency and key assumptions to monitor the goal and outcomes. Evaluation will generate knowledge and learning.
Document Title: Response Strategy for Water Resources Management

Family Name: The Green Industrial Initiative (Roadmap 2.0)
Family Summary: This roadmap aims to help Norway achieve its target of cutting climate emissions by 50% by 2030. The roadmap will also help boost Norwegian exports. This plan focuses on access to renewable energy, infrastructure, technology, and capital. The plan highlights nine priority sectors for green initiatives, including: offshore wind production, low-emission hydrogen production and distribution, CCSU, battery value chain development, energy-efficient process industry, solar industry, forestry, manufacturing, and maritime activities. The original initiative was launched by the Norwegian Government in 2022, and this updated "Roadmap 2.0" was launched in 2024.

Family Name: Agreement on the implementation of the transition aid from the Green tax reform for industry etc.
Family Summary:
This Agreement establishes the framework for implementing the transition support from the Green Tax Reform for Industry, etc., including the target group, type of support, design of support schemes and requirements for a climate audit in order to receive support. The transition support will be provided on the basis of specific technical transition. In this way, the transition support will contribute to additional CO2 reductions. The parties to the Agreement want to support the various technical transition options that companies in industry and business have. For some companies, the investment cost is the primary barrier to conversion, while the operating cost is the primary barrier to conversion for other companies.

This Agreement follows the Agreement on the Green Tax Reform for industry etc. of 22 June 2022, where the parties agreed to introduce a new and ambitious CO2 tax, which will be phased in from 2025 towards 2030.
Document Title: Agreement on the implementation of the transition aid from the Green tax reform for industry etc.

The final goal is to reduce GHGs emissions.

Family Name: Scheme for the Promotion of Manufacturing of Electric Passenger Cars
Family Summary: The Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electric Passenger Cars in India (SPMEPCI) was notified in March 2024. Applicants must commit to an investment of at least ₹4,150 crore, achieve 25% domestic value addition (DVA) within three years and ramp up to 50% DVA by the end of five years. The application portal for SPMEPCI has been launched on 24th June 2025 and it’s open until 21st October 2025. To draw global automakers to invest, the scheme grants approved applicants a five-year window to import Completely Built-in Units (CBUs) of electric four-wheelers (e-4W) valued at a minimum CIF (Cost, Insurance, and Freight) of USD 35,000 at a significantly reduced customs duty of 15%, starting from their application approval date. The scheme blends incentives with localization to drive clean-mobility growth along with the ‘Make in India’ and ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ initiatives.
Document Title: Scheme to promote manufacturing of electric passenger cars in India

Family Name: 2023/24:97 National strategy for climate adaptation
Family Summary:
In this document, the government presents the revised national strategy for climate adaptation and the government's action plan for the next five years. The government reports on the direction of the national work on climate adaptation. The document also has a section that briefly describes the work on climate adaptation at the international level. The direction is based on approved budget bills, approved investigations or ongoing EU processes. The document also contains announcements of new analyses that are required for the government to be able to take a position and possibly decide on measures later in the mandate period.

Sweden must be climate-adapted, resilient and take advantage of the opportunities that come with a changing climate. During the current mandate period, a number of measures need to be taken to create the conditions for structured, coordinated and socially effective work on climate adaptation that leads to reducing vulnerability to the effects of climate change. To accelerate climate adaptation measures, the Government intends to promote a number of measures, including establishing clear and appropriate targets and monitoring systems, ensuring that responsibility for climate adaptation work is clearly allocated and that there are good conditions to take responsibility. Furthermore, the Government intends to promote synergies with work on the prevention of natural disasters, crisis preparedness and security of supply.
Document Title: 2023/24:97 National strategy and Government action plan for climate adaptation

Family Name: Commission Communication on managing climate risks
Family Summary: The Communication presents an urgent call for the European Commission and Member States to move from climate‑risk awareness to systematic and proactive risk management, recognising that increasing temperatures, extreme weather events, and cascading disasters are now material threats to people, ecosystems, infrastructure and the economy. It identifies major risk clusters and outlines four pillars of action: improved governance (clearer responsibilities, stronger coordination at all levels), better tools for risk‑owners (data, modelling, early warning, capacity‑building), harnessing structural policies (spatial planning, critical‑infrastructure resilience, nature‑based solutions) and right pre‑conditions for financing climate resilience (public procurement, investment frameworks, private‑finance mobilisation). The Communication also sets out thematic priorities—ecosystems, water, health, food systems, infrastructure built environment—and proposes concrete EU‑level actions for each, aiming to embed resilience and adaptation into all sectors and ensure that climate risk‑informed decision‑making becomes standard practice across the Union.
Document Title: Commission Communication on managing climate risks

Family Name: Guatemala's Gender and Climate Change Action Plan (PAGcc) [Plan de Acción de Género y Cambio Climático de Guatemala (PAGcc)]
Family Summary:
The Gender and Climate Change Action Plan of Guatemala (PAGcc) represents a comprehensive policy framework designed to integrate gender-responsive and intersectional approaches into the country's climate commitments and actions. Developed through collaborative and consensual processes involving expert consultations, participatory workshops, and social validation by indigenous communities, youth, and civil society organisations, the plan seeks to address gender gaps within Guatemala's climate change response whilst aligning with national policy frameworks and international agreements.

The plan's climate change and energy transition elements are structured around five priority sectors corresponding to Guatemala's Nationally Determined Contribution: agriculture, coastal zones, forestry, environmental protected areas, and energy and water management. Each sector incorporates gender analysis resulting in specific sub-plans with dedicated objectives, actions, and indicators designed to ensure that climate adaptation and mitigation interventions are accessible to and beneficial for women, men, indigenous peoples, local communities, and young people. The overarching objective guarantees that Guatemala's national climate commitments are implemented through an intersectional and socially inclusive lens with a gender perspective, ensuring equitable access to, participation in, and benefits from climate adaptation and mitigation measures across all demographic groups and sectors.
Document Title: Guatemala's Gender and Climate Change Action Plan (PAGcc-Guatemala) [Plan de Acción de Género y Cambio Climático de Guatemala (PAGcc-Guatemala)]

Family Name: Norway’s strategy for developing a green, circular economy
Family Summary:
The strategy underpines the Norwegian government’s efforts to exploit the potential for value creation in Norwegian business and industry more fully, with a more circular economy as the basis. It includes specific action points for the sectors that have been identified as having the greatest potential for circularity and green competitiveness in Norway: the bio-based sectors; the process industries; construction and buildings; and service industries, including retail and wholesale trade.

Ciruclar economy will at the same time result in progress towards Norway’s climate and environmental policy targets, including Norway’s efforts to achieve the UN Sustainable Development Goals. In relation to climate-related actions:, the Norwegian government will:

  • promote a development pathway in which circular solutions within the bio-based sectors and more use of renewable resources to replace non-renewable alternatives are used to make the greatest possible contribution to progress towards climate and environmental targets and to sustainable value creation;
  • and support initiatives for high climate and environmental standards as a basis for moresustainable products and value chains under the EU Circular Economy Action Plan.
Document Title: Norway’s strategy for developing a green, circular economy

Family Name: Horizon Europe Programme
Family Summary:
Horizon Europe is the EU’s key funding programme for research and innovation. Following the Multiannual Financial Framework Midterm Review (MTR) decision, the indicative funding amount for Horizon Europe for the period 2021-2027 is EUR 93.5 billion. It tackles climate change, helps to achieve the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals and boosts the EU’s competitiveness and growth.The Horizon Europe strategic plan 2025-2027 steers research and innovation funding 2025-2027, addressing the key global challenges such as climate change, loss of biodiversity, the digital transition and an ageing population. The strategic plan sets out 3 strategic orientations:

  • Green transition
  • Digital transition

Family Name: Electricity Grid Development Plan 2037 with an Outlook to 2045 Version 2023
Family Summary: The Netzentwicklungsplan (NEP) 2037/2045 is Germany's strategic roadmap for expanding and modernizing the electricity transmission grid to support the energy transition and achieve climate neutrality by 2045. The current confirmed version, approved by the Bundesnetzagentur in March 2024, identifies the transmission infrastructure required to accommodate the large-scale integration of renewable energy, increasing electrification of transport, heating, and industry, and enhanced cross-border electricity exchange. It includes substantial investments in new high-voltage direct current (HVDC) corridors, reinforcement of the existing transmission network, and offshore grid connections to ensure a secure and reliable electricity supply. Building upon this foundation, the transmission system operators have already published the 2025 NEP (second draft). At the time of writing, this updated NEP is undergoing review by the Bundesnetzagentur following public consultation and has not yet been formally confirmed.

Family Name: H.E. Prime Minister Decree No: 636/2024 Amending provisions of the Egyptian Accounting Standards and Accounting Explanation No. 2/2024
Family Summary:
Decree No. 636/2024 adds the Egyptian Accounting Explanation No. 2, "Certificates of Carbon Emissions Reduction (Carbon Credits) to the Egyptian Accounting Standards.

The decree specifies how carbon credits are treated in terms of accounting depends on the specific arrangements and commercial purpose of their issuance or purchase. Factors considered for determining the appropriate accounting approach include:

- Understanding the carbon credit issuance cycle.

- The arrangement's nature and commercial purpose for buying or issuing carbon credits.

- Classifying carbon credits as financial or intangible assets based on the arrangement and purpose.

- Providing clear disclosures about carbon credits and accounting policies.

Different Cases of Accounting Approaches

The explanation outlines different scenarios and their respective accounting treatments, including initial measurement (i.e. the determination of the value of the carbon credit when first recognized in the financial statements), subsequent measurement, and derecognition, for:

- Carbon credits issued for owned carbon reduction projects (treated as intangible assets for internal use and financial instruments for sale).

- Carbon credits issued for non-owned carbon reduction projects (treated as financial instruments).

- Carbon credits purchased for internal use/retirement (treated as intangible assets).

- Carbon credits purchased for trading (treated as financial instruments).

Tax Treatment, Special Cases, and Disclosure

The explanation also addresses tax treatment according to Egyptian Accounting Standard No. 24 "Income Tax", special cases involving changes in acquisition purpose, and disclosure requirements related to accounting policies, valuation methods, and changes in carbon credit balances.
Document Title: H.E. Prime Minister Decree No: 636/2024 Amending provisions of the Egyptian Accounting Standards and Accounting Explanation No. 2/2024

Family Summary: This Strategy places a strong emphasis on climate action, aiming to integrate climate-resilient practices, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and promote sustainable land management. Family Name: Indicative Program for the Installation and Decommissioning of Power Plants (PIIRCE) [Programa Indicativo para la Instalación y Retiro de Centrales Eléctricas (PIIRCE)]
Family Summary: The Indicative Program for the Installation and Decommissioning of Power Plants (PIIRCE) is a planning tool mandated by Mexico’s Electricity Industry Law (LIE) to guide the installation and retirement of power plants, ensuring sufficient resources to meet the demand of the National Electric System (SEN) while fulfilling clean energy objectives. Developed by the Secretariat of Energy (SENER), the PIIRCE is integrated into the broader Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional (PRODESEN) and coordinates with programmes for the expansion and modernisation of the National Transmission Network (RNT) and General Distribution Networks (RGD), as well as gas pipeline infrastructure planning. It aims to enhance the reliability of the SEN, reduce electricity tariffs, and strengthen the role of the state-owned Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) as a key driver of national development, while encouraging private investment under a framework of legal certainty and transparency. The programme includes plans for the medium-term addition of combined-cycle plants, the rehabilitation and modernisation of existing hydroelectric facilities, and the equipping of new hydroelectric projects at existing sites.
Document Title: 5. Indicative Program for the Installation and Removal of Power Plants (PIIRCE) [5. Programa Indicativo para la Instalación y Retiro de Centrales Eléctricas (PIIRCE)]

Family Summary: The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) has developed the Singapore Sustainable Air Hub Blueprint as Singapore’s State Action Plan for the decarbonisation of its aviation sector and sustainable aviation growth. Through the Blueprint, Singapore also hopes to be a pathfinder and convenor for cross-sectoral and public-private partnership, to work with other countries and international organisations to support sustainable aviation growth. This is in line with the International Civil Aviation Organization's (ICAO) and its Member States' adoption of the long-term global aspirational goal (LTAG) of net zero carbon emissions for international aviation by 2050. The Blueprint covers the domain of airport; airline; air traffic management; and critical enablers to reduce energy use and deploy renewables; support the use of Sustainable Aviation Fuel; create operational improvements to increase efficiency and reduce fuel burn; and build coalitions for action.

Family Summary:
The purpose of this Decree-Law is to regulate matters concerning the National System of Protected Areas, regarding the exercise of its governance, control, and administration, management categories, their proposal and declaration, the protection regime, and the granting of authorisations for carrying out activities within them.

This Decree-Law is meant to contribute to climate change adaptation and mitigation.

The delimitation and categorisation of protected areas, as well as any modifications to both aspects, shall be carried out based on scientific assessments and consultation with the agencies of the Central State Administration and the entities involved, taking into account, amongst other factors: -

  1. The magnitude, significance, and degree of conservation of their values, especially in relation to biological diversity; and
  2. The degree of naturalness of the area, which considers the incidence of environmental impacts, including those related to the effects of climate change.
Document Title: Decree-Law No. 83 on the National System of Protected Areas

Family Name: 2025 Guidelines for Processing Subsidies for Electric Vehicle Supply Projects (and 2024 Guidelines)
Family Summary: The 2025 policy expands electric vehicle subsidies for young people and multi-child households. Young individuals purchasing an electric vehicle as their first-ever car will be able to receive an additional 20% of the government subsidy that is normally provided for each vehicle type. For multi-child households, the additional support previously set at 10% of the basic government subsidy has been reformed to a fixed amount (KRW 1 million to 3 million), allowing them to receive more subsidies than before. The 2024 guidelines for electric vehicle purchase subsidies are created to support EV adoption. These guidelines support the Republic of Korea's target of having 4.2 million EVs on the road by 2030. The 2024 EV guidelines provide KRW 1.7 trillion in subsidies, broken down by vehicle category: KRW 932 billion for light-duty passenger vehicles, KRW 140 billion for light- and medium-duty commercial vehicles, and KRW 630 billion for heavy-duty commercial vehicles. These guidelines are determined by factors including battery efficiency, ease of recycling, operations and maintenance availability, and vehicle cost. The guidelines promote the adoption of safe and efficient electric vehicles, use of longer-range vehicles, better technology innovation, manufacturer support for vehicle maintenance, and EV adoption in disadvantaged communities.
Document Title: 2025 Guidelines for Processing Subsidies for Electric Vehicle Supply Projects

Family Name: National Development Plan for the New Ecuador (2024–2025)
Family Summary:
The National Development Plan for the New Ecuador (2024–2025) is the country’s roadmap for sustainable and equitable development, mandated by Ecuador’s Constitution (arts. 3, 279, and 280), which requires the state to plan for national development, eradicate poverty, and promote sustainable resource management. The plan, guided by the principles of “Buen Vivir” (Good Living) and participatory governance, aims to align public policies, programs, and investments with national priorities. It is structured around four pillars: (1) social development; (2) economic development; (3) infrastructure, energy, and environment; and, (4) institutional and risk management.
On climate change, the plan integrates mitigation and adaptation actions into key sectors to foster low-emission, climate-resilient development. It emphasises conserving and restoring natural resources, promoting sustainable land use, and adopting circular economy models to reduce environmental contamination. Additionally, it strengthens disaster risk reduction frameworks and promotes the resilience of critical infrastructure to climate-related hazards. Water security is a key focus, with efforts to expand access to potable water, irrigation, and sanitation in the context of climate vulnerabilities. Equally, the plan sets measurable climate goals, including increasing land under hydrological protection, reducing climate vulnerability through enhanced adaptive capacity, and improving waste recovery rates.
Document Title: National Development Plan for the New Ecuador (2024–2025)

Sweden's climate aid contributes to the three main goals of the Paris Agreement through strategic investments in emissions reduction, climate change adaptation, and in aligning financial flows with the goals of Paris Agreement. Family Name: Philippine Sustainable Finance Taxonomy Guidelines
Family Summary:
The Philippine Sustainable Finance Taxonomy Guidelines (SFTG) was developed under the auspices of the Financial Sector Forum (FSF) following the recommendations in the Philippine Sustainable Finance Roadmap released by the Inter-agency Technical Working Group for Sustainable Finance (or the Green Force) in October 2021.

The SFTG serves as a tool to classify whether an economic activity is environmentally and socially sustainable and guides different stakeholders in making informed investment and financing decisions. The SFTG aims to direct, accelerate, and increase capital flows to economic activities that promote sustainability objectives. including reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and building climate resilience. It likewise promotes transparency and credibility by minimizing the risk of greenwashing and supports a just transition to a sustainable economy. Banks shall use the SFrG when extending credit. making investment decisions, or designing sustainable financial products and services, among others.

In issuing sustainable bonds, banks shall comply with the regulatory requirements articulated in the relevantsustainable bonds standards or guidelines issued by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). While the SEC Guidelines provide lists of eligible green and social project categories. the issuing bank may voluntarily apply the principles under the respective components of the SFTG to assess if such bond issuance is aligned with the Taxonomy. In addition. the considerations for the environmental objectives could provide additional guidance in assessing eligible green project and in determining substantial contribution to an environmental objective). There are decision trees and guiding questions provided for climate change adaptation and mitigation.
Document Title: Philippine Sustainable Finance Taxonomy Guidelines

HFCs are a potent greenhouse gas used in some air conditioning and industrial/domestic refrigeration, and the strategy aims for a total phase-out of HFCs in Jordan by 2030. The strategy also aims to enhance efficiency in supply chains requiring cooling, such as medical and food industries, helping to meet growing demand for cooling across the economy. Family Name: Strategy for green jobs in agriculture and related industries

This strategy presents initiatives within five key indicators to support green jobs in agriculture and related industries:

• Create a future-proof framework for innovation and growth

• Make Denmark a center for research and innovation in green solutions for agriculture and related industries

• Ensure Denmark has the competencies for the green jobs of the future

• Let Denmark lead the way to the effective rollout of green solutions

This Strategy acknowledges that the green transition means that some jobs will disappear, while new ones will arise. The animal sector faces challenges because a significant portion of the sector's emissions originate from here. Conversely, the development towards more plant-based foods and new ways of producing proteins for feed and food opens up new opportunities.

Family Name: FRA BOD Decree 30/2024: On Standards for the Adoption of Local Carbon Registers.
Family Summary:
Decree No. 30/2024 establishes the criteria for the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) to recognize local voluntary carbon registries in Egypt. It applies to local voluntary carbon registries seeking recognition by the FRA to operate on the Egyptian Voluntary Carbon Market Exchange (“Africarbonex”). International registries recognized by the International Carbon Reduction and Offset Alliance (ICROA) are automatically recognized.

To be recognized by the FRA, registries must meet requirements in the following six key areas:

General Requirements

- Project Registration: Registries must follow specific procedures for registering carbon emission reduction projects.

- Ownership Tracking: They must enable tracking of carbon credit ownership and transfers, from issuance to retirement, to achieve carbon neutrality.

- Unique Identifiers: Each project and credit must have a unique identification number.

- Information Dissemination: Registries are responsible for disseminating information about carbon emission reduction projects, including project descriptions, reports (follow-up, validation, verification), and legal data.

- Double Registration Prohibition: Registries must have measures in place to prevent double registration of projects, ensuring a project registered in one registry cannot be registered in another.

- Agreements with Developers: A formal agreement between the registry and project developers outlining rights and obligations is required.

- Connectivity with Trading Infrastructure: The registry should connect electronically with FRA-licensed settlement and clearing companies for data exchange, particularly related to carbon credit ownership.

Validation and Verification Requirements

- Approved Verification Bodies: The registry needs a list of approved validation and verification bodies, adhering to the provisions of FRA Decree No. (163) of 2023.

- Sector Eligibility: The registry should specify the sectors eligible for carbon emission reduction project registration.

- Conflict of Interest Prevention: Strict rules and procedures are needed to prevent conflicts of interest between the registry operator, project financers, and the validation and verification bodies.

Governance Requirements

- Maintain an appropriate organizational structure based on business volume.

- Board members must avoid conflicts of interest and seek approval for contracts involving personal interests.

- Establish IT Governance and Technology Risk Management Committees.

- Board members must exercise due diligence in Registry activities.

Information Systems Requirements

- Maintain a separate issuance system for validation, verification, and documentation.

- Operate a registry system to manage ownership transfers of credits, supporting various processes.

Technological Infrastructure Requirements

Hardware and network capacities must align with system requirements, using licensed software and robust security protocols to ensure continuous operation and data exchange, while security mechanisms like firewalls, multi-factor authentication, and data encryption protect the IT environment. Annual penetration tests, incident reporting to FRA, time synchronization, and comprehensive event logging for at least five years are essential for maintaining security and operational integrity.

Infrastructure-Related Requirements

A disaster recovery strategy matching the main system's specifications must be established at both headquarters and an alternate location, including energy, environmental, and safety controls. Physical security measures, reliable backup power, and efficient energy consumption strategies should be implemented to optimize data center performance and minimize carbon footprint
Document Title: FRA BOD Decree 30/2024: On Standards for the Adoption of Local Carbon Registers.

Family Name: FRA BOD Decree 31/2024: Rules and Regulations of Listing & Delisting Carbon Credits
Family Summary:
Decree No. 31/2024 details the process for listing and delisting carbon credits on Egyptian exchanges.

Registration Process

1) Project Registration with FRA: Before listing, projects must be registered in the FRA's Carbon Reduction Projects Database. This involves submitting an application and relevant documentation, including proof of carbon credit issuance post-Paris Agreement ratification, environmental impact assessments (if applicable), and validation and verification reports.

2) Listing Application to the Exchange: After FRA registration, an application to list carbon credits is submitted to the exchange. This application includes details about the project, the registry, and the carbon credits.

3) Committee Review: The exchange's Steering Committee reviews listing applications and makes decisions within five days.

4) Listing and Trading: Following the committee's approval, carbon credits are listed and traded based on the exchange's rules and regulations.

Disclosure and Delisting

- Disclosure Obligations: Carbon credit owners must inform the exchange about any significant information that might impact trading.

- Optional Delisting: Owners can request to delist carbon credits, for example, for retirement or transfer to a non-tradable account.

- Compulsory Delisting: Circumstances like project removal from the FRA database, violations, or project incompletion can lead to forced delisting. In such cases, the project owner or financer must repurchase the delisted certificates from investors.

Appeals Process: Applicants can appeal against the committee's decisions on listing or delisting. Appeals first go to the Exchange's Board of Directors and, if necessary, can be escalated to the FRA.
Document Title: FRA BOD Decree 31/2024: Rules and Regulations of Listing & Delisting Carbon Credits

Prepared jointly by the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry and the Ministry of the Environment, the roadmap sets out existing and new measures under three main objectives to support the wider implementation of river basin planning among authorities and stakeholders.

  • Objective 1 - Adopt a Whole of Government, Whole of Society Approach to Biodiversity   
  • Objective 2 - Meet Urgent Conservation and Restoration Needs
  • Objective 3 - Secure Nature’s Contribution to People
  • Objective 4 - Enhance the Evidence Base for Action on Biodiversity
  • Objective 5 - Strengthen Ireland’s Contribution to International Biodiversity Initiatives

Actions under the Plan contribute towards climate solutions. For instance, Peatland Finance Ireland combines finance streams from public investments, carbon credits and commercial finance to fund solutions across energy, forestry, water and agriculture. Another example is the advancement of climate and biodiversity research to strengthen the evidence base of the current and future impacts of climate change on biodiversity.

Family Summary:
This Decree lists the powers and responsibilities of the Minister of Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion, who prepares and implements the Government's policy in the areas of sustainable development, territorial cohesion, the fight against territorial inequalities, especially in popular neighborhoods of urban areas and rural territories, the environment, in particular climate and energy efficiency, the protection of nature and biodiversity, the prevention of natural and technological risks, industrial safety, transport and their infrastructure, equipment and housing, urban planning, the city, development and the fight against urban sprawl as well as the sea.

In respect of climate change, in conjunction with interested ministers, they prepare and implement the Government's policy on reducing greenhouse gas emissions, energy efficiency, including renovation and energy performance of buildings, decarbonization and adaptation to climate change. They define and implement, by associating the Minister of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty, the policy on the development of renewable heat as well as the policy on decarbonization and electrification of the road transport sector, in particular, the conversion of the vehicle fleet and the development of charging infrastructures for electric vehicles. They are associated with the Minister of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Soweignty in the development of energy policy, in particular the policy of energy saving certificates and carbon markets, in order, in particular, to ensure the fight against climate change and promote the energy transition.
Document Title: Decree No. 2024-38 of 24 January 2024 on the powers of the Minister of Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion

Family Name: Regulation 65/2024 on the implementation rules for the European Union Cohesion Policy Programme 2021-2027
Family Summary:
Regulation No. 65 establishes the implementation framework for measure 6.1.1.6. "Promoting the use of zero-emission vehicles in municipalities" under specific objective 6.1.1. "Mitigate the economic, social and environmental consequences of the transition to climate neutrality in the regions most affected" of the EU Cohesion Policy. It defines the eligibility requirements for municipalities seeking funding from the Just Transition Fund to acquire zero-emission vehicles, including financial allocations, reporting standards, and the legal responsibilities of the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Regional Development (VARAM).

The objective is to mitigate the socio-economic impacts of the "green transition" in Latvia's most vulnerable regions. By subsidizing zero-emission transport, the program ensures that autonomous municipal functions, such as education, social assistance, and healthcare access remain stable and environmentally sustainable during the shift to a carbon-neutral economy.
Document Title: Regulation 65/2024 on the implementation rules for measure 6.1.1.6. "Promoting the use of zero-emission vehicles in municipalities"

Family Name: Transition Strategy to Promote the Use of Cleaner Technologies and Fuels
Family Summary: The updated Strategy for Transition to Promote the Use of Cleaner Technologies and Fuels, published by Mexico's Ministry of Energy in accordance with the 2015 Energy Transition Law, establishes the policy framework for achieving clean energy and energy efficiency targets whilst reducing fossil fuel dependence under economic viability criteria. This triennial update reveals that clean electricity generation reached 31.2% in 2022, primarily through increased solar photovoltaic and wind capacity, demonstrating progress towards the medium and long-term targets despite obstacles in transmission infrastructure and storage systems. The strategy operationalises Mexico's climate commitments through four strategic lines: energy efficiency and conservation, clean energy deployment, social development integration, and enabling infrastructure development, coordinated across multiple federal institutions.
Document Title: Agreement approving and publishing the updated Transition Strategy to Promote the Use of Cleaner Technologies and Fuels (Acuerdo por el que se aprueba y publica la actualización de la Estrategia de Transición para Promover el Uso de Tecnologías y Combustibles más Limpios)

Family Name: Transition Strategy to Promote the Use of Cleaner Technologies and Fuels
Family Summary: This document represents an update to Mexico's strategy for promoting cleaner technologies and fuels, as mandated by the Ley de Transición Energética (LTE). The strategy aims to guide national policy on clean energy obligations, sustainable energy use, and improvements to the electricity industry in the medium to long term, with the goal of reducing pollutant emissions and the country's dependence on fossil fuels. The update acknowledges challenges, including the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and legal challenges to planning instruments, which have hindered progress towards established clean energy targets, whilst also highlighting the need for greater coordination across government sectors and more in-depth research into energy consumption trends to better inform policy decisions.Despite these obstacles, the update affirms that Mexico is progressing towards a less fossil fuel-dependent economy for electricity generation, with a notable increase in solar photovoltaic and wind energy contributions, reaching 31.2% clean energy generation in 2022. The document also acknowledges that energy efficiency gains have been uneven, necessitating more profound energy efficiency measures to stabilise energy consumption across sectors. The updated strategy emphasises the importance of continued efforts to incorporate cleaner, more efficient technologies and minimise transmission, distribution, and storage challenges to achieve national clean energy goals.
Document Title: Agreement approving and publishing the updated Transition Strategy to Promote the Use of Cleaner Technologies and Fuels (Acuerdo por el que se aprueba y publica la actualización de la Estrategia de Transición para Promover el Uso de Tecnologías y Combustibles más Limpios)

Family Name: New Industry Brazil (Nova Indústria Brasil) 2024-2026
Family Summary:
Nova Indústria Brasil, also known as the Neo-industrialization Action Plan is an industrial policy initiative launched by the Brazilian government in January 2024, aimed at reindustrializing the country by addressing historical challenges and enhancing productivity through innovation and sustainability. The policy focuses on six key missions, including food security, healthcare resilience, and energy transition, with a substantial financial commitment of over BRL 300 billion until 2026 to stimulate technological development and improve Brazil's competitiveness in the global market.

Targets for Mission 5 by 2026 and 2033:

  • Reduce greenhouse gas emissions intensity per product in line with the Climate Plan.
  • Increase the share of biofuels and electric vehicles in transportation to 27% by 2026 and 50% by 2033.
  • Achieve a 10% reduction in carbon emissions from national industry by 2026 and 30% by 2033, while enhancing biodiversity usage.
Document Title: Resolution CNDI/MDIC No. 4, approving New Industry Brazil

Family Name: Indonesia's Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance
Family Summary:
The Indonesian Financial Services Authority (OJK) published the Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance in Indonesia 2024 to help identify activities that support efforts to achieve the countries Sustainable Development Goals, and to increase sustainable capital allocation and financing in order to meet the country’s net zero target by 2060 (or earlier).

On February 11 2025, the OJK published Version 2 of the Taxonomy which expands the Taxonomy’s scope to include additional sectors and updated classification criteria.
Document Title: Version 2 of the Taxonomy
