Family Name: Order (19 January 2024) amending Order No. 4264 Establishing the Organising Committee for COP29
Family Summary: This Order includes more members to the Organising Committee of COP29, modifying the original list in Order No. 4264 dated 13 January 2024.
Document Title: Order (19 January 2024) amending Order No. 4264 Establishing the Organising Committee for COP29

Family Name: Regulations of the Law for the Promotion of the Establishment, Recovery, Restoration, Management, Production, and Protection of Forests in Guatemala (Reglamento de la Ley de fomento al establecimiento, recuperación, restauración, manejo, producción y protección de bosques en Guatemala)
Family Summary:
This regulation serves as the implementing framework for Guatemala’s PROBOSQUE Law, detailing the procedures and mechanisms for its effective application. The regulation aligns with the objectives of the parent law, aiming to increase forest cover, promote sustainable forest management, and enhance rural livelihoods through targeted incentives. It outlines specific provisions for project eligibility, incentive allocation, and compliance requirements, ensuring the programme’s alignment with national environmental and developmental priorities.

The regulation reinforces PROBOSQUE’s climate change mitigation and adaptation goals by establishing clear criteria for forest conservation and restoration projects. It defines eligible activities, such as industrial and energy-oriented forest plantations, agroforestry systems, and the restoration of degraded forest lands, all of which contribute to carbon sequestration and biodiversity preservation. The regulation prioritises projects in protected areas, watersheds, and areas of high ecological value, ensuring that incentives are directed toward regions with significant climate benefits. For energy transition, the regulation supports the development of forest plantations for biomass production, promoting renewable energy sources while reducing pressure on natural forests. Additionally, it mandates fire prevention measures and pest management to safeguard forest health, enhancing ecosystem resilience to climate change. The establishment of monitoring and evaluation mechanisms ensures transparency and accountability in project implementation, further reinforcing the regulation’s role in advancing Guatemala’s climate and energy objectives.
Document Title: National Forest Institute - Minutes Number: JD.35.2023 (Instituto Nacional de Bosques -  Acta Número: JD.35.2023)

Family Name: Energy Efficiency Strategy and Action Plan 2024-2030
Family Summary: Turkey's Energy Efficiency Strategy and Action Plan 2024-2030 was announced in January 2024 by the Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar, outlining a comprehensive approach to enhance energy efficiency across various sectors. The plan aims to invest $20.2 billion in energy efficiency measures by 2030, targeting a 16% reduction in primary energy consumption, which is expected to result in 100 million tons of CO2 equivalent greenhouse gas reduction and create new job opportunities in the green energy sector.
Document Title: Enerji Verimliliği 2030 Stratejisi ve II. Ulusal Enerji Verimliliği Eylem Planı (2024-2030)

The plan aims to invest $20.2 billion in energy efficiency measures by 2030, targeting a 16% reduction in primary energy consumption, which is expected to result in 100 million tons of CO2 equivalent greenhouse gas reduction and create new job opportunities in the green energy sector.
Document Title: Energy Efficiency 2030 Strategy and 2nd National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (2024-2030)

Family Name: Scaling Up Early Warning Systems Implementation Roadmap 2023-2027
Family Summary:
This Roadmap serves as a strategic guide to drive initiatives spanning national to local levels, channel investments towards enhancing Early Warning Systems for more effective Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), and facilitate the seamless integration of comprehensive early warning mechanisms. Early warning systems (EWS) are key elements of disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation, as they help reduce or avoid the detrimental impacts of hazardous events. Organisations are encouraged to incorporate these actions into their operational frameworks, aligning with their primary and supportive responsibilities. This harmonisation ensures the optimal utilisation of resources across the spectrum from national to local levels.

The primary objective of this Roadmap is to provide the national and local governments with a structured blueprint for fortifying a people-centric Early Warning System in Maldives through targeted actions and resource allocation. This Roadmap stems from an extensive gap analysis of Maldives’ EWS, which included the application of a Minimum Core Capability Checklist in the form of a workshop and a series of consultation meetings.
Document Title: Scaling Up Early Warning Systems Implementation Roadmap 2023-2027

Family Name: Order Establishing the Organising Committee for COP29
Family Summary: This Order appoints members of the organising committee for COP29, comprised of representatives from various Ministries, government agencies and state companies. The Order mandates that the organising committee prepare and implement an action plan for the organisation and holding of COP29, take measures to establish an operating company and ensure the financing for the implementation of said action plan.
Document Title: Order Establishing the Organising Committee for COP29

Family Name: Oman's Sustainable Finance Framework
Family Summary:
In January 2024, the Government of Oman, represented by the Ministry of Finance, took a historic step and unveiled a sustainable finance framework to aims to reduce its reliance on fossil fuels and attract environmental, social and governance (ESG) investors in line with the Government's efforts to promote foreign direct investment in the country. 

The framework outlines Oman's plans to issue financial instruments like green, social and sustainable bonds as well as loans and sukuks (i.e. bonds that comply with Islamic law) whose proceeds will be used to fund and refinance renewable energy projects. The framework emphasises Oman's commitment to addressing climate change including publishing its first update of the second Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) in November 2023, which demonstrates the country's ongoing commitment to address the climate emergency and offers a comprehensive view of Oman's ambition to achieve net zero GHG emissions by 2050 by transitioning to sustainable, low-carbon economy as well as striving towards economic diversification.
Document Title: Sustainable Finance Framework

Family Name: Updated Nationally Determined Contribution
Family Summary: This NDC sets the target to reduce the national net GHG emissions by 23% to 25% by 2030 compared with the reference year of 2005, and to realise net zero in 2050. The main actions to achieve this target are to reform the legal system for the amnagement of energy and electricity; transforming energy sources; green finance; carbon pricing; and international cooperation under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. It also outlines the number of adaptation actions taken.
Document Title: Updated Nationally Determined Contribution

Family Name: Egypt's National Low Carbon Hydrogen Strategy
Family Summary: Egypt launched its National Low-Carbon Hydrogen Strategy in August 2024, aiming to capture 5-8% of the global tradeable hydrogen market by 2040 and contribute $18 billion to its GDP. The strategy involves a phased approach with significant investments, targeting the production of 3.8-5.6 million tons of hydrogen annually by 2040 and creating over 100,000 new job opportunities through green hydrogen development.
Document Title: Egypt’s National Low Carbon Hydrogen Strategy – FULL Version

Family Name: Council of Ministers Resolution n.º 11/2024 - Approves the National Long-Term Strategy for Combating Energy Poverty 2023-2050.
Family Summary:
It approves the National Long-Term Strategy for Combating Energy Poverty 2023-2050. Embedded in the NECP 2030, it is established as an action point for the approval of a long-term strategy for combating energy poverty by elaborating the National Long-Term Strategy for Combating Energy Poverty (ELPPE, Portuguese acronym) 2023-2050.
The main goal of the ELPPE is to eradicate energy poverty in Portugal by 2050, protecting vulnerable consumers and actively integrating them into the energy and climate transition, which aims to be fair, democratic, and cohesive This resolution approves the ELPPE presented in its annex I and establishes further long term targets relative to the building sector.
Document Title: Council of Ministers Resolution 11/2024

Family Name: The Ministry of National Education Disaster and Emergency Management Action Plan (2023–2030)
Family Summary: This Action Plan aims to create disaster and emergency awareness, improve preparedness measures for disasters and emergencies, improve response services in disasters and emergencies, and improve recovery efforts after disasters and emergencies, in view of climate change-induced disasters.
Document Title: The Ministry of National Education Disaster and Emergency Management Action Plan (2023–2030)

Family Name: Interim Regulations on Carbon Emission Trading Management
Family Summary: This document regulates carbon emissions trading and related activities to promote carbon neutrality and low-carbon development in China. The Ecological Department of the State Council is responsible for managing and overseeing carbon emission rights trading. Carbon emission rights trading products include carbon emission quotas, among others.
Document Title: Interim Regulations on Carbon Emission Trading Management

Family Name: Decree-Law n.º 4/2024 - Establishes the voluntary carbon market and sets the rules for its operation.
Family Summary:
The decree establishes the voluntary carbon market, providing a framework for emission offset actions and financial contributions to climate action by individuals and organisations (both public and private). It allows these entities to meet their emission reduction goals and climate strategies by issuing, trading, and cancelling certified carbon credits. Projects and credits are registered on a public platform for tracking purposes.
Article 6 sets the requirements for the carbon projects, article 9 the methodology and article 10 the approval of the development, evaluation and approval of the projects.
Document Title: Decree-Law n.º 4/2024

Family Name: Interim Regulations on the Management of Carbon Emissions Trading
Family Summary: The Regulations set out the various authorities' responsibilities in relation to carbon emissions trading and rules on reporting and verification. The relevant environmental department in the local government is responsible for the transactions in its administrative region. The types of greenhouse gases and scope of industries covered are determined nationally, by the competent environmental department of the State Council in conjunction with other relevant departments such as relating to development and reform.
Document Title: Interim Regulations on the Management of Carbon Emissions Trading

Family Name: Directive on a national coordinator for the expansion of nuclear power (Dir. 2024:1)
Family Summary:
This Directive mandates that a special investigator shall, in the role of national coordinator, support the government's work to promote new nuclear power with the aim of achieving an effective expansion of nuclear power in accordance with the roadmap for new nuclear power in Sweden that the Sweden Democrats, the Moderates, the Christian Democrats and the Liberals have agreed on in an addendum to the Tidö Agreement.

Nuclear power will have a crucial role both in restoring a reliable and secure electricity supply and in achieving an effective climate transition. An expansion of nuclear power requires decisions and actions by a number of actors in society, such as authorities, municipalities, power companies, grid companies, suppliers, customers, developers and financiers. Many actors are thus involved in the process that leads to the construction of new nuclear power.

The coordinator shall, among other things, support the Government Offices in following up and analyzing how the work on the expansion of nuclear power is progressing and identifying the need for complementary measures in order to drive the work forward, and be a contact point for stakeholders and actors in the nuclear power sector and collaborate with them in order to increase the pace of the establishment of new nuclear power. The assignment shall be finalised no later than 31 December 2026.
Document Title: Directive on a national coordinator for the expansion of nuclear power (Dir. 2024:1)

Family Name: Integrated Resource Plan for Electricity (IRP)
Family Summary: Capacity targets to 2030 underline the decreasing share of coal in total installed capacity from 93% in 2011 to 46% in 2030 and substantial share of nuclear, 12.7% by 2030.
Document Title: Integrated Resource Plan for Electricity (IRP)

Family Name: Integrated Resource Plan 2023
Family Summary: This policy outlines a two-part strategy to pursue a diversified energy mix, in order to provide a secure electricity supply and comply with South Africa's emissions reduction plan. The near-term plan, Horizon One (2023–2030), aims to stabilise South Africa’s power supply. The IRP proposes a mix of gas, solar, wind, and battery storage to eliminate load-shedding. For Horizon Two (2031–2050), five pathways are evaluated, including renewable transitions, delayed coal shutdowns, and cleaner coal technologies.
Document Title: Integrated Resource Plan 2023

Collection Summary: The UK Climate Change Act, first passed in 2008 and amended in 2019, is the UK's framework law for the transition to a low-carbon economy, creating an obligation for the government to set legally-binding carbon budgets to act as stepping stones towards an overall 2050 emissions reduction target.
Family Name: The Vehicle Emissions Trading Schemes Order (S.I. 1394/2023)
Family Summary: This Order was made in terms of the Climate Change Act 2008. It establishes a zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) mandate and CO2 emissions standards for cars and vans in Great Britain. It requires manufacturers to ensure that 80% of new vehicles and 70% of new vans sold are zero-emission by 2030, increasing to 100% by 2035. It also sets a fine for qualifying manufacturers failing to meet the targets and allows them to purchase credits from manufacturers with a surplus.
Document Title: The Vehicle Emissions Trading Schemes Order 2023

Family Name: 2030 Strategic Plan to Reduce Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Achieve Green Growth in the Livestock Industry
Family Summary:
The goal is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the livestock industry to 7.7 million tonnes, down by 18% from 9.4 million tonnes in 2018. To this end, the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs will improve the treatment of livestock waste by transforming it into bioenergy, biochar, and solid fuels; carry out livestock management by providing low-methane-emitting feed; and improve the productivity of livestock species.

The Strategy contains measures to:

  1. Directly reduce the amount of generation by managing greenhouse gas emissions in the livestock sector;
  2. Reduce greenhouse gases in other fields by using the livestock industry
  3. Shifting the field's high-in-feed livestock breeding practice to low-in-low-in and low-emission structure; and
  4. Induce the voluntary carbon reduction of farmers to improve the transition power of livestock farmers.
Document Title: 2030 Strategic Plan to Reduce Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Achieve Green Growth in the Livestock Industry

Family Name: Official Mexican Standard for carbon dioxide emissions applicable to new light vehicles (NOM-163) [Norma Oficial Mexicana de emisiones de bióxido de carbono aplicable a vehículos ligeros nuevos (NOM-163)]
Family Summary: Norma Oficial Mexicana NOM-163-SEMARNAT-SCFI-2023 is a Mexican official standard that regulates the carbon dioxide pemissions from the exhaust of new motor vehicles with a gross vehicle weight up to 3,857 kilograms. This regulation updates and replaces a previous 2013 standard, introducing more stringent, gradual emission limits for new light-duty vehicles from model year 2025 onwards. The policy establishes a framework for calculating corporate average emissions targets and observed values, while also providing mechanisms for compliance. These include a system of credits for the introduction of highly efficient and innovative technologies, such as hybrid, electric, and fuel-cell vehicles, and a compensation mechanism where non-compliance can be offset through economic contributions to climate change projects.

Family Name: Mujib Climate Prosperity Plan 2022-2041
Family Summary:
This plan aims to secure Bangladesh's propserity by 2041, launching an economic transformation with actions that: increase growth by maximising resilience with loss and damage financing; strengthen employment in a green economy; promote well-being; secure resilience and energy independence and energy security. 

The plan includes an aim to reach 30% renewable energy by 2030 and up to 40% by 2041, with grid resilience and modernisation. It also sets out a "new economic vision for people-centric resilient growth", with plans to have 4.1 million new climate-resilience jobs by 2030. One of the key priority areas is the just transition of labour and future-proofing industry with technology transfer.
Document Title: Mujib Climate Prosperity Plan 2022-2041

Collection Name: Law 7/2021 on climate change and energy transition [Spain]
Collection Summary:
Enacted in 2021, this law establishes Spain's legal framework for achieving climate neutrality by 2050, aligning with the Paris Agreement and Sustainable Development Goals. It mandates a 23% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 (compared to 1990 levels), alongside ambitious renewable energy targets, including 42% of final energy consumption from renewables and 74% renewable electricity generation by 2030. Energy efficiency measures aim for a 39.5% reduction in primary energy consumption within the same timeframe. The law also prohibits new hydrocarbon and radioactive mineral exploitation, requires emission-free transport systems in cities with populations exceeding 50,000, and emphasises sustainable urban mobility.

The legislation includes a national Just Transition Strategy to ensure equitable economic opportunities, particularly for vulnerable regions, while fostering adaptation and resilience to climate risks across critical sectors such as water, biodiversity, and health. It creates governance mechanisms like the Expert Committee on Climate Change and Energy Transition to monitor progress and updates to Spain's Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC). Projecting investments exceeding €200 billion by 2030, the law is expected to enhance Spain’s GDP by €16.5–25.7 billion annually and generate 250,000–350,000 new jobs. The focus on education, innovation, and public awareness underscores its commitment to a holistic and inclusive transition.

This collection represent a body of policies, strategies, and plans enacted under this law.
Family Name: Strategic Action Plan of the Institute for Just Transition (ITJ), 2024-2026
Family Summary: The Strategic Action Plan of the Institute for Just Transition (ITJ), 2024-2026, outlines key objectives and initiatives to ensure a fair and inclusive ecological transition in Spain. In compliance with legal requirements, the plan builds on previous strategies (2021-2023) and aligns with the Climate Change and Energy Transition Law. It includes evaluating the first Just Transition Strategy (2019), preparing a new one for 2025, and advancing initiatives in areas impacted by coal, nuclear, and thermal power plant closures. Key areas of focus include gender equality, youth inclusion, managing European Just Transition Fund resources, fostering national and international dialogues, and enhancing communication tools. The ITJ aims to promote modernised, diversified economies and support vulnerable communities while driving internal transformation for greater efficiency and accountability.
Document Title: Strategic Action Plan of the Institute for Just Transition (ITJ), 2024-2026

Family Name: Action Plan for the Institute for Just Transition (ITJ) - 2024
Family Summary: The 2024 Action Plan for the Institute for Just Transition (ITJ) outlines strategic priorities for advancing a fair and inclusive ecological transition in Spain. Key focus areas include evaluating the current Just Transition Strategy, initiating the preparation of the new 2025 strategy, and supporting regions affected by economic and environmental shifts through agreements, infrastructure, and training programs. The ITJ will also enhance international collaboration, improve internal organisational processes, modernise its digital tools, and strengthen communication and public engagement. Transformation initiatives include updating staffing frameworks, implementing new financial management protocols, upgrading information systems for aid management, and fostering collaborative work environments. Through these efforts, the ITJ aims to promote sustainability, inclusivity, and operational excellence while addressing the socio-economic challenges of the energy transition.
Document Title: Action Plan for the Institute for Just Transition (ITJ) - 2024

Collection Name: Singapore's Green Data Centre Roadmap Implementation
Collection Summary: This Roadmap charts a sustainable pathway for the continued growth of data centres in Singapore to support its ambitions for the digital economy.
Family Name: Driving a Greener Digital Future: Singapore's Green Data Centre Roadmap
Family Summary: This Roadmap charts a sustainable pathway for the continued growth of data centres in Singapore to support its ambitions for the digital economy. Singapore aims to provide at least 300 megawatts of additional capacity in the near term, with much more through green energy deployments. According to Singapore's second NDC, demand-side measures to reduce energy and resultant emissions, such as this Roadmap, form a key thrust of its decarbonisation strategy.
Document Title: Driving a Greener Digital Future: Singapore's Green Data Centre Roadmap

Family Name: Long Term Climate Vision
Family Summary:
This is a long-term vision for a net-zero-emission and climate resilient development strategy in Lesotho. It has been developed with the support of the African Development Bank (AfDB) and 2050 Pathways Platform, and with funding from the Africa NDC Hub. It aims to achieve carbon neutrality while ensuring equitable socio-economic growth by 2050.

As Lesotho's economy is based on agriculture, its ecosystems and economic activities are highly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. Key areas of action/ measures that have been identified in the LTV formulation process as central to delivering the long-term vision include:

• Supporting climate resilient and low-carbon production and value chains in agriculture, forestry and livestock management

• Implementing a climate-smart land-use regulatory framework

• Developing climate-resilient water supply systems

• Improving climate information and advisory services

• Establish early warning systems and move towards proactive risk management

• Creating financial instruments to support climate action

• Mainstreaming climate change in education and institutionalizing indigenous knowledge

• Integrating climate change considerations in public procurement

• Encouraging low-carbon, increasingly electrified mobility and climate-resilient transport links

• Leveraging increasingly affordable clean technologies powered by renewables (e-mobility, batteries)

• Developing a renewable and resilient electricity system

• Encouraging a resource-efficient circular economy
Document Title: Long Term Climate Vision

Family Name: National Bioeconomy Strategy until 2035
Family Summary: The National Bioeconomy Strategy until 2035 aims to analyse and summarise Croatia's overarching directions and potential for development in the bioeconomy - that is, sectors primarily involved with renewable biomass-based commodities and services such as agriculture and forestry. It highlights growth in the bioeconomy as a key alternative to fossil fuel-led development, through economic usage of biomass byproducts such as from olive oil production, and general improvements in agricultural efficiency. The strategy aims to promote bioeconomic growth through a range of funding streams, but also through regulatory change to enable enhanced usage of wood and biodegradable plastics, which lack a regulatory framework at the time of writing.
Document Title: National Bioeconomy Strategy until 2035

Family Name: Resilience Program for the Safeguarding of the Fatherland (PRSP)
Family Summary:
The Resilience Program for the Safeguarding of the Fatherland (Programme de Résilience pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie - PRSP, 2024-2026) is Niger's core national strategy aimed at guiding the country out of its current crisis, with a global objective to impulse a new dynamic of endogenous development. The PRSP was formulated in a challenging context marked by several overlapping crises of Geopolitical Instability, Environmental degradation intensified by the effects of climate change (such as droughts and floods), Socio-Demographic Pressure, and Security and Migration.

The PRSP is intended to establish this new vision, redefine relations with international partners based on mutual interests, and leverage the growing influence of new actors and channels of communication to mobilise the population. The core strategy focuses on sovereignty and responsibility, mandating the effective participation of all citizens to achieve the plan's goals.
Document Title: Resilience Program for the Safeguarding of the Fatherland (PRSP)

Family Name: Fiji National Development Plan 2025-2029 and Vision 2050
Family Summary:
This Plan covers all dimensions of development – economy, social, environment and governance. In terms of the economy, the Plan identifies strategies to catalyse economic growth and build greater resilience, among others through diversification of the economy, moving up the value chain, promoting greater participation of the private sector in the economy and increasing the contribution of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. The Plan sets out to enhance the social wellbeing of the Fijian people by alleviating poverty and providing better quality of education, housing, healthcare and transport as well as increasing access to clean water, electrification, sanitation and the development of our rural and outer islands. The Plan also puts in place policies and strategies to conserve our environment and strengthen resilience to the impacts of climate change and natural disasters.

Examples of climate-related policies in this Plan are:

  • Implement vulnerability assessments, and climate change and natural hazards impact projections in infrastructure and urban planning;
  • Build resilient communities through disaster risk management on the impacts of climate change in iTaukei communities;
  • Improve resilience of energy infrastructure to the impacts of climate change and natural disasters;
  • Operationalise the Warsaw International Mechanism (WIM) for Loss and Damage; and
  • Reduce reliance on imported fossil fuels and gradually decarbonise the transport sector.
Document Title: Fiji National Development Plan 2025-2029 and Vision 2050

Family Name: Low-Carbon Roadmap for the Turkish Cement Sector
Family Summary: Cement producers exporting to the EU will be expected to report their direct and indirect CO2 emissions and implement emission reduction measures. Rapid implementation of carbon reduction measures in the cement sector, which accounts for a high amount of emissions, is of critical importance for the sector and to achieve Turkey's net zero target by 2053. This low-carbon roadmap for the Turkish cement sector will form the basis for the development of an investment plan and platform that will bring together relevant actors and support the implementation of relevant actions by sharing a common vision for the sector.
Document Title: Low-Carbon Roadmap for the Turkish Cement Sector

Family Name: Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2024-2030
Family Summary: The Climate Change Adaptation Plan sets out measures and motivations for increased adaptation and preparedness for the effects of climate change. It notes 243 million euros in recent climate damage nationally, and calls for a wide range of adaptation measures across sectors. Finally, it suggests funding sources for adaptation measures, and recommends a set of indicator statistics to track and enhance adaptation progress. Pre-existing and suggested measures in the plan include: public awareness campaigning; improving risk-mapping tools; technological improvement in agriculture; formation of reserve crisis teams within government services; mainstreaming green urbanism; wetland restoration.
Document Title: Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2024-2030

Family Name: 2024 National Waste Policy Action Plan
Family Summary:
The 2024 National Waste Policy Action Plan implements the 2018 National Waste Policy, which provides a framework for waste and resource recovery in Australia to achieve sustainable development goals (SDGs), including SDG 13: Climate Action. It includes targets and priorities to guide investment and efforts to 2030.

The seven targets are:

  1. Ban on export of waste plastic, paper, glass and tyres, commencing in the second half of 2020;
  2. Reduce total waste generated in Australia by 10% per person by 2030;
  3. 80% average resource recovery rate from all waste streams following the waste hierarchy by 2030;
  4. Significantly increase the use of recycled content by governments and industry;
  5. Continued phase out of problematic and unnecessary plastics;
  6. Halve the amount of organic waste sent to landfill for disposal by 2030; and
  7. Make comprehensive, economy-wide and timely data publicly available to support better consumer, investment and policy decisions.
Document Title: 2024 National Waste Policy Action Plan

Family Name: Australia's Strategy for Nature 2024-2030
Family Summary:
The Strategy for Nature is a shared roadmap to better understand, care for and sustainably manage nature. One of the targets is to minimise the impact of climate change on biodiversity. The goals are to:

  1. Connect all Australians with nature;
  2. Care for nature in all its diversity; and
  3. Share and build knowledge.
Document Title: Australia's Strategy for Nature 2024-2030

Family Name: Australian Government Drought Plan
Family Summary:
This plan covers the period from 2024 to 2029. It is focused on farming businesses and communities, who are mostaffected by drought, particularly in the context of climate change.

The Australian Government’s approach to supporting the agricultural sector to manage drought is built around a3-stage cycle:• Preparing – before drought, prepare for drier times ahead;• Responding – during drought, implement plans and strategies to manage the impacts; and• Recovering – after drought, recover and consider lessons learned.

The purpose of this plan is to:• explain the Australian Government’s drought policy;• provide greater transparency about government drought decision-making;• specify key drought-related programs that support farming businesses and communities across the drought cycle;• show how governments and stakeholders can work together on drought-related issues;• explain the monitoring, evaluation and learning arrangements for drought policy; and• show how drought policy links to other government policies.
Document Title: Australian Government Drought Plan

Family Name: Australia’s Circular Economy Framework
Family Summary:
The framework defines a circular economy for Australia and outlines its benefits. The framework offers businesses:

  • clear guidance
  • priorities
  • real-world examples to cut emissions and waste.

The framework will help Australia’s circular economy transition under a new national ambition to double Australia's circularity by 2035 and achieve the following targets:

  • Shrink Australia's per capita material footprint by 10%.
  • Lift Australia's material productivity by 30%.
  • Safely recover 80% of Australia's resources.

The priority sectors are: industry; the built environment; agriculture and food; and resources.
Document Title: Australia’s Circular Economy Framework

Family Name: National Reform Programme
Family Summary: he National Reform Programme of the Czech Republic (NRP), prepared annually within the EU’s European Semester framework, outlines planned government reforms and major public investments for the coming year in response to the European Commission’s 2023 Country Report and the Council’s 2023 Country Specific Recommendations. The 2024 NRP follows EC guidelines and places strong emphasis on climate and energy policy, acknowledging the country’s continued reliance on fossil fuels while reaffirming commitments to phase out coal by 2033 and reach climate neutrality by 2050. Although coal still accounts for a significant portion of electricity generation—declining from 50.4% in 2016 to 40.2% in 2021 and 43.4% in 2022—the programme outlines measures to accelerate the green transition, including support for sustainable transport, cleaner energy sources, expanded recycling and biodiversity initiatives, forestry and watercourse management, as well as renovations of buildings and heating system replacements.
Document Title: National Reform Programme

Family Name: NollCO2 2.0 Green Building Certification Framework
Family Summary:
The Sweden Green Building Council's (SGBC)NollCO2 certification has become a key standard for minimising building climate impact. The framework covers both new construction and refurbishments.

Developed in response to the EU’s 2050 climate neutrality goals and Sweden’s own 2045 net-zero target, NollCO2 is designed to push the construction and real estate sector toward radical emissions reductions across a building’s entire lifecycle. The framework is focused on immediate carbon reduction through verified life-cycle assessment (LCA) and limited offsetting, and shapes market behaviour in Sweden and influences design, procurement, and construction decisions from the earliest planning stages.
Document Title: NollCO2 2.0 Green Building Certification Framework

Family Name: Climate Adaptation Plan 1
Family Summary:
Denmark is a flat country with several thousand kilometers of coastline and countless islands, and is particularly vulnerable when sea levels and groundwater rise as a result of climate change.

Climate Adaptation Plan 1 includes, among other things:

  1. Government commitment to vulnerable coastal areas: The state will offer professional help to the municipalities, for example, in choosing a technical solution, developing a payment model, financial calculations or environmental assessments, depending on how far along the municipalities are in the project phase and what they want help with.
  2. Solution to the challenges of high groundwater levels: The government will give municipalities the authority to handle high groundwater levels and make it possible for wastewater companies to create collective solutions in areas where it is profitable for society.
  3. Extension of the coastal protection pool: To speed up climate adaptation, the government will extend the coastal protection pool in 2024 by 150 million kroner. Municipalities can apply for joint coastal protection projects throughout the country and the establishment or reinforcement of dikes in the Wadden Sea.
  4. Protection of Denmark's west coast: It is proposed to allocate more than 1 billion kroner to protect the west coast through sand replenishment and investments in critical lock and coastal facilities in Thorsminde and Hvide Sande.
  5. New advisory committee of civil servants: The government will establish a permanent committee of civil servants at department head level to continuously advise the government on the next steps in Denmark's climate adaptation. The committee may also establish rapid working groups with relevant parties to solve climate adaptation challenges across sectors.
Document Title: Climate Adaptation Plan 1

Family Name: Kenya Fourth Medium Term Plan (2023-2027)
Family Summary:
This Plan is the the final five-year development blueprint for Kenya Vision 2030.

For the environment and natural resources sector, the targeted interventions on adaptation and mitigation to climate change aim to create green jobs and reduce greenhouse gas emissions, build community resilience in Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASALs); and reduce human wildlife conflicts in vulnerable counties.
Document Title: Kenya Fourth Medium Term Plan (2023-2027)

Family Name: Ahti Programme: Improving the State of Waters and Marine Areas
Family Summary: The Ahti Programme for Improving the State of Waters and the Sea (2024–2027) aims to improve the ecological and chemical status of Finland’s surface and groundwater and the condition of the Baltic Sea. It continues and integrates the work of the Water Protection Enhancement Programme (2019–2023), the Nutrient Recycling Programme (2012–2023) and the Archipelago Sea Programme. Its four main priorities are reducing nutrient loading, improving soil structure, controlling hazardous substances, and recovering and reusing resources. The programme promotes catchment-based water management, restoration and pollution reduction, with particular emphasis on reducing nutrient loading in the Archipelago Sea catchment and improving the recycling of agricultural nutrients.
Document Title: Annual Plan Ahti Programme 2024

Family Name: Electric Vehicle Import Mandate and ICE Vehicle Ban
Family Summary: Ethiopia announced a ban on the importation of gasoline and diesel vehicles on January 29, 2024, becoming the first country in the world to implement such a policy, with the aim of reducing fuel import costs and air pollution. It is enforced through a combination of prohibitively high import duties on internal combustion engine vehicles and duty-free imports for electric and hybrid vehicles.
Document Title: Electric Vehicle Import Mandate and ICE Vehicle Ban

Family Name: Social Housing Energy Performance Initiative
Family Summary:
The Social Housing Energy Performance Initiative (SHEPI) is funding upgrades to help social housing residents access the benefits of the energy transformation.

SHEPI is delivering a range of upgrade types, including: thermal shell upgrades such as shading and insulation, installation of efficient electric appliances such as heating and cooling, hot water systems, ovens and cooktops, solar systems such as solar panels and batteries. The Australian Government is investing $800 million to co-fund the $1.1 billion SHEPI program in partnership with all state and territory governments.

The government announced its initial $300 million investment as part of the $1.7 billion Energy Savings Package in the 2023-24 Budget. On 30 November 2024, it announced an additional $500 million over 4 years from 2025-26.
Document Title: Social Housing Energy Performance Initiative (SHEPI)

Family Name: Indicative Plan for the Expansion of Electricity Coverage 2024 - 2028
Family Summary: Indicative Plan for the Expansion of Electricity Coverage is a multi-year indicative plan from Colombia's UPME for expanding electricity access nationwide. It serves as a strategic planning tool that identifies unserved households, proposes cost-optimized solutions like grid extensions and renewables, and quantifies required investments to reach universal coverage (investment of about 32.24 trillion Colombian pesos). The indicative plan proposes three main solutions for expanding electricity coverage: first, isolated hybrid systems configured as microgrids, which account for 46.8% of the total value and require an investment of about 15.09 trillion pesos; second, connecting homes directly to the existing distribution network, representing 29.21% with around 9.42 trillion pesos in investment; and third, individual isolated photovoltaic systems, making up 23.99% at an estimated cost of 7.73 trillion pesos.
Document Title: Indicative Plan for the Expansion of Electricity Coverage 2024 - 2028 (Plan Indicativo de Expansión de la Cobertura de Energía Eléctrica 2024-2028)

Family Name: Jordan National Urban Policy
Family Summary: Jordan's National Urban Policy (2023) recognises climate change as a key threat to the wellbeing and economic function of the country, and aims to promote both adaptation and mitigation measures for these threats in urban environments. It suggests a range of measures from institutional capacity building to more physical interventions in the urban environment. The policy seeks to: improve water conservation; improve geospatial databases for natural assets; develop enhanced standards for air quality; plan land use around public transportation; provide equitable access to green jobs.
Document Title: National Urban Policy

Family Name: Decree Law No.4/2024 (establishing the domestic voluntary carbon market)
Family Summary: This Decree establishes the domestic voluntary carbon market (VCM) and establishes the rules for its operation. According to the Decree, VCMs, by generating economic incentives to reduce emissions or increase carbon sequestration, strengthen the cost-effectiveness of GHG mitigation measures and promote innovative solutions and technologies, are an instrument that supports the fulfillment of national climate action objectives, accelerating the transition to a carbon-neutral society and strengthening the commitment to the Sustainable Development Goals of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development. It also contributes to combating biodiversity loss, improving the conservation status of natural heritage and promoting recognition of its value,
Document Title: Decree Law No.4/2024 (establishing the domestic voluntary carbon market)

Family Name: Multiannual Sectoral Strategic Plan for Transport and Communications 2024-2030 (Plan Estratégico Sectorial Multianual de Transporte y Comunicaciones 2024-2030)
Family Summary: The Multiannual Sectoral Strategic Plan (Plan Estratégico Sectorial Multianual "PESEM") 2024–2030 for Transport and Communications in Peru aims to align sectoral development with the National Strategic Development Plan (PEDN 2050) and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It prioritises four strategic objectives: enhancing security and reliability of transport and communication systems; expanding access to quality services nationwide; improving competitiveness through sustainable and resilient infrastructure; and strengthening governance to ensure regulatory compliance. The plan explicitly addresses climate change and energy transition challenges, recognising the need for infrastructure resilient to extreme weather events, such as floods, earthquakes, and cyclones, which threaten service continuity and economic stability. Measures include adopting international standards for climate-resilient infrastructure, integrating risk management into planning, and promoting sustainable transport modes to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.
Document Title: PESEM Multi-Year Sectoral Strategic Plan 2024-2030 (Plan Estratégico Sectorial Multianual PESEM 2024 - 2030)

Family Name: Agreement amending the Operating Rules of the Program for the Comprehensive Well-being of Indigenous Peoples for fiscal year 2024 (Acuerdo que modifica las Reglas de Operación del Programa para el Bienestar Integral de los Pueblos Indígenas, para el ejercicio fiscal 2024)
Family Summary: This policy establishes the operational rules for Mexico’s 2024 Programme for the Integral Well-being of Indigenous Peoples (PROBIPI), administered by the National Institute of Indigenous Peoples (INPI). It aims to advance the development of 68 recognised indigenous and Afro-Mexican communities as collective rights holders, emphasising self-determination, cultural preservation, and territorial integrity. The programme supports community-led projects across five pillars: rights implementation, economic development, infrastructure, cultural heritage, and healthcare. Key mechanisms include participatory planning, direct resource transfers, and coordination with federal agencies to address structural inequalities. Projects must align with indigenous governance systems and cultural practices, prioritising collective benefits over individual aid.The policy integrates climate change and energy transition objectives through dedicated funding for mitigation and adaptation actions. It finances ecosystem conservation, sustainable resource management, and climate-resilient practices (e.g., agroecology, community-based tourism) under its "Fortification of Indigenous Economies and Environment" component. It supports community-owned "gas stations for well-being" to improve energy access in remote regions while promoting low-carbon economic chains. The programme explicitly prohibits funding for fossil fuel-dependent activities (e.g., livestock purchases, vehicle acquisitions) and infrastructure unrelated to climate goals, instead favouring renewable energy-compatible initiatives like sustainable agriculture and nature-based tourism.

Family Name: Lithuania's Future Vision: Lithuania 2050
Family Summary: 'Lithuania 2050' sets out a vision for the development of long term reforms and strategic aspirations, and aims to represent a broad sample of Lithuanian society. The vision acknowledges climate change both as a major threat to economic and social development, and a key opportunity for green and sustainable growth. It enshrines emissions reduction and eventual climate neutrality as overarching strategic goals which synergise with other developmental aspirations. The vision calls for green reform in a range of areas such as disaster preparedness systems, urbanism and international co-operation/financing. It also stresses the importance of second-order effects such as climate-driven migration, and the need for future society to adapt to the corresponding geopolitics.
Document Title: Lithuania's Future Vision: Lithuania 2050

Family Name: Ministerial Decree 436/2023 (“Agrivoltaic Decree”)
Family Summary: This Decree, implements article 14, paragraph 1, letter c), of Legislative Decree No. 199/2021, and contains criteria and methods to identify agrophotovoltaic systems of experimental nature entitled to receive an incentive established by the Decree, in line with the measures to support the planned investments from the PNRR for a total power output of at least 1.04 GW and an indicative production of at least 1,300 GWh/year. The criteria are established in article 5 and 6. All in all, the beneficiaries are farmers. The decree ends its force on 31 July 2026.
Document Title: Ministerial Decree 436/2023 (“Agrivoltaic Decree”)

Collection Summary: This law contains provisions on the government's climate policy work, what the work will be aimed at and how it should be conducted. It provides that the Government will pursue a climate policy that (1) aims to prevent dangerous interference with the climate system, (2) helps to protect ecosystems and the present and future generations from the harmful effects of climate change, (3) focuses on reducing emissions of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases and to maintain and create features in the environment to combat climate change and its adverse effects, and (4) is based on evidence and on relevant technical, social, economic and environmental considerations. The Government's climate policy efforts should be based on the long-term, time-bound emission targets set by Parliament. The Government is also required to provide an annual climate report to Parliament in the Budget, and to develop a climate action plan every four years. The Act entered into force on January 1st, 2018.

Family Summary: The National Programme for Research and Innovation for the years 2024-2027 sets out priority areas for research and innovation, as well as setting targets for increased research spending overall. The programme aims to contribute to sustainable development, alongside reversing a decline in research sector employment. Strategic directions given in the policy include sustrainable and resilient agriculture, energy efficiency technologies, green transport, emission-free industry, energy storage and clean energy development.

Family Name: Climate Action Plan 2024
Family Summary:
On December 20th, 2023, Ireland approved the Climate Action Plan 2024 (CAP24), the third annual update to Ireland's Climate Action Plan. CAP24 along with Ireland's Long-term Climate Strategy, sets out the strategic direction for meeting the country's climate targets, specifically a 51% reduction emissions from 2021 to 2030 and achieving net-zero emissions no later than 2050, and aligns with the economy-wide carbon budgets and sectoral ceilings that were agreed upon by the Government in July 2022. 

CAP24 outlines the measures taken as part of Ireland "stock-taking" process of progress towards the achievement of the country's climate targets and elaborates on potential corrective actions to ensure that sectors stay within their respective sectoral emissions ceilings.

While CAP24 has been approved by the government, the plan is currently undergoing a public consultation which may entail adjustments to the plan based on feedback received from the public.
Document Title: Climate Action Plan 2024

Family Name: Greenhouse Gas Removals (GGR): Business Model
Family Summary: The Greenhouse Gas Removal (GGR) Business Model is a UK Government framework designed to support the development and commercial deployment of engineered greenhouse gas removal technologies, including Direct Air Carbon Capture and Storage (DACCS) and Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS). The model aims to attract private investment by providing revenue stability and sharing certain risks between government and project developers, initially supporting projects through contracts allocated via the Carbon Capture, Usage and Storage (CCUS). Projects must meet government GGR standards to ensure removals are measurable and verifiable, while the model is intended to facilitate participation in voluntary carbon markets and, in the longer term, the UK Emissions Trading Scheme. The August 2025 framework initially applied to GGR projects progressing through the HyNet Track-1 expansion process, with two prospective projects taken forward to negotiations.

Family Name: Brunei Darussalam Action Plan on Reduction of Aviation Emissions
Family Summary: The Brunei Darussalam Action Plan on Reduction of Aviation Emissions aims to contribute to international efforts to mitigate the climate effects of air travel, and was developed in co-ordination with the ICAO (International Civil Aviation Organisation). The key objectives of the document are carbon emission reporting, outlining mitigation measures, reporting data on ongoing measures, generating public awareness of these processes, and assessing Brunei Darussalam's overall progress on aviation emissions reduction. It promotes and reports on specific mitigation measures such as single-engine taxi-in, weight reduction, cleaner fuels, flight pattern changes, airport energy efficiency, emissions trading integration, LED airstrip lighting and the replacement of older aeroplane models.

Family Name: Offshore Wind Energy Lease Rules, 2023
Family Summary:
These Rules stipulate the conditions under which the central government may lease out the offshore area within the Exclusive Economic Zone for offshore wind energy and offshore wind transmission projects. The lease will be for an initial period of three years for resource measurement and related study/survey activities, further extendable for adequate reasons by an additional two years. There may then be an extension of 35 years and further extensions on a case-by-case basis for the construction and operation of offshore wind energy projects.

Under the Rules, the lessee is required to decommission all installations and clear the eabed from all obstructions created by the project.
Document Title: Offshore Wind Energy Lease Rules, 2023

Family Name: Electric Vehicle Availability Standard (regulated targets for zero-emission vehicles)
Family Summary: Auto manufacturers and importers are required to meet annual zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) regulated sales targets under the Electric Vehicle Availability Standard. Starting in the 2026 model year, they must offer at least 20% of new light-duty vehicles for sale as ZEVs. This percentage will increase annually, reaching 60% by 2030 and 100% by 2035.
Document Title: Electric Vehicle Availability Standard (regulated targets for zero-emission vehicles)

Family Name: 2023 National Security Strategy of Moldova
Family Summary: The 2023 National Security Strategy of Moldova defines national security objectives, and acts as an orientation document to motivate actions addressing each of the areas it lists. The strategy acknowledges climate change as a significant threat to national security, emphasising the importance of increased resilience and alignment with the adaptation and mitigation measures of the EU.
Document Title: 2023 National Security Strategy of Moldova

Family Name: Agreement on green aviation in Denmark
Family Summary:
This Agreement sets out the commitment to allocate funds to establish fully electric domestic aviation routes from 2025, and to ensure that all domestic air travel is electric by 2030 at the latest. Subsidies will be offered for the additional cost of purcashing electric powered aircraft.

In addition, funds will be provided to smaller regional airports to finance green infrastructure and for the restructuring of aviation, for instance in supporting the blending of sustainable aviation fuels such as Power-to-X fuels or other propellants (such as electricity and hydrogen), and the reduction of aromatic hydrocarbons in aviation fuel to reduce environmental impact.
Document Title: Agreement on green aviation in Denmark

Family Name: National Strategic Plan (NSP) for the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) 2023-2027
Family Summary:
This NSP is established by Regulation (EU) No 2021/2115 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 2 December 2021 establishing rules on support for strategic plans to be drawn up by Member States under the Common Agricultural Policy and financed by the European Agricultural Guarantee Fund (EAGF) and by the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD).

It contains actions relating to climate change mitigation and adaptation, including: climate measures for water quality and quantity management; climate measures for soil quality and protection; climate measures for food self-sufficiency; climate measures for the preservation of species and sustainable maintenance of agro-ecological infrastructure.
Document Title: National Strategic Plan (NSP) for the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) 2023-2027

Family Name: National strategy for water management 2023-2035
Family Summary:
This National Strategy for Water Management presents a vision to achieve the European objectives assumed by Romania as an EU Member State, namely "zero pollution" and energy independence by 2050, strengthening adaptive capacity and minimising vulnerability to the consequences of climate change in terms of water resource security, through a socially equitable transition, in a cost-effective manner.

  • Strategic objective 1. Integrated water resources management to ensure sustainable use of water resources
  • Strategic objective 2. Manage and protect water resources to achieve and maintain good status of surface and groundwater and prevent its deterioration
  • Strategic objective 3. Reduce water-related risks in the context of climate change (water scarcity and droughts, erosion of banks and cliffs; destructive actions of floods) on population, economic activity, environment and cultural heritage
  • Strategic objective 4. Develop the legislative, organisational and scientific framework for water management
Document Title: National strategy for water management 2023-2035

Family Name: Making environmental claims: A guide for business
Family Summary:
This guide explains the obligations under Australian Consumer Law, which businesses must comply with when making environmental and sustainability claims. Whilst this document is not legally binding, it informs businesses on how obligations under consumer protection law, including the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth), may apply and is therefore considered legally relevant.

The guide sets out eight principles to help businesses comply with their obligations under Australian Consumer Law. Under Principle 5 "Avoid broad and unqualified claims", there is guidance relevant to communcations around climate change. For example, claims that a business uses renewable energy should clearly explain how any renewable energy use (and any associated emissions reduction) has been calculated, in a way that consumers can readily understand. There is also a section on emissions related claims. For example, being transport about emission reductions activities versus reliance on purchased offsets; providing up-to-date information about the registry with details of the offsets relinquishes or cancelled each year; and taking care when relying on a certification scheme for offsets and emissions.
Document Title: Making environmental claims: A guide for business

Family Name: Comprehensive program for counteracting forest dieback processes in Poland and mitigation measures in the perspective of 2030
Family Summary: The Comprehensive Programme to Counter Forest Dieback in Poland up to 2030 (KPPPZL 2030) adopted by Decision 201 of the Director General of the State Forest addresses the increasing problem of forest dieback in Poland driven by climate change, drought, pests and habitat degradation, with a focus on preventing large-scale tree mortality and preserving healthy forest ecosystems. It sets out coordinated management, protection and adaptation measures to increase forest resilience, limit tree mortality, protect biodiversity and maintain forests’ ecological and climate functions, including carbon sequestration and water regulation.
Document Title: Comprehensive program for counteracting forest dieback processes in Poland and mitigation measures in the perspective of 2030

Family Name: Climate agreement on more green energy from solar and wind on land - Framework conditions for promoting the expansion of renewable energy on land (2023)
Family Summary:
This agreement paves the way for the state to play an active role in the planning of larger energy parks on land and support the expansion of renewable energy on land in general. The energy parks will be a supplement to the municipal planning of renewable energy projects and should be seen as a contribution to removing barriers to this. This agreement is the first follow-up agreement to last year's Climate Agreement on Green Electricity and Heat 2022. The energy parks are larger designated areas where a rapid expansion of several different renewable energy technologies can take place. Energy parks can, for example, be established as hybrid parks consisting of onshore wind turbines, solar cells and PtX plants, etc., where relevant.

In addition, the energy parks must be local green power centers that contribute to business development, more green jobs and help create development perspectives in the local communities and municipalities where the energy parks are set up. The economic benefits of wind turbines and solar cells must be felt by neighbors and local communities through a significant increase in the compensation schemes green pool and renewable energy bonus. The expansion of renewable energy on land can contribute green electricity to both direct electricity consumption in Denmark towards 2030 and green electricity for the production of green fuels for, for example, aircraft and ships. The parties to the agreement note that the quadrupling is an important part of the green transition of the transport sector and at the same time contributes to local business development.
Document Title: Climate agreement on more green energy from solar and wind on land - Framework conditions for promoting the expansion of renewable energy on land (2023)

Family Name: 30by30 on land: Delivery plan
Family Summary: The United Kingdom has committed to protecting 30% of the UK's land by 2030 (also know as '30by30'). The Delivering 30by30 on land in England strategy sets out how the UK government is taking action to achieve its 30 by 30 target and protect nature and biodiversity in the UK. It also introduces the 30by30 criteria, which outlines how different areas can also contribute to achieving land protection targets. The strategy builds on the proposals made in the Environmental Improvement Plan 2023, which recommends achieving the 30 by 30 taget through "ensuring effective policy and statutory safeguards and powers in place to improve management for nature, prevent degradation and ensure appropriate access for people... designature new protected areas and restore or create wildlife rich habitate outside of these... and invest in habitata restoration across our protected areas and beyond".
Document Title: 30by30 on land: Delivery plan

Family Name: Principles for Net-Zero Financing & Investment
Family Summary: This policy sets voluntary guidelines for net-zero financing and investment within the United States, produced by the US Department of the Treasury. The principles aim to guide financial institutions by highlighting the importance and value of financial institutions’ net-zero commitments; promoting consistency and credibility in financial institutions’ approaches to these commitments; and encouraging the adoption of best practices that relate to these commitments.
Document Title: Principles for Net-Zero Financing & Investment

Family Name: Romania's Long-Term Strategy for Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions
Family Summary:
Romania's long-term strategy for reducing greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) includes the target for Romania to become climate neutral in 2050, reaching 99% net emission reduction in 2050, compared to the 1990 level. Romania's long-term strategy reflects the long-term vision for a modern economy and an efficient energy system that will contribute to the fulfilment of the commitments assumed by the Paris Agreement, as well as the opportunities and challenges in terms of reducing anthropogenic gas emissions with a greenhouse effect and increasing absorptions by absorbers in order to reach the temperature targets set out in the Paris Agreement.

The mission to Decarbonise includes specific steps and roadmaps at the sectoral level, with the following key sectors:

a) energy 

b) industry (including the energy consuming industry together with industrial processes and product use - IPPU) 

c) transport: Road, Rail, Air, Water, Multimodal 

d) buildings and Heating & Cooling 

e) agriculture and Forestry 

f) waste
Document Title: Romania's Long-Term Strategy for Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions

Family Name: National Electricity Amendment (Amendment of the Market Price Cap, Cumulative Price Threshold and Administered Price Cap) Rule
Family Summary:
This Rule by the Australian Energy Market Commission (AEMC or Commission) amends the existing market price settings in the national electricity market (NEM). It will progressively increase the market price cap (MPC) and cumulative price threshold (CPT), and maintain the administered price cap (APC) at its current level from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2028. This Rule supports more energy generation, demand response, and storage entering the system to meet our electricity needs as the system transitions.

This Rule achieves the following:

1. Delivering eﬃcient levels of reliability — the final rule will deliver eﬃcient long-term levels of reliability that correspond to consumer willingness to pay.

2. Maximising outcomes for consumers — the final rule appropriately balances costs and benefits for consumers by minimising the costs of achieving eﬃcient levels of reliability.

3. Enhancing market eﬃciency — the final rule will enhance market eﬃciency across operational and investment timeframes through competition, rather than directions and obligations.

4. Principles of good regulatory practice — the final rule will support good regulatory practice by promoting predictability and stability in the regulatory framework, interacting constructively with other reforms underway, and appropriately balancing systemic financial risk and market eﬃciency considerations.

5. Emission reduction — the final rule will promote the long-term decarbonisation of the NEM to contribute to achieving government emissions reduction targets.
Document Title: National Electricity Amendment (Amendment of the Market Price Cap, Cumulative Price Threshold and Administered Price Cap) Rule

Family Name: Ministerial Decree 414 of 7 December 2023 concerning identification of an incentive tariff for renewable energy plants, in implementation of Legislative Decree 199/2021
Family Summary:
Ministerial Decree No. 414/2023 is a regulatory framework designed to execute Legislative Decree No. 199/2021 and fulfill a specific green energy investment (Mission 2, Component 2) within Italy’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR). Its primary goal is to incentivize the growth of renewable energy through collaborative models, specifically targeting Renewable Energy Communities (CERs) and various collective or individual self-consumption arrangements.

The Decree establishes two cumulative financial benefits for eligible projects:

  • PNRR Capital Grants: A direct, non-repayable contribution covering up to 40% of the initial investment costs. This specific fund is a geographic incentive, reserved for renewable plants built in smaller municipalities (those with 5,000 residents or fewer).
  • Incentive Feed-in Tariffs: A performance-based "premium" paid for the renewable electricity actually produced and shared within the community. Unlike the capital grant, this tariff is available nationwide and is guaranteed for a 20-year period starting from the date the plant begins commercial operations.

Eligibility for the incentives is subject to compliance with the conditions set forth in Article 3 of the Decree. These include: a maximum plant capacity, the prior establishment of the energy community before the plant’s entry into operation, and the requirement that participating enterprises be classified as small or medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).
Document Title: Legislative Decree 199/2021

Family Name: National Action Plan for the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (2024-2028)
Family Summary:
The overall goal of this Action Plan is to secure the gene pool for future agriculture and food production. The global trend of genetic erosion and genetic diversity loss not only increases the vulnerability of agriculture and forestry to the effects of climate change, but also reduces opportunities for the future. Key measures include:

  • Strengthen cooperation on genetic resources between the Nordic countries via the Nordic Council of Ministers and by working closely with NordGen.
  • Continue to participate in European cooperation on forest, livestock and crop genetic resources.
  • Continue to participate in international cooperation on genetic resources, with an emphasis on access and benefit sharing and Farmers’ Rights.
  • Increase the share of major food and forage crops whose seeds are stored at the Svalbard Global Seed Vault.

Action steps include strengthening livestock and plant breeding based on national genetic resources and thereby contributing to climate-friendly and sustainable food production.
Document Title: National Action Plan for the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (2024-2028)
