Family Name: Decree No. 2023-968 of 6 December 2023 establishing the Ministry of Environment, Sustainable Development and Ecological Transition
Family Summary: Decree No. 2023-968 of December 6, 2023, however, establishes the Ministry of the Environment, Sustainable Development and Ecological Transition. This decree revises Decree No. 2018-949 of December 18, 2018 in order to strengthen Ivorian climate action by placing a particular emphasis on the ecological transition, which is a fundamental aspect in the implementation and monitoring of progress made by its NDC.
Document Title: Decree No. 2023-968 of 6 December 2023 establishing the Ministry of Environment, Sustainable Development and Ecological Transition

Family Name: Strategy on climate foreign policy of the government of the Federal Republic of Germany
Family Summary:
With this whole-of-government strategy on climate foreign policy, the German Government are aligning their structures and instruments so as to contribute to implementing the global transition to a climate-neutral future in a socially just and economically successful way, and are actively shaping it in line with our values and interests. This strategy will guide the German Government’s international climate action and is coordinated amongst and implemented by the relevant ministries.

Priority action areas indicated in the climate foreign policy include:

  • Drastically reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 2030, accelerating the global energy transition;
  • Making the economy more competitive, fair and climate- and future-proof;
  • Acting in solidarity with the most vulnerable;
  • Protecting lives, livelihoods and health;
  • Protecting, restoring and promoting the sustainable use of ecosystems;
  • Strengthening resilience, peace and security;
  • Aligning international financial flows with a 1.5°C-compatible pathway and climate-resilient development;
Document Title: Strategy on Climate Foreign Policy

Family Name: Federal Decree No. 11.815/2023 on the National Programme of Conversion of Degraded Pastures into Sustainable Agricultural and Forestry Production Systems
Family Summary: This decree establishes the National Programme of Conversion of Degraded Pastures into Sustainable Agricultural and Forestry Production Systems and its Interministerial Management Committee. The program must contribute to the fulfilment of the targets for recovering degraded pastures, reducing deforestation and recovering native vegetation set out in the international commitments made by the Government of the Federative Republic of Brazil and in Plans and Policies such as the Sectoral Plan for Adaptation to Climate Change and Low Carbon Emissions in Agriculture and Livestock, with a view to Sustainable Development (2020-2030) - ABC+ Plan.
Document Title: Federal Decree No. 11.815/2023

Family Name: Singapore-Asia Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance
Family Summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore launched the Singapore-Asia Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance in December 2023. This sets out thresholds and criteria for defining green transition activities that contribute to climate change mitigation across eight sectors.
Document Title: Singapore-Asia Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance

Family Name: National Health and Climate Strategy
Family Summary: The National Health and Climate Strategy sets out a whole-of-government plan to address the health and wellbeing impacts of climate change and address the contribution of the health system to climate change. It was released on 3 December 2023.
Document Title: National Health and Climate Strategy

Family Name: Building Sector Decarbonisation Roadmap
Family Summary:
The roadmap is designed to reflect Turkey's emission reduction targets and has the goal of reducing whole life cycle emissions in buildings. It aims to transform the building sector by increasing energy efficiency, transitioning to renewable energy sources and promoting environmentally sound building materials and construction methods. Strategies for increasing the climate resilience of the building sector are also included. It will serve as a guideline for Turkey's transition towards zero-emission, efficient and resilient buildings, achieving decarbonisation targets for the building sector.

In the Turkish Building Sector Decarbonisation Roadmap, zero-carbon buildings are understood as highly energy-efficient buildings where carbon emissions from all operational energy consumed throughout the year are offset by renewable and/or other zero-emission energy sources. The roadmap also identifies possible actions that can reduce embedded emissions associated with building materials, and sets out possible steps that can be considered to transition to net-zero carbon buildings over the entire life cycle. Within the scope of the roadmap, national decarbonisation strategies are evaluated in 7 main sections: Construction and Demolition, Building Materials, Existing and New Buildings, Renewable Energy, Resilience and Climate Change Adaptation, Financing, Gender Equality.
Document Title: Building Sector Decarbonisation Roadmap

Family Name: Ghana Climate Prosperity Plan
Family Summary:
The Climate Prosperity Plan (CPP) embeds the aspirational pathway for Ghana from climate vulnerability to climate prosperity, meanwhile creating quality jobs, stimulating the economy while making it resilient, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

The CPP is centered around two principal goals: Climate Secure Ghana and Climate Prosperous Ghana. These goals are focused on promoting a range of priority efforts in the following sectors: energy, water, human mobility, food security, and finance. The former goal has two targets:

  • Ghana achieves a 100% electrification rate through deployment of renewable energy by 2035; and
  • Ghana’s population (100%) has access to at least basic water services by 2030.

The latter goal targets that:

  • In 2035, 100% of major urban centers in Ghana benefited from an extended public transportationnetwork running on electric vehicles;
  • 90-100% of national food and beverage consumption is domestically produced by 2035; and
  • Ghana’s coverage of biodiversity corridors and touch points to favor biodiversity conservation increasesby 30% in 2035.
Document Title: Ghana Climate Prosperity Plan

Family Name: Electric Vehicles White Paper (2023)
Family Summary:
The policy is driven by six core principles:

  1. Urgency in transitioning to EVs due to fast global market developments and long investment lead-times.
  2. A technology-agnostic approach—embracing various clean energy technologies.
  3. The need for investment support to build production capacity.
  4. Ensuring cost-effective and fiscally sustainable policy measures.
  5. Deepening localisation in the auto supply chain, including beneficiation of critical minerals via regional value chains.
  6. Commitment to a just transition for the automotive industry workforce.
Document Title: Electric Vehicles White Paper (2023)

Family Name: Australian Government Green Bond Framework
Family Summary:
This Green Bond Framework (the Framework) outlines how the Australian Government will issue green bonds, including the basis for identifying, selecting, managing, and reporting on expenditures financed with green bonds. It also sets out the Government’s key climate change and environmental priorities. Treasury is responsible for the Australian Government’s overall green bond program. The Australian Office of Financial Management (AOFM) issues debt securities on behalf of the Australian Government and is responsible for the issuance of sovereign green bonds. This Framework has been developed in accordance with, and is compliant with, the International Capital Markets Association (ICMA) Green Bond Principles (from The Green Bond Principles 2021). This Framework follows ICMA’s core components, which are: use of proceeds, process for project evaluation and selection, management of proceeds, and reporting and has been the subject of an external review.

Green bonds will help finance high‑quality Australian Government projects with targeted environmental outcomes that are monitored and reported (see Chapter 6). A well‑designed and credible sovereign green bond program is expected to mobilise additional climate‑aligned capital, deepen sustainable finance markets and signal the Government’s commitment to climate, energy and other environmental goals.
Document Title: Australian Government Green Bond Framework

Family Name: National Emissions Reduction Programme (NERP)
Family Summary:
The National Emissions Reduction Programme (NERP) is the fundamental conceptual material in the area of air quality and reduction of emissions from sources of air pollution. It is implemented on the basis of Article 8 of Act 201/2012 Coll., on Air Protection. The first Programme was adopted in 2007 and its latest version was approved in December 2023. The Programme complies with the requirements set by the Directive (EU) 2016/2284 on the reduction of national emissions of certain atmospheric pollutants for so called national air pollution control programmes (Article 6 of the Directive). The main objective of the NERP is to meet the national emission reduction commitments applicable from 2020 to 2029 and from

2030 onwards, as laid down by the Directive. For the implementation of the Programme a set of 3 priority measures, 11 subsidiary measures and 6 cross-sectional measures has been introduced at the national level directly aimed to reduce emissions and to improve air quality.
Document Title: National Emissions Reduction Programme (NERP)

Family Name: Regulation No. E-RD-04-1 on the calculation of the share of energy from renewable sources in gross final energy consumption and the share of renewable sources in transport, last amended in 2025.
Family Summary: It establishes Bulgaria’s methodology for calculating the share of energy from renewable sources in the gross final energy consumption of the country and the share of renewables (including biofuels and renewable electricity) used in the transport sector. The regulation ensures national renewable energy statistics are consistent with EU rules (both the original RED and the updated Renewable Energy Directive (EU) 2018/2001), and underpins Bulgaria’s progress tracking against renewable energy targets at the national and sectoral level. It repealed Regulation RD-16-869 of 02.08.2011.
Document Title: Regulation No. E-RD-04-1 on the calculation of the share of energy from renewable sources in gross final energy consumption and the share of renewable sources in transport

Family Name: Strategy for Organic Farming
Family Summary:
This Strategy, published by the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Fisheries, follows from the Agreement on the Green Transition of Danish Agriculture of 4 October 2021 (the Agricultural Agreement) concluded between the then government (the Social Democrats), the Liberal Party, the Danish People's Party, the Socialist People's Party, the Radical Left, the Unity List, the Conservatives, the New Civic Party, the Liberal Alliance, the Christian Democrats, and later adopted by the Moderates. The Agricultural Agreement decided that a strategy for organic farming should be developed that can support a doubling of the organic area, demand for organic goods, consumption and exports.

Organic farming is an important part of the green transition of agriculture, as more organic areas will promote production with fewer pesticides and fewer emissions for the benefit of the climate, environment, drinking water and nature.

With this strategy, the government will support the the doubling of the organic area in Denmark to 21 percent of the total Danish agricultural area by 2030; and the doubling of exports and retail of organic food. Actions include allocating more monies to the Fund for Plant-based Food, advising Danish export companies and marketing organic food.
Document Title: Strategy for Organic Farming

Family Name: Danish strategy for green proteins for animals and humans
Family Summary: The strategy is intended to set the direction for increased production of green proteins in Denmark. The Danish government's vision is that by 2030, Denmark will produce significantly more high-quality green proteins that can help replace imported feed, such as soy, support the transition to a more plant-based food sector, and provide alternative income opportunities for Danish businesses with an overall reduced environmental and climate impact. Actions include green biofening; boosting the growth and consumption of legumes and other protein-rich crops in Denmark; supporting the development of new proteins; and creating export opportunities.
Document Title: Danish strategy for green proteins for animals and humans

Family Name: Green Shipping Corridor Program
Family Summary:
The Green Shipping Corridor Program (GSCP) provides funding for projects that contribute to the establishment of green shipping corridors and the decarbonization of the marine sector along the Great Lakes, the St. Lawrence Seaway as well as Canada’s East and West Coasts by:

  • removing barriers to the adoption of emission-reducing equipment and infrastructure
  • incentivising industry-led partnerships and investments to accelerate the adoption of greenhouse gas (GHG) emission-reduction technologies and infrastructure
  • de-risking investments to increase the technology-readiness level of low-carbon and zero-emission ship technology and marine fuels for the domestic vessel fleet
  • building capacity among Canadian vessel owner/operators with respect to their ability to identify, plan and implement next generation low carbon and zero-emission ship technology and marine fuels into their vessel operations.

Funding is through two streams: 1) Clean Ports Stream; and 2) Clean Vessel Demonstration Stream. The Clean Ports Stream is providing up to $127.2M in contribution funding over 4 years from 2024 to 2028. The Clean Vessel Demonstration Stream is providing up to $22.5M in grant and contribution funding over 5 years from 2023 to 2028.

GSCP supports goals under the Federal Sustainable Development Strategy.
Document Title: Public statement on the strategic environmental assessment of the Green Shipping Corridor Program

Family Name: Carbon Capture, Usage and Storage: A Vision to Establish a Competitive Market
Family Summary: The UK Government’s December 2023 CCUS Vision sets out a long-term strategy to establish a commercial, competitive and ultimately self-sustaining carbon capture, usage and storage (CCUS) market in the UK. The approach is structured around three phases: market creation to reach 20–30 MtCO₂ of annual storage by 2030, market transition during the 2030s as private investment and competition increase, and a self-sustaining market capable of supporting the UK’s net-zero target by 2050. The government had committed up to £20 billion to support early CCUS deployment, with four clusters being developed and plans to expand infrastructure and storage capacity. The vision also sets out measures to improve investor confidence, reduce costs, develop CO₂ transport and storage networks, establish appropriate regulation and enable access to the UK’s substantial North Sea storage resources. CCUS is positioned as a key technology for decarbonising industry, power, hydrogen and low-carbon fuels, waste management and greenhouse gas removal, while also creating economic and supply-chain opportunities.
Document Title: Carbon Capture, Usage and Storage: A Vision to Establish a Competitive Market

Family Name: Amendment to Waste Management Act - includes standards to improve circularity of EV battery wastes
Family Summary: The Korean Ministry of Environment has enacted an amendment to the Waste Management Act to improve waste management, especially concerning hazardous chemicals, and to enhance regulations. This includes setting new standards to increase electric vehicle battery recycling.
Document Title: Amendment to Waste Management Act - includes standards to improve circularity of EV battery wastes

Family Name: 2018 - 2030 Methane Reduction Plan
Family Summary: South Korea joined the Global Methane Pledge and announced a methane reduction plan that sets a target to reduce national methane emissions by 30% below 2018 levels by 2030. Sectoral targets were announced for energy (28.6%), agriculture (20.9%), and waste (46.5%), all below 2018 levels by 2030.
Document Title: 2018 - 2030 Methane Reduction Plan

Family Name: Ecological Transformation Plan (Plano de Transformação Ecológica, PTE)
Family Summary: Brazil's Ecological Transformation Plan, unveiled on December 1, 2023, at COP28, aims to position the country as a leader in sustainable development by addressing ecological challenges through six pillars: sustainable funding, technological innovation, bioeconomy, energy transition, circular economy, and climate-resilient infrastructure. It seeks to promote environmentally sustainable and socially inclusive globalization, with measures such as a regulated carbon market, renewable energy expansion, and deforestation reduction.
Document Title: Ecological Transformation Plan

Family Name: Green Mobility and Innovation Program (Programa Mover)
Family Summary: The Green Mobility and Innovation Program (MOVER), announced by the Brazilian government in December 2023, aims to promote sustainability and innovation in the automotive industry by offering financial incentives and tax benefits for companies investing in decarbonization, energy efficiency, and new technologies. The program, which will allocate R$ 19.3 billion in financial credits between 2024 and 2028, includes measures such as the "IPI Verde" (Green IPI) tax adjustment, mandatory vehicle efficiency standards, and the creation of the National Fund for Industrial and Technological Development (FNDIT) to support priority programs in the automotive sector.
Document Title: Green Mobility and Innovation Program (Programa Mover)

Family Name: Scheme and Program for the Development of Electric Power System of Russia for 2024-2029
Family Summary: This strategy sets out Russia's official plan for the development of its national electricity system from 2024 to 2029, establishing planned investments in power generation capacity and grid infrastructure to meet projected energy demand, along with measures to ensure energy security and system reliability. The plan broadly maintains the existing balance of generation capacity by fuel type.
Document Title: Scheme and Program for the Development of Electric Power System of Russia for 2024-2029

Family Name: Kenya Energy Transition and Investment Plan 2023-2050
Family Summary: Kenya's Energy Transition and Investment Plan 2023-2050 aims to support global efforts to mitigate climate change and a national goal of net-zero by 2050, by investing in low-carbon technologies. It identifies new sectors for green economic growth, secure investments and opportunities to enhance national energy independence. It focuses on six key technological areas: electrification/efficiency/renewables; carbon capture and storage; low-carbon hydrogen; battery storage; clean cooking; and BECCS (bioenergy with carbon capture and storage). The plan claims that energy transition would require investing an additional 90bn USD cumulatively, supporting more than 500,000 additional jobs by 2050 and reducing oil and gas emissions by 94%.
Document Title: Kenya Energy Transition and Investment Plan 2023-2050

Family Name: National Biodiversity Strategy 2030
Family Summary:
This Strategy is structured around four axes:

  • reduce the pressure on biodiversity;
  • restore degraded biodiversity wherever possible;
  • mobilize all actors;
  • and guarantee the means to achieve these ambitions.

It outlines measures that reduce the impact of climate change on biodiversity through climate policies, and the contribution of the protection and restoration of ecosystems and the sustainable use of their resources to increasing carbon sinks.
Document Title: National Biodiversity Strategy 2030

Family Name: Ministerial Resolution No. 358-2023-MINAM. Guidelines for the operation of the Citizen Service Module for REDD+ (Resolución Ministerial Nº 358-2023-MINAM. Lineamiento para el funcionamiento del Módulo de Atención Ciudadana para REDD+)
Family Summary: The Ministerial Resolution N° 358-2023-MINAM establishes a Citizen Attention Mechanism (MAC REDD+) to operationalise Peru's national climate change policy framework, specifically implementing the provisions of Law N° 30754 on Climate Change. The mechanism provides a structured administrative process for receiving and addressing citizen inquiries related to REDD+ initiatives, including forest conservation strategies, emissions reduction efforts, and indigenous engagement in climate action. It delineates specific channels for citizen interaction, including presential, virtual, and telephonic platforms, and outlines the scope of acceptable inquiries ranging from document requests to technical consultations and complaints, with particular attention to intercultural accessibility and comprehensive stakeholder participation.
Document Title: Guidelines for the operation of the REDD+ citizen service module (Lineamiento para el funcionamiento del módulo de atención ciudadana REDD+)

Family Name: Ministerial Resolution No. 358-2023-MINAM. Guidelines for the operation of the Citizen Service Module for REDD+ (Resolución Ministerial Nº 358-2023-MINAM. Lineamiento para el funcionamiento del Módulo de Atención Ciudadana para REDD+)

Family Name: National Soil Action Plan 2023 to 2028
Family Summary:
The health of Australia's soil impacts water and air quality, human health and plays a vital role in resilience to climate change and natural disasters. The action plan sets out 4 priority actions. These guide the focus and design of support to action on soil by governments at all levels and partners over the next 5 years.

All priority actions are linked to the 3 broader goals of the National Soil Strategy:

  1. Prioritise soil health
  2. Empower soil innovation and stewards
  3. Strengthen soil knowledge and capability
Document Title: National Soil Action Plan 2023 to 2028

Family Name: Net Zero in Government Operations Strategy
Family Summary:
The Net Zero in Government Operations Strategy describes the approach for implementing the Australian Government’s commitment to achieve net zero in government operations by 2030. This target was included in Australia’s Nationally Determined Contribution Communication 2022 under the Paris Agreement. The Australian Government reaffirmed this ambitious target when it was one of 19 global partners to launch the Net Zero Government Initiative at the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change Conference of Parties meeting (COP27) in November 2022, and published its roadmap at COP28 on how it will reach net zero government operations through the Strategy.

A 2026-27 mid-term review will consider overall progress to date, domestic and international expectations at that time on climate action in government operations, and any recommended changes to policy or strategy to ensure the Government is still meeting its commitment to demonstrate leadership. The Net Zero in Government Operations Strategy supersedes the Energy Efficiency in Government Operations policy.

There are departmental emissions reduction plans following this Strategy.
Document Title: Net Zero in Government Operations Strategy - Roadmap

Family Name: Resolution No. 23/2023 approving the guide for the preparation of environmental impact studies
Family Summary: Resolution 23/2023 approves two guidance documents for environmental impact assessment (EIA): the Guide for the Preparation of Environmental Impact Studies (2023 Edition), in Annex I, and the Guide on Public Participation in Environmental Assessment (2023), in Annex II. The updated EIA guides embed climate change considerations into the assessment process for any work or activity likely to degrade the environment or significantly affect the quality of life of the population, as required under Article 11 of the General Environmental Law (No. 25,675).
Document Title: Annex II

Family Name: Decree No. 603-23 creating Commission for the Supervision of Public Infrastructure in the Face of Climate Change
Family Summary: This Decree creates a presidential commission to identify as quickly as possible the vulnerabilities of major public infrastructure, which, by virtue of being built on sites that pose a greater risk of deterioration as a result of the extreme changes brought about by climate change. The Commission shall report to the President, by submitting bimonthly reports so that the President may instruct the competent institution to make the appropriate corrective measures to prevent possible damage. The Commission shall also recommend to the President that he updated the preventive and corrective technical maintenance polciies for all public works to establish minimum standards for the supervision and maintenance of works for public use.
Document Title: Decree No. 603-23 creating Commission for the Supervision of Public Infrastructure in the Face of Climate Change

Family Name: National Sustainability Framework for the Visitor Economy
Family Summary: This Framework explains the different aspects of sustainability, covering 4 pillars of sustainable tourism: taking a managed approach to sustainability; implementing environmental and climate action; respecting culture; and creating positive social impact. The pillar on environmental and climate action involves taking action to protect wildlife and nature, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, adapt and build resilience to climate change, responsibly use resources, reduce waste and recycle.
Document Title: National Sustainability Framework for the Visitor Economy

Family Name: National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction 2023-2035
Family Summary: The Strategy aims to, inter alia, provide useful information for future investment decisions related to disasters and climate resilience. The Strategy also contributes to the progresive achievement of various Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), such as: Taking urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts. The Strategy will be implemented through an Action Plan, which will be updated every 3 years, depending on the results obtained in achieving the proposed objectives.
Document Title: National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction 2023-2035

Family Name: Law No. 2023-900 of 23 November 2023 establishing the Environmental Code
Family Summary:
The State shall prepare a report every five years on the state of the environment, including sectoral reports, relating to biodiversity, climate change, desertification, pollution levels, coastal areas, marine environments, and quality of life.

Environmental impact assessments are to take into account climate change.

The Code also contains a section on climate change, where the State is to adopt mitigation and adaptation strategies, promote technology transfer, publish reports every three years, and facilitate financing mechanisms.
Document Title: Law No. 2023-900 of 23 November 2023 establishing the Environmental Code

Family Name: Capacity Investment Scheme
Family Summary: The Capacity Investment Scheme (CIS) is a national framework that encourages new investment in renewable capacity, such as wind and solar, as well as clean dispatchable capacity, such as battery storage. The scheme aims to increase investment in clean energy and reduce reliance on fossil fuels. For projects selected through tenders, the Australian government offers long-term guarantee agreements with an agreed revenue floor and ceiling, thereby reducing investment risk and restraint.
Document Title: Tender Guidelines - Wholesale Electricity Market - Dispatchable Capacity

Family Name: The Financial Administration (Climate Resilience and Development Fund) Regulations (No. 45 of 2023)
Family Summary: These Regulations establish a special fund which serves as an instrument to collect Tourism Guest Levy and which will also be financed with a portion of the additional Revenue Recovery Charge (RRC) collected by the Customs and Excise Department. The Fund is managed by a governing body, with monies to be used for financing projects and programmes to build climate resilience; providing a buffer for public finances in times of natural disasters; funding development projects; and providing co-financing for projects funded by multilateral agencies and international development partners including Carribean Development Bank, Green Climate Fund and Global Environment Fund.
Document Title: The Financial Administration (Climate Resilience and Development Fund) Regulations (No. 45 of 2023)

Family Name: Comprehensive Investment and Policy Plan
Family Summary:
This sets out a roadmap and investment plan for Indonesia's Just Energy Transition Partnership. It consists of a set of key recommendations to facilitate the allocation
of resources to projects and programmes within the country to support the goals of the just energy transition.
Document Title: Comprehensive Investment and Policy Plan

Family Name: National Adaptation Plan (2021-2050)
Family Summary: The National Adaptation Plan sets out priority programmes in nine thematic sectors outlined in the National Climate Change Policy. This Plan identifies 64 priority adaptation programmes, with a total budget for implementation of USD 47.4 billion.
Document Title: National Adaptation Plan

Family Name: State Ecological Transformation Plan for Eco-Responsible Public Services (SPE)
Family Summary:
The new circular Eco-responsible Public Services No. 6425/SG is structured around 15 commitments / measures. Two cross-cutting measures concern, on the one hand, the training of State's executives and senior management, then all agents in the ecological transition (Measure 1), and on the other hand, the monitoring of State's greenhouse gas emissions (Measure 2), supported by the design of an interministerial "Low Carbon State" tool to support the production of greenhouse gas emissions assessments (BEGES), with an annual feedback of indicators, in order to comply with the trajectory defined in the State's decarbonization strategy and in application of Article L. 229-25 of the environmental code. The other thirteen measures are divided into five main themes:

  • Move better
  • Better produce and consume better
  • Eat better
  • Better manage state buildings
  • Better protect and enhance our ecosystems
Document Title: State Ecological Transformation Plan for Eco-Responsible Public Services (SPE)

Family Name: Federal Decree No. 11.786/2023 on the National Policy for Quilombola Territorial and Environmental Management
Family Summary: One of the general objectives of the National Policy for Quilombola Territorial and Environmental Management (PNGTAQ) is to promote socio-environmental development, improved quality of life, well-being, peace and climate justice, with the necessary conditions for the physical and cultural reproduction of current and future generations of Quilombola communities. Other objectives are to carry out information and awareness-raising actions on the impacts of the climate emergency, climate justice and environmental racism in and around Quilombola territories and to promote the creation of participatory systems for diagnosing and monitoring the climate emergency impacts, to draw up preventive strategies and mitigation and adaptation actions in Quilombola territories.
Document Title: Federal Decree No. 11.786/2023

Family Name: Royal Decree 829/2023 restructuring the ministerial departments
Family Summary: The Real Decreto 829/2023 redefines the organizational structure of Spain's government by establishing new ministerial departments and adjusting their roles to enhance administrative efficiency and address key national challenges. Notably, it strengthens the Ministry for Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge, which is tasked with proposing and executing government policies on climate change, energy, and environmental sustainability, as well as tackling demographic challenges, including territorial depopulation. This ministry is responsible for key areas such as climate action, water as a public good, and anti-depopulation strategies, with its functions split into two primary bodies: the State Secretariat for Energy and the State Secretariat for the Environment.
Document Title: Royal Decree 829/2023 restructuring the ministerial departments

Family Name: Circular Strategy on Environment 2023-2028
Family Summary:
The Circular Strategy on Environment 2023-2028 serves as a roadmap, outlining the priority actions with the aim of ensuring integrity, climate resilience, environmental sustainability, and promoting a green economy. The overarching goal is realising the Pentagonal strategy’s aim for Cambodia to be carbon-neutral, with 60 percent of forest cover by 2050. 

Three strategy has three angles, to enhance policy, establish digital administration, and broaden extension in order to achieve the aim of

  1. Being clean (controlling pollution, improving environmental impact assessment, and modernise the pollution measurement system)
  2. Going green (sustainable management of protected areas, enhancing livelihood of local communities, and intensifying the planting of trees)
  3. Being sustainable (cooperation, coordination, and compliance)
Document Title: Circular Strategy on Environment 2023-2028

Family Name: National Policy for Disaster Risk Reduction of Guatemala -PNRRD2024-2034 implemented by the Governmental Agreement No. 267/2023
Family Summary:
This Guatemala's National Policy for Disaster Risk Reduction (PNRRD) 2024–2034, approved by Governmental Agreement 267-2023, is the first national public instrument for comprehensive risk management in Guatemala. Its implementation involves 20 institutions of the CONRED System, with 29 interventions and 22 strategic guidelines, aimed at reducing human and material losses and moving towards a more resilient Guatemala. The general goal is to reduce disaster risk levels in Guatemala through an inclusive approach that considers vulnerable populations such as children, women, people with disabilities, and migrants. Also, there are 4 strategic pillars:

  • Risk Information Management aiming to produce and disseminate technical, scientific, and culturally relevant information on disaster risk factors through reliable and accessible information systems.
  • Risk Governance aiming to build institutional capacities and foster coordination among national, local, and community-level entities, including indigenous authorities and civil society organizations.
  • Investment in Reducing Vulnerabilities (with Integrated Risk Management approach – GIRRD) aiming at integrating disaster risk management into public and private investment planning and execution to protect infrastructure and livelihoods.
  • Population Preparedness, Response, and Recovery aiming to enhance the state's capacity for effective emergency response and sustainable recovery,e nsuring continuity of development after disasters.
Document Title: olítica Nacional para la Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres de Guatemala (PNRRD) 2024-2034 (National Policy for Disaster Risk Reduction (PNRRD) 2024–2034)

Family Name: Resolution 385/2023 (Resolución 385/2023)
Family Summary:
The National Strategy for the Use of Carbon Markets [Estrategia Nacional para el Uso de los Mercados de Carbono (ENUMeC)] aims to establish a common framework for the use of carbon markets at the national level. It seeks to foster enabling conditions for project development in the country, contribute to mitigation and adaptation efforts, and provide transparency, integrity, and certainty for all stakeholders involved. The strategy outlines 9 strategic axes and 63 associated actions, and proposes the development of specific roadmaps for its implementation.

From the 63 actions mentioned, 8 are relevant to the voluntary market, as listed below:

  • Identify activities aligned with national climate objectives.
  • Recommend high-integrity criteria for voluntary market implementation.
  • Promote the development of projects with associated environmental and social co-benefits, particularly those aligned with national and subnational adaptation priorities, with special attention to indigenous peoples and socially vulnerable groups.
  • Support the private sector in implementing voluntary markets with high environmental integrity criteria aligned with Article 6.4 of the Paris Agreement.
  • Facilitate exchange between voluntary market participants and subnational and national governments.
  • Define the tax framework for voluntary carbon markets in collaboration with relevant national public sector actors.
  • Guide the private sector on the possible uses of unauthorised credits (i.e., "mitigation contributions") and their alignment with national climate policy.
  • Strengthen the capacities of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) interested in accessing voluntary markets.

Further Considerations

  • Scope: Voluntary and regulated markets at the subnational, national and international level.
  • Sectors and gases: All sectors and gases covered by the National Greenhouse Gas Inventory (INGEI).
  • Stakeholders: All stakeholders involved in carbon market matters at the national government level, subnational governments, the private sector, and civil society.
  • Initiatives: It encompasses all agreements, programs, and projects related to carbon markets developed within the country.
  • The establishment of a national office for carbon markets, responsible for implementing the national strategy, is proposed as part of the institutional arrangements. However, it has not been formally adopted yet.
  • The strategy outlines principles for the use of carbon markets at the national level, institutional arrangements, and general requirements for monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) for ENUMeC implementation.
Document Title: Resolution 385/2023 (Resolución 385/2023)

Family Name: Principles for the Effective Management of Climate-related Financial Risk
Family Summary:
In 2023, the UAE’s Sustainable Finance Working Group (SFWG) published the Principles for the Effective Management of Climate-related Financial Risk, which sets seven principles that financial regulators in the UAE are expected to abide by to effectively manage climate-related financial risks. 

Principle 5 requires financial firms to implement monitoring and reporting systems that are “capable of producing relevant, accurate and timely information”. Information generated from these systems, including any reporting gaps, must then be reported to the board, senior management or other stakeholders. These principles were adopted by four regulators in the UAE, including the Securities and Commodities Authority (SCA), Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA) and Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA) and the Central Bank of the UAE.
Document Title: Principles

Family Name: National Climate Change Action Plan (NCCAP) III 2023-2027
Family Summary:
The National Climate Change Action Plan (NCCAP) III 2023 – 2027 is the third five-year plan that presents the detailed priority actions that Kenya will embark on to address climate change in the medium-term planning period and contribute to the achievement of our NDC under the Paris Agreement. Its development has involved deliberate consultations with the youth and children’s representatives.

NCCAP 2023–2027 proposes priority actions for implementation over the five-year period. These actions are classified in eight (8) Climate Change Priority Areas: Disaster Risk Management; Food Security and Nutrition; Water, Fisheries and the Blue Economy; Forestry, Wildlife and Tourism; Health and Human Settlements; Manufacturing; Energy and Transport; and Children and the Youth. The priority actions, building on achievements from the 2018–2022 period, propose adaptation and mitigation interventions, as well as enabling actions to facilitate their implementation. An implementation matrix has been prepared for each priority area, with an estimated budget that will guide execution. Each Climate Change Priority Area has a set of discrete National Indicators, as well as Key Performance Indicators to enable tracking and reporting of progress over the 2023–2027 period.
Document Title: National Climate Change Action Plan (NCCAP) III 2023-2027

Family Name: Funding decision for a sustainable transformation for climate action in a changing world
Family Summary:
This decision funds research projects that involve sustainable actions in climate change transformation. These projects are to provide knowledge about and for a sustainable climate change transformation that is robust in a changing world, and place the climate change transformation in a holistic perspective, based on the need for system-wide processes.

Funded projects can, for example, be about how different stakeholders can actively drive the processes of climate change transformation or provide knowledge about how different types of crises and challenges can create obstacles or opportunities for the transformation. The research can also provide knowledge about which capabilities and practices, such as different types of social, organisational and technological innovations, can promote proactive, robust and sustainable climate actions. It can also address how different stakeholders and groups in society affect and are affected by the transformation, or how they can better anticipate and manage crises and parallel challenges.
Document Title: A sustainable transformation for climate action in a changing world

Family Name: National heatwave warning framework (2023)
Family Summary:
The purpose of the National Heatwave Warning Framework (the Framework) is to provide the foundation for a consistent approach to heat health and heatwave warnings across Australian state and territories. The primary intent of the Framework is to reduce the health impact of heatwaves, noting that heatwaves also adversely impact sectors such as water, energy, infrastructure, agriculture and transport.

Improving knowledge of heat hazards can assist people and organisations to prepare for, and cope with, the effects of extreme heat and the impacts of a changing climate. The capacity of people and organisations to act is enhanced by nationally consistent and aligned guidance that clarifies methods, approaches, roles and responsibilities.
Document Title: National Heatwave Warning Framework

Family Name: Resolution SGR 469-2023 - National guidelines for the design, implementation, operation and sustainability of warning systems
Family Summary:
Approximately 62 million people have been directly affected by disasters, and most of them live in countries without functioning early warning systems. This situation clearly indicates that unless greater investment is made in building resilience by expanding the coverage of early warning systems, developing countries will face an increase in the number of people affected by hazards, especially as the population continues to grow.

According to the records of the Adverse Events Monitoring Directorate of the Risk Management Secretariat, there has been a considerable increase in the number of people directly affected by disasters in Ecuador over the past 12 years. The year 2021 was the year with the highest number of people affected, with 585,160. Due to its geographical location, Ecuador faces a variety of natural, socio-natural and anthropogenic hazards, resulting in frequent disasters with a significant impact on the population, economy and livelihoods. The most recurrent hazards in Ecuador include earthquakes, mass movements, floods and volcanic hazards.
Document Title: Resolution SGR 469-2023 - National guidelines for the design, implementation, operation and sustainability of warning systems ( RESOLUCIÓN Nro. SGR-469-2023 - Lineamientos nacionales para el diseño, implementación, funcionamiento y sostenibilidad de los sistemas de alerta)

Family Name: National Action Plan for Climate Change and Natural Disaster Risks (Decree no.362)
Family Summary: The National Action Plan for Climate Change and Natural Disaster Risks (Decree no.362) promotes a wide range of actions across sectors to reduce Uzbekistan's vulnerability to natural disasters, including those induced by climate change. It acknowledges particular climate-driven risk from extreme rainfall events, forest fires and physical vulnerability of dams and reservoirs. The action plan aims to build institutional capacity for proactive measures and response, educate the general population, attract investment and better predict and monitor climate risks. It promotes intervention through a range of sectors including healthcare, buildings, agriculture, meteorology, government ministries and financial institutions.
Document Title: National Action Plan for Climate Change and Natural Disaster Risks (Decree no.362)

Family Name: National Hydrogen Strategy and the Action Plan 2023-2030
Family Summary:
The vision of the National Hydrogen Strategy (NHS) and the Action Plan for Romania is to develop a hydrogen economy, with a focus on renewable hydrogen but with attention to low-carbon hydrogen at an affordable price, with a view of reducing emissions and sustainable and competitive economic and technological development, through the development of the following strategic directions for 2030:

  1. Decarbonisation of the economy through the use of renewable hydrogen in difficult sectors decarbonised by other methods (e.g. direct electrification impossible)
  2. Economic growth through sustainable development of technologies for industries difficult to decarbonise and focus on creating new jobs
  3. Technological development to ensure long-term mobilisation of the economyeconomy and to support the attraction of investment into the economy
  4. Energy security, through the use of hydrogen and Power-to-X solutions for optimising the integration of renewable energy sources and to achieve sectoral integration.
Document Title: Action Plan

Family Name: Methane Emissions Control Action Plan
Family Summary: The Action Plan defines the methane emission control targets for key areas during the 14th Five-Year Plan and 15th Five-Year Plan periods. In general, the targets are to improve the policies, technologies and standards relating to methane emissions in line with the national strategy to tackle climate change. It also sets out 8 key tasks for methane emissions control, including strengthening the construction of a methane emissions monitoring, accounting, reporting and verification system, promoting methane emissions control in energy and agriculture, strengthening methane emission control in waste and wastewater treatment, enhancing the coordinated control of pollutants and methane, fostering technological innovation and methane emission control supervision, accelerating the building of a legal and regulatory policy system, and strengthening global methane governance and cooperation.
Document Title: Methane Emissions Control Action Plan

Family Name: Maldives Energy Efficiency Guideline for Buildings
Family Summary:
Energy efficiency and conservation are crucial for the Maldives to mitigate climate change risks and achieve energy security. Maldives has a high dependence on fossil fuels to meet all of its domestic energy demand, and the use of fossil fuels has resulted in huge greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and its associated climate change risks. Maldives is also vulnerable to global oil price shocks due to dependence on imported fossil fuels. This Guideline mainstreams energy efficiency in building design practices to achieve a substantial reduction of energy consumption from buildings.

Actions include encouraging energy efficiency both at the construction stage and during the lifetime of the building, e.g. by climate-sensitive design which takes account of the orientation and surrounding features to control wind effects while optimising sunlight, daylight, and solar gain benefits.
Document Title: Maldives Energy Efficiency Guideline for Buildings

Family Name: Philippine Energy Plan 2020-2040
Family Summary: The Philippine Energy Plan formulates comprehensive sectoral roadmaps to make sure that the energy agenda will be implemented to meet the needs of the consumers. The Plan focuses on sustainability of all available energy sources and the diversification of the energy mix. The 2020-2040 plan version was approved following the approval of AmBisyon Natin 2040 by the president through Executive Order (EO) 5. It replaces the Philippine Energy Plan 2016-2030. The 2020-2040 Plan has been further updated to the Philippine Energy Plan (PEP) 2023-2050, which aims to achieve over 40% renewable energy in the total energy mix by 2030 and surpass 50% by 2040, while also incorporating nuclear energy and gradually reducing reliance on fossil fuels.The previous 2016-2030 plan povided the following targets for energy outlook (the base year used for the projections is 2015): 1) existing, committed, indicative and potential power projects + 30 percent share of RE in the capacity mix and higher natural gas share in power generation mix by 2030; 2) energy savings on all sectors for electricity and petroleum products of at least 6 percent yearly from 2016 to 2030; 3) increased utilization of alternative fuels for transport (CNG and electricity) from 2016-2030; 4) 10 percent biodiesel blend for 2030; 20 percent bioethanol blend for 2030.
Document Title: Philippine Energy Plan (2023-2050) Volume I, II, III merged

Family Name: Communication Strategy for the National Adaptation Planning Process in Zimbabwe
Family Summary:
This communication strategy is built upon Zimbabwe’s National Climate Policy, National Climate Change Response Strategy and the Nationally Determined Contributions. The communication strategy is developed on the premise that limited knowledge and understanding of climate change issues by key stakeholders has affected the successful inclusion of climate change in the country’s development frameworks and government engagement with citizens throughout the national adaptation process. It, therefore, seeks to provide for strategic climate change communication in order to increase the level of awareness and understanding of climate change issues among key stakeholders. The communication strategy focuses on five thematic areas, namely:

  • General knowledge on climate change - What are the causes of climate change, linkages with other sectors and how can one play a role in climate change mitigation?
  • Adaptation - What are the adaptation options available in various sectors and the key actions by the government to enhance adaptive capacity?
  • Climate change research - What are the key areas that need research and how do we disseminate research that has already be done or ongoing?
  • Gender and climate change - How do we address the gender gap in climate adaptation, climate resilience related support?
  • Financing - What are the climate change finance options available and what are the implications of not financing climate change adaptation?

Family Name: Japan Climate Transition Bond Framework
Family Summary: This Framework was formulated in the context of Japan's numerous energy supply shortages, which necessitates the move away from fossil fuels to decarbonisation technologies and clean energy for a stable energy supply (a process termed Green Transformation or GX). Another driving factor for the Framework is to increase the competitiveness of Japanese industry and place the Japanese economy back towards a path of growth, contributing towards achieving carbon neutrality and achiving economic growth through creating new demand and a market in decarbonisation. Japan expects the Framework to be a milestone for transition finance and a catalyst for further transition finance promotion and funding by private sectors.Japan will issue climate transition bonds based on the Framework, implementing 20 trillion yen scale of investment to increase policy predictability and achieve GX with public-private cooperation. The Framework lays out how the proceeds from the bonds will be allocated towards initiatives aligned with the GX Promotion Strategy, i.e., the eligibility criteria and exclusionary criteria for such initiatives; the process for project evaluation and selection; the management of proceeds; the requirements for allocation and impact reporting; and the process for external verification.
Document Title: Japan Climate Transition Bond Framework

Family Name: White Paper on the Climate Change Law of Georgia
Family Summary: The White Paper on the Climate Change Law of Georgia illustrates a holistic approach to gender considerations. While explicitly addressing gender justice, the paper seamlessly integrates an intersectional gender perspective across climate targets, governance, adaptation, just transition, and public participation. This inclusion recognizes the diverse impacts of climate change on women and men, highlighting the importance of gender- responsive approaches throughout all facets of climate action. Specifically, within the adaptation section, the White Paper underscores the need for NDC and mitigation actions to be inclusive and gender-responsive. It advocates for prioritizing the specific needs, challenges, and priorities of vulnerable groups, such as women, adolescents, internally displaced people, and ethnic minorities. By fostering inclusive engagement with diverse stakeholders, including marginalized communities and civil society organizations, the White Paper aims to promote empowerment and resilience-building among these groups. This approach not only aligns with global agreements like the Paris Agreement but also reflects Georgia’s commitment to advancing social justice and gender equality in its mitigation efforts.

Family Name: Disaster Risk Management Act (2023-91)
Family Summary:
This Act lays down provisions on the establishment and duties of the National Disaster Council, National Emergency Operations Committee, Recovery Coordination Committee, Disaster Resilience Committee, Clusters, Local government disaster committees, National Disaster Management Office, Disaster Coordinator and the National Emergency Operations Center. It also sets out rules as regards disaster planning at the national and local levels; declaration of state of disaster by executive orders; establishment and utilization of the Disaster Assistance Account; offences and penalties; and public cooperation to successfully prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters.

Family Name: Part 1 of the Carbon Market Framework for Zambia: Guidelines for the Submission and Evaluation of Proposed Mitigation Activities under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
Family Summary:
Issued by the Ministry of Green Economy and Environment, this guideline regulates the decision-making process for private mitigation activity development in Zambia. It is the first, in a series of guidelines, seeking to operationalize Zambia's participation in international carbon markets, under the provisions of Article 6 of the Paris Agreement (specifically under Articles 6.2 and 6.4). It builds on the "Interim Guidelines for Handling of Carbon Markets and Trading Zambia", published in 2022.

This document outlines the criteria for assessing A6 and non-A6 (voluntary) mitigation activities. It is specifically concerned with environmental integrity, sustainable development, and ambition raising criteria. It further describes the rules and obligations of all parties involved in developing mitigation activities under A6. Lastly, it creates a national registry to register mitigation outcomes from authorized mitigation activities.

Zambia’s Carbon Market Framework, published in 2025, outlines the institutional arrangements, evaluation criteria, share of proceeds and fees, and the functions of the national carbon registry.

Institutional arrangements

Implementtion of the framework is coordinated by the Ministry of Green Economy and Environment (MGEE) through its A6 Secretariat, supported by the Technical Subcommittee on Climate Change (TSCCC) and the Zambia Environmental Management Agency (ZEMA).

Approval process:

Activity proponents (APs) may submit a Mitigation Activity Information Note (MAIN) to the A6 Secretariat to request a Letter of No Objection (LNO). Formal approval and authorisation (LOAA) require submission of a Mitigation Activity Design Document (MADD) with a positive validation by a registered DOE.

ITMO issuance:

Issuance requests must include a monitoring report and verification report. The A6 Secretariat reviews submissions and TSCCC makes recommendations. Based on this, the A6 Secretariat issues LNOs/LOAAs and authorises ITMO transfers.

Registry:

ZEMA operates the national registry, manages activity and emissions data, and handles ITMO issuance, transfer, and cancellation. ZEMA provides regular updates to the TSCCC and supports UNFCCC reporting via the A6 Secretariat.

Additional roles: The TSCCC provides policy recommendations and updates to the carbon market framework, while the A6 Secretariat also maintains a national roster of validation and verification experts.

Evaluation criteria for A6 mitigation activities

Zambia’s assessment process for Article 6 mitigation activities includes two key stages: a concept phase (MAIN) and a full design phase (MADD). These are used to inform decisions on issuance of a Letter of No Objection (LNO) and a Letter of Approval and Authorisation (LOAA).

Assessment process

- At the MAIN stage, proponents must demonstrate alignment with Zambia’s climate goals and provide early evidence on sustainability and transformational potential.

- At the MADD stage, a detailed assessment is carried out following external validation, including baseline alignment with NDCs, demonstration of additionality, risk management, and sustainable development impacts.

Criteria

- 16 mandatory indicators, covering environmental integrity (e.g. baseline alignment, additionality, non-permanence, leakage), sustainable development (e.g. SDG contributions, EIA, benefit-sharing), and transformational change.

- Some indicators (e.g. carbon price estimation) are informational only; others must be fulfilled to receive a LNO/LOAA.

Fees, Share of Proceeds OMGE

Administrative Fees:

- Fee levels (in Zambian Kwacha) will be published in a future statutory instrument and may be adjusted annually for inflation.

- There will be MAIN assessment fee and MADD assessment fee, payable upon submission.

Share of Proceeds (SOP):

- SOPs apply to Article 6.2 transactions and voluntary projects requesting a Corresponding Adjustment (CA).

- SOP is paid per mitigation outcome at different price tiers depending on the volume of issued.

- SOPs are paid before ITMO issuance by ZEMA and collected in monetary form.

Article 6.4 projects and purely voluntary credits without CA are exempt from SOPs.

OMGE (Overall Mitigation in Global Emissions):

- Zambia requires cancellation of 2% of issued MOs (with CA) into the UNFCCC OMGE cancellation account.

- A higher OMGE rate may be negotiated bilaterally with acquiring parties.

National carbon registry

- ZEMA will manage the national carbon registry, which will track all mitigation activities under Article 6.2, Article 6.4, and the VCM, including those with and without Corresponding Adjustments.

- The registry enables the registration, issuance, tracking, cancellation, and reporting of Mitigation Outcomes (MOs) and ITMOs.

Information for Designated Operational Entities (DOEs)/Verification and Validation Bodies (VVBs)

Zambia allows UNFCCC-accredited DOEs, as well as validation and verification bodies under an independent internationalcarbon standard (e.g. the Verified Carbon Standard and/or Gold Standard) or VVBs accredited by the Swiss Federal Office for the Environment for “projects and programmes for emission reductions abroad”.
Document Title: Zambia Carbon Market Framework

Family Name: Strategic Contract for the Timber Sector 2023-2026
Family Summary:
This Strategic Contract was signed between the Minister of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty, Christophe Béchu, Minister of Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion, Agnès Pannier-Runacher, Minister of Energy Transition, Roland Lescure, Minister Delegate in charge of Industry, Patrice Vergriete, Minister Delegate for Housing and industry partners in the timber sector. It has four priorities:

  1. The ecological transition;
  2. Reindustrialisation, sovereignty and competitiveness;
  3. Innovation and digitalisation; and
  4. The development of skills and attractiveness.

This Strategic Contact aims to amplify the decarbonising role of the forest-wood sector in climate-carbon neutrality strategies by implementing a sector-wide tool to map material and carbon flows. These projects will focus on developing destination markets for wood (material, fibers, molecules, energy) and adapting supply throughout the value chain, all the way to the forest, supporting the sector's contributions to major climate challenges.

The forestry and timber sector aims to contribute to the discussion and inform the authorities about its optimised contribution to the SFEC, and more generally to the low-carbon transition, based on a projection from 2018 to 2050. To this end, it plans to integrate all the data relating to its carbon potential for the climate (sequestration by forest sinks, storage and substitution by products through the use of wood materials, substitution by renewable energy from biomass) and, as a main output, to be able to describe a central future scenario for the sector's contribution.

Another aim is to take sustainable action to adapt forests, maintain their vitality, support the carbon pump, and produce timber, with a forest renewal and risk management plan.
Document Title: Strategic Contract for the Timber Sector (2023-2026) - Press Release

Family Name: Green Finance Agenda (GFA)
Family Summary:
The Green Finance Agenda is centred around the theme “Investing in the future”. The central aspects of the Green Finance Agenda are mobilising capital for the protection of the climate, making Austria sustainable, the managing of climate-relevant risks accordingly, promoting transparency, and a long-term, cost-effective approach to the capital market. Under the Green Finance Agenda, many measures have already been implemented with success, among which the Green Finance Alliance, the Green Investment Hub, the issuing of the first Austrian Green Bond, and activities related to Green Financial Literacy. 

The Green Finance Agenda guides Austria on its way to a climate-friendly, ecologically sustainable financial sector. Moreover, it identifies action areas and implementation steps that enable the scaling of sustainable financial instruments for climate-friendly investments.

Family Name: National Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan
Family Summary:
The Plan contains seven main areas:

■ Infrastructure: Integrate adaptive flood control and flood management measures. Enhance the ability of transportation systems to carry out decision-making, withstand and recover from disruptions, and detect and respond to challenges. Bolster the ability of public works to resist climate shocks. ■ Water resources: Guarantee a stable water supply by developing a diverse range of new water resources, eliminating public water pipe leakages, conserving water and adopting smart technologies for water resource management. ■ Land use: Promote rational land use, such as by advancing nature-based solutions in holistic planning of rural areas, and encouraging water retention landscape design in urban renewal projects. ■ Oceans and coasts: Adopt nature-based solutions to strengthen the adaptability of coastal environments and maintain a dynamic ecological equilibrium. ■ Energy supply and industries: Raise awareness among industries regarding climate change adaptation. Help companies identify and evaluate the extent of risks to their infrastructure from climate hazards such as flooding and high winds. Provide companies with guidance on adaptation strategy planning. ■ Agricultural production and biodiversity: Improve agricultural risk management and lower agricultural losses by administering climate change impact assessments. Bolster ecological resilience by advancing nature-based solutions. ■ Health: Strengthen emergency medical services, disease control systems and occupational health and safety protections. Improve long-term environmental monitoring, risk identification and pollution control measures. Heighten public preparedness by establishing warning systems for extreme temperatures and other awareness mechanisms.
Document Title: National Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan (2023-2026)

Family Name: National Comprehensive Fire Management Strategy (Estrategia Nacional de Manejo Integral del Fuego)
Family Summary:
The National Comprehensive Fire Management Strategy is a comprehensive strategic framework developed in response to increasing environmental and climatic changes that have exacerbated the frequency, intensity, and severity of forest and wildland-urban interface fires in Guatemala. Recognising the significant social, economic, and environmental impacts of these fires (including deforestation, greenhouse gas emissions, and human casualties) the strategy was formulated through a participatory, interinstitutional process involving key national agencies such as CONRED, INAB, CONAP, MARN, MAGA, and international partners like the US Forest Service. The strategy aims to provide a long-term, integrated approach to fire management that balances the mitigation of negative impacts with the promotion of beneficial ecological and societal effects of fire.

The strategy establishes seven strategic lines of action encompassing governance and institutional coordination, fire prevention through legal frameworks and education, specialised fire response systems, knowledge management and technological development, restoration of fire-affected areas, and the development of local fire management plans for priority sites. It emphasises interinstitutional cooperation, standardisation, and interoperability in planning and operations, alongside community engagement and capacity building. The strategy also recognises the ecological role of fire and its potential as a climate change mitigation tool, advocating for a holistic approach that integrates biodiversity conservation, social equity, and cultural diversity. It aligns with international frameworks and sustainable development goals, aiming to strengthen Guatemala’s resilience to fire-related risks through science-based policies, coordinated governance, and inclusive participation.
Document Title: National Fire Management Strategy for Guatemala for the period 2023 to 2032 (Estrategia Nacional para la Gestión del Fuego para Guatemala para el período 2023 al 2032)

Family Name: Natura 2000 Management Programme for the 2023-2028
Family Summary:
The Natura 2000 Management Programme (PUN) for the 2023–2028 period is prepared in accordance with the Decree on Natura 2000 areas and covers both Special Protection Areas (SPA) for birds and Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) for habitats.The programme consists:

  • Detailed Conservation Objectives: Specific targets for zones, species, and habitat types to be maintained in a favorable state.
  • Management Measures: A diverse toolkit including direct nature conservation, adapted use of natural resources, adjusted agricultural practices (farming), and water management.
  • Monitoring and Indicators: Specific metrics to track the effectiveness of measures, including deadlines and funding sources.
  • Ecological Connectivity: Activities to ensure the European ecological network remains linked.
  • Research: Basic and applied science to improve the understanding of species ecology.

It also brings specialized Annexes to facilitate implementation across different sectors. The management programme is important also in the climate perspective due to future trends in emissions and removals in the sector will also be shaped by the restoration or enhancement of carbon-rich natural ecosystems. This includes the restoration of ecosystems such as peatlands, wetlands, shrublands, grasslands, and forest habitat types. The measure is aligned with the Natura 2000 Management Programme for the 2023-2028 period.
Document Title: Decision on Natura 2000 Management Programme for the 2023-2028

Family Name: Guidelines for the development of hydrogen refuelling infrastructure and the promotion of the use of hydrogen-powered road vehicles in Lithuania
Family Summary: The guidelines aim to provide objectives and measures to promote the use of hydrogen in road transport in Lithuania, and have been prepared in accordance with the Law on Alternative Fuels (2021). These actions are intended to increase energy security and contribute to climate mitigation efforts. The guidelines aim for a buildout of ten hydrogen refuelling points nationally by 2030, the first of which is expected in 2024, and also for 5% of new vehicles purchased to be hydrogen-powered by 2030. Other measures are suggested such as tax relief for consumers, and direct purchases of hydrogen-powered vehicles in public procurement.
Document Title: Guidelines for the development of hydrogen refuelling infrastructure and the promotion of the use of hydrogen-powered road vehicles in Lithuania

Family Name: National Shipping Programme until 2030
Family Summary: The National Shipping Programme until 2030 is aimed at increasing the role of inland waterway transport nationally and locally. It prioritises modernising hydrotechnical infrastructure on key river corridors (Odra and Wisła) to support efficient waterborne freight, which can shift cargo from road to lower-emission transport, and includes measures aimed at reducing the emissions intensity of inland vessels and promoting improved traffic management systems that can cut fuel use and pollution.
Document Title: Resolution 180/2023
