Family Name: Low Carbon Pathway for the Turkish Steel Sector
Family Summary:
This report, commissioned by the Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Industry and Technology with the financial support of the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development, presents the “Low Carbon Pathway for the Turkish Steel Sector” reaching net zero by 2053 in the light of these international steel decarbonisation roadmaps, as well as providing detailed information on achieving the desired level of emission reductions. Various scenarios have been constructed to analyse the possible pathways that the sector can follow based on input, technology and policy parameters and the corresponding investment requirements.

It aims to lay the groundwork for the Turkish steel sector to accomplish green transformation in a manner that complies with Paris Agreement objectives. The resulting policy recommendations are mapped to two key policy themes: A) Input and technology and B) Policy and market.

The Input and Technology policy theme includes: Input Optimisation; Technologies Reducing Direct Carbon Output; Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS) Technologies; Process Improvement; Green Energy; Inclusive Employment; and Upskilling/Reskilling of Labor Force.

The Policy and Market policy theme includes: Emission Trading System (ETS) Trade Models; National Policy Documents; Green Transformation; Finance; Cooperation; and Circular Economy.
Document Title: Low Carbon Pathway for the Turkish Steel Sector

Family Name: A Low Carbon Pathway for the Aluminium Sector in the Republic of Türkiye
Family Summary:
This report, commissioned by the Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Industry and Technology with the financial support of the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development, aims to lay the groundwork for the aluminium sector in Türkiye to accomplish green transformation in a manner that complies with Paris Agreement objectives. This project also serves to achieve Türkiye’s net zero target for 2053, and interim target as per its updated NDC. This includes laying the groundwork for Green Technology Roadmaps (to be prepared in 2023-2024 period).

The country has flourishing semi-aluminium processing operations with efficient yet very limited primary manufacturing. This study stands out as one of the initial ones to incorporate the modelling of semi-aluminium processing (remelting and refining) alongside primary aluminium production. This roadmap,can serve as foundation to developing investment plan and platform that helps to accelerate implementation of actions recommended by bringing together relevant actors and sharing a common vision for the sector. To bring the aluminium sector close to net zero emissions by 2053, the key decarbonisation levers identified by this study are: increased recycling (of aluminium), adoption of new, frontier technologies and transition to low-carbon energy.
Document Title: A Low Carbon Pathway for the Aluminium Sector in the Republic of Türkiye

Family Name: Strategy on Preparing the Romanian Armed Forces to Address Climate Change and Energy Transition 2023
Family Summary:
The Ministry of National Defence will continue to support national efforts to address climate change and energy transition through concrete measures and actions, based on national interests and taking into account the commitments assumed within NATO, EU and UN related to energy efficiency, resilience of defence capabilities and military infrastructure, limiting the environmental and logistical footprint of the Romanian Armed Forces as well as the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions.

At the same time, the military organisation will actively contribute to preventing and combating the effects of climate change in Romania, amid the increasing frequency of extreme weather events, floods and prolonged droughts. Through this Strategy, we make a strong commitment to improve the capacity to adapt and increase the resilience of military organisations to the impact of climate change, reducing pollution and significantly decreasing greenhouse gas emissions from military activities and facilities, without affecting the operational capability, cost efficiency and safety of military personnel. Thus, through its specialised units in environmental protection, climate change and sustainable development, the Ministry of National Defence aims to reduce the impact on the environment and biodiversity, in accordance with national and international standards. Considering the specificities of the defence sector, in particular the need to maintain and improve our capacity to perform missions, as well as depending on socio-economic and technical-scientific developments, an indicative target of a 50% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2040 is proposed.

The five main lines of action are: 1. Adapting policies, plans and regulatory framework; 2. Increasing energy efficiency of military capabilities; 3. Transition to sustainable energy for defence infrastructure; 4. Organisational transformation and staff training; and 5. Strengthening cooperation with EU Member States, NATO and partners.
Document Title: Strategy on Preparing the Romanian Armed Forces to Address Climate Change and Energy Transition 2023

Family Name: Charging Our Future: National electric vehicle charging strategy for Aotearoa New Zealand 2023-2035
Family Summary: This is the long-term vision and strategic plan for Aotearoa New Zealand’s electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure.As long term vision it will support an equitable transition to a low-emissions transport system, ensuring accessible, affordable, secure, and reliable charging is available to everyone who needs it. This vision guides the rapid expansion of the EV charging infrastructure system from 2023 to 2035.The stragegic plan lays down five long-term outcomes, amongst them the outcome 5, which will support the ransition to, and use of, low-emissions transport modes across the wider transport system by decarbonising transport modes across the system and ensuring a coordinated investment approach. This involves research into system-wide charging needs for heavy vehicles, planes, trains, and ships, including opportunities for co-location.The main target is to have a journey charging hub every 150-200km on main highways by 2028. Additionally, the strategy aims to support the installation of at least 600 EV charging stations in rural locations by 2028.
Document Title: Charging Our Future: National electric vehicle charging strategy for Aotearoa New Zealand 2023-2035

Family Name: National Strategy on Gender and Climate Change 2023-2030
Family Summary:
This Strategy is a planning document for all actions in the field of gender and climate change. It defines the Central African Republic's vision on gender issues related to climate change, in line with the guidelines of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It is jointly led by the National Climate Coordinator of the Ministry of the Environment and Sustainable Development, and the Directorate-General for Gender Promotion of the Ministry for the Promotion of Gender and the Protection of Women, Families and Children. The Strategy covers the strategic framework, the action plan, and the framework for implementation, monitoring, evaluation and financing.

The strategic areas are:

  1. Governance, coordination and climate finance;
  2. Specific actions in priority sectors for combating climate change;
  3. Capacity-building and knowledge transfer;
  4. Information, awareness-raising and communication; and
  5. Empowerment and climate leadership of women and vulnerable groups in a secure environment.
Document Title: National Strategy on Gender and Climate Change 2023-2030

Family Name: National Strategy on Gender and Climate Change in the Central African Republic (2023-2030)
Family Summary: The National Strategy on Gender and Climate Change in the Central African Republic (Stratégie Nationale Genre et Changements Climatiques de La République Centrafricaine 2023-2030) outlines a comprehensive, five-axis approach to ensure gender and social inclusion are integrated into the nation's climate action. The first axis focuses on governance, coordination, and climate finance, aiming to strengthen the institutional framework and mobilize funding to integrate gender in all climate actions (Objective 1). The second axis targets specific actions in priority sectors like agriculture, water resources, and energy, with the goal of mainstreaming the gender and social inclusion approach into the design and monitoring of adaptation and mitigation programs (Objective 2). To build a qualified workforce, the third axis emphasizes capacity building and knowledge transfer, seeking to improve stakeholders' expertise in gender-responsive adaptation and mitigation (Objective 3). Axes four and five address critical social aspects: the fourth focuses on Information, awareness, and communication to enhance understanding of the gender-climate link among all stakeholders (Objective 4), while the fifth aims at the empowerment and climate leadership of women and vulnerable groups in a secure environment (Objective 5), supporting their participation and building their financial, material, and intellectual capacity to lead climate resilience efforts.
Document Title: National Strategy on Gender and Climate Change in the Central African Republic (2023-2030)

Family Name: National Tourism Master Plan 2023 update
Family Summary: Belize's National Tourism Master Plan 2023 update sets long-term priorities and actions in the tourism sector. The plan acknowledges climate change as a particular threat to the industry, as tourism is concentrated along the coast where flooding impacts are expected to be most severe in extreme weather. It emphasises the need for detailed spatial planning with greater national co-ordination around disaster risks, and the need to mitigate emissions in the transport sector. The plan also discusses synergies with rural land use and forest systems.
Document Title: National Tourism Master Plan 2023 update

Family Name: Danish Action Plan for Plant-based Foods
Family Summary: This Action Plan constitutes a catalogue of initiatives from a number of departments, all of which are considered to promote plant-based foods, contributing to reducing the carbon footprint of the agricultural sector. It is intended to inspire action among all actors in Danish food systems who influence food choices every day; from the farmer and food producer to the retailer, the canteen provider and the export markets, and also the consumer on their daily trip to the supermarket. Actions include voluntary state-controlled climate labelling for foods and dietary advice for meals aimed at professional kitchens.
Document Title: Danish Action Plan for Plant-based Foods

Family Name: National Water and Sanitation Policy
Family Summary: The policy aims to guide the development of the water and sanitation sector in Rwanda, ensuring greater and more equitable access, and ensuring resilient infrastructure systems. It promotes the expansion and effective management of hydrological monitoring stations, catchment afforestation and erosion control, borehole management, transboundary watershed cooperation, and further expansion of the supporting legal/policy framework on water systems. It estimates a budget of 40,000 RwF to implement climate-resilient water supply projects over the 2023-2032 period.
Document Title: National Water and Sanitation Policy

Family Name: 8th Energy Research Programme
Family Summary:
The Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWE) has defined the guidelines for funding applied energy research through this programme as part of a mission-oriented innovation policy, aiming to help achieve a climate-neutral and resilient energy system by 2045. It supports the Federal Government's energy and climate policy goals, while also securing value creation, jobs, and prosperity in Germany, and strengthening the international competitiveness of German companies in modern energy technologies. It has 5 priority missions:Five priority missions:

  • Mission Energy System — research for a resilient and efficient energy system
  • Mission Heat Transition — research for a climate-neutral heating and cooling supply
  • Mission Electricity Transition — research for converting electricity supply to renewable energies
  • Mission Hydrogen — research for a sustainable hydrogen economy
  • Mission Transfer — rapid transfer of research results into practice
Document Title: Energy Research Programme

Family Name: National Gender and Climate Change Strategy of the Central African Republic
Family Summary: The Central African Republic's government is firmly committed to promoting gender equality and eliminating violence against women. The initial National Adaptation Plan (NAP) establishes gender sensitivity as one of its guiding principles and proposes some concrete actions to advance gender integration into adaptation policies and programs in the coming years. However, despite institutional progress, gender inequalities persist. This National Gender and Climate Change Strategy (NGCCS) was developed to address this weakness and help accelerate the implementation of actions to integrate gender into climate policies. The NGCS is a planning document for all actions in the field of gender and climate change. It defines the Central African Republic's vision on gender issues related to climate change, in accordance with the guidelines of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Document Title: Stratégie Nationale Genre et Changements Climatiques de La République Centrafricaine 2023-2030

Family Name: Honduras Biogas Roadmap
Family Summary: The Honduras Biogas Roadmap promotes biogas development nationally as a tool to promote energy security and contribute to net emissions mitigation goals. It also notes synergies across sectors, including biogas production slurry as a fertiliser contributing to climate resilience in agriculture.
Document Title: Honduras Biogas Roadmap

Family Name: Community Solar Banks Program and Community Batteries for Household Solar program
Family Summary:
The government has instituted two mechanisms to support community solar projects.

  1. The Community Batteries for Household Solar program makes up to AUD 200 million available to install over 400 batteries and provide flexibility to over 100,000 households across the country.
  2. The Community solar banks fund aims to support shared solar systems for people who cannot install solar systems on their own. Under the fund, the government is co-investing AUD 100 million to deploy these systems over the country.

Family Name: Ministerial Decree No. 348 on information system on renewable energy sources
Family Summary: This Decree determines the legal, organisational and technological foundations for the formation and implementation of the information system on renewable energy sources, and its integration with the information systems and resources of other institutions through the Electronic Government Information System. This includes an information system on renewable energy sources and the volume of revenue from the sale of carbon dioxide emission quotas for saved fuel. An atlas of renewable energy sources is created as an integral part of the information system on renewable energy sources.
Document Title: Ministerial Decree No. 348 on information system on renewable energy sources.

Family Name: Ministerial Decree No. 347 on the procedure and form for issuing a certificate on the source of electricity produced from renewable energy sources
Family Summary: This Decree regulates the issuance, renewal and termination of a certificate on the source of electricity produced from renewable energy sources. The certificate shall be issued by the State Agency for Renewable Energy Sources under the Ministry of Energy upon the application by conducting an inspection of generating facilities producing electricity from renewable energy sources.
Document Title: Ministerial Decree No. 347 on the procedure and form for issuing a certificate on the source of electricity produced from renewable energy sources

Family Name: Subsidy for hydrogen production by electrolysis (OWE)
Family Summary:
In order to meet the Dutch climate targets, the government wants to encourage the production of renewable hydrogen with an electrolyser. For the production, large electrolysis plants are needed. The subsidy for hydrogen production by electrolysis (OWE) is for companies that realise and use hydrogen production plants for the production of renewable hydrogen. For this, an electrolyser must have a capacity of 0.5 to a maximum of 50 megawatts. This scheme aims to make the investment in, and operation of, electrolysis plants more attractive. The OWE subsidy is a combination of an investment subsidy, and operational subsidy: you only receive the subsidy if you also produce hydrogen with your hydrogen production plant. 

The budget for the 2023 subsidy round was € 245.600.000. In 2024 a second round of applications will take place.
Document Title: Subsidy for hydrogen production by electrolysis (OWE)

Family Name: Executive Order on Withdrawal of Agricultural Production from Carbon-Rich Soils (Peatland Restoration)
Family Summary:
This Executive Order establishes a framework for projects that withdraw carbon-rich lowland soils from agricultural operation and, through the interruption of drains, closing of ditches etc., restores natural hydrology to the greatest extent possible (climate lowland projects).

The purpose of climate lowland projects is to achieve a reduction in CO2 emissions and at the same time support other considerations, particularly regarding nature, the environment and climate adaptation.

The Danish Environmental Protection Agency may, in accordance with the rules in this executive order, provide subsidies for climate lowland projects to municipalities, to landowners, to national park funds, and to funds with non-profit nature, environmental or climate purposes. The subsidy includes landowner compensation. The Danish Nature Agency may implement climate lowland projects within the framework of the allocated grant and purpose statement in Implementation may take place by fully or partially purchasing project land, purchasing replacement land, selling these, land distribution and agreeing on landowner compensation in accordance with the rules in this executive order.
Document Title: Executive Order on Withdrawal of Agricultural Production from Carbon-Rich Soils (Peatland Restoration)

Family Name: Energy Transition and Investment Plan
Family Summary: This Plan offers a consolidated strategy for the energy sector to decarbonise, covering the areas of renewable energy, energy efficiency, hydrogen, e-mobility, energy storage and sustainable cooking solutions. The Plan is led by the guiding principles of investment, new growth sectors, energy security and trade balance, employment impact, environmental sustainability and affordability.
Document Title: Energy Transition and Investment Plan

Family Name: K-ETS Market Enhancement Plan
Family Summary: This Plan is meant to improve emission market regulation and expand the number of participants. Korea's emission trading market has had a limit to inducing companies to invest in greenhouse gas reduction due to low trading volume and high price volatility, which has hindered the effectiveness of the system. Korea will introduce consignment transactions so that emissions can be easily traded through securities companies, and gradually expand the target audience that can participate in transactions such as financial institutions and individuals. In addition, in order to resolve the imbalance between supply and demand of emission rights, the mandatory deadline for companies applying the emission rights transaction system to convert their performance of reducing greenhouse gases to offset emission rights will be extended from the existing 2 years after the reduction performance certification to 5 years.
Document Title: K-ETS Market Enhancement Plan

Family Name: Agreement on strengthened framework conditions for CCS in Denmark of 20 September 2023
Family Summary:
The 20 September 2023 Agreement on strengthened framework conditions for CCS in Denmark consolidates establishes a CCUS Fund, which consolidates previous funding initiatives managed by the Danish Energy Agency, to accelerate the deployment of carbon capture, transport, and storage (CCS) technologies.

The agreement aims to deliver a significant portion of Denmark’s climate target of reducing CO2 emissions by 70% by 2030, with a target to capture and store at least 34 million tons of CO2. The Danish state, via Nordsøfonden, will take a 20% ownership stake in new onshore and offshore storage licenses to ensure public interest and oversight.
Document Title: CCS tenders and other funding for CCS development

Family Name: Principles for Net Zero Financing and Investment
Family Summary: This document outlines a set of guidelines for net-zero financing and investment within the United States, produced by the US Department of the Treasury. The principles aim to guide financial institutions by highlighting the importance and value of financial institutions’ net-zero commitments; promoting consistency and credibility in financial institutions’ approaches to these commitments; and encouraging the adoption of best practices that relate to these commitments.
Document Title: Guidelines on Principles for Net Zero Financing and Investment

Family Name: Decree-Law 77/2023 on Coastlines
Family Summary:
The purpose of this Decree-Law is to establish the set of mechanisms, actions, and instruments that must be applied in the coastal and protection zone, aimed at its sustainable use, as well as the protection of human settlements and the processes of economic and social development therein.

Climate-related provisions include:

  • Article 12: The Land Use and Urban Planning of the Coastal Zone aims to reduce the degree of exposure to hazards that may affect it, mainly those associated with climate change. Actions include contributing, through land use and urban planning management tools, to the progressive organisation of essential protection works to safeguard buildings exposed to the hazards identified in medium- and long-term climate scenarios, as well as the corresponding hazard, vulnerability, and risk studies.
  • Article 50.2: The Ministry of Science, Technology, and Environment is responsible for evaluating those cays with the characteristics indicated above, based on available scientific and technological results, medium- and long-term climate scenarios, and current strategic development plans and programs.

This Decree-Law is supported by Decree 97 - Regulations of Decree-Law 77 on Coastlines.
Document Title: Decree-Law 77/2023 on Coastlines and Decree 97

Family Name: Sustainable Finance Mobilization Strategy (EMFS)
Family Summary: Sustainable Financing Mobilization Strategy (EMFS), developed by Mexico's Ministry of Finance and Public Credit, represents a comprehensive framework for redirecting financial flows towards sustainable development whilst addressing climate change challenges. The strategy identifies a substantial financing gap of 13.6 trillion mexican pesos between 2023 and 2030, requiring annual mobilisation of 1.7 trillion pesos (equivalent to 5.4% of 2023 GDP) to achieve the country's sustainable development targets. Through its three foundational pillars (Sustainable Public Financial Management, Sustainable Finance Mobilisation, and Cross-cutting Actions) the EMFS aims to mobilise up to 15 trillion pesos during this period by engaging public, private, and social sectors in voluntary adoption of sustainable finance practices.The strategy places significant emphasis on climate change mitigation and adaptation, acknowledging that approximately 40% of Mexican territory and 68% of its population are exposed to climate impacts due to the country's geographical location and socioeconomic structure. The EMFS integrates climate risk management into public financial planning, promotes investment in resilient infrastructure and nature-based solutions, and addresses biodiversity loss as a critical environmental challenge. Underpinned by principles of climate justice, environmental justice, and social justice, the strategy seeks to align Mexico's economic development with international climate commitments, including the Paris Agreement and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. The framework particularly emphasises the nexus between poverty and climate vulnerability, incorporating gender perspectives and social inclusion measures to ensure that sustainable finance mobilisation addresses both environmental degradation and socioeconomic inequalities simultaneously.
Document Title: Sustainable Finance Mobilization Strategy (EMFS) [Estrategia de Movilización de Financiamiento Sostenible (EMFS)]

Family Name: Electricity Demand Side Management Measures
Family Summary:
These Measures apply to the demand-side management of electricity within China. The Measures were introduced to "implement the major strategic decisions of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council on carbon peaking and achieving carbon neutrality..." (Article 1).

Article 14 includes a target for "demand response capability". By 2025, the capacity of each province to respond to demand will reach 3%-5% of the maximum electricity load, with provinces with an annual peak valley difference rate of over 40% reaching 5% or more.

The Measures were introduced in accordance with existing laws and regulations, including the Electric Power Law, the Energy Conservation Law, the Regulations on the Supply and Use of Electric Power.
Document Title: Notice on Measures (2023 Edition)

Family Name: Updated Strategic Plan for National Development to 2050 ("PEDN al 2050") [Plan Estratégico de Desarrollo Nacional al 2050 actualizado ("PEDN al 2050")]
Family Summary:
The updated Strategic Plan for National Development to 2050 (PEDN al 2050), approved by Supreme Decree N° 103-2023-PCM, constitutes Peru's principal long-term strategic planning instrument. Issued by the National Centre for Strategic Planning (CEPLAN), it articulates a national vision and establishes four overarching National Objectives designed to guide public policy formulation across all levels of government. Central to this framework is the explicit integration of climate change and environmental sustainability. Specifically, National Objective 2 commits to the sustainable management of the territory in order to prevent and reduce risks affecting people and their livelihoods, expressly situated within the context of a changing climate.

The plan operationalises this commitment through a series of strategic priorities and immediate actions. These include measures aimed at catalysing an energy transition, such as replacing the fossil fuel-based transport matrix with electric vehicles and promoting the importation of components for solar energy systems. Furthermore, the strategy emphasises the need to strengthen the integral management of climate change, including the monitoring of greenhouse gas emissions reductions and the effective utilisation of international climate finance. Collectively, these provisions are designed to enhance Peru's adaptive capacity and address systemic environmental challenges, including deforestation and waste management, thereby aligning national development with principles of climate resilience and environmental stewardship.
Document Title: Indicators. National Strategic Development Plan to 2050 (Indicadores. Plan Estratégico de Desarrollo Nacional al 2050)

Family Name: National Strategic Development Plan (PEDN) to 2050 [Plan Estratégico de Desarrollo Nacional (PEDN) al 2050]
Family Summary:
The Supreme Decree updates the National Strategic Development Plan ( Plan Estratégico de Desarrollo Nacional "PEDN") to 2050, outlining a long-term vision for Peru’s socio-economic and environmental development. Central to this framework is Objective 2, which prioritizes gestión sostenible del territorio (sustainable territorial management) to mitigate climate-related risks, protect livelihoods, and integrate climate resilience into national planning. The policy emphasizes reducing vulnerability through disaster risk management, climate adaptation, and the use of science and technology, aligning with international climate commitments such as the Paris Agreement. It underscores the need for coordinated governance across sectors, including water resource management, biodiversity conservation, and territorial ordering, to address structural challenges like climate change, inequality, and institutional weaknesses. This approach reflects Fisher’s focus on statutory environmental governance, as it institutionalizes climate resilience within national development strategies, while Sands’ international law perspective is evident in its alignment with global climate frameworks and transnational cooperation.

The PEDN also outlines immediate actions to address climate impacts, including optimizing non-reimbursable climate funds, enhancing public education on waste management, promoting solar energy adoption, and transitioning to electric vehicles. These measures aim to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, strengthen climate adaptation, and foster sustainable economic growth. The plan integrates climate action with broader goals of social equity, digital transformation, and institutional strengthening, reflecting Setzer’s emphasis on pragmatic policy innovation. By linking climate resilience to territorial management, the PEDN positions climate change as a cross-cutting priority, requiring systemic reforms in governance, infrastructure, and resource use. The document highlights the interplay between national development and global climate imperatives, ensuring that Peru’s trajectory aligns with both domestic needs and international obligations, while addressing historical structural challenges such as corruption and institutional fragility.
Document Title: National Strategic Development Plan to 2050 - Vol. II (Plan Estratégico de Desarrollo Nacional al 2050 - Tomo II)

Collection Summary:
The National Climate Change Plan (the Climate Plan) guides adaptation and mitigation efforts to reduce the adverse effects of climate change and the vulnerability of environmental, social, and economic systems.
The Resolution No. 03, dated September 14, 2023, provides for the update of the Climate Plan and defines it as an instrument of the National Policy on Climate Change (PNMC) to consolidate the strategies, plans, and targets of the Federal Executive Branch, contributing to the objectives of the Policy and to the achievement of the targets established in the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) under the Paris Agreement.
Family Name: Brazil's Adaptation Climate Plan: Sectoral Plan for Industry and Mining
Family Summary:
Brazil’s Sectoral Plan for Industry and Mining aims to increase the climate resilience of industrial and mining sectors by integrating climate risk management into planning, strengthening adaptive capacity across value chains, and protecting productivity, infrastructure, and competitiveness from climate-related impacts.

The main objectives are:

  • Strengthen the adaptive capacity and resilience of industrial and mining sectors to climate change.
  • Identify, assess, and manage climate risks affecting production, infrastructure, logistics, and supply chains.
  • Integrate climate adaptation into industrial and mining planning, investment, and governance processes.
  • Promote technological innovation and resilient infrastructure to reduce climate vulnerabilities.
  • Enhance the long-term sustainability and competitiveness of industrial and mining value chains.
  • Develop territorial adaptation approaches for climate-vulnerable industrial and mining regions and clusters.
Document Title: Brazil's Adaptation Climate Plan: Sectoral Plan for Industry and Mining

Family Name: National Electricity Plan 2023-2027
Family Summary: The National Electricity Plan serves as the main high-level guidance for development, reforms, improvement and sustainability of the power sector from 2023-2027. It identifies three overarching goals for the sector for this period: access to affordable energy; energy security; and sustainability. The plan contains measures for both climate adaptation and resilience, acknowledging the threats of extreme weather to grid security, as well as the need to decarbonise the power supply. The plan aims to contribute to a 65% share of clean energy in the generation mix by 2030. The plan promotes the exploration of new financing mechanisms for this decarbonisation, such as green bonds, international climate funds and debt-nature swaps.
Document Title: National Electricity Plan 2023-2027

Family Name: Federal Decree No. 11.700/2023 on the National Urban and Peri-urban Agriculture Programme and the National Urban and Peri-urban Agriculture Programme Working Group
Family Summary: This decree establishes the National Urban and Peri-urban Agriculture Programme and the National Urban and Peri-urban Agriculture Programme Working Group. One of its objectives is to promote the development of healthier, more sustainable cities that are resilient to climate change, combat environmental racism and encourage the adoption of climate change adaptation and mitigation practices, and establish the measures that must be adopted by each competent body to this end.
Document Title: Federal Decree No. 11.700/2023

Family Name: Critical Minerals Strategy
Family Summary:
This Strategy sets the stage across the country for job creation, economic growth, the advancement of reconciliation with Indigenous peoples and close cooperation with Canada’s allies — in line with Canadian and international climate and nature protection objectives. The Strategy is meant to secure Canada’s advantage as the world’s supplier of choice for critical minerals and the clean technologies they enable, by further developing supply chains.

The Canadian Critical Minerals Strategy addresses five core objectives:

  1. supporting economic growth, competitiveness, and job creation;
  2. promoting climate action and environmental protection;
  3. advancing reconciliation with Indigenous peoples;
  4. fostering diverse and inclusive workforces and communities; and
  5. enhancing global security and partnerships with allies.

Under the second objective of promoting climate action and environmental protection, Canada seeks to advance "nature forward" approaches, which seek to incorporate practices that prevent biodiversity loss, protect species at risk and support nature protection. GHG emissions are reduced through the deployment of clean technologies and low-emission industrial processes, in line with Canada's Emissions Reduction Plan. In addition, waste is reduced, end-of-life products are reused, and their mineral content recycled by means of innovative technologies and processing techniques.

These objectives will be achieved by focusing on six areas of focus:

  1. driving research, innovation, and exploration;
  2. accelerating project development;
  3. building sustainable infrastructure;
  4. advancing reconciliation with Indigenous peoples;
  5. growing a diverse workforce and prosperous communities; and
  6. strengthening global leadership and security.
Document Title: The Canadian Critical Minerals Strategy

Family Name: Muscat Stock Exchange ESG Guidelines
Family Summary:
The Muscat Stock Exchange (MSX) has become the first state regulator in Oman to issue environmental, social and governance (ESG) guidelines (Guidelines). The MSX was formerly known as the Muscat Securities Market, which was established in 1988 and continues to operate under Oman's Capital Market Authority, the regulator of publicly listed companies in Oman. The MSX underwent a restructure in 2001 and its key mandate currently focuses on facilitating the listing and trading of securities in Oman and monitoring and regulating the Omani securities market.

In issuing the Guidelines, the MSX set out 30 metrics to measure a public company’s impact on environmental sustainability, societal responsibility and governance matters, including the measurement of carbon emissions.

The Guidelines are intended to promote transparency and robustness of ESG reporting by encouraging voluntary reporting in 2024 (for activities conducted in 2023). Reporting will be mandatory for public companies from 2025 onwards, with the first mandatory reports to be filed by 31 March 2025. Moreover, the Guidelines also introduce regional-level environmental responsibility initiatives, such as reducing single-use plastics and paper waste while promoting recycling and clean energy use, as well as, underlines Oman's ongoing commitment in establishing an inclusive and sustainable economic development.

From 2025, public companies will be required to publish standalone ESG reports according to Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Universal Standards. These reports must document changes in various performance metrics such as energy management sustainability oversight by senior management, ratio gender equality measures and diversity at various organisational levels.
Document Title: MSX ESG Guidelines

Family Name: Decree No. 2023-068/P/CNSP on the organization of the government and establishing the responsibilities of the Ministers of State
Family Summary: According to Decree No. 2023-068/P/CNSP, the Minister of Energy is responsible, in conjunction with the other ministers concerned, for the design, development, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of the national policy on energy and renewable energy, in accordance with the guidelines defined by the Government. In this capacity, he exercises, among other things, the following responsibilities: (i) the design, development and implementation of strategies and programs for the development of activities in the field of Energy; (ii) the development of technologies for the promotion of clean renewable energy; (iii) the development and implementation of strategies and programs promoting the use of wood energy substitutes in the fight against desertification and deforestation.
Document Title: Decree No. 2023-068/P/CNSP

Family Name: Canada Green Buildings Strategy (CGBS)
Family Summary:
The CGBS sets out the Government’s vision and next steps for greener, more energy efficient and affordable homes and buildings. It outlines how the Government is acting to drive down monthly energy bills, to help Canadians reduce their carbon emissions, and ensure that the homes and workplaces of Canadians are protected against the increasingly harmful effects of climate change. The CGBS aims to decarbonize and improve the resiliency of Canada’s buildings stock, while supporting affordability, job creation and economic growth. It centers around three priorities:

1. Accelerate retrofits

2. Build green and affordable from the start

3. Shape the buildings sector of the future
Document Title: The Canada Green Buildings Strategy

Family Name: National Electromobility Strategy
Family Summary: Honduras' National Electromobility Strategy aims to promote electrified transport systems nationally, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and enhancing energy independence through decreased fossil fuel demand. By 2050 the strategy aims to initiate a range of pilot projects across land and maritime transport, strengthen institutional support capacities and ensure the integration of electromobility systems with grid integration from renewable energy generation. It promotes the development of energy pricing and urban planning incentives, further regulation and the development of financing mechanisms.
Document Title: National Electromobility Strategy

Family Name: Green Hydrogen Strategy and Roadmap for Kenya
Family Summary: Kenya wishes to establish a green hydrogen industry. It will first develop a coordination committee and secretariat, followed by establishing local and international partnerships for training and capacity building, before expanding cooperation and partnerships on green hydrogen.
Document Title: Green Hydrogen Strategy and Roadmap for Kenya

Family Name: Climate Strategy Agriculture and Food 2050
Family Summary:
The Climate Strategy Agriculture and Food 2050 seeks to support the two sectors with climate mitigation and adaptation efforts and comprises two parts. The first (general) part contains principles, objectives, and directions.


The general principles require climate adaptation and mitigation efforts to follow sustainability principles and harness synergies. Further, it is stressed that climate adaptation and mitigation efforts are an overall societal task. Lastly, it is clarified that policy measures must be informed by the best available science and by the precautionary principle.


The strategy aims at realising the following three objectives by 2050:


  • The agriculture sector ensures climate and site-adapted production and achieves a self-sufficiency rate of at least 50%.
  • The population follows a healthy and balanced diet. As a result, the populations’ capita food-related environmental footprint is reduced by 2/3 compared to 2020 levels.
  • Greenhouse gas emissions from the agriculture sector are reduced by 40% compared to 1990 levels.


To reach these goals, the strategy seeks to expand research on food system reform. Additionally, existing policy instruments must be further developed. Ultimately, the aim is to ensure that the agriculture and food system contribute to the realisation of the economy-wide net zero target by 2050 and to keep climate risks to an absolute minimum.


The second part comprises 42 measures, including already existing and new measures.


These measures concern consumption and production and include mitigation and adaptation efforts or both.


The measures seek to expand knowledge, strengthen participation, and/or develop policies coherently and target consumption patterns, food waste, trade relations, production portfolios, nutrients, water, soil, and energy.


The strategy also clarifies whether the measures are possible based on current regulations or whether regulatory amendments are needed, such as is the case with the promotion of renewables.
Document Title: Strategy - Part 2

Family Name: Medium Term Program
Family Summary:
The 2024-2026 program sets out the national macroeconomic framework for 2024-2026, serving as a roadmap for the private sector and the general investment environment. Its main objectives are to 1) maintain a stable growth environment, 2) reduce inflation through implementing a tight monetary stance and fiscal discipline and 3) build a healthy business environment and increase employment opportunities by promoting green and digital transformations on production and export processes. The green transformation process supports climate change mitigation and adaptation strategies as well as national just transition objectives.

The 2026-2028 program's main objective is to ensure price stability, preserve financial stability, andstrengthen the competitive position of the economy. This will be achieved by increasing productivity in a manner that contributes to balanced, sustainable, and inclusive growth, supports permanent welfare gains, promotes fair income distribution, and maintains economic resilience. The program states that the green transformation process will be accelerated through renewable energy investments, the enhancement of domestic technology development capacity, and the use of sustainable financing instruments, prioritizing low-carbon production, resource efficiency, and circular economy practices, particularly in the energy, transport, industry, and agriculture sectors. This includes enacting secondary legislation containing provisions on greenhouse gas emission reduction and climate change adaptation under the Climate Law; implementing the emissions trading system; and establishing the Green Taxonomy.

The 2027-2029 program focuses on ensuring the continuation of the process to bring inflation down to single digits and to achieve price stability. Competition in product markets will be strengthened, and supply-side supportive policies will be implemented in relevant sectors, particularly food, housing, and education. The green transformation process remains similar to that of the 2026-2028 program under this program.
Document Title: Medium Term Program 2027-2029

Family Name: New Industrial Master Plan 2030
Family Summary: The plan provides strategic guidance, positions Malaysia’s industry for investor engagement, and enhances the government’s role in shaping the economy. Departing from previous industrial master plans, the 2030 Plan adopts a mission-based approach. Notably, Mission 3 - Push for Net Zero emphasises sustainable practices and green initiatives, aiming to reduce emissions and build a climate-resilient, environmentally friendly economy.
Document Title: New Industrial Master Plan 2030

Family Name: Canada’s Carbon Management Strategy
Family Summary:
This Strategy delivers on Canada’s commitment to develop a comprehensive Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS) Strategy. It focuses on technology-enabled carbon management solutions that support reducing, removing, and reusing CO2—while recognising the importance of nature-based solutions in supporting a net-zero economy.

This Strategy outlines 5 federal priorities guiding the Government’s approach to promoting a competitive and robust carbon management sector in Canada:

  1. Accelerating innovation and RDD
  2. Advancing policies and regulations
  3. Attracting investment and trade opportunities
  4. Scaling up projects and infrastructure
  5. Building partnerships and growing inclusive workforces
Document Title: Capturing the Opportunity: A Carbon Management Strategy for Canada

Family Name: National Strategy for the Development of a Hydrogen Economy
Family Summary: This strategy outlines Argentina’s plan to establish a competitive low-emissions hydrogen industry and position itself as a major exporter. It establishes a target to produce 5 mt/year of “low emissions hydrogen” by 2050, which will require 55 GW of renewable electricity generation capacity and 30 GW of electrolysis capacity. Around 80% of total production is expected to be exported.
Document Title: National Strategy for the Development of the Hydrogen Economy

Family Name: National Energy Transition Roadmap
Family Summary:
The Roadmap aims to accelerate Malaysia's shift to sustainable energy, boosting climate resilience and national prosperity. Through the Responsible Transition Pathway 2050, the Roadmap seeks to transition from fossil fuels to low-carbon alternatives. It includes 50 initiatives, 6 energy transition levers, 5 enablers, and 10 flagship projects, with funding through grants, loans, incentives, and investments.

The NETR sets out four guiding principles:

  • Align the energy sector with Malaysia’s national and sustainability goals.
  • Ensure inclusive, cost-effective transition benefits for all. It recognises the challenges faced by low-income and vulnerable populations, ensuring that the benefits and opportunities from the energy transition extend to all segments of society.
  • Foster effective governance and stakeholder collaboration. Collaboration among all stakeholders is essential to create a dynamic energy industry ecosystem that supports sustainability and facilitates the transition to a low-carbon economy.
  • Generate high-impact jobs and support small and medium enterprises' involvement.
Document Title: National Energy Transition Roadmap

Family Name: Fund for negative CO2 emissions (NECCS Fund)
Family Summary:
Under this Fund, Danish Energy Agency awarded contracts to three companies for new CCS projects. Together, the projects will ensure the capture and storage of 160,350 tonnes of CO2 annually during the period 2026 to 2032. This corresponds to the annual CO2 absorption from approximately 16,000 hectares of forest.

The NECCS fund aims to support the capture and storage of CO2 originating from biomass, so-called biogenic CO2.
Document Title: Fund for negative CO2 emissions (NECCS Fund)

Family Name: Notice on Deepening the Pilot Program of Climate Adaptable City Construction
Family Summary: The Notice on Deepening the Pilot Program of Climate Adaptable City Construction states the key tasks for the pilot selection for climate-adaptive city construction was organized and carried out. These pilot projects are meant to enhance the system and mechanism of urban ''physical examination'', further adjusted and improved the urban physical examination index system, incorporating metrics such as ''reduction in severe waterlogging-prone areas'' and ''emergency rescue capability for urban drainage and waterlogging prevention'', etc. into the index system. Through this system, there could be identification of existing challenges in urban resilience against extreme weather, such as rainstorms, and therefore implementation of targeted renovations to enhance urban safety and resilience.
Document Title: Notice on Deepening the Pilot Program of Climate Adaptable City Construction

Family Name: Regional Microgrids Program
Family Summary: This Program has two funding streams: Regional Australia Microgrid Pilots and First Nations Community Microgrids. This Program provides AU$125 million of grants delivered by ARENA over four years from the 2022-23 financial year to support development and deployment of microgrid projects, with AU$75 million allocated to First Nations communities.
Document Title: Regional Microgrids Program

Family Name: Federal Decree No. 11.666/2023 on the Kigali Amendment
Family Summary: Federal Decree 11.666/2023 promulgates the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer.
Document Title: Federal Decree 11.666/2023

Family Name: CMN Resolution 5.095/2023, which provides for funding from the National Climate Change Fund (FNMC)
Family Summary: This resolution regulates financing from the National Fund on Climate Change (FNMC), the purpose of which is to support the implementation of projects, technological development and productive capacity and the acquisition of machinery and equipment related to the mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions and adaptation to climate change and its effects.
Document Title: CMN Resolution 5.095/2023

Family Name: Carbon Net Zero 2050 Roadmap and Strategic Plan
Family Summary:
The Roadmap and Strategic Plan provide a broad and detailed guiding framework for the achievement of net-zero emissions in Sri Lanka by 2050, to be achieved by emissions reductions and expanding forest-based sequestration.

As immediate specific government priorities it promotes: review and update of nuclear energy regulation to facilitate projects; finalising the national transport policy; sustainability guidelines mainstreamed into industrial park development; developing policies for district heating and co-generation; introducing landfill gas recovery to the national waste management policy; introduction of waste-to-energy facilities; enhance legislation and enforcement around general NDC implementations; introduce mandatory household waste segregation; policy emphasis on agricultural renewable energy and fertiliser/water use in the coconut industry.

On the sequestration end, the plan promotes an afforestation/restoration/reforestation rate of 25,000 ha per year up to 2030, also halting any losses to urban tree cover. These figures include plantation trees.
Document Title: Carbon Net Zero 2050 Roadmap and Strategic Plan

Family Name: Guidelines for Tariff Based Competitive Bidding Process for Procurement of Power from Grid Connected Wind Solar Hybrid Projects
Family Summary:
These Guidelines outline the bidding and contracting processes and requirements for wind solar hybrid projects. The objectives of the Guidelines are to promote competitive procurement of electricity from grid connected wind solar hybrid power projects, by distribution licensees, to protect consumer interests; to facilitate renewable capacity addition and fulfilment of Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) requirement of DISCOMs; to facilitate transparency and fairness in procurement processes; and to provide a risk-sharing framework between various stakeholders and ensure reasonable returns to the investors involved in the wind solar hybrid power procurement, thereby encouraging further investments, enhanced bankability of the Projects and profitability for the investors.

The successful bidder's shareholding in the project shall remain at a minimum of 51% and state nodal agencies appointed by state governments will provide the necessary support to facilitate the required approvals and sanctions in a timebound manner.

Collection Name: The Mother Earth Law and Integral Development to Live Well, Framework Law No 300
Collection Summary:
The Mother Earth Law is a piece of legislation that epitomises Bolivia's dedication to sustainable development, respecting the balance between human life and the natural environment, and prioritising the rights and knowledge of the country's majority indigenous population. The expressed objective of the law is to 'establish the vision and fundamentals of integral development in harmony and balance with Mother Earth to Live Well, guaranteeing the continued capacity of Mother Earth to regenerate natural systems, recuperating and strengthening local and ancestral practices, within the framework of rights, obligations and responsibilities'.
 
 In relation to climate change the law has many provisions that outline the state's vision, citizens' rights, and responsibilities. It embraces the concept of 'climate justice', defined by the ability of all Bolivian citizens to 'Live Well', especially those who are most vulnerable to climate change. It reinforces the point that some states have more of a global responsibility to respond to climate change.
 
 To encourage sustainable development of natural resources, it states that climate change trajectories should be accounted for when planning and zoning responsible land use.
 
 The law focuses on reducing the risks posed by climate change through six lines of actions:
The permanent incorporation of prevention of and managed response to natural disasters into the System of Integral Planning
Risk management for the agricultural sector to prevent diminished crop yields and food insecurity
The adoption of risk management of disasters as well as adaption to climate change across state development projects; development of informational networks to issue early warnings in times of natural crisis as well as to assist the agricultural industry and indigenous communities plan according to climate conditions
Strengthening territorial management processes of sub-national governments through the incorporation of risk management and adaption to climate change perspectives
Articulation between public and private scientific research sectors to share knowledge and co-ordinate research regarding vulnerabilities related to climate change
 
 The Law defines 'Living Well' in relation to climate change and lays out the state's legal obligations. The state will develop policies, strategies and legal techniques to mitigate the effects of climate change and adapt to them through strengthening institutional capacities for the monitoring of climate with the purpose of long-term planning. The state will also encourage the recuperation of traditional indigenous practices that were historically sustainable and allowed for the natural regeneration of resources.
 
 The law also establishes the Plurinational Authority of Mother Earth, within the Ministry of Environment and Water, as the state entity responsible for much of the development, overseeing and co-ordination of projects, programmes and research as it relates to climate change and the objectives of the Plurinational Plan for Climate Change. It also co-ordinates scientific monitoring of GHG emissions. The entity will operate within the framework of 'climate justice,' following the principles of Bolivia's climate change politics.
 
 The Authority will operate through three mechanisms: (1) Joint Mechanism of Mitigation and Adaptation for the Integral and Sustainable Management of Mother Earth's Forests; (2) Mitigation Mechanism to 'Living Well'; and (3) Adaptation Mechanism to 'Living Well'.
 
 The Authority is also responsible for the management of the Plurinational Fund of Mother Earth. The Fund will be financed with multilateral and bilateral aid, public money from the national government allocated to mitigation or adaptation, funds from private donors, national or international loans, and funds at the disposal of the executive branch.
Family Name: Bolivian Plurinational Policy on Climate Change (PPCC), promoting integrated development in harmony with Mother Earth
Family Summary:
The Plurinational Policy on Climate Change (PPCC), updated in 2023 by Bolivia's Plurinational Authority of Mother Earth, provides a comprehensive framework for managing the climate crisis. Rooted in Law 300 (Law of Mother Earth and Integral Development for Living Well), the policy integrates ancestral knowledge and innovative strategies to address the dual challenges of mitigation and adaptation, aiming to protect the rights of Mother Earth while fostering sustainable development under the paradigm of Living Well (Vivir Bien).
The Bolivian Plurinational Policy adopts an interdisciplinary approach with four strategic pillars: (1) an integrated focus on forest and Mother Earth management; (2) climate mitigation, emphasising the energy, industrial, and service sectors; (3) climate adaptation and resilience in vulnerable regions; and (4) cross-cutting actions ensuring transparency, gender equity, and intergenerational justice.
These efforts aim to be aligned with Bolivia's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement, which target emission reductions and the preservation of ecosystems, including reducing deforestation by 80% and achieving universal access to resilient water systems by 2030. Operationally, the PPCC leverages mechanisms like the Joint Mitigation and Adaptation Mechanism and sectoral contributions to enhance forest conservation, renewable energy transitions, and sustainable agriculture. It underscores non-market approaches to climate finance, rejecting commodification of environmental functions. Guided by principles of climate justice, the PPCC addresses structural drivers of the climate crisis, advocating for collective global responsibility and the repayment of historical climate debts by developed nations.
Document Title: Bolivian Plurinational Policy on Climate Change (PPCC), promoting integrated development in harmony with Mother Earth

Family Summary: This ministerial resolution, issued by Peru’s Ministry of Housing, Construction, and Sanitation (MVCS), mandates the development and implementation of Planes de Mitigación y Adaptación al Cambio Climático (PMACC) by sanitary companies (Empresas Prestadoras de Servicios de Saneamiento "EPS"). Aligned with Peru’s Contribución Nacionalmente Determinada (NDC) and the Paris Agreement, the policy seeks to enhance climate resilience and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in the sanitation sector. Under the framework of Peru’s Climate Change Framework Law (Ley N° 30754), the resolution emphasises mitigation through GHG emission reductions from wastewater management and energy consumption, and adaptation via improved water resource management to address climate risks. EPS must utilise the Sistema de Información de Gestión de Saneamiento (SIGASS) to assess climate exposures, prioritising systems with high user populations or vulnerability to climate hazards.

Family Name: Biomass Strategy
Family Summary: The Biomass Strategy 2023 sets out the UK Government’s approach to using sustainable biomass as part of the transition to net zero, recognising biomass as a limited resource that should be prioritised where it offers the greatest emissions-reduction potential and where alternatives are limited. The strategy places strong emphasis on strengthening sustainability criteria to ensure biomass delivers genuine greenhouse gas savings, while assessing future domestic and imported biomass availability. It identifies harder-to-decarbonise sectors and, in the longer term, Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) as priority uses, with BECCS expected to provide negative emissions that help balance residual emissions from sectors that are difficult to fully decarbonise. It also considers biomass’s role in renewable power, biomethane, heat, low-carbon transport fuels, industrial decarbonisation and low-carbon hydrogen, while highlighting the need to manage competing demands for sustainable biomass and protect wider environmental objectives.
Document Title: Biomass Strategy

Family Name: Regulation on measures to prevent Carbon leakage through national fuel emissions trading (BEHG Carbon Leakage Ordinance - BECV)
Family Summary:
This regulation serves to establish measures in accordance with Section 11 Paragraph 3 of the Fuel Emissions Trading Act (BEHG) to prevent carbon leakage and to maintain the cross-border competitiveness of companies affected by the provisions of the BEHG, which result in higher fuel prices. Companies receiving subisidies under this Regulation must have made investments from 2023 onwards in measures that improve energy efficiency and are specifically identified within the framework of the energy management system in accordance with Section 10 of the Regulation, and are considered to be economically feasible. Only companies falling within the sectors and sub-sectors listed in Appendix 1 and 2 of the Regulation are eligible to apply for aid. This includes sectors and sub-sectors such as: cement, lead, wood and pulp, and bright steel production; the processing of nuclear fuel; sugar production; the production of synthetic rubber; the production and initial processing of copper; iron foundries; and the extraction of petroleum. The Appendices also indicate the degree to which the sectors and sub-sectors will be compensated in relation to their emissions intensity.

The European Commission approved the Regulation on August 10th, 2023, and approved the German government’s proposal for the European Commission to implement additional transparency requirements for companies receiving individual subsidy grants of more than 100,000 euros by publishing the names, size, region and primary economic sector of these companies.
Document Title: Regulation BECV

Family Name: FRA BOD Decree 163/2023: Promulgating the Standards of Registering Verification and validation Bodies for Carbon Emission Reduction Projects With FRA.
Family Summary:
Within the context of Decree No. 4664/2022 that creates a voluntary market for trading carbon credits, Decree 163/2023 focuses on the registration process for Validation and Verification Bodies (VVBs) with the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) in Egypt.

Article 1 announces the creation of a registry within the FRA specifically for approving VVBs for carbon emission reduction projects. This registry serves as a centralised database containing detailed information on each approved VVB. Only VVBs listed in this registry are authorised to conduct verification and validation for carbon emission reduction projects intended for trading in Egypt.

Eligibility Criteria for Egyptian VVBs

1. Legal Entity: The applying entity must be a legally registered corporate entity in Egypt.

2. ISO Certifications: The entity must hold certifications demonstrating adherence to international standards for validating and verifying environmental information and greenhouse gas statements. The required certifications include ISO 14065:2020, ISO/IEC 17029:2019, and ISO 14064-3:2019.

3. Professional Competence: The VVB must demonstrate its professional capability to perform the required verification and validation tasks.

4. CEO Interview: The CEO or a designated representative must successfully complete an interview conducted by the FRA. This ensures that the leadership of the VVB understands the requirements and expectations of the FRA.

5. Clean Criminal Record: The management team and personnel involved in verification and validation must not have been convicted of felonies or misdemeanors related to crimes against honor or trust within the past three years, unless their rights have been fully restored. This provision aims to maintain the integrity and trustworthiness of the VVBs.

Eligibility Critieria for International VVBs

- The entity must be recognized by established international climate organizations, such as being a Designated Operational Entity (DOE) under the UNFCCC, recognized under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, or listed in international voluntary carbon registries like the Gold Standard, VCS, or GCC.

- The VVB must submit documentation showcasing its expertise and experience in verification and validation, including at least three projects registered in recognized international voluntary carbon registries.

- The VVB must include at least one Egyptian expert within its verification and validation team.

Additional Provisions

- Trading guidelines: International entities trading carbon emission reduction certificates within Egypt must notify the FRA of their accredited VVBs.

- Application Procedure: VVBs must submit applications using the FRA's designated form, along with documentation proving compliance with decree criteria. The FRA reviews complete submissions within 30 days.

-Registration Maintenance: VVBs must adhere to registration terms, comply with their commitments, and renew annually.

- Registration fees: For Egyptian VVBs (EGP 10,000 initial, EGP 2,000 renewal); international VVBs (USD 500 initial, USD 100 renewal).
Document Title: FRA BOD Decree 163/2023: Promulgating the Standards of Registering Verification and validation Bodies for Carbon Emission Reduction Projects With FRA.

Family Name: National Biodiversity Strategy 2030
Family Summary:
In line with the objectives of the European Biodiversity Strategy to 2030 and the Ecological Transition Plan, it outlines a vision for the future and development centered on the need to reverse the current trend of biodiversity loss and ecosystem collapse.On August 3, 2023, Ministerial Decree No. 252 was signed, adopting the new National Biodiversity Strategy to 2030 and establishing its governing bodies.There are 18 actions distributed across the eight areas of intervention, for instance:

  • Legally protect at least 30% of the land area and 30% of the marine area through an integrated system of protected areas, the Natura 2000 network, and other legally protected areas.
  • Ensure that at least one-third of legally protected terrestrial and marine areas, including all primary and old-growth forests, are strictly protected.
  • Ensure the ecological and functional connectivity of protected areas at the local, national, and supranational levels.
  • Ensure adequate funding for protection
  • Ensure that for at least 30% of the species and habitats protected under the Birds and Habitats Directives whose conservation status is currently unsatisfactory, it becomes satisfactory by 2030 or shows a clear positive trend.
  • Ensure that all ecosystems do not deteriorate and that large areas of degraded ecosystems are restored, particularly those most suitable for capturing and storing carbon as well as for preventing and reducing the impact of natural disasters.
  • Achieve land degradation neutrality and zero net land-use change, and make significant progress in the remediation and restoration of degraded and contaminated land.
Document Title: Ministerial Decree 252/2023

Family Name: National Biodiversity Strategy 2030
Family Summary:
In line with the objectives of the European Biodiversity Strategy to 2030 and the Ecological Transition Plan, it outlines a vision for the future and development centered on the need to reverse the current trend of biodiversity loss and ecosystem collapse.On August 3, 2023, Ministerial Decree No. 252 was signed, adopting the new National Biodiversity Strategy to 2030 and establishing its governing bodies.There are 18 actions distributed across the eight areas of intervention, for instance:

  • Legally protect at least 30% of the land area and 30% of the marine area through an integrated system of protected areas, the Natura 2000 network, and other legally protected areas.
  • Ensure that at least one-third of legally protected terrestrial and marine areas, including all primary and old-growth forests, are strictly protected.
  • Ensure the ecological and functional connectivity of protected areas at the local, national, and supranational levels.
  • Ensure adequate funding for protection
  • Ensure that for at least 30% of the species and habitats protected under the Birds and Habitats Directives whose conservation status is currently unsatisfactory, it becomes satisfactory by 2030 or shows a clear positive trend.
  • Ensure that all ecosystems do not deteriorate and that large areas of degraded ecosystems are restored, particularly those most suitable for capturing and storing carbon as well as for preventing and reducing the impact of natural disasters.
  • Achieve land degradation neutrality and zero net land-use change, and make significant progress in the remediation and restoration of degraded and contaminated land.
Document Title: National Biodiversity Strategy 2030 (STRATEGIA NAZIONALE BIODIVERSITÀ 2030)

Family Name: National Strategy for the Use of Carbon Markets (ENUMeC)
Family Summary:
The National Strategy for the Use of Carbon Markets (ENUMeC) in the Argentine Republic is a framework that facilitates the development of carbon markets with the objective of reducing emissions and promoting sustainable development. These markets allow companies and governments to buy and sell emission rights, thus incentivizing emissions reduction and environmental compensation. The ENUMeC deepens the national position regarding the use of carbon markets and creates a common framework for their implementation in the national territory. Among the axes of the strategy are:

- Strengthen national and subnational access to climate financing.

- Participate in carbon markets regulated in the Paris Agreement and other national and international compliance markets.

- Accompany the participation of the private sector in voluntary markets.

- Generate non-commercial approaches and support subnational governments in the implementation of market schemes to fulfill their climate change response plans.
Document Title: National Strategy for the Use of Carbon Markets (ENUMeC)

Family Name: Roadmap for the Advancement of Electromobility in Chile
Family Summary: The Roadmap for the Advancement of Electromobility in Chile was published on August 1, 2023. It outlines defined actions for 2024-2026 to expand the use of electromobility technology, aligning with Chile's carbon neutrality goal by 2050 and the National Electromobility Strategy, which aims for 100% zero-emission sales in various vehicle categories by 2035. Priority measures include promotion of charging infrastructure, education and training, road safety, public transportation and decentralization, and regulation (both regulatory and legal).
Document Title: Hoja de Ruta para el Avance de la Electromovilidad en Chile - Acciones Concretas al 2026 para Masificar el Uso de esta Tecnología

Family Name: National Framework for Promoting Energy Storage Systems
Family Summary: The National Framework for Promoting Energy Storage Systems aims to support renewable energy dispatch, grid stability, peak shifting, and decarbonization. It includes a Viability Gap Funding scheme for battery energy storage systems (up to 40% of capital costs) and sets targets for the increase in energy storage (1% in 2023-2024 to 4% by 2029-2030).
Document Title: National Framework for Promoting Energy Storage Systems

Family Name: Guidelines for PM eBus Sewa
Family Summary: The PM eBus Sewa scheme was launched in August 2023 to boost public transport in cities. With a budget of ₹20,000 crore for deploying 10,000 electric buses under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model, the scheme focuses on making urban travel cleaner and more efficient. Eligible cities include those with a population between 3 and 40 lakh, as well as State and UT capitals with fewer than 3 lakh residents as per Census 2011. As of August 2025, 7,293 electric buses have been approved across 14 States and 4 Union Territories.
Document Title: Guidelines for PM eBus Sewa

Family Name: Circular No. 06/2023/TT-BTNMT dated 31 July 2023 guiding the integration of contents regarding the response to climate change to strategies and planning ("Circular 06")
Family Summary: Circular 06 sets out the principles, requirements, and steps to integrate contents regarding the response to climate change to national, industrial, regional and professional strategies and planning, including proposal for activities to integrate the content of responding to climate change in the explanation of strategy building tasks; analysis of the impacts of climate change and requirements to respond to climate change; identification of solutions to respond to climate change to integrate into the strategy; integration of climate change response content into the strategy; and obtaining opinions on integrated climate change response content.
Document Title: Circular No. 06/2023/TT-BTNMT

Family Name: Circular No. 25/2020 / TT-BCT dated 29 September 2020 on the implementation of plans for economical and efficient use of energy
Family Summary: Circular 25 regulates planning and reporting on economical and efficient use of energy. Circular 25 requires: (i) the preparation of annual list of primary energy consumers, (ii) the preparation of annual and 5-year plans and reports on economical and efficient use of energy of primary energy consumers, (iii) the preparation of annual plans and reports on the energy use of agencies and entities with at least 100,000 kWh of annual energy consumption, and (iv) procedures for implementation and contents of energy audit report.
Document Title: Circular No. 25/2020 / TT-BCT

Family Name: Guidelines for Tariff Based Competitive Bidding Process for Procurement of Power from Grid Connected Solar PV Power Projects.
Family Summary:
These Guidelines outline the bidding and contracting processes for solar PV power projects. The reason for these Guidelines is that the procurement of electricity through competitive bidding by the distribution licensees is expected to reduce the overall cost of procurement of power and facilitate the development of power markets.

Other objectives for these to provide a transparent, fair, standardised procurement framework based on open competitive bidding with appropriate risk-sharing between various stakeholders to enable procurement of power at competitive prices in consumer interest, improve bankability of projects and ensure reasonable returns to the investors; and to provide for a framework for the inter-state/ intra-state, long-term, sale-purchase of power as a further measure to de-risk the sector.

The Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) is expected to be signed within 140 days from the release of the bid (i.e., the zero date), while the bid submission is to be made within 22 days of the zero date. The PPA between the RE Project and Procurer/Intermediate procurer shall clearly indicate the scheduled commencement-of-supply date (SCSD) and the quantum of supply.

Through Memorandum F. No. 283/48/2018 dated 14 September 2022, part-commissioning of ISTS connected solar projects in lots of 10MW was allowed from 14 September 2022 to 31 March 2023 to facilitate expeditious commissioning of solar PV power projects.
Document Title: Memorandum F. No. 283/48/2018 dated 14 September 2022

Family Name: Renewable Generation Obligation for Coal/Lignite-Based Thermal Generating Stations
Family Summary: The Renewable Generation Obligation as per the Revised Tariff Policy, 2016 is contained in a Ministry of Power Resolution F. No. 09/02/2022-RCM.–1.0 dated 27 February 2023. The Resolution states that any generating company establishing a coal/lignite-based thermal generating station and having the Commercial Operation Date (COD) of the project on or after 1 April 2023 shall be required to establish renewable energy generating capacity (in MW) i.e. Renewable Generation Obligation (RGO) of a minimum of forty percent (40%) of the capacity (in MW). Alternatively, it shall procure and supply renewable energy equivalent to such capacity.
Document Title: Ministry of Power Resolution F. No. 09/02/2022-RCM.–1.0 dated 27 February 2023 re Renewable Generation Obligation

Family Name: Guidelines for Tariff Based Competitive Bidding Process for Procurement Power from Grid Connected Wind Power Projects
Family Summary:
These Guidelines have the following objectives to facilitate renewable capacity addition and fulfilment of Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) requirement of distribution licensees; to provide a transparent, fair, standardized procurement framework based on open competitive bidding with appropriate risk-sharing between various stakeholders to enable procurement of power at competitive prices in consumer interest, improve bankability of projects and ensure reasonable returns to the investors; and to provide for a framework for the inter-state/ intra-state, long-term, sale-purchase of power as a further measure to derisk the sector. The Guidelines cover the bidding and contracting processes.

In Circular No. 117/44/2018-Wind-Part(1) dated 9 January 2023, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy outlined its decision regarding bidding for wind energy projects to ensure faster capacity addition in the wind sector. The Ministry decided that bids of a cumulative capacity of about 8 GW will be issued each year from 2023 to 2030. Each bid will include composite sub-bids for all 8 windy states, and the technical and financial bids will be placed in two separate envelopes. The financial bid will only be opened when the bidders qualify in the technical bid. Amendments were made to the Guidelines accordingly.
Document Title: Circular No. 117/44/2018-Wind-Part(1) dated 9 January 2023

Family Name: National Energy Master Plan (2021-2030)
Family Summary: The Master Plan on National Energy is a roadmap for the energy sector to reach Viet Nam’s development goals while meeting its net zero target by 2050. It sets an energy-related GHG emissions target of 399-449 MtCO2e by 2030, (51-73% above 2021 levels) and 101 MtCO2e by 2050 (62% below 2021 levels).
Document Title: Decision Approving the National Energy Master Plan
