Family Name: Inefficient Fossil Fuel Subsidies Government of Canada – Self-Review Assessment Framework
Family Summary:
These Guidelines, which were jointly developed by the Minister of the Environment and Climate Change and the Minister of Finance, are the government's tool to achieve two objectives that are related to the G20 commitment to phase out inefficient fossil fuel subsidies:

  1. avoid creating new Measures that would be considered Inefficient Fossil Fuel Subsidies as per the Inefficient Fossil Fuel Subsidies Government of Canada – Self-Review Assessment Framework ("Assessment Framework"); and
  2. help ensure all support for the fossil fuel sector that meet the definition of a fossil fuel subsidy, as per the Assessment Framework, are aligned with one of the six inefficiency criteria below.

There are two Parts to these Guidelines. Part A of the Guidelines refers to the creation of a Measure, and Part B refers to spending decisions within a Measure.
Document Title: Inefficient Fossil Fuel Subsidies Government of Canada – Self-Review Assessment Framework

Family Name: Small-Scale Renewable Electricity Generation Scheme (SRESS)
Family Summary:
This Scheme helps farmers, community groups, schools, and businesses lower electricity costs and generate income through solar and wind projects.

  • The self-consumer grant, under the Non-Domestic Microgen Grant (NDMG) scheme helps those who want to install solar panels to power their farm, business, or community buildings. Renewable Self-Consumers above 50kW and up to 1MW are eligible to apply and receive up to €162,600.
  • The SRESS export tariff is for projects which export all electricity produced to the grid to earn income. The SRESS export tariff provides a 15-year tariff to successful export applicants, without an auction. The support rate is provided for the support lifetime, with successful applicants receiving a premium on the market revenues they receive for their renewable electricity.
Document Title: Small-Scale Renewable Electricity Generation Scheme (SRESS)

Family Name: Green Hydrogen Roadmap for Ecuador
Family Summary: The Green Hydrogen Roadmap outlines Ecuador's strategic plan for producing and utilising green hydrogen as a cornerstone of its energy transition. With an electricity matrix largely based on renewable hydropower (approximately 60% of installed capacity and 78% of generation in 2021), Ecuador aims to leverage its renewable resources and existing infrastructure to develop a green hydrogen economy.The roadmap emphasises the need to establish a regulatory framework to attract national and international investments, reduce production costs through incentives, and foster technological and knowledge transfer through regional and global partnerships. Key sectors such as agriculture, energy, and industrial manufacturing are identified as beneficiaries of green hydrogen and its derivatives, such as methanol and synthetic fuels. Additionally, green hydrogen is seen as a tool for reducing dependence on fossil fuels, creating jobs, and enabling the export of value-added sustainable products.The roadmap is structured into three phases: (i) initial (2025), (ii) medium-term deployment (2030), and (iii) long-term consolidation (2050), with ambitious capacity goals for green hydrogen production. It sets forth actions in research and development, regulatory frameworks, infrastructure development, and international cooperation to ensure the roadmap’s successful implementation.
Document Title: Green Hydrogen Roadmap for Ecuador

Collection Name: Law 7/2021 on climate change and energy transition [Spain]
Collection Summary:
Enacted in 2021, this law establishes Spain's legal framework for achieving climate neutrality by 2050, aligning with the Paris Agreement and Sustainable Development Goals. It mandates a 23% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 (compared to 1990 levels), alongside ambitious renewable energy targets, including 42% of final energy consumption from renewables and 74% renewable electricity generation by 2030. Energy efficiency measures aim for a 39.5% reduction in primary energy consumption within the same timeframe. The law also prohibits new hydrocarbon and radioactive mineral exploitation, requires emission-free transport systems in cities with populations exceeding 50,000, and emphasises sustainable urban mobility.

The legislation includes a national Just Transition Strategy to ensure equitable economic opportunities, particularly for vulnerable regions, while fostering adaptation and resilience to climate risks across critical sectors such as water, biodiversity, and health. It creates governance mechanisms like the Expert Committee on Climate Change and Energy Transition to monitor progress and updates to Spain's Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC). Projecting investments exceeding €200 billion by 2030, the law is expected to enhance Spain’s GDP by €16.5–25.7 billion annually and generate 250,000–350,000 new jobs. The focus on education, innovation, and public awareness underscores its commitment to a holistic and inclusive transition.

This collection represent a body of policies, strategies, and plans enacted under this law.
Family Name: Spanish strategy for International Climate Finance
Family Summary: The Spanish Strategy for International Climate Finance outlines Spain’s commitment to supporting global climate action through a coordinated framework aligned with the Paris Agreement and the Sustainable Development Goals. Mandated by the Climate Change and Energy Transition Law (Law 7/2021), the strategy focuses on enhancing climate-resilient, low-carbon development by aligning funding with their national climate priorities. It excludes support for unabated fossil fuel projects except in limited, clearly defined cases consistent with the 1.5°C target. Principles guiding the strategy include coherence with EU taxonomy, gender equality, human rights, and fostering public-private collaboration.Key objectives include fulfilling Spain’s international commitments by scaling up climate finance to €1.35 billion by 2025, integrating climate goals into development cooperation, and leveraging investment to advance ecological transitions. The strategy prioritises renewable energy, green transitions, and sustainable development projects while enhancing accountability and alignment with recipient countries’ climate plans.
Document Title: Spanish strategy for International Climate Finance

Family Name: Resolution 95/2023 on Sustainable Land Management
Family Summary: This Resolution (pages 2283 to 2287 of the Gazette) establishes the provision for granting recognition to Sustainable Land Management, which is a working strategy contributing to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals, specifically those related to food security, sustainable water management, biodiversity and terrestrial ecosystems and combating climate change, including neutrality in land degradation. It contains provisions on the requirements for obtaining recognition of sustainable land management; the application process; the group of expert evaluators; the approval and granting process; and the control of recognition and revocation.
Document Title: Resolution 95/2023 on Sustainable Land Management

Family Name: Resolution 26/2023 on Sustainable Consumption and Production, the Circular Economy and Plastics
Family Summary:
This Resolution (at pages 2288 to 2293 of the Gazette) contains regulations for work in sustainable consumption and production, the circular economy, and the gradual reduction of disposable or single-use plastics. The purpose of these regulations is to implement an environmental policy and management tool that will lead all sectors of society to orient their consumption and production patterns toward sustainability, thereby achieving a transition to higher levels of environmental protection and quality of life.

Actions include strengthening climate resilience and tackling climate cahnge both in terms of adaptation and mitigation in food systems and the tourism sector.
Document Title: Resolution 26/2023 on Sustainable Consumption and Production, the Circular Economy and Plastics

Family Name: The Third National Adaptation Programme (NAP3) and the Fourth Strategy for Climate Adaptation Reporting
Family Summary: This Programme consolidates policies and actions to address the climate change risks and opportunities identified in the third Climate Change Risk Assessment (CCRA3), as section 58 of the Climate Change Act 2008 requires. This programme covers England and non-devolved functions across the UK. It emphasises climate action in key areas, such as: infrastructure; natural environment; health, communities and built environment; business and industry; international impacts; adaptation reporting power and supporting evidence. The programme is organised around the themes of "action", "information", and "coordination" to provide for a comprehensive approach to adapt to climate change by ensuring that government actions are more targeted, informed, and well-coordinated over the five-year NAP period.
Document Title: The Third National Adaptation Programme (NAP3) and the Fourth Strategy for Climate Adaptation Reporting

Family Name: National Hydrogen Strategy
Family Summary:
This Strategy sets out how hydrogen will be produced and used in Ireland, as well as what needs to be done to enable the development of Ireland’s hydrogen sector. The three primary reasons to develop the sector are to decarbonise Ireland's economy, enhance its energy security and create industrial and export market opportunities. Hydrogen is expected to play a significant role in enabling the transition to a net-zero economy for Ireland by 2050.

This Strategy outlines hydrogen production pathways; the end uses of renewable hydrogen, transportation, storage and infrastructure development plans; safety and regulation; and research, cooperation and scaling up.
Document Title: National Hydrogen Strategy

Family Name: Energy Transition Mechanism Country Platform (ETMCP)
Family Summary: This program is the Governent of Indonesia's primary coordination and driving force to encourage a fair and affordable energy transition. The ETMCP coordinates various energy transition activities, channels fiscal support where necessary, and supports just transition at the community, regional, and national levels. This program was launched through the Ministry of Finance. The government will invest USD 4.6 billion through the ETMCP to expedite the retirement of 2 GW of coal-fired power plants (CFPP) and replace them with renewable sources.
Document Title: Indonesia Energy Transition

Family Name: General Regulations of the Fuel Alcohol Law (Reglamento general de la Ley del Alcohol Carburante)
Family Summary:
This regulation establishes the operational framework for Guatemala's Fuel Alcohol Law (Decree-Law No. 17-85), specifically designed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the transport sector through mandatory blending of renewable alcohol fuels with gasoline. The regulation updates previous regulatory provisions to align with current technological advances and international climate commitments, particularly Guatemala's Nationally Determined Contributions under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change. It establishes comprehensive procedures for the production, storage, handling, use, transport, and commercialisation of fuel alcohol, while creating institutional mechanisms for monitoring greenhouse gas emission reductions and promoting sustainable mobility.

The framework prioritises advanced ethanol with lower carbon intensity, requiring distributors to blend a minimum of sixty percent advanced ethanol in the total alcohol fuel mixture, with flexibility for market disruption circumstances. It establishes technical standards for fuel quality, mandates emission reduction monitoring through internationally recognised methodologies, and creates certification requirements for greenhouse gas emission calculations. The regulation incorporates lifecycle emission assessments, prioritises low-emission fuels, and establishes registration requirements for producers, thereby institutionalising a systematic approach to decarbonising Guatemala's transport sector while aiming to ensure compliance with international environmental obligations and constitutional protections for environmental sustainability.
Document Title: Ministry of Energy and Mines - Government Agreement 159-2023 (Ministerio de Energía y Minas - Acuerdo Gubernativo 159-2023)

Family Name: School Sector Technical Climate Action Roadmap 2023 to 2030
Family Summary: This Roadmap gives an overview of the school sector requirements and roadmap to 2030 and 2050 climate targets.
Document Title: School Sector Technical Climate Action Roadmap 2023 to 2030

Family Name: The National Strategy regarding the prevention and combating of desertification and land degradation 2021-2030
Family Summary:
Given the negative consequences of desertification and land degradation, this strategy aims to prevent and mitigate these processes by applying integrated measures aimed at long-term resource management. These measures will contribute to achieving land degradation and desertification neutrality by meeting the objectives and targets set by the 2030 Agenda to which Romania has committed itself to implement at national level. 

It includes the target to by 2030, combat desertification, land restoration and degraded land and soils, including land affected by desertification, drought and floods; and strive to achieve a land degradation neutral world, but also other interlinked objectives. 

The implementation period of the National Strategy on Preventing and Combating Desertification and Land Degradation is 2021-2030.

Specific objectives that will underpin the achievement of the overall objective to be met through the Strategy are the following:

1. Centralisation and evaluation of the data obtained from studies on the phenomenon of desertification in Romania carried out to date.

2. Analysis of the progress made at national level in the field of combatingdesertification

3. Identification and assessment of the projected environmental effects of the Strategy based on two scenarios: in the absence of the Strategy and by meeting the recommendations.

4. Establishment of measures to prevent, reduce, compensate and monitor effects of desertification on the environment according to the three scenarios.

5. Provide technical assistance/advice to the Ministry of Environment, Water and Forests on desertification until the completion of the contracted works.

6. Informing the public about desertification by organising debates and public consultations on the National Strategy on Prevention and Control of Desertification.

7. Drawing up the environmental report in accordance with the legal requirements in force and its endorsement by the competent authorities.

8. Preparation of the appropriate assessment study in accordance with the legal requirements in force. in force and its endorsement by the competent authorities.

9. Elaboration of the National Strategy on Prevention and Combating Desertification and Land Degradation and its endorsement by the competent authorities.
Document Title: The National Strategy regarding the prevention and combating of desertification and land degradation 2021-2030

Family Name: GX Promotion Strategy (Strategy to Promote the Transition to a Decarbonized Growth-Oriented Economic Structure)
Family Summary: The GX Strategy is based on the aspects of resolving the energy security challenges that Japan faces and the pursuit of efforts to limit the average global temperature increase to 1.5°C following the Paris Agreement. The Strategy was release following the enactment of the GX Promotion Act and the GX Decarbonization Power Supply Act. The GX Promotion Strategy approved by the Cabinet in July 2023 classified the main government initiatives into the following two categories: (1) GX initiatives based on the basic premise of securing a stable energy supply and energy self-sufficiency including using renewable energy and nuclear power; and (2) the realisation and implementation of the "Growth-Oriented Carbon Pricing Concept", including bold upfront investment support through "GX Economic Transition Bonds" and other means, upfront GX investment incentives through carbon pricing, and the use of new financial instruments.
Document Title: GX Promotion Strategy (Strategy to Promote the Transition to a Decarbonized Growth-Oriented Economic Structure)

Family Name: Sustainable Aviation Fuel Funding Initiative
Family Summary:
This Initiative provides up to $30 million to support the development of a sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) industry with production from renewable feedstocks in Australia. The intended outcomes are as follows:

  1. Advance the technology readiness level (TRL) and commercial readiness index (CRI) of SAF technologies for at-scale deployment;
  2. Facilitate a pathway to the technical and commercial viability of producing SAF from Renewable Feedstocks in Australia; and
  3. Build industry capacity in the production of SAF from Renewable Feedstocks in Australia.

Funded activities may include commercial or pre-commercial scale engineering feasibility, front-end-engineering-design (FEED) studies or other project development activities; pilot-scale or pre-commercial demonstrations of novel technologies to produce SAF; demonstration of novel and scalable approaches to establishing the supply chain required in a future SAF industry.

Family Name: Climate Action Framework for the Commercial Semi-State Sector
Family Summary:
The Climate Action Framework for the Commercial Semi-State Sector seeks to help the sector play a leading role in Ireland's net zero transition.


The Framework consists of a series of five commitments:


  • Governance of climate action objectives;
  • Emissions measurement and reduction target;
  • Emissions valuation in investment appraisal;
  • Circular economy and green procurement; and
  • Climate-related disclosures.


Commercial semi-State companies that sign up to the Framework would be entering into its commitments.
Document Title: Climate Action Framework for the Commercial Semi-State Sector

Family Name: National EV Roadmap
Family Summary:
"This strategic policy document includes a target of 30% share of EV sales in total domestic vehicle sales by 2030.

The roadmap is made up of a three-phase development plan. Under Phase 1 of the programme, which will run from this year until 2022, the government will promote electric motorcycles and support the development of its infrastructure nationwide.

From 2023 to 2025, it will initiate Phase 2, where the EV industry will be developed to produce 225,000 cars and pick-up trucks, 360,000 motorcycles and 18,000 buses/trucks, including the production of batteries. As indicated by the report, this first milestone is designed to deliver cost advantages via economies of scale.

In Phase 3, which will run from 2026 to 2030, the country will adopt a “30/30 policy,” working towards a target of producing 725,000 EV cars and pick-ups plus 675,000 EV motorcycles by 2030, which would constitute 30% of all auto production. This will also include the domestic manufacture of batteries."
Document Title: National EV Roadmap

Family Name: Canada Growth Fund
Family Summary: The Canada Growth Fund, which commenced operations in summer 2023, is deploying a suite of investment tools, including carbon contracts for difference, that will de-risk and bolster private investments in low-carbon projects, technologies, businesses, and supply chains. The Growth Fund is a pillar of Canada’s clean economy jobs plan. It is equipped with $ 15 billion over five years, and aims to transform Canada's clean economy on the path to net-zero.
Document Title: Canada Growth Fund

Family Name: Generation Expansion Plan (2022-2040)
Family Summary: Long-term planning framework prepared by the Costa Rican Electricity Institute (ICE), intended to guide the expansion of national electricity generation capacity through 2040. The plan prioritises renewable energy sources.

Family Name: Thailand Taxonomy Phase 1
Family Summary:
In June 2023, Thailand's Taxonomy Board issued the first phase of its taxonomy for a sustainable economy, which it has developed to serve as a reference tool for economic activities that contribute with  climate and environmental objectives. The taxonomy is based on the latest cliamte science and is aligned with the objective of reaching net-zero emissions by 2050 and Paris agreement temperature targets. Phase 1 of the taxonomy focuses only on mitigating climate change and only covers scope 1 and 2 emissions (unless otherwise stated), and focuses primarily on activities related to energy and shipping.
The taxonomy employs a "traffic light" system of green, amber, and red activities.The taxonomy defines the activities as follows:

"Green activities are substantially contributing to the goal of climate change mitigation by operating at or close to the net-zero goal by 2050" and include two categories of activities:

"Near zero activities: activities already at or near net-zero emissions that may require some further decarbonisation but not a significant transition (e.g., solar or wind power generation or operation of electric fleet-based transportation services).
Pathway to zero activities: activities that are needed beyond 2050 and have a clear 1.5-degree decarbonisation pathway to 2050 (e.g., shipping).Amber activities are facilitating significant emissions reductions in the short term with a reliable decarbonization pathways and prescribed sunset dates. The activities have not yet reached net zero emission but can still be improved with viable technologies.

The amber category is generally relevant only for the existing infrastructure and activities that can be retrofitted and cannot be applied to new ones (which should directly adopt green technologies) to avoid locking-in unsustainable technologies in new projects.
Red activities (“stranded”) are the ones that are currently not compatible with net-zero trajectory and are not going to become compatible anytime soon. For the transition to net zero by 2050 to happen, they should be phased out completely (for example, electricity generation from coal)."

The second phase of the taxonomy is under consultation from October 2024 to January 2025 and is focused on the manufacturing, agriculture, real estate and construction, and waste management sectors.
Document Title: Thailand Taxonomy Part 1

Family Name: Spatial Development Strategy for Slovenia 2050 (RESPR50)
Family Summary: The Spatial Development Strategy of Slovenia 2050 sets out the country’s long-term strategic objectives and guidelines for the development of activities in the spatial context. The strategy supports the development paradigm of spatial cohesion, which ensures balanced, harmonious and sustainable development of all areas in the country by taking into account and utilizing their endogenous spatial potentials (resources). It highlights the importance of reducing exposure to climate risks (e.g. floods, droughts, heatwaves) through spatial measures such as relocating development away from high-risk areas, improving water retention, and addressing urban heat island effects.Later, Slovenia published the Implementation Plan for the Spatial Development Strategy. The plan sets out a series of activities derived from the strategy's long-term objectives and priority areas. Implementing the proposed activities will enhance the resilience of settlements to climate change, support the preservation of cultural heritage, and improve their overall attractiveness and quality of life. The plan supports the transition to a low-carbon energy system through the spatial integration of renewable energy production, energy infrastructure, and efficient settlement patterns, while also encouraging sustainable mobility and reduced energy demand. All in all it translates national climate-neutrality ambitions into concrete spatial planning actions, ensuring that land-use decisions contribute to decarbonisation, energy efficiency, and climate adaptation goals.
Document Title: Implementation Plan for the Slovenian Spatial Development Strategy for the Period 2025–2034

Family Name: Canada’s National Adaptation Strategy and Adaptation Action Plan
Family Summary:
The National Adaptation Strategy sets out a vision, goals and near-term targets across five interconnected systems:

  • Disaster resilience
  • Health and wellbeing
  • Nature and biodiversity
  • Infrastructure
  • Economy and workers


Targets under the strategy include:

  • By 2025, 60% of Canadians, including northerners and Indigenous Peoples, are aware of the disaster risks facing their household.
  • By 2025, 50% of Canadians have taken concrete actions to better prepare for and respond to climate change risks facing their household.
  • By 2027, 80% of coastal communities and 60% of businesses located in coastal regions are implementing adaptation actions to increase climate resilience and reduce the economic impacts of climate change.
  • By 2028, the federal government, provinces, and territories have worked collaboratively to prioritise at least 200 higher-risk flood areas for new flood hazard maps / regional level modelling, and have taken evidence-based risk mitigation actions in accordance with scientific guidance.
  • Communities, including northern and Indigenous communities, in zones of high risk, as identified by provinces and territories, develop wildfire community prevention and mitigation plans by 2030, with up to 15% implemented by 2028. 
  • By 2030, robust guidance, codes and standards covering the top climate change risks for key public infrastructure systems are available to be adopted by all infrastructure decision-makers.
  • By 2040, deaths due to extreme heatwaves have been eliminated.


The Adaptation Action Plan provides the framework to achieve the goals of the National Adaptation Strategy.
Document Title: Government of Canada Adaptation Action Plan

Family Name: Energy Strategy Synthesis for 2035
Family Summary: The Energy Strategy Synthesis for 2035 sets a long term framework for the development of the energy sector in Tunisia. It aims to strengthen energy security, reduce fossil fuel imports, combat energy poverty, and contribute to carbon neutrality by 2050. The strategy promotes investment in renewables, electrification of transport and alternative fuels such as green hydrogen. It aims for a renewable energy capacity of 8350MW by 2035.
Document Title: Energy Strategy Synthesis for 2035

Family Name: Carbon Capture Storage and Use (CCUS) Strategy
Family Summary:
In June 2023, the French government released a draft CCUS strategy for consultation with industry.


In its strategy, the government outlines carbon capture targets for France that include:

  • 4 to 8.5 million tons of CO2 captured a year by 2030 
  • 15 to 20 million tons of CO2 captured a year by 2050 
  • an extra 10 million tons of CO2 captured a year in non-industrial sectors around 2050.


The strategy is built on the principle that CCUS should not be used to maintain a “business as usual” approach but to be used to manage residual emissions in the absence of other solutions for decarbonisation or as a transition solution.


Actions in the draft strategy include:

  • carrying out an assessment of the potential of storage by the end of 2023 or beginning of 2024 
  • launching a call for tenders for seismic surveys and test injections of CO2 in pilot sites, with initial tests starting in 2024-2025
  • launching a support scheme via contracts for difference (CCFD) to support industry decarbonisation projects, in particular in the service of carbon capture and sequestration.
Document Title: Draft Carbon Capture, Storage and Use (CCUS) Strategy

Family Name: National Mobility and Road Safety Strategy 2023-2042 (Estrategia Nacional de Movilidad y Seguridad Vial 2023-2042)
Family Summary: The National Strategy for Mobility and Road Safety 2023–2042 (ENAMOV) provides Mexico’s long-term policy framework to guarantee the constitutional right to mobility through safe, inclusive, sustainable, and equitable transport systems. Centred on social and spatial justice, the strategy prioritises vulnerable groups and aims to reduce inequality in access to mobility by integrating national, regional, and local planning. It promotes a systemic approach based on human rights and sustainability, aligned with existing legal instruments such as the General Laws on Climate Change, Environmental Protection, and Health, as well as international frameworks including the UN Decade of Action for Road Safety.Climate and environmental concerns are embedded within ENAMOV’s guiding principles, particularly through the promotion of decarbonised transport systems and the transition to clean energy. The strategy addresses the negative externalities of a car-centric model such as pollution, road injuries, and urban inequality; while advocating for public participation, energy sufficiency, innovation, and coordinated governance. Its implementation depends on intersectoral collaboration and the alignment of public and private actors to achieve national development goals that are equitable, efficient, and environmentally sustainable.
Document Title: National Mobility and Road Safety Strategy 2023-2042 (Estrategia Nacional de Movilidad y Seguridad Vial 2023-2042)

Family Name: National Policy for Sustainable Urban Mobility of Ecuador (PNMUS) 2023–2030
Family Summary: The National Policy for Sustainable Urban Mobility (PNMUS) 2023–2030 provides a strategic framework to address the environmental, economic, and social challenges of current mobility systems in Ecuador. Guided by the Constitution, the Organic Law on Land Transport, Traffic, and Road Safety, and international commitments such as the Paris Agreement and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, the policy aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve accessibility, and promote sustainable urban planning.On climate change, the plan incorporates three climate-focused approaches to enhance urban resilience and reduce environmental impacts: (1) promoting sustainable and efficient mobility modes, such as public transport and active transportation, to reduce private vehicle reliance; (2) developing resilient infrastructure to adapt to climate change, including climate-proof urban spaces and facilities; and (3) mitigating the effects of urban heat waves through nature-based solutions, such as green streets, shaded spaces, and microclimates. These approaches align with the policy's broader goals of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and fostering climate-resilient cities.The PNMUS serves as a comprehensive guide for local governments, supporting the implementation of Sustainable Urban Mobility Plans (PMUS) and providing technical and financial resources for cities to transition toward low-carbon and inclusive mobility systems.
Document Title: Guidelines to mainstream climate change in the National Policy for Sustainable Mobility

Family Name: Guidelines for Transition to a Circular Economy by 2035
Family Summary: The guidelines aim to provide provide a strategic framework to guide climate-neutral production, consumption and development in the economy along circular principles. It identifies gaps and inefficiencies in sustainability implementation across a range of sectors, and gives a range of capacity-building measures and funding directions, such as innovation in building materials, green public procurement, increased recycling capacity, and campaigns to affect consumer behaviour.
Document Title: Guidelines for Transition to a Circular Economy by 2035

Family Name: Environmental Land Management (ELM) update (2023)
Family Summary: The Environmental Land Management (ELM) update sets out the UK Government’s approach to reforming agricultural support in England by phasing out subsidies based primarily on land ownership and replacing them with payments for environmental, climate and sustainable farming outcomes. It establishes three complementary schemes: the Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) for universal, straightforward sustainable farming practices; Countryside Stewardship (CS), including CS Plus, for more targeted habitat, landscape and environmental actions; and Landscape Recovery for bespoke, long-term, large-scale projects. The schemes are intended to support food production while delivering benefits including improved soil and water quality, biodiversity recovery, flood and drought resilience, woodland creation, carbon reduction and carbon storage. The update also outlines the expansion and refinement of SFI and CS, including new standards, more flexible agreements, quarterly payments and improved access for tenants, alongside competitive funding for Landscape Recovery projects. Overall, the document represents a key policy framework for England’s agricultural transition, with government aiming to increase participation in environmental land-management schemes while redirecting the farming budget towards environmental outcomes alongside food production.
Document Title: Environmental Land Management (ELM) update (2023)

Family Name: Vehicle purchase tax exemption for NEVs
Family Summary: China exempted qualifying new energy vehicles from the vehicle purchase tax of around 10% of the vehicle price to support market uptake. The incentive has been extended several times. In 2023, the government extended the exemption for vehicles purchased in 2024–2025 and introduced a 50% tax reduction for purchases in 2026–2027, with tax relief capped at RMB 30,000 per vehicle in 2024–2025 and RMB 15,000 in 2026–2027.
Document Title: Vehicle purchase tax exemption for NEVs

Family Name: National expectations regarding regional and municipal planning 2023–2027
Family Summary:
This document summarises the Government’s most important priorities in the planning area for the coming four-year period. Its purpose is to establish a common basis for the county authorities, municipalities and central government authorities in order to ensure that planning processes are efficient and targeted and unnecessary objections are avoided. The expectations document is a guideline and does not convey all national goals, tasks and interests that planning must address. The document must therefore be viewed in conjunction with relevant laws, regulations, reports to the Storting (Norway’s parliament) and circulars, and cannot be used as an independent basis for objections.

It contains a section titled "Climate, nature and environment for the future". Important issues in regional and municipal plans will include consideration of nature diversity, the transition to a climate-resilient, low-emission society, long-term land use assessments to minimise the loss of natural areas and integrated management of water resources.
Document Title: National expectations regarding regional and municipal planning 2023–2027

Family Name: Ministerial Decision no. 1384/190515 of 2023. Determination of the Institutional framework for the implementation of the interventions of Article 31 of Regulation (EU) 2021/2115 and the intervention called  "eco-schemes" of the Strategic Plan of the Common Agriculture Policy of Greece 2023 -2027
Family Summary:
This Ministerial Decision defines the institutional framework for the implementation, management and monitoring of the ecological programmes for climate, environment and animal welfare, in compliance with the provisions of article 31 of the European Regulation (EU) 2021/2115 of the European Parliament and of the Council. 

The objectives of these ecological programs include: reducing greenhouse gas emissions, promoting the use of renewable energy, improving sustainable development and resource management, reversing biodiversity loss, strengthening ecosystem services, and protecting habitats.

Key aspects of the Decision include: 

- Establishing governing bodies and competent authorities. 

- Designating beneficiaries of the ecological programs, including farmers eligible for incentives.

 - Implementing a program to improve crop cover practices and enhance biodiversity. 

- Outlining farmers' rights and obligations. 

- Regulating the use of fertilisers and plant protection products.

 - Creating a program to implement a circular economy and enhance agricultural extension services.
Document Title: Ministerial Decision no. 1384/190515 of 2023

Family Name: Ministerial Agreement No. MAATE-2021-047: Technical Standard for the Ecuador Carbon Zero Program with Organisational Scope
Family Summary: This Ministerial Agreement establishes the guidelines and technical criteria for implementing the Ecuador Carbon Zero Program (PECC) at an organisational level, aligning with Ecuador’s constitutional provisions on environmental sustainability, the living well (buen-vivir or sumak kawsay) and the rights of nature. It enables organisations (public, private, national, or international) to voluntarily measure, reduce, and neutralise their greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from operational activities. The program applies a tiered certification system to encourage participants to advance from carbon footprint quantification (Level 1) to emission reduction (Level 2) and ultimately achieve carbon neutrality (Level 3).Proponents must develop an inventory of their organisational GHG emissions, covering direct (Scope 1), indirect (Scope 2), and selected value-chain emissions (Scope 3) for neutrality certification. The program follows international standards, such as the ISO 14064 series and the GHG Protocol, ensuring consistent methodologies for emission accounting and verification. Participants are required to set reduction targets, implement mitigation projects (e.g. renewable energy adoption, energy efficiency, and waste management) and engage in ongoing monitoring and reporting. Remaining emissions can be offset through nationally regulated compensation schemes.
Document Title: Ministerial Agreement No. MAATE-2021-047: Technical Standard for the Ecuador Carbon Zero Program with Organisational Scope

Family Name: Ministerial Agreement No. MAATE-2023-053. Technical standard for Ecuador's Greenhouse Gas Emissions Compensation Scheme
Family Summary: Rooted on constitutional provisions on sustainability, living well philosophy (Buen Vivir - Sumak Kawsay), this agreement establishes the regulatory framework for Ecuador’s National Greenhouse Gas Emissions Compensation Scheme, designed to facilitate voluntary initiatives that reduce or remove GHG emissions through mitigation projects. It applies to public, private, community, or mixed-sector initiatives developed within Ecuador, allowing national and international stakeholders to offset their carbon footprints by supporting certified projects. The scheme supports the broader goals of Ecuador's climate commitments, including the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement.The compensation scheme includes mechanisms for creating and trading Carbon Equivalent Units (Unidades de Carbono Equivalente - UCEs), representing verified emission reductions or removals equivalent to one ton of CO₂. Proponents must first reduce their emissions before compensating for any residuals via approved initiatives, such as forest conservation, renewable energy projects, or sustainable agricultural practices. The scheme ensures environmental and social safeguards, equitable benefit distribution, and alignment with national climate strategies, such as the REDD+ Action Plan and the National Climate Change Strategy.The Ministry of Environment, Water, and Ecological Transition (MAATE) oversees implementation through its Climate Change and Natural Heritage Subsecretariats, supported by accredited certification and verification bodies. It maintains a comprehensive registry for monitoring and tracking initiatives, UCEs, and compliance with program requirements. The system encourages transparency, additionality, and real, measurable outcomes that align with sustainable development goals while fostering multistakeholder collaboration across public and private sectors, Indigenous communities, and civil society.
Document Title: Ministerial Agreement No. MAATE-2023-053. Technical standard for Ecuador's Greenhouse Gas Emissions Compensation Scheme

Family Name: National plan for risk reduction in Ecuador
Family Summary:
With a projection to 2030, the National Plan for Risk Reduction in Ecuador results from close collaboration between various National Decentralized Risk Management System actors and marks a significant milestone in the search for a safer and more resilient territory for all Ecuadorians. It is based on international principles and guidelines like the Sendai Framework. It is aligned with the objectives and commitments of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the Ecuadorian National Development Plan.  

The document is based on local and sectoral needs to advance risk reduction through six strategic objectives that can guide the country's efforts to increase knowledge about risk management, governance, control and regularization of land use, promote safe infrastructure, encourage education, communication and citizen participation and, finally, strengthen preparation for response.

Family Summary: Sri Lanka's National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) for 2023-2030 emphasises the broad disaster risk posed by climate change through water scarcity and agro-ecological collapse, sea level rise, salinity intrusion and mosquito-borne disease risk from degraded land. Family Name: National Waste Management Plan 2028
Family Summary:
The National Waste Management Plan 2028 (Krajowy Plan Gospodarki Odpadami 2028) was adopted by the Resolution 96/2023 of the Council of Ministers.

It sets Poland’s strategic framework for waste policy through 2028 with a perspective to 2035, aligning domestic planning with EU waste-management and circular-economy goals.

The National Waste Management Plan 2028 aims to increase recycling and reuse, reduce landfilling, and promote biowaste treatment, which together help lower greenhouse gas emissions from waste and support climate mitigation, while building modern waste infrastructure and fostering a circular economy in Poland.
Document Title: National Waste Management Plan 2028

Family Name: Uzbekistan 2030 Strategy
Family Summary: The Uzbekistan 2030 Strategy aims to guide national development in the long term, with a wide range of priority directions and quantified aims across sectors. It aims to reduce the carbon intensity of the economy (emissions per unit GDP) by 30% compared to 2010, increase renewables to 40% of generation, enhance energy efficiency, adapt public transport to green fuels, and establish an MRV system covering all greenhouse gases to support emissions trading. On the environment the strategy commits to the creation of 600,000 ha of green space, the reclamation of over 6000 ha of degraded mining land, and achieve essentially total spatial coverage of early warning systems for weather and flooding. It promotes research into climate-resilient high yielding crop varieties, and improved water management systems to adapt to increasing water scarcity.
Document Title: Uzbekistan 2030 Strategy

Family Name: Presidential Decree No. 06-2023 - Creation Of The National Policy To Prevent Deforestation And Forest Degradation
Family Summary: This decree establishes the National Policy aimed at preventing deforestation and forest degradation in the country. It outlines strategies and actions to protect forests, promote sustainable land management, and restore affected ecosystems. The policy focuses on addressing the main causes of deforestation and forest degradation, while involving various stakeholders, including local communities, governmental institutions, and the private sector, to ensure the preservation and sustainable use of forest resources.
Document Title: Presidential Decree No. 06-2023 - National Policy To Prevent Deforestation And Forest Degradation

Family Name: Heatwave Management Plan
Family Summary: The objectives of this plan are to systematically prepare in advance of the summer period, anticipate the expected arrival of a heatwave, and define actions to be implemented at the national and local levels to prevent and limit its impacts. It considers the specificities of overseas territories which, due to their geographical and climatic situations, the impact of climate change, the rise in temperatures, and the lack of infrastructure and maintenance thereof, are confronted with significant heatwaves over long periods.This plan is not intended to replace the plan managed by the Ministry of Health regarding health risks, but to complement it. An interministerial feedback was conducted following the two heatwaves of 2019, as well as the drought episode of 2022. It was found that although the healthcare system was generally not strained during these episodes due to the activation of the national heatwave plan, these heatwaves impacted the entire population and had major consequences in many areas: closure of schools and daycare centers, postponement of school exams, cancellation of sports and cultural events, disruptions in public transport causing significant inconvenience to users, animal mortality, drying up of watercourses, difficulties in water supply, crop fires, among others. It was thus decided to extend the national heatwave management plan to take into account all impacts of these events.
Document Title: Heatwave Management Plan

Family Name: Memorandum No.5/1/2023-T&R (Mission on energy technologies)
Family Summary:
This Memorandum from the Ministry of Power and the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy sets up a Mission on Advanced and High-Impact Research (MAHIR) on the latest and emerging technologies in the energy sector. Th Mission will be for an initial period of five years, from 2023-2024 to 2027-28. The Mission is meant to support and provide funding for ideas to turn into products in the energy sector. Support will be in the form of identifying emerging technologies, supporting pilot projects for indigenous technologies, industrialising technologies, and leveraging foreign alliances and partnerships.

These are the eight areas identified for research: (1) alternatives to lithium-ion storage batteries; (2) modifying electric cookers/pans to suit Indian cooking methods; (3) green hydrogen for mobility (high efficiency fuel cell); (4) carbon capture); (5) geo-thermal energy; (6) solid state refrigeration; (7) nano technology for EV battery; and (8) indigenous CRGO technology.
Document Title: Memorandum No.5/1/2023-T&R (Mission on energy technologies)

Family Name: Interministerial Agreement No. MEF-SNP-MAATE-01. Ecuador Framework for Sovereign Green Bonds
Family Summary:
The Interministerial Agreement No. MEF-SNP-MAATE-01 establishes Ecuador's framework for sovereign green bonds, aimed at financing eligible green projects or refinancing public debt under favorable conditions. The framework aligns with the country’s environmental, financial, and development policies, emphasising sustainability and climate resilience.
The green bonds will support projects that contribute to environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, and ecological restoration, consistent with Ecuador’s constitutional mandate, the living well principle (Sumak Kawsay - Buen Vivir) and the Organic Environmental Code. The framework ensures compliance with national regulations on public debt issuance and green project criteria, with a validity of three years and provisions for updates by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Ecological Transition (MAATE), and the National Secretariat of Planning (SNP).
Key components include (i) use of resources for eligible green projects, (ii) transparent project evaluation and selection processes, (iii) efficient resource management, and (iv) monitoring and reporting mechanisms to track impact and accountability. Collaborative technical working groups will develop operational guidelines and ensure alignment with Ecuador’s planning and environmental strategies.
By leveraging green bonds, Ecuador seeks to attract investments, enhance sustainability efforts, and foster economic growth while addressing climate change and ecological challenges.
Document Title: Interministerial Agreement No. MEF-SNP-MAATE-01. Ecuador Framework for Sovereign Green Bonds

Family Name: Decree No. 11.546/2023 establishing the National Council for the 30th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
Family Summary: This Decree establishes a National Council to inform Brazil's plans to host COP30, the 30th meeting of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change. It sets requirements for membership of the Council.
Document Title: Decree No.11.546 text

Family Name: Decree No. 11.547/2023 on the Low Carbon Industry Technical Committee
Family Summary: This decree established the Law Carbon Industry Technical Committee, an independent body established to provide advice on the transition of the country's industrial sector. The decree establishes the mandate and composition of the committee. It also revoked Decree No. 10,275 of March 13, 2020.
Document Title: DECREE No. 11.547 text

Family Name: Decree no. 11.548/2023 establishing the National Comittee for REDD+
Family Summary:
This decree establishes the National Committee for the Reduction of Greenhouse Gas Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation, Conservation of Forest Carbon Stocks, Sustainable Management of Forests and Increase of Forest Carbon Stocks - REDD+.


This body is set up to provide guidance to state and federal governments and issue resolutions regarding the implementation of REDD+ in Brazil, in line with UNFCCC requirements. One of the Committee's responsibilities includes "the formulation, regulation and structuring of financial and market mechanisms to promote and encourage REDD+, pursuant to the provisions of art. 5th, art. 6th, art. 8 and art. 9 of Law No. 12,187, of December 29, 2009".


The decree sets out the mandate and composition of the Committee. The decree also revokes Decree No. 10.144, of November 28, 2019.
Document Title: Decree Nº 11.548 text

Family Name: Decree no. 11.550/2023 establishing the Interministerial Committee on Climate Change
Family Summary:
This decree institutes the Interministerial Committee on Climate Change as an institutional instrument of the federal Executive Branch to articulate government actions resulting from the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change - UNFCCC, enacted by Decree No. 2652, of July 1, 1998, including the objective of neutrality climate change and any future subsidiary instruments.The decree sets out the responsibilities of the Committee, including providing guidance on the country’s climate change actions and proposing new sectoral programmes to be incorporated into the National Policy on Climate Change (PNMC). It also sets out the requirements for the membership and operation of the Committee. It also creates individual mandates for Ministries ranging from the Ministry of Finance to the Ministry of Environment with regard to climate action.The decree also revokes Decree No. 10,845, of October 25, 2021 and Decree No. 10,846, of October 25, 2021. The first of these Instituted an Interministerial Committee on Climate Change and Green Growth and the second Instituted a National Programme for Green Growth. It also revokes Decree No. 11.075, of May 19, 2022, which created a previous National System for the Reduction of Greenhouse Gas Emissions (SINARE) and established the procedure for the elaboration of Sectorial Plans for Mitigation of Climate Changes. This Decree was updated by Decree 12.040/2024, which altered the provisions of some of its articles.

Resolution 6 of June 27, 2024 from the Inter Ministerial Committee on Climate Change (CIM) approves the Internal Regulations of the Inter Ministerial Committee on Climate Change (CIM). It defines the CIM’s Plenary composition and the purpose and components of the Subcommittee for COP 30, the Social Participation Chamber, the Interfederative Articulation Chamber and the Scientific Advisory Chamber, as well as providing for Technical Groups.
Document Title: Resolution 6, of June 27, 2024

Family Name: Low Carbon Development Strategy 2023-2030
Family Summary: This strategy examines and compares four business-as-usual scenarios and four mitigation scenarios, concluding that the most expensive scenario for the Republic of Serbia would be to ignore the costs related to climate change. Based on these results, the strategy seeks to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 13% by 2030 and 55% TO 69% by 2050 excluding land use, land use change, and forestry. It further aims to encourage the transition of the Republic of Serbia to a low-carbon and climate-resilient society.
Document Title: Low Carbon Development Strategy 2023-2030 with Projections until 2050

Family Name: Sector Action Plan on Environment and Climate Change
Family Summary:
The Action Plan outlines a strategic framework for integrating environmental sustainability and climate resilience into Bangladesh’s sectoral policies and programs. The Plan addresses pressing challenges such as deforestation, biodiversity loss, pollution, and climate change impacts, while advancing sustainable development goals across the Agriculture, Fisheries and Livestock sectors by managing land, water, environment and ecosystem to achieve food and nutrition security. The Plan seeks to strengthen climate adaptation and mitigation efforts, build institutional capacity, and foster collaboration among stakeholders to address environmental and climate-related issues. It incorporates green technologies, sustainable resource management practices, and community-based approaches to enhance resilience and sustainability. The specific goals that the Action Plan seek to achieve include:

  • Promoting and enhancing local level climate change adaptation and resilience.
  • Development and expansion of Climate Smart Agriculture.
  • Promoting sustainable land and water management to achieve land degradation neutrality.
  • Environmental pollution control and conservation of ecosystem and biodiversity.
  • Promoting green growth and low carbon development.
  • Establishment of sustainable financing mechanism and strengthening institutions for environment and climate change risk management.
Document Title: Sector Action Plan on Environment and Climate Change

Family Name: Third Comprehensive Plan for Improvement of Carbon Sinks (2023-2027)
Family Summary: The 3rd Comprehensive Plan for Promoting Carbon Absorption Sources is set with the vision of 'contributing to the realisation of carbon neutrality and green growth through forests' and aims to 'contribute to 21% (30 million tons) of the national greenhouse gas reduction by 2027'. To realise this, 6 major promotion strategies and 20 key tasks have been discovered and presented.
Document Title: Third Comprehensive Plan for Improvement of Carbon Sinks

Family Name: Green Growth and Climate Resilience Strategy 2023
Family Summary: Rwanda's Green Growth and Climate Resilience Strategy from 2023 aims to support sustainable socioeconomic development, climate adaptation/resilience, and mitigation progress towards a goal for carbon neutrality by 2050. The strategy supports renewable energy development (including hydro, wind, solar), climate-smart dense urbanism, electrified and public transport. It also emphasises the need to enhance irrigation efficiency in the agricultural sector, improving climate resilience and rural income. For landscape-level resilience, the strategy promotes agroforestry and forest restoration.
Document Title: Green Growth and Climate Resilience Strategy 2023

Family Name: National Strategy for International Climate Financing
Family Summary:
The strategy seeks to provide a clear framework to accelerate, expand and enhance the quality of international climate financing in line with the country's sustainable development objectives and the goals of the Paris Agreement. The Strategy proposes a roadmap articulated around four strategic axes and an action plan with short, medium and long-term measures to respond to the aforementioned challenges presented by climate change.

Of the four strategic axes, the first focuses on the development of actions and tools to facilitate an adequate flow of information and data for the analysis of climate financing, to support investment decision-making in climate change mitigation and adaptation initiatives.

The second strategic axis seeks to identify the available financing sources and generate the conditions necessary to access them.

The third strategic axis focuses on the design and implementation of financial and economic instruments that facilitate and make viable the flow of capital necessary to advance with various transitions towards a low emissions and climate resilient economy.

The fourth strategic axis responds to the needs to strengthen technical and human management of relevant actors to guarantee an efficient allocation of resources between the sectors, and the structuring, execution and monitoring of international climate financing.
Document Title: National Strategy for International Climate Financing

Family Name: Advanced Technologies for Carbon-Neutral (ALCA-Next) Program
Family Summary: This program provides funding for promising research ideas in priority areas for carbon neutrality, with a budget of 1.6 billion yen for FY2024. The program was launched in 2023 under the Japan Science and Technology Agency (JST) as one of the JST Strategic Basic Research Programs. The program focuses on exploring challenging key technologies that have not been actively researched by industries but have the potential to become innovative technology game-changers. Initially, the program will adopt multiple projects with relatively smaller budgets for a "small start" phase lasting 3.5 years. After this period, approximately one-third of the projects will be selected through stage-gate evaluations to receive increased funding, ensuring a continuous funding stream for projects that pass the evaluation.
Document Title: Advanced Technologies for Carbon-Neutral (ALCA-Next) Program

Family Name: Blue Carbon Strategy
Family Summary: The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries established a 'Blue Carbon Promotion Strategy' with the aim of achieving the 2030 NDC and 2050 carbon-neutral goals. The blue carbon promotion strategy includes three strategies: 1) strengthening the ocean's carbon absorption capacity and climate disaster response ability; 2) expanding participation in blue carbon creation such as private, regional, and international cooperation; and 3) new blue carbon certification and laying a foundation for long-term promotion.
Document Title: Blue Carbon Strategy

Family Name: Ordinance on the Establishment of the Climate Council
Family Summary: This ordinance establishes the Climate Council as an independent state scientific advisory body for climate policy. With four members proposed by public universities; three members proposed by the Slovenian Academy of Sciences and Arts and two members proposed by non-governmental organisation, the Council shall provide scientific advice in the form of expert opinions and recommendations to the Government in the field of climate change, particularly relative to monitor and implementation of the Long-Term Climate Strategy of the Republic of Slovenia, the NECP and other strategic documents governing climate change mitigation and adaptation, and to propose climate change mitigation and adaptation measures and their implementation in line with the latest scientific knowledge.
Document Title: Ordinance on the Establishment of the Climate Council

Family Name: Green Affordable Housing Program (IGAHP)
Family Summary: This program provides housing for low-income communities, applying the Green Building principle to achieve climate change targets by reducing carbon emissions. The program aims to build 100,000 green affordable housing units by 2024, build and retrofit one million units by 2030 (with a potential emissions reduction of 19-36 MtCO2), and achieve 100% net-zero housing by 2050 (PUPR, 2023). The program was launched by the Ministry of Public Works and Housing (PUPR: Kementerian Pekerjaan Umum dan Perumahan Rakyat). The IGAHP program is expected to save at least 20% water, save at least 20% energy, and reduce greenhouse gas effects by 29%.
Document Title: Indonesia Green Affordable Housing Program (IGAHP)

Family Name: National Electric System Development Program (PRODESEN) 2024-2038 [Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional (PRODESEN) 2024-2038]
Family Summary: The National Electric System Development Programme (PRODESEN) 2024-2038 constitutes Mexico's principal policy instrument for electricity sector planning, delineating a fifteen-year strategy for the National Electric System (SEN) that explicitly integrates climate change mitigation objectives into national energy infrastructure development. The programme establishes a framework for achieving an ordered energy transition whilst maintaining universal electricity access, incorporating increased generation capacity from clean and renewable energy sources, and developing the necessary transmission and distribution infrastructure to integrate these technologies. Climate considerations are embedded within the planning criteria, which mandate compliance with international environmental agreements, including the Paris Agreement and the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, under conditions of technical and economic viability that ensure affordable electricity supply without compromising public finances or state-owned enterprises.The programme addresses climate change through multiple strategic dimensions, including the promotion of electric mobility as articulated in the National Electric Mobility Strategy (ENME), which positions electrified transport as a sustainable alternative for reducing greenhouse gas emissions in the transport sector. Planning methodologies explicitly account for climate-related factors affecting electricity demand, including extreme weather events, seasonal variations, and changing precipitation patterns associated with phenomena such as El Niño and La Niña. Furthermore, PRODESEN aligns with Mexico's Special Climate Change Programme 2021-2024, incorporating specific actions to reduce emissions through public transport electrification, railway infrastructure development for passenger transport, and the promotion of low-carbon freight and public transport projects.
Document Title: PRODESEN 2024-2038

Family Name: Onshore Wind Energy Strategy
Family Summary:
The strategy aims to accelerate deployment of onshore wind energy in Germany and includes measures at the federal, state, and local levels including:

  • simplifying and accelerating consenting processes for projects,
  • improving the profitability of plants at locations with less potential,
  • increasing tender volumes and expansion paths, and
  • making it clear that renewables are in the overriding public interest and serve public safety.
Document Title: Onshore Wind Energy Strategy

Family Name: Decree 86/2023 on combating climate change
Family Summary:
This Decree's (pages 2179 to 2193 of the Gazette) objectives are as follows:

a) To strengthen the institutional framework for combating climate change, establish the responsibilities of the bodies and agencies of the Central State Administration, the business sector, the provincial governors of the People's Power and the municipal administration councils; of the State, the business sector, the provincial governors of the People's Power, and the municipal administration councils;

b) promote climate change adaptation and mitigation actions linked to food security, renewable energy use, energy efficiency, and integrated forest management, land use planning and urban planning instruments, cultural heritage, fisheries, agriculture, health, tourism, construction, transportation, and industry;

c) prioritise attention to climate change adaptation measures and disaster risk reduction management, with an emphasis on protecting people in vulnerable populations; land use planning and those resulting from the implementation of sectoral and coastal zone management policies;

d) strengthen mitigation actions, in accordance with the country's economic and social development priorities;

e) prioritise investments for the implementation of national measures and actions to address climate change in terms of mitigation and adaptation; and

f) promote scientific and technological training and innovation in line with climate change mitigation and adaptation actions.

This Decree contains provisions on the institutional framework for addressing climate change; the planning and orgaisation of government bodies; surveillance, early warning and assessment; the climate change information system; and the financing of actions to combat climate change and economic instruments.
Document Title: Decree 86/2023 on combating climate change

Family Name: Fifth Tourism Master Plan 2023-2027
Family Summary:
This Plan aims to strengthen Maldives’ position as a competitive and sustainable destination, enabling the industry,which has been the driving force in transforming the economy over the last 50 years, to continue leading the country’s growth. One of the goals is to build climate resilience and protect natural assets, which will be implemented through the following strategies:

  1. Improve planning guidelines and concept-approval processes to ensure sustainability is adequately addressed;
  2. Improve the management of common beach resources;
  3. Scale up and improve the quality of management systems to increase the resilience and health of coral reefs;
  4. Develop guidelines to ensure wildlife interactions are sustainable and in line with Maldives’ image and brand;
  5. Improve planning guidelines, knowledge sharing, and access to finance to adapt to climate change and build climate resilience into tourism infrastructure;
  6. Eliminate the use of single-use plastic products in tourist establishments in line with national targets;
  7. Reduce waste and develop and operationalise waste collection and processing infrastructure; and
  8. Develop a framework to renew and rejuvenate coconut palms and native vegetation.
Document Title: Fifth Tourism Master Plan 2023-2027

Family Name: National Strategy for Sustainable Finance
Family Summary: The National Strategy for Sustainable Finance (ENFS) is an initiative of the Ministry of Economy of Argentina that seeks to develop sustainable finance in the country. The ENFS defines axes and guidelines for the identification and addressing of risks and opportunities linked to climate change, contributing to the strengthening, development and stability of the Argentine financial system. The ENFS seeks to promote alternatives to mobilize in a scalable way the necessary resources to encourage public and private investments that contribute to achieving economic and social objectives within the framework of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Document Title: National Strategy for Sustainable Finance

Family Name: Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines
Family Summary: To meet the larger vision of achieving Zero Carbon Emission Goal, Ministry of Ports, Shipping Waterways has launched ‘Harit Sagar’ the Green Port Guidelines. They aim to reduce carbon emissions per ton of cargo by 30% by 2030, and by 70% by 2047.
Document Title: Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines

Family Name: Boursa Kuwait Capital Market Rules and Guidelines
Family Summary:
On May 22, 2023, the Capital Markets Authority (CMA), also known as "Boursa Kuwait” introduced new guidelines to help companies write their non-mandatory sustainability reports. 

These guidelines offer a starting point for companies to report on sustainability in ways that support Kuwait's goals for sustainable development as outlined in its Vision 2035 and its aim to have no net carbon emissions by 2060. The guidelines are based on international recommendations and are meant for all companies listed on Boursa Kuwait, but following them is not compulsory.

The guidelines suggest companies report on environmental issues like greenhouse gas emissions, energy and water use, and how they manage climate risks.
Document Title: Guidelines

Family Name: Resolution 418/2023 (housing energy efficiency labelling)
Family Summary: Resolution 418/2023 approves the procedure and national registry for the National Housing Labeling Program (PRONEV), a housing energy efficiency labelling system meant to quantify the energy equirements of houses throughout the country and to improve energy performance and reduce energy consumption in homes. PRONEV was established via Resolution 5/2023.
Document Title: Resolution 418/2023 (housing energy efficiency labelling)

Family Name: Decree specifying the conditions for the application of the ban on regular public air transport services for domestic passengers whose journey is also provided by rail in less than two and a half hours (No. 2023-385 of 22 May 2023)
Family Summary: This Decree prohibits air traffic on domestic air connections as long as the mode of rail transport provides a satisfactory alternative service. The decree specifies the extent to which a rail link can be considered as offering such an alternative and thus contributing to the fight against serious environmental problems. This Decree is meant to combat climate change and strengthen resilience to its effects.
Document Title: Decree specifying the conditions for the application of the ban on regular public air transport services for domestic passengers whose journey is also provided by rail in less than two and a half hours (No. 2023-385 of 22 May 2023)

Family Name: Agreement on Hydrogen Infrastructure (2023)
Family Summary:
The Agreement on Hydrogen Infrastructure (2023) considers the development of hydrogen infrastructure. Power-to-X fuels (PtX fuels) can replace fossil products in a number of highly adaptable sectors, including shipping, aviation, agriculture, parts of industry and parts of heavy road transport, and a Danish PtX sector can play a central role in both Denmark's and Europe's green transition. PtX is also a potentially important piece in the development of new green business and export opportunities for Denmark, where there is interest, particularly from Germany, in purchasing Danish hydrogen supported by hydrogen infrastructure.

Piped hydrogen infrastructure is the cheapest form of transport for larger quantities of hydrogen over longer distances. In addition, hydrogen infrastructure can support the development of a PtX sector in Denmark by supporting the possibility of storage and a stable purchase of hydrogen through hydrogen pipes. Hydrogen infrastructure also has an energy policy value and can support a future electricity system with an increasing share of renewable but fluctuating electricity production.
Document Title: Economic framework conditions for hydrogen infrastructure - 2nd partial agreement on pipeline hydrogen infrastructure (4 April 2024)

Collection Summary:
This collection is made up by documents that relate to Colombia's fair energy transition. 
The Fair Energy Transition is a key process in the fight against climate change, involving the transformation of current energy systems to one based on a low-GHG emitter, having fairer and more sustainable model. 
Colombia's green and fair energy transition strategy seeks to pursue descarbonisation in a way that takes into account paramount elements such as (i) equity and social, environmental and energy justice; (ii) graduality and sovereignty while pursuing the progressive replacement of the current matrix with a cleaner and more efficient one; (iii) social participation; and, (iv) knowledgeable to create economic alternatives.
Family Name: National Development Plan 2022-2026
Family Summary: The National Development Plan (NDP) 2022-2026 named "Colombia World Power for Life" is the document that serves as the basis and provides the strategic guidelines for public policies. It outlines its plan to advance a just energy transition, including working to accelerate the roll out of renewable energy and zero- and low-emission vehicles. More specifically, the 4th axis “Productive transformation, internationalisation and climate action” emphasises the fight against climate change and biodiversity loss, it states that Colombia’s dependency on fossil fuels undermines competitiveness and increases vulnerability, and draws attention to the climate finance gap.It was enacted by the Law 2294/2023.
Document Title: National Development Plan 2022-2026

Family Name: National Power Development Plan for 2021-2030, vision to 2050
Family Summary:
This Plan, approved by Decision No. No. 768/QĐ-TTg, sets out the following objectives: that by 2030, 50% of government buildings and 50% of residential homes will use self-generated and slef-consumed rooftop solar power; and to significantly expand renewable energy resources (excluding hydropower) for electricity generation, reaching a share of approximately 28-36% by 2030 and to 74-75% by 2050.

In addition, the Plan also aims to, by 2030, establish two inter-regional renewable energy industry and service hubs encompassing electricity generation, transmission, and consumption; renewable energy equipment manufacturing; construction; installation; and related services; and build a renewable energy industrial ecosystem in high-potential regions such as the North, South Central, and South regions when favorable conditions are met. The intention is to supply exports to Singapore, Malaysia and other regional partners.Actions include developing offshore wind power alongside solar power, onshore wind, nearshore wind, in order to produce new energy, such as hydrogen and green ammonia. This new Plan supersedes the previous version in Decision No. 500/QD-TTg on approving the National Electricity Development Plan for 2021-2030, vision to 2050.
Document Title: Implementation Plan for National Power Development Plan for 2021-2030, vision to 2050
