Family Name: Circular F. No. 13/02/2023-RCM re Determination of Green Tariff
Family Summary: This Circular from the Ministry of Power titled 'Determination of Green Tariff under Electricity (Promoting Renewable Energy Through Green Energy Open Access) Rules, 2022 and Implementation of the Rules' stipulates that the green tarffic should not be higher than the average power purchase cost of renewable energy and a surcharge of 20%. The Circular was issued following the phenomena of a few States setting green tariffs at a rate much higher than the average power pruchase cost of renewable energy procured by distribution companies. This Circular also conveyed to State Electricity Regulatory Commissions to set green tariffs and implement the Green Open Access Rules, and align Open Access Regulations in accordance with the rules.
Document Title: Circular F. No. 13/02/2023-RCM re Determination of Green Tariff

Family Name: Accelerating Coal Transition (ACT): Indonesia Country Investment Plan
Family Summary: This investment plan identifies potential areas for investment and support in order to retire and repurpose of coal-fired power plants (CFPPs) and mines. This plan provides a strategy for financing and promoting clean energy alternatives. The investment will allow Indonesia to accelerate the retirement of its coal power plants by 5-10 years. This plan also outlines a plan to provide social and economic benefits for employees of retired coal plants.
Document Title: CIF Accelerating Coal Transition (ACT): Indonesia Country Investment Plan (IP) Revision

Family Name: National Electric System Development Program 2023-2037 (Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional 2023-2037)
Family Summary: The National Electric System Development Program (PRODESEN) 2023-2037 serves as Mexico’s primary public policy instrument for the fifteen-year planning of the National Electric System (SEN), aligning with the National Development Plan (PND) 2019–2024 and reflecting the current government’s energy policy objectives. It integrates key elements from related planning tools, including the Indicative Programme for the Installation and Retirement of Power Plants (PIIRCE), and the expansion and modernisation programmes for the National Transmission Network (RNT) and General Distribution Networks (RGD). The PRODESEN aims to ensure universal access to electricity for over 125 million people, supporting social and economic development while addressing regional disparities. It prioritises the state-owned Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) in generation, transmission, and distribution, with plans to develop new power plants and modernise existing hydroelectric facilities, thereby reinforcing -according to the text- energy sovereignty and system reliability.The PRODESEN underscores Mexico’s commitment to international environmental agreements, including the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the Paris Agreement, and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, particularly focusing on reducing greenhouse gas emissions and promoting sustainable energy practices. It outlines a structured increase in clean and renewable energy generation, targeting a minimum of 35% of electricity from clean sources by 2024, as mandated by the Energy Transition Law (LTE) and the General Climate Change Law (LGCC). The programme includes planning for the integration of clean energy technologies, such as distributed generation, and emphasises energy efficiency and environmental protection, aiming a sustainable and orderly energy transition while maintaining system stability and affordability.
Document Title: National Electric System Development Program 2023-2036 (Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional 2023-2036)

Family Name: Photovoltaic Strategy
Family Summary:
By 2030, the quota of renewable electricity in total gross consumption shall reach 80% and the installed solar capacity shall reach 215 GW. To this end, the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action approved the Photovoltaic Strategy.

The Strategy sets out eleven fields of action. Broadly, these comprise:


  1. Expand ground-mounted systems more strongly;
  2. Facilitate rooftop photovoltaics;
  3. Simplify tenant electricity and communcal building supply;
  4. Facilitate the use of balcony PV;
  5. Accelerate grid connections;
  6. Strengthen acceptance;
  7. Ensure effective links between energy law and tax law;
  8. Secure supply chains and stimulate competitive, European production;
  9. Secure skilled workforce;
  10. Promote technology development; and
  11. Advance the rapid expansion of PV with European policy instruments.
Document Title: Photovoltaic Strategy

Family Name: Water Efficiency Strategy Document and Action Plan in the Framework of Adaptation to the Changing Climate (2023–2033)
Family Summary:
This document serves as a guide for stakeholders in achieving the objectives of protecting and utilising water resources in an equitable and efficient manner. Water efficiency targets, strategies and actions have been defined through the following main axes:I. Urban Water Use EfficiencyII. Agricultural Water Use EfficiencyIII. Industrial Water Use EfficiencyIV. Water Use Efficiency Affecting All Sectors

The efficient use of water resources is meant to also facilitate adaptation to a changing climate.
Document Title: Water Efficiency Strategy Document and Action Plan in the Framework of Adaptation to the Changing Climate (2023–2033)

Family Name: Zimbabwe National Forestry Policy 2023
Family Summary: The Zimbabwe National Forest Policy 2023 creates the framework for sustainable forest management to maintain biodiversity, productivity, regeneration capacity, and vitality. The policy aims “to enhance the contribution of the forestry sector to development and social equity through active participation of all stakeholders for the benefit of present and future generations.” Regarding climate change, the policy has an objective to “enhance forest carbon sinks and build communities’ resilience to climate change through sustainable forest management.” It proposes policy actions such as promoting land-use plans that recognise forestry at all governance levels, capacity building for sustainable forest management in the context of climate change, maintaining and accounting for carbon sinks with community participation, implementing a carbon credit framework as a guide in forest-based projects and promote gender-sensitive forest-based climate solutions.
Document Title: Zimbabwe National Forestry Policy 2023

Family Name: The Swedish Environmental Protection Agency's Action Plan for Climate Adaptation 2023–2026
Family Summary:
One of the main focuses of the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency's climate adaptation work is to spread knowledge and strengthen incentives for work with nature-based solutions.

Action objectives:

• The Swedish Environmental Protection Agency is based on nature's ability to contribute to reducing negative effects of a changing climate through nature-based solutions through measures that simultaneously strengthen biodiversity and promote human well-being.

• The Swedish Environmental Protection Agency's climate adaptation work shall contribute to the implementation of the Swedish Climate Act - to reduce emissions of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases by preserving, managing and creating new functions in the environment.

• Climate adaptation is an integral part of the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency's acquisition and property management of state property, in the protection and management of protected areas and in the coordination and development of outdoor life issues.

• The Swedish Environmental Protection Agency shall, through environmental monitoring and environmental analysis, work to ensure that changes in species and ecosystems as a result of a changing climate can be detected and explained.

• Climate adaptation is integrated into the application of the Environmental Code through planning, assessment and supervision.
Document Title: The Swedish Environmental Protection Agency's Action Plan for Climate Adaptation 2023–2026

Family Name: Circular Guide for the Implementation of Water Use Restriction Measures during Droughts
Family Summary: This Guide is meant for departments responsible for prescribing water use restrictions in mainland France and its overseas territories. It outlines the hydrological drought management system in order to optimise the organisation of crisis management and water shortage situations. Beyond annual drought management, the provisions of this guide are intended to be coordinated with the implementation of structural actions to reduce crisis episodes (by aiming for a maximum of two years out of ten requiring water use restriction orders), anticipate the effects of climate change, and avoid any risk of drinking water supply disruptions. It contains sections on restriction measures; adaptation of restriction measures to a user's request; publicity of orders for temporary restriction of water use; monitoring of water use restriction measures; measures taken at the national level to support action in the territories; the hydrological anticipation and monitoring committee; and the maintenance and deployment of national monitoring networks.
Document Title: Guide to implementing measures to restrict water use during drought periods (June 2022)

Family Name: Multimodal Electric Mobility Master Plan for Urban Public Transport and Logistics
Family Summary:
In 2023, the Multimodal Electric Mobility Master Plan for Urban Public Transport and Logistics in Paraguay was developed. This is a public policy tool complementary to the National Electromobility Strategy and will establish general and specific guidelines for a transition to the electrification of public transport and logistics in Paraguay. This comes as a commitment to supporting international efforts to reduce GHG emissions on the planet by replacing hydrocarbons with a clean energy source. At the same time, this transformation will allow Paraguay to take advantage of its 100% renewable generation matrix, reducing its dependence on petroleum derivatives.

The master plan has a vision to put Paraguay as a regional benchmark in promoting and driving electric mobility, with a sustainable, circular and comprehensive model, with 100% electric vehicles in public transport systems and 50% electric vehicles in logistics transport by 2040.
Document Title: Plan Maestro de Movilidad Eléctrica para El Transporte Público Urbano y Logístico de Paraguay (Multimodal Electric Mobility Master Plan for Urban Public Transport and Logistics)

Family Name: Decree 7189: Feed-in tariff subsidies to incentivise renewable energy
Family Summary:
Decree 7189 introduces a new feed-in tariff subsidy to incentivise renewable energy projects including onshore and offshore wind, solar PV and renewable plants that incorporate battery storage.

The feed-in tariff will provide a subsidy of around $0.05 to $0.08 USD per kWh depending on the type renewable energy generation.

The feed-in tariff will be higher for solar and wind projects that are built alongside battery storage capacity.

The subsidy will be awarded to projects built between 2021 and 2030 and will be provided to projects for a period of ten years with a bonus for locally sourced content.
Document Title: Decree 7189 on feed-in tariffs

Family Name: Long-term Strategy on Greenhouse Gas Emissions Reductions
Family Summary:
This Strategy sets out sector-specific and technology pathways to reaching Ireland's 2050 climate targets.


A key objective of the Strategy is to clarify sectoral adjustments required to reach net zero by 2050 and support policy stability and investment in the medium- and long-term.


The Strategy contains measures categorised according to the degree of certainty around their use and suitability to realise 2030 and 2050 targets.


Core measures include technologies and measures that already exist today and could deliver substantial emissions reduction. Those focus on delivering a renewable electricity system; GHG-efficient agricultural practices; electrification in transport, built environment, and industry; restoration of forestry and peatlands; fuel substitution; and a circular economy.


Further measures are those technologies and measures that are technologically more challenging or not yet available at scale but required to deliver the climate targets. Such measures are aimed at accelerating a sustainable transformation in agriculture and deploy zero-emission gas.


Alternative-further measures are those technologies which currently exist at research or pilot stage or have not reached commercial scale, such as radical demand reduction (e.g. aviation) and deploy carbon capture and storage in the industry sector.
Document Title: Long-term Strategy on Greenhouse Gas Emissions Reductions

Family Name: Adverse Weather and Health Plan (2024-2025 and 2025-2026)
Family Summary:
The first edition of the Adverse Weather and Health Plan (AWHP) aims to protect individuals and communities from the health effects of adverse weather and to build community resilience in England. The Plan is focused on achieving the following four goals: Prevent the increase in years of life lost due to adverse weather events, prevent mortality due to adverse weather events, prevent morbidity due to adverse weather events and reduce the use of healthcare services due to adverse weather events.

The Second Edition of the AWHP has been developed based on feedback, recommendations from reports, and reflections from the experience of implementing the first edition of the plan. The plan is centered around the same four goals, and includes nine action areas for delivery, namely 1) service delivery 2) capacity building 3) organisational arrangements 4) communication 5) risk management 6) early warning systems 7) data analysis 8) quality assurance 9) policy development and accountability. The second edition is also expanded to include a review of the AHWP guidance and further clarificaion of the role of the AWHP in improving long-term resilience.
Document Title: Adverse Weather and Health Plan 2025-2026

Family Name: Decree No. 57, establishing the Interministerial Committee for the Just Socio-ecological Transition
Family Summary: Driven by the constitutional mandate and grounded in structural administrative regulations, this Committee was established to provide a coordinated response to the climate and ecological crisis. The Committee's vision recognises that the current moment demands a fundamental shift in the relationship with the environment, particularly in degraded areas. To address this, the regulator considers a Just Socio-Ecological Transition crucial, involving governance that actively incorporates local territories.The primary function of the Committee is to advise the President on implementing a Just Socio-Ecological Transition, which encompasses social transformation, environmental protection, and sustainable economic development. The Transition prioritises decent work, gender and intergenerational equity, resilience, and ecological restoration. The Committee will facilitate coordination among various governmental bodies, propose policies and legislative changes, and gather relevant information. Additionally, it will create spaces for information sharing and skills development within the government.Chaired by the Minister of Environment, the Committee will meet regularly and may form subcommittees, inviting public authorities and private stakeholders if needed. The ultimate goal is to advance a new development model in Chile that balances economic activities with environmental protection, while striving to provide a better quality of life for its citizens.
Document Title: Decree No. 57, establishing the Interministerial Committee for the Just Socio-ecological Transition

Family Name: Coastal Zone Management Programme 2023-2032
Family Summary: The Coastal Zone Management Programme 2023-2032 aims primarily to preserve and restore coastal landforms and ecology, alongside reducing the impacts of climate change on Lithuania's coastline. The key climate measure in the plan is a significant restoration of dune systems, which alongside ecological aims is intended to reduce the risk to increased future storm surges to inland settlements and infrastructure.
Document Title: Coastal Zone Management Programme 2023-2032

Family Name: Energy Strategy of Ukraine until 2050
Family Summary:
Ukrainian Government Approved the Energy Strategy until 2050 Without Public Acces on April 21st, 2023.

On 21 April 2023, the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine adopted the Energy Strategy of Ukraine until 2050. The strategy was prepared by the Ministry of Energy with support from the UK Government and assistance from consultants at KPMG Ukraine. According to official sources, the drafting process also involved major energy-sector stakeholders, including NAEC Energoatom, NPC Ukrenergo, NJSC Naftogaz of Ukraine, the Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine (GTSOU), PJSC Ukrhydroenergo, and other industry participants.

Official statements indicate that the strategy is aligned with the objectives of the European Green Deal and is intended to provide a comprehensive framework for the development and implementation of Ukraine’s energy policy. However, a detailed assessment of the proposed measures is not possible, as the strategy has been designated “for official use only” and has not been publicly released.
Document Title: ORDER 373-r/2023 on the approval of the Energy Strategy of Ukraine for the period until 2050

Family Name: National Lithium Strategy
Family Summary: This strategy aims to guide the development of Chile's lithium industry, and plans to do so by creating public-private partnerships coordinated by a new National Lithium Company.
Document Title: National Lithium Strategy

Family Name: Directive on Mandatory Reporting on Greenhouse Gases
Family Summary: The Directive on Mandatory Reporting on Greenhouse Gases aims to enhance national monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) of greenhouse gas emissions and removals, forming a robust carbon accounting framework to guide future efforts such as nationally determined contributions. This directive begins the process of creating a national carbon inventory, and sets out the basic responsibilities of the Brunei Climate Change Secretariat to do so.
Document Title: Directive on Mandatory Reporting on Greenhouse Gases

Family Name: National Electric Vehicle Strategy
Family Summary: Australia’s National Electric Vehicle Strategy outlines the country’s objectives to increase the availability of affordable electric vehicles, establish the supporting systems and infrastructure to enable a rapid uptake of electric vehicles by Australians, as well as to encourage demand for electric vehicles. The Strategy also commits Australia to introducing a Fuel Efficiency Standard.
Document Title: National Electric Vehicle Strategy

Family Name: Environmental Defense Policy
Family Summary: Paraguay’s Environmental Defense Policy provides a strategic framework to strengthen the country’s capacity to respond to environmental threats and the impacts of climate change, with a clear focus on prevention, risk reduction, and inter-institutional coordination. The policy establishes seven strategic axes aiming to reduce vulnerabilities, improve institutional readiness, and foster rapid and coordinated responses to environmental risks, including those exacerbated by climate change.
Document Title: Política de Defensa Ambinetal (Environmental Defense Policy)

Family Name: Regulation 198/2023 on the Procedures for Granting Direct Payments to Farmers
Family Summary: This Regulation implements the CAP direct payment rules under EU Regulation 2021/2115. sets out how European Union direct payments are granted to farmers in Latvia, including various support types under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) such as basic income support, redistributive and young farmer payments, coupled support and, importantly, voluntary eco-schemes designed to reward environmentally- and climate-beneficial agricultural practices.
Document Title: Regulation 198/2023 on the Procedures for Granting Direct Payments to Farmers

Family Name: National plan for preventive actions on the health effects of excessive temperatures
Family Summary: During the summer months of 2003, exceptionally high temperatures were recorded across Europe, leading to a significant increase in morbidity and, as was later confirmed, mortality from causes in which excess temperature acted as a triggering factor. In order to prevent a recurrence of episodes such as those experienced that summer, the Ministry of Health launched the National Plan for Preventive Actions on the Health Effects of Excessive Temperatures in 2004. Since then, the Plan has been activated every summer from June to September.The implementation of the Plan has fulfilled its primary objective: preventing health impacts caused by excessive temperatures. From a public health perspective, exposure to extreme heat particularly affects children, older persons, and individuals with underlying chronic conditions. From a social perspective, factors such as marginalization, social isolation, dependency, disability, and inadequate housing conditions among lower-income populations add further risk, increasing the vulnerability of groups that, due to their socio-economic circumstances, should in fact receive greater support.The Plan sets out measures to reduce the effects associated with excessive temperatures and to coordinate the State Administration institutions involved. It also proposes actions that may be undertaken by Autonomous Communities and local authorities. The Plan defines prevention and control actions structured across several levels of intervention, according to the level of risk reached as a result of rising temperatures.
Document Title: National plan for preventive actions on the health effects of excessive temperatures (2024)

Family Name: National Strategy and First National Basic Plan for Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth
Family Summary: The Framework, established pursuant to Article 10 of the Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth to Cope with Climate Crisis (“Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality”), is a national plan for responding to the climate crisis and sustainable development. It implements Korea's 2030 NDC. It includes annual reduction goals and implementation measures for each sector (e.g., industry and transportation). The Framework will be updated every five years over the next 20 years between 2023 and 2042. In addition, this Framewrok will facilitate the establishment of subordinate plans (e.g., measures to adapt to the national climate crisis, basic plans for carbon neutrality and green growth for local cities, provinces, counties, and districts) and will impact on other mid-to long-term administrative plans on electric power, land use, and resource circulation.
Document Title: National Strategy and First National Basic Plan for Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth

Family Name: The Green Building Code of Pakistan (GBCP)
Family Summary: The Green Building Code of Pakistan (GBCP) provides detailed standards to promote green construction and renovation of buildings nationally. Key principles it implements include: passive solar design; green roofs; energy-efficient lighting; renewable energy supply; water-saving technologies; sustainable materials; and the use of building information modelling.
Document Title: The Green Building Code of Pakistan (GBCP)

Family Name: Climate Change Adaptation Plan of the Finnish Defence Administration
Family Summary:
This Defence Administration Climate Change Adaptation Plan complements the National Climate Change Adaptation Plan and, with regard to the Defence Administration, responds to national and international commitments. The plan includes objectives for the Defence Administration's climate change adaptation and identifies needs for action. The target year for the measures presented is 2030.

The objectives for the defence administration's adaptation to climate change are: Climate-resilient and energy-wise defence.

• The defence administration is aware of the impacts of climate change and the energy transition on the performance, training, training and planning of national defence.

• The defence administration understands the security impacts of climate change nationally and internationally and recognises and can anticipate its own role in relation to them.

• The defence administration has the ability to manage known climate risks and actively identify and assess new risks.

• The defence administration knows how to take advantage of the positive effects of climate change.

A coarse-level model was developed to assess exposure to climate change phenomena, vulnerability and the significance of risks. The assessment identified that other climate phenomena have a broad and multidimensional impact on operations. The most prominent ones were the effects of increased precipitation, changes in winter conditions, strong fluctuations in weather conditions, changes in the Baltic Sea and indirect health impacts.

In addition, the need for several one-off or ongoing measures was identified, which are categorised into the following means:

  1. Taking climate change and its associated phenomena into account in operations and their planning
  2. Adapting the operating environment to a changing climate.
  3. Adapting to the energy transition and preparing for energy shortages.
  4. Managing health risks.
  5. The Defense Forces, the Ministry of Defense, the Secretariat of the Security Committee or Defense Properties are responsible for the more detailed planning and implementation of the measures.
Document Title: Climate Change Adaptation Plan of the Finnish Defence Administration

Family Name: Comprehensive Roadmap for the Electric Vehicle Industry (CREVI)
Family Summary: CREVI is a comprehensive roadmap aligning with various policies and programs to tackle EV industry challenges. It focuses on developing charging stations, manufacturing, R&D, and human resource development. With short-, medium-, and long-term targets, it aims to overcome barriers, unify public and private efforts, and achieve a 50% EV fleet by 2040 in a Clean Energy Scenario.
Document Title: Comprehensive Roadmap for the Electric Vehicle Industry

Family Name: National Development Plan (NDP) 2023-2028
Family Summary: Eswatini's National Development Plan (NDP) for 2023-2028 serves as a five-year roadmap for sustainable growth in the economy and society, guiding policy interventions across sectors. The plan promotes climate adaptation measures in agriculture and institutional capacity, mainstreaming consideration of climate risks in development planning and building accessible early warning systems for extreme weather. To mitigate emissions it promotes green expansion of the energy supply using solar and hydroelectric generation.
Document Title: National Development Plan (NDP) 2023-2028

Family Name: Security Strategy for the Kingdom of the Netherlands (De Veiligheidsstrategie voor het Koninkrijk der Nederlanden)
Family Summary:
Outside of national safety concerning the geopolitical balance of power and instability, as well as in today’s digital world, this report includes the security strategy for “a ready and resilient society” to protect national security from climate and natural disasters, and the potential impact of climate change. Specifically for the Netherlands, it discusses the risk of drought, and wildfires, whereas for the Caribbean part of the Kingdom it discusses the threat of hurricanes and its consequences potentially being even greater if critical infrastructure and other processes are protected. It also refers to the rise in sea levels posing a significant threat to the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Moreover, it discusses the social tension that may arise from the increasing inequality or fundamentally different views on how to address climate change and the energy transition. 

Line of Action 9 discusses the need to intensify climate mitigation and adaptation, and discusses the priorities for 2023-2029, below discussed in short:  

A. Achieve climate mitigation goals and reduce international footprint

B. Increase the urgency of the implementation of national and international climate plans and agreements

C. Ensure that the Netherlands is fully circular by 2050

D. Ensure security of supply for critical materials needed for the energy and digital transitions

E. Take into account the risks to national security in the area of spatial planning

F. Strengthen the approach to wildfire prevention

G. Define a long-term approach to the effects of climate change for the Caribbean part of the Kingdom

H. Take climate risks and resilience into account in strategic and security policy

I. Disseminate Dutch knowledge regarding climate vulnerability and risk assessment, and stress the importance of following a conflict-sensitive approach in climate efforts

J. Contribute to greater water security and water safety in fragile states
Document Title: Report on the Security Strategy for the Kingdom of the Netherlands

Family Name: Climate Risk Management Guideline
Family Summary: The guidelines were developed by the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe in terms of section 6(1) (c) of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe Act [Chapter 22:15] aimed at strengthening the resilience of the country’s banking system to climate-related risks and support the transition to a low-carbon economy. They guide all institutions registered and supervised by the Reserve Bank in terms of the Banking Act [Chapter 24:20], the Building Societies Act [Chapter 24:02], and the Microfinance Act [Chapter 24:30] on the adoption of climate risk management principles to assess, monitor, and mitigate climate-related financial risks, including credit, market, liquidity, and operational risks.
Document Title: Climate Risk Management Guideline

Family Name: Third Enhanced National Climate Change Adaptation Plan (2023-2025)
Family Summary:
The enhanced plan considers climate disasters experienced by South Korea: flooding in the metropolitan area ('22.8), typhoon in Pohang ('22.9), drought in Gwangju, Jeollanam-do ('22.11), forest fire in Gangwon-do ('22.3), and strengthens the existing Third National Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2023 (2021-2025). It incorporates the latest IPCC climate projections and enhanced responses to extreme weather events, along with actionable implementation plans.

The four strategic directions are as follows:

  1. Improving climate forecast accuracy and enhancing public access to adaptation information;
  2. Adapting critical infrastructure to future climate risks and strengthen disaster response capabilities;
  3. Strengthening the resilience of living spaces and infrastructure while enhancing adaptation in agriculture, fisheries, and ecosystems; and
  4. Strengthening legal frameworks and foster collaboration among stakeholders, including national and local governments, industry, and the financial sector.
Document Title: Implementation Plan of Third Enhanced National Climate Adaptation Plan (2023-2025)

Family Name: Second Transitional National Development Plan
Family Summary:
This two-year Transitional National Development Plan (TNDP), with the theme “Towards a High-Income Economy: Transformation Now, Prosperity Tomorrow”, builds on other initiatives aimed at catapulting the country onto a path of socioeconomic progress towards 2036. The Plan outlines the national priorities, strategies, programmes and projects. It offers an opportunity to transition and institutionalise the necessary reforms into the planning system, laying a firm foundation for future Development Plans. This Plan contains actions on the development of climate-smart agriculture, climate change-resilient society, and green growth through reforms in the power sector.

The TNDP has identified eight key policy priorities to be pursued during its lifespan. The priorities were developed taking into account the global and domestic macroeconomic developments, the Reset Agenda, and the desire to achieve high growth status, among others. These priorities are: i) Supporting export-led growth and attracting inward Foreign Direct Investment; ii) Supporting the private sector through business environment reform and value-chain development; iii) Innovation and digital transformation; iv) Financial sector reform; v) Infrastructure development and spatial planning; vi) Green transition; vii) Fiscal sustainability; and xiii) Education and Human Capital Development.
Document Title: Second Transitional National Development Plan

Family Name: Bulgaria's electricity transmission network development plan for 2023-2032
Family Summary: The Bulgartransgaz TYNDP 2023–2032 supports the integration of renewable energy and decarbonisation by preparing the gas transmission system for a gradual transition from natural gas to low-carbon and renewable gases. The plan foresees infrastructure investments that enable the transport of hydrogen and hydrogen–natural gas blends, and support the role of gas networks as a balancing and backup solution for variable renewable electricity (especially solar and wind). It also aligns network development with national and EU climate targets.
Document Title: Bulgaria's electricity transmission network development plan for 2023-2032

Family Name: Bulgaria’s 2023 National Hydrogen Roadmap
Family Summary:
The National Hydrogen Roadmap aligns with both international and national strategies, including the UN Sustainable Development Goals, the European Green Deal, and the Paris Agreement.The Bulgarian National Hydrogen Roadmap aims to stimulate the growth of hydrogen technology, achieve climate targets, reduce emissions, promote renewable energy, and move toward a circular economy. It ensures a balanced transition to climate neutrality while considering Bulgaria’s unique economic factors.

It defines strategic objectives, including the decarbonization of the economy, the transition from traditional energy sources to hydrogen, and building the capacity to harness hydrogen technologies.

Family Name: Standard on the Disclosure of Greenhouse Gas Emissions and the Setting of Reduction Targets
Family Summary:
As part of the commitments set out in the Greening Government Strategy, Canada has produced a Standard on the Disclosure of Greenhouse Gas Emissions and the Setting of Reduction Targets (or the GHG Disclosure Standard), pursuant to the country's Policy on Green Procurement.


The Standard requires federal government departments and organisations to ensure that procurement process for contracts of more than $25 million induce suppliers to disclose their greenhouse gas emissions and adopt a GHG emissions reduction target that is in line with the Paris Agreement (outlined in subsection 3.2.1 of the Standard)


The organisations must report their total volume of spending and the number of contracts that have applied subsection 3.2.1, as well as the percentage of contract over $25 million, to which subsection 3.2.1. applies.


However, the Standard does not applied if it is determined that it is neither feasible nor appropriate to apple subsection 3.2.1. in the procurement process, or if it's non-application can be justified, such as through the provision of evidence that suppliers for a specific procurement process are not able to comply with subsection 3.2.1.
Document Title: Standard on the Disclosure of Greenhouse Gas Emissions and the Setting of Reduction Targets

Family Name: National Strategy for reducing social inequalities in health (Meld. St. 15 2022-2023)
Family Summary:
This Strategy contains actions to address social health disparities in public health work, which are particularly applicable to the contexts of climate change, demographic changes and international cooperation. It recognises that those with the lowest socio-economic backgrounds and children are the most vulnerable, and the climate crisis can threaten the development, upbringing and education of children, their access to clean water, health and sufficient, healthy and safe food and survival.

Under the section on climate adaptation, the government will:

  • strengthen knowledge in municipalities about the consequences of and measures against heat waves with the aim of protecting vulnerable groups, including how important it is to preserve and plant trees and other vegetation in cities and towns, and about the health risks of heat waves;
  • ask the Norwegian Food Safety Authority to prepare to meet the challenges that climate change and a tense international situation pose for the Norwegian food system, in order to ensure access to sufficient, safe and healthy food; and
  • establish a roadmap for a health sector with low greenhouse gas emissions, in collaboration with municipalities and relevant stakeholders by the end of 2023.
Document Title: National Strategy for reducing social inequalities in health (Meld. St. 15 2022-2023)

Collection Summary: The UK Climate Change Act, first passed in 2008 and amended in 2019, is the UK's framework law for the transition to a low-carbon economy, creating an obligation for the government to set legally-binding carbon budgets to act as stepping stones towards an overall 2050 emissions reduction target.
Family Name: Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan
Family Summary:
In 2023, the plan set out sectoral policies and proposals for decarbonising all sectors of the UK economy to meet the net zero target by 2050 and to achieve the emissions reductions required by the sixth carbon budget in particular. It replaced the Net Zero Strategy, which was successfully challenged before the courts for being insufficiently detailed. It was created pursuant to Section 14 of the Climate Change Act. The Plan It was revised in 2025.

The new plan is the government’s roadmap for meeting its legally binding carbon budgets and net-zero target while supporting economic growth, energy security, and job creation. Published under the Climate Change Act, the plan sets out policies and proposals across the economy (energy, transport, buildings, industry, agriculture, waste, and land use) to deliver emissions reductions through 2037. It emphasizes clean energy deployment, electrification, energy efficiency, low-carbon technologies, and investment in green industries, while positioning the net-zero transition as a driver of productivity, investment, and long-term economic competitiveness. The plan also demonstrates how the UK intends to meet its Fourth, Fifth, and Sixth Carbon Budgets (2033-2037) and align domestic climate action with its international climate commitments.
Document Title: Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan

The Energy Security Plan, part of "Powering Up Britain", sets out the UK government's strategy for creating greater energy independence and improving the UK's energy security, in ways that is consistent with the UK's net zero objectives and mitigate the impact of higher energy bills for households. The Plan builds on the British Energy Security Strategy and the Net Zero Strategy, and is complemented by the Net Zero Growth Plan. 


The Plan sets our a series of key commitments around alternative energy sources (such as the new nuclear programme, Great British Nuclear, the development of electrolytic hydrogen production, and the Net Zero Hydrogen Fund), carbon capture storage projects, and energy efficiency upgrades through the Great British Insulation Scheme and an extension to the Boiler Upgrade Scheme, amongst others.

Family Name: Action Plan for Resilient and Concerted Water Management
Family Summary:
This Action Plan aims to guarantee quality water for all and preserved ecosystems. Its 53 measures aim to respond to three major issues: sobriety of use, quality and availability of the resource given the increasing droughts in the face of climate change. This plan also improves the response to drought crises.

The objectives are:

  • secure the supply of drinking water by reducing leaks;
  • enhance unconventional waters (REUT, rainwater, grey water, etc.), by developing 1000 reuse projects in the territory, by 2027;
  • improve storage in soils, groundwater, works by remobilising existing resources, and meet the need to develop agricultural hydraulics, in compliance with regulations.

The general means to achieve the objectives are:

  • improve the governance of water management, by including all actors around open, more effective and more readable governance;
  • ensure adequate pricing and a level of financing for water resource management, with the objective of ensuring the financing of water policy and better encouraging sobriety in uses and better performance of networks;
  • invest in research and innovation throughout the water management value chain, in order to cross levels of innovation.
Document Title: Action Plan for Resilient and Concerted Water Management

It aims to reduce the adverse impacts of flooding on human health, the environment, cultural heritage, and economic activities through coordinated preventive actions, spatial planning measures, and infrastructure development.

The plan prioritises eco-friendly flood management, emphasizing nature-based solutions like floodplain restoration to boost biodiversity while lowering risk. Because climate change is altering weather patterns, the plan incorporates adaptive measures for extreme events. Execution requires a coordinated effort across all levels of government and water management sectors.

Family Name: 2023 Green Finance Strategy
Family Summary:
The 2023 Green Finance Strategy, updating the 2019 Strategy, aims to reinforce and expands the UK government’s position on green finance and investment by setting out five key objectives:

1. mobilising support to the financial services sector to improve support for climate and transition oriented projects;

2. encouraging private investment in the green economy;

3. producing an effective green finance framework to mitigate climate risks and improve financial stability;

4. incorporating nature and climate adaptation into the green finance policy framework to help support private investment in climate resilience; and 

5. supporting the alignment of global financial flows with climate and nature objectives in emerging and developing markets. 


The Strategy is published alongside Powering Up Britain, the Nature Markets Framework, the International Climate Finance Strategy, and the UK’s 2030 Strategy Framework for Climate and Nature and collectively form the UK’s response to driving progress on addressing climate change.
Document Title: 2023 Green Finance Strategy

Family Name: International Climate Finance Strategy 2023
Family Summary:
The UK International Climate Finance Strategy sets out how the government will deliver on its pledge to double its International Climate Finance (ICF) commitments to £11.6bn between 2021 and 2026, including at least £3bn on development solutions that protect and restore nature. The provision of ICF will be balanced between support for mitigation and adaptation measures. Over the five year period covered by the Strategy, the UK’s ICF will be spread across four key themes: 

1. Reducing global reliance on fossil fuels by supporting the acceleration of the transition to clean energy in energy-producing and energy-consuming sectors;

2. The protection, sustainable management and restoration of nature by ensuring that the global financial and economic systems tackle unattainable production and consumption, through supporting governments, central banks, businesses and financial institutions to integrate the value of nature into decision-making processes;

3. Building the capacity of people and communities to adapt and become more resilient to the impacts of climate change, supporting the transformation of systems, and helping countries and communities to address impacts when they occur; and

4. Supporting low-carbon, green and resilient urbanisation to promote sustainable and accessible cities, as well as enabling access to clean and reliable infrastructure.


The Strategy is published alongside Powering Up Britain, including the Net Zero Growth and Energy Security Plans, the 2023 Been Finance Strategy, and the UK’s 2030 Strategy Framework for Climate and Nature Action and collectively form the UK’s response to driving progress on addressing climate change.

  • Natural water balance with living rivers, lakes and floodplains;
  • Seas and coasts;
  • Wilderness and protected areas;
  • Forest ecosystems;
  • Soils as carbon sinks;
  • Natural climate protection on settlement and traffic areas;
  • Data collection, monitoring, modelling and reporting;
  • Research and capacity building; and
  • International and EU cooperation.

Family Name: Carbon Markets Rules for the Kingdom of Bhutan 2023
Family Summary:
The 2023 Carbon Markets Rules for the Kingdom of Bhutan provides guidance on how Bhutan will facilitate its participation in cooperative approaches with other parties to the Paris Agreement under Article 6.2.The rules are applicable to all activities within Bhutan that seek to participate in either compliance or voluntary carbon markets, specifically for the issuance of a Letter of Authorisation to facilitate corresponding adjustments. For activities of the voluntary market that do not require a Letter of Authorisation, entities do not need to obtain approval, as these activities do not impact Bhutan’s international climate commitments.

Institutional Arrangements

  • National Climate Change Committee (NCCC): This high-level committee sets the overall scope for Article 6 engagement and approves fees for corresponding adjustments.
  • Climate Change Coordination Committee (C4): This committee reviews and develops methodologies, oversees technical guidelines, and proposes activities eligible for carbon market participation for NCCC approval. It also sets technical standards, accredits third-party auditors, and handles the certification and issuance of emission reduction credits. C4 is responsible for authorising projects and participants to generate and transact Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs), and managing grievances and appeals.
  • Department of Environment and Climate Change (DECC): The DECC defines the carbon asset development process, accredits auditors, registers projects, and certifies emission reductions. It also proposes project authorisations for generating and transacting ITMOs, sets fees for corresponding adjustments, and executes the transfer of Article 6 units. Additionally, the DECC carries out corresponding adjustments and reports on projects and transfers in the Biennial Transfer Reports for Article 6 Technical Expert Review.

Process

  • Participation requirement: Entities must obtain a Letter of Authorisation from the DECC.
  • Validation and verification: Mitigation activities need to be validated and verified according to procedures established by the National Environment Commission (NEC).
  • Authorisation details: Once authorised, entities can manage, sell, and transfer any mitigation outcomes arising from the authorised activities, in accordance with the conditions set in the Letter of Authorisation.
  • Payment for corresponding adjustments: The DECC specifies the payment required for corresponding adjustments at the time of granting the Letter of Authorisation.
Document Title: Carbon Markets Rules for the Kingdom of Bhutan 2023

Family Name: Executive Order on Approval and Permits of Lifestock Farming (Methane Reduction Regulation)
Family Summary:
In connection with the agricultural agreement from 2021, as of 1 May 2023, a legal requirement for frequent discharge has been introduced in slaughterhouses.

In housing and stable sections for pigs on livestock farms, manure must be discharged from the housing section when the manure is 10 cm high, subject to discharge at a minimum interval of every 7 days. Discharge can be done either by manual or automatic discharge. Discharge must ensure that the manure is emptied from the housing section to an outdoor collection or storage facility. The legal requirement shall contribute to a reduction in Danish pig production's greenhouse gas emissions corresponding to 150,000 tons of CO2 equivalents per year in 2025, increasing to 170,000 tons of CO2 equivalents per year in 2030.

The requirement for frequent discharge does not apply to housing sections that use stable acidification as an ammonia-reducing technology, or to housing for organic pig production.
Document Title: Executive Order on Approval and Permits of Lifestock Farming (Methane Reduction Regulation)

Family Summary:
This document sets out guidance for preparing feasibility study reports for government investment projects. Section 8 sets out what types of impact analysis is required. Under this, Section 8(5) states the following: 

For high energy consuming and high emission projects, based on the analysis of project energy resource utilization, predict and calculate the total annual carbon emissions and main product carbon emission intensity of the project, propose a project carbon emission control plan, clarify the proposed path and methods to reduce carbon emissions, and analyze the impact of the project on the achievement of carbon peak and carbon neutrality goals in the region.

Section 2(2) also states that projects must comply with major policy objectives, including carbon peak and carbon neutrality objectives.
Document Title: Outline for Preparing Feasibility Study Reports for Government Investment Projects

Family Name: FRA BOD Decree No. 57/202: The Committee for Supervision and Monitoring of Carbon Credits and its Competences.
Family Summary:
Within the context of Decree No. 4664/2022 that creates a voluntary market for trading carbon credits, Decree No. 57/2023 establishes the "Committee for Supervision of Carbon Emission Reduction Units (Carbon Credits)" within the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA). The committee comprises members from the FRA, the Ministry of Environment, the Egyptian Exchange, and relevant experts.

The committee is tasked with:

- Developing regulations for carbon credit issuance, supervision, and monitoring, ensuring transparency in carbon emission reduction projects.

- Establishing criteria for selecting Validation and Verification Bodies (VVBs) for these projects.

- Creating guidelines to ensure the integrity and credibility of issued carbon credits.

- Formulating regulations to prevent conflicts of interest among stakeholders involved in the carbon credit issuance process.

- Identifying approved carbon registries where trading of issued carbon credits is permitted.

- Collaborating with relevant entities to establish the "Egyptian Registry for Carbon Credits".

- Defining and classifying different types of carbon credits.
Document Title: FRA BOD Decree No. 57/202: The Committee for Supervision and Monitoring of Carbon Credits and its Competences.

Family Name: Measures for the Energy Conservation Examination of Fixed-Asset Investment Project
Family Summary:
These Measures were adopted by the National Development and Reform Commission on 17 March 2023, and came into force on 1 June 2023. The Measures were formulated in accordance with the Energy Conservation Law, the Administrative Licensing Law, the Regulation on Energy Conservation of Civil Buildings, and the Regulations on Energy Conservation of Public Institutions. 

The Measures aim to improve energy consumption and strengthen energy management and efficiency in fixed-asset investment projects, in order to help realise China's target for carbon peaking. The Measures set out the assessment/examination procedures for fixed-asset investment projects (both public and private) in relation to energy conservation. For example, government investment projects must obtain energy conservation examination opinions before submitting a feasibility study report.

Family Name: Adaptation Roadmap to 2030
Family Summary:
Paraguay’s Adaptation Roadmap to 2030) serves as a practical guide to implement the country’s climate adaptation goals under its Updated NDCs and National Adaptation Plan (2022–2030). The roadmap outlines sectoral and cross-cutting adaptation actions, specifies the roles of institutions and subnational actors, and sets indicative timelines to strengthen resilience against climate impacts. Its purpose is to move beyond planning toward concrete, coordinated action at both national and local levels.

The document prioritises adaptation measures in key areas such as water management, cities, agriculture, health, ecosystems and biodiversity, energy, transport, and infrastructure, while also promoting governance, capacity building, and risk reduction. By clearly defining responsibilities and creating a framework for collaboration among stakeholders, the roadmap seeks to ensure that Paraguay is better prepared to face the risks of climate change and can build a more resilient, sustainable development pathway by 2030.
Document Title: Hoja de Ruta de Adaptación al 2030 Adaptation Roadmap to 2030)

Family Name: Sustainable Taxonomy of Mexico
Family Summary: The Mexican Sustainable Taxonomy is a national framework designed to classify economic activities, projects and investments that contribute positively to environmental and social objectives. It establishes a science‑based, transparent system of criteria and thresholds that allow financial markets to identify “sustainable” assets, thereby reducing green‑washing and directing capital toward climate‑friendly and socially inclusive projects. The taxonomy’s first phase focuses on four core objectives (climate‑change mitigation, climate‑change adaptation, gender equality, and sustainable cities) while also incorporating a broader set of environmental goals such as water management, biodiversity conservation, and circular economy practices. Activities are evaluated against “technical assessment criteria” that include a primary metric, a substantial contribution threshold, non‑harm criteria, and minimum safeguards covering human rights, labour standards and governance.In practice, the taxonomy covers six key sectors (agriculture, energy, construction, manufacturing, transport and waste management) and identifies 124 eligible activities that meet the established criteria. For climate‑change mitigation, metrics such as CO₂e emissions reductions and energy‑efficiency gains are used, while adaptation is assessed qualitatively through resilience to climate risks.
Document Title: Sustainable Taxonomy of Mexico (Taxonomia Sostenible de México)

Family Name: National Water Strategy
Family Summary:
The National Water Strategy primarily focuses on challenges and the measures needed for the protection and use of inland waters and groundwater, including the relevant impacts of sea level rise related to dike infrastructure and lowland drainage. During the two-year National Water Dialogue, participants developed proposals for a common vision for water management in 2050.

The strategy is divided into 10 strategic themes:

  1. Protect, restore and ensure a semi-natural water regime for the long term – prevent water scarcity and conflicting goals
  2. Ensure that land use in rural and urban areas is compatible with water bodies and adapted to the climate
  3. Further develop sustainable management of water bodies – achieve and preserve good status
  4. Mitigate risks caused by pollutants
  5. Further develop water infrastructure adapted to the climate – protect against extreme events and ensure supply
  6. Link water, energy and substance cycles
  7. Strengthen efficient administrations, improve data flows, optimise legal frameworks and secure financing
  8. Intensify protection of marine areas (North and Baltic Seas) from pollutants from land
  9. Raise awareness of water as a resource
  10. Work together to protect global water resources for the long term
Document Title: National Water Strategy

Family Summary: This decree implements Section 21 of Finland's Climate Change Act (423/2022), which mandated the creation of the Sámi Climate Council. It sets out detailed rules on the Council's tasks, composition, term of office, appointment procedure, and member remuneration. The purpose of the decree is to create an independent expert body that strengthens the knowledge base and identifies matters essential to promoting Sámi culture when preparing national climate policy plans. Its core task is to give statements/opinions on climate policy plans from the perspective of Sámi culture, and it may also carry out other knowledge-generating tasks related to climate change and Sámi culture and rights. Family Name: National Clean Air Policy
Family Summary:
The National Clean Air Policy (NCAP) aims to provide a framework for improving air quality in Pakistan by accelerating progress to reduce air pollutant emissions across all major sectors.


To do so, the NCAP identifies a priority intervention in each of the following five key sectors:

 

·        Transport: Implement Euro-5 and Euro-6 Fuel Quality Standards 

·        Industry: Enforce emission standards for industries 

·        Agriculture: Prevent burning of agricultural residues 

·        Waste: Prevent open burning of municipal solid waste 

·        Households/ Residential: Promote use of low emission cooking technologies 


The full implementation of these interventions under are projected to reduce particle pollution from fine particulates (PM2.5) emissions by 38% in 2030 compared to Pakistan’s current baseline scenario and by 21% compared to 2020 levels. By 2040, these five key interventions are projected to further reduce emissions by 81% in 2040 compared to the baseline scenario and by 70% compared to 2020 levels.
Document Title: National Clean Air Policy

Family Name: Guideline B-15: Climate Risk Management
Family Summary:
This guideline is a product of the 2022 budget commitments of the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). It outlines climate-related risks to federally-regulated financial institutions (FRFIs) and the broader financial system, and OSFI’s expectations regarding the management of these risks. The recognized climate-related risks are:

  • Physical risks which pertain to financial risks related to the climate-related extremes and events, gradual shifts, and indirect effects of climate change.
  • Transition risks which pertain to financial risks related to the transition to a low-emission economy, including risks from current and future policies, legislations, and regulations.

This guideline requires FRFIs to build financial and operational resilience against these risks through addressing, managing, and monitoring vulnerabilities in their business models and strategies, operations, and accounting procedures. It further seeks that FRFIs create adequate and robust governance and risk management practices through the improvement of their data quality and risk measurement methodologies.
Document Title: Guideline B-15: Climate Risk Management

A major upheaval of our time, global climate change will permanently alter the risk map facing France. Responsible for protecting and rescuing populations, Civil Security actors find themselves on the front line when it comes to these changes. They must therefore prepare and anticipate them.

Family Name: Strategy for climate change adaptation, disaster risk reduction and the fight against hunger
Family Summary:
This Strategy focuses on climate change adaptation, which has been identified as a priority area in Norwegian development policy. The Norwegian government recognises that while it is vital to reduce emissions, priority must also be given to increasing support for climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction in development cooperation and global climate action; climate-resilient development is needed across the world and developing countries must be given support to achieve this.

This strategy lays the foundation for intensified Norwegian efforts to assist vulnerable societies in adapting to climate change. The strategy identifies priority focus areas and tools for enhancing climate change adaptation. The focus areas are: early warning systems and climate services; nature-based solutions; climate-resilient food production; infrastructure; and innovative development financing mechanisms.

This strategy is linked to Norway’s Humanitarian Strategy. It follows up a priority area in the work to prevent humanitarian emergencies, with a focus on climate-related crises, as most natural disasters today are relatedto climate change.

Family Name: Universal Energy Access Plan 2023-2027 (Plan de Acceso Universal de la Energía 2023-2027)
Family Summary: Peru’s Universal Energy Access Plan 2023-2027 charts a near-term pathway to deliver modern, reliable and affordable energy to all households (especially low-income, rural and peri-urban communities) while advancing the broader energy-transition goals set in the National Energy Policy 2010-2040. Centred on the principle of equity, the Plan commits to full coverage of electricity and clean fuels, backed by targeted subsidies, diversified financing (including the Fondo de Inclusión Social Energético) and six programme clusters: mass expansion of natural-gas networks; LPG access schemes; frontier electrification projects; rural-energy efficiency and productive-use initiatives; tariff-compensation mechanisms; and infrastructure to distribute clean cooking fuels. Climate and sustainability considerations run through the document. Priority is given to shifting households and transport from petroleum-based fuels to natural gas, electricity or other low-carbon alternatives, deploying the most efficient technologies available, and embedding safety and quality standards.

Family Name: Federal Action Programme Natural climate protection
Family Summary:
Germany’s Action Plan on Nature-based Solutions for Climate and Biodiversity (ANK) is Germany's flagship initiative designed to tackle the climate crisis and biodiversity loss together that combines climate mitigation with nature conservation by restoring and strengthening ecosystems so they can function as natural carbon sinks. Its core principle is that only healthy, diverse ecosystems can act as reliable carbon sinks and protect communities against climate impacts like droughts and floods.

Anchored in the Federal Climate Change Act, the program sets legally binding targets to remove a net average of 25 million metric tons CO2eq/year from the atmosphere through land and forestry by 2030. Backed by billions in federal funding, it relies on voluntary financial incentives for farmers, foresters, and local municipalities across 10 key areas to expand wild habitats, restore degraded landscapes, and build climate resilience.

Family Summary:
Rwanda's national carbon market framework details the administrative and institutional framework for Article 6 implementation, as well as the guiding principles to facilitate Rwanda's participation in carbon markets both within and outside Article 6 (6.2 6.4) and in non-market approaches under Article 6.8.

Administrative and Institutional Framework

The institutional framework consists of an Extended Governing Board (Oversight Body) and an Article 6 Unit.

1) Oversight Body

The Oversight Body provides long-term oversight of adopting necessary legislation and institutional mandates for the support of Article 6 activities. Its responsibilities include:

  • Coordination among multiple ministries.
  • Advising on Article 6 participation strategy.
  • Monitoring of the implementation of the framework.
  • Coordination with other climate and sectoral initiatives.

2) Article 6 Unit

The Article 6 Unit, also known as the carbon market office, is tasked with defining and implementing the Article 6 Framework. It is responsible for:

  • Operationalizing activities;
  • Managing the share of proceeds;
  • Providing technical support;
  • Overseeing transparency and accounting requirements, including recording and reporting activities and managing corresponding adjustments;
  • Developing and implementing procedures to facilitate the country's participation in the framework, which includes:
    • Identifying eligible mitigation activities;
    • Establishing authorisation and approval mechanisms;
    • Verifying and issuing Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs);
    • Applying corresponding adjustments;
    • Integrating reporting and accounting into the national system for reporting to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

3) Designated National Authority

The Rwanda Environment Management Authority (REMA), previously the Designated National Authority (DNA) for the CDM has been designated as the focal point for Article 6.4.

Policy Framework and Guiding Principles

Rwanda's guidelines for participation are in line with provisions of the Paris Agreement, and come with additional specifications for Rwanda's case. The framework mentions that the Government of Rwanda approves Article 6.2 activities and Article 6.4 projects based on national interest, and activities seeking recognition as non-market approaches require approval, and offset projects in the voluntary market need a letter of no-objection. Voluntary market projects labelled as Article 6 will imply the contribution of a share of proceeds (which can be thought of as a tax on market mechanisms) for the administration of carbon markets provision. There will also be special attention paid to forestry sector projects under Article 6, which will have to adhere to Law n47bis/2013 on the sale of forestry services.

Share of Proceeds Fees

A share of proceeds will apply for the approval of Article 6 activities, and the issuance of a letter of no objection for voluntary market projects. However, the level of share of proceeds is yet to be determined.
Document Title: National Carbon Market Framework

Family Summary: The National Adaptation Plan seeks to integrate adaptation into territorial planning. As part of efforts to improve governance across sectors, the action plan calls for the integration of climate change measures into national strategies and policies, and improved education and awareness of climate adaptation issues. It promotes the development of robust systems for managing internal displacement caused by extreme climate events, motivated in part by the increasing frequency of these hazards.

Family Name: Deep Retrofit Accelerator Initiative
Family Summary:
The Deep Retrofit Accelerator Initiative (DRAI) provides funding to organisations and projects that facilitate the development of deep retrofits in commercial, institutional, and mid- or high-rise multi-unit residential buildings in Canada, in order for Canada to meet its climate targets.

The objectives of the program are to:

  • build capacity for, and address barriers to, deep retrofit project development and implementation;
  • facilitate the development of deep retrofit projects in Canada;
  • contribute to transforming the buildings sector in support of the Government of Canada’s climate goals.

Approximately $185.5 million is available until 31 March 2027 and funding covers two streams, one to provide support for deep retrofit accelerator organisations, and the other to provide support for deep retrofit capacity building activities.
Document Title: Deep Retrofit Accelerator Initiative

Family Name: Forest fire prevention and fight policy in a context of extension and intensification of the risk due to climate change
Family Summary:
Faced with the increasingly worrying developments in the risk of ‘forest fires’ in the context of climate change, the Minister of the Interior, the Minister of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty, the Minister of Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion and the Secretary of State for Biodiversity have entrusted the CGAAER, the Inspectorate General of Administration (IGA) and the Inspectorate General of the Environment and Sustainable Development (IGEDD) to carry out two missions relating to the intensification of the risk of forest and other vegetation fires and the extension of areas at risk by the middle and end of the century, and to forest and other vegetation fire prevention policies.

The report is in two volumes. The first is entitled ‘Coping in the short term’, and the second is entitled ‘Adapting to the change of era: learning to live with fire in the medium and long term’. The mission met with a very wide range of stakeholders (around 1,000 people) at national level and in the areas historically affected by fires and those where the risk of fire spreading is emerging. In addition, the team summarised the most recent scientific studies on climate projections up to 2100.In the first volume, the two missions put forward recommendations for significantly adapting the prevention strategy and continuing to improve fire-fighting, mainly through proposals for short-term action. Longer-term strategies, based on an analysis of the intensification and extension of the risk, are presented in Volume 2.
Document Title: Forest fire prevention and fight policy in a context of extension and intensification of the risk due to climate change - Volume 2( Politique de prévention et de lutte contre l’incendie de forêt dans un contexte d’extension et d’intensification du risque dû au changement climatique - Rapport Tome 2)

Family Name: Environmental Improvement Plan 2023
Family Summary: The Environmental Improvement Plan 2023 (EIP23) builds on the 25 Year Environment Plan published 5 years ago, by using the 10 goals set in the 25 Year Plan as the basis for EIP23. The overarching goal of EIP23 is to halt the decline in the UK’s biodiversity to achieve thriving plants and wildlife. EIP23 proposes measures to advance the UK’s progress towards achieving international biodiversity goals, as well as improving environmental quality and improving mitigation of climate change in the UK, specifically by publishing a Land Use Framework and publishing the third National Adaptation Programme in 2023. The Plan also proposes to reduce the risk of harm from environmental hazards exacerbated by climate change by delivering an investment plan to improve coastal and flood defences, including investing £100million on the most frequently flooded areas, amongst other measures.

Family Name: Philippine Development Plan 2023-2028
Family Summary:
The Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023-2028 is a plan for deep economic and social transformation to reinvigorate job creation and accelerate poverty reduction by steering the economy back on a high-growth path. This growth is intended to be inclusive, building an environment that provides equal opportunities to all Filipinos and equipping them with skills to participate fully in an innovative and globally competitive economy.

The plan contains actions on strengthening social protection, which include mitigating natural, health, climate and other human-induced hazards, such as :

  1. Further strengthen the coordination and collaboration among NDRRMC, Climate Change Commission, local government units, and the private and/or civil society sector;
  2. Ensure the implementation of mental health and psychosocial services in the disaster response package; Establish permanent and resilient evacuation centres;
  3. Strengthen social protection programs and introduce relevant products in responding to the pandemic and other health hazards;
  4. Implement and operationalise the Adaptive Shock Responsive Roadmap;
  5. Develop and implement anticipatory delivery mechanisms for various types of disasters and emergencies.

Other actions include actively participate in government-industry associations promoting and implementing employment and skills development policies and strategies; and creating and adopt climate- and disaster-resilient technologies for agriculture and infrastructure.

The overarching objective of the Mission is to make India a Global Hub for production, usage and export of Green Hydrogen and its derivatives, by targeting production of 5 MMT per annum of Green Hydrogen by 2030. The following components have been announced as part of the Mission:

i) Facilitating demand creation through exports and domestic utilization;

ii) Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition (SIGHT) programme, which includes incentives for manufacturing of electrolysers and production of green hydrogen;

iii) Pilot Projects for steel, mobility, shipping, decentralized energy applications, hydrogen production from biomass, hydrogen storage, etc.;

iv) Development of Green Hydrogen Hubs;

v) Support for infrastructure development;

vi) Establishing a robust framework of regulations and standards;

vii) Research Development programme including through a public-private partnership framework for RD;

viii) Skill development programme; and

ix) Public awareness and outreach programme.

The National Green Hydrogen Mission has an outlay of ₹ 600 crore for the FY 2024 – 25 under various heads.

The Green Hydrogen production capacity envisaged by 2030 is likely to leverage over ₹8 lakh crore in total investments in the Green Hydrogen industry. This investment is estimated to create 6,00,000 jobs by 2030.

Family Name: Sustainable Jobs Plan
Family Summary:
A sustainable job is defined as any job that is compatible with Canada’s pathway to achieving a net-zero-emissions and climate-resilient future and that reflects the concept of decent work, namely work — including a job in which the worker is represented by a trade union that has entered into a collective agreement — that can support the worker and their family over time and that includes elements such as fair income, job security, social protection and social dialogue.

Through this Action Plan, the Government of Canada is committed to ensuring that the transition to a stronger, more resilient economy generates high-quality, sustainable jobs in every region of the country. This includes supporting nation-building projects and using proven tools, such as community benefit agreements, prevailing wage requirements, unionized labour provisions, and Buy Canadian policies, to drive inclusive economic growth and ensure that workers share directly in the benefits of public investment.

There was an interim plan for 2023-2025 detailing concrete federal actions to advance economic prosperity and sustainable jobs in every region of the country.

This Plan outlines federal measures across 10 key action areas:

  1. Establish the Sustainable Jobs Secretariat
  2. Create a Sustainable Jobs Partnership Council
  3. Develop economic strategies through the Regional Energy and Resource Tables
  4. Introduce a sustainable jobs stream under the Union Training and Innovation Program
  5. Advance funding for skills development towards sustainable jobs
  6. Promote Indigenous-led solutions and a National Benefits-Sharing Framework
  7. Improve labour market data collection, tracking and analysis
  8. Motivate investors and draw in industry leadership to support workers
  9. Collaborate and lead on the global stage
  10. Establish legislation that ensures ongoing engagement and accountability

Family Summary:
The broad objective of the Livestock Policy is to utilize livestock resources for food and nutrition security and improved livelihoods while safeguarding the environment. The Policy aims to address diminishing availability of rangeland resources by proposing measures to address overgrazing, invasive plant species, pests, declining soil health, changing climate patterns, competing land use for settlement and crop development and inadequate supply of forage planting materials. The government will:

  • Facilitate the implementation of legislation and action plans relating to climate change.
  • Develop capacities and technologies to enhance adaptation and mitigation to effects of climate change.
  • Support programs to improve resilience of livestock keepers to effects of climate change.
  • Establish a contingency fund for disaster mitigation and emergencies.
  • Strengthen early warning systems and disaster preparedness.
  • Promote selection and development of appropriate livestock breeds and forage varieties.
  • Promote sustainable land management and green growth practices.
  • Promote climate financing and broaden mechanisms to attract investments in climate-smart agricultural practices along the commodity product value chain. Support adoption of insurance to mitigate climate risks.
Document Title: The Livestock Policy

Family Name: NDC Implementation Framework for Zambia 2023-2030
Family Summary: The Framework serves as a dashboard highlighting priority sectors, outcomes and output areas including key performance indicators, to reduce greenhouse gases and adapt to the impacts of climate change in various sectors: financial; agriculture; forestry; energy; infrastructure; water; livestock; industry; transport and health. The government is using this Framework to call for investments in the priority sectors such as renewable energy, transport and energy.
Document Title: NDC Implementation Framework for Zambia 2023-2030

Family Name: National Gender Policy 2023
Family Summary: One of the objectives of the Policy is to improve gender responsiveness in climate change and mainstream gender in climate change programmes. The Ministry responsible for Environmental matters is responsible for mainstreaming gender; facilitating the development of gender responsive interventions in the management of climate change for sustainable development; and reporting on the implementation of institutional gender programmes.
Document Title: National Gender Policy 2023

Family Name: Implementation Plan for the Philippines NDC 2020-2030
Family Summary: The NDC Implementation Plan (NDCIP) 2020-2030 outlines key actions, phasing, costs, and implementation arrangements for delivering the Philippines’ Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) under the identified policies and measures in the transport, energy, waste, industry, and agriculture sectors. The NDCIP also contains sections on financing the NDC and measurement, reporting and verification. Implementation is overseen by four sector departments: the Department of Agriculture (DA), Department of Energy (DOE), Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), and Department of Transportation (DOTr).
