Family Name: Water Sector Policy for Surface Water Utilization (2023)
Family Summary: This policy aims to mitigate flood and drought risks by improving the control and storage of surface water in Jordan. On top of ongoing risks, the increase in extreme rainfall and drought events due to climate change is named as a key motivator for this policy. A key element of the policy is more extensive mapping, assessment and monitoring of water usage and vulnerability. It aims more broadly to enhance and extend existing water storage and collection infrastructure, including by promoting land use changes to decrease sediment loads.
Document Title: Water Sector Policy for Surface Water Utilization (2023)

Family Name: Green Finance Strategy 2023‑2028 (Central Bank of Jordan)
Family Summary: The Green Finance Strategy 2023‑2028, by the Central Bank of Jordan (CBJ) with input from the Ministry of Environment and other agencies, aims to enhance the financing of climate change mitigation and adaptation projects. It recognises that rising temperatures in Jordan and worldwide pose a threat to the nation's financial systems. The strategy aims to: mobilise 30% more finance to green projects by 2028, relative to 2023; produce the first comprehensive climate risk assessment of the financial sector in Jordan; build climate governance and analytical capacity in the CBJ and broader sector; incorporate the Islamic finance sector and adopt a framework for Sharia-compliance in green investment.
Document Title: Green Finance Strategy 2023‑2028 (Central Bank of Jordan)

Family Name: National Water Strategy 2023–2040
Family Summary: Jordan's National Water Strategy 2023–2040 aims to improve the nation's water security and sustainability under increased threats from climate change and inefficient usage. It aligns with Jordan's Economic Modernisation Vision 2022-2033 and Public Sector Modernisation Roadmap. It aims to: upgrade monitoring and enforcement systems for efficient water use and distribution; incorporate clean energy into water processing to improve sustainability; launch national desalination projects; reduce the usage of non-revenue water; reduce pressure on threatened groundwater reserves; clarify the responsibilities of water companies and government ministries; increase surface storage capacity in reservoirs.
Document Title: National Water Strategy 2023–2040

Family Name: Water Sector Policy for Wastewater Management and Reuse 2023
Family Summary: Jordan's Water Sector Policy for Wastewater Management and Reuse from 2023 seeks to enhance water recycling capacity under increased threats to water security from climate change. It emphasises the importance of proper regulation and enforcement of existing wastewater control laws and building standards, and making regulations legible to key users such as the agriculture sector. It aims to expand sewerage system connectivity to prevent wastewater leakage, and outlines prioritisation rules for the substitution of water supplies with recycled wastewater across space and industry. Long term aims include decreased freshwater supplies to less sustainable highland irrigation, with wastewater substitution, and a stronger separation between wastewater and grey water in urban infrastructure.
Document Title: Water Sector Policy for Wastewater Management and Reuse 2023

Family Name: Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF 2023)
Family Summary:
This Framework serves as a tool to continuously identify nature, magnitude, extent and duration of environmental and social impacts. The environmental assessment to determine environmental and social costs, includes an assessment of climate change related impacts to build robust strategies to address and mitigate escalating impact on essentail structures like roads, bridges, tunnels and flyovers.

This Framework contains the procedures for environmental and social assessment; the baseline study of environmental and social components; impact assessment and mitigation measures; the environmental and social management plan; stakeholder consultation and information disclosure; the resettlement policy, indigenous people development and vulnerable community development framework, the grievance redress mechanism; occupational health and safety management; the gender equality and social inclusion and risk management plan; the environmental and social monitoring and environmental audit; and the institutional arrangements and implementation.
Document Title: Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF 2023)

Family Name: National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction (2023-2030)
Family Summary:
Jordan is affected by various risks, including flash floods, landslides and droughts. This Strategy outlines the strategic objectives, which are to improve the legal and institutional basis for disaster risk reduction (DRR); raise awareness of DRR; promote and support scientific research; sustain coordination and promote collaboration among stakeholders; and to integrate DRR and crisis management concepts within relevant national strategies, policies and priorities. It also covers the key challenges and gaps to be addressed; the alignment of this Strategy with national priorities, strategies and policies; the proposed tools for implementing this Strategy; and the Three-Year Action Plan listing six projects.

The proposed tools for implementing the strategy include decentralisation; creating partnerships at various levels; technology and innovation; resource mobilisation and financing; and identification of responsibilities and duties of all stakeholders in disaster preparedness, response and recovery.
Document Title: National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction (2023-2030)

Family Name: National Strategy for Adaptation to Climate Change in the Agricultural Sector (SPN2A-2035) - Action Plan 2022–2026
Family Summary:
The National Strategy for Adaptation to Climate Change in the Agricultural Sector (SPN2A-2035) and its Action Plan (2022-2026) is Niger's central framework for transitioning the AFOLU (Agriculture, Forestry, and Other Land Use) sector towards climate-smart agriculture. The strategy's main objective is to strengthen the climate resilience of producers and reduce the vulnerability of the rural population to climate risks, thereby fighting poverty and food and nutritional insecurity.

The strategy's implementation is structured around an adaptation continuum that integrates four distinct types of responses to climate change: (i) reducing vulnerability factors; (ii) strengthening response capacity; (iii) improving climate change risk management; and (iv) minimizing climate change impacts. Additionally, the planned activities provide significant mitigation co-benefits, contributing to global efforts to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.

The 2022–2026 Action Plan is the indispensable, budgeted five-year blueprint that details activities across six axes of intervention. These axes focus on: preserving natural resources, developing climate-smart agro-sylvopastoral and fisheries systems, reinforcing producer resilience, and integrating adaptation into sectoral planning.
Document Title: National Strategy for Adaptation to Climate Change in the Agricultural Sector (SPN2A-2035): Action Plan 2022–2026

Family Name: Green Growth Technology Roadmap
Family Summary: In line with Turkey's 2053 net zero emission target and green development policy, groundbreaking RD and innovation-based solutions have been determined as targets for 2026, 2030 and 2035 in the Iron-Steel, Aluminum, Cement, Chemicals, Plastic and Fertilizer sectors together with all stakeholders in the ecosystem. The prepared Green Growth Technology Roadmap is expected to start the creation of new projects, initiatives and platforms in line with the goals set up by academicians, public research centres, public institutions and especially industrial organisations with their own contributions. Future technologies are anticipated to adapt to combat climate change,
Document Title: Green Growth Technology Roadmap

Family Name: Flood Risk Management Plan 2023-2027
Family Summary: Flood Risk Management Plan 2023-2027 incorporates climate predictions, and implements the National Climate Change Management Strategy (2012) among other policies. The plan notes widespread hydrological regime changes across Lithuania, and acknowledges the increased risk of several flooding types due to climate change, alongside a possible decrease in spring flooding events.
Document Title: Flood Risk Management Plan 2023-2027

Family Name: Climate Change Authority Engagement Strategy 2023-25
Family Summary:
The Climate Change Authority is a statutory agency established under the Climate Change Authority Act 2011. Their purpose is to provide evidence-based advice on the response to climate change in order to:

  • accelerate emissions reductions and help Australia play its role in the global effort to limit temperature increases; and
  • enhance Australia’s prosperity and resilience as the climate changes and the world transitions to net zero emissions.

This Strategy lists down engagement approaches and consultation principles, which contractors are also required to follow.
Document Title: Climate Change Authority Engagement Strategy 2023-25

Family Name: National Agroecology Strategy (SND-AE) 2023-2027
Family Summary: Burkina Faso's National Agroecology Strategy (SND-AE) 2023-2027 aims to promote the sustainable development of agroecology in the agricultural sector, maintaining and increasing food security under increasing climate threats, while reversing land degradation. It aims to improve agroecology governance, increase the total uptake of agroecological practices, and strengthen the capacity of agroecological actors/stakeholders. The interventions promoted by the strategy are to be funded by a mix of state funds, international partners, NGOs and other sources.
Document Title: National Agroecology Strategy (SND-AE) 2023-2027

Family Name: CAP Strategic Plan (2023-2027)
Family Summary:
The Strategic Plan for the Common Agricultural Policy, which commenced on 1 January 2023, is a key instrument in supporting the transition to a sustainable, resilient, and modern agricultural sector in Bulgaria. The plan aims to foster the cultivation of special crops and varieties that are more suited to the evolving climate conditions, thus enhancing the agricultural sector's ability to adapt to climate change. It emphasizes measures such as irrigation systems, improved ventilation and cooling systems for animal husbandry, and sustainable farming practices to enhance resilience to climate change.

Environmental schemes for the climate, the environment and animal welfare included in the Strategic Plan for Agriculture and Rural Development 2023-2027 shall contribute directly or indirectly to the achievement of the objectives and priorities of the decarbonisation dimension.
Document Title: CAP Strategic Plan (2023-2027)

Family Name: Medium-Term Development Strategy 2022-2026
Family Summary: The strategy aims to guide national social and economic development initiatives in the short to medium term, and emphasises mainstreaming climate adaptation and mitigation across sectors. It supports a range of more detailed policies such as those on agroforestry and climate finance, and underscores the government's commitment to overarching emissions reduction and climate adaptation goals. A particular focus is climate smart agriculture, with provisions for training, financing and technological solutions such as evaporative cooling.
Document Title: Medium-Term Development Strategy 2022-2026

Family Name: Agricultural Methane Reduction Challenge
Family Summary:
Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada (AAFC) is looking to advance innovative, scalable and economically viable practices, processes, and technologies that contribute to the net reduction of enteric methane emissions from the cattle sector, specifically cow-calf operations, feedlot, and dairy.

The Agricultural Methane Reduction Challenge will award up to twenty semi-finalists with up to $250,000 each. In the next stage, ten finalists will receive up to $500,000 each. In the end, two winners will receive up to $1 million each to grow and scale their solution. All semi-finalists and finalists will also benefit from non-financial support such as mentorship and training opportunities.
Document Title: Agricultural Methane Reduction Challenge

Family Name: Slovenia’s Common Agricultural Policy Strategic Plan 2023-2027
Family Summary: The Strategic Plan for the Common Agricultural Policy 2023-2027 for Slovenia (SP 2023-2027) provides a set of measures (so-called interventions) for the implementation of 9 specific objectives of the European CAP and the horizontal objective for the dissemination of knowledge, innovation and digitalisation. In this way, the SP 2023-2027 pursues all 3 overarching objectives of the CAP: competitiveness and resilience of the agricultural sector, environmental and climate protection, and harmonious rural development.It is aimed at protecting and sustainably managing natural resources, mitigating and adapting to climate change and preserving biodiversity.The rules on conditionality are being tightened; they represent a standard above which payments for climate and environment schemes are designed within the framework of direct payments of Pillar I and agri-environment-climate payments and other area-based payments within Pillar II.

Family Name: Resources Methane Abatement Fund
Family Summary:
This Fund is for the development, prototype verification, validation, and demonstration-level projects of methane abatement technologies related to coal and gas industries. Funding is between AU$1 and 5 million for universities, publicly funded research organisations and non-profit research organisations to:

  • accelerate the development and deployment of methane abatement technologies;
  • reduce costs of abatement technologies;
  • reduce Australia’s methane emissions;
  • complement the Safeguard Mechanism reforms; and
  • support the Government’s commitments to the Global Methane Pledge.

The Fund is also intended to support opportunities for First Nations’ researchers to be involved in technology development.
Document Title: Resources Methane Abatement Fund

Family Name: CAP Strategic Plan 2023–2027
Family Summary:
Wallonia – CAP Strategic Plan 2023–2027

The Walloon CAP Strategic Plan 2023–2027 is designed to strengthen the economic resilience of farms while accelerating the environmental and climate transition of the agricultural sector. The plan supports a broad range of farming systems, including conventional, organic, livestock and arable production, and combines income support with rural development measures. Key priorities include improving farm competitiveness, encouraging generational renewal through dedicated support for young farmers, promoting cooperation and innovation, and increasing the use of digital technologies in agriculture and rural areas. Environmental objectives are integrated through eco-schemes and agri-environmental measures aimed at biodiversity protection, climate mitigation and sustainable land management. Wallonia’s plan forms part of the EU’s reformed Common Agricultural Policy and was approved by the European Commission for implementation during the 2023–2027 period.

Flanders – CAP Strategic Plan 2023–2027The Flemish CAP Strategic Plan 2023–2027 (Vlaams GLB-Strategisch Plan) sets out how Flanders implements the EU Common Agricultural Policy to achieve its economic, environmental and social objectives. The plan combines Pillar I measures—including direct income support and sectoral interventions for fruit, vegetables and beekeeping—with Pillar II rural development measures, which replace the previous Rural Development Programme (PDPO). A key feature of the Flemish strategy is its strengthened green architecture, integrating conditionality, eco-schemes, agri-environment-climate measures and management agreements to promote climate action, biodiversity conservation and the sustainable management of natural resources. The plan also supports farm competitiveness, innovation, knowledge transfer and generational renewal, while transferring part of the Pillar I budget to Pillar II to reinforce investments in rural development and environmental measures. The European Commission approved the Flemish CAP Strategic Plan on 5 December 2022, with subsequent amendments updating its implementation from 2024 onwards.
Document Title: Wallonia CAP Strategic Plan 2023-2027

Family Name: Federal funding for energy-efficient buildings (BEG) programme
Family Summary:
The Federal Funding for Efficient Buildings (Bundesförderung für effiziente Gebäude, BEG) is Germany's central federal subsidy programme for improving building energy efficiency and supporting the shift to climate-friendly heating. It is structured into four sub-programmes:

BEG Einzelmaßnahmen (EM), which funds the installation of new climate-friendly heating systems and individual renovation measures (e.g., insulation, window replacement) for both residential and non-residential buildings; BEG Wohngebäude (WG) and BEG Nichtwohngebäude (NWG), which offer low-interest loans with repayment subsidies for comprehensive renovations of existing residential and non-residential buildings to reach defined efficiency standards; and BEG Klimafreundlicher Neubau (KfN), which supports new climate-friendly building construction.Following a reform agreed by the German Bundestag's Budget Committee on July 8, 2026 and in force since July 21, 2026, funding has become more socially targeted: heating subsidies are now more strongly income- and family-based, renovation subsidies and a new bonus (from 2027) for renovating the worst-performing buildings.

Family Summary:

The Roadmap contains sections on policies and strategies impacting the maritime transport sector; a needs assessment; the Roadmap itself; recommendations for the facilitation of the Roadmap; actions, costs and benefits; financing requirements including potential sources for funding and collaboration with international organisations; and the implementation Plan.

The Roadmap involves the mapping of inter-atoll route patterns (to achieve economies of scale withn larger ships and higher loads), infrastructure, operations and the feet, and replacement of greenhouse gas-emitting gasoline outboards used by craft within lagoons.

The Plan places a specific focus on scaling up deployment of renewables to decarbonise the power sector; increase energy efficiency in buildings and deliver zero-emissions new builds; and reduce transport emissions.


The Plan seeks to facilitate a Just Transition, emphasises the necessity of citizen engagement throughout the transition to net-zero emissions; and highlights the leading role of the public sector in this regard.

Family Name: The UK Government Resilience Framework
Family Summary:
The UK Government Resilience Framework (2022) sets out a long-term approach to strengthening the UK’s ability to anticipate, prevent, prepare for, respond to and recover from a wide range of risks, including the increasing impacts of climate change. It establishes three core principles: developing a shared understanding of risks, prioritising prevention and preparation over response alone, and treating resilience as a “whole of society” responsibility. Climate change is identified as a chronic and interconnected risk requiring greater consideration of long-term vulnerabilities, including impacts on critical infrastructure, supply chains, communities and public services. The Framework establishes a plan to 2030 focused on strengthening risk assessment, government responsibilities, partnerships, community resilience, investment and skills, and complements dedicated climate adaptation policies such as the National Adaptation Programme.

The December 2023 update reports progress in implementing the Framework, including new processes for identifying chronic risks such as climate change, and greater focus on interconnected risks and critical infrastructure.
Document Title: The UK Government Resilience Framework 2023 Implementation Update

Family Summary:
Directive 2007/60/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2007 on the assessment and management of flood risks (Floods Directive) requires, among other things, the preparation of flood risk management plans. The President of the National Water Management Authority is responsible for developing flood risk management plans in accordance with the Water Law Act.

The Flood Risk Management Plan (PZRP) encompasses all elements of flood risk management, with particular emphasis on flood prevention and protection measures, as well as information on the state of preparedness in the event of a flood. Pursuant to the Water Law Act, flood protection is implemented in a manner that ensures coordination with activities aimed at achieving environmental and water protection objectives. Flood Risk Management Plans (PZRP) were developed for 6 river basins.

The Regulation of the Council of Ministers of 18 October 2016 adopted the Flood Risk Management Plan for the Vistula River Basin Area in line with the Water Act of 18 July 2001, which was later replaced by the Regulation of the Minister of Infrastructure of 18 October 2022 on the adoption of the Flood Risk Management Plan for the Vistula River Basin District, which entered into force in 23.03.2023, now in line with the Water Act of 20 July 2017 that superseded the former.

Family Name: Decree No 2022 - 698
Family Summary:
Decree No. 2022-698 establishes the procedures for registering carbon projects within the country. The Autorité d'Enregistrement des Projets Carbone (AEPC), or Carbon Project Registration Authority, is the government institution responsible for overseeing the implementation of this decree. The AEPC's mission includes promoting carbon projects, ensuring compliance with relevant norms and standards, and facilitating the registration and monitoring of these projects.

Project registration

All new carbon project developers in Benin must submit a registration request to the Autorité d’Enregistrement at least three weeks before submitting their validation report to a greenhouse gas certification program or relevant carbon standard. The request must include all required documentation for review.

Projects already certified or in the certification process when the decree was adopted must apply for registration within two months of its adoption.

The project document submitted for validation must include the following elements:

- Project description and development timeline

- Geographic area covered by the project

- Chosen greenhouse gas certification program or carbon standard

- Applied methodology

- Identification of stakeholders, including local communities, investors, and project developers

- Description of economic and social co-benefits

- Estimated greenhouse gas reductions and removals during the crediting period

- Proof of property rights or agreements with property owners related to the mitigation activity

- Stakeholder consultation details, including consent from local populations and communities

- Government authorizations, including environmental impact assessments and permits, if necessary

- Demonstration of project alignment with the Paris Agreement, Benin's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), and relevant goals.

Carbon rights

- Beninese citizens, communities, and registered entities have the right to participate in the carbon market, including proposing and developing projects.

- All carbon credits generated by projects in Benin are sovereign assets.

- The state can assign or transfer carbon rights to private developers.

- The terms for transferring or conceding carbon rights will be set by a decree from the Minister of Finance, based on a proposal from the Autorité d'Enregistrement.

Participation in Article 6

- The government of Benin decides, at its discretion, to participate in mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement to achieve emission reduction and other sustainable environmental goals.

- Private entities may be authorized to participate in these mechanisms after approval, based on criteria and guarantees set by the government.

- Emission reductions from carbon projects in Benin will contribute to the country’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).

- The government will assess scenarios for applying corresponding adjustments in line with Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, including relevant procedures, rules, and conditions.
Document Title: Decree No 2022 - 698

The plan also targets young farmers, social conditionality in labour practices, innovation and digitalisation, and seeks to improve quality of life in rural areas and protect natural resources, aligning with broader EU CAP and Green Deal objectives.
Document Title: Italy’s CAP Strategic Plan for 2023-2027

Family Name: The U.S. Global Change Research Program 2022–2031 Strategic Plan
Family Summary:
USGCRP’s 2022-2031 Strategic Plan lays the foundation for meeting a new set of challenges and demands for useful, accessible, and inclusive data and information alongside advancements in understanding of a rapidly changing environment.The pillars of this plan are formulated as following:
Advancing Science. Advance scientific knowledge of interconnected natural and human systems and risks to society from global change.Engaging the Nation. Enhance the Nation’s ability to understand and respond to global change by expanding participation in the Federal research enterprise.

Informing Decisions. Provide accessible, usable information to inform decisions on mitigation, adaptation, and resilience.

Collaborating Internationally. Build global capacity to respond to global change through international cooperation and collaboration.
Document Title: The U.S. Global Change Research Program 2022–2031 Strategic Plan

Family Name: Ghana's Framework on International Carbon Markets and Non-market Approaches
Family Summary: This framework provides operational guidelines for the development of the Article 6.2 cooperative approach in Ghana. It outlines relevant institutional arrangements for international transactions of authorized mitigation outcomes (carbon units stemming from emission reduction/removal actitvities) and provides the steps necessary develop and authorize mitigation activities.
Document Title: Ghana's Framework on International Carbon Markets and Non-market Approaches

Family Name: Malta’s Sustainable Development Vision for 2050
Family Summary: The vision aims to ensure that social cohesion, the protection of the environment, and economic growth move forward in a coherent and mutually beneficial way. It focuses on identifying existing gaps and provides guidelines and targets to effectively address emerging challenges and threats.
Document Title: Malta’s Sustainable Development Vision for 2050

Family Name: Guidelines for Canada’s International Support for the Clean Energy Transition
Family Summary:
On November 4, 2021, at the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) meeting in Glasgow, Scotland, Canada signed onto the Statement on International Public Support for the Clean Energy Transition (the “Glasgow Statement”), along with 38 other countries and institutions. The Glasgow Statement commits signatories to prioritise international public support fully towards the clean energy transition, using their resources to enhance what can be delivered by the private sector and to end new direct public support for the international unabated fossil fuel sector

This policy guides federal departments and agencies to implement the Glasgow Statement (Part A), effective from 1 January 2023, and outlines the limited exceptions to the policy such as for mitigation technology and humanitarian and emergency response (Part B).
Document Title: Guidelines for Canada’s International Support for the Clean Energy Transition

Family Name: Transport Infrastructure Ireland: Climate Adaptation Strategy
Family Summary:
This Strategy is Transport Infrastructure Ireland's (TII's) response to Action 297 of the Irish Climate Action Plan 2021 (CAP21), which is "Improve climate resilience and adapt to climate change on the Light rail and National Road Network".

TII’s seven climate adaptation strategic objectives are:

  1. Observe fewer network disruptions during climate- related events.
  2. Rapidly recover from any climate-related events.
  3. Have a robust, flexible, and equitable organisation that responds effectively during climate events.
  4. Enhance the climate resilience of lifeline roads in order to maintain community accessibility.
  5. Engage with the wider adaptation efforts across Ireland through partnerships and wider research.
  6. Embed climate adaptation within TII’s operations, policies, and procedures in order to ensure a safe and resilient network.
  7. Adopt a low-carbon approach in TII’s designs, standards, and processes when considering climate adaptation, while also considering wider social and environmental benefits.
Document Title: Transport Infrastructure Ireland: Climate Adaptation Strategy

Family Name: Decarbonising Transport Action Plan 2022–25
Family Summary:
The main purpose of New Zealand's Decarbonising Transport Action Plan 2022–25 is to detail how the New Zealand Government will implement its transport-related actions from the broader Emissions Reduction Plan (ERP) over the three-year period from 2022 to 2025.

It outlines how various government transport agencies will collaborate with Māori, local government, businesses, and communities to establish a long-term strategic approach to significantly reduce transport emissions. New Zealand's transport emissions are primarily from light vehicles (cars, 65.1%), requiring reductions in both driving distance and vehicle emissions. Heavy vehicles (trucks, 24.4%) are the second largest source, presenting a more difficult decarbonisation challenge due to fewer immediate alternative technologies. Other transport modes like rail, shipping, and aviation contribute a smaller proportion, and their full decarbonization is a long-term goal due to technology cost and availability, although initial efforts are underway. The plan has 4 axes:

  1. Reduce reliance on cars and support people to walk, cycle and use public transport
  2. Rapidly adopt lowemissions vehicles
  3. Begin work now to decarbonise heavy transport and freight
  4. Advancing cross-cutting and enabling actions
Document Title: Decarbonising Transport Action Plan 2022–25

Family Name: Nature Positive Plan: better for the environment, better for business
Family Summary:
This Plan sets out the Australian government’s commitment to reform Australia’s environmental laws to better protect, restore and manage our unique environment.

The government supports the recommendation of the review that proponents be required to publish their expected Scope 1 and 2 emissions. Further, proponents will be required to disclose how their project aligns with Australia’s national and international obligations to reduce emissions. The changing climate will also be a mandatory consideration in environmental planning approaches. Improvements in information and guidance will support these reforms.

The government recognises the risks global warming poses to Australia’s unique ecosystems and the link between climate and biodiversity. They will address this by embedding climate considerations in all roles and functions of government. In addition to their commitments to reduce national emissions to 43% below 2005 levels by 2030, and to achieve net zero emissions by 2050, the government will integrate climate change considerations, where relevant, throughout national environmental law without duplicating existing mechanisms for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. This includes improved transparency in project assessments; improved planning and landscape-scale approaches to facilitate adaptation to climate change; and improved information and climate-impact modelling.
Document Title: Nature Positive Plan: better for the environment, better for business

Family Name: Responsibility for Denmark - The political basis for the Government of Denmark
Family Summary:
This document contains a section on ambitious climate action, with sub-sections on the 70% emissios reduction target; new climate targets; vision for the future of Danish food production; marine plan and development of the Danish fishing industry; and more Danish forests.

While 2022 was the first time in many years that a majority government has been formed in Denmark, the government wants to maintain the tradition of the government promoting broad cooperation in the Folketing and negotiating with the parties in the Folketing to enter into broad agreements. The government will respect the current settlement and also pursue policies that strengthen community and trust in society, promoting openness and transparency.
Document Title: Responsibility for Denmark - The political basis for the Government of Denmark

Family Name: Ministerial Guidelines for Clean Cooking Technologies 2022
Family Summary: The guidelines aim to support and enforce the transition to more energy efficient cooking technologies, with the intent of mitigating greenhouse gas emissions, reducing air pollution, reducing pressure on woodland ecosystems, improving affordability and ultimately contributing to socioeconomic development nationally. It aims to contribute to goals to reduce the unprocessed biomass share of cooking energy from 78% to 42% by 2024. It assigns ministerial responsibilities for standards dissemination, and names a range of energy sources to favour such as processed biomass pellets, ethanol, methanol, biogas and electricity (favouring solar generation).
Document Title: Ministerial Guidelines for Clean Cooking Technologies 2022

Family Name: Rule on Prudence and Loyalty in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights, Amending the Investment Duties Regulation under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974
Family Summary:
This Rule was adopted by the US Department of Labour in December 2022 and entered into force in January 2023. The rule clarifies the circumstances in which pension fund managers' reliance on ESG factors in making investment decisions is aligned with their fiduciary duties under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974. The rule states "Risk and return factors may include the economic effects of climate change and other environmental, social, or governance factors on the particular investment or investment course of action. Whether any particular consideration is a risk-return factor depends on the individual facts and circumstances."

The new rule has been subject to legal challenge through the case of Utah v Walsh.
Document Title: Final Rule

Family Name: Action Plan for the Dialogue and Work Process on the Middle Class, Climate Protection and Transformation
Family Summary:
This Action Plan discusses how the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action will support SMEs with the transition to net zero. The Action Plan discusses the following challenges:


  • Energy prices;
  • Decarbonisation and sustainability;
  • Skilled workers;
  • Financing the transitions;
  • Company reporting on sustainability and due diligence;
  • Circular economy; and
  • Reducing bureaucracy and accelerating procedures.


Lastly, the Action Plan sets out industry-specific measures.
Document Title: Action Plan for the Dialogue and Work Process on the Middle Class, Climate Protection and Transformation

Family Name: Viet Nam: National adaptation plan for the period 2021-2030, with a vision to 2050
Family Summary: Viet Nam is a country that is particularly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. For this reason, Viet Nam fielded the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) for the period 2021-2030, with a vision to 2050.
Document Title: Viet Nam: National adaptation plan for the period 2021-2030, with a vision to 2050

Family Name: Environmental Building Reporting Program
Family Summary: The program mandates housing suppliers that provide a total of 20,000 metres squared or more floor area a year in Tokyo to ensure thermal insulation and high energy efficiency performance and install renewable energy equipment (solar power generation equipment) at small and medium-sized new buildings, including houses, with a total floor area of less than 2,000 metres squared. This policy impacts about 50 companies. The city government will also provide subsidies to encourage the installation of solar panels on existing buildings. This new regulation is expected to be impactful, as half of existing buildings will be replaced with new ones before 2050. This program mandates maintenance/operation of renewable energy equipment.
Document Title: Ordinance Revision to Halve Carbon Emissions (Carbon Half): Overview of the “Environmental Building Reporting” Program and Its Support Measures

Family Name: Framework Action Plan for Organic Food and Farming (2021-2030)
Family Summary: The Framework Action Plan for Organic Food and Farming in Poland for 2021-2030 has been updated to align with the European Union's "Farm to Fork" strategy. As of recent updates in 2024-2025, Poland’s Framework Action Plan for Organic Food and Farming in Poland for 2021–2030 aims to develop organic production, including the development of the organic products market in Poland and to allocate at least 7% of the agricultural area covered by the organic production system by 2030.This goal means doubling the area of ​​agricultural land covered by this system by 2030 compared to 2019 and striving to reach over one million hectares of this area.
Document Title: Framework Action Plan for Organic Food and Farming (2021-2030)

Family Name: Action Plan for the Implementation of the Election Program 'Just Kazakhstan'
Family Summary: This action plan includes an ‘ecological thinking’ category which includes activities that aim to reduce contaminants and strengthen environmental control, increase the national forestry area, adopt a new water code aimed at the protection of water resources and create the necessary infrastructure for electric cars. It is listed in Kazakhstan’s 2023 NDC as one of the relevant policy documents contributing to the achievement of the NDC target by 2030.
Document Title: Action Plan for the Implementation of the Election Program 'Just Kazakhstan'

Family Name: CAP Strategic Plan (2023-2027)
Family Summary: The Czech CAP Strategic Plan supports agriculture and rural development through EU funds, aiming to stabilise farm incomes, ensure affordable safe food, and promote sustainable agricultural and forestry practices while responding to climate change. Built on a comprehensive SWOT analysis, the plan allocates a large share of its budget to direct payments—especially for small and medium farms—and introduces 92 interventions covering income support, young farmer aid, production diversification, and measures to boost biodiversity and soil health. Nearly one-third of direct payments is dedicated to eco-schemes focused on environmental and climate benefits, including tackling soil degradation, erosion, water pollution, and nutrient and pesticide runoff. The strategy also supports emissions reduction and carbon sequestration through healthier soils and resilient land-management practices.
Document Title: CAP Strategic Plan (2023-2027)

Family Name: National Energy Efficiency Policy (NEEP) 2022 - 2030
Family Summary: The National Energy Efficiency Policy contains measures to reduce Cambodia's energy consumption by boosting energy efficiency. It sets country-wide targets for reducing energy consumption as well as sector-specific targets.
Document Title: National Energy Efficiency Policy 2022-2030

Family Name: Lithuanian Agriculture and Rural Development 2023-2027 strategic plan
Family Summary: The Agriculture and Rural Development 2023-2027 strategic plan aims to achieve stable development of Lithuania's food production and rural land, guiding the deployment of domestic policy and EU funding, and names contributing to climate goals among its main priorities. Climate adaptation measures in the plan emphasise the importance of widespread efficiency improvements to irrigation systems. The plan also contains significant measures for forest restoration; reconfiguration of crop systems to reverse declines in agricultural soil carbon storage across Lithuania; biogas installation and development; and funding for research, innovation and more general capacity-building.
Document Title: Lithuanian Agriculture and Rural Development 2023-2027 strategic plan

Family Name: Green Hydrogen Roadmap
Family Summary: The Green Hydrogen Roadmap aims to boost sustainable economic growth through the development of a green hydrogen sector, mitigating emissions and reducing fossil fuel dependence. It is coauthored between the Inter-American Development Bank and the state-owned National Energy Corporation, and is supported by a press release by the Ministry of Energy. The roadmap assesses and promotes the potential of offshore wind energy as a major renewable energy source for hydrogen production, and suggests potential annual output capacities of up to around 4 million tonnes. The accompanying 2022 ministerial press release notes the forthcoming development of a green hydrogen policy, and underscores the importance of adapting regulatory frameworks to promote hydrogen development.
Document Title: Ministerial press release for the Green Hydrogen Roadmap

Family Name: Germany’s CAP Strategic Plan 2023-2027
Family Summary: Germany's CAP Strategic Plan (GAP-Strategieplan) implements the EU's Common Agricultural Policy for the 2023–2027 funding period, combining both CAP pillars into a single national plan: Pillar 1 direct payments (including the voluntary "Öko-Regelungen," rewarding farmers for additional environmental services such as arable land set-aside, grassland extensification, or agroforestry) and Pillar 2 targeted programmes for sustainable land management and rural development. Covering roughly €30 billion in EU funding over the period and directly addressing over 300,000 applicants in the agricultural sector, the plan was developed in close coordination with federal ministries, the federal states, and economic, environmental, and social partners. It was initially approved by the European Commission on 21 November 2022 (Version 1.0); the currently valid version is 7.1, approved by the European Commission on 9 December 2025. More than half of EU funds under the plan are now directed toward environmental and climate objectives, positioning it as Germany's key implementing instrument contributing to the EU's Green Deal, Biodiversity Strategy, and Farm to Fork Strategy.
Document Title: Germany’s CAP Strategic Plan 2023-2027 - Summary

Family Name: Taxation of company cars: The appropriate percentage for tax years 2028 to 2029 and 2029 to 2030
Family Summary:
This measure will provide long term certainty on company car tax rates including continued incentives to support the take-up of zero emission and electric vehicles. In addition, the increase in appropriate percentages will ensure the tax system continues to support the sustainability of the public finances.

Rates for electric vehicles will increase gradually, while maintaining a significant differential between electric vehicles and internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles. Appropriate percentages for hybrid vehicles (with CO2 emissions of 1g to 50g per kilometre) will be increased to align more closely with ICE vehicles, to further focus support towards electric vehicles.
Document Title: Taxation of company cars: The appropriate percentage for tax years 2025 to 2026, 2026 to 2027 and 2027 to 2028

Family Name: Strategic Plan for Climate Change in the Agri-Food Sector - PLECCA (Plan Estratégico de Cambio Climático del sector Agroalimentario - PLECCA)
Family Summary: The Strategic Plan for Climate Change in the Agri-Food Sector (PLECCA) provides the framework for adopting a systemic, joint, and long-term vision for the Mexican agri-food sector under the conditions of a changing climate. Its main objective is to provide direction and coherence to the sector's actions to promote fair, diverse, sustainable, inclusive, low-carbon agri-food systems that are resilient to the effects of climate change.
Document Title: Strategic Climate Change Plan for the Agri-Food Sector (Plan Estratégico de Cambio Climático del sector Agroalimentario)

Family Name: Decree No. 58, establishing the Interministerial Committee for a Just Hydric Transition
Family Summary: 1. This Chilean presidential decree establishes an advisory Interministerial Committee for a Just Hydric Transition, designed to counsel the President on policy and institutional reforms necessary for a fair transition in water management. The creation of this body is framed by constitutional mandates, environmental regulation, sustainable development, alongside Chile's international commitments under the Paris Agreement and the Climate Change Framework Law. The pressing need for such a committee arises from a prolonged drought exacerbating socio-environmental degradation and the fragmented nature of current water management, involving numerous actors and often conflicting interests, thus necessitating a coordinated, systemic approach.The Committee's primary functions include advising the President on reforms for a just hydric transition based on equity, environmental justice, sustainability, and gender; facilitating inter-ministerial coordination; proposing coordinated policies, plans, legal modifications, and other measures to achieve a just transition; and receiving updates on relevant initiatives from member ministries. The Committee will meet at least quarterly, adopting decisions by absolute majority, with the Ministry of the Environment providing technical and administrative support through a dedicated Technical Secretariat.The decree specifies operational aspects, allowing the Committee to form subcommittees for specific tasks and invite other organisations and actors as necessary. Participants serve ad-honorem, and the Committee can establish its own operational procedures beyond those outlined in the decree. Ultimately, this body is tasked with fostering collaboration across State Administration bodies to achieve the objectives of a just hydric transition in response to the prevailing water crisis and broader ecological challenges facing Chile.
Document Title: Decree No. 58, establishing the Interministerial Committee for a Just Hydric Transition

Family Name: Decarbonization Strategy for Mexican Ports (Estrategia de Descarbonización de Puertos de México)
Family Summary: Mexico's Port Decarbonization Strategy (EDP) represents a framework for addressing the maritime sector's contribution to climate change, acknowledging that maritime transport accounts for 3% of GHG emissions. The strategy establishes specific reduction targets of 25% by 2030 and 45% by 2050 for CO₂ equivalent emissions across the National Port System's 103 ports and 15 terminals, aligning with Mexico's Paris Agreement commitments and its National Determined Contribution of 35% emission reduction by 2030. The policy mandates the creation of a standardised Port Emissions Inventory based on the Greenhouse Gas Protocol methodology, whilst promoting digitalisation, energy efficiency, sustainable infrastructure development, and strengthened port-city relationships through the intersecretarial Commission for Seas and Coasts (CIMARES).The strategy's climate-focused approach encompasses both mitigation and adaptation measures, recognising ports as multimodal logistics centres predominantly powered by fossil fuels with direct health impacts on adjacent communities. Implementation mechanisms include the ECOPIS digital platform integrated within the Intelligent Secure Port system for comprehensive emissions monitoring, regulatory framework updates to align concession titles and port master development programmes with decarbonisation objectives, and promotion of low-emission energy alternatives and equipment electrification.
Document Title: Port Decarbonization Strategy (EDP) [Estrategia de Descarbonización de Puertos (EDP)]

Family Name: National Action Plan on Human Rights, Gender and Climate Change (PNADHG-CC) [Plan Nacional de Acción de Derechos Humanos, Género y Cambio Climático (PNADHG-CC)]
Family Summary: The Mexican National Action Plan on Gender and Climate Change acknowledges Mexico's vulnerability to climate change, with rising temperatures, altered precipitation patterns, and vegetation loss disproportionately impacting vulnerable populations, particularly indigenous communities and women. The plan notes that Mexico´s CO2 emissions are significant on a global scale. These communities heavily rely on natural resources and often act as stewards of biodiversity. The plan aims to integrate a gender perspective into national climate change mitigation and adaptation efforts, as well as Mexico's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), to address the differentiated effects of climate change on women, girls, and youth.The National Action Plan is structured around three pillars: promoting the leadership of women; building and consolidating institutional capacities; and ensuring financing and cooperation. Actions include guaranteeing women's participation in climate change decision-making, strengthening institutional capacity on gender equality and human rights within climate action, and improving the availability of financial and technical resources for integrating gender perspectives into national climate change strategies. The plan will be reviewed biennially with the involvement of government, civil society, and international organisations, and is intended to be updated to reflect evolving needs and roles.
Document Title: National Action Plan on Human Rights, Gender and Climate Change (PNADHG-CC) [Plan Nacional de Acción de Derechos Humanos, Género y Cambio Climático (PNADHG-CC)]

Family Name: Sweden's Methane Action Plan
Family Summary:
This document is a foundation for further work on developing Sweden's action on methane. This, in turn is interlinked with the process of developing Sweden's forthcoming climate action plan that follows from the regulations set out in the climate policy framework.

This Action Plan sets out the sources and projections of methane emissions in Sweden. It then delineates the national strategies, policies, and measures. Lastly it provides an overview of international cooperation.
Document Title: Sweden's Methane Action Plan

Family Name: Ordinance No. RD-02-20-3 (2022) — Technical Requirements for Energy Performance of Buildings
Family Summary: Ordinance RD‑02‑20‑3 sets out the technical requirements for the energy performance of buildings in Bulgaria, including calculation methods, minimum performance standards, and energy classification. It applies to both new buildings and major renovations, specifying how energy demand, heat loss, and building envelope performance should be assessed. The regulation establishes the national methodology for energy performance calculations, defines energy efficiency classes, and sets minimum thresholds for energy consumption in heating, cooling, ventilation, and lighting. It ensures that Bulgaria’s building stock progressively meets higher energy efficiency and climate objectives.
Document Title: Ordinance No. RD-02-20-3 (2022) — Technical Requirements for Energy Performance of Buildings

Family Name: National Peatland Conservation Strategy (Nationale Moorschutzstrategie)
Family Summary: The strategy supports Germany's goal of achieving climate neutrality by 2045. Its measures aim to reduce annual greenhouse gas emissions from peat soils by at least 5 million tonnes of CO2-equivalent by 2030. Currently, more than 90% of Germany's moorlands are drained to the point of emitting roughly 53 million tonnes of CO2-equivalent annually, and peat soils represent Germany's largest terrestrial carbon store. The strategy centers on rewetting drained moors and peat soils, alongside climate-compatible long-term use of these areas, while also aiming to strengthen biodiversity in moorland regions.
Document Title: National Peatland Conservation Strategy (Nationale Moorschutzstrategie)

Family Name: National REDD+ Strategy
Family Summary: Pakistan's National REDD+ Strategy aims to provide a set of policies, actions and measures to restore forests nationally, decreasing net emissions and improving resilience to climate threats while allowing sustainable livelihoods for those dependent on forestry resources. It promotes several strategy options for implementation: reforestation/restoration/afforestation; sustainable forest management; payment for ecosystem services; silvo-pastoral/agroforestry practices; and sustainable/eco tourism. The strategy names synergies and barriers for these strategy options in its implementation framework, and then gives strategic policies/measures alongside a roadmap. It calls for addressing land tenure conflicts. strengthening institutional capacity, strengthening legal structures, improving cross-sectoral co-ordination, promoting public/stakeholder awareness, and the mainstreaming of gender in forest/REDD+ policy.
Document Title: National REDD+ Strategy

Family Name: National REDD+ Strategy
Family Summary: Gabon's National REDD+ Strategy aims to facilitate the sustainable management and restoration of forest resources, preserving their role in carbon sequestration to mitigate climate change while preserving rural livelihoods. It promotes increased efficiency of existing agriculture, allowing land-sparing, and the creation of timber plantations in already-degraded areas, reducing the impact on primary forest. It aims to introduce and enhance forest certifications, allowing better monitoring and funding by international carbon markets, and to increase forest-sector revenues by increasing the domestic processing of wood before export. The strategy also aims to improve enforcement of laws around logging and forest use, build general institutional capacity, and promote sustainable eco-tourism.
Document Title: National REDD+ Strategy

Family Name: Regulation 709/2022 on implementation rules of the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility Plan
Family Summary:
Regulation 709/2022 on implementation rules of the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility Plan Reform and Investment Axis 1.2. "Improving Energy Efficiency" 1.2.1.3.i. Investment for "Improving municipal buildings and infrastructure, promoting the transition to the use of renewable energy technologies and improving energy efficiency" sets out rules for the investment on the improvement of municipal buildings and infrastructure aiming at the promotion of renewable energy technologies and energy efficiency. The available funding from the EU RRF for the investment is 29,304,000 EUR.

The main objective is to improve the energy efficiency of municipal buildings and infrastructure in order to reduce annual primary energy consumption and achieve energy savings by implementing the most effective greenhouse gas emission reduction measures via energy efficiency and thermal insulation of municipal buildings. The target group of the investment is the municipalities of the Republic of Latvia.
Document Title: Regulation 709/2022 on implementation rules of the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility Plan Reform and Investment Axis 1.2. "Improving Energy Efficiency" 1.2.1.3.i. Investment for "Improving municipal buildings and infrastructure, promoting the transition to the use of renewable energy technologies and improving energy efficiency"

Family Name: The National Strategy for an Orderly Transition to Net Zero by 2025
Family Summary: The production of hydrocarbons has a dominant role in Oman's economy with oil and gas representing around 60% of the total export income. Therefore, in November of 2022, Oman announced its Natural Strategy for an Orderly Transition to Net Zero by 2025, in line with its efforts to tackle climate change. It sets a pathway for unlocking sources including renewable energy and hydrogen, whilst also decarbonizing existing hydrocarbon resources. To lead this transition towards a green economy, His Majesty Sultan Haitham Bin Tariq mandated the creation of the Oman Sustainability Centre, which aims to ensure the implementation of the National Net Zero Plan. The Centre will be the leading body undertaking the supervision and follow-up plans and programmes of carbon neutrality.
Document Title: National Strategy for an Orderly Transition to Net Zero

Family Name: Central Bank of Egypt Mandatory Regulations
Family Summary:
The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) issued mandatory regulations through a circular in November 2022 to require banks to: 

·       Set up an independent unit that deals with sustainability and sustainable finance by 1 April 2023; 

·       From 2024, submit periodic reports, including a quarterly report on sustainable finance activities, and a yearly sustainability report by 31 March of each year;

·       From July 2023, engage an environmental consultant certified by the Ministry of Environment to assess environmental risks for major projects seeking funding; and

·       Integrate sustainable finance policies into lending and investment policies.
Document Title: Circular

Family Name: Long-term climate change mitigation strategy by 2050
Family Summary: This strategy sets out Bulgaria's position and priorities for its low-carbon transition to climate neutrality by 2050. It outlines the main conclusions of the assessment of Bulgaria's potential bsaed on energy and climate modelling and building on Bulgaria's NECP. This strategy was prepared to fulfill requirements under the EU Governance Regulation.
Document Title: Long-term climate change mitigation strategy by 2050

Family Name: Egypt's Sovereign Sustainable Financing Framework
Family Summary: This framework updates Egypt’s 2020 Green Financing Framework, to include additional green and social projects to better align with the national strategy for sustainable development set out in Egypt’s Vision 2030. Green projects fall under the following categories: clean transportation, renewable energy, energy efficiency, climate change adaptation, pollution prevention and control, sustainable water and wastewater management, terrestrial and aquatic biodiversity conservation. Social projects fall under the following categories: affordable basic infrastructure, access to essential services including financing, education and healthcare services, affordable housing, socioeconomic advancement and empowerment, financing to support employment generation or unemployment alleviation, and food security and sustainable food systems.
Document Title: Egypt's Sovereign Sustainable Financing Framework

Family Name: National Plan for Mitigation and Adaptation to Climate Change
Family Summary: This plan lays out the measures and instruments to achieve national mitigation and adaptation targets set out in the country’s NDC and Law 27520 on Minimum Budgets for Adaptation and Mitigation to Global Climate Change. The primary mitigation target is for Argentina not to exceed 349 MtCO2e Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions until 2030 across all sectors. The primary adaptation target is to strengthen resilience and contribute to capacity building to reduce climate change vulnerability, accounting for gender equality. The Plan’s six strategic lines include energy transition, productive transition, sustainable mobility, sustainable and resilient territories, conservation of biodiversity and common goods, and sustainable management of food and systems.

Family Name: Framework for Climate Adaptive Buildings
Family Summary:
The Framework for Climate Adaptive Buildings has been developed by the Dutch Green Building Council (DGBC), in collaboration with more than 40 parties, and is meant for parties operating in the real estate sector: real estate parties, financiers, housing corporations and government authorities. This standard methodology enables the identification of the biggest physical climate risks within a portfolio. It can also be used to report on alignment with the EU Taxonomy relating to climate goal 2: climate adaptation. The methodology has been set up based on open climate data and is transparent on the methods used. The goal is to assess the climate impacts at the building level as accurately as possible. The methodology comprises three steps:

Part 1: Assessing the climate impacts for the area surrounding a building (the building environment score)

Part 2: Determining the building-specific vulnerability (the building score)

Part 3: Deciding on measures at the area and building levels (the adaptation strategy)
Document Title: Framework for Climate Adaptive Buildings (Part 3 - Adaptation Strategy)

Family Name: National Energy Transition Framework (2022-2070)
Family Summary:
This Framework is aimed at decarbonising the energy sector and is a long-term net-zero framework, expected to complement existing efforts with new measures, such as increased renewable energy penetration, conversion of thermal plants to natural gas and the integration of nuclear power into the energy mix. Ghana is determined to extract critical (green) minerals, including lithium and graphite, to make efficient use of them and establish Ghana as a hub for electric vehicles and the production of battery technologies.

Ghana will establish the National Energy Transition Implementation Committee, and set up the National Energy Transition Coordinating Office to drive the implementation of this framework, with participation by the key institutions including the Ministry of Energy, Ministry of Transport, and Ministry of Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation.

This Framework covers the electricity, petroleum, transport and critical minerals sectors, national greenhouse gas emissions, energy demand and production, economic, social and envrionmental imapcts, and cost and investment requirements.
Document Title: National Energy Transition Framework (2022-2070) - Abridged Version

Family Name: Energy Strategy 2030 & Vision 2050
Family Summary:
The Energy Strategy outlines the goals for the period of 2021 - 2030, the measures that are required to advance energy efficiency and the expansion of renewable energies. It also sets out a vision to 2050. 

The Energy Strategy 2030 sets out the following goals:
  • 20% reduction of energy demand with a 2008 baseline;
  • 30% renewable energies (17% produced domestically); and
  • 40% reduction of CO2 emissions (30% reduction of CO2 emissions domestically with a baseline of 1990; additional 10 % reduction of CO2 emissions through international market mechanisms).

Measures to increase energy efficiency (a central element of the Energy Strategy 2030), include building renovations and efficient new buildings, but also efficiency improvements in lighting, appliances and industrial plants. Further, the substitution of fossil energy sources, through electric heat pumps and the electrification of transport are expected to make important contributions to energy efficiency. 

The Energy Vision 2050 sets out the following goals:
  • 40% reduction of energy demand with a 2008 baseline;
  • 100% renewable energies; and
  • 100% reduction of CO2 emissions.

These goals imply a complete phaseout of fossil fuels in the transportation and buildings sectors.

The most important measures of the Energy Strategy 2030 are:
  • Sensitise population and stakeholders;
  • Tripple the currently installed photovoltaic capacity (+ 5 MWp/year);
  • Use sustainable biomass potential;
  • Increase the use of district heating from waste incineration plants by around 21 GWh/a;
  • Replace 75% of oil heating with renewable energies, heat pumps or district heating;
  • Introduce stricter energy standards for buildings to implement EU rules;
  • Implement provisions regarding large consumers and voluntary target agreements in the industry;
  • Create framework conditions for electric or renewable drives in the transport sector and transform public transport to renewable drive systems;
  • Improve the conditions for public transport and non-motorised transport; and
  • Support innovative projects.
Document Title: Energy Strategy 2030 & Vision 2050

Family Name: Climate Strategy 2050
Family Summary:
This document sets out Liechtenstein's climate strategy to 2050. This includes:

  • Reaching net zero by 2050;
  • By 2030, 50% GHG emissions reduction compared to 1990 levels. 40% are to be reduced domestically, 10% abroad; and
  • By 2050, reduce domestic emissions by 90% compared to 1990 levels. The remaining 10% are to be compensated.

The Strategy prioritises the energy sector. Compared to 1990 levels, emissions must be reduced by 50% by 2030, and completely by 2050. 

For the compensation of remaining emissions, the Strategy mentions carbon sinks such as forests and moors. It further announces monitoring the development of negative emissions technologies.

Lastly, the Strategy touches on emissions abroad which are to be reduced as well.
Document Title: Climate Strategy 2050

Family Name: Program for the Development of Electric Transport in the Republic of Tajikistan for 2023-2028
Family Summary: The program for the Development of Electric Transport in the Republic of Tajikistan for 2023-2028 aims to promote and support growth in electric vehicle use. It promotes the buildout of charging infrastructure and battery-scrapping technology, and eventually full domestic manufacturing of electric vehicles and their parts. To improve awareness of electric vehicles, it plans to issue green license plates.

Family Name: Common Agricultural Policy Strategic Plan 2023-2027
Family Summary:
Sweden’s strategy aims to increase the productivity, viability and competitiveness of the agricultural sector while protecting animal welfare and seeking increased ambition in environmental and climate standards. Increasing food production is another priority. The strategy also aims to contribute to the development of Sweden’s rural areas, to help ensure that these are attractive places to live and work in.

Farmers or other land managers may receive support for managing pastures and meadows to preserve and enhance their natural and cultural environmental values, with the aim of maintaining over 420 000 hectares annually.

Family Name: Forest Strategy 2050
Family Summary:
The Forest Strategy 2050 aims at adapting forests to climate change, climate protection, sustainable timber production and use, biodiversity and forest nature conservation, recreational use, and support for forest owners. The Strategy is guided by a vision for 2050 and sets out various milestones until 2030.


The milestones in furtherance of climate protection and climate adaptation by 2030 are as follows:


  • The climate protection contribution of forest and wood is maintained and expanded;
  • The use of wood from domestic forestry is expanded;
  • Establish a model for the remuneration of climate protection services;
  • Wind turbines in the forest contribute to the energy supply;
  • Implement action plans for the adaptation of forests;
  • Strengthen forest conversion;
  • Support measures for the adaptation of forests and for forest conversion; and
  • Establish monitoring of climate change.
Document Title: Forest Strategy 2050

Family Name: Strategy for Technology Innovation for Carbon Neutrality
Family Summary:
The Strategy for Technology Innovation for Carbon Neutrality sets out priority areas and technologies for achieving carbon neutrality. Support throughout the entire cycle has been strengthened to promote public and private technology development and investment. For GHG mitigation, the focus is particularly on developing innovative technologies that realise low-carbon transition in carbon-intensive and hard-to-abate industries.

The strategies cover strategies to develop the 10 key innovation technologies that can play a critical role in achieving carbon neutrality: ① Solar and Wind Power, ② Hydrogen, ③ Bioenergy, ④ Steel and Cement, ⑤ Petrochemical, ⑥ Industrial Process Advancement, ⑦ Transport Efficiency, ⑧ Building Efficiency, ⑨ Digitization, and ⑩ CCUS.
Document Title: Strategy for Technology Innovation for Carbon Neutrality

Family Name: Strategy for the transition to a circular economy 2022-2027
Family Summary: The Strategy for Circular Economy sets out Bulgaria’s framework for transitioning from a linear to a resource-efficient and low-waste economic model. It promotes waste prevention, reuse, recycling, and sustainable product design, with the aim of reducing resource consumption, environmental pressures, and greenhouse gas emissions. The strategy supports innovation, circular business models, and improved waste management, while aligning national policies with EU circular economy objectives, climate goals, and sustainable development priorities. It also encourages cross-sectoral cooperation and investment to increase competitiveness and resilience of the Bulgarian economy.
Document Title: Strategy for the transition to a circular economy 2022-2027

Family Name: Flood Risk Management Plan (PZRP): River basin: Odry
Family Summary:
Directive 2007/60/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2007 on the assessment and management of flood risks (Floods Directive) requires, among other things, the preparation of flood risk management plans. The President of the National Water Management Authority is responsible for developing flood risk management plans in accordance with the Water Law Act.

The Flood Risk Management Plan (PZRP) encompasses all elements of flood risk management, with particular emphasis on flood prevention and protection measures, as well as information on the state of preparedness in the event of a flood. Pursuant to the Water Law Act, flood protection is implemented in a manner that ensures coordination with activities aimed at achieving environmental and water protection objectives. Flood Risk Management Plans (PZRP) were developed for 6 river basins.

The Regulation of the Council of Ministers of 18 October 2016 adopted the Flood Risk Management Plan for the Odra River Basin District in line with the Water Act of 18 July 2001, which was later replaced by the Regulation of the Minister of Infrastructure of 26 October 2022 on the adoption of the Flood Risk Management Plan for the Odra River Basin District, which entered into force in 22.03.2023, now in line with the Water Act of 20 July 2017 that superseded the former.
Document Title: Flood Risk Management Plan (PZRP)

Family Name: Singapore's National Hydrogen Strategy
Family Summary: This Strategy sets out Singapore's plan for hydrogen deployment and infrastructure development in line with technological and global progress, with Singapore believing that low-carbon hydrogen has the potential to be a major decarbonisation pathway to support its transition towards net zero by 2050. The report sets out five key areas: 1) Experiment with the use of advanced hydrogen technologies at the cusp of commercial readiness through pathfinder projects; 2) Invest in research and development to unlock technological bottlenecks; 3) Pursue international collaborations to enable supply chains for low-carbon hydrogen; 4) Undertake long-term land and infrastructure planning; and 5) Support workforce training and development of our broader hydrogen economy.
Document Title: National Hydrogen Strategy

Family Name: Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No. 675/2022 on GHG inventory, projections and adaptation to climate change reporting system
Family Summary:
‘Regulation No. 675 defines the procedures for creating and maintaining the National Greenhouse Gas Inventory System and the Forecasting System. It outlines the specific responsibilities of various institutions in gathering activity data and emission factors. Its aim is to ensure that all data regarding pollution, carbon capture, and future forecasts are accurate, transparent, and compliant with international treaty obligations by outlining:

  1. the procedure for the establishment and maintenance of a national system for the preparation of an inventory of greenhouse gases;
  2. the procedures for the establishment and maintenance of the national greenhouse gas forecasting system; and
  3. the procedures for establishing and maintaining a national system for reporting on adaptation to climate change.
Document Title: Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No. 675/2022 ‘GHG inventory, projections and adaptation to climate change reporting system’

Family Name: Regulation 673/2022 on the Implementing Rules of the Latvia’s Plan of the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility
Family Summary: Regulation 673/2022 on the Implementing Rules of the Latvia’s Plan of the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility, the Third Component “Reducing inequalities", the reform No 3.1 “Regional policy”, the investment No 3.1.1.6.i for the “Purchase of zero-emission vehicles for implementation of municipal functions and provision of municipal services” sets out detailed rules for administering and financing Latvia’s programme to promote the acquisition of zero-emission vehicles (especially electric buses and charging infrastructure) by municipalities and other public sector entities as part of the implementation of the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) measures focused on climate and environmental improvements in transport. The available grant for this investment is 8,799,261 EUR. It defines eligibility criteria, application and implementation procedures, and how support is provided for procuring electric buses and associated infrastructure with the aim of reducing transport sector greenhouse gas emissions, accelerating the shift away from fossil fuels, and modernising public transport fleets in line with Latvia’s climate and energy targets.
Document Title: Regulation 673/2022 - Implementing Rules of the Latvia’s Plan of the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility, the Third Component “Reducing inequalities", the reform No 3.1 “Regional policy”, the investment No 3.1.1.6.i for the “Purchase of zero-emission vehicles for implementation of municipal functions and provision of municipal services”

Family Name: Regulation 21/2022 on Guidelines for Implementing the Carbon Economic Value
Family Summary:
In order to support the achievement of Indonesia’s NDC greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction targets and to implement the provisions of Presidential Regulation Number 98 of 2021 on the Implementation of Carbon Pricing to Achieve the Nationally Determined Contribution Target and Control Over Greenhouse Gas Emissions in National Development, this Regulation introduces the procedure for implementing carbon pricing in Indonesia. Carbon pricing applies to the following sectors: energy; waster; industrial processes and product uses; agriculture; forestry; and other sectors in accordance with developments in science and technology. The implementation of the carbon pricing is carried out through the following mechanisms: carbon trading; result-based payments; and carbon levies, as well as other mechanisms that accord with developments in science and technology. Carbon trading may be carried out through domestic and international trading procedures. The Regulation sets out the provisions of a Carbon Trading Roadmap, which carbon trading activities must comply with, and establishes the rules for offsetting GHG emissions from activities that are either uncapped or do not meet the sectoral GHG Emission Baseline.

The Regulation further outlines the procedures for Result-Based Payments and the Carbon Levy.
Document Title: Regulation 21/2022

Family Name: National disaster risk reduction and management plan 2020-2030
Family Summary: The Updated National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Plan (NDRRMP) establishes the linkage between disaster risk reduction and management (DRRM), climate change adaptation (CCA), and human security by focusing on climate and disaster risks. It aims to achieve the shared goals of Ambisyon Natin 2040, NDRRMP, National Climate Change Action Plan (NCCAP), and National Security Strategy (NSS) in risk reduction, resilience building, human security, and sustainable development.The Updated NDRRMP intends to:provide strategic direction and guidance to national government agencies (NGAs), local government units (LGUs), civil society organizations (CSOs), private sector, and development partners on disaster and climate-resilience actions in the Philippines;strengthen disaster and climate risk governance by clarifying the roles, accountabilities, strategies, and activities of disaster risk reduction and management (DRRM) stakeholders at all levels;strengthen linkages and interoperability of the DRRM thematic pillars;ensure the convergence of and synergy between DRRM and CCA; and,contribute to the achievement and coherence of global, regional, and national development and policy agenda.
Document Title: National disaster risk reduction and management plan 2020-2030

Family Name: France Nation Verte: Ecological Plan
Family Summary:
This document details how the concept of ecological planning, promoted by the government, should 1) enable green objectives to be declined sector by sector and territory by territory, 2) define specific actions, and 3) provide the means to reach the objectives. The five core goals that organise the document are the following:

  • Reduce greenhouse gas emissions and limit the effects of climate change;
  • Adapt to the inevitable consequences of climate change;
  • Restore biodiversity;
  • Reduce the exploitation of  natural resources to a sustainable rate;
  • Reduce all pollution that affects health.

Seven transversal projects are launched in parallel:
  • Funding that makes it possible to define credible and coherent investment trajectories
  • Territorial planning and differentiation according to the characteristics and specificities of each territory, including overseas territories
  • The transition of sectors with the management of jobs, training and skills
  • Environmental data
  • Exemplary public services
  • Just transition and accompanying measures, to leave no one behind
  • The sobriety of uses and resources.

The General Secretariat to Ecological Planning (SGPE) is created and placed under the authority of the Prime Minister.
Document Title: France Nation Verte: Ecological Plan

Family Name: Disaster Risk Management Strategy until 2030
Family Summary: Croatia's Disaster Risk Management Strategy aims to guide a proactive, comprehensive and sustainable programme of disaster risk management up to the year 2030. The strategy acknowledges climate change as a major threat to national economic development and wellbeing, and promotes a range of mitigation and adaptation considerations to reduce disaster risk. It calls for general capacity building and data/stakeholder co-ordination, enabling stronger implementation of a range of existing sectoral-level measures, such as those to reduce wildfire and flood risk. Early warning systems and risk mapping are strongly emphasised and for other hazards such as drought, the strategy promotes further research and development of new risk reduction measures, such as the breeding of more resilient crops.
Document Title: Disaster Risk Management Strategy until 2030

The commitment to retain the net zero target for 2045 remains.
