It amends a range of existing documents. Climate-related clauses include:

Article 22 amends corporation tax law 27/2014 to integrate a freedom of amortisation in investments that use energy from renewable sources.
Chapter VIII introduces  measures regarding the remuneration of public sector personnel and the protection of temporary agricultural workers affected by the drought.
Article 20 on saving and energy efficiency in outdoor lighting introduces changes to technical requirements for such devices. these include the introduction of an energy efficiency label that notably accounts for predicted annual carbon dioxide emissions.

Family Summary:
This Climate Change Policy, which is part of the broader Environmental and Social RiskManagement (ESRM) Policy Framework, establishes the principles and commitments that guide Export Development Canada's (EDC’s) approach to climate-change related risks and opportunities.

EDC can support Canadian businesses to become internationally recognized as leaders in sustainableand responsible business. Climate change presents real risks and opportunities that EDC and these businesses must identify, manage and mitigate as appropriate.

The Policy also states that from 13 October 2022, the EDC no longer provides new financing for the development, construction or expansion of unabated coal-fired power plants (CFPPs) regardless of geographic location.
Document Title: Export Development Canada's Climate Change Policy (Version 3.0)

Family Name: Order TED/989/2022 on the remuneration of energy production from renewable energy sources, cogeneration and waste
Family Summary: The object of this order is the establishment of new standard facilities in order to accommodate the facilities to which the maintenance of the remuneration established in Order TED/171/2020, of February 24, which updates the parameters, is applicable. remuneration of the standard installations applicable to certain installations for the production of electricity from renewable energy sources, cogeneration and waste, for the purposes of its application to the regulatory period that begins on January 1, 2020, in accordance with the application of the provisions of article 4 of Order TED/260/2021, of March 18, which adopts accompanying measures for facilities whose operating costs depend essentially on the price of fuel during the period of validity of the state of alarm due to the health crisis situation caused by COVID-19.

Family Name: Royal Decree 854/2022 creating the National Irrigation Board and the Irrigation Sustainability Observatory.
Family Summary: The purpose of this royal decree is to create and regulate the National Irrigation Board as a body for cooperation, communication and participation between the different competent administrations in matters of agriculture and the application of water in irrigation, and other parties interested in irrigation management, which facilitate its governance. Likewise, its composition, functions and operating regime are determined. In order to provide relevant information on the sustainability of irrigation to the different competent public administrations in this matter, to the rest of the interested parties, to the citizenry and to the National Irrigation Board itself, the Irrigation Sustainability Observatory is created. The functions of the National Irrigation Board and the functionalities of the Irrigation Sustainability Observatory will serve in the field of irrigation and related activities. The activities of the Board and the Observatory will in any case respect the competences of other departments in matters of the environment, energy and water, in particular with regard to hydrological planning and the activity of the National Water Council.Article 3.d states that the National Board of Irrigation will be in charge of developing studies and technical works related to irrigation, in particular, with regard to adaptation to climate change scenarios with less availability of water resources.
Document Title: Royal Decree 854/2022 creating the National Irrigation Board and the Irrigation Sustainability Observatory.

Family Name: The Netherlands' Global Climate Strategy (Internationale Klimaatstrategie)
Family Summary:
This is the first “whole-of-government” Global Climate Strategy that describes how the Netherlands wants to strengthen their response to the challenges that climate change poses, both domestically and globally. It's centred around four topics: 1) adaptation 2) mitigation 3) finance 4) loss and damage.

Adaptation: In order to reduce climate change vulnerability worldwide the Netherlands will

  • Double their adaptation finance (in line with the Glasgow Climate Pact)
  • Co-host the UN 2023 Water Conference
  • Provide an additional EUR 250 million until 2025 to increase accessibility to food in regions that are climate-vulnerable
  • Share Dutch knowledge and expertise on water management, the adaptation policy cycle, and smarter food production

Mitigation: Centred around helping the acceleration to a net-zero circular economy by 2050 globally

  • Raising its national target for CO2 reduction to at least 55%, with policies focused on pursuing of 60% reduction 
  • Focus on partnerships with other countries to support net-zero ambitions
  • Speed up the transition to zero-emission mobility and transport
  • Cooperate with relevant actors (civil society, financial and knowledge institutions, environmental organisations etc)
  • Double the financial contribution to stopping deforestation

Finance

  • Increase climate finance with more than EUR 0.5 billion a year
  • Develop instruments to mobilise more private capital for climate action in developing countries
  • Partner for clean energy transition
  • Strengthen sustainable investment, fighting greenwashing, and enhance the transparency in climate risks and impact

Loss and damage

  • Increase the support to disaster risk management, with a special focus on universally available early warning systems and capacity to act
Document Title: The Netherlands’ Global Climate Strategy

Family Name: Energy sobriety plan
Family Summary:
This plan calls for a mobilisation of everyone to achieve substantial overall energy savings. It caps a range of plans and circulars that originated in early 2022 following the invasion of Ukraine and subsequent constraints on European energy supply. The broader French energy strategy, announced by the President of the Republic in February 2022, is based on four pillars: energy sobriety, energy efficiency, accelerating the development of renewable energies (EnR), and the revival of the French nuclear industry.

The energy sobriety plan concerns different sectors and players, including in particular:
  • buildings (maximum temperature of 19°C in offices, 15-day delay in the start and end of the heating period, reduction in the use of domestic hot water in offices);
  • transport (privileged use of bicycles, public transport or carpooling);
  • the State (heating at 18°C ​​and work in staggered hours on days of high voltage on the electricity network, incentive to work from home in order to reduce fuel consumption, speed limit of 110 km/h on motorways for agents employing their service vehicle during non-urgent business trips, reduction of energy consumption of digital origin, etc.);
  • local authorities (reduction in electricity consumption linked to public lighting, limitation of the heating of sports equipment and reduction in the number of heated square meters by grouping public services in more suitable premises);
  • companies (switching off the interior lighting of buildings when the premises are unoccupied and reduction of exterior lighting, in particular advertising, control of heating, air conditioning and ventilation, elimination of unnecessary travel, etc.);
  • individuals (implementation of a sobriety bonus for households controlling their energy consumption, aid to switch from a gas boiler to a heat pump in individual housing, improvement of information for the French on the "weather of the 'electricity' via the Ecowatt signal(new window));
  • sport (reduction of lighting time before and after matches, reduction of heating in gymnasiums, reduction of water temperature in swimming pools, etc.);
  • culture (limiting the energy footprint of cinemas, etc.).
Document Title: Energy sobriety plan

Family Name: Decree No. 2022-1295 relating to the obligation to close the openings of buildings or parts of buildings for tertiary use, heated or cooled
Family Summary:
This decree amends the Code of Construction and Housing to introduce the following clauses:

" Art. R. 175-7.-I.- The openings of any building, or part of a building, in which market or non-market tertiary activities are carried out, including that belonging to a natural or legal person in the primary or secondary sector, heated or cooled using one or more heating or air conditioning systems, within the meaning of Article R. 175-1, overlooking outdoor spaces or an unheated or cooled part of the building, are equipped with manual or automatic closing systems limiting heat loss.
“II.- When one or more of these heating or air conditioning systems are in operation, these closing systems must not, under normal operating conditions, be kept open by the operator of the building or part of the building concerned. , including during opening hours for users.
“This provision does not apply when indoor air renewal requirements require it in order to prevent the risks mentioned in Article L. 153-2 or when the recommendations of the health authorities recommend it.
Document Title: Decree No. 2022-1295 relating to the obligation to close the openings of buildings or parts of buildings for tertiary use, heated or cooled

Family Name: Order granting market premiums under the Renewable Energy Expansion Act (EAG-Marktprämienverordnung 2022-EAG-MPV 2022)
Family Summary: With Austria’s goal to have electricity consumption covered 100% by renewable energy sources from 2030 onwards, an important element of promoting the electricity generation from renewable sources is the market premium. Under the Renewable Energy Expansion Act, this decree lays down more detailed provisions on the granting of these market premiums. Instead of the previously fixed feed-in tariffs for renewable electricity, the market premium subsidy subsidises the difference between the market revenue from direct marketing, and the production costs. These premiums are centred around promoting electricity generation from biomass, biogas, photovoltaics (PV), wind power, wind power, and hydropower.
Document Title: Market Premium Order

Family Name: National Strategy of Forests 2030
Family Summary:
The objectives include promoting a sustainable circular forest bioeconomy through long-lasting wood products, where the forest sector contributes to Romania's climate neutrality objectives by improving the use of wood and wood products, to stimulate the growth of absorbed CO2 stocks and reduce emissions.

Another objective is to protect, restore and expand forests in Romania, to have stable forests in the context of climate change, with rich biodiversity and a greater share in the surface area of ​​Romania,
Document Title: National Strategy of Forests 2030

Family Name: Decree No. 2022-1289 relating to the information of buyers and tenants on risks
Family Summary:
This decree makes it mandatory for the seller or lessor of real estate affected by one or more natural or technological risks or by a soil information sector to inform the potential buyer or tenant at each stage of the sale or of the rental, and this from the real estate announcement. The text specifies the content of the document stating these risks or describing the soil information sector and the conditions under which it must be given to the potential buyer or tenant in order to ensure that he is properly informed.

The risks on which information must be provided include natural disasters and the phenomenon of coast withdrawal.
Document Title: Decree No. 2022-1289 relating to the information of buyers and tenants on risks

Family Name: Implementation Strategy for the National Environmental Policy 2022 -2032
Family Summary:
The main goal of the Strategy is to provide policy guidance and oversight on environmental management for sustainable socio-economic development in Tanzania. It’s objective is to establish a national framework for guiding harmonised and coordinated environmental management to improve welfare of present and future generations. In terms of climate change, it seeks to strengthen the national capacity for addressing climate change impacts. The strategies identified to achieve this climate goal include:

  • Developing and implementing programmes to enhance national capacity on climate change adaptation and mitigation;
  • Developing and implementing mechanisms for strengthening mainstreaming of climate change in national development plans and sectoral policies;
  • Creating programmes for collaboration implement between Government and private sector in climate change adaptation and mitigation;
  • Developing and implementing programmes for raising public awareness on climate change issues;
  • Enhancing regional and international cooperation on addressing climate change;
  • Formulating and implementing programmes for promotion of development and transfer of green affordable technologies.
Document Title: Implementation Strategy for the National Environmental Policy 2022 -2032

Family Name: National Adaptation Plan of Bangladesh (2023-2050)
Family Summary:
The National Adaptation Plan (NAP) of Bangladesh (2023–2050) presents a long-term vision for enhancing climate resilience across all sectors of the economy. It outlines priority actions to reduce climate vulnerabilities, protect ecosystems, and assist communities in adapting to the impacts of climate change. The overall goal of the plan is to build a climate-resilient nation through effective adaptation strategies that foster a strong society, support ecosystems, and promote sustainable economic growth. The NAP integrates adaptation measures into national planning processes and encourages sustainable practices to protect essential sectors, including agriculture, water resources, health, and infrastructure. The following goals are established:

1. Ensure protection against climate change variability and induced natural disasters.

2. Develop climate-resilient agriculture to secure food, nutrition, and livelihoods.

3. Create climate-smart cities to enhance the urban environment and overall well-being.

4. Promote nature-based solutions for the conservation of forestry, biodiversity, and community well-being.

5. Strengthen governance by integrating adaptation strategies into planning processes.

6. Foster transformative capacity-building and innovation for climate change adaptation.

The principles guiding the NAP include: recognizing that priority sectors are interconnected and require a multidisciplinary approach; ensuring that the NAP process is driven by the country’s needs and is participatory, inclusive, and gender-sensitive; promoting nature-based solutions; engaging the private sector; and maintaining financial integrity through effective monitoring, evaluation, and learning.
Document Title: National Adaptation Plan of Bangladesh (2023-2050)

Family Name: Plan +SE, Plan for more energy security
Family Summary: The Plan +SE (Plan Más Seguridad Energética) is an initiative designed to enhance energy security amidst rising geopolitical tensions and market volatility. It aims to protect vulnerable consumers, strengthen strategic energy autonomy, and foster solidarity with other EU member states. The plan focuses on both immediate actions for the 2022/2023 winter and long-term structural improvements. Key measures include accelerating the consideration of climate change, the transition to renewable energy sources, promoting energy efficiency, and supporting consumers. The plan emphasises collaboration with stakeholders, including social agents, industry representatives, and government entities. It also aligns with the EU's Fit for 55 package and the RePowerEU plan, aiming to increase renewable energy targets and promote a more sustainable energy future. The Plan +SE is a dynamic document that will adapt to the evolving energy landscape and ensure Spain's energy security in the face of global challenges.
Document Title: Plan +SE, Plan for more energy security

Family Name: National Strategy for Digital Agriculture in Niger and its Action Plan (2023-2027)
Family Summary:
The National Strategy for Digital Agriculture in Niger (2023–2035) aims to harness digital technologies to strengthen food security and rural livelihoods through a sustainable transformation of the agricultural sector. Its vision emphasizes climate-resilient agriculture by ensuring the sustainable use of rural ecosystems, supporting efficient production systems, improving value chains, and expanding access to diversified food products. The strategy identifies four overarching objectives that align with Niger’s broader development agenda: sustainable management of agricultural ecosystems, improved agronomic and environmental performance of farms, stronger agricultural value chains, and increased use of digital services by rural communities.

To achieve these goals, the 2023–2027 Action Plan outlines six priority areas, many of which directly address climate change adaptation and resilience. These include deploying digital tools for preserving ecosystems, biodiversity, soils, and water resources; supporting secure land and pastoral management in the context of growing pressures on natural resources; and promoting efficient, climate-smart production systems that strengthen food and nutrition security. The plan also emphasises building rural actors’ digital skills, improving access to information and services, and enhancing market opportunities. Overall, this strategy will reinforce the country's capacity to adapt to climate change while fostering inclusive rural development.
Document Title: National Strategy for Digital Agriculture and its Action Plan (2023-2027)

Family Name: Australian Disaster Recovery Framework
Family Summary:
This Framework supports the recovery efforts of Australia's governments and recovery partners. It helps them work effectively individually, and together.

The Framework provides a common understanding of Australia’s approach to Disaster Recovery. It gives general guidance on recovery for planners and practitioners. It also describes mechanisms for coordination and collaboration between recovery stakeholders.

During events of nationally significant harm, it provides links to:

  • Legislation
  • Arrangements
  • Practice for recovery

Each of our state and territories have their own disaster recovery policies. This is because large-scale disasters often happen across different states at the same time. The ADRF provides a common understanding of the approach to disaster recovery.This video The three key area of the Framework are:

  1. Framework purpose and essential context;
  2. Recovery governance; and
  3. Recovery doctrine and policy.
Document Title: Australian Disaster Recovery Framework

Family Name: A roadmap for multi-hazard, impact-based early warning 2023-2030
Family Summary: Ethiopia’s early warning systems, developed over a 50-year span, faced challenges such as fragmentation, inadequate funding, and a lack of proactive measures. The focus on crisis management, rather than anticipatory actions, led to inefficient resource allocation. To address these issues, the Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission (EDRMC) and stakeholders propose transforming the early warning system into a comprehensive Multi-Hazard, Impact-Based Early Warning and Early Action System (MH-IB-EW-EAS).This integrated approach encompasses hazard monitoring, forecasting, risk assessment, communication, and preparedness. Aligned with the Sendai Framework’s four pathways - disaster risk knowledge; monitoring, observation, and forecasting; warning communication; and early action and response – the MH-IB-EW-EAS aims to foster resilient communities through proactive measures and effective response strategies. The implementation of the roadmap requires the participation and contribution of multiple stakeholders from the federal to the community level.
Document Title: A roadmap for multi-hazard, impact-based early warning 2023-2030

Family Name: Decree No. 2022-1282 on renewable energies in the transport sector, transposing Directive 2018/2001/EC
Family Summary:
This decree was issued for the application of Article 9 of Ordinance No. 2021-236 of March 3, 2021 transposing Directive 2018/2001/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of December 11, 2018 in the field of renewable energies in the transport sector. 

The energy code sets a 2030 target of 15% renewable energy in final energy consumption in the transport sector and an advanced biofuels and biogas target of 3.5%. Only biofuels, bioliquids and fuels or fuels derived from biomass that meet criteria that comply with the requirements of sustainable development, referred to as "criteria for sustainability and the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions", may be taken into account for assess compliance with these objectives. This decree specifies the methods for calculating these objectives.
Document Title: Decree No. 2022-1282 on renewable energies in the transport sector, transposing Directive 2018/2001/EC

Family Summary: The PDP outlines a comprehensive long-term plan for Cambodia's power sector that includes forecasts of demand, expansion of generation, and a plan for transmission and distribution from 2022 until 2040. The plan will oversee a rapid expansion of renewable energy resources.
Document Title: Power Development Master Plan 2022-2040

Family Name: Charging and Hydrogen Refuelling Infrastructure Initiative
Family Summary:
This Initiative is by the Canada Infrastructure Bank (CIB), whose mandate under the CIB Act is to invest and attract investment to support conditions that foster economic growth or contribute to the sustainability of infrastructure in Canada. This Initiative aims to reduce transportation sector emissions by accelerating the private sector’s rollout of large-scale ZEV chargers and hydrogen refuelling stations, helping to spur the market for private investment. CIB provides financing to the private sector to share in charging and refuelling infrastructure use risk by aligning repayment with use levels. If network use does not reach agreed levels, the required repayments will be proportionally lower. Conversely, in circumstances where use levels exceed expectations, the CIB’s return will increase proportionally. This financing structure addresses the uncertainty of ZEV adoption rates faced by developers and investors, so they can confidently invest in charging and refuelling infrastructure.

Through this initiative, the CIB has dedicated a minimum of $500 million to support the federal government’s goals as part of Canada’s 2030 Emissions Reduction Plan.
Document Title: Charging and Hydrogen Refuelling Infrastructure Initiative

Family Name: Guiding Opinion on Accelerating the Green and Intelligent Development of Inland River Vessels
Family Summary: To achieve carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, the Opinion aims to actively promote the adoption of new energy and clean energy vessels, encourage the development of vessels powered by LNG and batteries, foster the use of shore power for vessels docking in key regions such as the Yangtze River Economic Belt, accelerate the retrofits of shore power receiving facilities for vessels on the Yangtze River, and significantly increase the use of shore power.
Document Title: Guiding Opinion on Accelerating the Green and Intelligent Development of Inland River Vessels

Family Name: Protected Area Management Strategy 2022-2030
Family Summary:
This Strategy provides a clear roadmap to move ahead, creating climate-resilient ecosystems and self-sustaining protected area management in Nepal by 2030. The guiding principles of this strategy are as follows:

  • Species-focused ecosystem approach
  • Climate resilient and adaptive management
  • Human-wildlife coexistence
  • Balancing conservation and development needs
  • Zero tolerance on wildlife crime
  • Inclusive and good governance
  • Sustainable financing mechanism
  • Towards carbon neutrality.

Climate-related actions include:

  • Establish hydro-meteorological stations to monitor impacts of climate-induced risks
  • Develop an early warning system in each protected area, prepare a disaster risk reduction plan, and create climate refugia
  • Generate information on climatic variables, climate change impacts, risks, and vulnerabilities for integration in PA management
  • Collaborate with academic and research institutions and conservation partners
  • Develop climate smart species conservation action plans
  • Conduct periodic carbon inventory and designate carbon neutral protected areas
  • Develop climate smart protected area infrastructures, including all weather roads
Document Title: Protected Area Management Strategy 2022-2030

Family Name: Canada’s Methane Strategy
Family Summary:
As a signatory of the Global Methane Pledge, Canada has committed to reduce human-caused methane emissions across its economic sectors by at least 30% from 2020 levels by 2030. As part of this commitment, the Canadian government has produced this methane strategy which outlines the country’s plans for reducing methane emissions. These plans include improvements in monitoring methane emissions in the atmosphere, as well as mitigation specific measures in three key methane-producing sectors: oil and gas, landfills and waste, and agriculture.

Proposed mitigation measures include:

1.      strengthening methane regulations to achieve at least a 75% reduction of oil and gas methane emissions by 2030 from 2012 levels (set to be published in 2023);

2.      developing new technologies to reduce methane emissions through electrification, fuel switching, improvements to efficiency, and mitigating fugitive emissions;

3.      improving leak detection and repair processes and deploying gas capture technologies to reduce direct release into the atmosphere;

4.      developing new regulations to increase the recovery and destruction of methane from large municipal solid waste landfills by approximately 50% by 2030 from 2019 levels;

5.      working with provinces and territories to support and accelerate resource and energy recovery efforts for biodegradable waste;

6.      creating the On-Farm Climate Action Fund (OFCAF) as part of the Agricultural Climate Solutions programme, which will provide $670m in funding to support immediate on-farm action to tackle climate change, including methane-reducing measures;

7.      developing the Agricultural Clean Technology (ACT) programme to support the development and adoption of clean technologies in agriculture;

8.      developing a Livestock Feed Management protocol to use in Canada’s Greenhouse Gas Offset Credit System.
Document Title: Canada's Methane Strategy 2022

Family Name: National Energy Policy 2022-2040
Family Summary:
The Vision for the Policy is as follows:

• New areas of economic growth and employment related to energy, built on long-term competitive advantage.• Equitable and fair distribution of benefits and costs from energy transition.• Captures economic benefit and remains globally competitive by keeping pace with energy transition trends.• Affordable and reliable access to energy.• A leader in environmental sustainability and the green economy in ASEAN.• Continuous efficient utilisation of energy and indigenous energy resources.• Contribute to fiscal and trade balance health.

To this end, strategies and action plans have been built around optimising energy resources, stimulating growth and market opportunities, enhancing sustainability in the energy sector and ensuring energy security. Key actions include large-scale solar projects, increased use of biofuels, developing a hydrogen economy, promoting energy vehicles and continuing the development of petrochemical hubs in Sabah and Sarawak to improve and strengthen Malaysia's natural gas advantage.

The Policy also contains the Low Carbon Nation Aspiration 2040, which comprises targets in energy-related sectors such as transport, industrial, residential and commercial.
Document Title: National Energy Policy 2022-2040

Family Name: The Peat Use Reduction Strategy of the Federal Ministry of Food and Agriculture
Family Summary:
This Strategy recognises the potential of peatlands as carbon sinks and seeks to protect them. To this end, the aim is to reduce the use of peat in the commercial horticultural sector as far as possible by 2030. In the hobby sector, all use of peat is to be eliminated by 2026.


A central aspect of this Strategy is the development of alternatives to peat. The Strategy therefore outlines the support for farms which are converting to alternatives. The Strategy also outlines the establishment of service points which provide consultations during the conversion period.


The Strategy is in line with the National Peatland Strategy and the 2030 Climate Action Programme.
Document Title: Peat Use Reduction Strategy

Family Name: The Peat Use Reduction Strategy of the Federal Ministry of Food and Agriculture
Family Summary:
This Strategy recognises the potential of peatlands as carbon sinks and seeks to protect them. To this end, the aim is to reduce the use of peat in the commercial horticultural sector as far as possible by 2030. In the hobby sector, all use of peat is to be eliminated by 2026.


A central aspect of this Strategy is the development of alternatives to peat. The Strategy therefore outlines the support for farms which are converting to alternatives. The Strategy also outlines the establishment of service points which provide consultations during the conversion period.


The Strategy is in line with the National Peatland Strategy and the 2030 Climate Action Programme.
Document Title: Peat Use Reduction Strategy

Family Name: Fourth Comprehensive Plan for Climate Change Response in the Marine and Fisheries Sector
Family Summary:
The Plan contains short-term and specific implementation plans to establish a full-fledged carbon-neutrality implementation system. It proposes measures to minimise the impact of climate change experienced by the marine and fishery industry, coastal local residents, and marine ecosystems.

The key strategies and tasks are to reduce GHG emissions; expand blue carbon; establish a carbon-neutral shipping logistics network; and expand observation networks for abnormal monitoring in the waters near the Korean Peninsula and an early warning system for coastal disasters.
Document Title: Fourth Comprehensive Plan for Climate Change Response in the Marine and Fisheries Sector

Family Name: Executive Decree No. 22-322 on the administration of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (15 September 2022)
Family Summary:
Executive Decree No. 22-322 of 18 Safar 1444, corresponding to 15 September 2022, organises the central administration of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development. This Decree sets out that the Ministry is to propose all measures aimed at adapting crops and livestock farming to climate change in consultation with the relevant sectors, and to develop an outreach programme in this area, through its Directorate for the Development of Rural Territories and the Adaptation of Agriculture to Climate Change.

The Sub-Directorate for Irrigation and Adaptation of Climate Change is responsible for, inter alia, the establishment of a system to monitor climate change in agriculture; to participate, with the relevant sectors, in the development, implementation and evaluation of climate change adaptation programmes related to agriculture; and to initiate studies on the effects on climate change on agriculture.
Document Title: Executive Decree No. 22-322 on the administration of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (15 September 2022)

Family Name: National Disaster Risk Management Plan 2022-2030 (Plan Nacional de Gestión de Riesgo de Desastres 2022 - 2030)
Family Summary: The National Disaster Risk Management Plan 2022-2030 (PLANAGERD) establishes a comprehensive framework for reducing disaster risks in Peru, aligning with the Marco de Sendai 2015–2030 and the Act No. 29.664 (Ley N° 29664). It prioritises systemic risk reduction through six key objectives: (1) enhancing disaster risk understanding via integrated data systems and climate change considerations; (2) improving land use and occupation to mitigate vulnerabilities; (3) strengthening coordinated governance across sectors and levels of government; (4) integrating disaster risk into public and private investments; (5) ensuring timely and effective emergency response; and (6) promoting inclusive recovery for affected populations. The PLANAGERD underscores the critical role of data-driven risk assessment and interoperable digital platforms (e.g., SIGRID, GEOIDEP) to enhance preparedness and decision-making. It addresses vulnerabilities from informal land use and climate-driven disasters, advocating for sustainable infrastructure and resilient livelihoods. The plan also highlights the need to embed disaster risk management in public and private investments, ensuring that development projects avoid exacerbating risks.
Document Title: National Disaster Risk Management Plan - PLANAGERD 2022-2030 (Plan Nacional de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres - PLANAGERD 2022-2030)

Family Name: Canada's Aviation Climate Action Plan 2022-2030
Family Summary:
This Action Plan elaborates on following measures that are needed for the Canadian aviation sector to reach net-zero by 2050 (which has been termed a voluntary initiative):

1. Development and adoption of new green aerospace technology, including the gradual transition to new electric, hybrid and hydrogen propulsion;

2. improvement in ground and air operations;

3. the widespread availability and use of sustainable aviation fuels (SAF); and,

4. out-of-sector reductions (offsets to address residual emissions).
Document Title: Canada's Aviation Climate Action Plan 2022-2030

Family Name: Presidential Regulation No. 112 of 2022 on Accelerated Development of Renewable Energy for Electricity Supply
Family Summary:
On September 13, 2022, the President of the Republic of Indonesia issued the Presidential Regulation No. 112 of 2022 concerning the Acceleration of Development of Renewable Energy for Electric Power Supply (PR 112/2022). 


Key measures include:

  • Mandating the state’s electricity company to prioritise the purchase of electricity from power plants that utilise renewable energy sources. 
  • Allowing the state electricity company to implement more straightforward procurement processes when purchasing electricity from renewable energy power plants. 
  • Instructing the Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources to formulate a roadmap for the accelerated end date for coal-fired steam power plant operation.  
  • Banning any development of new coal-fired steam power plants unless it has been stipulated in the electricity supply business plan prior to the enactment of PR 112/2022, or if it meets set criteria (including being of strategic importance, and ceasing operation by 2050).
  • Enabling the government to grant incentives for development of renewable energy power plants.
Document Title: Presidential Regulation No. 112 of 2022 concerning the Acceleration of Development of Renewable Energy for Electric Power Supply

Family Name: Executive Decree No. 12 - National Environment Strategy 2021 -2031
Family Summary: This Decree approved the National Environmental Strategy 2021-203 (Environmental Management for the Restoration of Ecosystems and Sustainable and Inclusive Development). The main objective of the National Environmental Strategy is to outline the country's approach to addressing climate change through a comprehensive framework on environmental restoration and sustainable development. It aims to improve decision-making processes for environmental protection and conservation in the country, considering the environmental, social and economic challenges and opportunities at the national level and globally.
Document Title: Executive Decree No. 12 - National Environment Strategy 2021 -2031

Family Name: National Agricultural Development Policy 2022-2030
Family Summary: This Policy has the aim of transforming Cambodian agriculture into a modern, competitive, inclusive, climate-resilient and sustainable sector. It contains strategic actions under the theme of growing sustainably and increasing resilience to climate change which includes the forestry, fisheries and agricultural sectors.
Document Title: National Agricultural Development Policy 2022-2030

Family Name: National Clean Water Plan
Family Summary: Honduras' National Clean Water Plan aims to address issues with the sanitation and security of water supplies nationally, and notes climate change as a major national threat to health and wellbeing through extreme weather and its modulation of water availability. It primarily seeks to adapt to climate change through infrastructure expansion (water storage, surface water collection) and enhanced state capacity for hydrological predictions and water safety monitoring.
Document Title: National Clean Water Plan

Family Name: Opinion on Encouraging and Supporting Public Institutions to Adopt Energy Cost Management Services
Family Summary: This Opinion was issued, to promote the adoption of market-based approaches by public institutions at all levels to carry out green retrofits of existing buildings. This involves adopting energy cost custody as a form of contract energy management.
Document Title: Opinions on Encouraging and Supporting Public Institutions to Adopt Energy Cost Management Services

Family Name: Package of federal measures to secure an affordable energy supply and to increase income
Family Summary: In order to mitigate the financial impact of the sharp rise in energy costs on people and the economy, the federal government launched three relief packages with a total volume of around 95 billion euros to provide relief and social support. The third relief package was presented by the coalition parties on September 4. It includes short-term aid, housing benefit reforms, tax measures and structural changes to dampen energy price developments. A separate package of measures also supports companies that are affected by the sanctions or the war.The package has a component on the extension of the housing benefit entitlement, introduction of a heating cost and air conditioning, the planned increase in the CO2 price of five euros per ton and a nationwide public transport ticket was introduced to follow the time-limited 9-euro ticket . The responsibility for local public transport lies with the federal states and municipalities. These were all implemented and paid out between late 2022 and 2023.
Document Title: Package of federal measures to secure an affordable energy supply and to increase income

Family Name: Doctrine (Strategy) to Achieve Carbon Neutrality Until 2060
Family Summary:
This policy provides for the Strategy to achieve carbon neutrality by 2060 and has the following objectives:

  • Define goals and specific targets for the transition to climate neutrality by 2060;
  • Develop national priorities for GHG emissions reduction and increase carbon sequestration;
  • Identify key areas of technological development and specify infrastructure solutions needed to complete the transition to climate neutrality;
  • Describe key climate change mitigation policies to be developed and implemented in order to fulfil the objectives of this Strategy;
  • Assess investment and other financing needs to achieve climate goals;
  • Assess labour market implications of the transition;
  • Involve various stakeholders in the processes; and
  • Consider risks and impacts of climate change.
Document Title: Doctrine (Strategy) to Achieve Carbon Neutrality Until 2060

Family Name: Carbon Neutral Finland 2035: National Climate and Energy Strategy
Family Summary:
The primary goal of the strategy is to achieve carbon neutrality by 2035. It outlines the measures Finland will implement to meet the European Union’s climate commitments for 2030 and the targets set in the Climate Change Act, including a 60 percent reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 and achieving carbon neutrality by 2035.

The strategy addresses all greenhouse gas emissions across various sectors, including the emissions trading sector, the effort-sharing sector, and the land use sector. It also considers carbon sinks within the land use sector and other areas. The strategy encompasses the five dimensions of the EU’s Energy Union: decarbonisation of the economy, renewable energy, energy efficiency, internal energy market, energy security, and the promotion of research, innovation, and competitiveness.

Key provisions in the strategy include:

1. Utilising the emissions trading system as a key instrument to reduce emissions.

2. Integrating climate and energy policies to ensure a cohesive approach.

3. Involving various stakeholders, including businesses, communities, and government agencies, in the implementation of the strategy.

4. Establishing mechanisms for monitoring progress and reporting on the implementation of the strategy.

This strategy updated and strengthened Finland's energy and climate policy framework, reflecting the legally binding 2035 carbon-neutrality target, EU climate objectives and the need to accelerate the clean transition. It covers the energy, transport, buildings, industry, agriculture and land-use sectors and places particular emphasis on renewable energy, energy efficiency, electrification, energy security and reducing dependence on fossil fuels. The strategy also responds to the energy-market disruption caused by Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
Document Title: Carbon neutral Finland 2035 - national climate and energy strategy

Family Name: National Strategy for the Blue Economy
Family Summary:
This Strategy covers the management of the national maritime space and its resources and sustainable socio-economic development, creating the conditions for attracting public and private investment. It covers maritime and coastal activities, including fishing and aquaculture, maritime transport, port activities, coastal tourism, energy, shipbuilding and repair, seawater desalination, water treatment, non-economic telecommunications, including the protection of natural heritage, surveillance and monitoring of the marine and coastal environment, surveillance, control, and monitoring of marine activities, as well as scientific research.

This Strategy contains actions to respond to the climate challenge, in the marine areas and coastal infrastructures, and in reducing atmospheric emissions from maritime transport.
Document Title: National Strategy for the Blue Economy

Document Title: Government Action Plan for the Implementation of the President's Programme

Family Name: National Climate Change Policy of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan 2022-2050
Family Summary:
This policy sets out Jordan’s approach towards climate change and the institutional framework and plans in place for mitigation and adapt between 2022 and 2050. It is an update to the Climate Change Policy of 2013-2020 and serves as an overarching document for mainstreaming climate change in all sectoral policies, strategies, and action plans.


Ultimately, the policy aims at supporting Jordan in taking part in global efforts of reaching carbon neutrality by 2050 whilst also securing adaptation against climate change impacts. In doing so, this document incorporates considerations for different social categories: women, youth and children are also a focus within the adaptation section of the policy.


The document comprises the following sections:

  • Policy vision, objective and principles;
  • Adaptation and mitigation with proposed policies and accompanying actions and instruments;
  • Enabling factors such as capacity development;
  • Emerging issues, e.g. disaster risk management and refugees;
  • Monitoring and evaluation framework.
Document Title: National Climate Change Policy of Jordan 2022-2050

Family Name: New Plan for the Promotion of Biomass Utilization
Family Summary: Goals towards 2025: annual use of 26 million tons of biomass; implementation of 600 municipal biomass promotion plans; creation of a 500 bn yen market for biomass.
Document Title: New Plan for the Promotion of Biomass Utilization

Family Name: Energy Efficiency Grant (EEG)
Family Summary: This grant helps businesses transition towards being more energy efficient by co-funding investments in energy-efficient equipment. The grant provides up to 70% funding support for businesses to adopt pre-approved energy efficient equipment. The grant is available for eligible companies in the following sectors: Construction, Food Services, Manufacturing, Maritime, Retail sectors, and users of data centres.
Document Title: Energy Efficiency Grant (EEG)

Family Name: Environmental Policy Guidelines for 2021-2027
Family Summary:
The Environmental Policy Guidelines for 2021-2027 (EPGs 2027), adopted by the Cabinet Order 583/2022, are a medium-term policy planning document for the environmental sector.

They have been developed in accordance with the priorities set out in the Latvia 2030, Latvian NDP for 2021-2027 and the strategic objectives of the European Green Course and provide for:

  • achieving the 2030 greenhouse gas reduction target and achieve climate neutrality by 2050;
  • improving adaptability, strengthening resilience and reducing vulnerability to climate change;
  • making progress towards a renewable growth model by decoupling economic growth from resource use and environmental depletion and acceleration of the transition to a circular economy;
  • aiming for zero pollution in the environment free of toxic substances, including air, water and soil, and thus also protecting the health and well-being of Europeans;
  • protecting, preserving and restoring biodiversity and increasing natural capital, in particular air, water, soil, and forest, freshwater, wetland and marine ecosystems; and
  • promoting environmental sustainability and reducing environmental and climate pressures related to production and consumption, in the fields of energy, industrial development, buildings and infrastructure, mobility and food systems.
Document Title: Environmental Policy Guidelines for 2021-2027

Family Name: Poland's CAP Strategic Plan (2023-2027)
Family Summary: Poland’s CAP Strategic Plan (Plan strategiczny WPR 2023-2027) is the country’s national implementation of the EU’s Common Agricultural Policy for 2023-27, approved by the European Commission on 31 August 2022. It aims to support sustainable development of Polish farms and rural areas, boosting farm income, competitiveness, innovation and risk management, while placing strong emphasis on environmental and climate protection, including measures to improve water management, reduce greenhouse gas and ammonia emissions, protect soil, air and biodiversity, and promote sustainable energy and resource use. The plan also fosters social and economic activation in rural areas and the spread of innovation and digital solutions throughout agriculture.
Document Title: Strategic Plan for the Common Agricultural Policy for 2023-2027 – summary version 6.1

Family Name: Finland’s CAP Strategic Plan 2023-2027
Family Summary: The new CAP period from 2023 to 2027 began in January 2023. The main tasks of Finland's CAP Strategic Plan (CSP) include safeguarding active food production, climate and environmental sustainability in agriculture and strengthening the vitality of regenerating rural areas. In its CAP strategic plan, each EU country is obliged to display a higher ambition on environment and climate action compared to the previous programming period. Each country is also required to update the plan when climate and environmental legislation is modified. The aim is that 40 per cent of the total EU funding for CAP measures will be allocated to climate measures at the EU level. Member States are obliged to allocate 35 per cent of the rural development funds to environmental and climate measures at the national level. In addition to this, at least 25 per cent of the budget for direct payments is allocated to eco-schemes, providing stronger incentives for climate- and environment-friendly farming practices and approaches.Key targets include reducing agricultural greenhouse-gas emissions, improving nutrient management, protecting biodiversity, supporting sustainable farming practices, and strengthening rural businesses and communities. The plan also promotes knowledge, innovation and digitalisation in agriculture and rural areas. Its national objectives are assessed against the 2022 baseline, with targets set primarily for 2027.
Document Title: CAP Strategic Plan 2023-2027

Family Name: Roadmap for the sustainable management of mineral raw materials
Family Summary: Spain's Roadmap for Sustainable Management of Mineral Raw Materials presents a national strategy aimed at strengthening the country's strategic autonomy in mineral resources while aligning with European Union initiatives and the Green Deal objectives through 2050. According to the Spanish Government, the policy framework addresses critical challenges in the ecological transition, particularly focusing on reducing dependencies on foreign mineral resources through sustainable domestic production, circular economy initiatives, and strategic partnerships. The strategy outlines four key instrumental areas: (i) regulatory mechanisms for mining legislation alignment, (ii) sectoral instruments promoting circular economy and sustainable management, (iii) transversal instruments supporting public-private cooperation and social impact assessment, and (iv) Research  Development+Innovation (RD+I) promotion for technological advancement in mineral resource management. This roadmap, subject to quinquennial reviews, emphasises the development of resilient value chains and sustainable extraction practices while considering environmental protection, social welfare, and economic viability in the context of Spain's broader decarbonisation goals.
Document Title: Roadmap for the sustainable management of mineral raw materials

Family Name: Regulation No. 460/2022 on the approval of the Strategy for Agriculture, Rural Development and Fishing 2021-2027
Family Summary: This strategy outlines objectives for the sustainable development of the agro-food sector in Albania. It aims to develop policies that promote the sustainable use of natural resources and mitigate climate change impacts. This strategy aligns with and aims to facilitate the Western Balkans Green Agenda adopted in October 2023. The reforms in the fishing sector, specifically, are expected to contribute to the development of Albania's blue economy and support EU climate policies more broadly.
Document Title: Regulation No.460/2022 on the Strategy for Agriculture, Rural Development and Fishing 2021-2027

Family Name: Guidelines for Tariff Based Competitive Bidding Process for Procurement of Power for Thermal/ Hydro Power Stations
Family Summary:
These Guidelines are the Guidelines for Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding Process for Procurement of Power from Grid Connected RE Power Projects for utilisation under the scheme for flexibility in Generation and Scheduling of Thermal/ Hydro Power Stations through bundling with Renewable Energy and Storage Power. The objective of this mechanism is to promote bundling of cheaper Renewable Energy (RE) with costlier Thermal Power and to promote the Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) of Distribution Licensees.

The Guidelines outline the bidding process and standard provisions to be included in the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA). The PPA period should not be less than 25 years from the scheduled commissioning date, as the period influences the amount of tariff to be charged. Bids are to be submitted within 22 days, and the PPA is to be signed within 170 days of the release of the bid. The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) presides over arbitration of any tariff-related disputes.
Document Title: Guidelines for Tariff Based Competitive Bidding Process for Procurement of Power for fThermal/ Hydro Power Stations

Family Name: Nigeria Energy Transition Plan
Family Summary:
In August 2022 the government of Nigeria launched a new Energy Transition Plan, which seeks to use a data driven approach to generate new funding and investment opportunities for the energy transition in Nigeria, in line with Nigeria's goal of achieving Carbon Neutrality by 2060.

The plan sets out emissions reduction pathways and investment needs to achieve emissions reductions in energy, transport, oil and gas, cooking, and industry.
Document Title: Investing in Nigeria's Energy Transition Opportunity

Family Name: Action Plan on Promoting the Development of the Energy Electronics Industry
Family Summary: To implement carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, he Action Plan focuses on 10 fields of power equipment, namely, thermal power equipment, hydropower equipment, nuclear power equipment, wind power equipment, solar energy equipment, hydrogen energy equipment, energy storage equipment, power transmission equipment, power distribution equipment, and electricity equipment. It puts forward six actions: green upgrade of power equipment; improvement of technology; intelligent manufacturing; combination of public-private action; innovation in balancing demand and supply; and external cooperation for power equipment.
Document Title: Action Plan on Promoting the Development of the Energy Electronics Industry

Family Name: Decree creating the decentralised public body called Lithium for Mexico (LitioMx)
Family Summary: President of Mexico - Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador - issued a Decree setting up a new state-owned company called 'LitioMx' (Litio para Mexico), which will be responsible for managing the exploration, mining exploitation, and refining of lithium throughout the national territory of Mexico, as well as controlling the economic value chains of this mineral.
Document Title: Decree creating the decentralised public body called Lithium for Mexico (LitioMx)

Family Name: Fijian Sustainable Development Bond Framework 2022
Family Summary: The Framework builds on the experience of the Fiji Sovereign Green Bond issued in 2017. It creates a robust taxonomy for green, blue, and social projects, developed to demonstrate how Fiji select, finance and/ or re-finance eligible projects to deliver focussed social and environmental benefits which are in close alignment with national SDG targets. Fiji plans to catalyse blended ‘blue’ finance by issuing its first-ever sovereign blue bond in mid-2022 to support the operationalisation of its National Oceans Policy, its Climate Change Policy and its 5-Year and 20-Year National Development Plans.
Document Title: Fijian Sustainable Development Bond Framework 2022

Family Name: Action Plan for Green and Low-Carbon Development of the Information and Communication Industry (2022-2025)
Family Summary: This Plan is aligned with the overall plan of carbon peaking and carbon neutralisation., and contains five main actions, namely, optimising the overall layout of green development; the green upgrading of key facilities; the construction of a green industrial chain supply chain; the empowerment of the economic and social green development; and the strengthening of the overall management of the green development of the industry.
Document Title: Action Plan for Green and Low-Carbon Development of the Information and Communication Industry (2022-2025)

Family Name: Decree 334/2022 of 17-8-2022, which approves the Regulations of the aid program for the promotion of the circular economy.
Family Summary:
Embedded in the Law 25/2022, which allocates an article on aid for the promotion of the circular economy and provides for the possibility of developing calls and empowers the Government to issue the regulatory provisions, this Regulation aims to:
a) Create aid to promote the circular economy.
b) Establish the conditions for access to aid and the obligations and commitments of the beneficiaries.
c) Establish the types and characteristics of actions, the financing conditions of the grants and the criteria through which the promotion and transition towards the circular economy is evaluated.
Amongst the criteria, the decree outlines that any proposal must contribute to one of the six sustainability objectives ( Climate change mitigation, adaptation to climate change, sustainable use and protection of water resources, protection and restoration of biodiversity and ecosystems, pollution prevention and control, transition to a circular economy) and must not have a significant negative impact on the others.
Document Title: Decree 334/2022 of 17-8-2022, which approves the Regulations of the aid program for the promotion of the circular economy

Family Name: Ministerial Agreement No. MAATE - 2021 - 046. Technical framework focused on products for implementing the Ecuador Carbon Zero Program (PECC)
Family Summary: This Ministerial Agreement introduces the technical framework for implementing the Ecuador Carbon Zero Program (PECC) with a focus on products. It establishes guidelines for organisations to quantify, reduce, and neutralise greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across the life cycle of their products, aligning with Ecuador's constitutional provisions on environmental preservation, living well philosophy (“sumak kawsay” - buen vivir), and sustainable development. The program aims to promote cleaner production practices, reduce the carbon footprint of products, and support national and international climate goals.Central to the framework is the calculation of the Product Carbon Footprint (HCP), guided by international standards such as ISO 14067 and the GHG Protocol. Organization are required to inventory emissions, identify opportunities for reductions, and implement action plans for measurable mitigation. The program introduces certifications for Carbon Footprint Reduction and Carbon Neutrality, which incentivise continuous improvement. Through this policy, it is expected that businesses can achieve both environmental stewardship and competitive advantage, contributing to Ecuador’s transition to a low-carbon economy. Verification processes are handled by accredited conformity assessment bodies, ensuring transparency and adherence to rigorous standards.
Document Title: Ministerial Agreement No. MAATE - 2021 - 046. Technical framework focused on products for implementing the Ecuador Carbon Zero Program (PECC)

Family Name: Decree No. 2022-1151 relating to aid for the acquisition or rental of low-polluting vehicles
Family Summary: The increase in state aid for the purchase of a bicycle comes into force from Monday August 15, with additional amounts for people with disabilities or low income.
Document Title: Decree No. 2022-1151 relating to aid for the acquisition or rental of low-polluting vehicles

Family Name: Decision No. 942/QD-TTg on approving Action Plan for Methane Emissions Reduction by 2030
Family Summary: The Action Plan sets the general objective of making efforts to reduce overall methane emissions from cultivation, animal husbandry, solid waste management, wastewater treatment, oil and gas extraction, coal mining and fossil fuel consumption, by at least 30% below 2020 level by 2030.This is specified as follows: By 2030, overall methane emissions are expected to not exceed 77.9 million metric tons of CO2e, or to reduce by at least 30% below 2020 level. In which, methane emissions, measured in CO2e, are expected to not exceed 30.7 metric tons from cultivation, 15.2 metric tons from animal husbandry, 17.5 metric tons from solid waste management and wastewater treatment, 8.1 metric tons from oil and gas extraction, 2.0 metric tons from coal mining, and 0.8 metric tons from fossil fuel consumption.The Plan also sets specific objectives for 2025: By 2025, overall methane emissions are expected to not exceed 96.4 million metric tons of CO2 equivalent (CO2e), or to reduce by 13.34% below 2020 level. It specifies further for the different sectors: In which, methane emissions, measured in CO2e, are expected to not exceed 42.2 metric tons from cultivation, 16.8 metric tons from animal husbandry, 21.9 metric tons from solid waste management and wastewater treatment, 10.6 metric tons from oil and gas extraction, 3.5 metric tons from coal mining, and 1.3 metric tons from fossil fuel consumption.The Methane emissions reduction as set out in this Action Plan aims at implementing the Global Methane Pledge. Tasks and solutions for implementation of the Plan include formulating and revising mechanisms and policies; and implementing measures for reducing methane emission from the various sectors. Furthermore, the Plan suggests to do scientific research and technological development; promote information dissemination, education and increase of capacity and awareness; intensify bilateral and multilateral cooperation and mobilisation of resources, perform supervision and assessment tasks.
Document Title: Decision No. 942/QD-TTg on approving Action Plan for Methane Emissions Reduction by 2030

It specifies further for the different sectors: In which, methane emissions, measured in CO2e, are expected to not exceed 42.2 metric tons from cultivation, 16.8 metric tons from animal husbandry, 21.9 metric tons from solid waste management and wastewater treatment, 10.6 metric tons from oil and gas extraction, 3.5 metric tons from coal mining, and 1.3 metric tons from fossil fuel consumption.The Methane emissions reduction as set out in this Action Plan aims at implementing the Global Methane Pledge. Tasks and solutions for implementation of the Plan include formulating and revising mechanisms and policies; and implementing measures for reducing methane emission from the various sectors. Furthermore, the Plan suggests to do scientific research and technological development; promote information dissemination, education and increase of capacity and awareness; intensify bilateral and multilateral cooperation and mobilisation of resources, perform supervision and assessment tasks.
Document Title: Decision No. 942/QD-TTg on approving Action Plan for Methane Emissions Reduction by 2030

Family Name: State Programme on the Promotion of Energy Savings (EFEKT III)
Family Summary:
EFEKT III is the Czech state programme (2022–2027) run by the Ministry of Industry and Trade to support non‑investment energy efficiency projects. It has a budget of up to CZK 160 million per year. Its goal is to help Czech entities reduce energy consumption, prepare high‑quality renovation projects (including via EPC), build local energy plans, develop ISO 50001‑based energy management systems, and foster energy‑saving innovation.

The programme is structured around five support “axes”: (1) pre‑project preparation, (2) advisory services, (3) education, (4) energy management and local energy concepts, and (5) pilot projects.
Document Title: State Programme on the Promotion of Energy Savings (EFEKT)

Family Name: Decree No 2022-1119 relating to digital travel assistance services
Family Summary: this decree amends existing legislation. It obliges digital travel assistance services (such as Google Maps, Waze and Plans) to provide their users with at least information relating to the quantities of greenhouse gases and air pollutants emitted by the mode or modes of transport used for each route suggestion. The methodologies for calculating the quantities of greenhouse gases and air pollutants are made public and easily accessible by digital travel assistance services. For the application of 3° of Article L. 1115-8-1, digital services that aim to facilitate multimodal travel highlight proposed routes with the lowest impact in terms of emissions of greenhouse gases.
Document Title: Decree No 2022-1119 relating to digital travel assistance services

Family Name: Aotearoa New Zealand's First National Adaptation Plan
Family Summary:
“Adapt and thrive: Building a climate-resilient New Zealand” is Aotearoa New Zealand’s first national adaptation plan.


The plan has been developed in response to a national climate change risk assessment prepared by the independent Climate Change Commission.


The plan sets out what the government will do to enable better risk-informed decisions, drive climate-resilient development in the right locations, help communities assess adaptation options (including managed retreat) and embed climate resilience into all of the Government’s work.
Document Title: National Adaptation Plan Summary

Family Name: Cambodia's National Cooling Action Plan (NCAP)
Family Summary:
This National Cooling Action Plan (NCAP) is developed in collaboration with the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UNESCAP). The cooling sector in Cambodia contributed 6.27 million tons of carbon dioxide (CO2) equivalent emissions in 2020. Cooling is used in diverse sectors of the economy, and is rapidly expanding in Cambodia following economic and population growth.  

The plan follows the National Cooling Action Plan Methodology that is created by the Cool Coalition. It includes cross-sectoral domestic targets for cooling and interventions for supporting all economies that are vulnerable to risks associated with heat stress. The target is to reduce emissions by 17% by 2040, and reduce electricity consumption for cooling by 20% by 2040. Monitoring and evaluation are also critical components. 

The NCAP is centred around five main areas

  • Building Space Cooling
  • Food cold Chain
  • Health-care Cold Chain
  • Mobile Air Conditioning
  • Process Cooling
Document Title: Cambodia's National Cooling Action Plan (NCAP)

Family Name: Georgia's Sustainable Finance Taxonomy
Family Summary: This document sets out Georgie's Sustainable Finance Taxonomy. The Sustainable Finance (SF) Taxonomy for Georgia, developed by the National Bank of Georgia (NBG) in collaboration with local and international experts, serves as a crucial classification system to guide the country's transition toward sustainable development. Its main purpose is to create a common language for financial institutions, ensuring investments are directed toward activities that meet key environmental, climate, and social objectives.
Document Title: Georgia's Sustainable Finance Taxonomy

Family Name: Implementation Plan for Science and Technology Support for Carbon Peaking and Carbon Neutrality (2022-2030)
Family Summary: To achieve the goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, this Plan aims to improve the innovation systems and mechanisms, strengthen innovation capabilities and talent development, bolster fundamental applied research, and accelerate the RD and deployment of advanced, practical technologies. These include technologies for source carbon reduction, process carbon reduction; end-of-pipe carbon sequestration; cleaner and efficient coal utilisation carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS); offshore wind power industry technology and energy storage innovation. Actions include supporting industry development and international cooperation.
Document Title: Implementation Plan for Science and Technology Support for Carbon Peaking and Carbon Neutrality (2022-2030)

Family Name: National Cooling Action Plan
Family Summary: This Plan realises Cambodia’s long-term development vision in building a sustainable, green, clean, and low-carbon society based on climate-friendly and energy-efficient technology in the cooling sector, to reduce the use of electricity.
Document Title: National Cooling Action Plan

Family Name: Action Plan for the Development of Electric Vehicle Use and Charging Infrastructure
Family Summary: The action plan aims to promote the development and deployment of electric vehicles and their enabling infrastructure over the 2022-2030 period, in accordance with the 2021 Law on Alternative Fuels. Energy security and climate change mitigation are primary motivators for the action plan. The action plan emphasises several primary directions for development, such as the buildout of charging stations in private residences, apartment complexes and workplaces. It also promotes the acquisition of a significant electric vehicle stock by the public sector, and suggests adding electric vehicle ownership incentives to subsidies for private renewable energy generation products (i.e. solar installations). The action plan suggests that ministries clarify and expand their regulatory frameworks to simplify the process of administering electric vehicle deployment.
Document Title: Action Plan for the Development of Electric Vehicle Use and Charging Infrastructure

Family Name: Energy Agenda 2022-2026
Family Summary: This document was developed to support the short-term implementation of Chile's National Energy Policy. It lays out specific actions for the energy sector along eight key priority areas.
Document Title: Energy Agenda 2022-2026

Family Name: Plan on reaching peak CO2 emissions by 2030 in polluting industries
Family Summary: In February 2022, the government released guidelines  promoting the High-Quality Development of the Iron and Steel Industry and that required to reach peak CO2 emissions by 2030. In July, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology approved a plan to oblige companies in steel, building materials, petrochemicals, non-ferrous metals, consumer goods, equipment manufacturing and electronics sectors with an annual revenue of CNY20m (US$2.9m) or more to slash energy use by 13.5% from 2020 levels in 2025, and to reach peak carbon emissions by 2030.
Document Title: Plan on reaching peak CO2 emissions by 2030 in polluting industries

Family Name: Decree n° 2022-1085 regarding ways of aiding the acquisition or rental of low-polluting vehicles
Family Summary: This Decree modifies the eligibility threshold for the "ecological bonus" (a purchase grant) for plug-in hybrid vehicles stipulated in the Energy Code (articles D. 251-1, D. 251-7 and D. 251-8).  It also introduces a transitional period during which heavy vehicles ordered up until December 31, 2022 (or invoiced up until June 30, 2023) will be able to benefit from the ecological bonus.
Document Title: Decree n° 2022-1085 regarding ways of aiding the acquisition or rental of low-polluting vehicles

Family Name: Ordinance No. 2022-1075 of July 29, 2022 on the development of climate risk management tools in agriculture
Family Summary: On July 29, 2022, Ordinance No. 2022-1075 was issued in relation to Article 12 of  Law no. 2022-298 from March 2022, on improvements to crop insurance the reform of climate risk management tools in agriculture, which allowed the French government to take measures corning insurance against climate hazards in agriculture, to enable greater resilience to agricultural production in the long-term, as well as to guarantee farmers' broader access to an insurance scheme against risks posed by climate hazards. The central purpose of the Ordinance is to implement two aspects of the new 'architecture' for managing climate risks to agriculture (as defined by law): the establishment of a network of approved 'interlocutors' tasked with (on behalf of the State), 'national solidarity' compensation for catastrophic losses relating to harvest or crop production as well as the establishment of a co-reinsurance group between insurance companies that distribute subsidised multi-risk climate insurance.
Document Title: Ordinance No. 2022-1075 of July 29, 2022 on the development of climate risk management tools in agriculture

Family Name: Order from July 27, 2022 relating to the approval of the "Innovating to make the transitions in agroecological practices and food a success" call for projects document
Family Summary: This Order approves the specifications elaborated on in the call for projects, "Innovating to make the transitions in agroecological practices and food a success", a component of the France 2030 plan, relating to the "Demonstration in real conditions, priming, and commercial firsts" action, the future investment programme agreed on by the French government, ADEME, the National Agency and the Casse des dépôts et consignations, EPIC Bpifrance, and Bpifrance (a public limited company).

Family Name: Decision No. 876/QD-TTg on approving the Action Program for Transition to Green Energy and Mitigation of Carbon Dioxide and Methane Emissions from Transportation
Family Summary:
The overall objective of this Action Program is to develop a green transportation system towards the goal of net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050.

The roadmap for transition to green energy contains specific targets and concerns roadways; railways; inland waterways; shipping; aviation; and urban traffic.

In order to fulfil these tasks, the Action Program sets out solutions:
  • Formulate and complete mechanisms, policies and planning;
  • Develop programs and policies for the transition to vehicles running on electricity and green energy;
  • Develop green transport infrastructures;
  • Improve the energy efficiency and GHG emissions reduction;
  • Strengthen international cooperation, science and technology, develop human resources and communication.

The Action Program also establishes institutional mandates.
Document Title: Decision No. 876/QD-TTg on approving the Action Program for Transition to Green Energy and Mitigation of Carbon Dioxide and Methane Emissions from Transportation

Family Name: Decision No. 896/QD-TTg on approving the National Strategy for Climate Change until 2050
Family Summary:
• The Strategy reiterates the temperature of approximately 1,5 degrees by the end of this century. It also highlights the importance of achieving net zero emissions by 2050 as an essential goal of the world. The objectives of the Strategy are Effective adaptation to climate change;
  • Reduction of vulnerability losses, and damage caused by climate change;
  • Reduction of GHG emission following net zero emission target by 2050;
  • Positive contribution and responsibility to international community in protection the global climate;
  • Harnessing of opportunity brought by climate change adaptation to shift growth model, increase of resistance and competitiveness of the economy.

The Strategy sets adaptation and mitigation goal.Net zero shall be reached by 2050. It requires a nationwide greenhouse gas emission reduction by 43,5% compared to the BAU scenario by 2030.By 2030, the energy sector reduces 32,6%, emission does not exceed 457 million tonne of CO2 equivalent (CO2td); the agriculture sector reduces 43,0%, emission does not exceed 64 million tonne of CO2td; LULUCF sector reduces 70% and increases 20% of carbon absorption, total emission and absorption reach at least -95 million tonne of CO2td; waste sector reduces 60,7%, emission does not exceed 18 million tonne of CO2td; industrial processes sector reduces 38,3%, emission does not exceed 86 million tonne of CO2td. By 2050, total GHG emissions nationwide achieve net zero; emissions peak in 2035 and are reduced rapidly afterwards. The energy sector reduces 91,6%, emission does not exceed 101 million tonne CO2td; the agriculture sector reduces 63,1%, emission does not exceed 56 million tonne of CO2td; the LULUCF sector reduces 90% and increases 30% of carbon absorption, total emission and absorption reach at least -185 million tonne of CO2td; the waste sector reduces 90,7%, emission does not exceed 8 million tonne of CO2td; the industrial processes sector reduces 84,8%, emission does not exceed 20 million tonne of CO2td. The strategy then sets out tasks and solutions to reach adaptation and mitigation goals, means of implementation, and the funding sources for implementation.
Document Title: Decision No. 896/QD-TTg on approving the National Strategy for Climate Change until 2050
