Family Name: Circular no. 6363-SG relating to energy sobriety and exemplary behavior of State administrations
Family Summary: International tensions as well as the unavailability of part of the French nuclear fleet impose an unprecedented effort in terms of energy sobriety. With regard more specifically to State administrations, this circular enjoins the ministers, deputy ministers and secretaries of state to initiate, without delay, large-scale measures aimed at reducing energy consumption and accelerating the exit from fossil fuels.
Document Title: Circular no. 6363-SG relating to energy sobriety and exemplary behavior of State administrations

Family Name: Decision No. 888/QD-TTg on approval for Scheme Setting Out Tasks and Solutions for Implementation of Outcomes of the 26th Conference of the Parties to the Untied Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
Family Summary:
The Scheme's general objective is to set out the strategy for achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 and contribute to global efforts in response to climate change. 

Its specific objectives are:

  • Setting up a comprehensive legal framework;
  • Reforming strategies in order to be conform with net-zero commitments by 2050;
  • Promoting the reduction of GHG emissions in the sectors of energy, transport, production of building materials, agriculture and waste treatment;
    • By 2030, encourage the use of green energy and electricity in transport, and use of 100% of E5 petrol; decrease greenhouse gas emissions by 32,6% in energy, 43% in agriculture, 70% in forestry and land use sector in which the carbon sequestration capacity is expected to increase by 20%, 60,7% in waste treatment, and 38,3% in industrial processes (compared to the emission reduction stated in the BAU scenario). 
  • Identify potential of renewable energy sources;
    • By 2030, increase the ratio of sources of renewable energy, including hydroelectricity, wind power, solar power and biomass to at least 33% of total production of electricity.
  • Develop new zero-emission energy projects and energy storage technologies;
  • Establish carbon credit exchange and offsetting mechanisms, and domestic carbon credit market;
    • By 2030, the domestic carbon market shall be operated and connected with regional and global carbon markets.
  • Undertake climate change adaptation and natural resource and ecosystem restoration consistently and efficiently;
    • Implement UN initiatives accordingly.
  • Establish and participate in partnerships, alliances, and other international initiatives on emissions reduction and energy transition;
  • Promote climate diplomacy; do scientific research; improve capacity and communication activities.
Document Title: Decision No. 888/QD-TTg on approval for Scheme Setting Out Tasks and Solutions for Implementation of Outcomes of the 26th Conference of the Parties to the Untied Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change

Family Name: Social and Economic Development Strategy 2022-2026
Family Summary: This Strategy provides a framework for the implementation of the five national priorities outlined in “Azerbaijan 2030: National Priorities for Socio-Economic Development”. The strategic framework to implement the national priority on ‘clean environment and green growth’ include 1) the sustainable and viable use of natural resources, through the development of an effective waste management system, the upgrading of the environment monitoring system and the enhancement of biodiversity preservation, as well as 2) the improvement of energy regulations, through the expansion of renewable energy sources, the promotion of energy efficiency measures, and the deployment of environment-friendly vehicles and other green technologies. The action plan of the Strategy further includes the development of a Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) system for Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions.
Document Title: Social and Economic Development Strategy 2022-2026

Family Name: Order re Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) and Energy Storage Obligation Trajectory till 2029-2030
Family Summary:
This Order F. No. 09/13/2021-RCM made by the Ministry of Power stipulates the Renewable Purchase Obligations (RPO) for various renewable energy sources. For instance, in the year 2029-30, the wind RPO is 6.94% of total electricity consumption, the hydro power RPO (HPO) is 2.82%, and the other RPO is 33.57%, constituting a total RPO of 43.33%. The Order stipulates a capping price for renewable energy certificates for hydro power with an annual escalation, and hydro power imported from outside India does not meet the HPO.

There are also stipulations for the amount of storage as a percentage of the total energy consumed for solar/wind energy.

Corrigendum F. No. 09/13/2021-RCM was made on 19 September 2022 to recognise the significant amount of investment for wind power projects compared to other renewable energy technologies, benefitting states that have invested in wind power by considering the inclusion of wind energy, where it was above 7% of total energy consumption and consumed before 31 March 2022, in the RPO.
Document Title: Corrigendum F. No. 09/13/2021-RCM

Family Summary:
This strategy aims to achieve a total of 32 MtCO2e of forest carbon sequestration (domestic: 25.5 MtCO2e, foreign: 5 MtCO2e, biomass: 1.5 MtCO2e) until 2023. This target takes 10% of the NDC. This policy sets out the detailed strategies for the target as follows:

  • 1 million ha of forest restoration and afforestation in urban and deforested area and on idle land until 2027.
  • Apply forest tending on 319 thousand ha of forest area until 2027.
  • Enlargement of forest reserve up to 150 thousand ha until 2027.
  • Upgrade REDD+ pilot project in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos to Subnational REDD+ and figure out new projects by adding the partner countries (e.g., Vietnam, Peru, Mongolia)

Family Name: National plan for the development of combined transport in the Republic of Bulgaria until 2030
Family Summary: The Ministry of Transport and Communications has developed a National Plan for the Development of Combined Transport in the Republic of Bulgaria until 2030 (approved by Decision No 504 of the Council of Ministers of 21 July 2022). It is a reference document for the implementation of the policy to support sustainable modes of transport. A key climate-related aspect of the plan is its emphasis on shifting freight from road to rail and water transport, which is expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and air pollutants, supporting Bulgaria’s commitments under the EU Green Deal and the Sustainable and Smart Mobility Strategy. The plan also aligns with national climate and environmental policies, including the Climate Change Act and the National Air Pollution Control Programme, ensuring that transport development contributes to emission reduction targets, climate mitigation, and environmental sustainability.
Document Title: National plan for the development of combined transport in the Republic of Bulgaria until 2030

Family Name: Jet zero strategy
Family Summary:
This document sets the government's decarbonisation vision for the aviation sector in order to enable the country to meet its 2050 net zero target. It seeks to balance regional and international connectivity, economic benefits and a reduction of GHG emissions, and support sustainable airport growth. Intermediary targets and a five year delivery plan has been released as part of this strategy, in order to take urgent measures quickly. Progress will be monitored annually and through a five-year major review.

The strategy focuses on technological solutions, and the six following measures: System efficiencies, Sustainable Aviation Fuels (SAF), Zero emission flight (ZEF), Markets and removals, Influencing consumers, and addressing non-CO2 impacts and potential mitigation. It also asserts the UK's ambition to lead internationally on reaching an agreement on long-term aspirational goal for the CO2 emissions of international aviation that is aligned with the temperature goal of the Paris Agreement. It commits the government to work with the Jet Zero Council and other entities to bring up new technologies and other remission-cutting solutions. It aims to improve operational efficiency, notably for airports, on the short term.

The document seeks to support up to 5,200 UK jobs in the aerospace sector. 


The document further states that carbon markets will have a key role in delivering Jet Zero, and greenhouse gas removals (GGRs) are needed to address residual emissions. It says that the government will work with the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) to gather more evidence on providing consumers with environmental information at the time of booking a flight.
Document Title: Jet zero strategy

Collection Name: Law 7/2021 on climate change and energy transition [Spain]
Collection Summary:
Enacted in 2021, this law establishes Spain's legal framework for achieving climate neutrality by 2050, aligning with the Paris Agreement and Sustainable Development Goals. It mandates a 23% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 (compared to 1990 levels), alongside ambitious renewable energy targets, including 42% of final energy consumption from renewables and 74% renewable electricity generation by 2030. Energy efficiency measures aim for a 39.5% reduction in primary energy consumption within the same timeframe. The law also prohibits new hydrocarbon and radioactive mineral exploitation, requires emission-free transport systems in cities with populations exceeding 50,000, and emphasises sustainable urban mobility.

The legislation includes a national Just Transition Strategy to ensure equitable economic opportunities, particularly for vulnerable regions, while fostering adaptation and resilience to climate risks across critical sectors such as water, biodiversity, and health. It creates governance mechanisms like the Expert Committee on Climate Change and Energy Transition to monitor progress and updates to Spain's Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC). Projecting investments exceeding €200 billion by 2030, the law is expected to enhance Spain’s GDP by €16.5–25.7 billion annually and generate 250,000–350,000 new jobs. The focus on education, innovation, and public awareness underscores its commitment to a holistic and inclusive transition.

This collection represent a body of policies, strategies, and plans enacted under this law.
Family Name: Strategic guidelines on water and climate change
Family Summary:
The "Strategic Guidelines on Water and Climate Change" outline Spain's approach to integrating water management with climate change adaptation. Article 19 of the Climate Change and Energy Transition Law emphasises the need for water planning and management to ensure water security for people, biodiversity, and socioeconomic activities while reducing vulnerability to climate change. This is achieved by prioritising ecological flow regimes as a precondition rather than a competing use of water, aligning with hydrological plans, and adhering to the forthcoming "Water Strategy for Ecological Transition”.
Spain faces significant challenges due to its diverse hydrological systems, exacerbated by irregular rainfall, droughts, and flooding. Key priorities include enhancing wastewater treatment infrastructure to meet EU standards, addressing overexploitation and contamination of groundwater, and adapting water resources to climate risks such as altered flow regimes, rising temperatures, and sea-level rise. Strategic actions of this policy include advancing hydrological planning for 2022-2027, fostering sustainable water use, promoting renewable energy in water systems, restoring aquatic ecosystems, and modernizing monitoring technologies. Spain also aims to strengthen its international role in water governance through partnerships and alignment with global and EU environmental objectives.
Document Title: Strategic guidelines on water and climate change

Family Name: Export Development Canada Net Zero 2050 roadmap
Family Summary: This document outlines Export Development Canada’s (EDC) roadmap for achieving its net zero by 2050 target, which it committed to in July 2021. The roadmap includes calculating the EDC’s portfolio financed emissions in alignment with the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF) guidance; setting interim targets to reduce financing exposure to the six most carbon-intensive sectors as well as sectoral science-based targets that align with limiting warming to 1.5C or lower; reducing operational GHG emissions to nearly zero, with any remaining emissions neutralised through carbon removal credits; developing and expanding the solutions the EDC is able to procure to customers to help reduce their emissions through clean technology, sustainability-linked loans and other sustainable finance tools.
Document Title: Export Development Canada (EDC) Net Zero 2050: Steps Considerations and decisions along the path to net zero by 2050

Family Name: National Landscape Restoration Strategy for Belize 2022-2030
Family Summary: The strategy promotes landscape restoration as a key focus for climate mitigation, adaptation, biodiversity and to sustainably maintain ecosystem services and benefits to the rural economy. Document Title: National Landscape Restoration Strategy for Belize 2022-2030

Family Name: Latvia’s Territorial Just Transition Plan
Family Summary: The Latvian TJTP is a climate-action roadmap that mandates the total phase-out of peat for energy by 2030 and allocates significant funding to restore over 26,000 hectares of degraded peatlands, helping biodiversity but also the LULUCF sector of the country to recover carbon sinks. Beyond ecology, it focuses on social fairness by funding the reskilling of approximately 1,600 workers and supporting municipalities in switching from peat-fired heating to renewable energy sources like biomass and solar. Ultimately, the plan aims to diversify the regional economy by investing in green industrial zones, energy-efficient business infrastructure, and sustainable mobility.The plan was adopted by the Cabinet of Ministers Order 531/2022.
Document Title: Cabinet Order 531/2022 - Latvia’s Territorial Just Transition Plan

Family Name: Implementation Plan for Carbon Peaking in the Urban and Rural Development Sector
Family Summary: This Plan sets the target of carbon peaking in urban and rural development by 2030, with massive improvements in building energy efficiency and waste-to-resource management. The use of renewable resources is to reach an advanced level internationally. The Plan aims to construct green low-carbon cities, towns and villages.
Document Title: Implementation Plan for Carbon Peaking in the Urban and Rural Development Sector

Family Name: Order from 12/07/2022 on energy savings certificates
Family Summary: This Order replaced the "Heating of tertiary buildings" support scheme with the "Heating of collective residential and tertiary buildings" support scheme. In this regard, the connection of collective residential buildings to the heating networks is transferred from the "Heating" support scheme to the "Hearting of collective residential and tertiary buildings" support scheme. This modifies the Order issued on December 29th, 2015, that stipulates the terms of application of the energy savings certificate system. This new support scheme does not cover the installation of boilers.
Document Title: Order from July 12th, 2022 amending the Order from December 29th, 2014, that relate to the terms of the application of the energy savings certificate systems and the Order of December 22nd, 2014, defining standardised energy savings operations

Family Name: Medium-term Climate Change Policy Plan (2022)
Family Summary: The plan aims to meet Finland's emissions reduction targets within the effort-sharing sector to fulfil the country's climate obligations and achieve the goal of carbon neutrality by 2035. The effort-sharing sector includes emissions from activities not covered by the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS), such as transport, agriculture, heating in buildings, waste management, non-road mobile machinery, F-gases, and certain emissions from industrial and energy use. The plan identifies and assesses the necessary measures to reduce emissions in these sectors, ensuring they align with Finland's broader climate objectives.
Document Title: Medium-term Climate Change Policy Plan

Family Name: Implementation Plan for Carbon Peaking in the Industrial Sector
Family Summary: This Plan sets out the key tasks to decrease industrial energy consumption by 13.5% by 2025 compared with 2020: deeply adjust the industrial structure; promote energy conservation and carbon reduction; actively promote green manufacturing; develop the circular economy; accelerate the transformation of industrial green and low-carbon technology; promote the digital transformation of the industrial field; formulating carbon peaking implementation plans for key industrials of steel, construction materials, petrochemicals, non-ferrous metals and improve the supply of green low-carbon products.
Document Title: Implementation Plan for Carbon Peaking in the Industrial Sector

Family Name: Decree No. 2022-990 of 7 July 2022 on the General Secretariat for Ecological Planning
Family Summary: This Decree establishes the General Secretariat of Ecological Planning, which exercises the following powers, under the authority of the Prime Minister:1° It coordinates the development of national strategies on climate, energy, biodiversity and the circular economy, ensuring compliance with France's European and international commitments. It ensures in particular the sustainability of these strategies and their differentiation, in order to adapt to the particularities of each territory and to integrate economic and social issues;2° It ensures the implementation of these strategies by all the ministries concerned and their declination into action plans;3° It ensures the regular evaluation of the policies carried out under these strategies and action plans and the publication of indicators to report on them;4° It ensures the consistency of all public policies with the strategies mentioned in 1°;5° It prepares and coordinates the referrals and responses of the Government to the opinions of the High Council for Climate.
Document Title: Decree No. 2022-990 of 7 July 2022 on the General Secretariat for Ecological Planning

Family Name: National Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Plan (2021-2027)
Family Summary:
The National Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Plan of Thailand (2021–2027) outlines the country’s framework for managing disaster risks in an era of rapid global change. Anchored in the 20-Year National Strategy, the plan incorporates the Sufficiency Economy Philosophy, the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (SFDRR). It sets out a vision for a resilient Thai society that can effectively reduce existing risks, prevent new ones, and respond quickly and systematically when disasters occur. The plan emphasizes building public awareness, preparedness, and adaptive capacity so that communities can “know, adapt, and recover quickly in a sustainable way.”

To achieve this, the plan defines two main strategic areas: reducing disaster risks and standardizing disaster management. It includes measures such as strengthening risk assessment systems, developing risk reduction mechanisms, fostering innovation and information systems, promoting partnerships across sectors, and enhancing regional and international cooperation. It also highlights integrated emergency response, sustainable recovery efforts based on the principle of “Build Back Better,” and mechanisms for monitoring, evaluation, and continuous improvement. The policy reflects Thailand’s commitment to safety, resilience, and long-term sustainable development through a whole-of-society approach.
Document Title: National Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Plan (2021-2027)

Family Name: Agroenergy Programme (Agroenergia)
Family Summary:
The aim of the program is to increase energy production from renewable sources in the agricultural sector. The program will be implemented until 2027.The Agroenergia program consists of two parts:

  • Micro-installations, heat pumps and accompanying energy storage - Types of subsidized projects: photovoltaic installations, wind installations and heat pumps with an installed capacity above 10 kW and not exceeding 50 kW, including hybrid installations and accompanying electricity storage facilities.
  • Agricultural biogas plants and small hydropower plants - Types of subsidized projects: agricultural biogas plants with an accompanying agricultural biogas production installation and hydroelectric power plants with a capacity of no more than 500 kW with accompanying energy storage facilities.
Document Title: Agroenergy Programme (Agroenergia)

Family Name: Zambia Water Investment Programme 2022 - 2030
Family Summary: The Programme includes outputs to develop hydropower plants and constructing climate-resilient water supply infrastructure, to build climate resilience.
Document Title: Zambia Water Investment Programme 2022 - 2030

Family Name: Gender and Climate Change Action Plan 2023-2025
Family Summary:
The objective of this Plan is to promote the effective integration of gender in the implementation of climate change mitigation and adaptation measures in a manner that is equitable for both men and women. The main actions are: (i) mobilise institutional and community actors for gender-transformative climate actions, (ii) strengthen the capacities of structures and decision-makers, technicians, and populations for gender-transformative climate actions, and (iii) empower women, young people, people with disabilities, and rural communities to strengthen their resilience to climate change.

The nine sectors this Plan covers are: agriculture; energy; forestry; waste; water resources; health; ubran infrastructure and development; coastal and tourism. In addition to the main actions which are common to all nine sectors impacted by climate change, specific actions for each sector have been planned.
Document Title: Gender and Climate Change Action Plan 2023-2025

Family Name: Guyana Low Carbon Development Strategy 2030
Family Summary:
Guyana's Low Carbon Development Strategy 2030 forms the backbone of the country's efforts to mitigate and adapt to climate change from 2022-2030. The four primary objeectives of the strategy are: to value ecosystem services through voluntary global carbon markets and a bilateral partnership with Norway; to invest in clean energy, boosting green economic growth; to protect against climate change and biodiversity loss domestically; and to contribute to global climate goals

To maintain ecosystem services, the strategy aims to ensure that mining activities are low-impact and certified with respect to their effects on forestry. It also aims to sustainably regulate commercial forestry, expand natural mangrove systems as coastal protection, protect watersheds and enhance monitoring/research capacity nationally.

To achieve a clean electricity supply, the strategy plans to meet growing demand via a mixture of hydroelectricity and natural gas, with solar energy also playing a key role and combining with enhanced battery storage to provision off-grid regions. It also promotes early measures to electrify transport, including tax reductions for electric vehicles and the subsidised construction of charging stations.

To adapt to climate risks, a key element of the strategy is riverine and coastal flood prevention, through soft (mangroves and ecosystem restoration) and hard techniques. This aims to safeguard against these major risks to the agricultural and urban sectors concentrated around the coast.

On a global level the strategy supports carbon pricing and the achievement of net zero goals by 2050 and a 28% reduction in oil demand by 2030, while acknowledging the significant role of oil in Guyana's economy and emphasising the need for major incumbents in the sector to contribute to the same goals.
Document Title: Guyana Low Carbon Development Strategy 2030

Family Name: Public Sector Climate Action Mandate
Family Summary:
The Public Sector Climate Action Mandate seeks to support public sector bodies to lead by example. The mandate applies to public bodies in scope of the Climate Action Plan 2023, with the exception of local authorities, commercial semi-state bodies, and schools.


The Mandate sets out the climate action objectives for public bodies and is reviewed every year.


The targets are to reduce GHG emissions by 51% in 2030; increase energy efficiency in the public sector from 33% in 2020 to 50% by 2030; and update Climate Action Roadmaps annually in line with the updated Public Sector Climate Action Mandate.


Progress on the implementation of the mandate is assessed by using a ‘comply or explain approach’.
Document Title: Public Sector Climate Action Mandate

Family Name: Clean Hydrogen Industrial Hubs Program
Family Summary: Grant program to develop hydrogen hubs in seven locations, with the aim of developing the Australian hydrogen market. Clean hydrogen under this policy includes hydrogen made with gas and CCS
Document Title: Clean Hydrogen Industrial Hubs Program

Family Name: German strategy to strengthen resilience to disasters: Implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030) - Germany's contribution 2022-2030
Family Summary:
The Federal Government's strategy for strengthening resilience to disasters (resilience strategy for short) will make Germany more resilient to crises in the long term. The Federal Government is pursuing a holistic strategic approach in order to invest in prevention and to better cope with and recover from disasters and crises: The resilience strategy shows what efforts are already being made to this end and where overarching action is required in five specific fields of action:

  • Understanding disaster risk.
  • Strengthen intuitions to manage disaster risk.
  • Invest in disaster risk reduction to strengthen resilience.
  • Improve disaster preparedness and enable better recovery.
  • International cooperation

Crises and disasters have accompanied mankind since time immemorial. However, our recent past, our present and a look into the future show that crises and disasters present us with new and changing challenges. In Germany, risk and crisis management are national tasks and an integral part of our security architecture. Security is a fundamental human need for which the state bears a special responsibility. We must therefore place people at the centre of our initiatives to strengthen resilience to disasters.
Document Title: German strategy to strengthen resilience to disasters: Implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030) - Germany's contribution 2022-2030 (Summary)

Family Name: Arming our country against crises and climate impacts: a new start in civil protection
Family Summary:
For a crisis-proof Germany, the strengthening of civil protection is being addressed as part of the programme. All projects and measures therefore follow the four guidelines: Always prepared, early warning, efficient action, good post-crisis care. Ensuring the safety of citizens in the event of crises and disasters is a core task of the state. A well-equipped and efficient civil defence system is essential for the safety of all.

The pandemic, disasters caused by climate impacts such as the floods in summer 2021 or forest fires and the changed security situation in Europe due to the Russian war of aggression against Ukraine, which violates international law, have significantly increased and changed people's need for protection and security: Civil protection must be reorganised and Germany's federal structure must be made more crisis-proof and resilient. Civil protection must offer people effective protection across administrative levels and sectors. The focus must be on well thought-out preparation for crisis management.
Document Title: Arming our country against crises and climate impacts: a new start in civil protection (Unser Land gegen Krisen und Klimafolgen wappnen: Neustart im Bevölkerungsschutz)

Family Name: Implementation Plan for Carbon Peaking in Urban and Rural Construction (notice 53/2022)
Family Summary: The plan was introduced by a notice from the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development and the National Development and Reform Commission. According to this plan, new-build public buildings and factories in town and cities should be covered at 50% by solar panels by 2025.

Family Summary: This Decree establishes a mission team to accelerate the development of climate technologies and encourage investment into research and development.
Document Title: Decree 1685

Family Name: Agreement for a greener and safer Denmark (2022)
Family Summary:
Denmark will quadruple the production of solar and wind energy on land by 2030, as well as have the possibility of quintupling offshore wind turbine power. The ambition is that all gas in Denmark will be green by 2030, and that from 2035 there will be no homes heated with gas.

The parties to the agreement agree on important concrete initiatives that can support a quadrupling of total electricity production from solar energy and onshore wind by 2030.

The parties agree, among other things, on:

  • That the state should help realize large energy parks on land
  • To make it possible to install renewable energy plants in manor landscapes
  • To strengthen local support for the installation of solar and wind energy
  • A new fund to support renewable energy on less accessible areas (e.g. solar cells on roofs)
  • Faster and better work by authorities
  • Strengthened guidance on environmental assessments and nature directives
  • Better data basis for installers and authorities
  • To support the electricity grid to keep up
  • Fivefold increase in offshore wind

The parties to the agreement have agreed to enable the expansion of an additional 4 GW of offshore wind by the end of 2030. This will allow Denmark's offshore wind production to more than fivefold over the next 8 years.
Document Title: Agreement for a greener and safer Denmark (2022)

Family Name: Climate Agreement on Green Power and Heat (2022)
Family Summary: This Agreeemnt focuses on accelerating the green transition by phasing out fossil fuels in buildings, aiming for no gas boilers for home heating by 2035 and 100% green gas by 2030. It mandates local heat planning, expands district heating, and increases offshore wind capacity.
Document Title: Climate Agreement on Green Power and Heat (2022)

Family Name: Green Fund
Family Summary:
The governance reserves DKK 1½ billion in 2024 and DKK 3¼ billion annually from 2025-2040 for the green fund. Thus, a total of DKK 53½ billion is prioritized for the green fund from 2024-2040.

The green fund must be prioritised in the smartest way possible and contribute to Denmark's green transition, including meeting Denmark's climate goals. The green fund must be prioritized for larger and longer-term investments in climate, green energy and the environment, such as afforestation, CO2 capture and storage, climate adaptation, clean drinking water and pyrolysis.
Document Title: Agreement on partial implementation of the Green Fund (2024)

Family Name: National Program for Waste Management (PNGR)
Family Summary: The National Waste Management Program serves as a strategic guideline for the Regions and Autonomous Provinces in planning waste management. Specifically, the Program establishes the macro-objectives and defines the criteria and strategic guidelines for the development of waste management plans. In its initial implementation, it constitutes one of the structural reforms for the implementation of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR). With a six-year timeframe (2022–2028) and based on the European framework, it is designed to guide public policies and incentivize private initiatives for the development of a sustainable and circular economy, for the benefit of society and environmental quality.
Document Title: Ministerial Decree 257/2022

Family Name: Green Tax Reform Agreement
Family Summary:
Announced as part of Denmark’s 2021 Recovery and Resilience Plan, the Green Tax Reform introduces a more ambitious corporate carbon (CO2) tax. The agreement introduces a CO2 tax rate of 750 DKK/tonne of emitted CO2 in 2030 for companies that fall outside of the European ETS. The agreement also introduces a minimum price ‘floor’ that can come into effect if the European ETS underperforms in reducing emissions. The energy taxes that apply to fossil fuels will change to a total tax up to 750 DKK per tonne of CO2 emitted in 2025.

Other parts of the agreement include tax reliefs; a fund for green transition; increasing green business; and financing.
Document Title: Green Tax Reform - Report (February 2024)

Family Name: Regulation on Climate Change Presidency Service Units (Department of Climate Change)
Family Summary: The administrative organisation under the Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change for these activities is the Department of Climate Change (DOCC), according to Turkey's 2024 Biennial Transparency Report. The DOCC specifically focuses on climate policy development, monitoring, and reporting on climate change-related activities. The DOCC is also assigned as the focal national administration of Türkiye to the UNFCCC. The organisational structure, working procedures, and principles of the DOCC were officially established with the publication in the Official Gazette on 21 June 2022, numbered 31873. This legal framework provides the DOCC with a clear mandate and operational guidelines to effectively carry out its duties.
Document Title: Regulation on Climate Change Presidency Service Units (Department of Climate Change)

Family Name: Agreement on regulatory framework for CO2 storage in Denmark (2022)
Family Summary:
In this agreement, a decision was taken ensure that the Danish state will be a co-owner of CO2 storage licenses in Denmark. The Danish subsoil is a shared resource, and state participation ensures that the state can have influence on subsoil activities related to CCS. State participation will also ensure that Danish society gets a share in any potential economic gains from CO2 storage.

The parties to the agreement furthermore decided that state ownership will be assumed by Nordsøfonden (the Danish State Subsurface Resource Company), which is deemed to have the necessary experience and competence from its engagement in oil and gas activities to protect the state's interests.
Document Title: Agreement on regulatory framework for CO2 storage in Denmark (2022)

Family Name: National Strategy for the Circular Economy
Family Summary: The National strategy for the circular economy establishes Italy’s national framework for the transition from a linear economic model to a circular economy. It defines a roadmap of policy measures and targets aimed at strengthening the market for secondary raw materials, improving waste prevention, reuse and recycling, and promoting eco-design and product life-cycle sustainability. It also introduces regulatory, fiscal and governance tools to support circular supply chains, innovation and industrial symbiosis while contributing to national climate and environmental objectives.
Document Title: National strategy for the circular economy (Strategia Nazionale per l’Economia Circolare)

Family Name: Regulation on the Department of Climate Change
Family Summary:
The purpose of this Regulation is to establish the procedures and principles regarding the implementation of activities to be carried out by the Department of Climate Change, the duties and authority of its service units, and its organisational structure and operations. Its duties range from conducting studies and determining policies to monitoring international negotiation processes and managing revenue generated from the emissions trading system.

The Department is subordinate to the Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change. It has various service units on climate negotiations, climate change adaptation, climate finance, carbon pricing, greenhouse gas reduction policies, monitoring, technology and green transition, etc.
Document Title: Regulation on the Department of Climate Change

Family Name: Directive 2022:67 on economic instruments to promote the transition to a circular economy
Family Summary:
As promoting the green industrial revolution is one of the government's highest priority issues, this Directive sets up a committee to investigate which areas and what ways economic instruments can be used to promote the transition to a circular economy. The investigation shall focus on areas with a significant environmental or climate impact, where instruments can promote such a transition in a significant and socio-economically effective way.

The committee shall, among other things, analyse in which areas, e.g. material flows, product groups or services, it is appropriate to use economic instruments to promote the transition to a circular economy, suggest economic instruments that are appropriate to use for the areas identified and the reasons for the chosen instruments, and where applicable, report why an analysed area is less suitable for economic instruments to promote the transition to a circular economy. The committee must submit the report no later than 30 April 2024.
Document Title: Directive 2022:67 on economic instruments to promote the transition to a circular economy

Family Name: 14th Five-Year Plan for National Comprehensive Disaster Prevention and Reduction
Family Summary: This Plan seeks to prevent and reduce disasters and direct investment in technology that supports early warning systems and adaptation to climate change.
Document Title: 14th Five-Year Plan for National Comprehensive Disaster Prevention and Reduction

Family Name: Revised National Energy Policy
Family Summary: Nigeria's Revised National Energy Policy from 2022 provides overarching guidance, directions and context for the development of the energy sector. The policy is organised into sub-policies by subsector, including nuclear, renewables, bio-energy, energy efficiency, and environment/climate change. On renewable energy, it aligns with the National Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Policy (NREEEP) of 2015, promoting significant expansions in renewable electricity supply with a particular focus on hydropower and solar generation. The policy promotes additional decarbonisation through energy efficiency and technological innovation in high-emission sectors, aiming to mainstream the consideration of climate issues at both ends of any fossil fuel supply chains. In the Environment and Climate Change sub-policy, the need to protect forest systems is emphasised, and regulatory measures are promoted to reduce effects of energy infrastructure on forests.
Document Title: Revised National Energy Policy

Family Name: Agreement on follow-up to the evaluation of the Planning Act (2022)
Family Summary:
This is an Agreement between the government (Social Democracy), the Liberal Party, the Danish People's Party and the Conservative People's Party on the follow-up to the evaluation of the Planning Act, etc. dated 15 June 2022.

As follow-up to the agreement Denmark in better balance – Better framework for municipalities, citizens and businesses throughout the country, the rules of the Nature Protection Act on beach protection, dune conservation and the sea and river protection line were changed, and new appeal boards were established in the planning area and the environment. The parties also agreed that an evaluation should be carried out.

This Agreement follows up on the evaluation and implement a number of changes to the Planning Act and other relevant legislation.

The agreement covers the following main themes:

1. Climate, green transition and nature

2. Urban development, etc.

3. New development opportunities on the coasts and for tourism

4. Mobile coverage throughout the country

5. Simplification, administrative relief and digitalization

6. The complaints system

7. Changes to other rules

8. Køge Bugt Strandpark - modernisation and climate protection
Document Title: Agreement on follow-up to the evaluation of the Planning Act (2022)

Family Name: The National Strategy on Adaptation to Climate Change 2022-2030 (First version)
Family Summary:
The National Strategy on Adaptation to Climate Change for the period 2022- 2030 to 2050 (SNASC) and the National Action Plan for implementation of the National Strategy on Adaptation to Climate Change (NSSAC) focus on adaptation strategies in the following sectors/areas:

  • Forests
  • Biodiversity and ecosystem services
  • Population, public health and air quality
  • Education and awareness
  • Cultural heritage
  • Urban systems
  • Agriculture and rural development
  • Energy
  • Transport
  • Tourism
  • Industry
Document Title: The National Strategy on Adaptation to Climate Change 2022-2030 (First version)

Family Name: National Urban Policy 2030
Family Summary:
The Policy directs Polish cities treat the low-carbon and carbon-free collective transport and non-motorised traffic as their priorities, limit the use of resources, and adapt to the effects of climate change better. NUP 2030 proposes priority directions of solutions around, inter alia, the issue of quality of natural environment in cities and adaptation measures towards climate change.

The Policy states: Counteracting negative consequences of climate change for cities and inhabitants such as droughts or undercutting requires implementation of nature-based solutions. Nature-based solutions are the most effective in shaping urban climate. Urban greenery, including single trees and bushes, is of great importance, since they significantly improve water management and microclimate on a microscale.
Document Title: National Urban Policy 2030

Family Name: Implementation Plan for Synergies of Pollution-Carbon Reduction
Family Summary: To achieve the goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, this Plan was issued, promoting the synergies of pollution-carbon reduction through integrated planning, deployment, implementation, and assessment. The guiding principles are capturing synergy and efficiency gains, strengthening source control, optimising technical approaches, fostering innovative mechanisms, and encouraging pilot programs. The goals are, by 2025, establish a basic framework for synergies of pollution-carbon reduction, achieve significant progress in structural optimization and green low-carbon development in key regions and sectors, develop a number of replicable best practices, and effectively improve the synergy between pollution control and carbon reduction; and by 2030, significantly enhance the synergy capacity of pollution-carbon reduction, contributing to the carbon peaking target, and achieve significant progress in collaborative efforts of carbon peaking and air quality improvement in key regions for air pollution control". By 2030, the sales volume of new energy vehicles in the key regions for air pollution control will account for around 50% of the total new vehicle sales.
Document Title: Implementation Plan for Synergies of Pollution-Carbon Reduction

Family Name: National Food Strategy 2022
Family Summary: In June 2022, the Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs published the UK's National Food Strategy. In the objectives outlined in section 10 of the strategy, reducing greenhouse gas emissions in agricultural and food production, in line with net zero and biodiversity targets, is listed as one of the strategies key objectives. The document also states that the government will published a land use framework in 2023, that will outline a framework for meeting net zero and biodiversity targets in agricultural production, while continuing to support farmers adapt to climate change.
Document Title: National Food Strategy 2022

Family Name: Regulation on Green Certificate for Buildings and Settlements
Family Summary: The Green Certificate Regulation for Buildings and Settlements in Turkey, published in the Official Gazette 31864 by the Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change, establishes evaluation and certification systems aimed at reducing the environmental impact of buildings and settlements. It promotes the efficient use of natural resources and energy, and sets out the procedures and principles regarding the qualifications of green certificate experts, green certificate assessment experts, and educational organizations. The regulation also defines the evaluation criteria for green buildings and settlements, focusing on sustainability performance factors such as energy efficiency, resource use, and overall environmental impact.
Document Title: Regulation on Green Certificate for Buildings and Settlements

Family Summary: Resolution PP-277 co-ordinates ministries in response to ongoing land-degradation issues and approves an attached action plan for the short and medium term. Family Name: Electricity (Promoting Renewable Energy Through Green Energy Open Access) Rules, 2022
Family Summary:
These Rules allow businesses to buy renewable power directly from generators, bypassing traditional utility companies. Based on these Rules, there shall be a uniform renewable purchase obligation on all obligated entities in the area of a distribution licensee. Any entity, whether obligated or not, may elect to generate, purchase and consume renewable energy as per their requirements through the following means: their own generation from renewable energy sources where power shall be transmitted by using open access; by procuring renewable energy through open access from any developer either directly or through a trading licensee or through power markets; by requisition from a distribution licensee, by consuming green energy from a captive power plant; or by purcashing renewable energy certificates, or by purchasing green hydrogen or green ammonia.

All applications for open access to green energy in this regard shall be allowed by the nodal agency within a period of fifteen days.

The Rules were amended on 27 January 2023, amongst other changes, to allow any consumer to elect to purchase green energy either up to a certain percentage of the consumption or its entire consumption and they may place a requisition for this with their distribution licensee, which shall procure such quantity of green energy and supply it and the consumer shall have the flexibility to give separate requisition for solar and non-solar power.

A further amendment was made on 23 May 2023 to provide that only consumers who have contracted demand or sanctioned load of Hundred kW or more, either through single connection or through multiple connections aggregating HundredkW or more located in same electricity division of a distribution licensee, shall be eligible to take power through Green Energy Open Access and there shall be no limit of supply of power for the captive consumers taking power under Green Energy Open Access.
Document Title: Electricity (Promoting Renewable Energy Through Green Energy Open Access) (Second Amendment) Rules, 2023.

Family Name: Presidential Decree 5681 on Regulatory Impact Analysis
Family Summary: Presidential decree on the Procedures and Principles for the Implementation of Regulatory Impact Analysis was published in the Official Gazette on 4 June 2022, under issue number 31856, outlined the mandatory guidelines for conducting regulatory impact assessments (RIAs) and strategic environmental assessments (SEAs). These critical tools ensure that regulatory and non-regulatory proposals are developed with a clear understanding of their potential impacts. Türkiye mandated the preparation of RIAs to systematise the evaluation of potential effects of proposed regulations, including climate change-related ones.
Document Title: Presidential Decree 5681 on Regulatory Impact Analysis

Family Name: Roadmap for the Development of Offshore Wind Energy
Family Summary: This Roadmap was developed with the support of the International Finance Corporation (IFC), in line the country’s commitments to decarbonization and sustainable development. It considers a high-growth scenario in which 7.2 GW of offshore wind power plants are planned be implemented by 2040 and a low growth scenario with an estimated potential of 1.5 GW implemented offshore wind power plants.
Document Title: Roadmap for the Development of Offshore Wind Energy

Family Name: Long-term Climate Strategy
Family Summary: This strategy is mandated by Chile's Framework Law on Climate Change. It sets out the country's mitigation and adaptation goals to comply with international commitments. It seeks to increase the share of renewable energy to 65% in 2025 and 80% of the general energy supply in 2030. Furthermore, it seeks to reduce emissions in the mining sector by 40% and in the transport sector by 40% by 2025.
Document Title: Long-term Climate Strategy

Family Name: National strategy for the reduction of Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (ENREDD+)
Family Summary: This is a management strategy, national in scope, which seeks to contribute to global emissions reduction by improving forest governance in the country and managing financial incentives to reduce forest loss and degradation, as well as for forest conservation, increasing forest cover and sustainable forest management. It was launched within the scope of the UNFCCC in alignment with the National Strategy Forestry 2050; the National Program of Forest Restoration 2021–2025; the strategy Panama Climate Change National (ENCCP) 2050; the National Change Plan Climate for the Agricultural Sector; the Nationally Determined Contribution updated to 2020, Law No. 1 of 3 of February 1994 and the draft framework law of climate change.
Document Title: National strategy for the reduction of Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (ENREDD+)

Family Name: Hydrogen Strategy for Austria
Family Summary: This strategy sets out the Austrian Government's approach to promoting the production and use of climate-neutral hydrogen in certain hard to abate sectors, as part of its approach to acheiving climate neutrality by 2040.
Document Title: Executive summary of Hydrogen Strategy

Family Name: National Environmental Master Plan for Strategic Interventions (NEMPSI) (2022-2032)
Family Summary:
The NEMPSI seek to address environmental degradation and guide strategic interventions over 10 years, aligned to national and international frameworks like the Tanzania Development Vision 2025 and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The overall objective of the NEMPSI is to guide strategic and coordinated environmental interventions at all levels based on spatial variation of environmental challenges and intervention options.

It identifies Tanzania’s major environmental challenges to include land degradation, deforestation, biodiversity loss, climate change, deterioration of water sources, coastal and marine degradation, waste management, environmental pollution, biotechnology and invasive species. Interventions for addressing climate change impacts are provided to meet the goal of reducing climate vulnerability and enhancing resilience to climate change impacts. They are intended to enhance climate resilience of people, ecosystems and productive sectors by reducing adverse impacts of climate change and building capacity for harnessing climate change mitigation opportunities.
Document Title: National Environmental Master Plan for Strategic Interventions 2022 -2032

Family Name: Water Policy Concept of the Slovak Republic to the year 2030
Family Summary:
The implementation of the Water Policy Concept is based on the application of and compliance with the following principles:• Water as a vital environmental component and natural resourceWatercourses and the land under them are owned by the state. Water is essential for the functioning of society and ecosystems. Water and water-dependent ecosystems provide services and functions that a fundamental impact on the quality, quantity, availability and distribution of water. The use of water and ecosystems is only possible to the that their resilience is not impaired and that at least good ecological status of surface water bodies or good quantitative and chemical status of groundwater can be achieved/maintained.• Adapting to climate changeThe effects of climate change are manifested in all areas by an increase in the frequency of extreme meteorological and hydrological events (drought and water scarcity, floods), changes in the distribution of annual runoff, changes in groundwater recharge, landslides and soil erosion, changes in the stability of ecosystems and thus their ability to retain water and transform surface runoff, the spread of invasive species, etc. Adaptation measures and increasing the resilience of the landscape take precedence over addressing the consequences and negative impacts.• Water as a human rightAccess to water and sanitation is recognised as a fundamental human right and every member of society must have access to water in sufficient quantity and of adequate quality, including vulnerable and socially disadvantaged groups or individuals.

The objective is to have a resilient landscape capable of retaining water and mitigating the negative impacts of climate change, creating water resources of the required quality for sustainable consumption.
Document Title: Resolution 372/2022 n the Draft Water Policy Concept of the Slovak Republic through 2030 with a Vision to 2050

Family Name: Energy Resiliency Policy
Family Summary: The Policy's vision is for the Philippines to have climate change-adaptive and resilient energy infrastructures and systems for enhanced energy security. The goal is to transform into a climate-proof and resilient infrastructure and systems to withstand, reduce the impact, recover faster, and Build Back Better against evolving hazards and threats to sustain the socio-economic development of the country. The interventions are in the areas of energy resiliency; disaster prevention and mitigation; disaster preparedness; disaster response and early recovery; and disaster rehabilitation and recovery.
Document Title: Energy Resiliency Policy

Family Name: Water and Sewerage Master Plan Republic of Maldives 2021-2035
Family Summary: This Plan is aimed at ensuring water security, integrated water resources management, sewerage and wastewater management. Climate-related strategies include ensuring climate-resilient and cost-effective water supply and sewerage systems, and promoting environmentally sound technologies and practices towards building sustainable climate-resilient island communities.
Document Title: Water and Sewerage Master Plan Republic of Maldives 2021-2035

Family Name: Resolution on the Slovenian Scientific Research and Innovation Strategy 2030 (ReZrIS30)
Family Summary: The Resolution on the Slovenian Scientific Research and Innovation Strategy 2030 (ReZrIS30) integrates climate and energy objectives as core priorities of Slovenia’s research and innovation policy, aligning them with the 2030 Agenda and the green transition. It emphasises research on environmental protection, sustainable management of natural resources, and biodiversity, alongside the development of climate-resilient systems for energy, food, and water. It establishes 5 key objectives contributing to moving towards this goal.
Document Title: Resolution on the Slovenian Scientific Research and Innovation Strategy 2030 (ReZrIS30)

Family Name: National Health Strategic Plan 2022-2026
Family Summary: The National Health Strategic Plan 2022-2026 provides a framework for guiding healthcare development nationally in the near and long term, taking into account a wide range of challenges and influences. The plan underscores the need to improve climate resilience, in order to minimise the growing public health threats of extreme weather. It promotes the development of a Health National Adaptation Plan, harmonised with the national climate policy of 2020, and suggests increased access to global climate finance for healthcare investment. The plan also promotes general awareness-raising, closer collaboration with the national climate change department, and a mainstreaming of climate concerns in the development of new healthcare facilities.
Document Title: National Health Strategic Plan 2022-2026

Family Name: National Roadmap for Net Zero Carbon Buildings
Family Summary: This roadmap highlights key actions such as urban planning, sustainable materials, efficient transportation and distribution, innovative design, labelling and certification, as well as optimized water and energy use, and effective waste management. It also evaluates the current state of the buildings sector and examines the potential social and environmental impacts of achieving net zero buildings on a national scale.
Document Title: National Roadmap for Net Zero Carbon Buildings

Family Name: Notice on Financial Support for Carbon Neutralisation
Family Summary:
This document provides guidelines on leveraging the role of fiscal policies to achieve the country's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, set in 2021 in the "1+N" Action Plan. According to the guidelines, the country will update its financial policy framework by 2030 to support green and low-carbon development, notably making use of market mechanisms like carbon and pollution discharge trading. 

According to its stated objectives, a first step in the enrichment of fiscal policy tools as well as the tax policy framework will be reached by 2025. This should cover all regions and industries. Before 2030, the fiscal and taxation policy system will be finalised, enabling the carbon-peaking threshold. A long-term mechanism to promote green and low-carbon development will be gradually established. Before 2060, the policy system of financial support for green and low-carbon development will enable to reach carbon neutrality.
Document Title: Notice on Financial Support for Carbon Neutralization

Family Name: White Paper on Transport Policy 2021
Family Summary: This White Paper is a policy document aimed at providing a transport system that is environmentally benign and supports economic and environmental sustainability and inclusive growth. This Paper was published after a review of the White Paper on National Transport Policy of 1996. One of the environmental considerations is to reduce the impact of transport on climate change by promoting low-carbon modes of transport in the design of transportation systems. The White Paper sets out the policy of planning for the provision of transport infrastructure within an integrated environmental management approach which will include, inter alia, the performance of environmental impact assessments. Considerations will include environmental impacts, energy conservation, the transport of dangerous materials and the conservation of scarce infrastructure construction materials. In addition, low-carbon modes of transportation should be prioritised in the design of transportation systems. Other policy measures include fuel efficiency; lower energy intensity; reduction of negative impact on biodiversity and air quality; and the mixed-use developments to provide places of work close to home.

Family Summary: Sri Lanka's National Environmental Action Plan 2022-2030 implements national law and policy to promote a range of measures ensuring environmental protection and sustainability. Family Name: Egypt National Climate Change Strategy (NCCS) 2050
Family Summary:
Egypt's National Climate Change strategy is designed to consolidate all aspects of climate change in one document to be a basic reference that ensures the integration of climate change dimension into general planning of all sectors in the country. It was developed at the request of the National Council for Climate Change.

The strategy contains five key goals and sets directions to achieve each objective:
Goal 1: Achieving Sustainable Economic Growth and Low-Emission Development in Various Sectors 
Goal 2: Enhancing Adaptive Capacity and Resilience to Climate Change and Alleviating the Associated Negative Impacts 
Goal 3: Enhancing Climate Change Action Governance 
Goal 4: Enhancing Climate Financing Infrastructure 
Goal 5: Enhancing Scientific Research, Technology Transfer, Knowledge Management and Awareness to Combat Climate Change
Document Title: Egypt National Climate Change Strategy (NCCS) 2050

Family Name: Research Infrastructure Roadmap 2030 (NRRI 2030)
Family Summary: The Research Infrastructure Roadmap 2030 (NRRI 2030) is Slovenia’s strategic document defining national priorities for the development, upgrading, and international integration of research infrastructures as a key foundation for scientific excellence and innovation. It identifies priority international projects and national infrastructure areas, aligns them with EU frameworks (notably ESFRI) and the national Research and Innovation Strategy, and sets directions for funding, governance, and long-term sustainability. The roadmap emphasises improving access to advanced research facilities, strengthening cooperation between academia and industry, and enhancing Slovenia’s participation in European research networks. It also highlights the role of research infrastructures in addressing environmental, technological, and economic transitions. It mentions energy and energy efficiency as a national priority field
Document Title: Research Infrastructure Roadmap 2030 (NRRI 2030)

Family Name: European Commission Communication: REPowerEU Plan
Family Summary:
This plan has been prepared by the EU Commission and seeks to "rapidly reduce dependence on Russian fossil fuels and fast forward the green transition". It sets the Commission's specific objectives in that regard, calls for enhancing targets' ambitions, and is supported by a number of strategies and plans, such as the EU solar strategy, the EU 'Save Energy' communication and the Biomethane action plan. 

The plan notably aims to 1) improve long-term energy efficiency measures, including an increase from 9% to 13% of the binding Energy Efficiency Target under the ‘Fit for 55' package, 2) diversify supplies, 3) scale up and speeding-up of renewable energy, and 4) reduce fossil fuel consumption in industry and transport.

The plan further quantifies the investments needed to meet the targets; for the Commission, an additional investment of €210 billion between now and 2027 is required.
Document Title: European Commission Communication: REPowerEU Plan

Family Summary: Nigeria's National Agricultural Technology and Innovation Policy 2022-2027 aims to promote technological enhancement of the agricultural sector, to improve productivity and resilience in the medium-term. A key component of this is the introduction and expansion of climate-smart agricultural practices. This includes digital systems to collect, analyse and distribute data, including climatic data, early warning systems and insurance services. It also includes directly physical interventions such as the deployment of water storage and distribution infrastructure.
Document Title: National Agricultural Technology and Innovation Policy 2022-2027

Family Name: Royal Decree 376/2022 on Sustainability Criteria for Biofuels and Renewable Gases
Family Summary:
The Royal Decree 376/2022 implements elements of the European Directive (EU) 2018/2001, promoting the use of renewable energy. It establishes sustainability criteria and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction targets for biofuels, bioliquids, and biomass-based fuels. These criteria are prerequisites for financial support and inclusion in renewable energy objectives. Key measures include verification systems to ensure compliance, energy efficiency requirements for electricity generation facilities, and incentives such as double-counting for certain advanced biofuels and biogas in transportation.
The decree also sets sales and consumption targets for biofuels and biogas (2023-2026) and limits the contribution of food-based biofuels. It regulates the guarantees of origin for renewable gases, ensuring transparency and consumer information. To demonstrate compliance, stakeholders must use accredited certification systems, ensuring sustainable practices across the production and commercialization chain. This policy aims to align Spain’s energy transition with EU climate goals.
Document Title: Royal Decree 376/2022 on Sustainability Criteria for Biofuels and Renewable Gases

Family Name: Royal Decree 962/2024 on  electricity production from renewable marine sources
Family Summary:
The Royal Decree 962/2024 regulates the production of electricity from renewable marine energy sources, such as offshore wind and ocean energy, in Spain. The decree sets out procedures for competitive bidding for the authorisation of such installations, focusing on minimising environmental impacts and ensuring compatibility with other maritime activities. It outlines a competitive bidding process for renewable marine energy projects, where successful bids receive economic incentives, capacity access to the energy grid, and priority for maritime land occupation concessions. Special provisions are made for innovative projects and installations located in ports of national interest.
The decree also aligns with European and national climate and energy objectives, including Spain's 2030 renewable energy targets. It is designed to foster the development of renewable marine energy, boost technological innovation, and meet the goals of decarbonization and energy security. Furthermore, it incorporates elements from Spain's Plan de Recuperación and updates prior regulations, such as the 2007 Royal Decree 1028, to account for advances in floating technologies and the growing scope of offshore renewable projects.
Document Title: Royal Decree 962/2024 on  electricity production from renewable marine sources

Family Summary:

Family Summary:

Family Name: Aotearoa New Zealand's First Emissions Reduction Plan (ERP)
Family Summary:
"Te hau mārohi ki anamata - Towards a productive, sustainable and inclusive economy" is Aotearoa New Zealand's first emissions reduction plan. It was developed following the advice of the Ināia tonu nei: a low emissions future for Aotearoa report submitted by the Climate Change Commission in June 2021. The ERP contains strategies, policies and actions for achieving the first emissions budget.


Notable actions promoted by the ERP include the following:
  •  increasing access to electric vehicles (EVs), beginning the process of decarbonising heavy transport and freight and helping more people to walk, cycle and take public transport
  • supporting businesses to improve energy efficiency and move away from fossil fuels, such as coal, by continuing to roll out the Government Investment in Decarbonising Industry fund
  • banning new low- and medium-temperature coal boilers and phasing out existing ones
  • introducing an emissions pricing mechanism for agriculture
  • accelerating the delivery of agricultural emissions reduction tools and technologies for farmers and farming businesses through the establishment of a new Centre for Climate Action on Agricultural Emissions
  • reducing the amount of waste (including food waste) going to landfills, investing in waste infrastructure and expanding landfill gas capture
  • establishing native forests at scale to develop long-term carbon sinks and improve biodiversity
  • accelerating the supply of woody biomass to replace coal and other carbon intensive fuels and materials
  • driving mission-led innovation in some of the most challenging parts of our economy through climate innovation platforms and the wider research, science and innovation system
  • requiring refrigerants to be captured and destroyed when heating and cooling systems reach the end of their life.
Document Title: Aotearoa New Zealand's First Emissions Reduction Plan (ERP)

Family Name: Climate Adaptation Action Plan - The Swedish Board of Agriculture's work on climate adaptation
Family Summary:
The Swedish Board of Agriculture developed an action plan for climate adaptation in 2017. According to the Ordinance (2018:1428) on government agencies' climate adaptation work, the Swedish Board of Agriculture must revise the action plan at least every five years. This report is the Swedish Board of Agriculture's action plan for climate adaptation for 2022 and beyond.

The three overall strategic goals are:

• Sweden shall have competitive, profitable and growing food production.

• Sweden shall achieve its environmental goals and production shall become more resource-efficient.

• Sweden shall have good animal health, good animal welfare and good plant protection.
Document Title: Climate Adaptation Action Plan The Swedish Board of Agriculture's work on climate adaptation

Family Name: Permitting Action Plan
Family Summary:
This action plan aims to enable the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law's objectives (economic growth, communities resilience, climate change combatting, and nature conservation) to be fulfilled. It focuses on making environmental review and permitting processes more efficient and transparent, guided by science, and shaped by early and meaningful public input. To achieve this, five actions should be undertaken: (1) accelerating permitting through early cross-agency coordination to appropriately scope reviews, reduce bottlenecks, and use the expertise of sector-specific teams; (2) establishing clear timeline goals and tracking key project information to improve transparency and accountability, providing increased certainty for project sponsors and the public; (3) engaging in early and meaningful outreach and communication with Tribal Nations, States, territories, and local communities; (4) improving agency responsiveness, technical assistance, and support to navigate the environmental review and permitting process effectively and efficiently; and (5) adequately resourcing agencies and using the environmental review process to improve environmental and community outcomes.The document states that it "leverages existing permitting authorities and new provisions included in the BIL, such as new coordination and timeline requirements3 that apply to major transportation projects, and new FAST-41 requirements and authorities, including those for covered projects in the renewable or conventional energy production, electricity transmission, water resources, broadband, pipelines, carbon capture, and other infrastructure sectors."

Under this plan, the administration gathered experts on the following topics:

  • Offshore wind energy and transmission;
  • Onshore renewable energy and transmission;
  • Broadband;
  • Production and processing of critical minerals;
  • Transportation; and
  • Climate-smart infrastructure.

Family Name: Water Plan of Slovakia
Family Summary:
The Water Plan of Slovakia incorporates climate change primarily from an adaptation perspective, recognising it as a key driver affecting water resources and management. The document focuses on assessing and monitoring the impacts of climate change on hydrological systems, including changes in water availability, groundwater levels, and the increasing frequency and intensity of droughts and floods. It emphasises the development of tools and data systems for early detection and management of extreme events, as well as the integration of climate considerations into long-term water planning and risk management. Chapter 9 focuses on the protection from the harmful effects of water and climate change.

This plan is valid from 2022 to 2027.

Family Summary: Technical Guideline TSG-1-004:2022 Energy Efficiency replaces echnical Guideline TSG-1-004:2010 and sets out key requirements for the thermal protection of building envelopes and energy systems in accordance with the Energy Efficiency in Buildings Regulations (PURES). Family Name: Rules on the efficient use of energy in buildings
Family Summary:
These Rules set out the technical requirements for the construction of nearly zero-energy buildings, which must be met in order to achieve the energy efficiency of buildings, specifically regarding insulation, heating, cooling, domestic hot water preparation, lighting, and renewable energy sources including on-site electricity production. These rules are in accordance with EU legislation.

The installation of high-efficiency combined heat and power (CHP) systems and solar photovoltaic (PV) systems for electricity generation is further encouraged through these rules, which stipulate that a building is considered energy efficient if at least 50% of its final energy demand for heating, cooling, and domestic hot water is met through such systems.

Beyond energy performance, it emphasises resource efficiency, including durability, reparability, recyclability and use of recycled materials.The plan seeks to accelerate energy savings, strengthen market surveillance, and modernise labels to guide consumers and support the transition to a circular and climate-neutral economy. It contributes to EU goals on energy security and affordability, responding to the need for reduced energy demand and more sustainable product design across the single market.

Family Name: Export Development Canada's Sustainable Finance Guarantee
Family Summary:
Export Development Canada (EDC) has launched a new guarantee product to help carbon-intensive companies secure financing as they transition towards cleaner activities. It will partially guarantee loans from commercial lenders to heavy-emitting companies in the country, including in sectors such as cement, aerospace, and oil and gas, to support their carbon reduction efforts. Such efforts include projects for hydrogen, bioenergy, carbon capture and storage, carbon trading, renewable infrastructure, sustainable agriculture, microgrids, grid modernisation, as well as production efficient technology.

Bank of Montreal (BMO) is the first financial institution to sign up to the new initiative, with EDC set to cover 50% of loans the bank provides to Canadian companies, up to a maximum amount of US$60mn per obligor and with a tenor limit of seven years.

Family Summary: This Plan lays out key tasks in three areas: crop farming; animal husbandry. These tasks include reducing methane emissions from rice paddies, lowering the intensity of enteric methane emissions from ruminants, and decreasing methane and nitrogen dioxide emissions from livestock manure management. Low-carbon practices will also be used for the fisheries sector. As for carbon sequestration, protective and organic agricultural practices will be utilised, including the protection of black soil; and fishery practices that improve carbon sequestration will be used.

Family Summary:
Sida is the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, , a government agency that works to reduce poverty and promote development in other countries. This policy is part of Sida’s management system for climate and environment based on the Regulation for Environmental Management in Government Agencies (2009:907) and the Regulation for Government Climate Adaptation Work (2018:1428).This policy shall guide the formulation of Sida’s internal goals and proposals for strategic objectives that Sida proposes to the Swedish Government.

Sida's strategic areas are: climate adaptation and mitigation; sustainable use, restoration and conservation of forest, land, water and marine resources; and reduction of air, soil and water pollution.
Document Title: Sida's Climate and Environment Policy

Family Name: A new reform package for the Danish economy (2022)
Family Summary:
This reform package invests in the labour market of the future, in the context of the green transition, technological development and globalisation which are changing the needs of companies and placing new demands on the skills of the workforce.

Three climate vocational schools will be established to offer vocational and continuing education that is particularly relevant for sectors that contribute to meeting the climate goals in 2030 and in the longer term in 2050. This applies to, for example, education within the agricultural, transport, energy, construction, industry and waste sectors. The climate vocational schools can also enter into collaborations with, for example, business academies, knowledge centers, other vocational education institutions. Climate vocational schools must be powerhouses for education and competence development for green transition and showcases for leading technologies in close collaboration with leading companies in the green area.

There is agreement that the business community, including large Danish green export companies and foundations, is invited to participate actively in the establishment of the climate vocational schools. 100 million DKK will be allocated annually in 2024-2029 and 30 million DKK annually thereafter.
Document Title: A new reform package for the Danish economy (2022)

Family Name: Slovenian Tourism Strategy 2022-2028
Family Summary:
According to the Slovenian Tourism Strategy 2022-2028, tourism contributed 9.9% to Slovenia's GDP in 2019 and represents a key economic sector. However, it is also highly sensitive to the impacts of climate change. Winter tourism is among the sectors particularly vulnerable to climate-related risks.

The Strategy has 5 strategic goals, being the Strategic Goal 4 “Decarbonising and Rebalancing Slovenian Tourism” with a stakeholders’ responsibility and commitment to reduce environmental and climate impacts, and become the most advanced industry in terms of the EU's sustainability commitments and Slovenia’s transition towards carbon neutrality.
Document Title: Slovenian Tourism Strategy 2022-2028

Family Name: Resolution No. 790 on the approval of rules for the carbon credit registry
Family Summary:
This Resolution contains rules for the creation and maintenance of a carbon credit registry and carbon credit transactions.

The designated operator of the registry shall register climate projects, amend data, open and close accounts, perform transactions, issue carbon units for circulation and conduct other transactions relating to legislation on the limitation of greenhouse gas emissions. The Resolution outlines the information on the account holders and the climate projects that the registry shall contain.

The Resolution is in effect from 1 September 2022 to 1 September 2028.
Document Title: Resolution No. 790 on the approval of rules for the carbon credit registry
