Family Name: Resolution 40156/2022 - Indicative Action Plan 2022-2030 for the development of the Rational and Efficient Energy Use Program (PROURE).
Family Summary:
The resolution adopts the Indicative Action Plan (PAI) for the development of the Rational and Efficient Energy Use Program (PROURE) 2022-2030, which is an integral part of the resolution. The PAI-PROURE 2022-2030 aims to reduce the technological gap in energy use by 2030 through the adoption of cost-efficient measures, equipment and fuel change. The goal is for the technological transformation of the energy sector to be a key part of Colombia's sustainable development.

The specific goals of the PAI-PROURE 2022-2030 are:

  • Update the inventory of energy efficiency measures in different consumption sectors, considering technological innovations and advances.
  • Integrate energy efficiency actions and measures in the hydrocarbon extraction and production sectors, mining, and thermoelectric generation.
  • Determine national indicative energy savings goals based on a cost-effectiveness evaluation of the energy efficiency measures.
  • Identify which energy efficiency measures should be eligible for tax incentives.
  • Propose complementary public policy actions to help achieve the energy efficiency goals set in the PAI-PROURE 2022-2030.
Document Title: Indicative Action Plan 2022-2030 for the development of the Rational and Efficient Energy Use Program (PROURE)

Family Name: 14th Five-Year Plan for Urban Drainage and Flood Prevention System Construction Action Plan
Family Summary: This Plan includes an action to strengthen the assessment of urban waterlogging risks, with the analysis of the changing characteristics of local rainstorms in time and space under the context of climate change. This assessment involves the timely revision of the urban rainstorm intensity formula and urban flood control and drainage planning, fully considering flood risks, and compiling urban waterlogging risk maps. The construction of new urban areas should strengthen site selection demonstration, rationally lay out urban functions, and strictly implement drainage and flood control facilities, storage space, rainwater runoff and vertical control requirements. The Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, the Ministry of Water Resources, and the China Meteorological Administration are responsible according to their respective duties.
Document Title: 14th Five-Year Plan for Urban Drainage and Flood Prevention System Construction Action Plan

Family Name: The Government’s Bioeconomy Strategy
Family Summary:
This Strategy targets sustainable, effective and profitable production, extraction and use of renewable, biological resources into food, feed, ingredients, health products, energy, materials, chemicals, paper, textiles and numerous other products. National focus on the bioeconomy should lead to increased value creation and employment, reduced emission of climate gasses, as well as more efficient, profitable and sustainable use of renewable biological resources.

This Strategy regards the internalisation of negative effects on the climate and the environment in the product prices would be the most efficient way of promoting the bioeconomy. Climate-related measures include:

  • Developing know-how on climate effects from increased use of bio-based alternatives to fossil-based materials and chemicals;
  • Establishing a new investment company which will contribute to the reduction of climate gas emissions;
  • Ensuring a public procurement practise contributing to the reduction of environmentally degrading effects and an advancement of climate friendly solutions, where relevant, which includes taking life cycle costs into consideration;
  • Following up on forest related measures to increase carbon storage and access to environmentally friendly raw materials and building materials; and
  • Upgrading industry skills regarding efficient, climate friendly and sustainable production and extraction.
Document Title: The Government’s Bioeconomy Strategy

Family Name: Decree No. 2022-615 relating to the experimentation of an interest-free loan to buy low-carbon vehicles in low-emission zones
Family Summary:
This decree validates interest-free loans for the acquisition of low-emission vehicles in certain low-emission mobility zones (ZFE-m), in line with article 107 of the 2021 climate and resilience law. Eligible vehicles must emit 50 grams of CO2 emissions per kilometre or less and be priced under 45,000 euros for a private car and under 60,000 euros for commercial vans. Applying households must meet conditions of revenue (must be under 14,000 euros). 

Pending local data on air quality in 2022, the ZFE-m of Paris and the Greater Paris Metropolises, Lyon, Aix-Marseille and Rouen are eligible for the scheme.
Document Title: Information on Decree No. 2022-615

Family Name: PNM 2035 - National mobility plan
Family Summary: This document sets the government's plan for the transport sector over the period 2022-2035. It notably seeks to increase the modal share of active transport modes.
Document Title: PNM 2035 - National mobility plan

Family Name: National Gender and Climate Action Plan
Family Summary: The National Gender and Climate Change Plan outlines a strategy for promoting gender equality in Panama’s response to climate change. It aligns the climate commitments in Panama’s energy, forests, watersheds, marine-coastal sector, biodiversity, agriculture, livestock and aquaculture, resilient human settlements, public health, sustainable infrastructure, and circular economy sectors to gender theory concepts.
Document Title: National Gender and Climate Change Plan

Family Name: Rules for the Submission and Verification of Greenhouse Gas Emissions Reports
Family Summary: Establishes Russia's MRV system under the Federal Law on Limiting Greenhouse Gas Emissions and creates the national GHG emissions register, defining how regulated organisations must prepare, submit, and verify their annual inventories.
Document Title: Resolution No. 707/2022 on Rules for the Submission and Verification of Greenhouse Gas Emissions Reports

Family Name: Work Plan for Strengthening the Higher Education Talent Training System for Carbon Peak and Carbon Neutrality
Family Summary: This Work Plan sets out the actions for cultivating various talent pools to achieve carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, which requires broad and profound eocnomic and social systemic change. The key tasks include strengthening green and low-carbon education; building a high-level science and technology platform; accelerating the development of disciplines and talents for energy storage, hydrogen energy, carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS), and carbon finance and trading; upgrade traditional energy education; and deepening the integration of industry and education sector collaboration.
Document Title: Work Plan for Strengthening the Higher Education Talent Training System for Carbon Peak and Carbon Neutrality

Family Name: Resolution No. 126 of 2022 adopting Policy Guidelines for Sustainable Cattle Farming 2022-2050
Family Summary:
This resolution of the Ministry of Agriculture and the Ministry of Environment adopts Policy Guidelines for Sustainable Cattle Farming in line with Colombia's Constitutional norms for the protection of the natural environment and international commitments, including under the UNFCCC.


The Guidelines set out a roadmap for the period between 2022 - 2050, with the aim of ensuring that livestock farming in Colombia is modernized and reconverted to sustainable livestock production systems, low in GHG emissions and adapted to climate change to ensure the reilience of the territory. The Guidlines aim to operate in a way that preserves the social and cultural fabric around livestock and promotes green growth and responsible consumption.
Document Title: Resolution No. 126 of 2022

Family Name: Decree No. 2022-538 defining the system of penalties applicable in the event of disregard of the provisions relating to claims of carbon neutrality in advertising
Family Summary: This decree sets procedural rules on sanctions relating to the assertion in an advertisement that a product or service is carbon neutral. It amends chapter IX of Title II of Book II of the Environmental Code by adding article R. 229-110. This article gives the Minister responsible for the environment the ability to sanction non-compliance with the band and failure to fulfil obligations provided for in Article L. 229- 68.
Document Title: Decree No. 2022-538 defining the system of penalties applicable in the event of disregard of the provisions relating to claims of carbon neutrality in advertising

Family Name: Decree No. 2022-539 relating to carbon offsetting and claims of carbon neutrality in advertising
Family Summary: This decree aims to prevent greenwashing. It amends the Environment Code to specify the rules applying to advertisers claiming in an advertisement that a product or service is “carbon neutral”, “zero carbon”, “with zero carbon footprint”, “climate neutral”, “fully offset”, “100% offset” or employs any wording of equivalent meaning or scope. It obliges advertisers to produce a report on the greenhouse gas emissions of the product or service concerned covering its entire life cycle. This report is updated every year. Emission reductions resulting from projects to offset greenhouse gas emissions must also be reported according to rules set in the decree.
Document Title: Decree No. 2022-539 relating to carbon offsetting and claims of carbon neutrality in advertising

Family Name: Ministerial Resolution No. 090-2022-MINAM. Guidelines to be followed for the preparation of Regional Greenhouse Gas Inventories (IRGEI) [Resolución Ministerial Nº090-2022-MINAM. Pautas que deben seguirse para la elaboración de los Inventarios Regionales de Gases de Efecto Invernadero (IRGEI)]
Family Summary: Peru's Ministerial Resolution N° 090-2022-MINAM establishes comprehensive guidelines for the elaboration of Regional Greenhouse Gas Inventories, providing regional governments with standardised methodological tools to quantify emissions and removals at the departmental level. These guidelines align with the IPCC 2006 methodology and support the implementation of Regional Climate Change Strategies by enabling the identification of emission sources across four key sectors: Energy, Industrial Processes and Product Use, Agriculture/Forestry/Land Use, and Waste. The framework ensures consistency between regional inventories and the National Greenhouse Gas Inventory (INFOCARBONO), whilst providing calculation spreadsheets and technical guidance adapted to departmental characteristics and economic activities.
Document Title: Guidelines for the preparation of regional greenhouse gas inventories (Pautas para la elaboración de inventarios regionales de gases de efecto invernadero)

Family Name: National environmental protection strategy by 2030, vision 2050
Family Summary:
The overall aim of the strategy by 2030 is to prevent the increasing pollution trend and environment degradation; solve urgent environmental issues; and gradually improve and restore environmental quality; prevent biodiversity decline; increase capacities in climate change response in an active manner; ensure environmental security; develop models of circular economy, green economy, low carbon; strive to achieve the country’s 2030 sustainable development goals.

Vision to 2050 includes having a good quality of the environment, ensuring the people’s right to live in a clean and safe environment; biodiversity is preserved and conserved and ecological balance is ensured; proactively responding to climate change; society is in harmony with nature, a circular economy, green and low-carbon economy is formed and developed, towards the goal of carbon neutrality by 2050.
Document Title: National environmental protection strategy by 2030, vision 2050

Family Name: National Solid Waste Plan (PLANARES)
Family Summary: Sets out a long-term strategy for modernising Brazil’s solid waste management and operationalising the National Solid Waste Policy. It includes targets such as the conversion of open dumpsites into sanitary landfills by 2024, and increasing waste recovery to 50% over the next two decades. It aims to support Brazil’s broader methane-reduction targets through improved disposal practices and expanding biomass and related energy-recovery measures.
Document Title: National Solid Waste Plan

Family Name: Costa Rica's National Plan of adaptation to Climate Change (2022-2026)
Family Summary: This plan is approved under the first Action Plan of the National Policy for Adaptation to Climate Change of Costa Rica 2018 - 2030 (PNACC). It aims to implement the adaptation objectives set out in the country's updated NDC, namely to strengthen the conditions of social, economic and environmental resilience of the country in the face of the effects of climate change, through the development of capacities and information for decision-making, the inclusion of adaptation criteria in financing and planning instruments, the adaptation of services public, productive systems and infrastructure, and the implementation of nature-based solutions.
Document Title: Costa Rica's National Plan of adaptation to Climate Change (2022-2026)

Family Name: National Determined Contribution (NDC) Implementation Plan
Family Summary: This document was identified in the country's updated NDC as well as in an official press release. However, the full text of was not available at the time of writing.
Document Title: National Determined Contribution (NDC) Implementation Plan

Family Name: Decree No. 2022-540 relating to the health, citizenship and environmental education committee
Family Summary: This decree sets rules for the implementation of the extension of the jurisdiction of health and citizenship education committees to environmental issues. The decree was taken in application of the 2021 Climate and Resilience law. The decree modernises the functioning of this body.
Document Title: Decree No. 2022-540 relating to the health, citizenship and environmental education committee

Family Name: National Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy and Action Plan to 2030 (Stratégie nationale de réduction des risques de catastrophe à l’horizon 2030 et plan d‘action)
Family Summary: Tunisia's National Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy and Action Plan to 2030 aims to strengthen disaster preparation and response in the long term. It acknowledges climate change as a major threat, and elevates climate adaptation as a key instrument for disaster risk reduction. The action plan contains provisions to: enhance funding and capacity to meteorological monitoring infrastructure and early-warning systems; mainstream climate adaptation in education at all levels; enact governance reforms to improve inter-sectoral co-ordination.
Document Title: National Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy and Action Plan to 2030 (Stratégie nationale de réduction des risques de catastrophe à l’horizon 2030 et plan d‘action)

Family Name: Strategic Forestry Program for Mexico 2025 (PEF 2025) [Programa Estratégico Forestal para México 2025 (PEF 2025)]
Family Summary: The Strategic Forestry Program for Mexico 2025 (PEF 2025) is Mexico’s first long-term strategic framework for sustainable forest development, aiming to balance economic productivity with ecological preservation. The policy acknowledges the growing global emphasis on environmental sustainability and the need to shift from exploitative resource use to circular, low-waste models. It highlights climate change as a critical challenge, noting that rising temperatures and drought frequency threaten forest productivity, increase wildfire risks, and disrupt water cycles. To counter these threats, the plan promotes sustainable forest management (SFM), including fire prevention, reforestation, and biodiversity conservation, while reducing deforestation rates by an estimated 3.9 million hectares compared to business-as-usual scenarios.
Document Title: Strategic Forestry Program for Mexico 2025 (Programa Estratégico Forestal para México 2025)

Family Name: Energy Security Strategy (UK)
Family Summary:
This document was released in the wake of rising energy prices notably induced by consequences of the COVID-19-induced economic crisis and the invasion of Ukraine. It builds on policies set out in the "ten point plan for a green industrial revolution" and the "net zero strategy". It aims at providing secure, clean and affordable British energy for the long term, by weaning the country off "expensive fossil fuels" and developing "diverse sources of homegrown energy". 

The strategy:
  • Provides immediate financial support to households and the industry to reduce energy bills
  • sets targets of energy efficiency improvements in the buildings sector
  • aims to "fully utilise" the North Sea fossil fuels reserves, use the empty caverns for CO2 Storage, bring through hydrogen to use as an alternative to natural gas and use  offshore expertise to support the offshore wind sector
  • sets enhanced mid-term targets of new renewables capacity, especially offshore wind, and to a lesser extent onshore wind and solar.
  • focus on building new nuclear plants
  • boost hydrogen production, notably to store excess renewable electricity
  • on networks, storage and flexibility: anticipate needs to minimise cost and public disruption, and hyper-flexibility in matching supply and demand to reduce energy waste.
  • work with international partners to maintain stable energy markets and prices, reduce the use of fossil fuels globally, reduce global reliance on Russian fossil fuels whilst pivoting towards clean, affordable energy.
Document Title: British Energy Security Strategy

Family Name: Wildfire Risk Five-Year Monitoring, Maintenance, and Treatment Plan
Family Summary: This plan is coupled with the 10-year wildfire crisis strategy. It aims at reducing wildfire risk by improving fuel management treatments, monitoring hasardous fuels management effectiveness, and maintain investments. It also calls for a more strategic cooperation between federal agencies and local actors, to enhance geospatial mitigation planning, and to leverage existing authorities and resources.
Document Title: Wildfire Risk Five-Year Monitoring, Maintenance, and Treatment Plan

Family Name: Charging Service Regulation
Family Summary:
The purpose of this Regulation is to determine the procedures and principles regarding the establishment of charging units and stations that provide electrical energy to electric vehicles, the operation of charging networks and charging stations connected to the charging network, and the provision of charging services.

This Regulation covers the establishment and operation of charging units and charging stations, excluding mobile charging units that provide electrical energy for roadside assistance to electric vehicles, the creation of a charging network, the licensing of charging network operators and the regulation of their activities, the rights and obligations of charging network operators and charging station operators and users, and the procedures and principles regarding the establishment and operation of a free access platform.
Document Title: Charging Service Regulation

Family Name: Polar strategy of France on the horizon 2030
Family Summary: This document sets France's vision for the Arctic and the Antarctic regions to 2030. It defines a geopolitical vision, stresses the need to enhance research efforts, and discusses governance matters. All aspects are discussed with climate change as a key theoretical component.
Document Title: Information presented to the National Assembly on the issue of the Arctic and Antarctic Poles

Family Name: Advanced energy-saving investment promotion support project
Family Summary:
This subsidy aims to support renewal of equipment with high energy consumption efficiency performed at factories and business sites.
(A) Advanced business: Focusing on energy -saving investments that have high technical and energy -saving performance and are now expected to expand their introduction potential, etc.
(B) Made -to -order business: We provide support for equipment renewal, process renovation, and energy -saving efforts in which multiple businesses are linked, including the introduction of custom -made equipment that requires individual design.
(C) Designated equipment introduction project: Supports renewal to specific Uti triti facilities, production equipment, etc. with high energy saving performance.
(D) Enemiya business: Energy management support services with enema business operators will be concluded, and we will support efficient and effective energy -saving efforts by EMS control and operation improvement.

This policy is part of a 10 year strategy, and should contribute to the reduction of 18.46 million kl in crude oil conversion by further promotion of energy -saving capital investment.
Document Title: Advanced energy-saving investment promotion support project

Family Name: National Transport and Logistics Master Plan by 2053
Family Summary: This plan aims to ensure environmental awareness in and increase the efficiency of the transportation and logistics sectors. It seeks to integrate climate change mitigation and adaptation strategies by 1) increasing the use of renewable energy sources, 2) reducing the country’s dependency on oil, 3) applying the “polluters pay” principle and 4) developing green transportation infrastructure and green logistics investments and practices.
Document Title: National Transport and Logistics Master Plan by 2053

Family Name: The Environmental Foundation
Family Summary:
The Environmental Foundation is a joint project, initiated by the Federal Ministry for Climate Protection, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology, along with the Ministry of Labour and social partners. This project aims to train at least 1000 workers in the field of environmental and climate protection in three years time.

The foundation began operations in April 2022, and aims to provide training to primarily unemployed people who do not have sufficient qualifications to find employment. This project aims to provide these job seekers with the required qualifications and training around the clean energy sector, e.g. installing PV panels, constructing wind turbines, and switching to modern heating systems.

The project has a total cost of EUR 17.5 million, of which EUR 10 million will come from the government’s labour budget and EUR 7.5 million will be supplied by companies. The educational foundation follows the 2021 Job.ReAct pilot programme in Austria, which offered jobs in ecological and sustainable sectors to unemployed people, co-funded by the European Union’s European Social Fund.
Document Title: The Environmental Foundation

Family Name: National Electric Mobility Policy and Market Readiness Framework for Zimbabwe
Family Summary: The policy and framework aims to support Zimbabwe’s transition to a low-carbon transport system, in line with the country’s commitments under the Paris Agreement and its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). This is intended to achieve the national objectives for sustainable development, reduce the country’s greenhouse gas emissions, and improve air quality. It identifies barriers and potential policy measures for large-scale deployment of electric vehicles in Zimbabwe.
Document Title: National Electric Mobility Policy and Market Readiness Framework for Zimbabwe

Family Name: National Food Security Research Programme
Family Summary:
The strategic objectives of the Programme are: consolidating a sustainable agricultural policy capable of strengthening the country's food security; increasing domestic agricultural yields, reducing imports of basic agricultural and food products; reducing waste and ensuring the non-exploitation of products; modernising agricultural administration and its governance; combating desertification, protecting natural ecosystems, particularly forests, and conserving soils; and increasing the production of animal and plant proteins; the development and optimisation of fisheries and aquaculture resources; the integrated management of water resources; and the reuse of treated wastewater.

The programme covers climate change adaptation, including evaluating the risks of climate change; identifying the agricultural zones with high risk; developing systems and indicators to be alert to such risks, and implementing strategies for adaptation.
Document Title: National Food Security Research Programme

Family Name: 2022-2030 Environmental Protection and Climate Change Management Development Programme
Family Summary: The Environmental Protection and Climate Change Management Development Programme outlines a wide range of challenges and potential measures for mitigating and adapting to climate change over the 2022-2030 time period. A particular emphasis in the programme is on the challenges posed by inefficient heat use in the buildings sector, which reduces the climate benefits of existing renewables deployment by inflating overall energy demand. Other issues the programme articulates include lack of trained personnel in the green sector, and poor transparency of climate risk and mitigation data. It calls for improved training, governance and regulatory enforcement in a range of sectors.
Document Title: 2022-2030 Environmental Protection and Climate Change Management Development Programme

Family Name: Guidance on climate adaptation in planning
Family Summary: The Danish Housing and Planning Agency, in collaboration with the Danish Environmental Protection Agency, the Danish Coastal Directorate, the Danish Institute for Water Resources and Energy and in dialogue with the Danish Council for Local Government, has prepared a guide that was first published in 2019 and is now available in a final version. The guide provides guidance on the rules of the Planning Act from 2018, which require the designation of areas threatened by flooding and erosion, as well as the establishment of mitigation measures when planning for new urban areas, densification of existing cities or special technical facilities within the designated areas.
Document Title: Guidance on climate adaptation in planning

Family Name: Guidance on planning for flood and erosion prevention
Family Summary:
The Housing and Planning Agency, in collaboration with the Danish Environmental Protection Agency, the Danish Coastal Directorate, the Danish Institute for Infrastructure and Transport, the Danish Agency for Data Supply and Efficiency, the Danish Energy Agency and the Danish Local Government Authority, have prepared this guidance, which can support municipalities in their work with preventive planning for flooding and erosion.

In the future, Denmark is expected to experience more severe weather, which may mean more floods and more coastal retreat (erosion). This can be expensive – both for the private economy and the economy as a whole. Physical planning is an important tool when municipalities need to secure new and existing urban and summer house areas against flooding and erosion.

The guidance provides factual knowledge about the legal possibilities and concrete examples from existing municipal plans and local plans, where municipalities have incorporated flood protection and prevention in their planning in various ways. It is hoped that this guidance can create a good basis for how the rules in the Planning Act can contribute to preventing flooding and erosion.
Document Title: Guidance on planning for flood and erosion prevention

Family Name: British Energy Security Strategy
Family Summary: This strategy sets out the UK's plan to increase energy independence, which includes increasing energy efficiency, reducing demand, increasing renewable power generation and increasing domestic production of oil and gas.
Document Title: British Energy Security Strategy

Family Name: Climate and defence strategy
Family Summary: The French Ministry for the Armed Forces has developed a comprehensive “Climate Defence” strategy to prepare the defence tool for the climate challenge. It is based on strengthening the Ministry’s organisation in terms of knowledge and anticipation of strategic climate change issues and the implementation of an ambitious adaptation policy by all the armed forces, directorates and departments.Implementation of the Climate Defence strategy must be based on a level of strategic coordination and general policy direction in order to federate and engage all of the Ministry’s stakeholders in a comprehensive approach structured around four main focus areas:Developing knowledge and the ability to anticipate the strategic challenges associated with climate change;Initiating a process to adapt the defence tool to predictable disruptions caused by climate change;Continuing the Ministry for the Armed Forces’ contribution to collective efforts for mitigation and the energy transition;Stepping up cooperation on the defence issues of climate change within the Ministry and at the interministerial and international levels.
Document Title: Climate and defence strategy

Family Name: National Biodiversity Strategy 2023-2030
Family Summary:
The Strategy is formulated based on Article 6 of the Convention on Biological Diversity and as a basic plan under Article 11 of the Basic Act on Biodiversity (Act No. 58 of 2008), to achieve the target to effectively conserve 30% or more of land and sea ecosystems by 2030. The Strategy contains many references to climate issues, including: utilising nature-based solutions for disaster prevention and mitigation and community development; promoting nature restoration for climate change adaptation and mitigation, as carbon sinks, including in marine ecosystems; promotion of the consideration of biodiversity in the introduction of renewable energy; realising a nature-positive economy, with investment and financing promoting activities to conserve and restore biodiversity.

The Strategy sets out the goals for 2030; the basic strategies; the foundations and mechanisms for effective implementation of the strategy including basic principles, evaluation of progress, roles for each actor and collaboration; and the action plan. The action plan consists of restoring the ecosystem health; using nature to resolve societal issues; realising a nature-positive economy; recognising the value of biodiversity and taking action in daily living and consumption activities; and establishing infrastructure to support biodiversity initiatives and promote international collaboration.
Document Title: National Biodiversity Strategy 2023-2030

Family Name: Forestry Development Program for 2022-2026
Family Summary: Tajikistan's Forestry Development Program for 2022-2026 aims to create and restore over 15,000 ha of forests, acknowledging their role in climate change adaptation and mitigation nationally and internationally. It promotes potential future participation in the Green Climate Fund, to invest in further adaptation measures. It also promotes the incorporation of a larger diversity of native trees and shrubs into forestry schemes, to ensure the climate-resilience of forest ecosystems and their beneficial effects.
Document Title: Forestry Development Program for 2022-2026

Family Name: Decree No. 2022-452 relating to the ban on the use of heating or air conditioning systems in the public domain outdoors
Family Summary: This decree restricts the use of heating and air conditioning systems (AC) in outdoor settings. In July 2022, other decrees were issued to restrict the use of AC for shops that let their doors open.
Document Title: Decree No. 2022-452 relating to the ban on the use of heating or air conditioning systems in the public domain outdoors

Family Name: Pathway to Net-Zero Emissions in 2050
Family Summary: In March 2022, Taiwan published its action pathway to achieve 2050 net zero emissions. It contains four major transition strategies: energy transition, industrial transition, lifestyle transition, and social transition. It also set outs two governance areas: technology R&D and climate legislation. Finally, it establishes 12 key strategies: wind/solar PV, hydrogen, innovative energy, power systems and energy storage, energy saving and efficiency, CCUS, carbon-free and electric vehicles, resource recycling and zero waste, carbon sinks, green lifestyle, green finance and just transition.

Family Name: 2030 emissions reduction plan - Canada’s Next Steps for Clean Air and a Strong Economy
Family Summary:
This plan is the first developed under the Canadian Net-Zero Emissions Accountability Act. It develops sectoral projections of emissions reductions to 2030 with a view on achieving net-zero by 2050, details the government's low-carbon strategy and announces $9.1 billion in new federal investments. The government notably states its objective of reducing methane emissions from the fossil fuel industry. Progress under the plan will be reviewed in 2023, 2025, and 2027. Additional targets and plans will be developed for 2035 through to 2050.

Sectoral goals, funding and measures laid out in the document include the following: 

  • Homes and buildings: develop a $150 million Canada Green Buildings Strategy and provide $458.5 million of new investment to the Canada Greener Homes Loan program in order to reduce energy costs
  • Indigenous climate action: the Low Carbon Economy Fund is renewed ($2.2 billion funding) and include a dedicated $180 million Indigenous Leadership Fund
  • Energy systems: support regional growth, jobs and transformation of energy systems with a $25 million investment in Regional Strategic Initiatives
  • Electricity grid: aim of establishing a Pan-Canadian Grid Council to promote clean electricity infrastructure investments in coordination with provinces and utilities. Investment of $600 million in the Smart Renewables and Electrification Pathways Program and $250 million to support predevelopment work for large clean electricity projects
  • Clean transport: reduction of emissions from light, and heavy vehicles. provision of $1.7 billion to extend the Incentives for Zero-Emission Vehicles (iZEV). $400 million in additional funding for zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) charging stations. The Canada Infrastructure Bank will also invest $500 million in ZEV charging and refueling infrastructure. Sales mandate to be put in place to ensure thresholds of clean vehicles sales. Development of a MHDV ZEV (medium- and heavy-duty zero emission vehicles) regulation. 
  • Industry: developing a carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) strategy, introducing an investment tax credit to incentivize the development and adoption of this important technology, and investing $194 million to expand the Industrial Energy Management System to support ISO 50001 certification, energy managers, cohort- based training, audits, and energy efficiency-focused retrofits for key small-to-moderate projects.
  • Agriculture: help the sector to adopt sustainable practices thanks to an investment of $470 million in the Agricultural Climate Solutions: On-Farm Climate Action Fund. Further to this, there will be a tripling of investment of the funding for the Agricultural Clean Technology Program (to $330 million) to support the purchase of energy-efficient equipment. $100 million will also be invested on science to support a sectoral transition to net-zero by 2050.
  • Environment: promote nature-based emissions reductions through an additional provision of $780 million for the Nature Smart Climate Solutions Fund.
  • carbon pricing: develop strategy to "guarantee the price of pollution", using legislative approaches and investment approaches, like carbon contracts for differences. Aims to see carbon price rising by $15 a year in order to reach $170/tonne by 2030.
Document Title: 2023 Progress Report

Collection Summary:
This collection is made up by documents that relate to Colombia's fair energy transition. 
The Fair Energy Transition is a key process in the fight against climate change, involving the transformation of current energy systems to one based on a low-GHG emitter, having fairer and more sustainable model. 
Colombia's green and fair energy transition strategy seeks to pursue descarbonisation in a way that takes into account paramount elements such as (i) equity and social, environmental and energy justice; (ii) graduality and sovereignty while pursuing the progressive replacement of the current matrix with a cleaner and more efficient one; (iii) social participation; and, (iv) knowledgeable to create economic alternatives.

Family Summary: The general objective of the policy is to consolidate the energy transition process through the formulation and implementation of intersectoral actions and strategies that promote the country's economic, energy, technological, environmental and social growth in order to advance towards its energy transformation.This policy contains four strategic axes with the aim of (i) increasing energy security; (ii) encouraging knowledge and innovation in energy transition; (iii) generating greater competitiveness and economic development from the energy sector; and (iv) developing an energy system with low GHG emissions to reduce the effects of climate change.

Family Name: Forest Action Plan 2020-2030
Family Summary:
This Plan identifies the Marshall Islands' highest priorities for forest resource management and needs for assistance from the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Forest Service (USFS). It contains a Statewide Forest Resource Assessment that provides an analysis of forest conditions and trends in the state and delineates priority rural and urban forest landscape areas; and a Statewide Forest Resource Strategy that provides long-term strategies for investing resources to manage priority landscapes identified in the assessment.

The priority issues identified are conservation of biodiversity; food security and sustainable livelihoods; coastal reinforcement; and urbanisation. One of the climate-related actions involves managing and restoring trees and forests, for instance through management plans, and establishing a Forestry Division within the Ministry of Natural Resources and Commerce. Another climate-related actioin is to restore fire-adapted lands and reduce the risk of wildfire impacts.

Family Name: National Zero Methane Programme
Family Summary:
The National Zero Methane Program is another action by the Brazilian government that encourages the development of a sustainable economy and aims to reduce methane emissions into the environment.

Brazil will stimulate and help sectors of the economy - such as agriculture and livestock - in the production and use of biomethane and biogas. Financial support will come from public banks, through specific financing and a line of credit.

These incentives will enable the insertion and construction of new centers for the production of biomethane, increasing the product's supply. There will also be the installation of green corridors for the supply of heavy vehicles.

The program will also develop scientific-technological research on biogas and biomethane and will encourage national and international cooperation for actions to reduce methane emissions.

Family Name: Qatar Financial Centre Sustainable Sukuk and Bonds Framework
Family Summary:
In 2022, the Qatar Financial Centre (QFC) developed a Sustainable Sukuk and Bonds Framework, which is based on the International Capital Markets Association (ICMA)’s Green Bond Principles (GBP) 2021, Social Bond Principles (SBP) 2021, and Sustainability Bond Guidelines (SBG) 2021. This framework would collectively, provide voluntary yet internationally accepted principles and guidelines for the issuance of such instruments. 

The proceeds from any Sukuk / bonds must always be utilized solely for purposes that are aligned with the type of issuance (i.e. Green, Social or Sustainability) and provide clear environmental and/or social benefits.

The net proceeds from an issuance, can be used by way of investment in, financing and/or refinancing of eligible green and/or social projects. Examples of eligible green projects include: 

(a)            Climate Change Adaptation or Mitigation (including efforts to make infrastructure more resilient to impacts of climate change, as well as information support systems, such as climate observation and early warning systems).

(b)            Pollution Prevention and Control (including reduction of air emissions, greenhouse gas control, soil remediation, waste prevention, waste reduction, waste recycling and energy/ emission-efficient waste to energy).

(c)            Renewable Energy (including production, transmission, appliances and products).

(d)            Sustainable Water and Wastewater Management (including sustainable infrastructure for clean and/or drinking water, wastewater treatment, sustainable urban drainage systems and river training and other forms of flooding mitigation).

(e)            Energy Efficiency / Green Technology (such as in new and refurbished buildings, energy storage, district heating, smart grids, appliances and products).

(f)             Circular Economy Adapted Products, Production Technologies, and Processes (such as the design and introduction of reusable, recyclable and refurbished materials, components, and products; circular tools and services).

(g)            Clean Transportation (such as electric, hybrid, public, rail, non-motorized, multi-modal transportation, infrastructure for clean energy vehicles and reduction of harmful emissions).

(h)            Green Buildings (that meet regional, national or internationally recognized standards or certifications for environmental performance or projects that reduce pollution, produce energy through renewable energy).

(i)              Environmentally sustainable management of living natural resources and land use (including environmentally sustainable agriculture; environmentally sustainable animal husbandry; climate smart farm inputs such as biological crop protection or drip-irrigation; environmentally sustainable).

(j)              Terrestrial and aquatic biodiversity conservation (including the protection of coastal, marine and watershed environments).

The QFC Sustainable Sukuk and Bonds Framework is a voluntary guideline that neither constitutes an offer to purchase or sell securities nor constitute specific advice of whatever form (tax, legal, environmental, accounting or regulatory) in respect of Green, Social or Sustainable Sukuk and Bonds or any other securities. Issuers opt to adopt and implement the framework voluntarily and independently.
Document Title: QFC Sustainable Sukuk and Bonds Framework

Family Name: Carbon Credit Management Guideline and Mechanism
Family Summary:
The Carbon Credit Management guidelines and mechanism aim to provide guidelines regarding carbon credit management for the purpose of achieving the national greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets under the Paris Agreement. The trading and utilisation of carbon credits in Thailand can occur either over the counter or through a designated carbon credit trading center, each governed by specific regulations. Participants, whether buyers, sellers, or users, must adhere to the requirements set forth by the Thailand Greenhouse Gas Management Organisation, including opening an account in the registry system, registering trades or transfers of credits, and reporting their use to the organisation for recording and unit cancellation. Carbon credit traders must establish agreements, ensure compatibility between trading and registry systems, and report transactions through the trading center. Additionally, third-party Validation and Verification Bodies must seek registration with the Organisation to conduct project validation and verification activities.

Obligations of Project Developers

  • Register project implementation with Thailand Greenhouse Gas Management Organisation for any projects located in Thailand that use independent standards and issue carbon credits.
  • Report the issuance, purchase, sale, transfer, cancellation, and use of carbon credits.
  • Apply for registration of the project and open an account in the registry system.
  • Apply for issuance of the carbon credits coming from the implementation of its project.
  • Marking the carbon credits for offsetting or compensation purposes should be in accordance with the law establishing the Thailand Greenhouse Gas Management Organisation.

Use of Carbon Credits for International Purposes - carbon credits should be generated via the following project types:

  • Renewable energy or energy that substitutes fossil fuels;
  • Increase of the efficiency of electricity generation and heat generation;
  • Use of public transportation system;
  • Use of electric vehicles;
  • Increase of engine efficiency;
  • Increase of the efficiency of energy consumption in buildings and factories, and in households;
  • Use of clinker substitutes;
  • Waste management;
  • Community wastewater management;
  • Methane gas recovery;
  • Industrial wastewater management;
  • Mitigation, absorption, and removal of greenhouse gases from forestry and the agricultural sector;
  • Capture, storage, and/or utilisation of greenhouse gases; and other projects specified by the Committee.

Project characteristics:

  1. Project leading to GHG reduction, enhancement of GHG sinks or reservoirs in addition to those highlighted in national GHG mitigation plans.
  2. Project supporting GHG reduction in order to achieve Thailand's nationally determined contribution (NDC) and its Long-Term Low GHG Emissions Development Strategy.
  3. Fair credit allocation considering investment contribution, international rules or international framework, or applicable regulation.
  4. Crediting period not exceeding the timeframe of the NDC implementation period.
  5. Project promotes development and transfer of advanced technology and innovation.
  6. The mitigation outcomes operated in Thailand for international use should be certified in tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2eq).
  7. Issuance of a letter of authorisation to use carbon credits for an international objective should follow these steps:
  • Detailed project summary in accordance with the international agreement and submit it to the Office;

Family Name: Carbon Credit Management Guideline and Mechanism
Family Summary:
The Carbon Credit Management guidelines and mechanism aim to provide guidelines regarding carbon credit management for the purpose of achieving the national greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets under the Paris Agreement. The trading and utilisation of carbon credits in Thailand can occur either over the counter or through a designated carbon credit trading center, each governed by specific regulations. Participants, whether buyers, sellers, or users, must adhere to the requirements set forth by the Thailand Greenhouse Gas Management Organisation, including opening an account in the registry system, registering trades or transfers of credits, and reporting their use to the organisation for recording and unit cancellation. Carbon credit traders must establish agreements, ensure compatibility between trading and registry systems, and report transactions through the trading center. Additionally, third-party Validation and Verification Bodies must seek registration with the Organisation to conduct project validation and verification activities.

Obligations of Project Developers

  • Register project implementation with Thailand Greenhouse Gas Management Organisation for any projects located in Thailand that use independent standards and issue carbon credits.
  • Report the issuance, purchase, sale, transfer, cancellation, and use of carbon credits.
  • Apply for registration of the project and open an account in the registry system.
  • Apply for issuance of the carbon credits coming from the implementation of its project.
  • Marking the carbon credits for offsetting or compensation purposes should be in accordance with the law establishing the Thailand Greenhouse Gas Management Organisation.

Use of Carbon Credits for International Purposes - carbon credits should be generated via the following project types:

  • Renewable energy or energy that substitutes fossil fuels;
  • Increase of the efficiency of electricity generation and heat generation;
  • Use of public transportation system;
  • Use of electric vehicles;
  • Increase of engine efficiency;
  • Increase of the efficiency of energy consumption in buildings and factories, and in households;
  • Use of clinker substitutes;
  • Waste management;
  • Community wastewater management;
  • Methane gas recovery;
  • Industrial wastewater management;
  • Mitigation, absorption, and removal of greenhouse gases from forestry and the agricultural sector;
  • Capture, storage, and/or utilisation of greenhouse gases; and other projects specified by the Committee.

Project characteristics:

  1. Project leading to GHG reduction, enhancement of GHG sinks or reservoirs in addition to those highlighted in national GHG mitigation plans.
  2. Project supporting GHG reduction in order to achieve Thailand's nationally determined contribution (NDC) and its Long-Term Low GHG Emissions Development Strategy.
  3. Fair credit allocation considering investment contribution, international rules or international framework, or applicable regulation.
  4. Crediting period not exceeding the timeframe of the NDC implementation period.
  5. Project promotes development and transfer of advanced technology and innovation.
  6. The mitigation outcomes operated in Thailand for international use should be certified in tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2eq).

Family Name: Sectoral roadmaps for Promoting Transition Finance
Family Summary:
The Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) developed this document to set a direction for transition toward achieving carbon neutrality in 2050 for GHG-intensive industries. The roadmap is expected to assist financial institutions in determining whether a company's strategies and initiatives toward decarbonisation qualify for transition finance when the company raises funds.

  • Chemical 
  • Power

  • Oil

Family Name: Presidential Decree No. 22-122 creating a High Energy Council
Family Summary: The Council decides on the strategies to be followed with regard to the country’s energy security, especially through preserving, renewing and developing national reserves of hydrocarbons, following up and evaluating the implementation of long-term plans to develop the basic structures for the production, transport, supply, storage and distribution of energy materials and the development of new and renewable energies. The Council also decided on strategies regarding the energy transition towards a new national model for energy production and consumption.
Document Title: Presidential Decree No. 22-122 creating a High Energy Council

Family Name: Presidential Decree No. 22-112 establishing the High Energy Council (15 March 2022)
Family Summary: Presidential Decree No. 22-112 of 12 Shaabane 1443, corresponding to 15 March 2022, establishes the High Energy Council and specifies its missions and composition. This decree is part of the general and strategic development of energy policy for the preservation, renewal, and development of national hydrocarbon reserves, monitoring and evaluating the implementation of long-term plans for the development of infrastructure for the production, transportation, supply, storage, and distribution of energy products, as well as the introduction and development of new and renewable energies, while ensuring the mineral resources necessary for their development, and also developing energy strategies related to the environment and climate change.
Document Title: Presidential Decree No. 22-112 establishing the High Energy Council (15 March 2022)

Family Name: Agreement on the development and promotion of hydrogen and green fuels (Power-to-X strategy) (2022)
Family Summary:
This Agreement states that the path to a green society must be achieved through direct electrification and indirect electrification via the use of Power-to-X (PtX), among other things. PtX refers to technologies that convert surplus renewable electricity into carbon-neutral, storable energy carriers, fuels, or chemical feedstocks, such as hydrogen, ammonia or synthetic liquid fuels. PtX can contribute to an integrated and flexible energy system, where PtX is integrated into the energy system in a way that supports and supplements existing supply sectors, such as electricity, gas and district heating. PtX technology makes it possible to produce fuels and chemicals that can replace fossil products in a number of sectors that are difficult to convert, such as shipping, aviation, agriculture, parts of industry and parts of heavy road transport. PtX processes also generate large amounts of surplus heat, which can potentially be utilised in the district heating sector. As PtX is a new technology, the government and the agreement group will follow developments closely.

The parties agree that Denmark should aim to build 4-6 GW of electrolysis capacity by 2030. The government and the parties to the agreement will closely monitor developments with the certification system. The expansion of PtX must, as far as possible, take place on market terms and with due consideration for the security of supply for Danes, and must also support the realisation of Denmark's export and business potential in the PtX area. The objective can also contribute to reducing Denmark's global climate footprint and achieving national and international climate targets.
Document Title: Agreement on the development and promotion of hydrogen and green fuels (Power-to-X strategy) (2022)

Family Name: National Economic and Social Development Plan (2021 and 2022)
Family Summary:
This document sets the country's yearly development priorities. It notably seeks to guarantee security of supply of energy, materials and food. The plan sets policies with regard to a range of fossil fuels that aim to maintain affordable access to power sources. However, it also examines initiatives to reach peak carbon emissions and achieve carbon neutrality, and how to coordinate them. The government is tasked to
  • formulate implementation plans for sectors such as energy, industry, urban and rural development, transport, and agriculture and rural areas as well as for key industries
  • Formulate support plans in the fields of science and technology, budgeting, finance, carbon absorption capacity, statistical accounting, personnel training, and inspection and evaluation
  • Develop hydropower "in accordance with local conditions" and develop nuclear power "while ensuring absolute safety"
  • Ensure energy efficiency compliance among coal-fired power plants and carry out coordinated transformation of such plants to improve their energy efficiency, heating supply systems, and power flexibility
  •  Promote energy conservation and carbon reduction in key fields and launch initiatives in key industries such as iron and steel, electrolytic aluminum, cement, plate glass, oil refinery, ethylene, synthetic ammonia, and calcium carbide
  • Encourage deeper integration between emerging technologies and green, low-carbon industries and transform the industrial structure from high carbon to low carbon
  • Advocate a simple, modest, green, low-carbon, and healthy lifestyle to rein in carbon emissions at the source
  • Establish a carbon emissions statistical accounting system with unified standards
  • Refine regulations and institutions governing the national market for trading carbon emission rights to strengthen supervision over enterprises and third-party organisations
  • Advance pilot programs for building low-carbon cities and for investing in and financing the response to climate change, and build up climate change response capacities at the local level

The document also stresses that China will continue to actively engage in international climate negotiations and global green governance, "and step up international cooperation in the areas of green economy, trade, technology, and finance."
Document Title: Implementation Report on the National Economic and Social Development Plan (2021 and 2022)

Family Summary: This decree establishes the National Committee for the Mitigation of Greenhouse Gas Emissions in Nicaragua. The committee's main objective is to coordinate and implement strategies aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions, in alignment with national and international climate change goals and and promote sustainable development.
Document Title: Presidential Decree No. 06-2022: Creation of the National Committee for Greenhouse Gas Emission Mitigation

Family Name: Ecological Transition Plan
Family Summary: The Ecological Transition Plan (Piano per la Transizione Ecologica (PTE) in Italian) is Italy’s national strategic framework guiding the transition toward a sustainable and climate-neutral economy, aligned with the European Green Deal and long-term decarbonisation objectives to 2050. The plan defines policy directions and actions across energy, environmental protection and resource management, and coordinates national measures with instruments such as the RRF plan and the NECP. Its main priorities include achieving climate neutrality, reducing pollution, adapting to climate change, restoring biodiversity and ecosystems, and promoting a circular and bio-based economy, while accelerating renewable energy deployment, improving energy efficiency, and supporting sustainable mobility and resource use.

Family Name: NDC Implementation Plan of Nepal, 2023
Family Summary:
This Plan lays out a detailed roadmap for achieving the country’s emission reduction targets, aligning with its broader climate goals. It focuses on both mitigation and adaptation measures. For mitigation, the plan prioritises the expansion of renewable energy sources, particularly hydropower, solar, and wind power, as well as improving energy efficiency in various sectors. To adapt to climate change, the plan emphasises building climate resilience in agriculture, water resources, and infrastructure. Additionally, it prioritises disaster risk reduction, early warning systems, and community-based adaptation measures. The implementation plan aims to mobilise domestic and international resources, strengthen institutional capacity, and promote public awareness to ensure its successful execution.

The Plan highlights the importance of policy support and financial incentives to accelerate the shift towards low-emission technologies. This includes access to climate finance, government subsidies for cleaner technologies, and public-private partnerships to drive innovation. It also sets out a framework for capacity building, aiming to enhance the technical skills and knowledge of industry stakeholders and strengthen the regulatory environment to enforce compliance with emission reduction targets.
Document Title: NDC Implementation Plan of Nepal, 2023 - Draft

Family Name: Decree on the energy and environmental performance requirements for the construction of office and primary or secondary education buildings in metropolitan France (No. 2022-305 of 1 March 2022)
Family Summary: This Decree sets the requirements that must be met by office and primary or secondary education buildings, in respect of energy design, energy consumption, climate change impacts, and limitation of discomfort during the summer.
Document Title: Decree on the energy and environmental performance requirements for the construction of office and primary or secondary education buildings in metropolitan France (No. 2022-305 of 1 March 2022)

Family Name: National Action Plan for the reduction of CO2 emissions by civil aircraft operators of the Republic of Belarus
Family Summary: The action plan implements a series of recommendations derived from Belarus' participation in CORSIA (Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation) since 2019, aiming to mitigate emissions from the aviation sector. Its provisions include general fleet modernisation (for efficiency gains), long-term incorporation of biofuels, 1% reductions in flight time through route optimisation, improvements to airfield layouts, participation in EU emissions trading schemes, and the creation of a central environmental monitoring organisation for aviation. The action plan is approved by the Council of Ministers through Resolution No. 112, 2022.
Document Title: National Action Plan for the reduction of CO2 emissions by civil aircraft operators of the Republic of Belarus

Family Name: National Mining Policy 2050
Family Summary: Long-term roadmap for the sustainable development of Chile’s mining sector, which is integral to its economy. The policy includes a target to reduce emissions from large mining operations by at least 50% by 2030, and become a carbon neutral sector by 2040. It also sets renewable electricity procurement targets, aiming for 90% of electricity contracts to come from renewable sources by 2030 and 100% by 2050. Measures include the electrification of mining equipment, adoption of green hydrogen technologies, and energy efficiency improvements in operations. The Ministry of Mining is responsible for the plan’s monitoring and implementation, and is directed to establish scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions reduction targets that align with Chile’s 2030 NDC commitment.
Document Title: National Mining Policy 2050 (Politica Nacional Minera 2050)

It aims to keep the forests healthy, increase their cover and the ecological, economical, and socio-cultural benefits. It calls for a collaborative approach and the promotion of traditional knowledge.

Family Name: Automotive (investor) roadmap
Family Summary:
This document sets the government's roadmap to enable the automotive sector and its entire supply chain to embark on the decarbonisation road. The roadmap reiterates the commitment to electrification through investments of over £5 billion across infrastructure, manufacturing and research & development. 

The government further commits to create an adequate regulatory environment, accelerate the deployment of charging infrastructure. It also identifies the need to readying the electricity system for EV demand, notably through an uptake in renewables.

Family Name: National Policy for Climate Change (Government Resolution 8/2022)
Family Summary:
This policy, approved by a governmental resolution, aims 1) to make Timor Leste more resilient, promoting the rights of its citizens to a healthy, ecologically balanced and humane environment, 2) reinforce capacity to cope to adverse effects of climate change, and 3) set the economy on the road to sustainable development. 

The main objective of this National Policy on Climate Change is to establish a clear statement according to which political principles and laws should be read and interpreted, through which mechanisms are established to clarify how the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste intends to respond to the climate change. The National Policy on Climate Change provides a common platform that brings together and reconciles for the first time the wide range of adaptation and mitigation policies that are currently in place in Timor-Leste across different economic sectors. This approach includes existing policy commitments in all major international and national policy documents for Timor-Leste, including the Strategic Development Plan 2011 - 2030, the Nationally Determined Contribution (CDNN), the National Adaptation Program of Action (PANA) , as well as a number of sector-specific policy documents.

The National Policy on Climate Change will thus strengthen coordination between ministries and ensure exemption from duplication and application of outdated policy measures. Establishing this clear policy statement also provides the basis on which future climate change policies (sectoral and cross-cutting) can be identified and prioritized. The National Policy on Climate Change also lays the groundwork for the future establishment of the National Strategy and Action Plan for Climate Change (EPANAC), which will help the government to effectively implement, finance and monitor the implementation of established policies. It is also envisaged that this National Policy for Climate Change and EPANAC will be supported through the establishment of a binding national legislative instrument, which will reinforce the basis on which climate change policies are implemented in Timor-Leste, including a legal mandate.

Through this policy, the Government of Timor-Leste will continue its development program to build a strong, low-carbon economy capable of managing the adverse impacts of climate change on our environment and our people, while adhering to the principles of sustainable development: “development based on effective environmental management that meets the needs of the current generation without compromising the environmental balance and the ability of future generations to meet their needs as well” .
Document Title: National Policy for Climate Change (Government Resolution 8/2022)

Family Name: South African Green Finance Taxonomy
Family Summary: In March 2022 South Africa's Treasury issued the first edition of its Sustainable Finance Taxonomy. The taxonomy defines a minimum set of assets, projects, activities and sectors that are eligible to be defined as "green" in line with international best practice and national priorities. It is intended to be used by legislators, executive actors and regulators, as well as by the financial services industry. Use of the taxonomy is not mandatory.
Document Title: South African Green Finance Taxonomy

Family Name: Bangladesh Third Country Investment Plan - Sustainable, Nutrition Sensitive and Resilient Food Systems 2021 -2025 (CIP3)
Family Summary: The Investment Plan aims to mobilise and direct funding toward sustainable, nutrition-sensitive, and resilient investments that will enhance food and nutrition security while significantly contributing to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals. The plan highlights the importance of integrating climate change adaptation and mitigation measures into food production and distribution systems to ensure food security and nutrition. It also emphasises enhancing the resilience of food systems against climate-related shocks and stresses, promoting sustainable agricultural practices, and improving communities' capacity to adapt to the impacts of climate change.
Document Title: Bangladesh Third Country Investment Plan - Sustainable, Nutrition Sensitive and Resilient Food Systems 2021 -2025 (CIP3)

Family Name: 14th Five-Year Plan for Building Energy Efficiency and Green Building Development
Family Summary: This Plan aims to enhance building energy efficiency to achieve carbon peaking sooner and realise the national goal of carbon neutrality by 2060. The Plan sets overall targets for the energy efficiency of new buildings and the amount of coal use for building operations. It sets out the key tasks, which include strengthening the use of high-quality building materials; setting comprehensive standrds for the management of green buildings; enhancing the energy efficiency standards of new and existing buildings; promoting the use of renewable energy, including solar and geothermal energy.
Document Title: 14th Five-Year Plan for Building Energy Efficiency and Green Building Development

Family Name: 14th Five-Year Plan for Science and Technology for Housing and Urban-Rural Development
Family Summary: This Plan seeks to achieve breakthroughs in key low-carbon technologies and major infrastructure; strengthen technological prowess; and significantly improve the standard of the support system for scientific innovation, to achieve low-carbon outcomes for the housing and development sector. The Plan covers, amongst other areas, research for low-carbon technologies in development, including zero-carbon buildings and neighbourhoods.
Document Title: 14th Five-Year Plan for Science and Technology for Housing and Urban-Rural Development

Family Name: Setting Lebanon’s Electricity Sector on a Sustainable Growth Path (2022)
Family Summary: 'Setting Lebanon’s Electricity Sector on a Sustainable Growth Path (2022)' is a policy statement and plan by the Lebanese Ministry of Environment, based on the Least Cost Generation Plan (Ministry of Energy and Water, World Bank, EDF Energy; 2021). It promotes enhancing renewable generation capacity to meet Lebanon's climate mitigation commitments and energy demand forecasts, alongside significant natural gas development. The plan aims for a 15% renewable share in the energy mix by 2026, reaching 30% by 2030.
Document Title: Setting Lebanon’s Electricity Sector on a Sustainable Growth Path (2022)

Family Name: Energy Renovation Programme for the Public Sector up to 2030
Family Summary: The Energy Renovation Programme aims to improve the energy efficiency of public sector buildings in Croatia, with a strategic focus on those with the lowest efficiency ratings. It acknowledges climate change mitigation and adaptation as primary motivators. The programme aims to contribute to broader national goals in energy renovation, such as cumulative 25% of buildings renovated nationally by 2030, and all buildings nationally operating at near-zero-energy by 2050.
Document Title: Energy Renovation Programme for the Public Sector up to 2030

The objective of this initiative is to decrease environmental impact and enhance residential energy efficiency. Support is provided for the installation of renewable energy systems for self-consumption or for establishing connections to centralized district heating systems.

Family Summary: This policy aims to ensure the long term climate-resilience of coffee production in Honduras, creating economic benefits and also helping to mitigate net greenhouse emissions through sustainable land use and agroecology. Family Name: Rebbelib 2050: National Transport Decarbonisation Framework
Family Summary:
Rebbelib 2050 is designed to support the Marshall Islands' National Strategic Plan 2030, implement the transport-related provisions of the updated Second Nationally Determined Contribution (2020), and integrate its transport planning into the overall national climate crisis response. The vision statement is to develop sustainable, appropriate, affordable and accessible transport connectivity for the Marshall Islands, within a decarbonising world, which can serve as a model for other climate-vulnerable states.

The Framework contains nine different workstreams: Partnerships; Education and Training; Mapping and Data; Heritage History; Economic Analysis; Policy Review Development; Technology; Knowledge Transfer; and Monitoring, Evaluation Learning. There are priority actions listed for each workstream. For Technology, technologies across maritime, aviation, land transport, and fuel production and energy generation/storage are being considered. There are several maritime priority projects, including a fleet refit and replacement strategy, rotor trial, fishing ship efficiency research, medical service and disaster response model, amongst others.
Document Title: Rebbelib 2050: National Transport Decarbonisation Framework

Family Name: Climate Change and Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2022-2030
Family Summary: The Climate Change and Disaster Risk Reduction Policy takes a practical approach, taking into consideration Vanuatu's resources, exposure to risks, and demographic situation. It seeks to strengthen existing capacity at national, provincial and area council levels, drawing on the country's rich heritage, traditional knowledge and the lessons learned from the broad range of initiatives regarding climate change and disaster risk reduction. The policy will apply six principles: 1) accountability, 2) sustainability, 3) equity, 4) community focus, 5) collaboration, and 6) innovation.The vision of this policy is for Vanuatu to be a nation whose communities, environment and economy are resilient to the impacts of climate change and disaster risks. It aims to be accessible to and implemented by all government agencies and non-governmental stakeholders.
Document Title: Climate Change and Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2022-2030

Actions include modernising the production system; modifying the access to agricultural production factors and production conditions, taking into account the pressure of agricultural activity on natural resources and environments, as well as climate change; investing in fertilisers and plant protection products in line with agro-environmental and climate measures; and the development of organic farming. Family Name: The Biden-⁠Harris Plan to Revitalize American Manufacturing and Secure Critical Supply Chains in 2022
Family Summary:
This plan builds on the conclusions from seven sectoral reports published by federal agencies (linked in the full text). These reports identify key weaknesses in crucial supply chains and set multi-year strategies accordingly. The Biden-Harris plan announces additional measures to enhance long-term resilience of critical supply chains, and formally institutionalises supply chain resilience throughout the Federal government.The administration notably indicates that it will invest in sustainable domestic production and processing of critical minerals, from rare earths serving in electric motors to carbon fibre used for airplanes. In parallel to this document, it announced plans to expand domestic rare earth processing, strengthen the National Defense Stockpile; update mining regulations to ensure sustainable and responsible practices; and issue recommendations for comprehensive reform of mining laws. The plan further charges the Department of Energy to investigate the feasibility of extracting rare-earth from mine waste. As part of the Mining Innovations for Negative Emissions Resources (MINER) Program, the Department is releasing a $44 million funding opportunity "to provide commercial-ready technologies that give the United States a net-zero or net negative emissions pathway toward increased domestic supplies of copper, nickel, lithium, cobalt, rare earth elements, and other critical elements required for a clean energy transition."

As of March 2025, the status of this entry is likely impacted by the Trump-Vance administration’s regulatory rollback on climate action. To learn more about the rollback, visit the Sabin Center’s Climate Backtracker.
Document Title: Factsheet on the The Biden-⁠Harris Plan to Revitalize American Manufacturing and Secure Critical Supply Chains in 2022

Family Name: Law no. 2022-298 from 2 March 2022 relating to a better allocation of crop insurance in agriculture and reforming the tools for managing climate risks in agriculture
Family Summary:
This law sets out the objectives, strategy and financial and operational programming of the French state's intervention to strengthen the resilience of French agriculture in the face of climate change through the mobilization of a universal management system of risks in agriculture for the period 2023-2030.

The programme contributes to ensuring the sustainability and resilience of agricultural production systems in a context of accelerating climate change by guaranteeing farmers' access to a universal system for managing climate risks in agriculture, has four objectives:
i) Ensure a balanced distribution of support between the different actors concerned by the management of climate risks in agriculture;
ii) Develop prevention and protection systems adapted to all agricultural strains;
iii) Create and better allocate insurance products and compensation mechanisms that are effective and complementary, in support of strategies for adapting sectors and production areas;
iv) Allow for "national solidarity" state intervention mechanisms in the event of "catastrophic" climate hazards, such as compensation or indemnification for losses suffered. 

The implementation of this new system is part of a budget that could reach up to 600 million euros annually in public expenditures, during the 2023-2030 period, as the insurance programme develops.
Document Title: Law no. 2022-298 from 2 March 2022 relating to a better allocation of crop insurance in agriculture and reforming the tools for managing climate risks in agriculture

Family Name: America’s Strategy to Secure the Supply Chain for a Robust Clean Energy Transition
Family Summary: This is the Department of Energy's response to Executive Order 14017 on America’s Supply Chains. It lays out the challenges and opportunities faced by the United States in the energy supply chain as well a s the Federal Government plans to address these challenges and opportunities. The DOE states that it recognises that a secure, resilient supply chain will be critical in harnessing emissions outcomes and capturing the economic opportunity inherent in the energy sector transition. Potential vulnerabilities and risks to the Energy Sector Industrial Base must be addressed throughout every stage of this transition.
Document Title: America’s Strategy to Secure the Supply Chain for a Robust Clean Energy Transition

Family Name: Guidelines on Green Debt Instruments, Sustainable Debt Instruments, Green Lease Certificates and Sustainable Lease Certificates
Family Summary: In February 2022, the Capital Markets Board of Turkey produced a set of Guidelines that sets out the key aspects of green debt instruments, sustainable debt instruments, green lease certificates, amongst other instruments, as well as the principles that should be adhered to, to ensure that the instruments and certificates are in compliance with the best international practices and standards. The Guidelines advise the disclosure of relevant information within the scope of the issuer's climate mitigation and adaptation strategies in Annex 1 of the document.

Family Name: Operational Plan for Indonesia's FOLU Net Sink 2030
Family Summary:
This Operational Plan details the mitigation actions and priority locations for the development of a low-carbon, sustainable and resource-efficient Forestry and Other Land Use (FOLU) sector. The target is to achieve a net carbon sink in the sector by 2030 to contribute to Indonesia's NDC targets, as outlined in Indonesia's Long-Term Strategy: Low Carbon and Climate Resilience 2050.

Actions include preventing deforestation and degradation, plantation forest development, sustainable forest management, enhancement of forest carbon stocks, peatland management and natural forest conservation.

The Plan covers the various environmental and forestry policies and instruments; a spatial analysis of forestry and land emissions reductions; the mitigation actions and target locations; and rules for implementation and organisation.
Document Title: Operational Plan for Indonesia's FOLU Net Sink 2030
