Family Name: Mandatory Climate Information Reporting for Companies
Family Summary: This policy sets out a new regulatory scheme for large businesses to report on climate related information and financial risk. The regulations were made on 17 January 2022 and apply to reporting for financial years starting on or after 6 April 2022.
Document Title: Mandatory Climate Information Reporting for Companies

Family Name: Presidential Decree No. 04-2022: Approval of the National Climate Change Policy
Family Summary:
Approved on February 18, 2022, this decree formalises the approval of the National Climate Change Policy aiming to address the challenges posed by climate change in the country. This policy outlines the country's approach to mitigating and adapting to climate change, focusing on sustainable development, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and enhancing resilience to climate impacts. It also promotes cooperation between governmental institutions, local communities, and the private sector to address climate challenges effectively. Moreover, the policy focuses on integrating climate considerations into national development plans.

The National Climate Change Policy is annexed in this regulation and has as core principles:

  • The policy promotes climate justice, especially for marginalized groups like Indigenous Peoples and Afrodescendants.
  • It advocates for human development and sustainable economic growth with a focus on environmental conservation and the principles of "Good Living."
  • Reparation of climate-related losses
  • The active participation of youth and shared responsibility among all levels of government and stakeholders.
  • The policy encourages a dialogue of knowledge, integrating traditional and modern approaches to climate action.
  • Climate finance
Document Title: Presidential Decree No. 04-2022: Approval of the National Climate Change Policy

Family Name: Green Hydrogen / Green Ammonia Policy
Family Summary: Building on the National Hydrogen Mission released by the Prime Minister in August 2021, this document sets India's strategy to meet its goal of becoming a global green hydrogen hub. It identifies the production of hydrogen and ammonia from unconsumed renewable power and connectivity to the grid as priorities. The policy sets the framework so that hydrogen / ammonia manufacturers can purchase and use unconsumed renewable power. Waiver of inter-state transmission charges for a period of 25 years will be allowed to the manufacturers for projects commissioned before 30th June 2025. The manufacturers of Green Hydrogen / Ammonia and the renewable energy plant shall be given connectivity to the grid on priority basis to avoid any procedural delays.The document also seeks to develop bunkers near ports for storage and export or direct use by ships. The land for the storage for this purpose shall be provided by the respective Port Authorities at applicable charges.
Document Title: Green Hydrogen / Green Ammonia Policy

Family Name: Slovakia’s CAP Strategic Plan 2023-2027
Family Summary: Slovakia’s strategy is aimed at ensuring the sustainable competitiveness and resilience of farms and a fairer income for agricultural producers with special attention to small and young farmers. At the same time, the Plan also focuses on improving the protection of natural resources and the climate. It contributes substantially to improving the vitality and quality of life in rural areas through investments, knowledge transfer and innovation.A substantial part of the support of the Slovak Republic Rural Development Plan for the period 2023 - 2027 is focused on adaptation and mitigation to climate change. The planned measures are intended to contribute to the specific objective of CAP S04: SO4 "Contribute to climate change mitigation and adaptation, including the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and improved carbon storage as well as the promotion of sustainable energies'.

It defines a number of targets, including an expansion of grain and meat production. The following clauses are of specific relevance for climate change action: 
  • it aims to develop avenues to produce cultivated meat
  • monitoring of disasters notably caused/amplified by climate change will be performed. The disasters cited are crop diseases, pests, weeds, rats, livestock and poultry, and aquatic diseases.
  • recycling and use of agricultural waste (including manure) should be enhanced.

It aims to carry out about 7.5 million energy-efficiency renovations (including 4.7 million deep renovations) by mid-century, support the transition to climate-neutral buildings, accelerate replacement of high-emission heating sources, and integrate national and EU financial and legislative support to make renovations cost-effective and socially equitable while boosting jobs and economic benefits.

Family Name: Climate Council's Recommendations 2022
Family Summary: Turkey's first Climate Council was held from 21 to 25 February 2022 by the Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change, where recommendations were adopted for Turkey's long-term climate roadmap in consultation with stakeholders. Approximately 5,000 representatives from the public and private sectors, universities, NGOs, and student groups attended the Council. This document features recommendations covering future planning for transformations in energy, transportation, industry, agriculture (and LULUCF) that are required to meet the country’s 2053 Net Zero Emissions Target that was announced in 2021. It emphasises the use of new (and future) technologies such as blockchain-based traceability technologies, autonomous robots and ‘smart transport’ to help catalyse these sectoral transformations. It also includes a proposal for developing an integrated ecosystem and biodiversity monitoring network, to address potential biodiversity loss. The Roadmap recognises the importance of including stakeholders from across levels of government and proposes the formation of a Climate Coordination Board in each province of the country, that will allow for ‘localised’ policy management.
Document Title: Climate Council's Recommendations 2022

Family Name: Export Development Canada Sustainable Bond Framework
Family Summary:
Export Development Canada (“EDC” or “we”) is Canada’s official export credit agency, a self-financing Crown corporation dedicated to helping Canadian companies of all sizes succeed on the world stage. Their mandate is to support and develop, directly or indirectly, Canada’s export trade and respond to international business opportunities.

This Framework is intended to guide future issuances of Green, Social, Sustainability and Transition Bonds (collectively referred to as “Sustainable Bonds”). The use of proceeds from these Sustainable Bond transactions will be earmarked for a portfolio of Eligible Assets, defined, selected, tracked and reported on in accordance with this Framework.

This Framework is informed by the guidance from ICMA’s Climate Transition Finance Handbook (2020) as it relates to practices, actions and disclosures for allocating capital for climate transition-related purposes, to be updated as market practices evolve.
Document Title: Export Development Canada Sustainable Bond Framework

Family Name: Hydrogen Society Roadmap

• Decarbonisation of heavy-duty transport;

• Decarbonisation of energy-intensive industry (cement, steel, mining, refineries);

• Enhanced and green power sector (main and micro-grids);

• Centre of Excellence in Manufacturing for hydrogen products and fuel cell components;

Family Name: Agricultural and Rural 100% Renewable Energy (RE100) Demonstration Projects
Family Summary: This plan provides KRW 3.67 billion in funding for 100% renewable energy demonstration projects in four rural communities. The plan allocates KRW 918 million for each project, and local and provincial governments will provide matching funds. This plan is congruent with the Republic of Korea's target to increase its renewable energy share to 29.2%  by 2038, outlined in the 11th Basic Plan for Supply and Demand of Power. The projects will involve solar PV installation and energy efficiency upgrades to demonstrate the feasibility of reducing energy costs and meeting demand through renewable energy. The projects will be conducted over a two-year period. Participating communities will receive an energy diagnostic of their community energy demands; install renewable energy projects in residential, commercial, and community spaces; and carry out building renovation upgrades aimed at increasing energy efficiency.
Document Title: Agricultural and Rural 100% Renewable Energy (RE100) Demonstration Projects

It seeks to advance knowledge and capacity in a range of different storage technologies.


The plan notably calls for the development of pilot schemes and an enhancement of the involvement of the academic and research world on the issue.

  • Strengthen resilience and the capacity to adapt to climate change in the following sectors:
    • Agriculture, forestry and fishery;
    • Environment and biodiversity;
    • Water resources;
    • Transport;
    • Construction;
    • Industry;
    • Health;
    • Labour and society;
    • Culture.

  • Resources for climate change adaptation;
  • Science, technology and international cooperation;
  • Training and education.

Family Name: Decree No. 06/2022/ND-CP on Mitigation of Green House Gas (GHG) Emissions and Protection of Ozone Layer
Family Summary:
As stated in article 1, this Decree elaborates some articles of the Law on Environmental Protection, including article 91 on reduction of GHG emissions, article 92 on ozone layer protection, and article 139 on the organisation and development of a domestic carbon market. Section 1 concerns the mitigation of GHG emissions. Inter alia, this Section prescribes the inventory of GHG for certain establishments. It also sets up a national MRV system.Section 2 delineates the architecture and development of the domestic carbon market. It outlines a development roadmap for the period of up to the end of 2027, and from 2028, and touches on the participants of the domestic carbon market, the certification of carbon credits, the exchange of GHG emissions quotas and carbon credits, the registration of programs and projects, and the responsibility for further development of the market. Section 3 concerns the protection of ozone layer. This section deals with controlled substances and provides roadmap for management and phaseout of controlled ozone-depleting substances and greenhouse gases. The various measures for the promotion of GHG emission mitigation and ozone layer protection are outlined in chapter IV. Such measures concern:

  • Cooperation mechanisms and methods;
  • Research and development; and
  • Capacity building and raising awareness.

Decree No. 119/2025/ND-CP dated 9 June 2025 amending and supplementing certain provisions of Decree No. 06/2022/ND-CP contains provisions on carbon credit transfer and carbon trading mechanisms under Articles 6.2 and 6.4 of the Paris Agreement, responsibilities of various government agencies and provincial authorities for greenhouse gas emissions monitoring
Document Title: Decision No. 13/2024/QD-TTg on entities mandated to carry out a greenhouse gas inventory

Family Name: Decree No. 2022-8 relating to the minimum environmental performance result concerning the installation of heating or domestic hot water production equipment in a building
Family Summary:
This decree stipulates that the level of greenhouse gas emissions from a heating or domestic hot water production equipment must be less than 300 gCO2eq / kWh NCV. This de facto sets the end of new coal- and fuel oil-powered heating devices in residential buildings.

The provisions of this article are applicable to the construction of new buildings for which the application for a building permit is submitted after July 1, 2022 and to existing buildings for which the work mentioned in I is undertaken after July 1, 2022.
Document Title: Decree No. 2022-8 relating to the minimum environmental performance result concerning the installation of heating or domestic hot water production equipment in a building

Family Name: European Funds for Infrastructure, Climate, Environment 2021-2027  Programme (FEnIKS)
Family Summary: The European Funds for Infrastructure, Climate, Environment 2021-2027 Programme is a tool for the implementation of EU Cohesion Policy funds. It is a continuation of the Operational Programme Infrastructure and Environment 2014-2020. The main objective of the programme is to improve the conditions for the development of the country through the construction of technical and social infrastructure in line with sustainable development, including through: decarbonising the economy, developing RES and energy infrastructure, transforming towards an environmentally friendly and circular economy, building an efficient and resilient transport system with the lowest possible negative impact on the environment.Overall, the programme contributes to the development of a low-emission economy, environmental protection, and mitigating and adapting to climate change. The programme has a budget of more than EUR 24 billion. It was adopted by the Council of Ministers on 4 January 2022 and approved by the European Commission on 6 October 2022.
Document Title: European Funds for Infrastructure, Climate, Environment 2021-2027 Programme (FEnIKS)

Family Name: Regulations for the Energy Rating of Houses (CEV)
Family Summary: Calificación Energética de Viviendas (CEV) is Chile’s national energy rating framework, initially established in 2011, to evaluate and label homes according to their expected energy consumption (from A to G). This regulation mandates the CEV certification for all new residential housing projects from October 2025, and the energy rating must be disclosed in building permits and in all promotional or sales materials.

Family Summary:

It also aims at reducing the cost of operation by focusing on projects to produce electricity from renewable energy, especially solar and wind energies, as well as the distribution networks.

Family Name: Zimbabwe National Strategy and Action Plan for Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture 2022 - 2032
Family Summary: The Zimbabwe National Strategy and Action Plan for Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (PGRFA), focuses on the conservation, sustainable use, and management of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture in line with international agreements. The strategy aims to enhance the resilience and sustainability of agriculture in the face of climate change, ensuring food and nutrition security. It provides strategies for broad research and development of PGRFA that are adaptable to climate change centred around 6 components.
Document Title: Zimbabwe National Strategy and Action Plan for Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture

Family Name: National Disaster Management Strategy (NDMS) 2022 -2027
Family Summary: The goal of this strategy is to provide guidance on disaster risk management interventions in Tanzania in order to enhance socio-economic resilience and humanitarian responses. It also seeks to promote coherence between climate change adaptation, disaster risk reduction, and sustainable development to prevent new and reduce existing and future disaster risks. The strategy provides for a multi-hazard, multi-sectoral, and whole-of-society approach to disaster risk management to achieve resilience for sustainable development at all levels, from national to village level. By adopting a multi-hazard approach, this strategy aims to build resilience to more than one type of risk and to use resources more efficiently.
Document Title: National Disaster Management Strategy (NDMS) 2022 -2027

Family Name: National Disaster Preparedness and Response Plan 2022
Family Summary:
The Strategy addresses Tanzania's persistent vulnerability to natural and man-made disasters, exacerbated by factors like climate change, urbanisation, and environmental degradation. The NDMS focuses on building resilience and enhancing humanitarian responses with ten core objectives, aiming to improve understanding, preparedness, and response capacities across all levels of society. Key goals include:

  • Promoting understanding of disaster risks to improve community resilience.
  • Enhancing prevention and preparedness strategies to mitigate risks and strengthen community resilience.
  • Implementing comprehensive, people-centered multi-hazard early warning systems.
  • Strengthening disaster response capabilities and improving humanitarian aid delivery.
  • Developing capacity to “build back better” in recovery efforts, promoting sustainable rehabilitation.

Additionally, the NDMS emphasises governance, funding, and private sector investment in disaster risk management, with a focus on inclusivity for vulnerable groups and alignment with regional and international practices.
Document Title: National Disaster Preparedness and Response Plan 2022

Family Name: National Waste Plan 2027 - From Recycling to Circular Economy
Family Summary: The national waste plan, which is aligned with the EU waste directive (2008/98/EC), outlines strategic goals and measures for waste management in Finland. This plan aims to reduce both the quantity and harmfulness of waste, focusing on preventing future waste generation. It covers all of Finland, excluding the Åland Islands, which will develop its own waste management strategy. The plan seeks to conserve natural resources and mitigate climate change by promoting material-efficient production and consumption.
Document Title: National Waste Plan 2027 - From Recycling to Circular Economy

Family Name: Finland's National Forest Strategy 2035
Family Summary: Finland’s National Forest Strategy 2035 is the statutory national forest programme guiding Finland’s forest policy towards 2035. It coordinates economic, environmental and social objectives and responds to changes in the forest sector, including climate change and biodiversity loss. Its vision is to create growing wellbeing from forests and for forests, with priorities focused on increasing forest growth, carbon sequestration and timber production, strengthening biodiversity in commercial forests, and creating a competitive and responsible forest-based sector. The strategy also emphasises sustainable and diverse forest use, forest resilience, and knowledge-based management.
Document Title: Finland's National Forest Strategy 2035

Family Name: National Board of Health and Welfare - Action plan for climate adaptation 2022 – 2025
Family Summary:
The National Board of Health and Welfare has analysed the consequences that a changing climate can have on human health and the health and care sector and, based on this, analyzed how the agency can contribute to reducing the negative consequences through its activities. It also sees a need for increased knowledge about the impact of climate change on the health and care sector in order to be able to make the right decisions. The National Board of Health and Welfare also has the opportunity to contribute to increasing knowledge through the dissemination of information.

The National Board of Health and Welfare shall contribute to developing the ability of health and care to counteract the negative effects of climate change on vulnerable groups within health and care.

The goal shall be long-term and is intended to fulfil the National Board of Health and Welfare’s mission as the government’s administrative authority for activities related to health and medical care, dental care and social services, support and service for certain disabled people.

The goal should also be linked to possible and relevant indicators to measure, for example: heat-related mortality, and the proportion of homes with heat wave preparedness plans.

The agency goal for climate adaptation is also divided into two action goals:

1. Climate adaptation is integrated into the agency's work; and

2. The National Board of Health and Welfare has contributed to improving and developing work on climate adaptation in society.
Document Title: National Board of Health and Welfare - Action plan for climate adaptation 2022 – 2025

Family Name: Eighth National Development Plan (8NDP) 2022-2026
Family Summary:
The Eighth National Development Plan (8NDP) sets out Zambia’s strategic direction in terms of the development priorities and implementation strategies for the period 2022 to 2026. The 8NDP introduces strategic interventions anchored on:

  • Economic Transformation and Job Creation;
  • Human and Social Development;
  • Environmental Sustainability; and
  • Good Governance Environment.

Under environmental sustainability, the development outcomes include enhanced mitigation and adaptation to climate change, and enhanced disaster risk reduction and response. The Plan sets out programmes to achieve these outcomes.
Document Title: Eighth National Development Plan (8NDP) 2022-2026

Family Name: Gender Mainstreaming Policy and Strategic Framework in Agriculture
Family Summary: This Policy identifies issues and constraints in the contributions of Cambodian women to agricultural labour, production, harvesting, processing, marketing and in agri-food supply chains, and proposes some sector-specific outcomes and target indicators. It also recognises that climate change is a cross-cutting issue which affects agriculture, livestock, fisheries and forestry practices, and women's vulnerability to climate change. Actions include: promoting greater access for women to information, knowledge and technical skill services to support their work in the agricultural sector, including emerging areas such as intensification and diversification, and climate change related opportunities; ad improving collaboration and coordination between all stakeholders in agriculturesector, climate change and natural resource management.
Document Title: Gender Mainstreaming Policy and Strategic Framework in Agriculture

Family Name: Economic Modernisation Vision 2022–2033
Family Summary: Jordan's Economic Modernisation Vision 2022–2033 aims to accelerate economic growth while providing equitable quality of life improvements for its citizens and enhancing sustainability in the economy. It provides overarching long term directions for sectors such as energy and transport. Recommendations to improve sustainability and mitigate climate change include renewable energy expansion, modernisation of the agriculture sector and efficiency gains in water and waste management. It also emphasises enhancement of sustainability institutions and governance, proposing greater inter-sector coordination and the production of a national energy transition roadmap.
Document Title: Economic Modernisation Vision 2022–2033

Family Name: Climate Change Gender Action Plan
Family Summary:
This Plan, developed by the Ministry of Climate Change (MOCC) and the International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN), aims to support policy measures and strengthen institutional processes that enhance women’s participation in climate decision-making and implementation. It was formulated under the first Gender Responsive Readiness Grant of the Green Climate Fund (GCF).

The cross-cutting priority actions are as follows:

  1. Ensure the participation and representation of women at all levels of climate policy, planning and decision making across sectors;
  2. Strengthen coordination and promote institutionalisation to address gender issues and support gender mainstreaming;
  3. Develop gender responsive climate actions through national and provincial policies and programmes;
  4. Collect gender disaggregated data to fill information gaps Invest in context specific research to inform policy making and programming; and
  5. Develop a framework to monitor progress on ccGAP implementation.

This Plan is divided into six sections, covering the priority sectors aligned with the National Climate Change Policy (NCCP) of 2021: disaster risk reduction; agriculture and food security; forests and biodiversity; integrated coastal management; water and sanitation; and energy and transport. Each section covers the gender-related concerns, relevant polciies and institutional frameworks, programmes and projects that focus on women or contain a women-related component; and a sector-specific action plan to strengthen the inclusion and leadership of women in climate action.
Document Title: Climate Change Gender Action Plan

Family Name: National Electric Mobility Strategy (2022)
Family Summary:
National Electric Mobility Strategy lays out Paraguay’s long-term vision for transitioning its transport sector toward electric mobility by 2030, aiming to promote decarbonisation, mitigate climate change and enhance quality of life by improving air quality. It defines five strategic axes (including regulation standards, infrastructure, financing, technology, and promotion awareness), with specific objectives and lines of action under each.

It also aims to transform public transport (e.g. buses, taxis) and other key vehicle fleets to electric, boosting local industry, and improving regulatory and technical frameworks to support the shift.

Decree 8.840/2023 approved the Strategy.

Family Name: National Energy Transformation Partnership
Family Summary:
The National Energy Transformation Partnership (the Partnership) is a framework for the Australian Government, and state and territory governments to collaborate on the transformation of Australia’s energy systems to net zero by 2050.

The principles for collaboration include that all governments:2. Agree that the needs of consumers are central to the transformation, and that affordable, clean, reliable and secure energy is fundamental to a strong economy.3. Agree that decarbonised electricity systems are critical to the broader energy transformation, and fundamental to supporting Australia’s future economic opportunities.
Document Title: National Energy Transformation Partnership

Family Name: National Fisheries and Aquaculture Development Policy (2022-2026)
Family Summary:
The National Fisheries and Aquaculture Development Policy (2022-2026) (PONADEPA) is the coherent framework for programming public and private investments in the livestock and fisheries sector for the period 2022-2026.

It has the overall objective of guaranteeing food security in terms of quality animal protein and creating jobs, thus aligning with the ambition of the President of the Republic, His Excellency Alassane Ouattara, to make Côte d'Ivoire a united country, based on vigorous, sustained, and inclusive growth. The overall objective of PONADEPA has been broken down into three (3) strategic objectives: (i) improving governance of the sector; (ii) improving the productivity and competitiveness of environmentally sound animal and fisheries sectors; and (iii)improving the livelihoods of stakeholders.

It contains climate adaptation strategies, such as improved systems for accessing finance and mitigating the impacts of climate change, aligned with sustainable fisheries management.
Document Title: National Fisheries and Aquaculture Development Policy (2022-2026)

Family Name: National Fisheries and Aquaculture Development Policy (2022-2026)
Family Summary: The National Fisheries and Aquaculture Development Policy (2022-2026) lists the national priorities and strategies in fisheries and aquaculture, to inform stakeholders (local communities, the private sector, technical and financial partners) and ensure the transparency of actions undertaken. The Policy takes into account environmental preservation and climate change in the management of farms, fisheries and operations by respecting good practices and standards. For instance, one of the measures is to promote agroecology.
Document Title: National Fisheries and Aquaculture Development Policy (2022-2026)

Family Name: Plan of Action for Cocoa and Forests Initiative (ICF) 2022-2025
Family Summary:
The Cocoa and Forests Initiative (ICF) is a joint partnership of the governments of Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana, and 35 companies in the cocoa and chocolate sector representing 85% of the world's cocoa trade, aimed at eliminating deforestation from the cocoa supply chain and combating climate change. Actions also include practising climate-smart agroforestry.

The first phase of the ICF implementation, from 2018 to 2020, which served as a pilot phase, focused on the implementation of projects carried out individually or in small coalitions by the signatories of the initiative.

This Phase II for 2022-2025 will remain focused on the three (3) pillars of the ICF, namely:

1. Forest protection and restoration: the implementation of large-scale public-private partnership projects for the protection and restoration of classified forests and selected parks and reserves, and surrounding landscapes. The classified forests of Yapo-Abbé (24,592 ha), Tamin (24,934 ha), and Cavally (64,200 ha), the Mont-Péko National Park (34,000 ha), the Mabi-Yaya Reserve (61,282 ha), and the Bossématié Reserve (21,550 ha), along with their surrounding areas, are among the priority landscapes identified for these public-private partnerships.

2. Agroforestry and sustainable cocoa production: These themes are promoted through sustainability programs implemented by the ICF signatories. Strengthening the mapping of cocoa supply chains, with the establishment of a national traceability system, is a key priority for the signatories under this pillar.

It should be noted that community participation will be taken into account in the implementation of all activities planned in the 2022-2025 action plan. The same applies to the gender aspect.
Document Title: Plan of Action for Cocoa and Forests Initiative (ICF) 2022-2025

Family Name: Disaster Risk Management Plan
Family Summary:
The plan analyses how climate change, together with national socio-economic and demographic trends, contributes to disaster risk and population vulnerability in Bulgaria. Climate change is expected to have an overall negative impact. A general declining trend in precipitation is projected, with significant regional variation. In Eastern Bulgaria, average precipitation is expected to decrease by 5–10%, and in some areas by as much as 15–20%. Winters classified as cold under current climate conditions are expected to occur less frequently by the 2050s and to largely disappear by the 2080s, while hot summers are projected to become increasingly frequent.

Regional climate scenario models for Bulgaria estimate changes in air temperature and precipitation for two time horizons: the near future (2021–2050) and the distant future (2071–2100). Average annual air temperature is expected to increase by 1.6–3.1°C in the near future and by 2.9–4.1°C in the distant future. Over the coming decades, a steady increase in climate-related disasters, such as heat waves, droughts, heavy rainfall, and floods, is anticipated. With medium to high confidence, extreme heat, droughts, and forest fires are expected to intensify by 2050. While projections for precipitation-related hazards such as floods and landslides are more uncertain, recent trends of increasing precipitation intensity suggest that the frequency and severity of these events are also likely to rise by mid-century.
Document Title: Disaster Risk Management Plan

Family Name: Ministry of Education Climate Change Action Plan 2022
Family Summary:
The Climate Change Action Plan, published in 2022 by the Ministry of National Education, identifies climate change education as a critical area for emission reduction and climate crisis adaptation policies. The objectives of climate change education are stated as follows:

Climate change education has started to form its own identity at every level of education, from preschool to higher education. In this context, the fundamental task of climate change education is to train environmentally conscious individuals who understand the basic principles of the climate system, can evaluate scientifically reliable climate information, can minimize the effects of climate change, can make conscious decisions, and can contribute to the formation of sustainable communities by developing environmental attitudes and behaviours.
Document Title: Ministry of Education Climate Change Action Plan 2022

Family Name: Mobility Vehicles & Technologies Roadmap
Family Summary:
This Roadmap, launched by the Ministry of Industry and Technology, outlines a strategic push towards green, smart, and technologically advanced transport, aiming for 35% EV market share, 75% local content in vehicles, and regional leadership in e-mobility by 2030, supporting the national 2053 Net Zero target by integrating electrification, digitalisation, and sustainable production.

The Roadmap examines the current state of the sector, the global context, and trends, and identifies short-term (2023), medium-term (2025), and long-term (2030) objectives for Türkiye. It includes 14 strategic objectives, 46 sub-objectives, 184 actions, and 9 critical projects under the headings of electric, connected, autonomous, and shared vehicles; rail transportation vehicles and systems; marine vehicles and port operations; UAVs and flying cars; as well as human capital, entrepreneurship, technology-oriented support programs, and effective participation in international legislation.
Document Title: Mobility Vehicles & Technologies Roadmap

Family Name: Climate Change Adaptation Program (2022-2027)
Family Summary:
Natural Resources Canada’s (NRCan) $39.5 million Climate Change Adaptation Program (CCAP) (2022–2027) supports Canada’s regions and sectors to adapt to a changing climate. The program aims to:

  • support decision-makers in identifying and implementing adaptation actions;
  • enhance adaptation knowledge and skills among Canada’s workforce; and
  • increase access to climate change adaptation tools and resources.

The program is co-funding projects across Canada that enhance skills for adapting to climate change, advance adaptation in the natural resource sectors (forestry, mining, and energy), and expand knowledge on the economics of adaptation and on key emerging issues. Up to $15 million has been allocated for these projects.

Recognizing the disproportionate impacts of climate change on Indigenous, remote, and northern communities and the need to reduce barriers to accessing federal funding for their climate change adaptation initiatives, the program is providing up to an additional $2 million in funding specifically for Indigenous-led projects and up to a further $2.25 million for projects that support enhancing skills to meet the specific adaptation needs of the Territories.
Document Title: Climate Change Adaptation Program (2022-2027)

Family Name: Agricultural Climate Solutions - Living Labs Program
Family Summary:
The goal of the Agricultural Climate Solutions Program (ACS) – Living Labs Program is to accelerate co-development, testing, adoption, dissemination and monitoring of technologies and practices, including beneficial management practices (BMPs), that sequester carbon and/or mitigate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.

Through a collaborative approach, projects will focus on the on-farm co-development, testing, adoption and monitoring of new BMPs and technologies. Projects funded under ACS will follow the living lab innovation approach. A living lab is an integrated approach to agricultural innovation that brings together farmers, scientists, and other participants to co-develop, test, and monitor new BMPs and technologies in a real-life context where they will be used: on Canadian farms.

The program will consider projects within the following 2 priority areas:

  • Carbon sequestration (for example, cover crops, intercropping, conversion of marginal land to permanent cover, shelterbelts, inclusion of pulses in rotations)
  • Greenhouse gas mitigation (for example, nutrient management, feeding strategies).

It is expected that approved comprehensive projects will start project activities in spring 2023.
Document Title: Agricultural Climate Solutions - Living Labs Program

Family Name: Emissions Reduction Fund – Onshore Program
Family Summary:
The Canadian government has committed to an increased reduction target for oil and gas methane emissions of at least 75% by 2030. The $675M Emissions Reduction Fund (ERF) – Onshore Program was designed to help Canadian onshore oil and gas companies invest in green solutions and infrastructure to continue their progress toward reducing methane emissions while facing the COVID-19 pandemic. The final intake closed on 31 March 2022, and funding eligibility closed by 31 March 2023.

The ERF Onshore Program funded 24 companies, to implement 91 projects across Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta and British Columbia, representing $170M in repayable and partially repayable Natural Resouces Canada funding.
Document Title: Emissions Reduction Fund – Onshore Program

Family Name: Guide for preparing the Regional Environmental Impact Statement
Family Summary: Mexico's Secretariat of Environment and Natural Resources (SEMARNAT) published the Technical Guidelines in 2022, which set out the requirements for preparing a Regional Environmental Impact Statement under the country's environmental assessment procedure. The guide establishes a framework requiring project proponents to identify cumulative environmental impacts. Proponents should identify greenhouse gas emissions and assess ecosystem vulnerability to climate change factors such as sea level rise, hurricanes, floods, and temperature increases, and use simulation models to project environmental factor changes over 5, 10, 15, and 20-year timeframes. Projects should include specific climate change adaptation and mitigation measures and disaster prevention and vulnerability reduction strategies.
Document Title: Technical Guidelines

Family Name: Renewed Forest Bioeconomy Framework
Family Summary:
The vision of this Framework is for Canada to be a global leader in the use of forest biomass for advanced bioproducts and innovative solutions. This vision places the forest bioeconomy at the centre of Canadian efforts to address climate change as a provider of low carbon building solutions, renewable energy, and feedstocks for sustainable chemicals and materials. It asserts that Canada’s forest sector can take collaborative action to provide these solutions sustainably while contributing to Indigenous reconciliation and rural prosperity.

This vision is built on four pillars to enhance policy coherence and collaboration across jurisdictions. Pillar 1 is Communities and Relationships. Pillar 2 is Supply of Forest Resources and Advanced Bioproducts. Pillar 3 is Demand for Advanced Forest Bioproducts and Services. Pillar 4 is Support for Innovation.
Document Title: Renewed Forest Bioeconomy Framework

Family Name: National Climate Change and Health Policy and Revised Action Plan
Family Summary:
The goal of this Policy is to improve the coordination and effectiveness of measures that will lead the country into a climate-resilient and healthier future. Climate change causes sea-level rise, resulting in coastal erosion, flooding, and seawater intrusion affecting freshwater resources. Diarrheal diseases are common in the Marshall Islands, especially among children, which will only worsen with changing rainfall patterns associated with climate change. Climate change is also affecting food production and consumption patterns.

Actions include sustainable agricultural practices, advanced weather forecasts, increased rainwater harvesting, water quality testing, promotion of healthy nutrition, elimination of mosquito breeding sites, improved waste disposal and recycling, better walking and cycling infrastructure, measures to promote sport and exercise, and flood and heat protection measures.

The Action Plan covers the period 2021-2025, with yearly progress reports recommended.
Document Title: National Climate Change and Health Policy and Revised Action Plan

Family Name: National Agroforestry Strategy 2022-2032
Family Summary: The strategy focuses on: the establishment of a policy and institutional basis for the wider promotion and adoption of agroforestry in The Gambia; the enhancement of coordination in agroforestry programmatic designs and implementation to promote institutional collaboration and technical backstopping; promotion of agroforestry knowledge creation, dissemination, adoption and monitoring for effective adoption of context-appropriate agroforestry practices at scale; adoption of investment mechanisms for agroforestry through wood and non-wood-based value chains promotion, including: multilateral environmental agreement, participatory forest management, protected areas, energy production through fuelwood; creation of an environment for inclusive participation of all stakeholders in agroforestry promotion and the associated value chains.
Document Title: National Agroforestry Strategy 2022-2032

Family Name: Finance Act 2079 Income Tax Reduction for EV Assembly Industry
Family Summary: New industries that manufacture four-wheeled electric vehicles are eligible for a 40% income tax break for five years from the date they begin operations.
Document Title: Finance Act 2079 Income Tax Reduction for EV Assembly Industry

Family Name: Resolution No. 490 on requirements of the Air Pollution Control Programme for Motor Vehicles
Family Summary: This 2022 regulation sets conventional emission standards (PROCONVE 8), based on Euro VI standards. The standard will apply to all new road heavy-duty vehicles, from January 2022 for new vehicle models, and January 2023 for the rest of the industry.
Document Title: Resolution No. 490 on requirements of the Air Pollution Control Programme for Motor Vehicles

Family Name: Resolution 40715/2019: Wholesale Energy Market with RES
Family Summary: To reach a more eco-friendly energy matrix, the Ministry of Mines and Energy approved resolution 40715 that stipulates that, as of 2023, at least 10% of electricity purchases of wholesalers of the Wholesale Energy Market destined to serve end users must come from renewables (FNCER), through long-term contracts.
Document Title: Resolution 40715/2019: Wholesale Energy Market with RES

Family Name: Vehicle emissions standards
Family Summary:
"Chilean heavy-duty vehicles adhere either to European or US Standards, with the Euro V/US 2007 standards currently in place for PM emissions and the Euro IV/US 2004 standards in place for NOx emissions. Euro VI standards are projected to be implemented in Chile by September 2020

As with heavy-duty vehicles, light and medium-duty vehicles in Chile conform to either US or European standards. Light and medium-duty diesel and gasoline vehicles were adopted to Euro 5/US Tier 2 in 2012 and 2014, with Euro VI standards to be implemented by September 2022"
Document Title: Vehicle emissions standards

Family Name: Adapt and thrive: Building a climate-resilient New Zealand
Family Summary: This document sets out Aotearoa New Zealand’s long-term strategy and first national adaptation plan.
Document Title: Adapt and thrive: Building a climate-resilient New Zealand

Family Name: Taxonomy of Green Projects
Family Summary:
The “Classification (taxonomy) of “green” projects subject to financing through “green” bonds and “green” loans” (as approved by Decree of the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 996 dated December 31, 2021) is a unified system of classification of economic activities, project categories, and assets aimed at increasing the efficiency of use of existing natural resources, lowering the level of negative environmental impacts, increasing energy efficiency, energy savings, climate change mitigation, and climate change adaptation.

According to the AIFC's (Astana International Finance Centre) Green Finance Centre (https://aifc.kz/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/green-finance-market-kz-10-m-2023.pdf), adoption of this Taxonomy contributed to market players’ rising interest in sustainable financial instruments as well as in projects on the transition of the country’s economy to low-carbon development.

This Taxonomy (updated on 27 March 2024) covers eight project categories:

  1. Renewable energy;
  2. Energy efficiency;
  3. Green buildings;
  4. Pollution prevention and control;
  5. Sustainable water use and waste;
  6. Sustainable agriculture, land management, forestry, biodiversity conservation and ecotourism;
  7. Clean transport; and
  8. Transitory energy (additional category).
Document Title: Taxonomy of Green Projects

Family Name: Programme for the Development of Green Infrastructure in Urban Areas for the period 2021-2030
Family Summary: The Programme for the Development of Green Infrastructure in Urban Areas for the period 2021-2030 aims to promote green urban development, at a higher standard than existing services and with strong public awareness of its benefits. The programme acknowledges climate change as a major threat to the development and maintenance of urban areas, with the most significant direct hazards including flooding, extreme heat and wind. It recognises the uneven and sparse distribution of existing green infrastructure, and promotes capacity building for effective planning, as well as an allocation of funding to new green projects. Through projects increasing energy efficiency, the programme also aims to mitigate greenhouse emissions and their effect on climate change.
Document Title: Programme for the Development of Green Infrastructure in Urban Areas for the period 2021-2030

Family Summary:
This regulation partially transposes Directive (EU) 2018/2001 and sets out the shares of energy from renewable energy sources for use in the transport sector and the method of their calculation.

Article 4 establishes energy share from renewable energy sources in the transport sector in each calendar year, starting from 10.1% in 2022 until 20.8% in 2030.

Family Name: Light-Duty Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Emissions Standards
Family Summary: In December 2021, Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) finalized revised national greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions standards for passenger cars and light trucks for Model Years 2023- 2026. Family Name: Decree No. 441/021 (establishing a carbon tax)
Family Summary:
On January 1st, 2022 the Uruguayan carbon tax was established through Presidential Decree No. 441/021. 
The executive branch of government may update the tax rate annually, and may increase the rate in accordance with any variation established by the Consumer Price Index. The tax applies to all liquid fuels, with the exception of jet fuel. Sales of fuel to manufacturers of gasoline, for the purposes of producing gasoline, are also exempted from the tax. The carbon tax rate for 2022 is UYU 5,645.45 (approximately USD 137.29).
Document Title: Decree No. 441/021 (establishing a carbon tax)

Family Name: 14th Five Year Plan: Energy Conservation Emissions Reduction Work Plan (2021-2025)
Family Summary:
This plan 1) promotes energy conservation and emission reduction, 2) aims to enhance pollution prevention and control efforts, 3) seeks to accelerate the establishment and improvement of a green, low-carbon and circular development economic system, 4) promotes a comprehensive green transformation of economic and social development, and 5) seeks to help achieve carbon peak and neutrality goals.

The plan notably aims to implement key projects of energy conservation and emission reduction within key industries such as iron and steel, non-ferrous metals, building materials, petrochemicals and chemicals. It also calls for the development of urban green planning, green construction, and green operation management, and promote the construction of low-carbon cities, resilient cities, sponge cities, and "waste-free cities".

The plan identifies the following sectoral measures to advance (non-exhaustive list):
  • Transport : promote the construction of green railways, green roads, green ports, green waterways, and green airports, and promote the construction of infrastructure such as charging and replacing electricity, filling (gas), hydrogen refueling, and shore power at ports and airports in an orderly manner. Increase the proportion of new energy vehicles used in urban public transport, rental, logistics, sanitation cleaning and other vehicles. Speed ​​up the transport of bulk cargo and medium- and long-distance goods by "road-to-rail" and "road-to-water", and vigorously develop multimodal transport such as hot metal, road-rail, and public-water. Fully implement the China VI emission standards for automobiles and the China IV emission standards for non-road mobile diesel machinery, and basically eliminate vehicles with emission standards of China III and below. (...)
  • Rural areas and agriculture: Accelerate the application of wind energy, solar energy, biomass energy and other renewable energy in agricultural production and rural life, and promote clean heating in rural areas in an orderly manner. Promote the application of agricultural electric vehicles, energy-saving and environmentally friendly agricultural machinery and fishing boats, develop energy-saving agricultural greenhouses, and promote energy-saving renovation of farm buildings and the construction of green farm buildings.  (...)
  • Energy efficiency improvement projects of public institutions: Accelerate the energy-saving renovation of existing building envelopes, heating, cooling, lighting and other facilities and equipment in public institutions, and encourage the use of contract energy management models such as energy cost trusteeship. Take the lead in phasing out old cars, take the lead in purchasing and using energy-saving and new energy vehicles.  (...)
  • Coal: "clean and efficient utilisation of coal", and promote the transformation of existing coal-fired power units to save coal and reduce consumption, the transformation of heating supply, and the transformation of flexibility. Reform and linkage”, continue to promote the ultra-low emission transformation of coal-fired power units.  (...)
  • Environmental infrastructure level improvement projects: accelerate the construction of an environmental infrastructure system integrating sewage, garbage, solid waste, hazardous waste, medical waste treatment and disposal facilities and monitoring and supervision capabilities, and promote the formation of an environmental infrastructure network extending from cities to towns and villages. (...)
Document Title: 14th Five Year Plan: Energy Conservation Emissions Reduction Work Plan (2021-2025)

Family Name: Decree No. 2021-1841 on the promotion of active or shared mobility or public transport in advertising messages for motorised land vehicles
Family Summary: This decree sets the methods of application of the obligation to promote active or shared mobility or public transport in advertising messages in favor of motorised land vehicles.
Document Title: Decree No. 2021-1841 on the promotion of active or shared mobility or public transport in advertising messages for motorised land vehicles

Family Name: National Climate Finance Strategy of Belize 2021-2026
Family Summary: The National Climate Finance Strategy of Belize 2021-2026 notes that the ambition level of the country's NDCs is highly dependent on access to adequate finance, and as such the strategy aims to enhance climate financing for adaptation and mitigation in the short to medium term. As core strategic directions it aims to prioritise climate adaptation, leverage international private and public finance, promote domestic private climate finance, enhance financing based on carbon assets, climate-proof development projects across the economy, build a co-ordinated risk financing mechanism, and explore non-conventional climate finance strategies.
Document Title: National Climate Finance Strategy of Belize 2021-2026

Family Name: National Forest Strategy
Family Summary: The National Forest Strategy (SFN), adopted pursuant to Article 6(1) of Decreto Legislativo 3 aprile 2018, n. 34, establishes Italy’s strategic framework for the conservation, enhancement and sustainable management of the national forest heritage. Its overall aim is to protect and strengthen Italy’s forests so that they remain resilient, biodiversity-rich ecosystems capable of contributing to climate change mitigation and adaptation, while providing environmental, social and economic benefits. The strategy defines national guidelines for the development of the forestry sector and its related supply chains, in line with international and European commitments, including the EU Forest Strategy.The strategy is structured around three main objectives: (A) promoting sustainable forest management and the multifunctional role of forests, including biodiversity conservation, ecosystem services, land protection and climate mitigation; (B) improving the efficient use of forest resources to support sustainable economic development and strengthen forestry supply chains in rural, inland and urban areas; and (C) enhancing knowledge, research public awareness and international cooperation on forest policies.
Document Title: Interministerial Decree approving the National Forest Strategy

Family Summary: This resolution amends resolution CVM 480, introducing criteria for Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) information disclosure by listed companies/ security issuers. These companies are required to disclose, or explain reasons for not disclosing information on their management of potential climate risks, their GHG inventories, and their compliance with the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosure (TCFD) or other recommendations.
Document Title: CVM Resolution 59/2021

Family Name: Climate Investment and Financing Pilot Work Plan
Family Summary:
This work plan was released by the Ministry of Ecology and the Environment, the National Development and Reform Commission, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, the People’s Bank of China, the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission, the China Banking Regulatory Commission, the General Office of the China Securities Regulatory Commission and the Office of the State Administration of Management. It aims at translating strategic decisions on carbon peaking and carbon neutrality at the local level, and to explore differentiated climate investment and financing systems, mechanisms, organisational forms, service methods and management systems.

The document sets the rules and requirements to select pilot programs that will implement innovating climate financing frameworks.
Document Title: Climate Investment and Financing Pilot Work Plan

Family Name: The overall plan for the pilot program of the comprehensive reform of the market-based allocation of production factors (notice 51 of the State Office)
Family Summary:
This plan defines the government's plan for the pilot program on a wide range of reforms of the market determinants of production factors. It notably establishes 1) a system of green accounting, 2) the concept of ecological products value realisation, and 3) environmental responsibility for public and private entities. 

Section 24 of the document states that the government will support the creation of a "green factor trading mechanism". This would notably entail the trading of carbon emission rights, pollution discharge rights, energy use rights, water rights, etc. The government will also also explore other schemes, such as a paid-for-acquisition mechanism for carbon emission quotas and energy use rights indicators.
Document Title: The overall plan for the pilot program of the comprehensive reform of the market-based allocation of production factors (notice 51 of the State Office)

Family Name: Spanish Self-Consumption Roadmap
Family Summary: The Spanish Self-Consumption Roadmap establishes an ambitious framework to promote distributed energy generation, targeting between 9,000 MW and 14,000 MW of installed self-consumption capacity by 2030. The policy outlines 37 specific measures focusing on public awareness, professional training, and regulatory improvements, supported by European Next Generation funds with an initial allocation of 660 million euros (expandable to 1.32 billion euros). The strategy emphasises collective self-consumption initiatives, particularly in residential communities, and industrial applications, while establishing coordination mechanisms between different administrative levels through a National Self-Consumption Board. This policy builds upon Spain's competitive advantages in renewable resources, particularly solar energy, and aims to contribute to the country's broader decarbonisation goals while stimulating economic growth through the creation of an estimated 25,000 direct and indirect jobs.
Document Title: Spanish Self-Consumption Roadmap

Family Name: Law No. 145 on Territorial and Urban Planning and Land Management
Family Summary:
The objectives of this Law are to define the instruments of territorial and urban planning, their content, scope, reach, approval bodies, and management. Urbanisation and building approvals are regulated to be granted through the final approval of the building permit, when the territorial and urban planning determinations and regulations established in the territorial and urban planning instruments, the technical standards for construction, the prevention of natural and anthropogenic hazards, and the impact of climate change have been complied with. The Ministry of Science, Technology and the Environment and the Ministry of Construction are responsible for ensuring the integration of climate change adaptation in land use and urban planning, and housing construction, respectively.

On undevelopable land, the competent authority may, in exceptional cases, authorise the construction of isolated infrastructure, buildings, and dwellings necessary for the exploitation of these territories, avoiding risk situations by ensuring preventive protection or adaptation works in the face of exposure to natural or anthropogenic hazards or the expected impact of climate change.

In coastal areas and areas vulnerable to climate change, planning shall take into account the principles of depopulation and reduction of population density, as appropriate.
Document Title: Law No. 145 on Territorial and Urban Planning and Land Management

Family Name: Regulation 896/2021 of the open call for support for the purchase of zero-emission and low-emission vehicles under the Emissions Trading Facility
Family Summary:
Regulation No. 896 establishes the procedural framework for an open project tender designed to reduce transport-sector greenhouse gas emissions. It utilizes funds from the Emissions Trading Facility to provide financial support for purchasing "green" vehicles, outlining all administrative requirements from application to final audit.The primary objective is to incentivize the use of environmentally friendly transportation in Latvia. Eligible vehicles are defined by two technical categories:

  • Fully Electric: 0g CO2/km emission profile using pure electric propulsion.
  • Externally Chargeable Hybrids: Vehicles combining electric and internal combustion power that emit no more than 50g CO2/km according to standard WLTP testing.

The total funding available is EUR 30,000,000
Document Title: Regulation 896/2021 of the open call for proposals for projects financed by the Emissions Trading Facility "Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions in the transport sector - support for the purchase of zero-emission and low-emission vehicles"

Family Name: National Risk Management Strategy for Security Threats of the Slovak Republic
Family Summary:
The vision of the Strategy is to consolidate the civil protection and crisis management system as a tool based on an integrated approach to risk management and multi-sectoral cooperation. It gives priority to the protection of life and health of persons, property, the environment, natural heritage and social values, and the associated need for society to adapt to the negative effects of climate change. Preventive measures, planning and use of modern technologies, training, comprehensive rescue and search equipment and crisis communication, as well as information sharing and quality education in this area, create the preconditions for reducing vulnerability and increasing resilience of the population and the territory of the Slovak. The strategy aims to improve the institutional, professional, knowledge, technological, competence and legislative framework as a tool for achieving resilience and better coordination of risk management, targeted accountability of actors, diversified funding, early warning and public information, including an adequate response to climate change, as well as the subsequent use of lessons learned from emergencies and crisis situations in planning for reducing the impact of hazards.

To effectively build environmental and socio-economic resilience to climate change at the regional level, a proactive approach and long-term integrated planning are needed that addresses existing aspects of sustainable development, taking into account increased vulnerability, and leads to the economic development of the region. Key risk reduction activities are the assessment and analysis of damages and the related investments and subsequent forms of financing, including lump sum budget measures to ensure prevention and preparedness in each municipality, the establishment of special fees, taxes or tax disincentives in relation to regional development, climate change or energy.

Since specific financial proposals for the allocation of resources for prevention and adaptation to the risks of security threats associated with climate change can only be implemented on the basis of damage assessments and long-term estimates of potential damage due to ongoing trends of disasters, crisis situations and emergencies, it is important to ensure a methodology for damage assessment also in cooperation with rural and municipal authorities. To this end, the introduction of a unified damage planning system is envisaged. In addition, we plan to involve scientific research capacities in the assessment of potential damage, with a view to planning long-term investments in reducing the risk of security threats associated with climate change.
Document Title: Resolution 65/2022 on the National Strategy for the Management of Security Threats in the Slovak Republic

Family Name: Administrative Measures for Legal (ESG) Disclosure of Enterprise Environmental Information
Family Summary:
These measures aim to standardise  legal disclosure of corporate environmental information (ESG) "and strengthen social supervision, in accordance with the Environmental Protection Law, the Cleaner Production Promotion Law, the Measures for the Formulation of Provisions on Information Disclosure by Public Enterprises and Institutions, and the Legal Disclosure of Environmental Information. These Measures are applicable to the disclosure of environmental information by enterprises in accordance with the law and their supervision and management activities (art. 2). The Ministry of Ecology and Environment shall be responsible for the organisation, guidance, supervision and management of the legal disclosure of environmental information across the country (art. 3).

Under Chapter III on disclosure content and time limit, art. 12 states that an enterprise's annual environmental information disclosure report according to law shall include the following contents:
(1) Basic information of the enterprise, including basic information on production and ecological environment protection of the enterprise;
(...)
(4) Carbon emission information, including information on emissions, emission facilities, etc.

Article 15 states that "when disclosing annual environmental information, listed companies and bond-issuing enterprises shall disclose relevant information in accordance with the following provisions in addition to the environmental information specified in Article 12:
(1) If a listed company raises funds by issuing stocks, bonds, depositary receipts, medium-term notes, short-term financing bills, ultra-short-term financing bills, asset securitisation, bank loans, etc., it shall disclose the annual financing form, amount, investment direction and other information, as well as information on climate change, ecological and environmental protection of the projects invested by the financing;
(2) Where a bond-issuing enterprise raises funds by issuing stocks, bonds, depositary receipts, exchangeable bonds, medium-term notes, short-term financing bills, ultra-short-term financing bills, asset securitization, bank loans, etc., it shall disclose the annual financing form and amount , investment direction and other information, as well as information on climate change, ecological and environmental protection of the projects invested by financing."
Document Title: Administrative Measures for Legal (ESG) Disclosure of Enterprise Environmental Information

Family Name: 2050 Carbon Neutrality Roadmap for the Marine and Fisheries Sector
Family Summary:
The Roadmap 2050 Carbon Neutrality Roadmap for the Marine and Fisheries Sector setts the sector’s net greenhouse gas emissions target for 2050 at -3.24 million tons. This is a proactive goal that represents a reduction of 7.3 million tons compared with the 2018 emissions of the marine and fisheries sector. The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries set the target with the intention of pursuing a wide variety of policy measures, including replacing fossil fuels with marine energy and maximizing the absorption of blue carbon.

The Roadmap covers the sectors of: Shipping; Fisheries and fishing villages; Marine energy; Blue carbon; Ports; and other sectors and basis for implementation (carbon capture and storage and marine waste).
Document Title: 2050 Carbon Neutrality Roadmap for the Marine and Fisheries Sector

Family Name: Transport Canada’s Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2021/22 to 2025/26
Family Summary:
Transport Canada's Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2021/22 to 2025/26 is a five-year plan designed to build the department's climate resilience and support broader adaptation efforts across the Canadian transportation sector.

The main goals of the plan are to:

  • Goal 1: Strengthen internal knowledge and capacity: This focuses on educating Transport Canada employees and teams about climate risks and opportunities, enabling them to take adaptation actions in their work. It includes learning activities, identifying information gaps, and sharing knowledge.
  • Goal 2: Embed climate change considerations: This aims to integrate climate considerations into Transport Canada's corporate planning, decision-making tools, regulatory processes, programs, plans, and strategies.
  • Goal 3: Understand climate change impacts on the transportation system: This goal supports Transport Canada's ability to maintain a safe, secure, efficient, and environmentally responsible transportation system despite evolving climate change impacts. Activities include cost-benefit analyses of adaptation and research on co-benefits of climate mitigation and adaptation in the transportation sector.
  • Goal 4: Demonstrate continued leadership in transportation adaptation: This involves Transport Canada's ongoing engagement with domestic and international forums, leveraging partnerships, and exchanging knowledge to optimize its adaptation outcomes and contribute its expertise to the field of transportation adaptation

This plan is "evergreen," allowing for continuous integration of new or evolving climate risks and opportunities over its five-year span. It also contributes to the department's integrated risk management efforts.
Document Title: Transport Canada’s Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2021/22 to 2025/26

Family Name: Decree on the environmental declaration of construction and decoration products as well as electrical, electronic and climate engineering equipment (No. 2021-1674 of 16 December 2021)
Family Summary: This Decree regulates the environmental data necessary to assess the environmental performance of buildings or parts of buildings, to determine their environmental impacts, in particular on climate change.
Document Title: Decree on the environmental declaration of construction and decoration products as well as electrical, electronic and climate engineering equipment (No. 2021-1674 of 16 December 2021)

Family Name: Work Plan for Promoting the Development of Multimodal Transport and Optimizing the Transport Structure (2021-2025)
Family Summary: This Work Plan contributes to China's target of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality by optimising the transport structure. It promotes the shift of bulk cargo and medium-long distance freight transport from highway to railway, and from highway to waterway. It continues the application of innovative "single-bill" and "single-container" systems for multimodal transport. Through this Work Plan, actions are set out for the optimisation of the transport structure for multimodal transport development, the formulation of standards such as Intermodal loading unit identification and Classification and codes of intermodal transport cargo, and the strengthening of the connection between different modes of transport. According to China's 2024 Biennial Transparency Report, by the end of 2022, a total of 116 multimodal transport demonstration projects had been launched in four batches. In 2022, the demonstration routes covered the national integrated transport hubs and the main framework of the three-dimensional transport network. In 2022, the national railway and waterway freight volume increased by 432 million tons and 937 million tons, respectively compared to 2020, with growth rates of 9.49% and 12.31% respectively.
Document Title: Work Plan for Promoting the Development of Multimodal Transport and Optimizing the Transport Structure (2021-2025)

Family Name: 14th Five-Year Plan for Railway Development
Family Summary: This Plan sets out the actions relating to green development in the railway sector, to achieve China's target of carbon neutrality by 2060. The actions include integrating green technology in railway equipment; construction; and energy consumption; to utilise technology for ecological protection and restoration; adn to reduce pollution.
Document Title: 14th Five-Year Plan for Railway Development

Family Name: EU Urban Mobility Framework
Family Summary:
The new European Urban Mobility Framework outlines a common a list of measures and initiatives for cities to meet the challenge of making their mobility more sustainable.


The framework announces:

  • A more ambitious approach to sustainable urban mobility planning and related indicators. 
  • Stronger action to create climate-neutral cities. Action points cover making urban transport resilient, environmentally-friendly and energy-efficient and identifying zero-emission solutions for urban logistics.
  • More targeted EU funding and better synergies between different programmes to support these action points. 
  • New measures to promote active mobility and protect vulnerable road users in the form of a greater focus on walking and cycling in revised Sustainable Urban Mobility Plan (SUMP) guidance documents, guidance on the safe use of micromobility devices, and guidance on quality infrastructure for vulnerable road users.
  • More effective zero-emission city freight logistics and last-mile deliveries thanks to the integration of sustainable urban logistics plans (SULPs) within the SUMP framework, and voluntary data sharing between all types of stakeholder;
  • Guidance on passenger transport-on-demand (taxis and Private Hire Vehicles with drivers (PHV) so it can become more sustainable and deliver efficient services to citizens while addressing social and safety concerns.
  • Accelerate digitalisation and innovation by incorporating urban mobility in the work on commercially-sensitive data for multimodal digital mobility services such as Mobility as a Service (MaaS) applications, and on a common European mobility data space to facilitate access to and sharing of mobility data.
  • Efforts to increase awareness and reinforce citizen engagement within and beyond the EU.
  • A reformed EU-level group that involves cities, regions Member States and urban mobility stakeholders more closely.


In 2023, the European Parliament passed a resolution calling for aspects of the EU Urban Mobility Framework to be updated or strengthened.
Document Title: EU Urban Mobility Framework
