Family Name: Roadmap for the development of offshore wind and marine energy in Spain
Family Summary:
The roadmap for offshore wind and marine energy highlights the strategic role of these renewable energy sources (collectively termed "blue energy") in Spain's transition to a decarbonised economy. According to this roadmap, offshore wind, particularly floating technology suitable for deep waters, complements other renewables with its stable, predictable output, especially in Spanish autumn and winter. Equally, the roadmap considers that marine energies, including wave and tidal power, are advancing from pre-commercial stages to scalable market deployment, offering long-term potential beyond 2030. The initiative aims to position Spain as a European hub for technological innovation and industrial development in this sector, leveraging its robust wind, shipbuilding, and maritime engineering industries to enhance local supply chains, create skilled jobs, and foster economic growth.
Aligned with the EU's Renewable Energy Strategy and Spain's Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC) 2021–2030, the roadmap sets different goals, including deploying 1–3 GW of offshore wind and 40–60 MW of marine energy by 2030. It emphasises environmental sustainability, calling for compatibility with marine biodiversity conservation and spatial planning. The roadmap also integrates funding under Spain's Recovery, Transformation, and Resilience Plan, ensuring adherence to the "do no significant harm" principle. By fostering innovation and attracting investment, it aspires to establish Spain as a leader in marine renewable energy, contributing to EU climate targets and the global energy transition.
Document Title: Roadmap for the Development of Offshore Wind and Marine Energy in Spain

Collection Name: Law 7/2021 on climate change and energy transition [Spain]
Collection Summary:
Enacted in 2021, this law establishes Spain's legal framework for achieving climate neutrality by 2050, aligning with the Paris Agreement and Sustainable Development Goals. It mandates a 23% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 (compared to 1990 levels), alongside ambitious renewable energy targets, including 42% of final energy consumption from renewables and 74% renewable electricity generation by 2030. Energy efficiency measures aim for a 39.5% reduction in primary energy consumption within the same timeframe. The law also prohibits new hydrocarbon and radioactive mineral exploitation, requires emission-free transport systems in cities with populations exceeding 50,000, and emphasises sustainable urban mobility.

The legislation includes a national Just Transition Strategy to ensure equitable economic opportunities, particularly for vulnerable regions, while fostering adaptation and resilience to climate risks across critical sectors such as water, biodiversity, and health. It creates governance mechanisms like the Expert Committee on Climate Change and Energy Transition to monitor progress and updates to Spain's Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC). Projecting investments exceeding €200 billion by 2030, the law is expected to enhance Spain’s GDP by €16.5–25.7 billion annually and generate 250,000–350,000 new jobs. The focus on education, innovation, and public awareness underscores its commitment to a holistic and inclusive transition.

This collection represent a body of policies, strategies, and plans enacted under this law.
Family Name: National Climate Change Adaptation Plan. Working program 2021-2025
Family Summary: The Spanish government, recognising the urgency demanded by scientific consensus on climate action, has established a comprehensive legal framework to address climate change. Central to this effort is the National Climate Change Adaptation Plan (PNACC) 2021–2030, the primary tool for coordinating national adaptation strategies. This framework is implemented through five-year Work Programmes, with the first covering 2021–2025. The Work Programme outlines 257 measures and 11 sub-measures addressing 85 of the 88 action lines defined in the PNACC. These measures span diverse sectors, including health, water resources, biodiversity, urban planning, and energy, while incorporating cross-cutting themes such as gender equality, social vulnerability, and climate risk prevention. Responsibilities are distributed across national ministries, regional governments, and local authorities, ensuring a collaborative approach to adaptation. The programme’s design aims to mobilise public and private actors, ensuring alignment with broader societal and environmental goals, while advancing Spain’s commitment to climate resilience and sustainable development.
Document Title: National Climate Change Adaptation Plan. Working program 2021-2025

Family Name: Medium-Term Development Policy Framework 2022-2025
Family Summary:
This document sets the government's development vision as following:  “create an optimistic, self-confident and prosperous nation, through the creative exploitation of our human and natural resources, and operating within a democratic, open and fair society in which mutual trust and economic opportunities exist for all”. To realise this vision, the document defines the following priorities:  economic growth; digitisation; science, technology, and innovation; urbanisation and infrastructural deficits; youth unemployment; public health; emergency preparedness, the fight against pandemics; and climate change.

The document sets specific targets to protect the natural and built environments, notably to  promote sustainable extraction of mineral resources; improve coastal and marine management; combat deforestation, desertification and soil erosion; enhance climate change resilience; improve efficiency and effectiveness of road transport infrastructure and services; modernise and extend railway network; expand the digital landscape; mainstream science, technology and innovation in all socio-economic activities; ensure availability of clean, affordable and accessible energy; promote sustainable spatially integrated development of human settlements; enhance the quality of life in rural areas; promote resilient urban development; and efficient and effective land administration.
Document Title: Medium-Term Development Policy Framework 2022-2025

Family Name: 14th Five-Year Plan for the Development of a Modern Integrated Transport System
Family Summary: In line with China's goal to acheive carbon neutrality by 2060, the Plan includes a chapter on actions to comprehensively promote green and low-carbon transformation, by optimising the transportation structure, promoting low-carbon facilities and equipment, preventing pollution, improving the effiency of reesource utilisation; and improving carbon emissions monitoring and management.
Document Title: 14th Five-Year Plan for the Development of a Modern Integrated Transport System

Family Name: Order on certificates of taking into account energy and environmental performance requirements and carrying out a feasibility study on the various energy supply solutions for building construction in metropolitan France (9 December 2021)
Family Summary: This is the Order of 9 December 2021 on certificates of taking into account energy and environmental performance requirements and carrying out a feasibility study on the various energy supply solutions for building construction in metropolitan France and amending the decree of 11 October 2011 on certificates of taking into account thermal regulations and carrying out a feasibility study on energy supplies for new buildings or new parts of buildings.The study and certificates consider the impact of climate change assoicated with building components including the construction site and requires hte client to undertake to comply with justifying the impact on climate change, and the climate change impacts arising from primary energy consumption and building components. The summer discomfort level is also measured.
Document Title: Order on certificates of taking into account energy and environmental performance requirements and carrying out a feasibility study on the various energy supply solutions for building construction in metropolitan France (9 December 2021)

Family Name: Polish Hydrogen Strategy to 2030, in perspective until 2040
Family Summary: This strategy sets out the Polish government's approach to promoting the use of hydrogen in the transition to a low-emission economy. The strategy sets out six goas relating to increasing the use of hydrogen technology in energy and heating; the use of hydrogen as an alternative fuel in transport; the use of hydrogen to support the decarbonization of industry; supporting hydrogen production; developing transmission, distribution, and storage infrastructure; and creating a stable regulatory environment for the industry.
Document Title: Polish Hydrogen Strategy to 2030, in perspective until 2040

Family Name: Agreement on Investments in a continually greener Denmark
Family Summary:
The government and a political majority signed a political agreement on Investments in a continually greener Denmark on December 4, 2021, as part of the 2022 Finance Act. With the green sub-agreement on the 2022 Finance Act (FL22), a new fund of DKK 2.5 billion is introduced with the aim of achieving additional negative emissions of 0.5 million tons annually from 2025 onwards through CO2 capture. The fund operates with a support period of 8 years, which is intended to ensure that the cheapest biogenic sources are not committed long-term to storage purposes, but can be released for utilisation purposes.

The fund can provide support for negative emissions from CO2 capture and storage from biogenic sources and subsequent storage underground. Biogenic sources refer to CO2 capture during biogas upgrading, biomass-based power and heat production, the biogenic share of CO2 captured at waste incineration plants, as well as carbon capture directly from the atmosphere (DACCS).
Document Title: Agreement on Investments in a continually greener Denmark

Family Name: Forest Act
Family Summary:
The Forest Act establishes the Forestry Commission to manage State forests and protect forests. It also establishes a Mining Timber Permit Board and provides for the conservation of timber resources and the compulsory afforestation of private land, and regulates and controls the trade in forest produce.

One of the guiding principles of the Act is that the role of forests and trees in climate change should be recognised, given their unique ability to contribute to both climate change adaptation and mitigation.
Document Title: Forest Amendment Act, 2021

Family Name: Powering Australia
Family Summary: The Australian Government’s Powering Australia plan aims to create jobs, reduce pressure on energy bills, and lower emissions by boosting renewable energy. The plan contains measures across sectors funded in the 2023-2024 budget. It supports Australia's commitment to reach Net-Zero by 2050.
Document Title: Powering Australia

Family Name: Global Gateway
Family Summary:
The Global Gateway updates the European Union's foreign policy strategy and defines its major objectives as being the digital transition, energy and climate change, transport, health, and education and research. The core concepts that organise the strategy are connectivity, infrastructure and development. The strategy was developed in partnership with the EU's member states. It aims at channeling EUR 300 billion of investments through a range of financial instruments between 2021 and 2027 in the aforementioned core objectives. 

The strategy builds on existing official collaborations, notably the 2018 EU-Asia Connectivity Strategy, the Connectivity Partnerships with Japan and India, the Economic and Investment Plan for the Western Balkans , the Eastern Partnership , and the Southern Neighbourhood.
Document Title: Information on the Global Gateway

Family Name: Resolution 18/2024 approving the National Waste Management Plan
Family Summary:
The National Waste Management Plan "Uruguay + Circular," formulated by the Ministry of Environment for the period 2023-2033 is approved by the Resolution 18/2024.The National Waste Management Plan (PNGR) is Uruguay’s first national strategy under the Comprehensive Waste Management Law (Law 19.829/2019), aimed at improving waste management and promoting a circular economy. It supports sustainable development by reducing waste-related impacts and recognizing waste as a resource for economic and social transformation.Developed through collaborative efforts, the PNGR integrates environmental, economic, social, and gender perspectives. It covers all waste types under the law and sets strategic goals for the next ten years, structured into four key chapters:

  • General Framework – Defines the policy, international context, and main directions.
  • Baseline – Assesses Uruguay’s current waste management situation.
  • Strategic Objectives Actions – Sets goals, indicators, and strategies.
  • Monitoring Evaluation – Establishes tracking mechanisms and key actor

The plan aims to enhance local waste management, mobilize resources, and drive sustainable transformation in the sector. It also suggests mainstreaming climate change considerations (impacts on food systems, mitigation and adaptation measures) and includes measures for building resilient food systems. It proposes generation synergies with partnerships to fulfil the Sustainable Development Goals and climate change commitments.
Document Title: Resolution 18/024

Family Name: National Energy and Climate Plan
Family Summary: This plan aims to address the five dimensions of the Energy Union, namely energy security, the internal energy market, energy efficiency, decarbonization, and research, innovation, and competitiveness. It seeks to review targets and policies in the energy sector to alleviate energy poverty and provide affordable energy, to provide and ensure accessibility to quantitative data on the sector as well as to inform relevant stakeholders on the plan. The key policies and objectives focus on the increase in renewable energy sources, reduction of fossil fuels in transport and industry, incorporation of fuel switching and energy efficiency measures targetting the building sector, and the improvement of forestry management. The targets set in the plan include 18.7% emission savings and 54.4% renewable energy share in energy demand.
Document Title: National Energy and Climate Plan 2019 Draft

Family Name: Strategy on Agriculture and Rural Development 2022-2028
Family Summary:
This strategy guides the implementation of the Agriculture and Rural Development Program. It aims to transform agro-rural economies by making them more resilient, inclusive, and sustainable. It specifically seeks to improve the efficiency and sustainability of farm production and natural resource management, to support businesses in rural areas, and to create efficient public services through comprehensive institutional and sector reforms.

To advance Kosovo's commitment to climate change mitigation and adaptation, this strategy identifies challenges and opportunities within the agriculture
sector, including challenges in reducing GHG emissions from enteric fermentation and in producing energy from biomass, as well as investment barriers in implementing the climate change adaptation measure of rehabilitating and modernising the irrigation and drainage system in the country
Document Title: Strategy for Agriculture and Rural Development 2022-2028

Family Name: Sustainable Banking Strategic Plan 2022-2025
Family Summary: This plan seeks to guide, facilitate, and inform the banking sector to effectively finance Turkey’s transition to a low carbon economy through sustainable finance. Its goals include 1) managing and supervising climate-related financial risks, 2) improving the required finance for the development of sustainable economy, and 3) developing cooperation between relevant parties to support the first two goals.
Document Title: Sustainable Banking Strategic Plan 2022-2025

Family Name: National Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2021
Family Summary:
Madagascar’s National Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2021 is centred around three strategic areas 1) strengthen the governance and integration of adaptation 2) implement a priority sectoral action programme and 3) financing adaptation to climate change. 

Overall, the adaptation plan includes the following goals:

  • Establishment of a green belt to strengthen the fight against desertification and resilience to climate change
  • Strengthening the adaptation of the agricultural sector and the resilience of rural populations in the far South
  • Strengthening the resilience of rural populations through the development and organisation of export sectors
  • Strengthening the adaptation of the fisheries sector and developing warning systems and associated action plans 
  • Improving access to drinking water in urban and rural areas
  • Strengthening early warning systems to ensure the health sector's resilience in the face of climate change 
  • Accelerating reforestation through the operationalisation of the REDD+ mechanism and the development of ecosystem services
  • Improving the conservation of natural forests and the management of protected areas including the development of climate refuge zones in the interior and on the periphery
  • Protection of coastal infrastructures and economic activities (including tourism) against the rise sea level rise
  • Improving early warning systems for cyclones, as part of a regional effort at the level of the Indian Ocean level
  • Development of resilient rice paddies that emit less methane
  • Optimisation of the resilience of new technologies
Document Title: National Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2021

Family Name: Supreme Decree 4632, creating agricultural development programs according to the productive reconstruction and food sovereignty policies
Family Summary: The Bolivian Supreme Decree 4632 establishes six national agricultural development programmes for 2022-2025, representing a significant investment grounded in constitutional provisions promoting sustainable agricultural productivity and comprehensive rural development. This initiative includes the National Programme for Beekeeping Production Support and Strengthening, which explicitly incorporates climate change resilience criteria and receives a dedicated budget for policy implementation.The decree also includes programmes for urban and peri-urban agriculture and sustainable fishing and aquaculture, both contributing to environmental sustainability through local food systems and reduced transport emissions. Additional programmes focus on cotton production, Andean grains (including quinoa, cañahua, amaranth, and tarwi), and tubers and roots development. Through these programmes, Bolivia aims to enhance food sovereignty and security whilst promoting sustainable agricultural methods.
Document Title: Supreme Decree 4632, creating agricultural development programs according to the productive reconstruction and food sovereignty policies

Family Name: Climate change in the healthcare and social welfare sector: Climate change adaptation plan of Ministry of Social Affairs and Health (2021–2031)
Family Summary:
The Adaptation Plan is based on the National Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2022 and the climate change and adaptation work carried out in the healthcare and social welfare sector.

The Adaptation Plan focuses particularly on health protection and the adaptation of healthcare in the administrative branch of the Ministry of Social Affairs and Health. The aim of the Adaptation Plan is to assess the current state of adaptation and the structures supporting it, to identify current and new adaptation measures in the health and wellbeing sector and to translate the measures into more concrete terms and clarify them in the area of responsibility of the Ministry of Social Affairs and Health's administrative branch. The intention is to introduce the Adaptation Plan to healthcare and social welfare operators and to increase risk awareness in the healthcare and social welfare sectors.

The Adaptation Plan contains 43 objectives and 92 recommendations for measures. The measures cover areas relating to environmental health, health and social services (including occupational safety and health), social effects, mitigation measures and repercussions. The Ministry of Social Affairs and Health is responsible for implementing, monitoring and assessing the Adaptation Plan.
Document Title: Climate change in the healthcare and social welfare sector: Climate change adaptation plan of Ministry of Social Affairs and Health (2021–2031)

Family Name: K-Taxonomy
Family Summary:
The Korean green classification system (K-Taxonomy) was established in 2021, to define and categorise sustainable economic activities, providing clear principles and standards for green economic activities for investors and companies. It is meant to enable the financial industry to smoothly develop green finance without worrying about greenwashing. Through this, it is expected that confidence in green finance will be increased and the inflow of green funds into green businesses will be promoted, forming favourable conditions for the growth of the green market.

The revisions in December 2024 included the addition of green economic activities relating to the sustainable conservation of water; transition to a circular economy including refill stations and waste recycling technology; pollution prevention and management; and biodiversity conservation.
Document Title: K-Taxonomy (2022 version)

Family Name: Circular Spatial and Building Management Development Programme for the period 2021-2030
Family Summary: The Circular Spatial and Building Management Development Programme recognises climate change mitigation and adaptation as major challenges for Croatia, and aims to mainstream circular principles in building management and spatial development up to 2030. Goals include greater energy efficiency, integration of renewable energy sources, greater use of recycled material, reduced building waste, increased building lifespans, and revitalisation of unused buildings, among others. The programme calls for stronger data collection infrastructure, improved public awareness of circularity, and general capacity building in the construction sector and others.
Document Title: Circular Spatial and Building Management Development Programme for the period 2021-2030

Family Name: Ten-Year Transmission Grid Development Plan 2022-2031
Family Summary: This plan aligns with the energy development strategy (2021) in promoting a 'moderate' transition to low-carbon energy sources, and aligns with EU objectives to increase the renewable energy share nationally. The plan contains measures to build further wind, solar and hydroelectric generation sources, and the grid interconnections enabling their efficient integration.
Document Title: Ten-Year Transmission Grid Development Plan 2022-2031

Family Name: Strategic Development Plan 2022–2026 for Fisan
Family Summary: The Investment Fund for Food and Nutritional Security (FISAN) has the objective to facilitate private and community investment in all segments of the food and agri-food value chains with the ultimate goal of increasing the volume and quality of agricultural financing offers. All orientations aim to align with policies and strategies at international, national and sectoral levels to ensure food security, improve nutrition and promote sustainable rural agriculture. FISAN will intervene by i) targeting interventions based on three dimensions (sub-regional geographical concentration, value chains and density of units) ii) a particular focus on support for young people and start-ups iii) strengthening the resilience of private agricultural operators to climate change; iv) an inclusive approach that takes gender issues into account; v) enhanced access to information through a local communication strategy; vi) performance-based partnership management; vii) rigorous fiduciary risk management; and viii) digitalisation as a factor for inclusive development.
Document Title: Strategic Development Plan 2022–2026 for Fisan

Family Name: Kingdom of Denmark Green Bond Framework
Family Summary:
The Danish government will also issue green bonds governed by this Framework in order to contribute to the sustainable transition of the economy and reach the objectives set out in the Paris Agreement and the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, which call for significant investments.

This Green Bond Framework is aligned with the 2021 version of the Green Bond Principles (GBP), as published by the International Capital Market Association (ICMA). The Danish government recognises the importance of a common definition of sustainable economic activities that enhances transparency, thereby supporting the continued development of the green bond market. Consequently, eligible green expenditures under this framework are evaluated according to, and to the extent possible, aligned with the criteria in the EU classification system forsustainable economic activities (the “EU Taxonomy”) as adopted by the Commission on 4 June 2021 in the Delegated Act for climate change mitigation and climate change adaptation activities. Further, this framework has sought to alignwith key elements of the proposed regulation on a European Green Bond Standard (EU GBS) on 6 July 2021 including the bond-related, reporting, and external verification requirements.

This Framework may be amended from time to time to reflect market developments, including changes to the EU Taxonomy and the ICMA GBP, as well as developments around the EU GBS, with the aim of adapting to, and aligning with, best market practices.
Document Title: Kingdom of Denmark Green Bond Framework

Family Name: Universal Access by 2025 and Transforming the Electricity Sub-sector Strategic Roadmap 2021-2040
Family Summary: This Strategic Electricity Sector Roadmap 2021-2040’s goals are to transform the electricity sector in order to exploit new sources of reliable and affordable electricity and to achieve the Universal Access target by 2025.
Document Title: Universal Access by 2025 and Transforming the Electricity Sub-sector Strategic Roadmap 2021-2040

Family Name: Science and Technology Innovation Plan for the Energy Sector in the 14th Five-Year Plan Period
Family Summary: To achieve the goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, this Plan aims to improve the innovation systems and mechanisms, strengthen innovation capabilities and talent development, bolster fundamental applied research, and accelerate the RD and deployment of advanced, practical technologies. These include technologies for source carbon reduction, process carbon reduction; end-of-pipe carbon sequestration; cleaner and efficient coal utilisation carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS); offshore wind power industry technology and energy storage innovation.
Document Title: Science and Technology Innovation Plan for the Energy Sector in the 14th Five-Year Plan Period

Family Name: Resolution 355/2021 - Comprehensive Climate Change Management Plan for the Agricultural Sector (PIGCCS)
Family Summary:
The objective of the Comprehensive Climate Change Management Plan for the Agricultural Sector (PIGCCS) is to identify, coordinate, and guide the implementation of measures that the agricultural sector must develop to mitigate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and reduce its vulnerability to climate change. Additionally, this plan aims to increase sector productivity, contribute to food security, improve the well-being of rural populations, and preserve the natural resources that sustain it.

This document consists of eight chapters. The general objective is to align the sector's efforts to mitigate GHG emissions while enhancing productivity, ensuring food security, supporting rural well-being, and protecting the natural foundation of agriculture.

The strategic topics defined for the plan’s development include:

  • Scientific data and traditional knowledge for decision-making.
  • Transitioning agricultural production toward sustainability.
  • Integrating disaster risk management with climate change adaptation.
  • Developing climate financing mechanisms and recognizing the differentiated impacts of climate change on men and women.
  • Strengthening and creating new leadership at national and local levels.
Document Title: Resolution 355/2021 - Comprehensive Climate Change Management Plan for the Agricultural Sector

Family Name: Ministry of Power's Orders No. 13/12/2016-R&R (waiver of transmission charges for renewable energy energy)
Family Summary:
Various Ministry of Power's Orders, all numbered 23/12/2016-RR, but dated differently. The Orders dated 23 November 2021 and 30 November 2021 waive inter-state transmission charges for the transmission of electricity generated from solar and wind sources of energy.

The Order dated 1 December 2022 waives similar transmission charges for energy produced from hydro power projects where the power purchase agreement is signed on or before 30 June 2025. Subsequently, charges will be levied each year incrementally at 25%, 50%, 75% and finally at 100% from 1 July 2028.

The addendum Order 12/07/2023-RCM dated 29 May 2023 waives transmission charges for energy from offshore wind power projects commissioned on or before 31 December 2032, and for green hydrogen or green ammonia projects commissioned after 31 December 2030, also with charges levied incrementally thereafter. The stated intention is to facilitate the execution of offshore wind energy initiatives, to promote the expansion of green hydrogen/green ammonia projects, to promote development of pump storage plants, and to encourgae the offtake of renewable energy from energy storage system projects.
Document Title: Ministry of Power Order 12/07/2023-RCM dated 29 May 2023

Family Name: National Response Plan with a Multi-Threat and Health Approach 2020
Family Summary:
In 2008, the Government of Reconciliation and National Unity (GRUN) presented the National Response Plan (PNR) as a regulatory instrument of SINAPRED reference for the coordination of response plans, as well as for the development of policies, strategies, conceptual and methodological instruments that allow for the generation of common planning for all response actors at the institutional, sectoral, and territorial levels. In light of the achievements and progress of the last 12 years, a new version of the National Response Plan is being presented, updated and in line with the state of risk management in our country.

This document is organized into 10 chapters. The first three are introductory and contextual aspects (this Introduction, Regulatory Framework, and Objectives). This is followed, in a logical order, by the definition of scenarios from a multi-hazard approach, the national response organization, alert systems, the sectoral and institutional response strategy, activation of the National Risk Management Plan (PNR), and support systems and resources. A chapter on post-disaster recovery concludes the PNR, emphasizing that pre-disaster recovery planning and preparation must occur alongside response preparation, and highlighting progress and prospects for strengthening this aspect of comprehensive risk management.
Document Title: National Response Plan with a Multi-Threat and Health Approach 2020 (Plan Nacional de Respuesta con Enfoque Multiamenaza y Salud 2020)

Family Name: 14th Five-Year Plan for Energy and Resource Conservation in Public Institutions
Family Summary: This Plan sets targets for controlling the total energy consumption, carbon emissions, and energy/carbon intensity of public institutions. Public institutions are to reach carbon peaking by 2025 for specified areas, while nationally they will reach carbon peaking by 2030. The key tasks are to promote the electrification of heating; promote solar projects; control coal consumption; promote electric vehicles; develop green buildings; enhance energy efficiency of existing buildings; green data centres; promote green low-carbon technology products through government procurement; and enhance publicity of the concept of low-carbon development.
Document Title: 14th Five-Year Plan for Energy and Resource Conservation in Public Institutions

Family Name: Implementation Plan for Deepening Green and Low-Carbon Leadership Actions in Public Institutions to Promote Carbon Peaking
Family Summary: This Implementation Plan defines the goals and tasks for the green and low-carbon development of public institutions, and proposes key measures such as accelerating the green and low-carbon transformation of energy use and improving the green and low-carbon operation of buildings.
Document Title: Implementation Plan for Deepening Green and Low-Carbon Leadership Actions in Public Institutions to Promote Carbon Peaking

Family Name: Carbon Neutral Industry and Energy R&D Strategy
Family Summary:
The Carbon Neutral Industry and Energy RD Strategy was established to promote technology development in sectors where GHG mitigation is essential for achieving carbon neutrality, such as steel, petrochemicals, cement, and semiconductors/displays.

It targets to:1. Transform industrial energy consumption structure into carbon neutral one;2. Develop and diffuse carbon neutral energy technologies widely in all industries; and3. Promote carbon neutral new markets and jobs.For these goals, it identifies 17 specific technological fields in four categories including: i) energy, ii) industry, iii) transportation, and iv) cross-cutting. To support RD in these areas, this strategy focuses on strengthening support system and reinforcing infrastructures.
Document Title: Carbon Neutral Industry and Energy R&D Strategy

Family Name: EU Soil Strategy for 2030
Family Summary: The EU Soil Strategy aims for healthy, resilient soils across the EU by 2050, making soil protection, sustainable use, and restoration the norm. By 2030, it targets combating desertification, restoring degraded and carbon-rich soils, achieving net greenhouse gas removals in land use, reducing nutrient losses and hazardous pesticide use, and improving water and soil quality. By 2050, the strategy seeks no net land take, minimal soil pollution, climate neutrality, and a fully climate-resilient society, while contributing to biodiversity, circular economy, and human health objectives.
Document Title: EU Soil Strategy for 2030

Family Name: Transport Development Strategy of the Republic of Slovenia Until 2030
Family Summary: The Transport Development Strategy of the Republic of Slovenia until 2030 integrates climate and energy objectives by promoting the transition toward a sustainable, low-emission transport system, addressing the sector’s significant contribution to greenhouse gas emissions. The strategy highlights that, without structural changes, transport emissions would rise substantially by 2030 despite technological improvements, underscoring the need for systemic measures. It therefore supports improved energy efficiency, reduced reliance on fossil fuels, and a modal shift toward public transport, rail, and intermodal solutions. In line with national and EU climate policy, it incorporates indicative sectoral targets, including halting the growth of transport emissions by 2020 compared to 2008, and limiting their increase to no more than 18% by 2030 relative to 2005 (equivalent to a 15% reduction compared to 2008). These objectives are to be achieved through sustainable mobility measures, infrastructure optimisation, and integration with broader decarbonisation efforts, positioning transport as a key sector in Slovenia’s transition toward long-term climate mitigation.
Document Title: Transport Development Strategy of the Republic of Slovenia Until 2030

Family Name: Resolution 383/2021 on GHG performance labelling for light-duty vehicles
Family Summary: Since May 2022, new vehicles on sale have to display information about their fuel consumption and emissions level.
Document Title: Resolution 383/2021on GHG performance labelling for light-duty vehicles

Family Name: 14th Five-Year Plan for Green Industrial Development
Family Summary:
The Plan, aimed at achieving carbon neutrality, contains actions on green manufacturing; accelerating the optimisation and upgrading of industrial structure, vigorously promoting industrial energy conservation and carbon reduction; comprehensively improving resource utilisation efficiency; actively promoting clean production transformation; improving the supply capacity of green low-carbon technology, green products and services; and mutual promoting and deeply integrating of industrial green low-carbon transformation and industrial empowerment green development.

The Plan proposes that by 2025, the green and low-carbon transformation of industrial structure an d production mode will achieve remarkable results, the wide application of green low-carbon technology and equipment, the efficiency of energy resource utilisation will be greatly improved, and the level of green manufacturing will be comprehensively improved, laying a solid foundation for the carbon peaking in the industrial field in 2030.

It notably seeks to increase awareness to climate issues, boost the production and use of renewable energy sources, and generally create the conditions for making the economy sustainable.

Family Name: Opinion on Deepening the Fight Against Pollution
Family Summary: In line with the goal of carbon neutrality, the Opinion calls for synergies of pollution-carbon reduction, and outlines seven measures to advance the carbon peaking action. During the 14th Five-Year Plan period, China will strictly control the growth of coal consumption. The coal consumption in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region and its surrounding areas will decrease by around 10%, the Yangtze River Delta region by around 5%, and the Fenwei Plain will see negative growth in coal consumption. In principle, the addition of new self-provided coal-fired units will no longer be permitted. Support will be provided for the implementation of clean energy alternatives for existing self-provided coal-fired units, and there will be encouragement for self-provided power plants to transition into public power plants. China will push for a simultaneous increase in natural gas use and decrease in coal use, prioritising natural gas for households and clean heating. China will boost the share of electricity in overall energy consumption and eliminate scattered coal use in key plain areas. China will steadily expand the pilot program for clean heating to more cities and steadily improve clean heating in the northern regions.
Document Title: Opinion on Deepening the Fight Against Pollution

Family Name: Resolution 252/2021 to approve the Catalogue of Cuban Beaches
Family Summary: The Catalogue of Cuban Beaches is the basis on which the concept, baseline and analysis of progress in the conservation and restoration of the country's beaches will be established. This Catalogue establishes administrative control of sandy beaches and includes as priority the coastal zone sectors identified in the State Plan for Combating Climate Change. The Institute of Marine Sectors is the agency responsible.
Document Title: Resolution 252/2021 to approve the Catalogue of Cuban Beaches

Family Name: UAE’s Hydrogen Leadership Roadmap
Family Summary:
The UAE's Hydrogen Leadership Roadmap is a comprehensive national blueprint to support domestic low-carbon industries, contribute to the net-zero emissions ambition, and position the country as a competitive exporter of clean hydrogen, as stated in the Updated Second Nationally Determined Contribution of the United Arab Emirates.

The Roadmap comprises three core objectives:
  1. Unlocking new sources of value creation through exports of low carbon hydrogen, derivatives and products to key importing regions;
  2. Fostering new hydrogen derivative opportunities through low-carbon steel, sustainable kerosene as well as other priority UAE industries; and
  3. Contributing to the UAE's 2050 net zero commitments. 

The UAE aims to support the low-carbon hydrogen business through five enablers:
  1. A clear regulatory framework backed by policies, incentives, standards, and certifications;
  2. Best-in-class technology through value-add partnerships and the UAE domestic research and development structure;
  3. Access to existing and new Government-to-Government relationships to accelerate growth of a domestic ecosystem;
  4. Readily available land and infrastructure resources to support domestic production; and
  5. Green financing within the UAE and in international capital markets.

This information is based on the Emirates News Agency WAM.
Document Title: UAE’s Hydrogen Leadership Roadmap

Family Name: Climate Action Plan
Family Summary:
The Climate Action Plan 2021 provides a roadmap for achieving 51% reduction in overall greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 and reaching net zero emissions by 2050.


The Plan lists actions required to deliver on these climate targets and sets indicative ranges of emissions reductions for each sector of the economy.


The Plan seeks to facilitate a Just Transition and suggests a Just Transition implementation plan for the Midlands Region. It emphasises the necessity of fostering citizen engagement and proposes several measures in this regard. The Plan also emphasises the leading role that the public sector is expected to play in the net zero transition through including a Public Sector Climate Action Mandate.
Document Title: Climate Action Plan 2021

Family Name: Decree No. 4612 establishing the Presidential Commission for Climate Change
Family Summary: Venezuela established a permanent Presidential Commission for Climate Change through Decree No. 4.612. This commission serves as an advisory body to the President on climate change matters and comprises representatives from five ministries: ecosocialism (presiding), planning, foreign relations, industries and national production, and science and technology. The commission operates under a technical secretariat exercised by the Ministry of Popular Power for Ecosocialism and may convene additional government bodies and subject matter experts as required.The commission's primary functions encompass advising the President on climate change issues, developing proposals for national climate change regulations, and coordinating the creation of the National Climate Change Strategy alongside National Adaptation and Mitigation Plans for presidential approval. Additional responsibilities include ensuring effective technical, administrative and financial information management; strengthening state, regional and municipal monitoring, reporting and verification capacities for climate adaptation and mitigation; and promoting risk management measures to address climate change vulnerabilities and impacts. The commission is empowered to establish working groups for specific topics and must develop its internal operating regulations within ninety days of the decree's publication.
Document Title: Decree No. 4612 establishing the Presidential Commission for Climate Change (Decreto No. 4612 que establece la Comisión Presidencial para el Cambio Climático)

Family Name: Decree No. 4.586 (Green Climate Fund)
Family Summary: The decree 4.586, published in the official gazette 42.246, creates the National Committee of Green Climate Fund. Family Summary: The Future Fuels and Vehicles Strategy sets out how the Australian Government will support a technology-led approach to reducing emissions in the transport sector. This strategy was published under the previous Australian Government.
Document Title: Future Fuels and Vehicles Strategy

Family Name: National Adaptation Plan to Climate Variability and Change for the Coastal Zone
Family Summary:
The Plan recognises climate change as one of the main threats to the country's coastal zones, and thus, sets the following objectives:

  • Capacity building to identify impacts and vulnerabilities of coastal zones;
  • Capacity building to define concrete adaptation measures in coastal zones;
  • Use Uruguay's experience as a reference model for other countries, establishing a knowledge transfer process between countries in the region.
Document Title: National Adaptation Plan to Climate Variability and Change for the Coastal Zone

Family Name: Guyana Power and Light Development and Expansion Programme 2022-2026
Family Summary: The Guyana Power and Light Development and Expansion Programme for 2022-2026 functions as the core program for electricity infrastructure development, through the state-owned and ministerially controlled Guyana Power and Light Incorporated. The programme includes provisions to contribute to global climate change mitigation efforts, including substantial expansions to hydropower supply which are expected to cover over 90% of energy demand once complete. There are further planned expansions for biomass, wind and solar, and natural gas is favoured over oil as a fossil fuel. The programme also contains provisions to increase grid and power source resilience to flooding and temperature threats, which are projected to increase under climate change.
Document Title: Guyana Power and Light Development and Expansion Programme 2022-2026

Family Name: Long-Term Vision 2050
Family Summary: Nigeria's Long-Term Vision 2050 serves as a precursor to its subsequent Long-Term Low Emissions Development Strategy (LT-LEDS), and aims towards a low-carbon, climate-resilient high-growth circular economy by 2050, halving greenhouse gas emissions compared to the current levels (at time of writing). It aims to remain gender-responsive, and aim for further emissions reductions to net zero in the long term. The vision draws its guiding principles from the National Climate Change Policy (2021-2030)`: a focus on local action, combined with global thinking; sustainable economic growth with robust adaptation; effective citizenship participation; shared vision of social inclusion and stakeholder responsibility; identification of low-carbon-enabling activities; promotion of environmental quality and ecological equilibrium; transparency accountability and equity; robust ongoing monitoring, evaluation and reporting; international partnership/co-operation; policy co-ordination; and good governance.
Document Title: Long-Term Vision 2050

Family Name: Sustainable Finance Framework
Family Summary:
This Framework supports Turkey's sustainability commitments and outlines how it plans to raise Green and Social Sustainable Financing Instruments, contributing to the domestic and international development of the sustainable financing market. Turkey may issue green, social and sustainability financing instruments under this Framework, funding eligible green and/or social projects that conform to the International Capital Market Association (ICMA) Green Bond Principles and Social Bond Principles, and Loan Market Association (LMA) Green Loan Principles.

One of the eligible sustainable project categories is climate change adaptation, with the following impact reporting metrics:

  • Reduced/avoided water loss (in reservoirs / waterways / natural habitats etc.) (m³);

Family Name: Presidential Regulation No. 110 of 2025 on Implementation of Carbon Economic Value Instruments and National Greenhouse Gas Emission Control
Family Summary:
This Presidential Regulation introduces several important changes that reshape Indonesia’s carbon governance framework. It replaces Presidential Regulation No. 98 of 2021 on Carbon Economic Value (the Implementation of Carbon Pricing to Achieve the Nationally Determined Contribution Target and Control over Greenhouse Gas Emissions in the National Development). The key elements are:

  1. The recognition of Voluntary Carbon Market (VCM) activities;
  2. The acknowledgement of established international standards, and abolition of the earlier Mutual Recognition Agreement (MRA) mecahnism;
  3. Carbon projects may choose to obtain certification either from the Indonesian government (Sertifikat Pengurangan Emisi – SPE) or from other recognized certification bodies (non-SPE);
  4. Differentiation between Correpsonding Adjustment (CA) units under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement for carbon units authorised for international transfer, and non-CA units that remain within the boundaries of Indonesia;
  5. A centralised registry (Sistem Registri Unit Karbon; SRUK) for all carbon unit data and transactions; and
  6. Continuity of Implementing Regulations: Although Presidential Regulation No. 98 of 2021 is revoked, its implementing regulations (Regulation 21/2022 on Guidelines for Implementing the Carbon Economic Value) remain in effect insofar as they do not contradict the new regulation.
Document Title: Presidential Regulation No. 110 of 2025 on Implementation of Carbon Economic Value Instruments and National Greenhouse Gas Emission Control

Family Name: Action Plan for Carbon Dioxide Peaking before 2030 (‘1+N’)
Family Summary:
This Action Plan aims to enable carbon dioxide peaking by 2030 and ultimately achieve carbon neutrality. It covers the 14th and 15th five-year plan periods. It seeks to strengthen the government's ability to mobilise the nation as a whole and involve the private sector into the decarbonisation efforts. It highlights 1) the promotion of innovation in green and low-carbon science and technology, 2) institutional reform in energy and other relevant fields, 3) the development of incentives and constraint mechanisms, and 4) the need to "avoid excessive side effects" of decarbonisation policies, so as to maintain energy security and economic development as the bottom line. The plan also calls for stimulating international cooperation, notably through 1) global climate governance, 2) green cooperation on business, technology, and finance, and 3) making Belt and Road Initiative green.

The Action Plan further seeks to enhance policy support by developing  a unified and standardised carbon emissions measuring and counting system; improve laws, regulations and standards; optimise economic policies; and establish further market mechanisms. It should be implemented through a strengthening of planning and coordination efforts, ensuring that responsibilities are taken at all levels, and develop a strict oversight and assessment system.

The document lists a series of sectoral policy goals which are as following.

Energy demand and supply:
  • Promote coal substitution as well as transformation and upgrading. The document mandates to "strictly control the scale of supplementary coal power" and of coal consumption growth.
  • Develop wind, solar and hydropower according to local context.
  • Develop nuclear power through a safe and orderly approach 
  • Rationally regulating oil and gas consumption. The plan notably promotes alternatives like advanced liquid biofuels and sustainable aviation fuel, the use of liquid natural gas for peak shaving power stations and as fuel for vehicles and ships.
  • Speed up the development of the new electric power system.
  • Raise capacity for managing energy conservation across the board. It notably seeks to introduce an energy budget management approach, intensify energy conservation reviews regarding fixed-asset investment projects, and conduct comprehensive assessments of projects’ energy use and carbon emissions.
  • Implement key energy conservation and carbon reduction projects.
  • Advance better energy saving performance and higher efficiency of major energy consuming equipments.
  • Strengthen energy conservation and carbon reduction in new types of infrastructure.

Industry sector:
  • Promote green and low-carbon development in the industrial domain. implement the green manufacturing project, vigorously promote green design, refine the green manufacturing system, and build green factories and industrial parks. 
  • Push the steel industry to peak carbon dioxide emissions 
  • Push the non-ferrous metals industry to peak carbon dioxide emissions 
  • Push the building materials industry to peak carbon dioxide emissions 
  • Push the petrochemical industry to peak carbon dioxide emissions 
  • Curb the irrational expansion of energy-intensive and high-emission projects 

Urban and rural development:
  • Promoting green and low-carbon transformation in urban and rural development
  • Accelerating building energy efficiency improvement
  • Accelerating the optimization of building energy consumption structure
  • Promoting a low-carbon transition in rural development and energy consumption

Transport:
  • Promote low-carbon transformation of transport vehicles and equipment
  • Develop green, high efficiency transport systems
  • Accelerate construction of green transport infrastructure

Promotion of circular economy:
  • Push industrial parks to develop in a circular manner
  • Strengthen the comprehensive use of bulk solid waste
  • Refine systems for resource recycling
  • Promote efforts to reduce and recycle household waste

Advance of green and low-carbon technology innovation:
  • Improve innovation mechanisms and systems. The document states that intellectual property rights protection for green and low-carbon technologies and products will be strengthened, and the testing, evaluation, and certification systems for them will be improved.
  • Enhance innovation capability and personnel training
  • Boost application-oriented basic research 
  • Accelerate the R&D and wider application of advanced practical technologies.

Consolidation and enhancement of carbon sink capacities:
  • The plan mandates to adopt a system thinking, holistic approach to the conservation of mountain, river, forest, farmland, lake, grassland, and desert ecosystems.
  • Boslster the carbon sequestration capacity of ecosystems, including through large-scale protection and restoration of major ecosystems, afforestation, and increase of grassland resources.
  • Strengthen the foundation for ecological system carbon sinks, notably by improving mechanisms for ecological compensation, measure and value carbon sinks, and establish rules for carbon sink projects in the national carbon market.
  • Promote carbon emissions reduction and carbon sequestration in agriculture and rural areas

Societal aspects:
  • Strengthen publicity and education for ecological civilization
  • Advocate green and low-carbon living patterns
  • Encourage enterprises to fulfill their social responsibilities
  • Increase training for cadres 

Subnational (regional) action:
  • Setting sound, systematic targets
  • Promote green and low-carbon development according to local conditions
  • Formulate local peaking carbon dioxide emissions plans through coordination between central and local authorities
  • Carry out pilot projects
Document Title: Action Plan for Carbon Dioxide Peaking Before 2030 (English Translation)

Family Name: Report (White paper) on China's Policies and Actions to Address Climate Change
Family Summary:
This white paper was prepared and published to report on China's progress on responding to climate change, share its practices and experiences, and enhance the understanding of the international community on its policies regarding climate change. It defines the government's long-term conceptual vision as aiming at promoting the construction of an ecological civilisation with high-quality development.


The paper reiterates that China's 14th Five-Year Plan outlines a binding indicator of "reducing carbon dioxide emissions per unit of GDP by 18% compared to 2020". It further states that in as of the end of 2019, China exceeded its 2020 target ahead of schedule and in 2020, China announced a new target: to peak its carbon dioxide emissions by 2030 and strive to achieve carbon neutrality by 2060. By 2030, China's carbon dioxide emissions per unit of GDP will decrease by more than 65% compared to 2005, and the proportion of non fossil fuels in primary energy consumption will reach about 25%. The forest stock will increase by 6 billion cubic meters compared to 2005, and the total installed capacity of wind and solar power will reach over 1.2 billion kilowatts. The proportion of non fossil fuels in primary energy consumption is increased by another five percentage points, and the target for increasing the installed capacity of non fossil fuels is increased. The forest storage volume is increased by another 1.5 billion cubic meters, with a clear goal of achieving carbon neutrality by 2060.


The paper also notes that in 2021 China announced that it would no longer build new overseas coal-fired power projects.
Document Title: Report (White paper) on China's Policies and Actions to Address Climate Change

Family Name: Resolution No. 433/2021 from the National Council of Justice (CNJ)
Family Summary: The resolution establishes the National Environmental Policy of the Judiciary. Article 12 establishes that funds from monetary payments linked to environmental crimes can be directed to public or private entities with the social purpose of preserving the environment, and may prioritise restoration projects that mitigate the effects of climate change, especially those that use renewable energies. Article 14 establishes that in condemning environmental damage, the judge must consider, among other parameters, the impact of this damage on global climate change, the diffuse damage to the peoples and communities affected and the dissuasive effect on the environmental externalities caused by the polluting activity.
Document Title: Resolution

Family Name: Australia's long term emissions reduction plan : A whole-of-economy Plan to achieve net zero emissions by 2050
Family Summary:
This plan sets out a roadmap for how Australia plans to achieve its target of net zero emissions by 2050. The plan is based on five key principles:1. Technology not taxes – no new costs for households or businesses,2. Expand choices, not mandates – we will work to expand consumer choice, both domestically and with our trading partners,3. Drive down the cost of a range of new energy technologies – bringing a portfolio of technologies to parity is the objective of Australia’s Technology Investment Roadmap,

4. Keep energy prices down with affordable and reliable power – our Plan will consolidate our advantage in affordable and reliable energy, protecting the competitiveness of our industries and the jobs they support, and

5. Be accountable for progress – transparency is essential to converting ambition into achievement. Family Name: National Action Plan on Climate Change 2022-2026
Family Summary:
The National Action Plan aims to set a clear direction for reducing greenhouse gas emissions, adapting to the impacts of climate change, and transitioning to a low-carbon economy.

 

Key objectives of the plan include:

·       Establishing emission reduction targets in line with international commitments.

·       Promoting renewable energy sources and energy efficiency.

·       Enhancing sustainable transportation and reducing reliance on fossil fuels.

·       Implementing measures to increase resilience to climate change impacts, such as extreme weather events and water scarcity.

·       Encouraging climate-smart agriculture and sustainable land use practices.

·       Investing in green technologies and innovation.

·       Raising public awareness and education on climate change. 

·       Strengthening climate governance and policy frameworks.
Document Title: National Action Plan

Family Name: National Agrofood Policy 2021-2030 (NAP 2.0)
Family Summary: The Policy aims to enhance the economic contribution of the agro-food sector to Malaysia’s economy. For this purpose, the contribution is measured by various parameters, including the sector's contribution to national GDP, average annual value-added growth, the compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of food trade balance, and food loss. The Policy thus seeks to achieve a paradigm shift towards a sustainable food system adapted to climate change, ensuring that the development of the agro-food sector does not compromise the environment.
Document Title: National Agrifood Policy 2021-2030 (NAP 2.0)

Family Name: Global Warming Countermeasures Plan
Family Summary:
This Plan sets out the direction for Japan's countermeasures, including the integrated improvement of the environment, economy and society; green recovery from Covid-19; changing the awareness, behaviour and cooperation of all actors; and contributing to GHG reductions and decarbonisation technologies. The Plan sets out the plans for reducing various GHGs and carbon sinks, including carbon pricing. The Plan also outlines the roles of the state, local governments, businesses and citizens. The measures are aligned to the Paris Agreement and the overseas deployment of countermeasures is also stated.

The Plan was revised on 18 February 2025, alongside the submission of Japan's second NDC. The revised Plan sets the targets of reduction of greenhouse gases in FY2035 and FY2040 by 60% and 73% respectively from FY2013.

Family Name: Climate Change Adaptation Plan
Family Summary:
This Plan is aimed at comprehensively and systematically implementing measures related to climate change adaptation based on scientific findings, to create a society that ensures safety, security and sustainability by preventing and reducing damage from climate change-induced impacts, stabilising people's lives, promoting the sound development of society and the economy, preserving the natural environment and building national resilience. The original version of the Plan was formulated in November 2018, just before the the Adaptation Act came into force on 1 December 2018. Following the government's publication of the Assessment Report on Climate Change Impacts in Japan in December 2020, the Adaptation Plan had been revised taking into account the latest scientific findings and after going through coordination among relevant ministries and agencies, reporting to the Climate Change Impact Assessment Subcommittee under the Global Environment Committee of the Central Environment Council and inviting public comments.

The Plan sets out the basic roles of stakeholders; the basic directions and strategies for use of scientific findings and various stakeholders including local governments and business operators; management and assessment of the progress of this Plan; sectoral measures for climate change adaptation; and fundamental measures for adaptation.

Family Name: Ministerial Resolution No. 185-2021-MINAM. Guide for the operation of the Peru Carbon Footprint tool (Resolución Ministerial Nº185-2021-MINAM. Guía para el funcionamiento de la herramienta Huella de Carbono Perú)
Family Summary: Peru's Ministerial Resolution N°185-2021-MINAM establishes the operational framework for the Peru Carbon Footprint (Huella de Carbono Perú) tool, a voluntary digital platform designed to promote greenhouse gas emissions management amongst public and private organisations. Created under Article 55 of the Climate Change Framework Law regulations, this free tool enables organisations to measure, verify, and reduce their GHG emissions whilst contributing to Peru's Nationally Determined Contributions implementation. The platform operates through a four-level system encompassing emissions measurement, third-party verification by accredited conformity assessment bodies, emissions reduction actions, and complementary measures, all aligned with international standards including ISO 14064-1:2020 and the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard.The tool functions as part of Peru's System for Monitoring Adaptation and Mitigation Measures, serving multiple climate objectives including sensitising organisations to emissions measurement through GHG inventory reporting, fostering emissions reductions that support NDC implementation, improving data quality for the national INFOCARBONO system, and establishing synergies between public and private climate initiatives.
Document Title: Guide for the operation of the Peru carbon footprint tool (Guia para el funcionamiento de la herramiento huella de carbono Perú)

Family Summary:
This Resolution from the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Brazil provides for the forwarding of information on social, environmental and climate risks. The Resolution establishes that financial institutions in segments S1, S2, S3 and S4 must send the Central Bank of Brazil information on the assessment of the social, environmental and climate risks of their exposures in credit operations and securities, and of their respective debtors. This information includes: I - identification; II - economic sector; III - risk aggravating and mitigating factors; IV - outstanding balance; V - social risk assessment; VI - environmental risk assessment; VII - climate risk assessment; VIII - information on how the exposure fits into the concepts of social nature, environmental nature and climate nature defined in the regulations in force relating to the Social, Environmental and Climate Responsibility Policy (PRSAC); IX - information on the emission, neutralisation and absorption of greenhouse gases; and X - location.

The guidance recognises that climate change poses a substantial risk and can pose an opportunity for the financial sector and requires banks to:
a)  embed the consideration of the financial risks from climate change in their governance arrangements.
b)  incorporate the financial risks from climate change into their existing financial risk management practice.
c)  develop an approach to disclosure on the financial risks from climate change.

Document Title: Agenda For Jobs II (2022-2025): Creating Prosperity And Equal Opportunity For All (2022-2025)

Family Name: Belize's REDD+ Strategy
Family Summary: Belize's REDD+ strategy operates within the REDD+ mechanism to conserve and enhance the country's forest carbon stocks, promoting good forestry practice and climate-resilient landscapes. The strategy aims to: lower net greenhouse gas emissions, transform government-level land use planning and oversight; generate sustainable economic benefits nationally; support forest-dependent communities as users and stewards of forest resources; harmonise carbon storage with biodiversity gain in restored systems; and to develop information systems to monitor forested land and prioritise strategic efforts.
Document Title: Belize's REDD+ Strategy

Family Name: Federal Plan on Sustainable Development (2021-2026)
Family Summary:
The Federal Plan for Sustainable Development 2021–2026 is Belgium’s federal government strategy for integrating sustainable development and the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into federal policymaking. It was adopted on 1 October 2021 and serves as the federal implementation framework for the UN Agenda 2030 and Belgium’s long-term sustainability vision. The plan aims to:

  • Mainstream the SDGs across all federal competences rather than treat sustainability as a separate policy area.
  • Promote cross-government coordination, so ministries and public agencies work together instead of acting in isolated policy silos.
  • Ensure policies reflect principles such as “Leave No One Behind,” gender equality, and an intersectional approach to vulnerable groups.
  • Support the transition toward a low-carbon, more circular, and socially inclusive economy.
  • Make the federal government itself operate more sustainably (e.g., procurement, administration, mobility, management practices).
Document Title: Royal Decree establishing the federal sustainable development plan

Family Name: Electricity Supply Business Plan (Rencana Usaha Penyediaan Tenaga Listrik, RUPTL)
Family Summary:
The Electricity Supply Business Plan 2021-2030 (Rencana Usaha Penyediaan Tenaga Listrik, RUPTL) prioritises development of new renewable energy (Green RUPTL), implementation of minimum energy performance standards for appliances, as well as the development of new renewable energy in Indonesia. Regarding renewables, the RUPTL plans for the 23% share from renewables in 2025 as dictated by the 2014 National Energy Policy. It also emphasises that in 2025 the role of oil will be less than 25%, coal will be at least 30%, and natural gas will be at least 22%.The RUPTL 2025–2034 continued the 10-year planning cycle, with updated projections for electricity demand, energy mix, and infrastructure development.

The latest RUPTL (2025-2034) has set a target of 42.6 GW of renewable energy capacity and 10.3 GW of energy storage by 2034. Of this, solar energy is expected to contribute 17.2 GW, while hydropower will account for 11.7 GW. In the second half of the planning period (2030-2034), 70% of the renewable energy developments are scheduled to take place. The RUPTL also includes plans to utilize nuclear energy as a baseload source, with a planned capacity of 500 MW projected for 2033, coming from two proposed projects. Additionally, the RUPTL features plans to add 3.4 GW of new grid-connected coal capacity by 2029, with another 2.8 GW planned for 2034.
Document Title: Electricity Supply Business Plan (RUPTL) 2025-2034

Family Name: National REDD+ Strategy
Family Summary: The strategy is a 30-year living document that defines key performance objectives to measure the country’s progress towards reaching its emission reduction targets. Family Name: National Electricity Policy 2021
Family Summary: Pakistan's National Electricity Policy of 2021 proposes a three-pronged goal for the power sector, namely access to afforable energy, energy security (uninterrupted supply) and sustainable energy. Family Name: General Plan for the Territory of the Republic of Lithuania
Family Summary: The General Plan establishes a guiding framework for the development of Lithuania's territory, and forms a comprehensive spatial plan for the state. Climate change mitigation and adaptation are named as major priorities in the spatial development of Lithuania. Alongside more holistic aims for green growth, decarbonisation of the transport sector is named as a key priority. The plan also aims to mainstream low-carbon development into a range of other sectors including agriculture, buildings renovation and urbanism more generally.
Document Title: General Plan for the Territory of the Republic of Lithuania

Family Name: Be Cyclist 2.0 action plan (2026–2029)
Family Summary:
The federal government has adopted the new Be Cyclist 2.0 action plan (2026–2029) , which represents a further ambitious step in promoting cycling in Belgium. This plan provides strategic direction for long-term federal cycling policy and also contributes directly to the implementation of the National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP).

It aims to accelerate Belgium's modal shift, utilizing levers like taxation and rail to complement regional infrastructure. By 2040, the goal is for 22% of all trips to be made by bike

The action plan revolves around three core pillars, integrating cycling with climate, economic, and public health policies:

  • Attractive Mobility Modal Shift by strengthening the combination of bikes and trains.The National Railway Company (NMBS/SNCB) aims to provide 164,000 fietsparkeerplaatsen by 2032 to improve home-to-station intermodal commuting.
  • Safety, Health Accessibility by expanding the national mybike.belgium.be registration platform, with the ambition to register 50% of bikes in Belgium to combat theft.
  • Adapting the highway code (wegcode) to enhance protection for vulnerable road users.
Document Title: Federal Government Action Plan for the Promotion of Bicycling ' Be Cyclist 2.0' 2026-2029

Family Name: Decree 303/2021 of 22-9-2021 approving the Regulation of the National Greenhouse Gas Emissions Compensation Market.
Family Summary: The purpose of this Regulation is to establish the technical and administrative conditions that regulate the national greenhouse gas emissions compensation market. It defines concepts as ‘voluntary GHG emissions compensation’, ‘offset projects’ and ‘carbon credits’. The offsets, which are voluntary, must serve as a tool that promotes and enhances the creation of innovative projects in the field of the fight against climate change at a local level and, at the same time, reinforce environmental mitigation policies to achieve the emission reduction objectives set by Andorra. The governmental agency responsible for the Market Registry and issuance of carbon credits is the Office of Energy and Climate Change.
Document Title: National greenhouse gas emissions compensation market

Family Name: Working Guidance for Carbon Dioxide Peaking and Carbon Neutrality in Full and Faithful Implementation of the New Development Philosophy
Family Summary: This Guidance from the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council states that to realise the goals of carbon peaking and neutrality, the principles of national coordination, prioritising conservation, public-private collaboration, international competition and collaboration, and risk prevention must be followed. By 2030, the carbon dioxide emissions per unit of GDP shall decrease by more than 65% compared to 2005 levels and non-fossil fuel consumption shall reach around 25%. The Opinion contains actions including for green and low-carbon development planning; green production; adjustment of the industrial infrastructure and curbing the development of high-emission projects; accelerating the construction of a low-carbon and efficient energy system; accelerating the construction of a low-carbon transportation system; scientific and technological development; and improving the ability of carbon sinks. Policy and monitoring systems will also be improved.

The taxonomy outlines the taxonomies for green projects, adaptation projects, and social projects, whose definitions are established by the goals and main directions of sustainble (including green) development of the Russian Federation, approved by Order N. 1912-r from July 14, 2021. The taxonomy covers waste management, energy, construction, industry, transport, water supply, biodiversity, and agriculture and broadly aligns with the taxonomies produced by the CBI and the EU.

Family Name: Green Claims Code
Family Summary:
The UK Green Claims Code is guidance from the UK Competitions & Markets Authority, which sets out principles to help businesses comply with their existing obligations under consumer protection law when making environmental claims.


The Code gives examples of how each of the principles apply and provides more detailed case studies where multiple principles apply.


Whilst this document is not legally binding, it informs businesses on how obligations under consumer protection law, including the Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 and Business Protection from Misleading Marketing Regulations 2008, may apply and is therefore considered legally relevant.

Family Name: UAE National Pathway for Food Systems Transformation
Family Summary:
The UAE developed a whole of nation food security strategy with a vision by 2051, of becoming a world-leading hub in innovation-driven food security, and aiming to be the first on the global food security index by 2051. By launching the strategy, the UAE aims to achieve zero hunger by ensuring access to safe, nutritious and sufficient food all year round throughout the world. The UAE is also the first country in the world that have appointed a Minister of State for Food and Water Security.

This Pathway identifies the status and challenges for UAE food systems, with the following strategic directions in the context of climate change as a major impediment to agricultural productivity and local food production:

  • Facilitate global agri-business trade and diversify international food sources;
  • Enhance sustainable technology-enabled domestic food supply across thevalue chain;
  • Reduce food loss and waste;
  • Sustain food safety and improve nutritional intake; and
  • Enhance capacity to respond to food security risks and crises.
Document Title: UAE National Pathway for Food Systems Transformation

Family Name: National Rail Freight Strategy
Family Summary: This Strategy aims to revitalise rail transport, which is less noisy, less polluting and less dangerous than road transport. It contains actions to increase resilience against the hazards of climate change, including low water and flooding in rail networks and in convergent initiatives with the river freight sector. Low water levels may restrict river navigation and bad weather may cause the closure of railway lines. The shift of freight traffic from road to rail is also a major priority for achieving the European Union's climate objectives.
Document Title: National Rail Freight Strategy

Family Name: Federal programme for energy efficiency and CO2-emission reduction in the agricultural and horticultural sector
Family Summary: This programme enables small and medium-sized enterprises in agriculture and horticulture to access funding opportunities for measures that significantly reduce CO2 emissions. It promotes investments in individual large or several affiliated agricultural companies, contractors or commercial machinery rings. The subsidy cap is raised to up to 900 euros per tonne of CO2 saved.
