Family Name: Adaptation strategy to climate change in the Czech Republic
Family Summary:
The Czech Climate Change Adaptation Strategy is a national adaptation strategy and is in line with the EU Adaptation Strategy.

This strategy assesses the likely impacts of climate change, makes proposals for concrete adaptation measures, and discusses legislative and economic consequences. The document further focuses on the monitoring and analysis of adaptation to the environment and public health, but also on forestry, agriculture, water regime in the landscape and water management, urbanised landscape, biodiversity and ecosystem services, tourism, transport, industry, and energy, emergencies and protection of the population.

The updated Adaptation Strategy reflects advances in the knowledge base and articulates goals for 2030 with a vision to 2050. Compared to the original document from 2015, there are, among others, updates on climate change trends and impacts or a more detailed analysis of financial costs and economic instruments.
Document Title: Adaptation strategy to climate change in the Czech Republic (1st update for the period 2021-2030)

Family Name: Qatar National Environment and Climate Change Strategy
Family Summary:
The Qatar National Environment and Climate Change Strategy (QNE) was launched in 2021 in Qatar and outlines practical steps to achieve the environment pillar of the Quatar’s National Vision 2030.

The plan sets out Qatar’s commitment to tackle climate change by diversifying the economy, building capabilities, and optimising the use of natural resources. It establishes national climate targets to enhance climate resilience and identifies a number of environmental priorities:

(a)            greenhouse gas emissions;

(b)            air quality;

(c)            biodiversity;

(d)            water;

(e)            circular economy;

(f)             waste management; and

(g)            land use,

indicating that a governance system has been established to implement the strategy, to reach the specific goals by 2030, including reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 25% by the end of 2030, as well as the establishment of 30 air quality monitoring stations by 2023, and the increase in the number of reserves concerning biodiversity.

The QNE states that plans should be reviewed every 5 years.

The QNE outlines national projects which adopt tangible measures to reduce GHGs, including: (i) the largest carbon capture project in the MENA region; (ii) improving the efficiency of the hydrocarbon toxicity treatment; (iii) the Tarsheed program (National Program for Conservation and Energy Efficiency) which conserves electricity and water consumption, including initiatives by Kahramaa, the national water authority, to reduce the loss of desalinated water and to encourage water recycling and reuse; and iv) the building of the Al Kharsaah solar power station with a capacity of 800 MW.
Document Title: Strategy

Family Name: Belgium’s recovery and resilience plan
Family Summary:
To benefit from the support of the Recovery and Resilience Facility set up by the EU in the aftermath of the COVID-19-induced economic crisis, Member States submit their recovery and resilience plans to the European Commission. Each plan sets out the reforms and investments to be implemented by end-2026 and Member States can receive financing up to a previously agreed allocation. Each plan should effectively address challenges identified in the European Semester, particularly the country-specific recommendations of 2019 and 2020 adopted by the Council. To benefit from the support of the Recovery and Resilience Facility set up by the EU in the aftermath of the COVID-19-induced economic crisis, Member States submit their recovery and resilience plans to the European Commission. Each plan sets out the reforms and investments to be implemented by end-2026 and Member States can receive financing up to a previously agreed allocation. Each plan should effectively address challenges identified in the European Semester, particularly the country-specific recommendations of 2019 and 2020 adopted by the Council. It should also advance the green and digital transitions and make Member States’ economies and societies more resilient. The Commission validates the plan after which it effectively enters in force and EU subsidies can start flowing towards the member state.

Malta is expected to receive circa €316 million in grants under the Facility. 54% of the plan’s total allocation are assessed to be directed toward reforms and investments support climate objectives. Notable investments:

  •  Energy-efficiency renovations and greening of private and public buildings: including hospitals and schools – financing deep retrofitting and renewable energy installations. €60 million
  • Access to free public transport: granting access to free public transport to selected cohorts of the population to address congestion and make transport more sustainable.
  •  A new ferry-landing place at St Paul’s Bay/Buġibba: shifting transport from road to sea and reducing emissions from the transport sector. €16 million
Document Title: Information on the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF)

Family Name: Recovery and resilience plan for Romania
Family Summary:
To benefit from the support of the Recovery and Resilience Facility set up by the EU in the aftermath of the COVID-19-induced economic crisis, Member States submit their recovery and resilience plans to the European Commission. Each plan sets out the reforms and investments to be implemented by end-2026 and Member States can receive financing up to a previously agreed allocation. Each plan should effectively address challenges identified in the European Semester, particularly the country-specific recommendations of 2019 and 2020 adopted by the Council. It should also advance the green and digital transitions and make Member States’ economies and societies more resilient. The Commission validates the plan after which it effectively enters in force and EU subsidies can start flowing towards the member state. As of March 28th, 2022, the Implementing Decision has not been released.


41% of the plan’s total allocation for reforms and investments supports climate objectives. 
  •  Railway modernisation: modernising railway infrastructure, including electrified or zero-emission railways and rolling stock. €3.9 billion
  • Urban mobility: infrastructure for a green and more secure urban transport. €1.8 billion
  • Clean energy production: phasing-out of coal and lignite power production, deployment of renewables as well as related production processes, and hydrogen. €855 million
  •  Energy efficiency of buildings: energy-efficient renovation and seismic renovation of buildings to reduce CO2 emissions by at least 0.15 million tons in private buildings and 0.075 million tons in public buildings. €2.7 billion
  • Biodiversity and environmental protection: afforestation and reforestation and forest nurseries, as well as other biodiversity measures for ecological reconstruction and species protection. €1.1 billion

In its plan, Romania indicates that it aims to exit coal by 2032, and that it will legislate on the future of mines, jobs and socio-economic support by mid 2022.

Family Name: Code on Environmental Sustainability Measures for Existing Buildings (Edition 3.0)
Family Summary: This Code follows the commitment in the Singapore Green Building Masterplan 2021 to pursue sustainability standards in Singapore's built environment. It sets out the minimum environmental sustainability standard for existing buildings and the administrative requirements in complying with the Building Control (Environmental Sustainability Measures for Existing Buildings) Regulations 2013. It includes the compliance method for determining the level of environmental sustainability of an existing building. Updated in 2021 alongside the Code for Environmental Sustainability of Buildings (Edition 4.0), one of the key changes to the Environmental Sustainability requirements will include raising the minimum energy performance standards to ensure energy efficiency improvements of 50% over the 2005 baseline for new buildings and 40% over the 2005 baseline for existing buildings which have undergone major retrofit.
Document Title: Code on Environmental Sustainability Measures for Existing Buildings (Edition 3.0)

Family Name: In View of the Climate Crisis: Iceland's Strategy on Adaptation to Climate Change
Family Summary:
This Strategy is the basis for the climate adaptation plan, as Article 5(a) of the Climate Change Act No 70/2012 provides that the Minister shall have such a plan prepared. It sets out various core values, core goals and goals for policy areas, coordination, working procedures and general oversight and evaluation.

The goals cover the areas of natural hazards; planning; water and sewage; energy; transport; private sector; fisheries and marine fish farming; agriculture; tourism; insurance and financial activities; public health; national interests, the labour market and social infrastructure; coordination of research and information; coordination of efforts to elaborate and implement measures and general goals across societal structures; and planning, status assessment and general oversight and evaluation of adaptation efforts.
Document Title: In View of the Climate Crisis: Iceland's Strategy on Adaptation to Climate Change

Family Summary: Lebanon's Least Cost Generation Plan (2021), written by the Ministry of Environment in collaboration with the World Bank, presents a roadmap for enhancing energy security and increasing production levels by 2030, while optimising for energy generation cost. The plan promotes increased adoption of solar and wind power, alongside hydroelectric pumped storage capacity and some natural gas development replacing more carbon-intensive fossil fuels.

Family Summary: This Roadmap contains specific sectoral measures and timelines, following the publication of the Climate Action Plan 2020. It covers the energy, industry, waste, agriculture, transport sectors, and green fuels.

Family Name: The 14th Five-Year Plan For Protection and Development in the Forest and Grassland Sector (2021-2025)
Family Summary: This policy sets out several targets, including forest coverage to reach 24.1% (ca. 230.53 million hectare) with forest stock volume of 19 billion cubic meters, commercial harvest over natural forest to be prohibited to preserve 1.944 billion mu of forests (129.6 million hectares), grassland vegetation cover to reach 57% and protection rate of wetland to reach 55%, an increase of nature reserve areas to 18% of national land area, and transformation of decertified land by 0.1 billion mu (6.67 million hectares).

Family Summary: This regulation updates the blending requirements for biofuels. The guidelines state that for low-sulphur grade diesel, a maximum of 5% volume by volume biodiesel should be blended. Family Name: Tonga Strategic Roadmap for Emergency and Disaster Risk Management 2021 - 2023
Family Summary:
The Tonga Strategic Roadmap for Emergency and Disaster Risk Management (DRM) is a joint outcome of the National Emergency Management Office (NEMO) and National Emergency stakeholders and supports the implementation of Tonga’s Strategic Development Framework 2015-2025, particularly the objectives relating to enhancing Tonga’s resilience to climate change and its associated risks.

The Roadmap aims to enhance dialogue and facilitate coordinated action over Tonga’s DRM response, as well as to identify mechanisms for monitoring progress, and highlights six priority outcomes to implement over the next three years:

“1: Tonga has fully functioning Emergency Operation Centres supported by an established emergency coordination and communications system.

2: Tonga’s emergency and disaster risk management sector is more inclusive.

3: Government Policy, planning, budget and procurement processes actively supports the mainstreaming of disaster risk management in Tonga.

4: The Cluster System in Tonga is fully institutionalised and strengthened.

5: Tonga has clear standards and guidelines for evacuation process management in Tonga with increased safety and security of Evacuation Centres.

6: Tonga practices Participatory Village Emergency and Disaster Risk Management planning and implementation.”

Family Name: Cabinet Decision of 25 August 2021 on Sustainability Action Programme in federal buildings
Family Summary: The Cabinet Decision of 25 August 2021 adopted the Sustainability Programme – Update 2021 (Maßnahmenprogramm Nachhaltigkeit – Weiterentwicklung 2021), which establishes the framework for implementing sustainable practices across the German federal administration. A central objective of the programme is to achieve a climate-neutral federal administration by 2030, with measures covering federal buildings, mobility, public procurement, events, catering, and organizational governance. For the federal building stock, the programme introduces the Energy Efficiency Requirements for Federal Buildings (EEFB) as mandatory minimum standards for new construction, extensions, and major renovations within the direct federal administration, while also requiring the systematic integration of renewable energy technologies wherever technically and economically feasible.
Document Title: Cabinet Decision of 25 August 2021 on Sustainability Action Programme in federal buildings

Family Name: Arable Farming Strategy 2035
Family Summary:

Family Name: 2020-2035 Waste Management Strategy
Family Summary: Tunisia's 2020-2035 Waste Management Strategy aims to enhance the waste sector over the long term while reducing waste production where possible. The strategy names three key objectives downstream from this: to protect the environment and conserve natural resources; to improve quality of life nationally; and to reduce the effects of climate change. It aims to reduce household waste per capita 10% by 2035, achieve a 20% household recycling rate and direct 40% of applicable waste towards productive organic or energy-generating disposal systems.
Document Title: 2020-2035 Waste Management Strategy

Family Name: Ministerial Regulation No. 26 26/2021 on  Rooftop Solar Power Plants
Family Summary: This Ministerial regulation improves the governance and economics of rooftop solar PV. Based on projections made by the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources, the target for Rooftop Solar Power Plants of 3.6 GW which will be carried out in stages until 2025, will have a positive impact on reducing Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions by 4.58 Million Tons of CO2e.The main refinements are (1) export provision of electricity increases from 65% to 100%, (2) excess accumulated difference in bills extended from 3 months to 6 months, (3) application period shortened to 5 days, (4) application mechanism introduced to ease submission, reporting, and supervision of Rooftop solar PV program, (5) opportunity for carbon trading from rooftop solar PV, (6) complaint centre opened for rooftop solar PV customers, and (7) arrangement extended to include non-PLN customers (IUPTLU Holders).

Family Name: UK Hydrogen Strategy
Family Summary: This document sets the government's strategy to create an integrated low carbon hydrogen sector in the UK. It considers changes to the regulatory framework, aims to assess jobs opportunity, and makes a range of financial commitments and targets, notably: 1) 5GW of low carbon hydrogen production capacity by 2030 (1GW by 2025), 2) provision of £240m for the Net Zero Hydrogen Fund out to 2024/25, 3) deliver hydrogen for heat trials, and 4) provide up to £120 million this year through the Zero Emission Bus Regional Areas (ZEBRA) scheme towards 4,000 new zero emission buses, either hydrogen or battery electric, and infrastructure needed to support them. The strategy also calls for the development of metrics to monitor progress against outcomes and the commitments made, including incorporating data on hydrogen production into the Digest of UK Energy Statistics.

Family Name: Ministerial Agreement No. MMAE-2021-018. Ecuador Carbon Zero Program
Family Summary:
The Ecuador Carbon Zero Program (Programa Ecuador Carbono Cero) is a comprehensive national initiative aimed at promoting sustainable development compatible with climate goals by addressing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through quantification, reduction, and compensation measures. Rooted in the constitutional principles of environmental protection, living well (buen vivir -  sumak kawsay), and sustainable economic practices, the program incentivises public, private, and community-led organisations to adopt positive climate practices while enhancing competitiveness. It establishes a structured framework to guide organisations in achieving certifications for carbon reduction and neutrality, including the use of international standards such as ISO 14064 and ISO 14067.
This program emphasises the mitigation of climate change by transitioning to sustainable production and consumption patterns. It promotes the conservation and restoration of ecosystems to sequester carbon, reduce deforestation, and generate environmental, social, and economic co-benefits. Key features include the introduction of the “Green Point” (“Punto Verde”) certification, awarded at three levels: Carbon Footprint Quantification, Carbon Reduction, and Carbon Neutrality. The program also incorporates compensation mechanisms through validated initiatives establishing Emissions Compensation Unities (Unidades de Compensación de Emisiones - UCEs) as a transactional system.
Document Title: Ministerial Agreement No. MMAE-2021-018. Ecuador Carbon Zero Program

Family Name: Ministerial Resolution No. 152-2021-MINAM. Methodological guidelines for the formulation and updating of Regional Climate Change Strategies (Resolución Ministerial Nº152-2021-MINAM. Lineamientos metodológicos para la formulación y la actualización de las Estrategias Regionales de Cambio Climático)
Family Summary: Peru's Ministerial Resolution N° 152-2021-MINAM establishes methodological guidelines for the formulation and updating of Regional Climate Change Strategies (ERCC), positioning them as mandatory instruments that operationalise climate action at the subnational level. These strategies, aligned with Peru's National Climate Change Strategy and Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), must incorporate both adaptation and mitigation measures across five mitigation sectors (energy, industrial processes, agriculture, land use and forestry, and waste) and seven adaptation areas (water, agriculture, forests, health, fisheries and aquaculture, tourism, and transport). The guidelines mandate that regional governments integrate climate measures into their Regional Development Plans, Strategic Institutional Plans, Operational Plans, budget programmes, and investment projects.The resolution outlines a structured five-phase methodology comprising Organisation, Territory Analysis, Planning, Implementation, and Monitoring and Evaluation, emphasising participatory processes that ensure effective engagement with state and non-state actors, particularly indigenous peoples. Regional governments must establish working groups within their Regional Environmental Commissions to lead strategy development, ensuring climate risk analysis, identification of greenhouse gas emission sources, and determination of adaptation and mitigation measures with enabling conditions.
Document Title: Methodological guidelines for the formulation and updating of Regional Climate Change Strategies (Lineamientos metodológicos para la formulación y actualización de Estrategias Regionales de Cambio Climático)

Family Name: National Social and Economic Development Plan 2021-2025 (PNDES-II)
Family Summary: Burkina Faso's National Social and Economic Development Plan 2021-2025 (PNDES-II) aims to promote sustainable development in the economy and social spheres. It also outlines key gaps in existing adaptation strategy, such as the mainstreaming of environmental considerations in education, and a lack of intersection between climate and sanitation planning.

Family Name: Climate Action Plan for Ministry of Agriculture and Food
Family Summary:
The Plan was established following the Ecological Defense Council on November 27, 2020, where the Prime Minister asked four ministries with the largest in terms of greenhouse gas emissions, to establish a climate action plan consistent with France's public policies and commitments.

This plan is structured around six axes:

  • Axis 1: Accelerate the development of agricultural practices that reduce greenhouse gas emissions;
  • Axis 2: Develop the potential for carbon sequestration in soils and forest biomass;
  • Axis 3: Support demand and consumption of food products towards practices with less environmental impact, in conjunction with the National Food and Nutrition Program (PNAN);
  • Axis 4: Supporting the adaptation of agricultural and forestry sectors to the consequences of climate change;
  • Axis 5: Teaching how to produce differently and innovating with agricultural research and development; and
  • Axis 6: With a view to achieve exemplarity, the ministry is increasing its actions to guarantee a high level of eco-responsibility.
Document Title: Climate Action Plan for Ministry of Agriculture and Food

Family Name: Decree-Law 50/2021 on the Conservation, Improvement and Sustainable Management of Soils and the Use of Fertilisers
Family Summary:
The purpose of this Decree-Law is to establish the general regulations for the conservation, improvement, and sustainable management of agricultural, livestock, and forestry soils and the use of fertilisers.

This Decree-Law provides for the National Soil Conservation and Improvement Programme, which includes a set of studies, measures, and actions aimed at conserving and improving the chemical, physical, and biological characteristics of soils - it supports food sovereignty and security, adaptation to and mitigation of the effects of climate change, and ecosystem protection.

The Decree-Law is supported by regulations in Decree 52.

Family Name: Royal Decree 690/2021 regulating the Ecological Restoration and Resilience Fund
Family Summary: The purpose of this royal decree is to regulate the Fondo de Ecological Restoration and Resilience Fund, F.C.P.J. ( FRER). FRER aims to develop  measures supporting the achievement of the objectives contemplated in the framework of the Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan within the scope of the Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge. FRER may finance actions of an annual and multiannual nature of the General State Administration, within its scope of competences. Likewise, it may act as a co-financing instrument aimed at ensuring territorial cohesion, exclusively to the extent that they are compatible with the objectives assigned in the Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan.Actions eligible for funding from the Fund include those dealing with "Climate change, its mitigation and adaptation and the strengthening of climate resilience.", and "meteorology and climatology".

Family Name: National Action Plan for the implementation of the Adaptation Strategy of Slovakia
Family Summary:
The main objective of the National Action Plan is to increase Slovakia's preparedness for the adverse effects of climate change through the implementation of cross-cutting and specific adaptation measures and tasks

The strategic priorities are:

▪ Strategic priority 1 Promote climate change adaptation as a strategic priority for the Slovak Republic, mainstream and integrate climate change adaptation into the policy and legal framework and strengthen the theme of adaptation in existing and upcoming national and sectoral plans and programs.

▪ Strategic Priority 2 Strengthen the implementation of adaptation policies and legislation, reduce bureaucratic burdens constraining the implementation of measures and improve enforcement through transparency, improved competencies and strengthened control and sanction mechanisms.

▪ Strategic Priority 3 To build and develop an effective, feasible and functioning change adaptation system in the Slovak Republic, based on the principle of subsidiarity and joint efforts of all stakeholders and the public.

▪ Strategic Priority 4 Develop the knowledge base, data collection, monitoring and research associated with the dissemination of data and information. Encourage data dissemination through open data sharing.

▪ Strategic Priority 5 Promote climate change education and solutions throughout the education process and at all levels of education. Contribute to raising public awareness.

▪ Strategic Priority 6 Promote and develop a multi-source change adaptation financing system.
Document Title: Resolution 476/2021 Regarding the Action Plan for the Implementation of the Slovak Republic’s Strategy for Adaptation to Climate Change

Family Name: National Climate Change Communication Strategy
Family Summary:
The National Climate Change Communication Strategy (NCCCS) is meant to be a tool that will guide the country's efforts to address the effects of climate change and ensure that people understand them and are able to adapt and adopt behaviour that reduces their vulnerability to its effects.

The following are the key objectives of the Strategy:

  1. To sensitise, educate and raise awareness about climate change among different sectors of the society.
  2. To interpret and translate difficult messages and concepts of climate change and ensure that people understand what they need to do to reduce their vulnerability against the climate change (behavioural change).
  3. To share lessons of the climate change initiatives implemented by the Government of Lesotho and other actors.
  4. To enable the Lesotho Meteorological Services and other key sectors to get feedback from the stakeholders about the implementation of the climate change initiatives.
  5. To raise the profile of Government Counterparts and other development partners so as to attract meaningful partnerships, collaborations and funding for wide-ranging and inclusive solutions to climate change programmes.
  6. To harmonise the indigenous knowledge and the scientific knowledge and address wrong perceptions and myths that affects adaptation and mitigation.

The guiding principles are to simplify the technical language of climate change in English and Sesotho; advocate for behaviour change; create a two-way communication platform with stakeholders; promote harmonisation of programmes and unity for climate change; and promote strong partnerships.
Document Title: National Climate Change Communication Strategy

Family Name: National Gender Equality Policy 2020-2030
Family Summary: Vanuatu's National Gender Equality Policy 2020-2030 acknowledges the disproportionate impact of climate change on women and girls, making community-driven gender-inclusive climate/disaster resilience one of its five core strategic areas. It aims to promote the incorporation of gender-responsiveness into climate adaptation and disaster laws, and build institutional capacity (including a National Gender Action Plan) for ensuring these elements are considered.
Document Title: National Gender Equality Policy 2020-2030

Family Name: Climate strategy for cultural environment management 2021-2030
Family Summary:
The Strategy aims to show how cultural environments can help reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and to help the actors in the cultural heritage field to be better equipped to deal with climate change in the years to come.

The goals of this Strategy are are:

  1. Cultural environments are managed through coordinated land use planning, with the aim of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and safeguarding cultural-historical values and interests;
  2. Buildings are preserved and used so that greenhouse gas emissions are reduced, and cultural environments safeguarded
  3. Improve the energy performance in existing buildings so that greenhouse gas emissions are reduced and cultural-historical values safeguarded;
  4. Strengthen expertise to safeguard cultural environments in a changing climate; and
  5. Prevent and reduce climate-related loss of and damage to cultural environments.
Document Title: Climate strategy for cultural environment management 2021-2030

Family Name: Zero Emission Transit Fund
Family Summary:
This Fund helps communities invest in zero emission transit and school transportation options, which will provide communities with environmental and health benefits by decreasing greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution. The transportation sector accounts for 25% of Canada's greenhouse gas emissions.

Support is provided to public transit and school bus operators across Canada who are electrifying their fleets, which delivers on the federal government's commitment to help purchase 5,000 zero emission buses. This Fund is closely coordinated with the Canada Infrastructure Bank's (CIB) Zero Emission Bus Initiative, through which the CIB has committed more than $1.5 billion to supporting the deployment of zero-emission buses.

Eligible projects are:

  1. Planning Projects: Eligible projects include studies, modelling and feasibility analysis that will support the development of future larger scale capital projects.
  2. Capital Projects: Eligible capital projects include buses, charging and refueling infrastructure, and other supporting infrastructure needs.

It includes $2.75 billion in funding over five years.
Document Title: CIB's Zero-Emission Buses Initiative presentation dated May 2022

Family Summary: Peru's framework for REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and forest Degradation) actions, established through this Ministerial Resolution, operationalises the country's commitments under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the 2018 Climate Change Framework Law (Law No. 30754). The framework identifies eight specific REDD+ actions aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions from the Land Use, Land Use Change and Forestry sector whilst enhancing forest ecosystem resilience, particularly for indigenous peoples and rural communities who depend on these ecosystems.The identified REDD+ actions encompass deforestation-free sustainable family agriculture, sustainable forest management, indigenous-led integrated territorial management (RIA and RIAC), community forest management, forest conservation on indigenous and peasant community lands, titling and governance mechanisms with community monitoring, strengthening of Protected Natural Areas, and landscape-scale forest restoration and reforestation activities. The framework emphasises participatory and transparent climate change management measures, positioning Peru's Ministry of Environment as the national authority responsible for monitoring and evaluating climate change management implementation across all government levels.

Family Summary: The Supreme Decree approving Peru’s Sustainable Construction Technical Code introduces mandatory, nationwide standards that complement the National Building Regulations and align the built-environment sector with the country’s climate and Sustainable Development Goal commitments. The Code sets performance-based requirements for new buildings and urban developments to cut greenhouse-gas emissions, enhance climate-resilience and improve quality of life through energy and water efficiency, waste minimisation, indoor-environment quality and promotion of sustainable mobility. Key provisions mandate the use of xerophytic or native plant species in private and public green areas according to bioclimatic zones, efficient irrigation, and the integration of renewable energy systems—allowing alternative designs or exemptions where on-site renewables achieve equivalent or superior energy- or water-use benchmarks. Collectively, the instrument positions sustainable construction as a core mechanism for meeting Peru’s NDC targets while fostering inclusive, low-impact urban growth.

Family Name: Supreme Decree No. 023-2021-MINAM. Approves the National Environmental Policy for 2030 (Decreto Supremo Nº 023-2021-MINAM. Aprueba la Política Nacional del Ambiente al 2030)
Family Summary: This supreme decree approves Peru's National Environmental Policy to 2030, establishing a comprehensive framework to address the public problem of "diminishing goods and services provided by ecosystems affecting people's development and environmental sustainability." The policy identifies that approximately 18 million hectares of Peru's ecosystems show degradation, with the Land Use, Land-Use Change and Forestry (LULUCF) sector accounting for 53% of the country's net GHG emissions according to the 2016 National GHG Inventory. The policy establishes eight priority objectives, including Objective 5 (increasing climate change adaptation) targeting a 20% reduction in climate-related damages and losses, and Objective 8 (reducing GHG emissions) aiming for 100% compliance with NDC emission targets. The framework addresses key challenges including deforestation (2.28 million hectares lost between 2001-2018), biodiversity loss, environmental quality deterioration, and increased climate risks. Implementation involves mandatory compliance by all public administration entities, with the Ministry of Environment conducting policy through its Directorate General of Environmental Management Policies and Instruments. The policy integrates ecosystem-based approaches, promotes eco-efficient production processes, strengthens environmental governance with citizen participation, and emphasises the recovery of ecosystem services to ensure sustainable development whilst meeting Peru's international climate commitments.
Document Title: National Environmental Policy to 2030 (Política Nacional del Ambiente al 2030)

Collection Name: Law 7/2021 on climate change and energy transition [Spain]
Collection Summary:
Enacted in 2021, this law establishes Spain's legal framework for achieving climate neutrality by 2050, aligning with the Paris Agreement and Sustainable Development Goals. It mandates a 23% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 (compared to 1990 levels), alongside ambitious renewable energy targets, including 42% of final energy consumption from renewables and 74% renewable electricity generation by 2030. Energy efficiency measures aim for a 39.5% reduction in primary energy consumption within the same timeframe. The law also prohibits new hydrocarbon and radioactive mineral exploitation, requires emission-free transport systems in cities with populations exceeding 50,000, and emphasises sustainable urban mobility.

The legislation includes a national Just Transition Strategy to ensure equitable economic opportunities, particularly for vulnerable regions, while fostering adaptation and resilience to climate risks across critical sectors such as water, biodiversity, and health. It creates governance mechanisms like the Expert Committee on Climate Change and Energy Transition to monitor progress and updates to Spain's Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC). Projecting investments exceeding €200 billion by 2030, the law is expected to enhance Spain’s GDP by €16.5–25.7 billion annually and generate 250,000–350,000 new jobs. The focus on education, innovation, and public awareness underscores its commitment to a holistic and inclusive transition.

This collection represent a body of policies, strategies, and plans enacted under this law.
Family Name: Strategy for the Adaptation of the Spanish Coastline to Climate Change
Family Summary: The Strategy for the Adaptation of the Spanish Coastline to Climate Change outlines Spain’s commitment to enhancing coastal resilience to climate change impacts through a structured, evidence-based approach. Developed by the Spanish Climate Change Office (OECC) in collaboration with the University of Cantabria, the strategy progresses in three phases. The first phase evaluates changes in coastal dynamics and projects future trends under various climate scenarios. The second phase assesses potential impacts on natural spaces and human uses of the coastline. Finally, the third phase establishes actionable policies supported by objective indicators to mitigate and prevent climate-related effects. Central to this initiative is the Law 2/2013, which incorporates climate adaptation into Spain's Coastal Law, mandating prospective climate impact assessments for public projects and outlining strategies to safeguard coastal areas.The strategy is guided by principles of sustainability, including rational use of resources, energy efficiency, and the preservation of biodiversity, ecosystems, and cultural heritage. It highlights the interplay of anthropogenic activities, such as emissions and land use changes, with climate risks, advocating for coordinated measures to minimise their combined effects. Strategic Environmental Assessments and inter-administrative collaboration are integral to its implementation, ensuring robust diagnostics and adaptive interventions to protect Spain’s coastal integrity against the dual pressures of climate change and human activities.
Document Title: Strategy for the Adaptation of the Spanish Coastline to Climate Change

Family Name: National Agrarian Policy 2021 – 2030 (Política Nacional Agraria 2021 – 2030)
Family Summary: Peru’s Supreme Decree adopting the National Agrarian Policy 2021-2030 charts a decade-long programme to lift the “low level of agrarian competitive development” that characterises a sector dominated by small-scale family farming (97 % of producers). Grounded in statistical evidence from CENAGRO and ENAHO, the Policy sets a 36 % improvement target by 2030, to be achieved through three priority objectives, fourteen policy guidelines and twenty-two public services. Central measures include: deepening farmers’ vertical integration into value chains; reducing the proportion of subsistence holdings; and enhancing the sustainable management of soil, water and forest resources. Climate variability and change are recognised as cross-cutting stressors that erode ecosystem services and rural incomes, especially in the Andean and Amazon regions; hence the Policy embeds resource-efficient practices, risk-informed planning and support for technological upgrading, all intended to bolster food security, rural livelihoods and Peru’s progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals.

The plan focuses on projects around 100MW with high voltage grid connections, implementing solar, wind, biomass and hydroelectric sources. It provides guidance on spatial planning, and criteria for prioritising sites for renewable development.

Collection Summary: This Communication from the European Commission to the other European Institutions provides an initial roadmap of key policies and strategies required to achieve the European Union's "new growth strategy", centred on the concept of the European Green Deal. It aims at enhancing the union's climate targets and sets four core goals: 1) climate-neutrality by 2050, 2) protection of human life, animals and plants by cutting pollution, 3) helping companies become world leaders in clean products and technologies, and 4) help ensure a just and inclusive transition. These goals should be reached by developing a circular economy, decarbonising the energy sector, renovate buildings, support the industry to innovate, and green private and public transport systems.
Family Name: EU Forest Strategy for 2030
Family Summary: The main goals of the EU Forest Strategy for 2030 are to improve the quantity and quality of EU forests, enhance their resilience to climate change, and support the communities that depend on them. This strategy is a key part of the European Green Deal and aims to contribute to the EU's biodiversity and climate goals, including reducing greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030 and achieving climate neutrality by 2050. It includes measures for strengthening forest protection and restoration, enhancing sustainable forest management, and improving the monitoring and effective decentralised planning on forests in the EU with a view to ensuring resilient forest ecosystems and enabling forests to deliver on their multifunctional role. To further support sustainable forest-based bioeconomy for a climate neutral future, the strategy proposes measures for innovation and promotion of new materials and products to replace fossil-based counterparts as well as for boosting the non-wood forest economy, including ecotourism. The Strategy also focuses on sustainable re- and afforestation and is accompanied by a roadmap for planting at least 3 billion additional trees in the EU by 2030.
Document Title: EU Forest Strategy 2030

Family Name: Polish National Plan for Counteracting the Effects of Drought (2021–2027)
Family Summary:
The Polish National Plan for Counteracting the Effects of Drought (Plan przeciwdziałania skutkom suszy (PPSS)) is the first national planning document addressing the issue of minimizing the effects of drought. Its development stemmed from the provisions of EU directives and guidelines (the Water Framework Directive) as well as national law (Article 184 of the Water Law Act). It was adopted by the Regulation of the Minister of Infrastructure on 15 July 2021 (Dz.U. 2021 poz. 1615).

It provides a comprehensive analysis of drought risk, outlines proposals to increase available water resources, enhance natural and artificial retention, and sets out a detailed catalogue of measures to reduce the impacts of drought on society, the economy and the environment. The plan is structured around four specific goals: effective water resource management, increasing water retention, education and coordination on drought issues, and mechanisms for implementation and financing. While not an investment plan itself, PPSS includes proposals for water infrastructure projects and retention solutions and complements other national water-management planning instruments, helping improve resilience to drought and secure water availability.
Document Title: Polish National Plan for Counteracting the Effects of Drought (2021–2027) - Non Specialist version

Family Name: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain
Family Summary:
This plan sets out the government’s commitments and the actions needed to decarbonise the UK's transport system. It defines a sectoral net zero pathway that combines 1) decarbonising efforts in all forms of transport, and 2) transversal measures such as a push for hydrogen and the unlocking of green finance. The plan calls for decarbonisation strategies that maximise health, economic and social co-benefits.


The plan followed on from "Decarbonising transport: setting the challenge", published in March 2020, which laid out the scale of additional reductions needed to deliver transport’s contribution to legally binding carbon budgets and delivering net zero by 2050.


"Decarbonising transport: one-year-on review" was published in July 2022, summarising progress over the 12 months since the plan was published and outlined upcoming milestones.
Document Title: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain

Family Name: Italy's National Plan for Resilience and Recovery
Family Summary:
To benefit from the support of the Recovery and Resilience Facility set up by the EU in the aftermath of the COVID-19-induced economic crisis, Member States submit their recovery and resilience plans to the European Commission. Each plan sets out the reforms and investments to be implemented by end-2026 and Member States can receive financing up to a previously agreed allocation. Each plan should effectively address challenges identified in the European Semester, particularly the country-specific recommendations of 2019 and 2020 adopted by the Council. It should also advance the green and digital transitions and make Member States’ economies and societies more resilient. The Commission validates the plan after which it effectively enters in force and EU subsidies can start flowing towards the member state.37% of the plan’s total allocation is assessed to be directed towards reforms and investments supports climate objectives. Notable investments include the following:Sustainable mobility: integrate more regions into the high-speed rail network and complete the rail freight corridors; boost sustainable local transport through the extension of cycle lanes, metros, tramways and zero- emission buses, including the construction of electric charging stations across the country and hydrogen refuelling points for road and rail transport. €32.1 billion

  • Energy efficiency in residential buildings: financing large-scale renovation of residential buildings to make them more energy efficient. €12.1 billion The plan supports interventions for the improvement of energy efficiency of residential buildings by which beneficiaries may benefit from a tax rebate over the next five years for the amounts spent, provided that the energy savings of those interventions are higher than 30%. By the end of 2025, building renovation interventions will be completed for at least 32 million square meters.
  • Renewable energy and circular economy: developing the production and incentivising the use of renewable energies including green hydrogen as well as increasing recycling, reducing landfill waste and improving water management. €11.2 billion

After that, Italy requested 03 more updates to the plan, 1 in 2024 and 2 in 2025, being the last one on 10 October 2025 and so- called "NextGenerationEU – The road to 2026". The Commission approved it on 4 November 2025 and the Council as well. Ultimately, the measures (investments and reforms) subject to amendment amount to 173. The total number of targets and objectives has been reduced from 614 to 575. Ten new measures have been introduced, including four instruments that operate as financial vehicles: the National Connectivity Fund; the Agrisolar Park Facility; the Grant Scheme for Investments in Water Infrastructure; and the Student Housing Fund
Document Title: ANNEX of COUNCIL IMPLEMENTING DECISION amending the Implementing Decision of 13 July 2021 on the approval of the assessment of Italy’s Recovery and Resilience Plan (RePower EU)

Family Name: Micro-generation Support Scheme (MSS)
Family Summary:
Initially, domestic applicants could apply to the Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI) for a grant towards the cost of installing Solar PV equipment. The scheme was then expanded to non-domestic applicants such as businesses, farms, schools, and community buildings to apply for a grant for installations up to 6kW, at the same grant amounts as domestic customers, i.e., up to a maximum of €2,400.

An extended funding range from €2,700 to €162,600 was introduced in July 2023 to support non-domestic installation sizes between 7 kWp and 1,000 kWp (1 MW) capacity, on a pilot basis to the end of 2023. Support under the MSS has been gradually reduced over time from 2024 to take account of reducing system costs.
Document Title: Micro-generation

Family Name: Strategy for Financing the Transition to a Sustainable Economy  (EU Sustainable Finance Strategy)
Family Summary: The strategy outlines how the European Union intends to align finance flows with its climate-neutrality and sustainability goals by 2050. It builds on the existing sustainable-finance framework (taxonomy of sustainable activities, mandatory disclosures, investment tools) and sets four priority action areas: (i) financing the real-economy transition including recognition of transitional activities; (ii) expanding access to sustainable finance for retail investors, SMEs and households; (iii) enhancing resilience and the financial sector’s contribution to sustainability through double-materiality risk integration; and (iv) strengthening global ambition and cooperation in sustainable finance.
Document Title: Strategy for Financing the Transition to a Sustainable Economy

Family Name: National Policy of Land Management (PNOT)
Family Summary:
This policy was prepared in 2019 and approved by a ministerial decree published in July 2021. 

Objective 1.2 of the policy is to promote the occupation and development of the territory in a safe and resilient way that contributes to disaster risk reduction and adaptation to climate change.

Guideline 1.2.c states that management tools and mechanisms in land use planning that reduce disaster risk, increase resilience and consider adaptation to climate change by human settlements and strategic infrastructure must be considered. 

Guideline 1.2.d commands to incorporate the functions of natural systems as tools for mitigating threats and adapting to climate change, in order to reduce the risk of disasters that may affect the lives and health of people, infrastructure, services, or the environment.

Guideline 3.1.d promotes public and private investment in all types of infrastructure, and the generation of knowledge that contributes to the sustainable use of critical natural resources, such as water, renewable energies and soils.
Document Title: National Policy of Land Management (PNOT)

Family Name: Presidential Decree 400/2021 on the National Security Strategy of the Russian Federation
Family Summary:
This decree approves a new version of the country's national security strategy (attached to the decree's text). The Russian government has been acknowledging in its security strategy the threats deriving from climate change since 2015 (decree 683/2015, repealed by this document). 

This strategy notably states that climate change is used as a pretext by the world community "for restricting the access of Russian companies to export markets, curbing the development of Russian industry, establishing control over transport routes, and preventing Russia from developing the Arctic." 

In article 25.6, the strategy states that among Russia's national interests and strategic priorities are environmental protection, conservation of natural resources and rational use of natural resources, adaptation to climate change.
Document Title: Presidential Decree 400/2021 on the National Security Strategy of the Russian Federation

Family Name: "Roofs To Reefs" National Resilience Plan
Family Summary:
This plan aims at protecting the population's private and community roofs from extreme weather events, such as tropical storms. It also seeks to encourage the use of renewable energy sources, rainwater harvesting, and nature-based solutions to reduce runoff into the coastal environment.

Family Name: Ghana National Cooling Plan (Framework for Green and Efficient Cooling)
Family Summary: This Plan serves as a roadmap to transform Ghana's refrigeration and air conditioning (RAC) sector to the best available technologies to achieve sustainable cooling that will support economic growth and reduce overall impact on the environment, mitigating climate change. It examines the state of each RAC sub-sector, identifies the deficiencies facing the sub-sector and presents technical proposals to guide its transformation to clean and efficient cooling. The plan aims to bring together all cooling-related stakeholders, such as the Ministries, academic institutions, professional bodies, estate developers, the private sector, financial institutions, etc., to synergise and to transform the RAC industry to achieve clean and efficient cooling that is affordable, sustainable, and accessible to all.

Family Name: Strategy for Mobility Digitalisation and Decarbonisation
Family Summary:
This Strategy - which is part of the Acceleration Strategies under France 2030 - covers passenger and freight mobility, reducing greenhouse gas emissions from transport, which accounts for 30% of the emissions in France.

The central scenario projects a 28% reduction in the sector's emissions by 2030 and near-complete decarbonisation by 2050. Actions include:

  • Supporting design methods that are efficient in their life cycle and resilient to climate change (particularly in terms of sizing) and more efficient and sustainable maintenance methods to increase the lifespan of infrastructure and reduce maintenance operations;
  • New generation of full electric urban and peri-urban Bus Rapid Transit systems to strengthen climate-friendly mass transport;
  • Greenhouse gas aviation emissions reduction technologies towards climate neutrality by 2050;
  • Enabling climate-neutral, clean, smart, and competitive waterborne transport;
  • Climate resilient and environmentally sustainable transport infrastructure, with a focus on inland waterways; and
  • Logistics networks integration and harmonisation through operational connectivity to optimise freight flows and drive logistics to climate neutrality.
Document Title: Strategy for Mobility Digitalisation and Decarbonisation

Family Name: Action Plan for Circular Economy
Family Summary:
The Danish Government's Action Plan for Circular Economy is also the national plan for the prevention and management of waste for 2020-2032. The Action Plan for Circular Economy describes the Danish targets, indicators, policies and initiatives in the entire circular value chain, which ranges from design and consumption to waste management, from which natural resources are recycled into new products and materials. In addition to several initiatives along the value chain in general, the Action Plan for Circular Economy focuses on three areas with significant environmental and climate impact: biomass, construction and plastics.

Government visions for circular economy are:

  • The waste curve has to be bent – less waste, higher resource productivity and more reuse. This will i.a. be achieved by setting quantitative targets for waste reduction in Denmark, when similar targets are agreed upon in the EU.
  • Climate-neutral waste sector by 2030.
  • By 2030, Denmark will reduce the amount of incinerated plastic waste by 80 percent
Document Title: Action Plan for Circular Economy

Family Name: Central African Republic National REDD+ Strategy
Family Summary: The Central African Republic's REDD+ strategy aims to guide the long-term conservation, restoration and sustainable economic development of forest ecosystems. REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation) is a voluntary framework for climate change mitigation developed under the UNFCCC, with a focus on the challenges faced by developing countries. The strategy names slash-and-burn land clearance, as well as routine burning of silvopastoral systems, as key drivers of forest carbon loss and reduced ecosystem integrity, and proposes expansion of agroecological practices such as the introduction of tree nurseries to rehabilitate coffee plantations as agroforestry systems. It also proposes investment in improved rainwater harvesting, to improve dry-season yields and reduce the rate of land clearance.
Document Title: Central African Republic National REDD+ Strategy

Family Name: National Climate Change Management Agenda
Family Summary:
The Agenda is an updated version of the National Strategy for Climate Change Management Policy for the period 2021-2050, and was approved in Resolution No XIX-490.

The Agenda sets out targets and objectives for 2030, 2040 and 2050 both regarding climate change mitigation and adaptation. The mitigation policy aims at increasing ambition on greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction as well as their removals. The Agenda emphasises the importance of mitigation for the sectors energy, transport, industry, agriculture, waste and forestry.

In Chapter IV, the Agenda sets out detailed mitigation targets for the different time periods and sectors. Notably, in section 23.1, the Agenda sets out "to reduce GHG emissions by 100% compared to 1990 levels by switching to innovative, low-emission, environmentally friendly technologies and the use of RES in all economic sectors, including up to 20 % of removals by natural sinks from the LULUCF sector, and the use of environmentally safe carbon capture and utilisation (CCU) technologies to offset GHG emissions in sectors where technological options for zero GHG emissions will not be available."
Document Title: National Climate Change Management Agenda

Family Name: National Electric System Development Program 2021-2035 (Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional 2021-2035)
Family Summary: The Programa para el Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional (PRODESEN) 2021-2035 is a key planning instrument for Mexico’s National Electric System (SEN), outlining a fifteen-year strategy for electricity generation, transmission, and distribution, in alignment with the National Development Plan. It integrates various planning tools, such as the Indicative Programme for the Installation and Retirement of Power Plants (PIIRCE) and programmes for the expansion and modernisation of the National Transmission Network (RNT) and General Distribution Networks (RGD). The PRODESEN aims to ensure a reliable electricity supply for over 120 million users across two million square kilometres, while addressing the growing demand, reducing electricity costs, and enhancing system reliability. A core objective is to strengthen the role of the state-owned Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) in generation and transmission, including the reactivation of combined-cycle plants and the modernisation of hydroelectric facilities, to support national energy sovereignty and economic development.In relation to climate change and energy transition, the PRODESEN explicitly incorporates Mexico’s international commitments under frameworks such as the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the Kyoto Protocol, the Paris Agreement, and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. It emphasises the reduction of GHG emissions, targeting a limit of 139 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2030, as part of Mexico’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). The programme promotes the orderly integration of clean and renewable energy sources into the national energy mix, with a significant focus on distributed generation, particularly solar photovoltaic systems, which are projected to grow substantially by 2035. Additionally, it underscores energy efficiency measures and the expansion of electricity access to rural communities, aligning energy policy with sustainable development goals and environmental protection.
Document Title: National Electric System Development Program 2021-2035 (Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional 2021-2035)

Family Name: Infrastructure Plan 2035
Family Summary:
The Plan is an agreement between the government (Social Democracy), the Liberal Party, Danish People's Party, Socialist People's Party, Radical Left, Union List, Conservative People's Party, New Civic Party, Liberal Alliance, and Alternative and Christian Democrats. There are four-related climate actions:

  1. The parties agree to prioritize DKK 910 million (including tax losses) for climate-friendly asphalt in the period 2022-2035, which reduces cars' fuel consumption and thereby CO2 emissions by reducing rolling resistance between tires and the road surface.
  2. The parties also agree to allocate a pool of DKK 250 million DKK in the period 2022-2026 for more green buses and more green flex traffic. The pool will help support the regions in complying with and implementing the current climate cooperation agreements that the government has entered into with 23 municipalities and the five regions.
  3. The parties have agreed to allocate a pool of DKK 150 million in the period 2022-2035 to promote biodiversity along roads and railways. The pool will, among other things, help reduce the barrier effect of the railway and increase biodiversity along the road network.
  4. The parties have agreed to promote cycling in Denmark for the good of the climate and public health. A well-functioning and modern bicycle transport requires a well-developed bicycle infrastructure that both encourages more people to choose the bicycle and at the same time ensures safety in traffic among other road users.
Document Title: Infrastructure Plan 2035

Family Name: 2022 Immediate Climate Action Programme
Family Summary:
With the 2022 Immediate Climate Action Programme, the German Cabinet approved additional 8 billion euros which will be used for specific measures to achieve the more ambitious climate targets of the amended Federal Climate Protection Act (2021).

Family Name: Clean Technology Regulatory Review Roadmap

  • Clean Technology Regulatory Review Roadmap initiatives

Family Name: A roadmap for capture, transport and storage of CO2
Family Summary:
On 30 June 2021, the Government and a broad range of parliamentary parties agreed on A roadmap for CO2 storage – first part of a CCS strategy. The agreement consists of a number of initiatives enabling storage in the Danish subsoil in both the short and long terms. Specifically, the agreement started the process of preparing for the granting of licenses for CO2 storage in the Danish part of the North Sea, so that storage in depleted oil and gas fields could take place as early as 2025. The agreement also enables the import, export and transport of CO2 across national borders. Furthermore, the agreement has allocated funding of DKK 210 million for studies of all relevant and potential storage possibilities in the Danish subsoil with close involvement of relevant municipalities, citizens, etc.

On 14 December 2021, an agreement on A roadmap for capture, transport and storage of CO2 – Second part of a CCS strategy was reached by the Government and several political parties. The agreement focused on the entire CCS value chain (i.e. capture, transport, storage and use of CO2) and aimed at ensuring that the first CO2 capture plants and stores are in operation in Denmark by 2025.
Document Title: A roadmap for capture, transport and storage of CO2 – Second part of a CCS strategy

Family Name: National Drought Plan. Together building resilience 2021-2025
Family Summary:
The National Drought Plan - Together building resilience (“PNS”) of Ecuador provides a strategic framework to address the growing challenges of drought, which severely impact the country's agricultural production, hydroelectric power generation, and water and sanitation systems. Developed by the Ministry of Environment, Water, and Ecological Transition (MAATE) in collaboration with the National Risk and Emergency Management Service (SNGRE), the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (MAG), and the CIIFEN (International Research Center on El Niño Phenomenon) through the Euroclima+ project, the PNS aims to mitigate drought risks while enhancing resilience at the national level.

The plan highlights the devastating effects of drought, including crop and livestock losses, water shortages, and ecosystem imbalances, which exacerbate economic losses, food insecurity, and health issues. With a long-term perspective, it prioritises reducing drought risk through integrated planning, intersectoral coordination, and leveraging climate data to establish effective monitoring systems. By focusing on sectors like territorial planning, agriculture, water resources, risk management, and the environment, the plan addresses gaps in information and capacity, promoting evidence-based strategies and collaboration among public and private stakeholders, academia, and civil society.

The PNS aligns national policies with global frameworks and emphasises the development of innovative programs for risk reduction, response, and recovery. It sets objectives to strengthen the adaptive capacity of vulnerable communities, minimise economic losses, enhance drought monitoring, and generate evidence of the impacts of drought under current and future climate scenarios.
Document Title: National Drought Plan. Together building resilience 2021-2025

Family Name: National Waste Management Plan 2021-2028
Family Summary: The plan aims to reduce the harmful impact of waste on the environment and public health, as well as to achieve the most efficient use of resources, opening up new markets, and creating new jobs. An important part of the Plan is to create the best possible conditions for preventing waste generation. The NWMP’s objectives focus on reducing waste generation, increasing recycling, preventing landfilling of biodegradable waste, and promoting waste prevention and reuse — all of which help lower greenhouse gas emissions associated with waste decomposition and energy use. By reducing the volume of waste sent to landfills and improving recycling and recovery, the plan supports national climate goals and contributes to national action on climate change as the reduction of waste disposal directly relates to reduced methane and CO₂ emissions.The National Waste Management Plan 2021–2028 for Bulgaria was officially adopted by the Council of Ministers on 17 June 2021, when the government approved the strategic document covering the period 2021–2028.
Document Title: National Waste Management Plan 2021-2028

Family Name: The Financial Supervisory Authority's climate adaptation work
Family Summary:
Since 2020, the objective of the Finansinspektionen's (FI's) activities has been to work to ensure that the financial system contributes to sustainable development. Against this background, FI believes that financial companies need to increase their transparency regarding the exposures they have to both physical climate risks and transition risks. The overall objective of the authority for FI's climate adaptation work in accordance with the Climate Adaptation Regulation should be that the financial system contributes to sustainable development and that companies falling within FI's area of ​​responsibility should report and manage the risks that arise as a result of climate change in an adequate manner. FI assesses that it is not practically possible to specify a measurable target.

This action plan applies to the period 2021-2026 and consists of three measures that FI intends to take, or is already taking, in order to achieve the government's goal that the financial system should contribute to sustainable development and that Swedish financial companies should manage the risks arising from climate change in an adequate manner. The three measures are:

  1. FI shall promote understandable and comparable sustainability-related information.
  2. FI shall develop methods for measuring climate-related risks.
  3. FI shall work to ensure that financial companies integrate physical risks and the effects of climate adaptation into their operations.
Document Title: The Financial Supervisory Authority's climate adaptation work

Family Summary: This policy aims to enable Japan meet its decarbonisation commitments by getting involved into projects based in partner countries. Family Name: Financial Regulatory Authority Decrees No. 107 and 108
Family Summary:
The Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA), which is in charge of supervising non-bank financial institutions and markets, including the stock exchange, issued two decrees on 5 July 2021 requiring listed companies and non-banking financial institutions (subject to a specific threshold) to make annual disclosures pertaining to environmental, social and governance practices. If the issued capital of the company or its net shareholder equity exceeds EGP 500m, the board of directors will have to make certain climate-related financial disclosures. Decree 107 relates to disclosure rules for companies in non-banking financial services. Decree 108 relates to the disclosure rules for companies that issue securities on the Egyptian Stock Exchange.

The disclosures are not expected to be in the form of narrative reports written by the companies. The FRA prepared two forms for the required disclosures and annexed them to the decrees. Each form includes a set of questions that reflect the standards that are being evaluated. The company is required to answer each question with ‘Yes’ or ‘No’, and to write a clarification or comment on its answer. For example, the company may comment that it is in the process of taking specific procedures to comply with this element and that it is expected to finalise these procedures within a specific period. In some circumstances, the FRA determines the information that is required to be clarified.

The environmental disclosures include questions related to environmental operations and supervision, carbon emissions, used energy sources, use of water and waste management. Social disclosures include questions related to gender diversity, wages, turnover rates of employees, non-discrimination, professional health and safety, children, forced labour, and labour rights. Governance related disclosures include diversity in the board of directors, anti-corruption measures, codes of ethics, and data privacy. As to climate-related financial disclosures, they include elements of governance, strategy, risk managements, metrics and targets. The FRA further requires listed companies, targeted by the two decrees, to submit to the FRA a quarterly report stating the procedures that the company has taken or will take in relation to the required disclosures from 1 January 2022.
Document Title: Decree 108

Family Name: Energy for work – long-term value creation from Norwegian energy resources (Meld. St. 36 2020-2021)
Family Summary:
Under this white paper, the Norwegian government will maintain Norway's position as an energy nation and lay the foundation for energy resources to continue to be used to create value, jobs and welfare in Norway. This is a policy for long-term value creation from Norwegian energy resources organized according to four goals:

  1. value creation that provides the basis for jobs in Norway;
  2. electrification will make Norway greener and better;

3. establishment of new, profitable industries; and

4. further develop a future-oriented oil and gas industry within the framework of the climate goals.

Actions include:

  • require companies to make climate risks visible in their development plans;
  • facilitate the further development of both the oil and gas industry and other marine industries;
  • support the industry's work to increase value creation through efficiency, digitalization and innovation; and
  • continue the focus on petroleum-based research to increase value creation, strengthen international competitiveness and reduce the climate and environmental impact of the business.
Document Title: Energy for work – long-term value creation from Norwegian energy resources (Meld. St. 36 2020-2021)

Family Name: Resolution No. 40179
Family Summary:
Resolution No. 40179 defines the parameters for long-term contracting auctions for electricity generation projects.It convokes a long-term energy contract auction for renewable energy projects. It sets key parameters for the auction process, such as:

1- Energy Demand: It outlines the target demand for renewable energy to be auctioned

2- Contract Period: It defines the contract length and when the obligations to supply electricity begin.

3- Renewable Energy Targets: It supports the goal to incorporate non-conventional renewable energy sources into the country’s energy matrix, as outlined in the National Expansion Plan.

4- Previous Auctions: It acknowledges prior energy contracts and identifies a gap in meeting renewable energy goals for 2031.

This resolution aims to bolster energy generation, especially from NCRES, as part of Colombia's commitment to reducing carbon emissions and enhancing energy security.

Family Name: Supreme Decree No. 012-2021-MINAM. Adapts the National Commission on Climate Change (Decreto Supremo Nº 012-2021-MINAM. Adecúa la Comisión Nacional sobre el Cambio Climático)
Family Summary:
The Decree Supreme No. 012-2021-MINAM adapts the National Commission on Climate Change (Comisión Nacional sobre el Cambio Climático) to the legal framework established by Law No. 30754, the Climate Change Framework Law, and its implementing regulations. The instrument formalises the Commission as a permanent, multisectoral body under the technical supervision of the Ministry of Environment, with the primary function of monitoring the implementation of national climate policies and international commitments under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). The Commission is designed as a consultative and oversight mechanism that facilitates coordination between state institutions and civil society actors across all levels of government. Its mandate includes tracking compliance with national climate objectives, evaluating policy effectiveness, and generating technical recommendations for decision-making at both institutional and governmental levels.

The Commission’s composition reflects a structured approach to inclusive governance: it comprises 22 state representatives (designated from key ministries, regional and municipal associations, and intergovernmental bodies) and 22 non-state representatives drawn from diverse civil society groups, including Indigenous organisations (PPICC), Afro-Peruvian networks, environmental NGOs, youth collectives, women’s coalitions, trade unions, academic institutions, professional colleges, and private-sector associations. All members, whether state or non-state, possess equal voting rights, reinforcing principles of participatory legitimacy. The Secretariat Technical is housed within the Ministry of Environment and provides administrative and analytical support, while the Commission may convene specialised technical working groups and seek expert input from affiliated public institutions such as SENAMHI, CONCYTEC, SERFOR, SERNANP, OEFA, and CEPLAN. The body operates under an internal regulation that governs procedural matters, including quorum requirements, voting procedures, and meeting schedules. By institutionalising multi-stakeholder engagement and establishing clear mechanisms for information exchange, reporting, and accountability, the decree aims to strength Peru’s domestic climate governance architecture, ensuring alignment with international obligations, particularly those related to transparency, periodic NDC reporting, and the integration of subnational inputs into national climate planning.

As a result of administrative reorganisations, the Supreme Decree N° 005-2023-MINAM modifies the composition of the High-Level Climate Change Commission (CANCC), expanding its membership to include five additional ministries: Defense, Interior, Justice and Human Rights, Labor and Employment Promotion, and Foreign Trade and Tourism. This modification aims to enhance inter-ministerial coordination and strengthen Peru's national climate change response strategy by broadening governmental participation in climate action planning and implementation. The decree seeks to create a more comprehensive and integrated approach to developing and executing national climate change mitigation and adaptation measures, reflecting a whole-of-government strategy in addressing climate challenges.

Family Name: Procurement Policy Note 06/21
Family Summary:
In light of the UK government's net zero target, passed into law in 2019, the government has issued a Procurement Policy Note (PPN) on government procurement processes to promote the achievement of the net zero target. The provisions of the PPN apply to all central government departments, their executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies ('in-scope organisations). The PNN state that in-scope organisations should "take action to apply this PPN when procuring good and/or services and/or works with an anticipated contract value above £5million per annum (excluding VAT) which are subject to the Public Contracts Regulation 2015 save where it would not be related and proportionate to the contract". The PPN further states that in-scope organisations should include a requirement for bidding suppliers to provide a Carbon Reduction Plan, confirming the suppliers commitment to achieving net zero by 2050 in the UK, amongst other provisions, as part of the assessment process in the procurement of goods and services.


Organisations that fall within the scope of the PPN guidelines must apply the PPN's provisions to procurement processes from September 30th, 2021 onwards.
Document Title: Procurement Policy Note

Collection Summary: The EU Taxonomy Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2020/852) establishes a framework to classify which economic activities are environmentally sustainable, helping investors, companies, and policymakers channel finance toward activities that support the EU’s climate and environmental goals while ensuring they do no significant harm to other environmental objectives.
Family Name: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2139 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2020/852 by establishing the technical screening criteria for an economic activity qualifies as contributing to climate change mitigation, adaptation or to cause no significant harm
Family Summary:
This Delegated Regulation supplements Regulation (EU) 2020/852 (the EU Taxonomy Regulation) by setting detailed technical screening criteria for economic activities. It specifies under what conditions an activity can be considered to make a substantial contribution to climate change mitigation or adaptation, and simultaneously ensures that it does no significant harm (DNSH) to the other environmental objectives listed in the Taxonomy Regulation.

The Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/1214 amended this document in order to include specific economic activities in the nuclear-energy and fossil-gas sectors, under strict conditions, into the list of environmentally sustainable activities defined by Regulation (EU) 2020/852. The Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2485 amends Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2139 by adding additional technical screening criteria under the Regulation (EU) 2020/852 (EU Taxonomy)‑framework, for instance regarding Electricity generation from certain low-carbon fuels.
Document Title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2485

Family Name: Regulation 2021:524 on Government credit guarantees for green investments
Family Summary:
The Swedish government suggests loan guarantees for green projects in the budget plan for 2021. The plan intends to make it possible for larger industrial investment projects to be carried out in Sweden that help the country meet the objectives of the environmental goal system and the framework for climate policy.

The credit guarantees are expected to be given for several years beginning in the first half of 2021 and will be evaluated using technology-neutral criteria. The proposed credit guarantees would not exceed SEK 10 billion in 2021. The guarantee structure is projected to cost SEK 15 billion in 2022 and SEK 25 billion in 2023.
Document Title: Regulation (2021:524) on government credit guarantees for green investments
