Family Name: National Climate Change Learning Strategy of Zambia
Family Summary:
This document systematically examines the country's learning and skills development needs to respond to the impacts of climate change. It aims to strengthen individual and institutional systemic capacities of the energy, health, forestry, agriculture and education sectors to enable them deliver climate change learning and contribute to the implementation of the NDC and NAPs.

The strategy covers the period up to 2030. Priority actions are phased as short term (1-2 years); medium term (3-5 years); and long term (6-10 years). Each of the five sectors will deal with the three national priority actions: 1) awareness raising and knowledge strengthening; 2) individual and institutional capacity building and 3) mainstreaming climate change learning into the priority sector policies and systems in the short, medium and long-terms.
Document Title: National Climate Change Learning Strategy of Zambia

Family Name: The Gambia 2050 Climate Vision
Family Summary:
This document sets the government's strategy to meet commitments made under the Paris Agreement, move towards resilience and net zero carbon emissions by 2050. It underlines the long-term strategy (LTS) for low greenhouse gas emissions and climate-resilient development.

Four strategic axes of policy action are identified: 1) Climate-resilient food and landscapes: Agriculture, food security, forestry and natural resources (including water, biodiversity and wildlife), 2) Low emissions and resilient economy: Energy, transport, infrastructure and the key economic sectors of tourism and financial services, 3) Climate-resilient people: Health, education, equitable social development and human settlements, and 4) Climate-aware Integrated Coastal Zone Management.
Document Title: The Gambia 2050 Climate Vision

Family Name: HK Roadmap on popularisation of electric vehicles
Family Summary: This document sets Hong Kong's vision on how to achieve zero carbon transport, clean air and smart city features. The roadmap summarises a large range of decisions aiming at electrify the country's mobility. Measures include 1) the creation of a Green Tech Fund, 2) imposes no new registration of fuel-propelled private cars including hybrid vehicles in 2035 or earlier, 3) sets a range of policies aimed at public transport and other commercial vehicles, 4) sets policies to boost the charging network, 5) promotes training and maintenance services, and 6) seeks to develop battery recycling.
Document Title: HK Roadmap on popularisation of electric vehicles

Family Name: Sudan National REDD+ Strategy and Action Plan
Family Summary: Sudan's REDD+ strategy aims to guide the long-term conservation, restoration and sustainable economic development of forest ecosystems. REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation) is a voluntary framework for climate change mitigation developed under the UNFCCC, with a focus on the challenges faced by developing countries.
Document Title: Sudan National REDD+ Strategy and Action Plan

Family Name: National Disaster Risk Management Policy to 2050
Family Summary:
The National Disaster Risk Management Policy for 2050 establishes six priority objectives:

  • Improve understanding of disaster risk for decision-making at the level of the population and state entities;
  • Improve conditions for land occupation and use, taking disaster risk into account;
  • Improve the coordinated implementation of disaster risk management in the territory;
  • Strengthen the incorporation of disaster risk management into public and private investment;
  • Ensure public care in the event of emergencies and disasters;
  • Improve the recovery of populations and their livelihoods affected by emergencies and disasters.

Family Name: National Organic Waste Strategy
Family Summary: This strategy aims to increase Chile’s organic waste recovery from 1% to 66% by 2040, as a key action to reduce methane emissions. Collection Summary: This Communication from the European Commission to the other European Institutions provides an initial roadmap of key policies and strategies required to achieve the European Union's "new growth strategy", centred on the concept of the European Green Deal. It aims at enhancing the union's climate targets and sets four core goals: 1) climate-neutrality by 2050, 2) protection of human life, animals and plants by cutting pollution, 3) helping companies become world leaders in clean products and technologies, and 4) help ensure a just and inclusive transition. These goals should be reached by developing a circular economy, decarbonising the energy sector, renovate buildings, support the industry to innovate, and green private and public transport systems.
Family Name: EU strategy on adaptation to climate change
Family Summary:
This document aims at making the European Union resilient to the adverse effects of climate change by 2050. The European Commission adopted its new EU strategy on adaptation to climate change on 24 February 2021.The strategy focuses on four key objectives:

  • Smarter adaptation: Using better data and tools to guide actions, such as protecting homes, businesses, and farms.
  • Faster adaptation: Developing solutions to reduce climate risks, enhance protection, and secure water resources.
  • More systemic adaptation: Addressing climate impacts across all sectors by integrating climate resilience into policies, supporting local actions, and promoting nature-based solutions.
  • Stepping up international action: Increasing global support, financing, and cooperation for climate resilience.

Overall, the new strategy sets out how the European Union can adapt to the unavoidable impacts of climate change and become climate resilient by 2050.

In October 2023, the Commission published a progress report on adaptation at EU level. While the EU has made broad progress on adaptation to climate change, through the ongoing implemen- tation of the EU Adaptation Strategy, progress has been uneven across policy areas. Moreover, due to the rapidly changing climate, especially in Europe, according to science and Member States' own reporting, there are significant and growing vulnerabilities, e.g. for agriculture, water management and the energy sector
Document Title: Report on the implementation of the Adaptation strategy

Family Name: National Climate Finance Strategy 2021-2030
Family Summary:
This strategy outlines objectives, strategies, conditions and lines of action that must be implemented to accelerate the mobilization of climate financing from public, private, national and international sources for the benefit of all sectors and actors involved in the implementation of climate actions and measures. The strategy was formulated in 2020 through a participatory process that included eight virtual dialogues with actors from the public, private and financial sectors, as well as local governments, international cooperation, academia, indigenous peoples and civil society. The strategy pushes forward a multi-actor and multisector vision of climate financing. 

This strategy envisions that by 2030, Ecuador will be able to effectively and efficiently mobilize and channel national, international, public and private resources for the management of climate change, promoting low-emission and climate-resilient development in the country, in compliance with national and  international commitment on climate change. 

Specific objectives include: 

1)    Establishing institutional arrangements and a governance framework that facilitates multi-level and multi-sector articulation of actors involved in climate financing. 

2)    Promoting a financial system that mainstreams the risks and opportunities derived from climate change management. 

3)    Identifying and designing mechanisms and instruments that allow climate financing resources to be mobilized in a transparent, effective and efficient manner.

4)    Promoting conditions that facilitate and democratize the access, allocation, management and mobilization of climate finance.

5)    Promoting a regulatory framework that provides certainty and incentives to leverage climate financing in all sectors.

6)    Facilitating an adequate flow of information and knowledge on climate financing.
Document Title: National Climate Finance Strategy 2021-2030

Family Name: Summary of sector-specific low-carbon roadmaps
Family Summary:
"The outcomes of the sectoral roadmaps created over the previous year were summarized in a report published by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment. It demonstrates:

- With current or emerging technology, the government's objective of a carbon-neutral Finland by 2035 is feasible for industry and other sectors, but would require a supportive investment climate;

- The reduction of sectoral greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions is mostly dependent on electrification, clean energy, and RDI investments. The availability of professionals, a transparent and predictable working environment, RDI investments, and easy regulation are essential prerequisites for the implementation of the roadmaps. Targeting RDI investments will shape future trends, making it one of the key concerns for building a low-carbon society.

Technologies for low-emission energy production, material and energy efficiency, alternative propulsion technologies (biofuels, hydrogen, electrification), waste heat recovery, and carbon capture, usage, and storage are among the technological solutions that are featured."

Family Name: Maritime India Vision 2030
Family Summary:
"The Maritime India Vision (MIV) 2030 provides a comprehensive framework for the holistic development of India’s maritime sector, encompassing ports, shipping, and waterways. MIV 2030 outlines 150 initiatives aimed at propelling India to global maritime leadership.

Its 10 interconnected themes such as port infrastructure development, enhancing logistics efficiency, improving Indian shipbuilding tonnage, increasing coastal and waterway traffic, fostering technology innovation and policy support, promoting sustainability and global collaboration, address every facet of the maritime ecosystem, ensuring a well-rounded approach to transforming India into a leading maritime nation."

The Vision is in line with the Harit Sagar Green Ports Guidelines of 2030, and reiterates the target of reducing carbon emissions per ton of cargo by 30% by 2030 and by 70% by 2047. Ports ought to increase the share of renewables to over 60% by 2030 and over 90% by 2047.
Document Title: Maritime India Vision 2030

Family Name: Guiding Opinion on Coordinating and Strengthening Work Related to Addressing Climate Change and Eco-Environment Protection
Family Summary:
To achieve the carbon neutrality by 2060 goal, this Opinion lays out the principal requirements of unified planning, unified deployment, unified implementation, and unified inspection for work related to addressing climate change and eco-environmental protection, and clarifies the goals and tasks in the areas of strategic planning, policies and regulations, institutional systems, pilot demonstrations, and international cooperation.

For the waste sector, this Opinion calls for the strengthening of environmental management of centralised treatment facilities for sewage and waste, and coordinating the control of GHGs such as methane and nitrogen dioxide; promoting the thermal energy utilisation technologies such as sludge biogas co-generation and Water-Source Heat Pumps (WSHP) in wastewater treatment plants; and enhancing sludge disposal and comprehensive utilisation.
Document Title: Guiding Opinion on Coordinating and Strengthening Work Related to Addressing Climate Change and Eco-Environment Protection

The programme supports a range of energy-efficiency and renewables-related measures, such as building envelope upgrades (insulation), upgrading heating and ventilation systems, and deploying renewable energy technologies including solar. The improvements must lead to reduced energy consumption and higher energy-efficiency classes (e.g., at least class C).

Family Name: Bulgaria's recovery and resilience plan
Family Summary: To benefit from the support of the Recovery and Resilience Facility set up by the EU in the aftermath of the COVID-19-induced economic crisis, Member States submit their recovery and resilience plans to the European Commission. Each plan sets out the reforms and investments to be implemented by end-2026 and Member States can receive financing up to a previously agreed allocation. Each plan should effectively address challenges identified in the European Semester, particularly the country-specific recommendations of 2019 and 2020 adopted by the Council. It should also advance the green and digital transitions and make Member States’ economies and societies more resilient. The Commission validates the plan after which it effectively enters in force and EU subsidies can start flowing towards the member state.The plan notably aims to enable the phasing out of the use of coal for electricity generation and the phased replacement of the fuel base in the thermal power plants in coal areas of the country by using alternative, environmentally-friendly energy sources such as hydrogen.

Family Summary:
With the climate agreement of 22 June 2020, it was decided that Denmark will continue the tradition of harnessing offshore wind by building two energy islands – one in the North Sea and one on Bornholm.

In 2022, Denmark and Germany signed several key agreements to advance the Bornholm Energy Island project, establishing it as a joint, cross-border initiative. The main 2022 developments focused on expanding capacity, sharing costs, and initiating formal cooperation between the two nations to secure energy independence. In Denmark, the policy framework on the island is contained in the Supplementary Agreement on Climate on Energy and Industry of 22 June 2020 regarding Ownership and Construction of Energy Islands etc. of 4 February 2021 and the Supplementary agreement on Bornholm Energy Island of 29 August 2022.

The Agreement on tender framework for 6 GW offshore wind and Bornholm Energy Island (2023) sets the framework for the largest expansion of offshore wind in Danish history of 9 GW, which could potentially increase to 14 GW or more if the offshore wind developers take advantage of the freedom included in the agreement to build as much capacity as possible on the areas.

The market for offshore wind has become much more favorable in recent years. This Agreement ensures that that society has a share of the gains from utilising the Danish sea area, which is a common resource, taking into account nature and biodiversity. Tenders for the offshore wind farms are decided with price as the only competitive parameter, while a number of access requirements are set that raise the bar for sustainability and social responsibility compared to previous tenders. The purpose is to ensure a fast, simple and transparent tendering process, while at the same time ensuring increased sustainability and social responsibility.
Document Title: Supplementary agreement on Bornholm Energy Island of 29 August 2022

- Households: Actions to reduce poverty, improve economic stability, and mitigate the loss of human capital.

- Productive Sector: Strengthening sustainable and sophisticated production to create jobs and enhance internationalization.

- Institutional Framework: Improving institutional capacities for effective reactivation.

- Digital Development: Accelerating and strengthening digital infrastructure and capabilities.

The strategy contains framework goals for 2050 and interim goals for 2030 and 2040. In terms of content, it addresses the vision, framework, goals, indicators, an overview of the building stock by different sectors (residential, non-residential, public), obstacles and opportunities for the renovation of public buildings, cost-effective approaches to the renovation of public buildings, policies and measures, and financing the implementation of measures.

Family Name: Resolution of the 13th National Party Congress of the Communist Party of Vietnam
Family Summary:
This Resolution sets out the results of implementing the Resolution of the previous 12th Congress, and sets out the vision and development orientation for the coming years.

In relation to climate change, the Resolution states that resource management, environmental protection, and adaptation to climate change are still inadequate. The national development orientation for the period 2021-2030, key tasks and strategic actions therefore include the following:

  • Strictly manage and rationally and effectively use land and resources; protect and improve the environment; proactively and actively implement solutions to adapt to climate change and severe natural disasters.
  • Actively and effectively adapt to climate change, prevent, combat and mitigate natural disasters and epidemics, manage, exploit and use resources rationally, economically, efficiently and sustainably; take the protection of the living environment and people's health as the top goal; resolutely eliminate projects that cause environmental pollution, ensure the quality of the living environment, protect biodiversity and ecosystems; build a green economy, a circular economy, and an environmentally friendly economy.
  • Build a synchronous and modern infrastructure system in both economic and social aspects; prioritise the development of some key national projects on transportation, adapting to climate change; focus on developing information and telecommunication infrastructure, creating a foundation for national digital transformation, gradually developing the digital economy and digital society.

Family Name: Long-Term Climate Strategy, 2021
Family Summary:
This document aims to outline the path to reach net zero emissions by 2050, a goal decided by the Federal Council on August 28, 2019. The strategic principles set out in this document are as following:

  1. Switzerland will take advantage of the opportunities presented by a systematic transition to net zero.

  2. Switzerland will assume its climate policy responsibility.

  3. Priority will be given to reducing domestic emissions.

  4. Emissions will be reduced across entire value chains.

  5. All energy sources will be used effectively taking account of their optimal usage potential.

  6. The Swiss Confederation and the cantons will gear their planning activities to net zero in all climate- relevant areas.

  7. The transition to net zero will be carried out in a socially acceptable way.

  8. The transition to net zero will be achieved in an economically viable way.

  9. The transition to net zero will also improve environmental quality.

  10. The Long-Term Climate Strategy is based on openness to all types of technology.

Family Name: National strategy for sustainable wind power expansion
Family Summary:
To achieve its goal of 100 per cent renewable electricity production by 2040, the directors general of the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency and the Swedish Energy Agency presented a joint national strategy for sustainable wind power expansion.

This Strategy is aimed at ensuring that the expansion of wind power in the future can be carried out sustainably and with a greater degree of consensus and predictability.

To implement the Strategy's planning process, the county administrative boards in Dalarna and Värmland counties have, with funding from the Swedish Energy Agency, started work with regional analysts to investigate the potential for sustainable wind power expansion in Dalarna and Värmland counties.

The project will involve:

  1. A planning basis that shows areas with potential for wind power expansion.
  2. A regional analysis that shows the possibilities of achieving the expansion specified in the national strategy for the two counties, and a description of the opportunities and limitations that exist in the counties.
  3. Methodology for possible approaches to include the interests linked to the military part of the total defence in the planning process for wind power.
  4. Regional analysis to investigate the potential for wind power in Dalarna and Värmland counties

Planning support is also provided for the following areas:

  • Cultural environment and landscape
  • Reindeer management and Sami interests
  • Interests of the Armed Forces
Document Title: National strategy for sustainable wind power expansion

The sub-goals are:

  • Sub-goal 1 - The Swedish National Board of Housing, Building and Planning shall contribute to better coordination and communication between the government authorities in the national climate adaptation work for the built environment.
  • Sub-goal 2 - The Swedish National Board of Housing, Building and Planning's work on climate adaptation contributes to increased knowledge among municipalities, industry and other authorities.
  • Sub-goal 3 - The Swedish National Board of Housing, Building and Planning contributes to strengthening society's resilience to climate change by developing appropriate regulations and other policy instruments.

This is done, for example, by creating nationwide, separate and safe bicycle traffic networks, by expanding the bicycle traffic infrastructure, especially for cargo bikes, or by using safe and modern parking facilities.

Under the special programme for urban and rural areas, the Federal Government provides funding to the Länder and local authorities for the expansion of a safe and comprehensive bike lane network. The special programme for urban and rural areas will be expanded to include two new priority areas: (a) “Vision Zero” – upgrading and renovation of cycling infrastructure and (b) bicycle and pedelec parking spaces with charging infrastructure at public transport nodes (bus and train).

The programme will focus on: 
  • New construction, conversion and expansion of comprehensive, separate and safer bicycle traffic networks
  • separate bike lanes
  • bicycle streets
  • Cycle path bridges or underpasses
  • Parking facilities and bicycle parking garages
  • cargo bike traffic

Family Name: National Waste Management Plan for 2021-2028
Family Summary:
The National Waste Management Plan for 2021-2028 (Atkritumu apsaimniekošanas valsts plāns) was approved by the Cabinet Order No. 45/2021 on 22 January 2021.

It is a strategic policy framework designed to shift the country’s waste system toward a circular economy, significantly reduce waste generation and landfill rates, and improve recycling and reuse across key waste streams. It builds on EU Green Deal and circular economy goals, emphasizing prevention of waste at source, expanded separate collection (including textiles and biowaste), higher recycling and material recovery targets, and stronger infrastructure and governance to manage waste more sustainably. Through measures like “pay-as-you-throw,” enhanced sorting systems, and public education, the plan aims to cut environmental pressures, enhance compliance with regulatory enactments and policies in the field of climate and air quality, conserve resources, and support climate neutrality and sustainable consumption/production patterns by 2028.
Document Title: Cabinet Order No. 45/2021 - National Waste Management Plan for 2021-2028

Family Name: National Guidance on Voluntary Carbon Market Mechanisms
Family Summary:
The National Guidance on Voluntary Carbon Market Mechanisms includes provisions related to the institutional arrangement in the carbon market in Malaysia, specifically on the roles and responsibilities of project participants and the ministry in charge of climate change. The guidance sets out the technical requirements for a carbon project and requirements for project registration and reporting. The guidance also provides a short description and status of Malaysia's domestic emissions trading scheme.

Responsibilities of the carbon project developer

Project participants shall report the following to the Ministry in charge of climate change (Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability of Malaysia) and National Steering Committee on Climate Change (NSCCC):

a) Information on the carbon project;

b) The scope of the activity and the crediting periods;

c) The project boundary;

d) The methodology used and baselines developed;

e) Policy guidance applied to achieve the emission reductions; and

f) Annual reporting of units generated, sold, retired and cancelled.

For forestry projects, a project developer shall report the above to the National Steering Committee on REDD Plus (NSC REDD Plus)

Responsibilities of the Ministry in charge of climate change (Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability of Malaysia)

a) Host the Secretariat to the National Steering Committee on Climate Change (NSCCC) or any specific committee established under the NSCCC;

b) Provide guidance on carbon markets and propose mechanisms for domestic carbon markets as appropriate;

c) Maintain a registry to track all carbon projects;

d) Verify that no double counting occurs when reporting on nationally determined contribution (NDC) progress and achievement;

e) Undertake corresponding adjustments consistent with the decisions of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) on Article 6 of the Paris Agreement;

f) Report to UNFCCC on Malaysia’s participation in market mechanisms under the UNFCCC and voluntary carbon market;

g) Maintain Malaysia’s NDC in accordance with Article 4 paragraph 2 of Paris Agreement and decision 4/CMA.1 under the UNFCCC;

h) Ensure Malaysia’s participation in the voluntary carbon markets contributes to the implementation of Malaysia’s NDC and long-term low GHG emission development strategy;

i) Any other requirements agreed under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement.

Technical requirements of a carbon project

Activity design

  • The mitigation activity must

a) deliver real, measurable and long-term benefits related to climate;

b) minimise the risk of reversals and displacements of emission reductions, and where such reversals occur, ensure that they are fully addressed;

c) avoid negative environmental and social impacts;

d) avoid double financing;

e) establish a robust accounting system

  • In developing a carbon project, project developer/proponent must undergo stakeholder consultations including with local communities and indigenous peoples
  • There must be a transfer of technology, the applied technology must be environmentally sound and applicable for local environment
  • The mitigation activity must also 1) set a baseline 2) be additional 3) be monitored and 4) be quantifiable.

In addition to activity design, the national guidance also sets out the key requirements for carbon accounting, risks and reversal, corresponding adjustments, validation and verification, monitoring, issuance and renewal (Section 4.3 of the Guidance), as well as guidance on project registration and reporting (Section 5).
Document Title: National Guidance on Voluntary Carbon Market Mechanisms

  • 8.3.Promote life systems with a healthy, protected and balanced environment in harmony with Mother Earth.
  • 8.4. Promote the system of protected areas, wetlands, bofedales, as part of the country's natural heritage.
  • 8.5. Strengthen the integrated management of surface and groundwater resources to achieve water security.


The plan also seeks to guarantee food security and sovereignty, with a specific focus on indigenous populations. It promotes productive capacities and potentialities, under comprehensive management of basins (water), air, soil, forest resources, flora, fauna, risk management and adaptation to climate change based on the formulation of a Plan with a Comprehensive Management approach of their Territories.

The plan further calls for an increase in renewable energy capacity.
Document Title: Economic and Social Development Plan - PDES 2021-2025

Family Name: National Development Plan (PND) 2021-2025
Family Summary: The National Development Plan (PND) 2021-2025 is the reference document for national development planning. In this document, the State devotes one of the six priority axes, in particular axis 5, to the fight against climatic changes.
Document Title: National Development Plan (PND) 2021-2025

Family Name: UAE Sustainable Finance Framework
Family Summary:
The UAE Sustainable Finance Framework aims to deepen cooperation between the public and private sectors and seeks to create an improved enabling environment to mainstream sustainable finance practices, resulting in greater volumes of climate- and green investments in the UAE. 

The Framework presents multiple recommendations to mitigate the private sector's risks and to incentivise sustainable finance products/initiatives. An improved supply and demand of sustainable finance products and climate- and green investments projects pose a key action theme within the Framework. The Framework also highlights the provision of capacity building to existing and future sustainable finance professionals. 

The framework is based on three pillars:
  1. Mainstream sustainability in financial decision-making and risk management;
  2. Enhance supply and demand for sustainable finance products and green investments projects; and
  3. Strengthen enabling environment that promotes sustainable finance practices through collaboration between financial and real sector stakeholders.
Document Title: UAE Sustainable Finance Framework

Family Name: National Climate Resilience and Adaptation Strategy
Family Summary:
The National Climate Resilience and Adaptation Strategy (the Strategy) positions Australia to better anticipate, manage and adapt to climate change. The Strategy is designed to support governments, communities and businesses to better adapt, recognising that adaptation is a shared responsibility that requires sustained and ongoing action. The Strategy operates across four domains — natural, built, social and economic — to drive forward adaptation. It recognises that effective adaptation must be: informed by the best available science and information; delivered through partnerships and investments; and guided by effective governance and coordination.

The Strategy details three objectives to enable more effective adaptation across Australia:

  • Drive investment and action through collaboration;
  • Improve climate information and services; and
  • Assess progress and improve over time.
Document Title: National Climate Resilience and Adaptation Strategy 2021-2025

Family Name: National Strategy on Agriculture and Rural Development 2021-2027
Family Summary: This strategy aims to ensure the sustainable development of rural areas. It seeks to contribute to mitigation and adaptation strategies to climate change through the application of specific environmental practices in the production of agricultural goods.
Document Title: National Strategy on Agriculture and Rural Development 2021-2027

Family Name: Waste Management Program 2022-2031
Family Summary: The program determines the strategic goals for the improvement of the waste management system in the Republic of Serbia for the period 2022-2031. This program was preceded by the Waste Management Strategy of 2010-2019, which aimed to establish an integrated waste management system. The 2022-2031 program addresses and responds to the goals of the 2010-2019 strategy which were not fully achieved as well as to the new EU goals on waste management within the green transition and the establishment of a circular economy in the EU. This program seeks to reduce theharmful impact of waste on the environment and climate change, and realize the necessary preconditions for the role of a sustainable waste management system in the circular economy. This system will be designed to control waste generation and recovery as well as to create incentives to invest and promote economic opportunities deriving from waste. The principles guiding this Program include the principle of extended producer responsibility in which manufacturers bear the greatest responsibility for the generation of waste, and the polluter pays principle. The management of waste fromagricultural, mining, medical, and pharmaceutical activities is incorporated into sectoral planning documents.
Document Title: Waste Management Program 2022-2031

Family Name: Nationally Determined Contribution Investment Plan for Transport and Energy Efficiency
Family Summary: This plan outlines fifteen potential GHG mitigation opportunities - nine of which in the transport sector and six of which in energy efficiency sector – and estimated financing sources. The opportunities identified in the transport system include bicycle/e-bike financing initiative, biofuels blends in land and maritime transport, multi-model transit initiatives, electric vehicle network development, whole of lifecycle vehicle program, and land transport infrastructure upgrade for non-motorized transport. The opportunities identified in the energy efficiency sector include strengthening and expanding the standards and labelling programme for appliances, and capacity building for integrated energy planning and energy statistics.
Document Title: Nationally Determined Contribution Investment Plan for Transport and Energy Efficiency

Family Name: Papua New Guinea Fisheries Strategic Plan 2021-2030
Family Summary: The Papua New Guinea Fisheries Strategic Plan 2021-2030 is an overarching framework to align strategic purposes, priorities, actions and outcomes for the fisheries sector. The negative impacts of climate change on the fisheries sector can be devastating, including the rising sea temperatures and sea levels which in turn impacts the oceans, ecosystems and fish stocks. This increases the importance to consider ways to climate proof the sector, focusing on adaptive management approaches, mitigation, and resilient strategies. These include the rising sea temperatures and sea levels which in turn impacts the oceans, ecosystems and fish stocks.
Document Title: Papua New Guinea Fisheries Strategic Plan 2021-2030

Family Name: Environmental And Social Management System
Family Summary: The Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) supports the Ministry of Economy by setting out the principles for environmental and social safeguard review and management for the implementation of eco-centric developmental projects it is involved in administering and implementing that include a climate adaptation or mitigation component.
Document Title: Environmental And Social Management System

Family Name: National Climate Change Response Strategy 2021 – 2026
Family Summary:
The overall the objective of the Strategy is to enhance the national resilience to the adverse impacts of climate change and enable the country to pursue low-emission development pathways to achieve sustainable development. The specific objectives of the NCCRS are to: - i) Enhance mainstreaming of climate change issues into national sector and local government development plans and budgets; ii). Facilitate implementation and monitoring of the Tanzania’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC); iii) Align climate change interventions with the national development agenda of industrialised economy; iv) Devise and implement strategic adaptation and mitigation measures in line with the national circumstances, requirements of climate change related multilateral environmental agreements, sustainable development goals (SDGs) and related bilateral and regional agreements; v) Enhance research, public awareness, education and capacity building on climate change issues; vi) Enhance coordination and institutional capacity, including provision of climate services and implementation of the national framework for climate services; vii) Facilitate mobilisation of sustainable and adequate finance and technologies to support climate change adaptation and mitigation interventions; viii) Promote and facilitate transfer of climate-smart technologies to support climate change adaptation and mitigation; ix) Promote gender-responsive climate change adaptation and mitigation interventions; and x) Promote inclusive engagement of stakeholders, including community, media, civil society organisations and private sector in designing, implementing and monitoring sustainable climate change adaptation and mitigation interventions.

It provides strategic interventions and action plan for climate change adaptation, climate change mitigations, disaster risk management and climate finance, among other issues.
Document Title: National Climate Change Response Strategy

Family Name: National Strategy on Internal Displacement Management 2021
Family Summary: The National Strategy on Internal Displacement Management addresses internal displacement in Bangladesh caused by climate-related disasters such as floods, tropical cyclones, storm surges, and droughts. It provides a comprehensive framework to manage displacement across three phases: pre-displacement, during displacement, and post-displacement (durable solutions). The Strategy is aligned with international frameworks, including the UN Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015–2030), the UN Guiding Principles on Internal Displacement (1998), and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Document Title: National Strategy on Internal Displacement Management 2021

Family Name: Net Zero Roadmap for the Singapore Public Sector
Family Summary: As Singapore has committed to achieve net zero emissions by 2050, the public sector has taken the lead by committing to achieve net zero emissions earlier around 2045, after peaking emissions around 2025, in this Roadmap. The public sector will reduce emissions from its operations; replace its current energy source with lower-carbon alterantives and remove carbon by exploring new technologies. Actions include designing energy-efficient infrastructure; using alternative using cars and buses running on cleaner energy; deploying solar energy; and exploring low-carbon electricity imports.This Roadmap arises from the Singapore Public Sector's membership in the Net Zero Government Initiative. Participating countries commit to achieving net zero emission from national government operations no later than 2050, and develop a roadmap that outlines the pathway for achieving the net zero commitment.
Document Title: Net Zero Roadmap for the Singapore Public Sector

Family Name: National Energy Policy
Family Summary: The National Energy Policy serves as a blueprint to transform Ghana's energy sector into a sustainable, climate-resilient, low-carbon energy economy that will accelerate development and provide quality service to homes and industry. This Policy provides the policy context; an overview of Ghana's energy sector, including the institutional and legal framework; and sub-sector policy goals, objectives, issues and policy directions. The policy directions include evaluating the impact of climate change interventions on petroleum activities and resolving inadequate climate change interventions in the energy sector.
Document Title: National Energy Policy

Family Name: Feed-In-Tariffs Policy On Renewable Energy Resource Generated Electricity (Small hydro, Biomass And Biogas)
Family Summary: The Feed-in-Tariffs (FiT)Policy is an instrument for promoting generation of electricity from renewable energy sources. FiT allows power producers to sell renewable energy generated electricity to an Off-taker at a pre-determined tariff for a given period of time. The 2021 FiT Policy expressly states that it applies to RE power plants not exceeding 20MW in biomass, biogas and small hydro technologies. All solar and wind projects as well as other RE projects larger than 20MW will be procured under the Renewable Energy Auctions Policy
Document Title: Feed-In-Tariffs Policy On Renewable Energy Resource Generated Electricity (Small hydro, Biomass And Biogas)

Family Name: Renewable Energy Auctions Policy (REAP)
Family Summary: This REAP outlines the approach to renewable energy procurement in Kenya based on competitive auctions. The policy applies to all Solar and Wind power projects, as well as other RE projects larger than 20MW. The primary objective of this policy is to procure Renewable Energy capacity at competitive prices and aligned to the Least Cost Power Development Plan (LCPDP)/Integrated National Energy Plan (INEP).The Energy sector has identified a number of areas which could benefit from localised generation that would provide voltage support, improve power quality and stimulate demand growth.
Document Title: Renewable Energy Auctions Policy (REAP)

Family Name: Research and Innovation Policy
Family Summary:
According to the Policy, eradicating poverty with the current climate changes for a country whose economy has been known to be dominated by the agricultural sector, can only be done through innovative ideas leading to climate-smart agriculture. Hence, the Policy promotes heavy engagement in research and development for better innovations and informed decision-making.

The government will support the adoption of technologies for emerging applications with a strong focus on technical training to initiate a rapid transition to climate-resilient agriculture, quality healthcare, ICT, manufacturing digitisation and the green economy. Climate resilient agriculture is described as an approach that includes the sustainable use of natural resources through crop and livestock production systems to achieve long-term productivity and farm incomes under climate variabilities.
Document Title: Research and Innovation Policy

Family Name: National Climate Change Research Strategy (2020-2030)
Family Summary:
This Strategy has the goal of enhancing the availability and use of climate change-relevant information in national decision-making. This will be achieved by informing the design and execution of climate change-related scientific research initiatives in Saint Lucia about the critical data and knowledge gaps the country needs to address in order to execute its climate change agenda. The two strategic objectives are to (1) generate climate, environmental, and socioeconomic data and science-based information, critical to climate action across sectors, including adaptation, mitigation, and addressing loss and damage; and (2) enhance research and systematic observation (RSO) capacity in themes that are critical to climate action across sectors, including adaptation, mitigation, and loss and damage.

This Strategy facilitates the implementation of the National Climate Change Research Policy by offering guidance to research partners on the existing critical knowledge gaps that limit climate change-relevant policy and decision making in the country and, therefore are the topics of interest for research collaboration with the government of Saint Lucia.

It contains broad topics and research questions, and indicative research activities across the following themes:

1. Cross-cutting research and information for science-based decision making

2. Biodiversity, ecosystems, and ecosystem services

3. Coastal, marine, and ocean environments

4. Food production (agriculture and fisheries, including aquaculture)

5. Water

6. Energy and transport

7. Human health

8. Human settlements, the urban environment, and critical infrastructure

9. Tourism

10. Human mobility (displacement, national relocation, and international migration as last-resort options due to climate change)

11. Climate risk transfer mechanisms
Document Title: National Climate Change Research Strategy (2020-2030)

Family Name: Greenhouse Gas Reduction Promotion Plan
Family Summary:
The Environmental Protection Administration (EPA) has formulated this Plan in accordance with Article 9, Paragraph 1 of the Greenhouse Gas Reduction and Management Act. This Plan will initiate national and cross-departmental response actions, aiming to establish an operational mechanism involving central and local governments, public-private partnerships, and the public. The plan will implement national greenhouse gas mitigation policies, conduct a rolling review every five years, and actively promote implementation.

This Plan will be implemented through the greenhouse gas emission control action plans for the energy, manufacturing, transportation, housing and commerce, agriculture, and environment sectors, as well as the greenhouse gas emission control implementation plans formulated by the municipal and county (city) authorities. These implementation plans shall be approved by the Environmental Protection Administration in consultation with the central government's competent authorities within one year of the approval of the aforementioned promotion and action plans. Each plan should be reviewed every five years. The funds required for implementation will be allocated from the budgets of relevant government agencies at all levels. Dedicated units will be established as necessary to promote emission reductions. Relevant agencies implementing each plan should regularly report their progress and effectiveness through the online platform established by the EPA. The EPA will prepare and approve emission control implementation reports by 30 September of each year, in conjunction with the central government-run government agencies in charge of relevant sectors.
Document Title: Phase I Greenhouse Gas Reduction Promotion Plan (2016 to 2020)

Family Name: National Environmental Strategy 2021-2025
Family Summary:
This Strategy aims to acheive a higher level of conservation, protection and rational use of natural resources, environmental quality in human settlements, and climate change mitigation, with an ecosystem approach, to ensure the constitutional right of Cubans to live in a healthy and balanced environment.

This Strategy covers the national and international context for the development of a new strategic environmental cycle to 2030; the main environmental problems in Cuba; the conceptualisation of the Strategy; environmental indicators; and the implementation mechanisms.
Document Title: National Environmental Strategy 2021-2025

Family Name: Strategic Plan of the Common Agricultural Policy of the Republic of Croatia 2023 - 2027
Family Summary: This Strategic Plan of the Common Agricultural Policy both recognises climate change as a major threat to agriculture in Croatia, and the agricultural sector as a major source of climate mitigation potential. The plan contains a wide range of measures to reduce emissions, enhance carbon storage and increase climate resilience in the agricultural sector nationally, interfacing with government, industry and the public. Greenhouse gas emissions reduction is named a major area of action in the plan, with high prioritisation. The plan aims to increase the usage of renewable energy sources in agricultural developments, and optimise land use and plantings for carbon storage. It highlights the potential for significant expansion in biomass energy production. It also proposes major forest restoration, and capacity building including the creation of a national forest registry. A major adaptation measure in the plan is to increase the total area of artificially irrigated land, improving crop supply resilience.
Document Title: Strategic Plan of the Common Agricultural Policy of the Republic of Croatia 2023 - 2027

Family Name: 3N Initiative Action Plan 2021-2025
Family Summary:
The 3N Initiative is the national strategy for food and nutrition security and sustainable agricultural development. It is designed around five strategic areas covering various complementary fields that constitute the specificity of this innovative strategy, recognised as such since its inception in 2011. These five (5) strategic areas are translated into five (5) strategic programmes: (i) increasing and diversifying agro-sylvo-pastoral and fisheries production; (ii) ensuring a regular supply of agricultural and agri-food products to rural and urban markets; (iii) improving the resilience of populations to climate change, crises and disasters; (iv) improving the nutritional status of Nigeriens; and (v) facilitating, coordinating and driving reforms. It also defines a coherent set of normative measures and investment actions to be carried out in the short, medium and long term through the relevant ministries and administrations.

The 2021-2025 Action Plan consists of ten (10) operational programmes derived from the five (5) strategic programmes of the 3N Initiative and reflecting the six (6) priorities of the Renaissance Programme Act III: i) water management for irrigation; ii) environmental restoration; iii) the Maison de Paysan (Farmer's House); iv) the development of value chains for agro-sylvo-pastoral and fishery products; v) the resilience of populations to climate shocks and hazards; and vi) improving the nutritional status of Nigeriens.
Document Title: 3N Initiative Action Plan 2021-2025

Family Name: Gender Equality Strategy 2021-2030 (Strategy 2021+)
Family Summary:
The Czech Gender Equality Strategy 2021–2030 (Strategy 2021+) envisions a society where everyone can freely develop their potential regardless of gender, and aims to eliminate systemic gender‑based inequalities.

It is built around eight priority areas — work care, decision‑making, safety, health, knowledge, society, external relations, and institutions — with 26 strategic objectives and hundreds of concrete measures to close the gender pay gap, boost women’s representation, prevent gender-based violence, mainstream gender in education and policymaking, and strengthen institutional capacities.

The strategy also includes clear tools like indicators, action plans, and gender focal points in ministries to monitor progress.

Family Name: New Green Savings Programme (2021+)
Family Summary:
The most effective subsidy program in the Czech Republic focused on energy savings in buildings intended for permanent housing. It supports reducing the energy consumption of residential buildings (insulation), low-energy new buildings, environmentally friendly heating methods, renewable energy sources, and adaptation and mitigation measures in response to climate change.

The main objective of the program is to improve the state of the environment by reducing the production of pollutant emissions and greenhouse gases (primarily CO2 emissions ) . The program contributes to energy savings in final consumption and stimulation of the Czech economy, along with other social benefits, such as increasing the quality of citizens' housing, improving the appearance of cities and municipalities, and starting long-term progressive trends.

Family Name: Circular Economy: Action Plan for the Transition of Sweden
Family Summary:
The vision of this Action Plan is a society where resources are used efficiently in non-toxic circular flows and replace virgin materials. The overall objective is that the transition to a circular economy shall contribute to achieving the environmental and climate goals, as well as the global goals in the 2030 Agenda (for sustainable development).

Climate-related actions include:

  • Develop long-term economic instruments based on the polluter pays principle so that the cost of materials and products also includes the cost of the environmental and climate impact.
  • Strengthen the innovation and business climate so that more circular companies can grow and offer their products and services for both the domestic market and export.
Document Title: Circular Economy: Action Plan for the Transition of Sweden

Family Name: Climate Programme
Family Summary:
The Climate Act sets a target for Denmark to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 70 per cent in 2030 compared to 1990 levels. In the longer term, Denmark must be a climate-neutral society by 2050 at the latest. Each year, the Minister for Climate, Energy and Utilities must prepare a climate programme for the Danish Parliament, in which the minister must give his or her assessment of whether it can be demonstrated that the national climate targets will be achieved. The assessment of whether it is possible to demonstrate that the targets of the Climate Act will be achieved is based on an overall assessment of the short- and long-term effects of initiatives, where for some initiatives it will be possible to estimate a specific reduction effect. For other initiatives, an assessment of the expected reduction effect is made based on professional assumptions.

In accordance with the Climate Act, the Climate Council assessed the government's climate action in February 2021. The Climate Council assessed that the government had not demonstrated that the 70% target for 2030 would be achieved, in particular due to a lack of concrete climate action. Against this background, the Climate Council recommended, among other things, that the government present a roadmap for achieving the 70% target. With Climate Programme 2021, for instance, the government is presenting a comprehensive roadmap for achieving the 70% target in 2030, which demonstrates that the climate targets will be achieved. The roadmap states that by 2025 at the latest, the government will have presented proposals to ensure that the review is revisited all sectors and that we can make the necessary decisions towards 2025 to meet the 70% target. The roadmap is based on analyses by the Danish Energy Agency and relevant ministries of implementation speeds, scenarios, barriers, costs and maturity assessments of the individual technologies. The roadmap ensures that the necessary decisions can be made before it is too late, but also that decisions are not made too early in relation to the maturity of the technologies.
Document Title: Climate Programme 2022

Family Name: Green Gas Strategy
Family Summary:
Thie Strategy outlines the government's ambitions for Denmark's future gas consumption and gas infrastructure. It states the following principles:

  1. Green gas must complement electrification and be used where it has the greatest value.
  2. Green gas in industry must support jobs in Denmark for the benefit of growth and employment.
  3. The transition to green gas must take place under taking into account competitive tariffs and commercial terms.
  4. Green gas must eventually operate on market terms.
  5. Green gases must be produced sustainably.
  6. Development of green gas production and gas infrastructure must be carried out with close involvement of the citizens affected and take into account biodiversity and the environment.
  7. The gas system must support and be used for the green gases of the future.
  8. The gas system must be adapted and effectively support the energy system of the future and contribute with flexibility and security of supply.
  9. Denmark must work towards the development of a well-functioning European market for green gases.

As Denmark continues replacing fossil fuels with renewable energy from wind, sun and green gases, this requires that green gases are used where electrification is not an option for technical and economic reasons – especially in heavy industry. While Danish gas consumption in 2021 consists of around 20 percent biogas and 80 percent natural gas, gas consumption in 2030 will consist of around 70 percent biogas and only 30 percent natural gas.
Document Title: Green Gas Strategy

Family Name: Power-to-X Strategy
Family Summary:
Power-to-X (PtX) covers a range of technologies, all of which are based on the use of electricity to produce hydrogen. The hydrogen can then be used directly as fuel in road transport or industry, or it can be further converted into other fuels, chemicals and materials. The Danish government has four benchmarks to promote PtX in Denmark:1) Power-to-X must be able to contribute to the fulfilment of Denmark's Climate Act.2) The regulatory framework and infrastructure must be in place so thatDenmark's strengths can be exploited and Power-to-X can eventually operateon market terms.3) The interaction between Power-to-X and the energy system must be strengthened.4) Denmark must be able to export Power-to-X products and technologies.

This Strategy elaborates on how these benchmarks can be achieved.
Document Title: Power-to-X Strategy

Family Name: Agricultural Climate Solutions – On-Farm Climate Action Fund
Family Summary:
The objective of the fund is to support farmers in adopting beneficial management practices (BMPs) that store carbon and reduce greenhouse gases, specifically in the areas of:

  1. nitrogen management
  2. cover cropping
  3. rotational grazing practices

These practices also provide other environmental benefits such as improved biodiversity and soil health.

Other activities to support the adoption of beneficial management practices, such as outreach, education and training are offered.
Document Title: Agricultural Climate Solutions – On-Farm Climate Action Fund

Family Name: Natural Climate Solutions Fund
Family Summary:
To address climate change and biodiversity loss, the Government of Canada has established the Natural Climate Solutions Fund, which will invest over $5 billion from 2021 to 2031. This initiative consists of three distinct, but related, programs:

•   2 Billion Trees Program led by Natural Resources Canada ($3.19 billion): However, as announced in the Federal Fall Budget of 2025, the Government of Canada will wind down the 2 Billion Trees (2BT) program. While existing agreements will be honoured, the program is no longer accepting applications.

  • Nature Smart Climate Solutions led by Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) ($1.4 billion). Within this fund, up to $76.9 million has been set aside for Indigenous-led Natural Climate Solutions, to provide targeted support to Indigenous Nations, communities and organizations to engage as leaders in natural climate solutions.
  • Agricultural Climate Solutions led by Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada ($885 million)

The objectives are to:

  • Avoid GHG emissions by halting or reducing the conversion of carbon rich ecosystems to another less carbon rich ecosystem (e.g. from a forest/grassland/wetland to cropland or an urban development)
  • Restore carbon storage and biodiversity in converted or degraded ecosystems
  • Reduce GHG emissions caused by natural resource use, including by implementing new forest harvesting management practices
  • Develop policies, programs or tools with key actors in priority sectors, and implement them to reduce GHG emissions and improve biodiversity
  • Measure and report on GHG outcomes from natural climate solutions
  • Provide biodiversity and human well-being co-benefits
  • Advance the federal commitment to reconciliation with Indigenous people
  • Advance science and knowledge on natural climate solutions in Canada
Document Title: Agricultural Climate Solutions

Family Summary: The Smart Renewables and Electrification Pathways Program (SREPs) is a $4.5-billion program designed to support the deployment of grid modernization, energy storage and renewable energy technologies in every region of Canada, helping to grow the grid in a sustainable, affordable and reliable manner. The program also includes support for transmission and distribution infrastructure, and continues to support Indigenous-led clean energy projects. The program is currently expected to end March 31, 2036.
Document Title: Smart Renewables and Electrification Pathways Program

Family Name: Italy's Long-Term Strategy for Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions
Family Summary: The long-term Italian strategy on reducing emissions of greenhouse gases is a national multisectoral strategy of Italy for the period up to 2050. Its main objective is to identify, in compliance with the Paris Agreement, possible paths to reach, by 2050, a condition of climate neutrality, in which the residual greenhouse gas emissions are offset by the absorption of CO2 and from the possible use of forms of geological storage and reuse of CO2.
Document Title: Italy's long-term strategy for reducing greenhouse gas emissions ( Strategia Italiana di Lungo Termine sulla Riduzione delle Emissioni dei Gas a Effetto Serra)

Family Name: Natural Infrastructure Fund
Family Summary:
Announced in June 2021, the $200 million Natural Infrastructure Fund supports projects that use natural or hybrid approaches to protect the natural environment, support healthy and resilient communities, and contribute to economic growth and jobs.

The Natural Infrastructure Fund will bring real benefits to communities across Canada, including:

  • Increasing climate change resilience
  • Mitigating carbon emissions
  • Improving the environment, such as contributing to cleaner air and water
  • Protecting and preserving biodiversity and wildlife habitats
  • Promoting people's access to nature

A minimum of 10% of the overall program envelope will be allocated to Indigenous-led projects.
Document Title: Natural Infrastructure Fund

Family Name: Clean Fuels Fund
Family Summary:
Budget 2021 invested $1.5 billion over five years to establish a Clean Fuels Fund to de-risk the capital investment required to build new or expand existing clean fuel production facilities (including facility conversions). Support was also available for feasibility and front-end engineering and design (FEED) studies, and the establishment of biomass supply chains to improve logistics for the collection, supply, and distribution of biomass materials (e.g., forest residues, municipal solid waste, and agriculture crop residues) as a feedstock in clean fuel production facilities. Resources were also available to address gaps and misalignment in codes, standards and regulations related to the production, distribution and end-use of clean fuels.

Budget 2024 announced the retooling of the Clean Fuels Fund and its extension to March 31, 2030. Support is available to de-risk capital investments and studies that expand Canada’s clean fuel production capacity, and to address gaps and misalignment in codes, standards and regulations. The program has shifted to a continuous intake process to deliver funding faster and will streamline negotiations and decision-making processes to expedite delivery.
Document Title: Clean Fuels Fund

Family Name: Low Carbon Mobility Blueprint 2021-2030
Family Summary:
This Blueprint seeks to reduce emissions from the transportation sector, which currently ranks as the second-largest CO2 emitter in Malaysia after the energy sector, contributing 25% to 30% of the nation’s GHG emissions with predominantly internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles on the road.

This Blueprint mainstreams the shift towards electrification in the transportation industry. The focus areas are vehicle fuel economy and emissions improvement; electric mobility adoption in strategic applications (electric cars, buses and motorcycles); alternative fuel adoption; and electric mobility adoption in strategic applications. There is an aim for 10,000 EV charging points throughout Malaysia by 2025.
Document Title: Low Carbon Mobility Blueprint 2021-2030

Family Name: National Water Resources Strategy
Family Summary:
The National Water Resource Strategy, which the Water Act mandates the formulation of, outlines the challenges to water supply due to climate change, and the cross cutting issues of mainstreaming of climate change and gender in the water sector.

The objectives and actions are to:

i) Develop a view of the climate change trends and projections in Kenya including key climate change impacts and potential response options for the water sector;

ii) Develop water sector adaptation scenarios for future climate conditions using the information, data and models from the climate change trends and projections;

iii) Develop and implement strategies for early warning and response, and ensure preparedness for extreme water-related weather events;

iv) Plan and develop water infrastructure with operational flexibility to perform under different future climate conditions;

v) Strengthen the institutional framework within the water sector agencies to mainstream climate change into the water sector; and

vi) Enhance the capacity of the water sector agencies to attract and absorb domestic and international climate change financing.
Document Title: National Water Resources Strategy

Family Name: National Climate Change Learning Strategy (2021-2031)
Family Summary:
This Learning Strategy contributes to addressing capacity challenges and supporting implementation of the NDC and National Adaptation Plan 2015-2030. It contains eight strategic objectives:

Family Name: First national adaption plan for climate change: Republic of South Sudan
Family Summary:
This document, South Sudan’s first NAP for climate change, is a landmark achievement in the country’s response to climate change. The first NAP represents an important milestone in establishing a coordinated approach to building adaptive capacity and resilience to better manage the challenges the country faces, including changing environmental conditions associated with climate change and global warming. The first NAP also follows guidelines introduced by the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) in 2019.
The vision of the NAP is to mainstream adaptation planning within South Sudan’s development planning across different government line ministries and climate resilient communities. This will ensure climate-centric development for long term resilience and interruption of the poverty cycle. The mandate of the NAP is to build leadership and ensure stakeholder participation to fulfill South Sudan’s commitment to the UNFCCC and to operationalize climate change adaptation at all levels. The NAP will play a number of key roles for South Sudan, including the following:

Provide a roadmap of the steps needed to mainstream climate change adaptation into planning and budgeting at national, state and local levels.
Identify actions that are needed to create enabling conditions for scaled up access to international climate finance from both public and private sources.
Provide a baseline and starting point for climate change adaptation in South Sudan by consolidating all relevant information on the physical processes and impacts of climate change to establish a common understanding for all stakeholders.
Provide a common and coherent articulation of adaptation priorities to guide and coordinate all stakeholders, including government agencies, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), development partners, civil society organizations and the private sector, along the same pathway to a resilient and climate-adapted South Sudan. This includes providing a framework for determining and fulfilling South Sudan’s international commitments with respect to climate change adaptation.
Document Title: First national adaption plan for climate change: Republic of South Sudan

Family Name: Development and Cohesion Fund (FSC 2021-2027)
Family Summary: The Development and Cohesion Fund (FSC), which acquired this current denomination in 2011, is the main financial instrument through which policies for the development of economic, social, and territorial cohesion and the elimination of economic and social imbalances. The FSC is multi-year in nature, consistent with the programming schedule of the European Union's Structural Funds, ensuring the unity and complementarity of the procedures for activating the relevant resources with those provided for EU funds. Specifically, the Fund's intervention is aimed at financing strategic projects, both infrastructural and intangible, of national, interregional, and regional importance.The distribution of funds is regulated by the Interministerial Committee for Economic Planning and Sustainable Development (CIPESS). The current programme cycle is the FSC 2021-2027, which has a budget of 50,000 million euros approved by the Budget law 2021 (article 1, paragraph 177). The 2022 budget law (law no. 234 of December 30, 2021) subsequently provided for the refinancing of the FSC, programming period 2021-2027, for a total amount of €23.5 billion, at the rate of €3 billion for each of the years from 2022 to 2028 and €2.5 billion for 2029.Especifically regarding the Green Transition, the resolution CIPESS 1/2022 allocated €4,680.085 million to finance sustainable mobility infrastructure projects and, in particular, to the primary and secondary road network, the railway network, and works of regional interest, in compliance with the regulatory percentage distribution criterion of 80 percent to Southern Italy and 20 percent to Central-Northern Italy. Delibera CIPESS 35/2022 approved more €1.6 billion to cope with prices aiming to advance sustainable mobility nationwide.
Document Title: Delibera CIPESS 1/2022

Family Name: Eighth Five Year Plan (July 2020 -June 2025)
Family Summary:
The Eighth Five-Year Plan outlines Bangladesh's development strategy from July 2020 to June 2025. It aims to promote prosperity and inclusivity, strongly focusing on sustainable development and resilience to climate change. The plan revolves around six core themes:

i) Rapid recovery from COVID-19.  

ii) Accelerating GDP growth, generating employment, and significantly reducing poverty through a broad-based inclusiveness strategy.  

iii) Establishing a sustainable development pathway that is resilient to disasters and climate change.  

iv) Ensuring the sustainable use of natural resources and effectively managing the inevitable transition to urbanisation. 

v) Developing and improving critical institutions.  

vi) Achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) targets while addressing the challenges posed by the graduation from Least Developed Country (LDC) status.

Family Name: CONPES 4021 - National Policy for the Control of Deforestation and Sustainable Management of Forests
Family Summary:
This CONPES document provides policy guidelines to counteract deforestation and promote sustainable forest management. Through the analysis of the causes that affect the processes of land use change and loss of natural forest, it identifies the actions that the national government should develop in coordination with the sectors, communities and other actors so that, based on the recognition of the particularities and needs of the territories, this problem can be controlled and at the same time the conservation and sustainable management of forests can be promoted.

In particular, four strategic lines are established to lead the country to achieve the goal of zero net deforestation by 2030: (i) integrate strategies for the sustainable use of forests to improve the quality of life and the local economy of communities; (ii) articulate cross-sectoral actions that allow the national government to work together to manage forests and address territorial conflicts; (iii) promote prevention strategies and territorial control to reduce illegal dynamics, and (iv) strengthen the management of information for decision-making.

This policy focuses on actions foreseen under the Integrated Strategy for the Control of Deforestation and Forest Management (EICD).

The first comprehensive climate action plan consists of the sector strategies agreed with the Folketing, initiated initiatives to involve business and civil society, and indicators for the various sectors. The sector strategies, the decision of the Funen Power Plant to stop coal, the agreement on green tax reform, and the finance law agreements for 2020 and 2021 bring the total expected reduction to 7.2 million tonnes in 2030. This corresponds to one third of the necessary reductions up to 2030.

Family Summary:
Through this programme, placed under the support of the Federal Ministry of Economics and Climate Protection (BMWK), the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMU) focuses on energy-intensive industries that aim to reduce process-related greenhouse gas emissions that are difficult or impossible to avoid using the current state of the art, as far as possible and permanently. The funded projects make a substantial contribution on the way to greenhouse gas neutrality, combined with a clear perspective for the medium to long-term, complete replacement of fossil fuels and raw materials. The funded projects have a high innovative and demonstration character and should be transferrable to other companies as models. The directive aims to reduce annual greenhouse gas emissions from energy-intensive industries by 2.5 million tonnes of CO2 equivalents in 2030.

As part of the decarbonisation of industry programme, the Federal Government will expand the pilot scheme for carbon contracts for difference. Carbon contracts help mitigate the higher operating costs of low- and zero-emission processes. The Chemistry4Climate platform will also be set up as part of the programme.

In June 2023, the government announced approximately €50 billion would be made available for carbon contracts for difference and invited firms to make bids for funding to decarbonise their operations.
Document Title: Information on the Funding Programme on the Decarbonisation of Industry

Family Name: Guyana Water Strategic Plan 2021-2025
Family Summary: The Guyana Water Strategic Plan 2021-2025 functions as the comprehensive planning document for water in Guyana, via the state-owned and ministerially controlled Guyana Water Incorporated. The plan acknowledges climate change as a major threat to water resources in Guyana, through drought, over-reliance on groundwater, and resulting groundwater saline intrusion. A primary aim of the plan is to improve the security and availability of surface water resources, including the reuse of wastewater, to help adapt to the growing threats of climate change.
Document Title: Guyana Water Strategic Plan 2021-2025

Collection Summary: he Effort Sharing Regulation (ESR) is an EU law that sets binding annual greenhouse gas emission targets for each member state in sectors not covered by the EU Emissions Trading System — like transport, buildings, agriculture, and waste. Its goal is to ensure a fair contribution from all countries toward the EU’s overall climate targets.
Family Name: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2020/2126 on setting out the annual emission allocations of the Member States for the period from 2021 to 2030 pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2018/842
Family Summary:
Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2020/2126, adopted on 16 December 2020, establishes the annual greenhouse gas emission allocations (AEAs) for each EU Member State for the period 2021–2030 under the Effort Sharing Regulation (ESR). It defines the 2005 baseline emissions for every Member State and specifies the annual emission limits each country must respect throughout the decade. The Decision also sets out the total quantities that can be used for compliance through flexibility mechanisms, such as limited use of ETS allowances or land-use credits. Three annexes provide detailed data: Annex I lists the 2005 baseline emissions, Annex II gives the annual emission allocations for each year from 2021 to 2030, and Annex III sets out the total quantities available under flexibility provisions.

Since its adoption, the Decision has been amended several times to update the data and reflect changes in EU climate policy. Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1319 revised the AEAs for 2023–2030 to align with the higher climate ambition introduced by the revised Effort Sharing Regulation. Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/1884 introduced further updates and corrections to the national allocations, ensuring consistency with the most recent emissions data. Finally, Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/1405 made additional adjustments, likely to incorporate updated figures or methodological improvements. Together, these amendments ensure that Member States’ emission limits remain accurate and in line with the evolving EU legislative framework and climate targets.
Document Title: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/1405 amending Implementing Decision (EU) 2020/2126 as regards the total quantities of cancelled EU ETS allowances that may be taken into account for certain Member States’ compliance under Regulation (EU) 2018/842

Family Name: National Budget
Family Summary:
Japan's finance law contains a number of climate-relevant clauses.

2020 third supplementary budget

  • encourages increases in energy efficiency in ventilation equipments as a co-benefit to COVID-19 air renewal measures.


2021 budget and supplementary budgets

  • 100 billion yen allocated to domestic battery storage production  
  • 1 billion yen allocated to technology demonstration projects and research and development to reduce CO2 emissions in hygiene-related products through increased energy efficiency
  • 8 billion yen allocated to independent solar power generation equipment and storage batteries including electric vehicles through on-site PPA
  • 800 million allocated to the maritime sector to help on decarbonisation efforts

Other budget lines are allocated to the decarbonisation of buildings (5.5 billion yen), decarbonisation of residential homes (4.5 billion yen), creation of a Green Innovation Fund Business (2 trillion yen), heat pumps (46.5 billion yen), low-carbon energy equipment installations in facilities (3.76 billion yen), Offshore wind power generation (2.75 billion yen), solar power (5 billion yen), sewage sludge-to-energy conversion (5 billion yen), program to achieve zero-carbon cities (20 billion yen), development of GOSAT-GW satellites to monitor emissions of GHGs (3.853 billion yen), R&D into fusion nuclear energy, livestock biomass energy solutions such as biogas (2.8 billion yen), and increased subsidy to EVS and fuel cells vehicles.

 


2022 budget

  • diplomacy expenditure shall notably be directed to humanitarian assistance needs, including on climate change countermeasures.
  • Subsidies to solar power, offshore wind power, and geothermal power, and clean energy vehicles, and accelerate R&D for the practical use and diffusion of hydrogen, ammonia, etc. (about ¥100bn). Establishing a grant to provide continuous and comprehensive support for local governments that are making efforts to decarbonize (¥20bn).
  • budget allocated to public works expenditures related to disaster prevention and disaster mitigation.
Document Title: Supplementary Budget for 2021
