Family Name: Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 Plan
Family Summary: The Plan, intended for the period 2021-2025, sets out the need for Singapore to understand, mitigate and adapt to climate change. Singapore will invest in research that deepens its understanding of climate change impact, such as in sea level rise and changing weather patterns, and research on opportunities to conserve and leverage our natural assets to meet its sustainability goals. Singapore will also invest in research on enhancing its resource resilience, such as in energy, water and food, and on transforming the built environment sector.
Document Title: Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 Plan

Family Name: Financial Conduct Authority Rules to Enhance Climate-related Disclosures
Family Summary: As of December 2020 the UK's Financial Conduct Authority issued new rules requiring publically listed companies incorporated in the UK to either comply with the recommendations of the Task Force for Climate related Financial Disclosure and include information on climate-related financial disclosures in their annual report or explain the absence of such disclosures.
Document Title: Financial Conduct Authority: Proposals to enhance climate-related disclosures by listed issuers and clarification of existing disclosure obligations

Family Name: National Agroforestry Policy
Family Summary: Belize's National Agroforestry Policy notes climate change as a key threat to agricultural systems nationally, through drought, flooding and other extreme weather, and underscores the importance of developing agroforestry techniques and practice to enhance climate resilience and long-term sustainability. It aims to contribute to sustainable development goals on poverty, hunger, gender equality, climate action and biodiversity. The policy promotes agroforestry as a convenient synergy with REDD+ efforts, integrating trees and shrubs into crop and pasture systems, enhancing overall carbon storage and landscape resilience. It notes that some existing agroforestry techniques are unsustainable, leading to ecosystem degradation, and promotes measures to implement crop rotation and better manage fallow land. It aims to enhance investment and awareness in agroforestry best-practice across the country.
Document Title: National Agroforestry Policy

Family Name: Regulation 730/2020 on Minimum energy performance requirements for existing buildings
Family Summary: It sets mandatory minimum energy performance and energy-efficiency requirements for existing (exploited) buildings in Latvia, complementing the Energy Efficiency Law and aligning with relevant EU directives. They define how a building’s energy and primary energy consumption levels must meet at least a specified benchmarking class (typically E class or higher), require functional automation and control systems and temperature-regulating devices to optimise indoor climate and energy use, and stipulate measurement and accounting of energy carriers, including individual and remote-read metering for heat and hot water consumption in multi-unit buildings. The rules also promote infrastructure supporting electric vehicle charging and modern energy monitoring systems, all designed to improve building energy performance, reduce energy waste and associated emissions, and contribute to Latvia’s climate-related energy-saving and decarbonisation goals.
Document Title: Regulation 730/2020 on Minimum energy performance requirements for existing buildings

Family Name: Strategic Emergency Management Guideline 4 - Climate Change Adaptation
Family Summary:
The Strategic Emergency Management (SEM) Guideline 4 – Climate Change Adaptation, provides guidance that addresses: a) Consideration of climate change projections for Ireland during the response to emergencies and in emergency planning, b) Ensuring that relevant likely impacts of climate change in Ireland on diverse sectors are addressed, in order to build resilience to climate change across Irish society and the economy, c) Where to find information on climate change projections, predicted impacts, adaptation options, and national policy on climate change adaptation, in particular, the National Adaptation Framework (NAF) and Sectoral Adaptation Plans, d) National, regional and local coordinating structures for climate change adaptation, and e) Integration of national policy and approaches within the wider European Union (EU) and international policy on climate change adaptation.

This Guideline is part of the Strategic Emergency Management (SEM) National Structures and Framework document, approved by the Government on 26 July 2017. The SEM identifies 50 different emergency/incident types across a range of lead government departments. It provides the basis for national-level strategic emergency management and the support required should such emergencies occur were a national-level response is warranted, including security-related emergencies.
Document Title: Strategic Emergency Management Guideline 4 - Climate Change Adaptation

Family Name: Lithuanian Transport Development Strategy until 2050
Family Summary: The Transport Development Strategy aims to guide the long term development of transport in Lithuania, accounting for the need to mitigate and adapt to emerging challenges such as climate change. The strategy promotes general expansion of low carbon transport, calling for the establishment of a sustainable mobility fund, and the use of tax incentives to guide development. Recommendations include electric vehicle promotion, rail electrification and improvements in monitoring administration. It also acknowledges threats to existing transport infrastructure by flooding and extreme weather, as they increase in frequency under climate change.
Document Title: Lithuanian Transport Development Strategy until 2050

Family Name: Guidelines on Environmental Risk Management for Banks
Family Summary: These guidelines set out MAS' expectations on environmental risk management for all banks, merchant banks, and finance companies. Environmental issues that are of concern include climate change, loss of biodiversity, pollution and changes in land use. The Guidelines apply on a group basis for locally-incorporated banks.The guidelines cover: Governance and strategy; Risk management and Disclosure of environmental risk information.
Document Title: Guidelines on Environmental Risk Management for Banks

Family Name: Regulation for mandatory energy performance certificates
Family Summary: The regulation applies to four different classes of larger-scale buildings with a requirement that all buildings must to be compliant until the end of 2022.
Document Title: Regulation for mandatory energy performance certificates

Family Name: Agreement on green transformation on road transport
Family Summary:
The government (Social Democracy), the Danish Social Democratic Party, the Socialist People's Party and the United Unity Party have entered into an Agreement to implement changes in the following areas:

• Green transformation of road transport

• Ambition of 1 million green cars in 2030

• Work towards a halt to the sale of new fossil-fuel cars by 2030 at the latest

• Restructuring the registration tax for passenger cars and vans

• Low electricity tax for charging cars

• CO2 displacement requirements for renewable fuels

• Kilometer-based taxes for trucks

• Other initiatives

• Increase and restructuring of current car taxes

• Handling of outstanding indexation of the registration tax

• Financing contribution from the agreement on restructuring the car taxes from 2017

• Financing, etc.

• Administrative costs
Document Title: Agreement on green transformation on road transport

Family Name: Agreement on the future of oil and gas extraction in the North Sea (2020)
Family Summary:
The Government and a broad majority in the Danish Parliament decided to allocate DKK 200 million in 2021-22 for development projects for CO2 storage in the North Sea. This was based on the rationale that the North Sea holds great potential for storing CO2 in former oil and gas reservoirs and can support Denmark's green transition and path towards the 70% reduction target in 2030 and climate neutrality by 2050. At the same time, CCS projects have the potential to support local employment in the same areas as the oil and gas sector is based.

The agreement also cancels the 8th tender round and sets an end date for oil and gas extraction in the North Sea in 2050, to achieve the Paris Agreement's goal of limiting the global temperature increase to 1.5 degrees and fulfill Denmark's obligation to act on behalf of future generations.
Document Title: Agreement on the future of oil and gas extraction in the North Sea (2020)

Family Name: Green solutions of the future - Strategy for investments in green research, technology, and innovation
Family Summary:
The strategy sets a clear direction for the Danish green research and innovation effort in order to accelerate the development of technologies and solutions, which can help protect the climate, nature and environment.

The strategy points out four missions that focus on challenges where the need for new solutions and the potential for meeting the green objectives are the largest in Denmark as well as on a global scale. The missions are to be accomplished by green partnerships in which knowledge institutions, businesses, public authorities, and private players join forces in a strategic research and innovation effort over several years.

The goal is to enable greenhouse gas reductions and strengthen the green frontrunner position of Danish industries to the benefit of exports and green jobs in Denmark.
Document Title: Green solutions of the future - Strategy for investments in green research, technology, and innovation

Family Name: National Drought Plan and resilience framework for Somalia
Family Summary:
The National Drought Plan and the Drought Impact & Needs Assessment and Recovery & Resilience Framework are two separate, complementary documents.

The Drought Plan seeks to provide Somalia with a system and mechanism to mitigate droughts and enable the establishment of a resilient society that can withstand the drought shocks. It focuses on the following strategic themes: 1) Drought Monitoring and Prediction, 2) Drought Impact assessment, 3) Drought Preparedness through sustainable use of Water, Land and Natural resources, and 4) Improving Emergency Drought Response.

The Recovery and Resilience Framework aims to provide the basis for policymaking, institutionalisation and financing of recovery and long- term development. It is supported by the Drought Impact & Needs Assessment that provides an assessment of drought damage and loss impacts and an estimation of recovery and resilience needs.
Document Title: National Drought Plan For Somalia

Family Summary: The 2050 carbon neutral strategy is South Korea's UN-LEDS. It outlines five key elements to achieve carbon neutrality: Expanding the use of clean power and hydrogen across all sectors; Improving energy efficiency to a significant level; Commercial deployment of carbon removal and other future technologies; Scaling up the circular economy to improve industrial sustainability; Enhancing carbon sinks. It further sets sectoral decarbonisation orientations.

Family Name: Canada's hydrogen strategy
Family Summary:
This document, subtitled "Seizing the Opportunities for Hydrogen - A Call to Action", sets the government's vision to increase the production and use of hydrogen in the country. It was developed with a range of non-state stakeholders. It seeks to modernise the country's energy systems through building new hydrogen supply and distribution infrastructure and fostering uptake in various end-uses in order to achieve short- and long-term decarbonisation. The strategy further seeks to make Canada a net exporter of H2.

Over the next five years, Canada aims to: 
  • Encourage early deployment HUBs in mature applications, and Canadian demonstrations in emerging applications;
  • employ regulations, including the forth-coming Clean Fuel Standard to drive near-term investments; and
  •  frame new policy and regulatory measures needed to reach net-zero by 2050.
Document Title: Information on the Hydrogen Strategy for Canada

Family Name: Energy White Paper
Family Summary:
In December 2020 the UK Secretary for Business, Energy, and Industrial Strategy issued an Energy White Paper entitled "Powering our Net Zero Future". The aim of the White Paper is to transform energy, support a green recovery from the COVID19 crisis and create a fair deal for consumers. The government estimates that the measures set out in the White Paper could reduce emissions across power, industry and buildings by up to 230MtCO2e in the period to 2032, as well as creating thousands of jobs.

Among the measures proposed, the paper includes further detail on previous policies regarding a ban on the sale of new petrol and diesel cars by 2030, financial support for an extra 40 gigawatts (40GW) of new offshore wind, and £3bn in funding for home energy improvements. The paper also envisages experimentation with a number of other mechanisms to keep energy affordable for consumers.

One of the key elements of the paper is the provision of details on the establishment of the UK Emissions Trading Scheme, which will include a cap on emissions that is 5% lower than under the previous EU Emissions Trading Scheme and will be lowered further over time to ensure a net zero trajectory. 

The paper also sets out Government plans for nuclear energy, including the intention to create a commercially viable nuclear fusion plant by 2040. Additional funding is also intended to be made available for the development of new carbon capture and storage technologies.
Document Title: Energy White Paper

Family Name: Canada’s Small Modular Reactor Action Plan
Family Summary:
Canada's Small Modular Reactor (SMR) Action Plan is Canada's plan for the development, demonstration and deployment of SMRs for multiple applications at home and abroad. This Action Plan is part of Canada's transition to clean electricity.

The Action Plan is launched by the Govenrment and is a compilation of chapters, each contributed by key enablers from across Canada – the federal government, provinces and territories, Indigenous Peoples and communities, power utilities, industry, innovators, laboratories, academia, and civil society. Each chapter describes a concrete set of actions the contributor is taking to seize the SMR opportunity for Canada.

Family Name: Long-Term Strategy for the Renovation of the National Building Stock
Family Summary: The strategy aims to set out measures and challenges for renovating buildings in Croatia, in order to decarbonise the sector and contribute significantly to national climate change mitigation and adaptation efforts. The strategy covers: the current state of the national building stock, projections at current renovation rates, possible methods to organise renovation, analyses of previous policies on energy retrofitting, likely funding streams, and national initiatives to promote development of enhanced green technology for building renovation. The strategy also includes a plan with measures, quantified goals and progress indicators, organised by timeframe. It aims for 100% of buildings nationally to be highly energy efficient by 2050, 60% by 2040 and 25% by 2030. The strategy estimates overall energy savings and broader benefits from these measures, in addition.
Document Title: Long-Term Strategy for the Renovation of the National Building Stock

Family Name: Vision 2050
Family Summary: Rwanda's Vision 2050 sets out a long term vision for national development aiming for sustainable growth across a wide range of sectors, robust climate resilience and low emissions. It aims to achieve high income and carbon neutral status by 2050. The vision places a particular emphasis on climate adaptation in the agri-food sector, promoting measures such as new forms of crop risk insurance, decentralised grain reserves, irrigation and general technological improvements to productivity. Through these efficiency gains and growth in other sectors, it aims to bring the portion of the population employed in agriculture to below 30%.
Document Title: Vision 2050

Family Name: Vision and Development Strategy of Slovakia until 2030
Family Summary:
This long-term sustainable development strategy, approved by Government Resolution No. 41 of 20 January 2021, also fulfils the role of the National Strategy for Regional Development of the Slovak Republic. It thus integrates sectoral priorities and regional and territorial development priorities. It is based on four principles: sustainability, the priority of quality of life over economic growth, efficiency based on synergies, and the integration of policies and their instruments.

In terms of environmental objectives, Slovakia 2030 is to ensure the protection, restoration and enhancement of natural resources, including ensuring the stability and health of ecosystems and their services, and the reflection of adaptation and mitigation measures to the adverse effects of climate change in all departmental strategic documents and municipal and regional development documents as an overriding public interest (e.g. in transport planning, energy, spatial planning, spatial planning, water management, land management, forestry, sustainable tourism, overall care of the countryside, etc.).
Document Title: Resolution 41/2021 approving the Vision and Development Strategy

Family Name: Guideline on climate-friendly commercial vehicles and infrastructure
Family Summary: The Guideline on climate-friendly commercial vehicles and infrastructure implements one of the three core measures from the 2030 Climate Action Programme to decarbonise (heavy) road freight traffic. Recognizing that no single technology can satisfy all freight transport applications, the concept adopts a technology-neutral approach that promotes battery-electric and hydrogen fuel cell vehicles according to their respective operational strengths. To enable the market ramp-up of zero-emission commercial vehicles, the strategy combines three complementary pillars: financial support for vehicle deployment, coordinated development of charging and hydrogen refueling infrastructure, and the establishment of a supportive regulatory framework, including CO₂-based road toll differentiation.Its overarching objective is for approximately one-third of heavy-duty freight transport activity in Germany to be carried out using electric or electricity-based propulsion technologies by 2030.

This Ordinance is currently under review and amendment.

On November 25, 2020, the Federal Council adopted the revised CO2 ordinance, which is scheduled to enter into force on January 1, 2021. The revision consists in particular of extending the key climate protection instruments until the end of 2021. It helps prevent a regulatory vacuum until the complete revision of the CO2 law comes into force. The amendment to the ordinance also aims to implement a requirement of Parliament, namely a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions of 1.5% in 2021 compared to 1990. The Swiss people refused the law's full revision in June 2021. According to a World Bank report, in December 2021, the Swiss Parliament passed a prolongation of the CO2 Act until 2024, guaranteeing the continuation of existing measures, including the carbon levy, currently at a rate of CHF 120/tCO2e.

Family Summary:

Climate Change adaptation, mitigation and disaster risk management are identified as a priority in achieving the national targets. Strategies identified for improved climate action include:

  • Prioritising the mainstreaming of climate change and related financing in all national programmes;
  • Strengthening early warning systems;
  • Promoting climate-smart innovations and technology transfer;
  • Strengthening capacity building and awareness of climate change adaptation and mitigation;
  • Upgrading meteorological radar seismology and weather station network;
  • Implementing disaster risk management;
  • Cloud seeding;

Family Name: Resolution PP-4896 On Measures to Further Improve the Activities of the Hydrometeorological Service Center of the Republic of Uzbekistan

It enshrines the necessity of funding ongoing climate change research, and the integration of this service with national climate adaptation efforts. It also promotes the public dissemination and awareness of climate change data, through publications, seminars, internships and other means. The resolution underscores the importance of fulfilling international obligations on climate reporting and action, and envisages participation of national climate research authorities in the development of international legal acts. Specific research projects promoted by this resolution include glacial mass balance predictions under climate change, and hydrological forecasting to ensure the suitability of river systems for hydropower installation.

Family Name: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Order 2020 (S.I. 1265/2020)
Family Summary:
This order established a new UK emissions trading regime as the successor to the EU Emissions Trading Scheme following the UK's Withdrawal from the European Union. The scheme applies to greenhouse gas emissions from power and heat generations, energy intensive industries, and aviation.The order provides details on the rules governing the issuance and surrender of "allowances" equivalent to emissions falling within the scope of the sceheme. A number of derogations from the general rules are created for hospitals and small and ultra-small emitters. A modified version of the EU Monitoring, Reporting and Verification scheme is also mandated under the legislation.The order also describes the different agencies responsible for the regulation of the scheme across the UK and provides for enforcement of the scheme and sets out the penalty regime for non-compliance.The first UKA auction took place in May 2021.

The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) (No. 2) Order 2024 (S.I. 2024/1366) introduces key updates to the primary 2020 UK ETS Order (S.I. 2020/1265) to align the UK Emissions Trading Scheme with Net Zero targets:

  • Tighter Emissions Cap: Significantly lowers the overall scheme cap and the yearly base allowances from 2024 through 2030 to align carbon budgets with net-zero trajectories.
  • Flexible Reserve: Establishes a new "flexible reserve" pool of allowances to manage unallocated or returned free allowances and support future market stability mechanisms.
  • Aviation Scope Expansion: Expands aviation compliance obligations
Document Title: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Order 2020

Family Name: Long-term decarbonisation Strategy. Strategy for a modern, competitive and climate neutral Spanish economy by 2050
Family Summary:
This Spanish long-term strategy outlines the roadmap for Spain to achieve climate neutrality by 2050, aligning with the European Union's commitment under the European Green Deal and the Paris Agreement. Recognising Spain's vulnerability to climate change, the strategy aims to transform the economy to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, with intermediate milestones in 2030 and 2040. It emphasises leveraging the opportunities presented by this transition for economic modernisation and increased competitiveness, while ensuring a socially just and inclusive process that leaves no one behind.
The strategy is built on the principle of technological neutrality, encouraging the development of cost-effective decarbonisation solutions across all sectors. It seeks to provide long-term signals to investors and stakeholders, fostering innovation, job creation, and strengthening Spain's research and development capabilities. This plan builds upon existing frameworks like the National Integrated Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC) and emphasises the importance of a just transition, addressing energy poverty, and adapting to the impacts of climate change. The strategy also recognises the need to accelerate the ecological transition as part of the post-COVID-19 recovery efforts.

Family Name: Agricultural Transition Plan
Family Summary: The Agricultural Transition Plan is the UK government’s plan for restructuring agricultural policy in England from 2021-2028 following Brexit and the end of EU subsidies. The plan seeks to gradually phase out the Basic Payment Scheme (BPS), replacing it with new initiatives focused on environmental sustainability, productivity, and animal welfare. The proposals in the plan aim to support farmers in adapting to new business models while addressing climate change and biodiversity challenges.

Family Name: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEEAP)
Family Summary: The NEEAP is a strategic policy document which sets out the country’s final and intermediate national energy savings targets to 2030 and includes concrete measures and actions to meet these targets. The work is financed by the Ministry of Finance of the Slovak Republic. The NEEAP has been prepared by ENVIROS, s.r.o. who were commissioned by The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) with the support of the Department for Energy Efficiency (DEE) of the State Committee for Standardization of the Republic of Belarus in response to a request by the Administration of the President of Belarus in December 2017. While the development and adoption of a NEEAP is a requirement for EU Member States under the EU Energy Efficiency Directive (EED) as well as for the Energy Community Contracting Parties, the Republic of Belarus applied to become an Observer to the Energy Community in 2016 and preparation of a NEEAP is hence not mandatory for Belarus. Nevertheless, the country decided to prepare its first NEEAP in line with the Energy Community guidelines. The NEEAP is complementary to other current initiatives in Belarus including the national Sustainability Strategy and informs the next submission of the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) to the Paris Agreement (due in 2020) and the development of the forthcoming State Energy Savings Programme for 2021 to 2025.

Its purpose is to enable indigenous peoples to adapt to climate change, reduce disaster risk, preserve their forests and biodiversity, and integrate their traditional knowledge with technological tools. Overall, the plan aims to strengthen indigenous resilience, protect territories, and ensure that adaptation and mitigation are grounded in indigenous perspectives, cultures, intergenerational knowledge, and fairness.

Family Name: A Green and Sustainable World - Global Climate Action Strategy
Family Summary:
The Danish Government’s new long-term strategy on global climate action sets the direction for Denmark’s international climate efforts. The aim is to:

  • Increase global climate ambition: Denmark will work to influence states and non-state actors to commit to ambitious objectives contributing to limiting global warming. It will work with States, multilateral organisations and civil society for ambitious efforts on climate adaptation, resilience and sustainable development.
  • Reduce global greenhouse gas emissions: Denmark will work for a global green transition focused on reducing emissions of large emitters and sustainable development in developing countries.
  • Strengthen focus on adaptation and sustainable development: Denmark wants to inspire and drive resilience and adaptation initiatives. It wants a far more climate-oriented development cooperation focused on climate change and sustainable development in the poorest and most fragile developing countries, and to spread Danish prevention and adaptation solutions globally.
  • Shift financial flows to green: Denmark will contribute to shifting global financial flows from fossil fuels to green, climate-friendly investments. It will support the greening of financial markets and the energy markets and systems designed to foster investments in renewables. It will also strive to increase the mobilisation of climate finance for the poorest and most fragile countries.
  • Cooperate with the private sector on green solutions: To drive successful global climate action, Denmark will work with the private sector to promote green Danish solutions globally, with exports providing a basis for increased green growth in Denmark.
Document Title: One-page summary of the Global Climate Action Strategy

Family Name: Strategy for Green Public Procurement - Action Plan for Green Public Procurement 2020-2030
Family Summary:
This Strategy was launched with the aim of public procurement helping to achieve the goal of a 70 percent reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030. The strategy is based on three tracks, all of which focus on procurement areas in the public sector that currently have a significant climate footprint, including:

  1. An implementation track that creates green action now,
  2. a development path that creates long-term green action towards 2030,
  3. and a track related to green knowledge and green tools.

Under these three tracks, the strategy presents initiatives that are already being launched, as well as initiatives with a longer development horizon. The initiatives range widely across both stages of the procurement process and procurement areas.

For instance, 60 percent of the food must be organic, that food waste from canteen operations be combated, and that a meat-free alternative is always offered. Climate compensation for all government flights is paid annually to the Climate Forest Fund, to ensure that new forests are planted in Denmark.

For longer-term initiatives, work has been initiated to draw up a plan for a shift to emission-free cars in the state, municipalities and regions, so that the public car fleet can be emission-free in 2030. The Secretariat for Green Procurement in the Danish Environmental Protection Agency is being strengthened and made the main entry point for guidance, advice and knowledge sharing and dissemination regarding green public procurement.

Family Name: Ministerial Resolution No. 197-2020-MINAM. Determines the composition and functions of the Indigenous Peoples' Platform to Address Climate Change (PPICC) [Resolución Ministerial Nº 197-2020-MINAM. Determina la conformación y funciones de la Plataforma de Pueblos Indígenas para enfrentar el Cambio Climático (PPICC)]
Family Summary:
The Resolución Ministerial N° 197‑2020‑MINAM formally establishes the Platform of Indigenous Peoples to Confront Climate Change (Plataforma de Pueblos Indígenas para Enfrentar el Cambio Climático, PPICC), a permanent participatory body designed to give effect to indigenous peoples’ rights in Peru’s climate governance. Rooted in the UNFCCC framework (Decisions 1/CP.21 and 2/CP.24) and the domestic Climate Change Framework Law (Law No. 30754), the Platform ensures the systematic incorporation of indigenous knowledge, practices and proposals into national adaptation and mitigation policy.

The PPICC brings together state actors (including the Ministries of Environment and Culture) and representative national indigenous organisations, operating on principles of parity, interculturality, and intergenerational equity. Its functions extend from generating and disseminating indigenous proposals on adaptation, mitigation and forest management, to monitoring the implementation of policies such as the National Strategy on Forests and Climate Change. It also tracks financing flows, safeguards traditional knowledge systems, and creates a channel of structured dialogue between indigenous constituencies and national decision‑makers. In this way, the Platform seeks to embed indigenous perspectives into Peru’s long‑term climate and energy transition strategies, while simultaneously reinforcing social inclusion and environmental integrity.
Document Title: Ministerial Resolution No. 197-2020-MINAM (Resolución Ministerial N° 197-2020-MINAM)

LLike those who built the longships, the Norwegians also aim to take their technology out into the world, but only by peaceful means. It also includes a development plan for the Northern Lights CCS project, which is a subsea reservoir for CCS.

Family Name: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1294 on the Union renewable energy financing mechanism.
Family Summary: According to the CAT, "This Mechanism allows member states to reach their renewable energy goals by funding development of renewables in other EU member states where it could be more cost competitive. To avoid double-counting, the countries in which these projects are hosted cannot account for the installed capacity in their renewable energy goals, but benefit from the emissions reduction, job creation, and reduced energy dependency. The potential of the Mechanism is significantly increased by also opening it to private investors, and the possibility of using resources from the recovery fund."
Document Title: Regulation on the EU renewable energy financing mechanism 2020/1294

Family Name: Just Transition Framework for South Africa
Family Summary: At its Sixth Meeting held on 27 May 2022, the Presidential Climate Commission (PCCC) adopted the Just Transition Framework. A final version was published in July 2022, with policy recommendations. According to the PCC, the Just Transition Framework is a planning tool for achieving a just transition in South Africa, setting out the actions that the government and its social partners will take to achieve a just transition, and the outcomes to be realised in the short, medium, and long term. The Just Transition Framework is organised into seven main actions: (1) Foundations on which the framework builds; (2) Definition of a Just Transition for South Africa; (3) Principles to guide the transition; (4) At-risk sectors and value chains; (5) Key policy areas to give effect to the transition; (6) Effective governance arrangements; (7) Financing a Just Transition.
Document Title: Initial Just Transition Framework (May 2022)

Family Name: National Progress Plan 2021-2030
Family Summary: The National Progress Plan 2021-2030 aims to address the main changes to the state, in terms of actions and priorities, over the next decade. The plan names climate action, among other priorities such as inequality, as a major motivation for increasing the share of GDP redistributed by the state. Climate action is framed in terms of the UN's Sustainable Development Goals, and is named among five top priorities for the state. The plan acknowledges that achieving these goals may significantly reorient consumption, employment patterns and lifestyle, and emphasises the importance of a just transition. However, it highlights the green transition as a significant opportunity for economic growth.
Document Title: National Progress Plan 2021-2030

Family Name: Strategy for Sustainable Energy Development of the Republic of Bulgaria until 2030, with a horizon to 2050
Family Summary:
This Strategy has been drawn up pursuant to Article 4(2)(1) of the Energy Act and reflects the state’s vision for the development of the energy sector up to 2030, with a horizon to 2050, in line with the current European energy policy framework and global trends in the development of new energy technologies. The key priorities are:

1. Ensuring energy security and sustainable energy development;

2. Developing an integrated and competitive energy market and protecting consumers by ensuring transparent, competitive and non-discriminatory conditions for the use of energy services;

3. Improving energy efficiency across the entire energy chain, from production to end use;

4. Sustainable energy development for clean energy and decarbonisation of the economy; and

5. Implementation of innovative technologies for sustainable energy development.

The target is to achieve a 27.09% share of energy from renewable sources in gross final energy consumption by 2030, which will be derived from solar and geothermal energy and biomass including waste and residues of biological origin from agriculture, forestry, industry and households. Currently, Bulgaria's electricity generation mix is dominated by coal-fired thermal power stations, followed by the Kozloduy Nuclear Power Plant. Bulgaria will continue its policy of increasing renewable energy use in the following sectors: electricity, heating, cooling and transport.
Document Title: Strategy for Sustainable Energy Development of the Republic of Bulgaria until 2030, with a horizon to 2050

Family Name: National strategy for the development of carbon-free hydrogen in France
Family Summary:
This document aims to 1) Decarbonise the industry sector by creating a national electrolysis sector, 2) Develop heavy mobility using carbon-free hydrogen, and 3) Support research, innovation and skills development in order to promote future uses.

The updated 2025 Strtategy provides for "smoothing of the objectives of electrolysis installation on the territory over the long period, with up to 4.5 gigawatts targeted for 2030 and a new target of 8 gigawatts installed in 2035". It adopts a "low-carbon hydrogen production support mechanism of four billion euros to secure the competitiveness of low-carbon hydrogen over fifteen years compared to fossil hydrogen".

A new call for projects for the deployment of hydrogen commercial vehicles aims to promote the technological development of fuel cells and tanks with support for the purchase of light commercial vehicles in 2025.
Document Title: National strategy for the development of carbon-free hydrogen in France 2025

Collection Name: Law 7/2021 on climate change and energy transition [Spain]
Collection Summary:
Enacted in 2021, this law establishes Spain's legal framework for achieving climate neutrality by 2050, aligning with the Paris Agreement and Sustainable Development Goals. It mandates a 23% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 (compared to 1990 levels), alongside ambitious renewable energy targets, including 42% of final energy consumption from renewables and 74% renewable electricity generation by 2030. Energy efficiency measures aim for a 39.5% reduction in primary energy consumption within the same timeframe. The law also prohibits new hydrocarbon and radioactive mineral exploitation, requires emission-free transport systems in cities with populations exceeding 50,000, and emphasises sustainable urban mobility.

The legislation includes a national Just Transition Strategy to ensure equitable economic opportunities, particularly for vulnerable regions, while fostering adaptation and resilience to climate risks across critical sectors such as water, biodiversity, and health. It creates governance mechanisms like the Expert Committee on Climate Change and Energy Transition to monitor progress and updates to Spain's Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC). Projecting investments exceeding €200 billion by 2030, the law is expected to enhance Spain’s GDP by €16.5–25.7 billion annually and generate 250,000–350,000 new jobs. The focus on education, innovation, and public awareness underscores its commitment to a holistic and inclusive transition.

This collection represent a body of policies, strategies, and plans enacted under this law.
Family Name: Spanish Strategy for Science, Technology, and Innovation 2021-2027 (EECTI 2021-2027)
Family Summary: The Spanish Strategy for Science, Technology, and Innovation 2021-2027 (EECTI 2021-2027) serves as the foundational framework for strengthening and consolidating Spain's Science, Technology, and Innovation System (SECTI) over seven years. It aligns national RDI policies with the European Union's strategies, leveraging synergies to enhance scientific, technological, and industrial progress. Drafted during the COVID-19 pandemic, the strategy addresses pandemic-related challenges and underscores the critical role of science and innovation in socio-economic recovery and resilience. It adopts a phased approach: the first phase (2021–2023) focuses on reinforcing existing strengths, investing in healthcare RDI, ecological transition, and digitalisation, while the second phase (2024–2027) prioritises knowledge-driven economic growth and institutionalising RDI as a cornerstone of national development.The EECTI 2021-2027 identifies six thematic clusters essential for addressing Spain’s strategic priorities: health, inclusive society and creativity, societal security, digital and industrial advancements, climate and energy, and sustainable food systems. It integrates the objectives of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and EU programmes, particularly Horizon Europe. The strategy also emphasises enhancing investment in RDI, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration, and advancing technologies to mitigate demographic challenges and promote regional equity. Ultimately, the EECTI aims to position Spain as a leader in innovation, fostering high-quality employment and long-term socio-economic sustainability.
Document Title: Spanish Strategy for Science, Technology, and Innovation 2021-2027 (EECTI 2021-2027)

Family Name: Lebanon National Agriculture Strategy (NAS). 2020-2025.
Family Summary: Lebanon's National Agriculture Strategy (NAS). 2020-2025 recognises climate change as a major threat to the security of the agricultural sector, and names climate resilience among its five overarching pillars: restoring the livelihoods of producers; increasing agricultural production; enhancing efficiency of value chains; improving climate change adaptation and sustainable management of agrifood systems and natural resources; strengthening and enabling the institutional environment. Climate-related provisions include plans for significant afforestation, both for climate mitigation and to build landscape-level resilience, and the use of renewable energy in the agricultural sector where possible. The strategy also notes that more efficient water usage is a key element of agricultural adaptation to climate change, and promotes the adoption of modernised irrigation techniques.
Document Title: Lebanon National Agriculture Strategy (NAS). 2020-2025.

Family Name: Guidelines for water management in agriculture and forestry in a changing environment
Family Summary:
Guidelines for water management in agriculture and forestry in a changing environment set out objectives and measures for sustainable water management in agriculture and forestry, including in the light of changing climate conditions.

The proposed water management measures have been divided into six categories: Governance measures, financing, planning and implementation, research and development, education, training and advice, and digitalisation. These key measures include investments in studies on the level of catchments, understanding the current state of and opportunities offered by water management measures, ensuring the numbers and level of competence of water management planners, contractors, advisers and experts, and new and innovative solutions through research, pilot projects and digitalisation.
Document Title: Guidelines for water management in agriculture and forestry in a changing environment

Family Name: France Relaunch Plan ("France Relance")
Family Summary:
This document aims to enable the economic, social and ecological rebuilding of the country over the period 2020-2030. The document is divided into three major topics: ecology, competitiveness and social cohesion. The budget allocated stands at 100 billion euro, 40 % of which coming from the European Union stimulus plan.

30 billion euro of the total budget is to be allocated to "ecology": 1) energy renovation of buildings and SMEs, 2) biodiversity and fight against artificialisation of soils, 3) decarbonisation of industry, 4) circular economy, 5) ecological transition of the agriculture sector, 6) making fisheries and ports more environmentally-friendly, 7) accelerating the transition to low-carbon transport and related-infrastructure, 8) strengthen the uptake of green technologies including hydrogen, and 9) establishing new "climate products" under BPI France (the national public investment bank).
Document Title: France Relaunch Plan

Family Name: National Energy Policy 2050 (2nd edition)
Family Summary: This long-term energy policy proposes a vision of Chile’s energy sector by the year 2050 as being reliable, inclusive, competitive and sustainable. It is sustained by four pillars: Security and Quality Supply, Energy as a Driver for Development Environmentally-friendly Energy, Energy Efficiency and Education. The proposed measures and action plans shall be developed on the basis of these pillars between 2016 and the year 2050. This Policy outlined targets including renewable power generation share targets of 60% by 2035 and 70% by 2050. The Policy was developed through the Participatory Process for Energy Policy (Proceso Participativo de la Política Energética), which sought to promote an open process and a multisectoral effort that would articulate a shared vision for the future development of the energy sector.
Document Title: National Energy Policy 2050 (2nd edition)

Family Name: Regulation 560/2020 on the production of electricity using renewable energy resources, as well as on the pricing procedure and monitoring, last amended by Resolution 648/2025
Family Summary: This regulation sets out the conditions and procedures for generating electricity from renewable energy sources (RES) in Latvia, including the criteria for qualifying producers, how the mandatory purchase (“obligatory procurement”) of RES electricity is determined and monitored, and the price-setting mechanisms for electricity produced from renewables. It defines, among other points, which technologies qualify (e.g., hydro, biomass, biogas, certain wind installations).

Family Name: President's Expanded Priority Program (PROPEP 2020-2023)
Family Summary: This document introduces a stimulus programme to combat the adverse effects of the COVID-19-induced economic crisis. It seeks to 1) intensify public investment, particularly in priority productive sectors with a view to accelerating the achievement of food self-sufficiency and in green sectors; 2) establish a Strategic Investment Fund; 3) initiate the formalisation of the economy; 4) simplify administrative procedures; 5) improve the business environment; and 6) lay the institutional foundations for strong and effective governance to support the private sector.The program notably allocates funds towards reforestation and sustainable forest management efforts, and the creation of green jobs. It aims to restore and ensure sustainable management of forest areas and degraded lands with a view to improving the livelihoods of local populations. It also contributes to better pollution management and the promotion of waste recovery channels capable of creating sustainable jobs, especially for young people. The envelope devoted to this axis represents an amount of MRU 961.9 million, or 4% of the overall funding.From this specific envelope, 350 million MRU will go toward the national reforestation program, including schools and public spaces. Further details on the allocation of this envelope are as follows:- Reinforcement of the national initiative of the great green wall for an envelope of 250 million MRU, or 26% of the financing of axis, allowing the realization of multipurpose gardens or Integrated Community Agricultural Farms,- Reduce pollution and improve the management and recovery of urban solid waste. for an overall envelope of MRU 361.9 million, i.e. 37.6% of the funding for the axis. This envelope will be intended for the ongoing program to clean up 33 municipalities in the interior of the country and its renewal for an additional year, as well as the development and introduction of a mercury-free extraction process for artisanal gold.
Document Title: President's Expanded Priority Program (PROPEP 2020-2023)

Family Name: National Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2021-2030
Family Summary: The National Climate Change Adaptation Plan is a reference framework for the co-ordination of the Public Administrations in the activities of impact assessment, vulnerability studies and adaptation to climate change in Spain. This document replaces an earlier version published in 2006 and spanning the period 2006-2020. The Plan considers a series of ecological systems and socio-economic sectors for impact assessment, vulnerability studies and adaptation to climate change: biodiversity, hydro resources, forests, agricultural sector, coastal areas, continental hunting and fishing, mountain areas, fishing and marine ecosystems, transport, human health, industry and energy, tourism, financial services, urban planning and construction. The Plan aims to facilitate and to provide continuous assistance to all the interested administrations and organisations - public and private, at all levels, to evaluate the impacts of climate change in Spain in the sector/system of their interest, and to provide all the information available on the subject, and the available elements, tools and assessment methods, for purposes of promoting the process of participation between the ones involved that can lead to the definition of the best adaptation options to climate change.

Family Name: Zimbabwe Vision 2030
Family Summary: Zimbabwe Vision 2030 embodies the aspirations towards a Prosperous Upper Middle-Income Nation by 2030, in line with the Sustainable Development Goals and African Union Agenda 2063. It provides for plans to partner with development partners to “broaden climate change mitigation and adaptation activities to include critical elements such as water management and harvesting measures to mitigate the effects of drought, respect for biodiversity and wetland management issues.”
Document Title: Zimbabwe Vision 2030

Family Name: National Action Programme to Combat Desertification and Manage Natural Resources
Family Summary:
The National Action Programme to Combat Desertification and Manage Natural Resources (PAN-LCD/GRN) is a multisectoral document covering the whole of Niger. Its main objectives are to improve and sustain productive capital (soil, water, etc.) on the one hand, and the living environment on the other.

The document's general objectives are: to identify the factors contributing to desertification and the concrete measures to be taken to combat it and mitigate the effects of drought; to create conditions conducive to improving food security, resolving the domestic energy crisis, promoting the economic development of local communities, and empowering them to manage natural resources.
Document Title: National Action Programme to Combat Desertification and Manage Natural Resources (PAN-LCD/GRN)

Family Name: Sustainability Bond Framework
Family Summary:
This document is aimed at supporting the development of the green, social and/or sustainability capital market with the issuance of safe (AAA-rated) and liquid sovereign green, social and/or sustainability bond(s).

Under this Framework, the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg may issue 3 types of bonds: 1) Green Bonds where an amount equal to the net proceeds will be exclusively used to (re)finance eligible expenditures falling within the Eligible Green categories, 2) Social Bonds where an amount equal to the net proceeds will be exclusively used to (re)finance eligible expenditures falling within the Eligible Social categories,, and 3) Sustainability Bonds where an amount equal to the net proceeds will be exclusively used to (re)finance eligible expenditures falling within both Eligible Green and Social categories.
Document Title: Sustainability Bond Framework

Family Name: Sectoral Climate Change Management Plan for Housing and Urban Territory (PIGCCS)
Family Summary: Sectoral plan to reduce emissions by 4 MtCO2e in 2030 from the buildings and waste sectors through implementation of mitigation measures.
Document Title: Sectoral Climate Change Management Plan for Housing and Urban Territory (PIGCCS)

Family Name: Papua New Guinea's Sustainable Development Goal 13 roadmap: 30 actions by 2030
Family Summary: Papua New Guinea's Sustainable Development Goal 13 Roadmap consists of a set of 30 actions ranging from topics in climate governance, energy, forestry, infrastructure, agriculture, minerals, health, biodiversity and tourism.These 30 sets of actions that must be completed between 2020 and 2030 in order for PNG to meet SDG 13 and make progress across all 17 of the SDGs. It provides a path towards climate compatible development which will reduce the PNG’s vulnerability to climate change and contribute to global action on reducing greenhouse emissions.The 30 by 30 Roadmap is structured by nine sectors, with one cross-sectorial category called Climate Change Governance and Knowledge. The Roadmap is a product of an extensive mapping exercise where stakeholders and scientists were engaged to identify climate hazards and risks.
Document Title: Papua New Guinea's Sustainable Development Goal 13 roadmap: 30 actions by 2030

Family Name: National Civil Protection Plan
Family Summary:
This regulation, Cabinet of Ministers Order No. 476 (adopted August 26, 2020), approves the National Civil Protection Plan. It serves as the master blueprint for how Latvia manages major crises, consistent with existing strategies for climate change adaptation.

This plan acts as the official guidebook for how the government, local municipalities, and the public should act during a major emergency. It covers everything from early warning and prevention to how to clean up after a disaster. It also explains how the civil system supports the military if there is a war or invasion. The main goals are to keep people safe, protect the environment, and ensure that basic needs (like food and water) are met during a crisis.
Document Title: Cabinet of Ministers Order No. 476 about the National Civil Protection Plan

Family Name: Adaptation to climate change in Switzerland: Action Plan 2020-2025
Family Summary:
This second action plan regulates implementation in the years 2020-2025. The 2020-2025 action plan comprises 75 measures at the federal level. 63 of these measures are activities in the sectors of water management, dealing with natural hazards, soil protection, agriculture, forestry, energy, housing, tourism, biodiversity management, health (humans and animals), and spatial development. 12 measures cross-sectoral.

The action plan aims to improve the knowledge base, transfer knowledge, coordinate, and promote the implementation of the Adaptation Strategy. The measures have been prioritized by the responsible federal agencies and will be specified and implemented by them as part of the respective sector policy. They are intended to help manage the risks of climate change in Switzerland, exploit any opportunities that arise, and increase the adaptability of the systems. They are brought together in the action plan from a cross-sectoral perspective to coordinate the approach to overcoming the challenges of climate change.
Document Title: Adaptation to climate change in Switzerland: Action Plan 2020-2025

Family Name: Solid Waste Masterplan 2020-2035
Family Summary: The Seychelles' Solid Waste Masterplan 2020-2035, prepared by the Delegation of the European Union to the Republic of Mauritius and to the Republic of the Seychelles, seeks to guide the long term development of the solid waste sector, ensuring efficient, resilient and sustainable operation. It notes that the sector requires significant modernisation, through expansion of recycling, efficient and waste-to-energy incineration, better-aerated 'windrow' composting, biogas and other technologies, which if implemented would help to mitigate emissions intensity across the economy and from both the production and disposal ends of the commodity value chain.
Document Title: Solid Waste Masterplan 2020-2035

Family Name: The National Strategy for Climate Change Adaptation
Family Summary: The National Climate Change Adaptation Strategy (NCCAS) provides a common vision of climate change adaptation and climate resilience for South Africa, and outlines priority areas for achieving this vision. It draws on South Africa's National Climate Change Response Policy (NCCRP) (DEA 2011), the National Development Plan (NDP) (NPC 2011), the adaptation commitments included in its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC), sector adaptation plans, provincial adaptation plans and local government adaptation plans. The main objective of the document is to provide guidance across all levels of government, sectors, and stakeholders affected by climate variability and change. It should also serve as the country's National Adaptation Plan and fulfils the commitment to its international obligations under the Paris Agreement. It is divided into sets of strategic objectives, interventions and outcomes with associated actions.
Document Title: National Climate Change Adaptation Strategy

RenovaBio provides for 1) Biofuels certification, 2) the goals of reducing GHG emissions in the fuel matrix and 3) issue and trading decarbonisation credits(CBios ). Normative Resolution 14/2017 sets the strategy for RenovaBio. Decree 9.308 details the application of the law. Family Name: National Strategy for Biological Diversity and its Action Plan 2012-2022 (Estrategia Nacional de Diversidad Biológica y su Plan de Acción 2012-2022)
Family Summary:
The National Strategy for Biological Diversity and its Action Plan 2012-2022, developed under Guatemala’s commitments to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), provides the national framework for conserving, valuing, and sustainably using biological diversity, while ensuring its integration into broader development and climate change policies. The strategy responds to accelerating biodiversity loss, deforestation, and ecosystem degradation, which undermine rural livelihoods, food security, and national economic sectors such as forestry, hydropower, and tourism. Recognising biodiversity as a foundation of national development and a critical instrument for climate change adaptation, it aligns with the Política Nacional de Diversidad Biológica and incorporates cross‑sectoral objectives that link environmental governance with poverty reduction and sustainable development.

The strategy is structured around five thematic axes: (i) knowledge and valuation of biodiversity, including scientific research and traditional practices; (ii) conservation and restoration, emphasising in situ and ex situ measures, ecosystem recovery, and community engagement; (iii) sustainable use, through productive systems and equitable benefit-sharing; (iv) biodiversity and climate change, promoting adaptive and mitigation strategies and financing mechanisms such as REDD+, payments for ecosystem services, and carbon markets; and (v) implementation and governance, which seeks to strengthen legal, institutional, and financial capacities. Specific lines of action focus on reducing deforestation and degradation to lower greenhouse gas emissions, securing ecosystem services related to water, food, and energy, and reducing socio‑environmental vulnerability. The plan establishes a monitoring and evaluation framework, with indicators to assess outcomes and to foster accountability across government ministries, local authorities, the Consejo Nacional de Áreas Protegidas (CONAP), civil society, indigenous organisations, and the private sector.
Document Title: National Policy on Biological Diversity - Government Agreement 220-2011 / National Strategy on Biological Diversity and its Action Plan 2012-2022 (Política Nacional de Diversidad Biológica - Acuerdo Gubernativo 220-2011 / Estrategia Nacioal de Diversidad Biológica y su Plan de Acción 2012-2022)

Family Name: Ireland National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary: The National Energy and Climate (ENCP) Plan is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness. The plan establishes key measures to address the five dimensions of the EU Energy Union : 1) Decarbonisation : to reduce emissions from sectors outside the EU's Emissions Trading System, carbon pricing to create behavioural change and avoid locking in carbon intensive technologies, eliminate non-recyclable plastic and impose higher fees on the production of materials which are difficult to recycle, promote the increased use of domestic harvested wood in longer lived product, mainstream biodiversity across the decision making process in the State, increase electricity generated from renewable sources to 70%, etc;2) Energy efficiency : to set stricter requirements for new buildings and substantial refurbishment, 600,000 heatpumps installed over the period 2021-2030, scale-up and improve the Sustainable Energy Communities and Better Energy Communities, etc; 3) Energy security : to support efforts to increase indigenous renewable sources in the energy mix, including wind, solar and bioenergy, etc; 4) Internal energy market : continue to deepen the integration of IRL’s wholesale electricity market and its regulation with the EU internal energy market (IEM), etc;5) Research, innovation and competitivenes : to increase investment in knowledge-based capital, to strengthen delivery of public funding for basic and applied research to meet Ireland’s decarbonisation objectives, etc.
Document Title: Ireland's National Energy and Climate Plan

Family Name: Gear Change, A bold vision for cycling and walking (Cycling and walking plan for England)
Family Summary:
This document aims fostering walking and cycling in England. Four themes are laid out in the document: 1) better streets for cycling and people, 2) cycling and walking at the heart of decision-making, 3) empowering and encouraging local authorities, 4) enabling people to cycle and protecting them when they do. Physical and mental health is explicitly mentioned as an argument for increasing walking and cycling rates.

Under this plan, the government will build more (protected) cycle lanes, provide cycle training for everyone and bikes available on prescription. It will also create a long term cycling programme, consult to strengthen the Highway Code for safety purposes, support local authorities to crack down on traffic offenses, create low traffic neighbourhoods to improve air quality, focus on areas with poor average health and increase access to e-bikes. 

A budget of two billion pounds has been allocated to this plan. Bike repair vouchers worth £50 will be released under a pilot plan. A scheme to support bike repairers is also considered.
Document Title: Information on Gear Change: A bold vision for cycling and walking

Art. 7 states that CENABC's internal regulations will be prepared by the General Coordination of Climate Change of the Department of Sustainable Production and Irrigation of the Secretariat of Innovation, Rural Development and Irrigation of the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Supply.

Family Name: Decision No. 1055/QD-TTg on promulgating the National Climate Change Adaptation Plan for 2021 - 2030 Period with a Vision by 2050
Family Summary:
The National Climate Change Adaptation Plan aims at implementing climate commitments under the Paris Agreement. The Plan provides specificities of the adaptation component of Vietnam's NDC.

According to section 2(a) the general objectives of the Plan are to reduce vulnerability and risks from climate change impacts through strengthening resilience and adaptation capacity of communities, economic sectors and ecosystems; promote the integration of climate change adaptation contents into relevant strategies and planning.

It aims to do so through the following means:
  1. Intensifying the state management of climate change, including climate change adaptation contents, and promoting the integration of climate change adaptation contents into relevant strategies and planning;
  2. Making investments in adaptation actions, science and technology, and increasing public awareness to be ready to adapt to climate change; and
  3. Reduce disaster risks and minimise damage in order to be ready to cope with disasters and extreme climate events increased due to climate change.

The Plan sets out two implementation phases: 2021 - 2025 phase; 2026 - 2030 phase. It also sets out a vision for 2050.

A list of tasks of the Plan is enclosed. These tasks concern:
  • Intensifying state management and resources;
  • Agricultural sector;
  • Disaster management;
  • Environment and biodiversity;
  • Water resources; and
  • Infrastructure facilities.
Document Title: Decision No. 1055/QD-TTg on promulgating the National Climate Change Adaptation Plan for 2021 - 2030 Period with a Vision by 2050

Family Name: Council of Ministers Resolution n.º 53/2020, last amended by Council of Ministers Resolution n.º 149/2024 approving the update of the NECP 2030
Family Summary:
The Resolution 53/2020 approves the National Energy and Climate Plans (NECP) 2030 and assigns to the newly renamed Commission for Climate Action the responsibility of overseeing and monitoring the implementation of the NECP 2030, as well as ensuring compliance with the established targets. It also establishes that the National System of Policies and Measures is responsible for the monitoring, evaluation, development of policies and measures, and projections of the NECP 2030.
Amid their goals, the resolutions aims to highlight the importance of meeting:
1 - National targets of the NECP 2030 for the year 2030, aligned with a carbon-neutral trajectory by 2050:
a) Reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 45% to 55%, compared to emissions recorded in 2005.
b) Incorporate 47% of energy from renewable sources into gross final energy consumption.
c) Reduce primary energy consumption by 35% to improve energy efficiency.
d) Achieve 15% electricity interconnections.
2 - Sector-specific greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets, compared to emissions recorded in 2005:
a) 70% in the services sector.
b) 35% in the residential sector.
c) 40% in the transport sector.
d) 11% in the agriculture sector.
e) 30% in the waste and wastewater sector.
In 2024, Resolution 49/2024 updated the NECP 2030 to reflect a a higher level of ambition than set in the initial version, in response to national and European developments and new legislation (i.e. Fit for 55 package).
The eight key objectives are: i) decarbonize the national economy; ii) prioritize energy efficiency; iii) increase renewable energy use and reduce energy dependence; iv) ensure supply security; v) promote sustainable mobility; vi) support sustainable agriculture and forestry, enhancing carbon sequestration; vii) develop an innovative and competitive industry; and viii) ensure a just, equitable, democratic, and cohesive transition.
Document Title: National Energy and Climate Plan 2030

Family Name: Supreme Decree No. 006-2020-MINAM. Establishes the High-Level Commission on Climate Change (Decreto Supremo Nº 006-2020-MINAM. Crea Comisión de Alto Nivel de Cambio Climático)
Family Summary:
The Decree Supreme establishing the Permanent Multisectoral Commission known as the High-Level Commission on Climate Change (CANCC) creates a formal, institutional mechanism for coordinating national climate policy in Peru. The instrument is grounded in constitutional provisions affirming the right to an adequate and balanced environment (Article 2, inciso 22 of the Constitution), as well as Peru’s international obligations under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). The creation of the CANCC responds directly to the mandate contained in Law No. 30754, the Climate Change Framework Law, which establishes the need for a high-level intergovernmental body to support the formulation, review, and reporting of nationally determined contributions (NDCs) in alignment with international commitments. As a permanent body, the CANCC operates under the technical oversight of the Ministry of Environment and is presided over by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, reflecting its central role in cross-sectoral governance.

The Commission’s primary functions are defined in Article 3 and include: (i) proposing adaptation and mitigation measures within the framework of the National Strategy on Climate Change; (ii) supervising the development and updating of methodologies for greenhouse gas (GHG) emission projections; (iii) formulating recommendations for inclusion in the NDCs; (iv) assessing proposals from regional and local governments to inform progressive strengthening of national targets; (v) preparing and submitting technical reports on the NDCs every five years to the UNFCCC focal point; and (vi) evaluating recommendations from the National Commission on Climate Change (CNCC) and the Indigenous Peoples’ Platform for Climate Change, with a view to their implementation. The structure of the Commission ensures multisectoral representation, including government institutions, civil society, scientific bodies, and Indigenous organisations, thereby embedding principles of participatory governance, transparency, and accountability into the national climate policy architecture.
Document Title: Supreme Decree No. 006-2020-MINAM (Decreto Supremo No. 006-2020-MINAM)

The plan also addresses science and technology, especially by integrate its use in the agricultural, housing,  roads and solar power projects. It promotes research in renewable and alternative energy sources.

Family Summary: German Resource Efficiency Programme III (ProgRess III) – 2020–2023: Germany’s national programme aims to reduce the consumption of primary raw materials and improve resource efficiency across the entire value chain, from raw-material extraction and product design to production, consumption, reuse and recycling. It promotes longer product lifetimes, repair, reuse, resource-efficient production, greater use of secondary raw materials and the development of a circular economy. The programme also supports innovation, digitalisation, sustainable supply chains and resource-efficient construction, infrastructure and mobility. Overall, ProgRess III seeks to decouple economic growth from resource consumption while supporting climate protection, environmental sustainability, competitiveness and responsible use of natural resources.

Family Name: Plan to promote the value chain of the automotive industry
Family Summary:
This document promotes the modernisation, decarbonisation and digitisation of the automotive sector in the country. It is based on five pillars: 1) Renewal of the vehicle fleet towards a more modern and efficient one, 2) Investments and regulatory reforms to boost competitiveness and sustainability, 3) Research, development and innovation for new challenges, 4) Taxation to boost the competitiveness of the sector, and 5) Measures in the field of training and professional qualification. 

The document details extra spending for 1) the MOVES programme, including on public transport, charging points, shared electric bikes schemes, 2) replacing state's car fleet to zero-emission vehicles, 3) research in sustainable mobility, 4) scrap old cars to buy ecologically-friendly new cars, and 5) training in transport-related new technologies.
Document Title: Plan to promote the value chain of the automotive industry

Family Name: Agricultural Sector Policy Framework (MPSA) 2020–2030
Family Summary:
The Agricultural Sector Policy Framework (MPSA) 2020–2030 provides a national roadmap for Paraguay’s agrarian sector, integrating environmental, social, and economic dimensions along with agro-industry. It focuses on three main pillars: developing competitive markets for agricultural, livestock, and forestry products; securing access to rural land through property regularization; and strengthening public support services such as research, extension, animal and plant health, land governance, and financing.

It includes issues related to climate change mitigation and adaptation, such as working on the development of a program that includes varieties adapted to climate and soil conditions, as well as improvements in rice production. Additionally, it also includes the design of mechanisms for implementing better agronomic and soil management practices and promotes sustainable forestry practices, afforestation and reforestation for energy purposes, and the valorization of native forests through mechanisms like international carbon credit sales.

The policy framework was approved by Resolution 466/2020.
Document Title: Marco de Politica del Sector Agropecuario (MPSA) 2020–2030

Family Name: Sweden's sovereign green bond framework
Family Summary:
The framework for Swedish sovereign green bonds was developed in accordance with the guidelines in the Green Bond Principles: (1) use of proceeds and eligible green expenditures; (2) process for project evaluation and selection; (3) management of proceeds; (4) reporting; and (5) external reviews. 

(1) Examples of eligible expenditures are those aimed at mitigating climate change, strengthening biodiversity, promoting renewable energy projects or reducing carbon emissions in the transport sector. Not included are expenditures related to nuclear energy, fossil energy, new investments in large-scale hydro power or exclusively administrative appropriations. 

(2) The evaluation and selection process comprises three steps. First, the conditions for the use of the expenditure must fulfil certain criteria. The use must significantly contribute to at least one of the environmental quality objectives; and it must not significantly counteract another environmental quality objective; lastly, it must be highly likely that the use will contribute to long-term net positive environmental results and impacts. Second, the recommendation of eligible green expenditures is being prepared at the Government Offices. Third, the portfolio with eligible green expenditures is established through a government decision.

(3)  The Swedish National Debt Office is responsible for issuing Swedish sovereign green bonds. The proceeds are monitored and documented by the National Debt Office according to special procedures and administered within the regular liquidity and debt management .

(4) The Swedish National Debt Office must publish investor reports. 

(5) The Center for International Climate and Environmental Research, appointed by the Government Offices, has evaluated this framework and issued a second party opinion.
Document Title: Sweden's sovereign green bond framework
