Family Name: National Climate Change Research Policy 2020-2030
Family Summary:
This Policy's vision is that the best available science and evidence support the decisions that Saint Lucia’s institutions and people make to build resilience to climate change.

This Policy seeks to ensure that climate change-focused scientific research efforts conducted in the country address adaptation, mitigation, as well as loss and damage questions of national priority, offer high-quality data and information to support sectoral and cross-sectoral decision-making and outreach processes, and increase the capacity of Saint Lucia’s institutions to effectively execute the country’s climate change agenda. It establishes simple procedures to streamline the process of request and execution of research collaboration efforts on climate change issues between the GoSL and interested actors, to foster collaboration that contributes toward strengthening national research and technical capacities (e.g., capacities for the systematic observation and monitoring of climate, environmental and socioeconomic information) and to ensure that the country has access to and benefits from the results of all climate change-related research conducted in/on its territory.
Document Title: National Climate Change Research Policy 2020-2030

Family Name: Medium-Term Development Strategy 2020-2023
Family Summary:
This Strategy aims to:

  1. Achieve a higher rate of economic growth, which will generate jobs and energise the private sector as a whole and micro small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in particular;
  2. Increase the resilience of both Saint Lucia’s economy and its society to both economic and natural disaster-related exogenous shocks;
  3. Ensure that all subgroupings of the Saint Lucian society are adequately accommodated and represented in the development process;
  4. Place the country's economy on a high growth path without compromising its fiscal position and environmental conditions; and
  5. Ensure that all members of the society enjoy the benefits that will be derived from robust economic growth.

It contains sections on disaster risk management, resilience and sustainable development in response to climate change; efforts to promote cleaner energy to combat climate change; and reducing the exposure of the agricultural sector to climate change and climate variability.
Document Title: Medium-Term Development Strategy 2020-2023

Family Name: Gender and Social Inclusion Action Plan for Climate Change Policy 2020-2030
Family Summary: This Policy aims to mainstream gender and social inclusion in policy formulation, institutional structures, and program implementation related to climate change. It emphasises facilitating livelihood enhancement by integrating and simplifying gender and social inclusion considerations. Furthermore, based on the experiences gained from various studies and research, as well as recommendations derived from different practices in the field of adaptation, a deeper analysis has been conducted in Nepal's climate change policies. This analysis aims to comprehensively address the various societal, economic, and political aspects to address social justice issues as high priorities.
Document Title: Gender and Social Inclusion Action Plan for Climate Change Policy 2020-2030

Family Name: National Action Plan on Gender and Climate Change
Family Summary:
The main goal of this Plan is to ensure that national climate change efforts in Nigeria mainstream gender considerations so that women, men, youth and other vulnerable groups can have access to, participate in, contribute to and hence optimally benefit from climate change initiatives, programs, policies and funds. It serves as a guide for states and local governments to mainstream geneder considerations to address climate change challenges in Nigeria, and is meant to be socialised through Climate Change desk offices in states and subsequently cascaded to local communities.

This Plan focuses on the priority sectors of agriculture, forestry and land use; food security and health, energy and transport, waste management; and water and sanitation.
Document Title: National Action Plan on Gender and Climate Change

Family Name: National Plan For Integrated Management of Urban Solid Waste
Family Summary: The National Plan for Integrated Management of Urban Solid Waste is a nationwide strategy aimed at improving quality of life and ensuring a healthy environment for Paraguay’s urban populations by 2030. It is structured around five key strategies: strengthening the institutional framework for waste management; expanding universal access to urban sanitation services; promoting waste prevention, reuse, and treatment; ensuring proper final disposal through sanitary landfills while closing and remediating open dumps; and advancing community environmental education, training, and technological development.
Document Title: National Plan For Integrated Management of Urban Solid Waste

Family Name: National Policy on Conservation and Sustainable Utilization of Mangrove Ecosystems (2020)
Family Summary: The policy acknowledges the centrality of mangrove systems in coastal climate adaptation and mitigation, as well as their broader ecosystem services, and aims to promote their protection and restoration nationally. It also encourages the development of voluntary carbon market integration for Sri Lanka's mangroves and their restoration efforts.
Document Title: National Policy on Conservation and Sustainable Utilization of Mangrove Ecosystems (2020)

Family Name: Green and Inclusive Community Buildings Program
Family Summary:
In 2020, the Government of Canada announced up to $1.5 billion in federal funding over five years to establish the Green and Inclusive Community Buildings (GICB) program. The GICB Program supports retrofits, repairs or upgrades of existing publicly-accessible community buildings and the construction of new publicly-accessible community buildings for underserved and high-needs communities across Canada.

It supports the first pillar of the Strengthened Climate Plan (named A Healthy Environment and a Healthy Economy), by improving the places where Canadians live and gather – which will cut pollution, make life more affordable and create thousands of jobs in construction.

On April 16, 2024, the Government of Canada released Budget 2024 which provided a $500 million top-up and extended the program until March 2029.
Document Title: Green and Inclusive Community Buildings Program

Family Name: Offshore Emissions Reduction Fund
Family Summary:
This Fund is a $75 million offshore investment as part of the Emissions Reduction Fund (ERF) that helps Canada meet its environmental commitments, rebuild the economy, and create a lower carbon economy, especially towards reducing greenhouse gas emissions (GHGs), in the oil and gas industry. The offshore portion of the ERF has two components:

  • The Offshore Deployment Program is a $42 million investment supporting capital projects designed to either reduce offshore GHGs or improve the environmental performance of offshore oil spill monitoring, detection and response activities.
  • The Offshore RDD Program is a $33 million investment supporting research, development and demonstration projects that advance solutions to decarbonize Newfoundland and Labrador’s offshore industry. It is being delivered in collaboration with Energy Research Innovation Newfoundland Labrador.
Document Title: ERF Offshore Deployment Program

Family Name: Offshore Emissions Reduction Fund
Family Summary:
This Fund is a $75 million offshore investment as part of the Emissions Reduction Fund (ERF) that helps Canada meet its environmental commitments, rebuild the economy, and create a lower carbon economy, especially towards reducing greenhouse gas emissions (GHGs), in the oil and gas industry. The offshore portion of the ERF has two components:

  • The Offshore Deployment Program is a $42 million investment supporting capital projects designed to either reduce offshore GHGs or improve the environmental performance of offshore oil spill monitoring, detection and response activities.
  • The Offshore RDD Program is a $33 million investment supporting research, development and demonstration projects that advance solutions to decarbonize Newfoundland and Labrador’s offshore industry. It is being delivered in collaboration with Energy Research Innovation Newfoundland Labrador.
Document Title: ERF Offshore RD&D Program

Family Name: National Strategic Plan 2020-2030
Family Summary:
This Plan provides a roadmap for progress in the Marshall Islands' priorities in strategic areas of social services and cultural identity, economic development, infrastructure, environmental awareness, climate change and governance.

For climate change, the goal is to have a holistic response to climate change for sustainable social and economic development and the well-being of the Marshall Islands and its people. Policy objectives include adaptation and resilience, mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions to pursue net zero emissions by 2050; increased climate finances to enable the necessary response to climate change impacts; and strong advocacy, diplomacy and regional/global leadership to enhance urgent global climate action.

On adaptation, the Plan states that the Marshall Islands is considering whether to relocate all 55,000 citizens, by understanding the risks atoll by atoll.
Document Title: National Strategic Plan 2020-2030

Family Name: National Energy Efficiency and Conservation Strategy
Family Summary: This Strategy establishes targets in the five thematic sectors to be accomplished within a five-year timeline up to 2025. The sectors are household; buildings; industry and agriculture; transport; and utilities. Energy efficiency is viewed as key to achieving Kenya's climate mitigation targets.
Document Title: National Energy Efficiency and Conservation Strategy

Family Name: Bioenergy Strategy (2020–2027)
Family Summary: This Strategy covers solid biomass fuels, liquid biofuels and gaseous biofuels. The goals for this Strategy are to promote sustainable production and consumption of bioenergy to accelerate the transition to clean cooking technologies and fuels; to provide potential investors with requisite information on viable opportunities for bioenergy development in Kenya; and to serve as a framework for regional and international cooperation and trade in bioenergy and related feedstocks.
Document Title: Bioenergy Strategy (2020–2027)

Family Name: "MaPrimeRénov" Program
Family Summary:
The Decree No. 2020‑26 of 14 January 2020 established the “prime à la transition énergétique”, now known as "MaPrimeRénov" Programme. This decree set up the rules governing eligibility, eligible works, and the application process for the programme.

This "MaPrimeRénov" Programme aims at helping low-income individuals and households to renovate their housings in order to make them more energy efficient and better isolated. Family Summary:
The National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. 

The plan aims to define measures adapted to different dimensions: 1) decarbonisation dimension: reduction of GHG emissions by 35% in 2030 compared to 2005 for non-ET sectors, a Belgian contribution of 17.4% of renewable energies compared to gross final energy consumption; 2) energy efficiency dimension : Belgium has set a contribution to the European target of 32.5% by 2030 (15% in primary energy and 12% in final energy); 3) energy security dimension : one of the most important challenges for Belgium, in the short and medium term. Family Name: Building Regulations 2018 (BR18)
Family Summary:
These Regulations introduce mandatory lifecycle CO2 assessment and stricter limit values for CO2.

In 2023, the first phase of new requirements was introduced into the Danish building regulations which defined a threshold limit value of 12kg CO2e/m2/year for new buildings larger than 1,000m2. This threshold value comprised building related greenhouse gas emissions from particular life cycle phases (A1-A3, B4, B6, C3, and C4). Phase two, which came into force in 2025, updated the framework and lowered the limits, with two more phases coming in 2027 and 2029.

The required climate impact reporting will now be based on the following life cycle phases: A1-A5 (construction), B4, B6 (use), C3, C4 (end-of-life), and D (reuse, recovery and recycling potential). However, the requirements must be met without including the possible gains from stage D. Furthermore, the construction phase emissions from A4 and A5 must be calculated and reported separately and have its own limit value of 1.5 kgCO2e/m2/year.
Document Title: Building Regulations (BR18)

Family Summary:
The objective of this Plan is to guide the design, coordination, prioritisation and implementation of policies, programs and projects that address the particular climate vulnerability of the agricultural production systems in Uruguay.
In doing so, a shift towards a resilient and adapted development path for agriculture is proposed that includes co-benefits of productivity and climate mitigation.

The overall aim is to improve the livelihoods of rural populations. To this end, a Strategy with an outlook to 2050 is advanced which considers four key areas:
  1. Production systems;
  2. Ecosystems and natural resources;
  3. Livelihoods;
  4. Institutional capacities.

Next to the 2050 Strategy, a 2025 Action Plan is proposed to achieve these goals. 

66 (short term) adaptation measures are established, inter alia considering the following key issues:
  • Research and development;
  • Technology transfer;
  • Information systems;
  • Climate insurances;
  • Resilient infrastructure;
  • Promotion of good farming practices;
  • Strengthening farmer's networks and organisations; and
  • Enhancing institutional capacities for adaptation.

Family Name: Colombian Low-Carbon Development Strategy
Family Summary: The Colombian Low-Carbon Development Strategy (ECDBC) was launched in February 2012 as a tool to deliver the objectives of the National Development Plan 2011-2014 and the CONPES Document on Climate Change by promoting efficient low-carbon growth. It foresees the identification of a GHG emissions baseline and the formulation and implementation of low-carbon development plans for the sectors of energy, mining, agriculture, transport, industry, waste and construction. The ECDBC (Strategic Framework for the Integrated Management of National Climate Change) is an intersectoral planning and implementation process for the comprehensive management of national climate change. The goal is to facilitate the planning, implementation, and capacity building in various ministries to achieve the country’s climate goals for the short, medium, and long term, aimed at achieving carbon neutrality and climate resilience within the framework of sustainable development. These goals are defined in the National Development Plans (PND), Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC), and the Long-Term Climate Strategy (E2050).The strategy is divided into 4 phases. At the end of phase 2 – Planning (2019-2023), medium- and long-term climate scenarios and targets were updated, incorporating adaptation, cross-cutting approaches, and climate justice in the public policy tools and strategies for climate change. The phase 3 is called present and runs from 2024 to 2030 and the phase 4, future, from 2030 to 2050.
Document Title: Colombian Low-Carbon Development Strategy Updated

Family Name: National Strategy for the implementation of the 2030 Agenda in Mexico (Estrategia Nacional para la implementación de la Agenda 2030 en México)
Family Summary: Mexico's National Strategy for the 2030 Agenda establishes a framework for sustainable development, placing climate change action as a central pillar. It commits to transitioning towards a low-greenhouse-gas emission development model by 2030, prioritising sustainable natural resource management, clean and renewable energy adoption, and the integration of climate resilience into economic growth. The strategy underscores alignment with international objectives to limit global temperature increase to below 2°C and pursue efforts towards 1.5°C, emphasising the urgency of both mitigating emissions and adapting to climate impacts to safeguard ecosystems, communities, and future prosperity.The policy details specific climate-focused measures, including strengthening ecosystem adaptation through protected area management, reforestation, and community-based adaptation plans; promoting low-carbon technologies and processes across industry, energy, and waste sectors via regulations, incentives, and carbon pricing mechanisms; and consolidating institutional coordination through the National Climate Change System (SINACC) to ensure policy coherence and effective implementation across all government levels. It further stresses inclusivity, integrating gender and human rights perspectives to address disproportionate climate vulnerabilities, and highlights the mobilisation of public and private finance—through strategic investment, insurance mechanisms, and international cooperation—to support mitigation, adaptation, and disaster risk reduction efforts.
Document Title: National Strategy for the implementation of the 2030 Agenda in Mexico. Family Name: Denmark’s Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan
Family Summary:
The National Energy and Climate (ENCP) Plan is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets.  

The plan exposes the key objectives and its measures : 
1) decarbonisation : reduction of GHG emissions, transport green transition with a stop to sales of all new diesel and petrol cars as of 2030, ban on burning of straw residues on fields, public afforestation and a grant scheme for afforestation on private agricultural land and subsidy for conversion of arable land on organic soils to nature, etc; 
2) renewable energy : three new offshore wind farms of at least 800 MW each, reduction of the electrical heating tax and of the electricity tax, support of geothermal energy, etc; 
3) energy efficiency : to build a competitive subsidy scheme related to private enterprises, efficiency of existing buildings through renovation, etc; 
4) energy security : stable energy supply thanks to laws on responsibilities regarding electricity supply, gas supply and emergency plans, prevention of risks in the energy system, increased international cooperation, interconnectivity concerning energy supply.

  • Ensuring the efficient use of water resources

  • Developing aquaculture and water management plans
  • Implementing flood risk management strategies
  • Managing coastal zones
  • Preventing and responding to forest fires
  • Promoting sustainable food production and farm management
  • Optimising agricultural land use

Family Name: Decree-Law 345/2019 on the development of renewable energy
Family Summary:
The purpose of this Decree-Law is to establish regulations for the development of renewable sources and the efficient use of energy, in order to contribute to:

a) Increasing the share of renewable energy sources in electricity generation;

b) The progressive replacement of fossil fuels;

c) The diversification of the structure of fossil fuels used in electricity generation;

d) Increasing energy efficiency and savings;

e) the stimulation of investment, research, and the increase in energy efficiency, as well as the production and use of energy from renewable sources, through the establishment of incentives and other instruments that stimulate their development;

f) the development of the production of equipment, resources, and spare parts by the national industry for the use of renewable sources and energy efficiency; and

g) the establishment of a work system in the state sector, which includes the planning of tasks that enable the achievement of the established objectives.

The Cuban government stated in its 2024 Biennial Transparency Report that a fundamental transformation of the national legal framework occurred with the promulgation of this Decree-Law. Future expansion of the national electricity system's (SEN) generation will be essentially based on the increase in renewable energy sources, the strengthening of conventional thermal generation, and the increase in combined cycle gas generation capacity from petroleum-based natural gas.
Document Title: Decree-Law 345/2019 on the development of renewable energy

Family Name: Proposed Methodology for Estimation of Electricity Generated from Biomass in Biomass Co-fired Thermal Power Plants
Family Summary:
Ministry of Power, Government of India, vide letter No. 11/86/2017-Th11 dated 17th November 2017 has issued the "Policy for Biomass Utilization for Power Generation through Co-firing in Pulverized Coal Fired Boilers" wherein it is envisaged that fluidized bed and pulverized coal units shall endeavour to use 5-10% blend of biomass pellets made, primarily of agro residue along with coal. in order to promote co-firing of biomass in thermal power plants, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Government of India, vide its notification dated 26.9.2019 has clarified that the power generated from co-firing of biomass in thermal power plants is renewable energy and is eligible for meeting non-solar Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) and has requested this Commission to formulate and notify the procedure/methodology for quantifying the energy produced from biomass in biomass co-fired thermal power plants in a reliable and accurate manner.

In 2022 this policy was updated to set a mandatory minimum use of 7% biomass pellets.
Document Title: Proposed Methodology for Estimation of Electricity Generated from Biomass in Biomass Co-fired Thermal Power Plants

Family Name: Royal decree-law 17/2019 establishing the new rate of reasonable return for renewable energy
Family Summary: The royal decree-law introduces a series of measures aimed at guaranteeing a stable regulatory and economic framework to encourage the development of renewable energy generation in Spain. The act aims 1) to update certain remuneration parameters of generation plants with a specific remuneration system, including additional remuneration for generation plants located in non-peninsular electricity systems, before the start of the next regulatory period on 1 January 2020, and 2) to adopt a new regulation governing access to the network in nodes affected by the closure of coal and thermonuclear power plants and concessions for the private use of water after the closure of these generation plants where new renewable generation projects may offer an alternative. More specificly, the royal decree-law introduces a number of amendments relating to the reasonable cost effectiveness of installations producing electricity from renewable sources: 1) the reasonable return on the remaining regulatory lifetime of installations producing electricity from renewable energy sources is set at 7.09% for the second regulatory period (from 1 January 2020), 2) the financial remuneration rate for production activity in non-peninsular electricity systems with an additional remuneration system will be 5.58% for the second regulatory period.The royal decree-law also amends Electricity Sector Act to maintain the existing reasonable rate of return for renewable energy electricity production plants which were already in operation before the passing of Royal Decree-Law 9/2013, of 12 July, which adopts measures to guarantee the financial stability of the electricity system (RDL 9/2013). The reasonable rate of return is guaranteed for the next two regulatory periods.The document introduces a 22nd Additional Provision of the Electricity Sector Act in respect of access and connection rights connected to coal and thermonuclear plants set for closure.
Document Title: Royal decree-law 17/2019 establishing the new rate of reasonable return for renewable energy

Family Name: Board of Directors Resolution No. 039-2019-SUNASS-CD. Approves the new Directive on Mechanisms for the Remuneration of Water Ecosystem Services (Resolución de Consejo Directivo N.° 039-2019-SUNASS-CD. Aprueba la nueva Directiva de Mecanismos de Retribución por Servicios ecosistémicos Hídricos)
Family Summary: This directive, issued by Peru’s Superintendencia Nacional de Servicios de Saneamiento (SUNASS), establishes a regulatory framework for sanitary companies (Empresas Prestadoras de Servicios de Saneamiento "EPS") to design, implement, and compensate for ecosystem services retribution (Mecanismos de Retribución por Servicios Ecosistémicos Hídricos "MRSE Hídricos"). Aligned with Peru’s international climate commitments under the Paris Agreement, the policy aims to incentivise water ecosystem service management by integrating MRSE Hídricos into EPS’s Planes Maestros Optimizados (PMO) and sanitation tariffs. Key elements include hydrological resource diagnosis, intervention planning, good governance platforms, stakeholder characterisation, and hydrological monitoring systems. The ecosystem services retribution (MRSE Hídricos) are positioned as a tool to reconcile service delivery with ecological sustainability, requiring EPS to identify intervention areas (e.g., watersheds, sources) and align projects with climate adaptation and disaster risk management strategies (article 15).
Document Title: Board of Directors Resolution approving the new "Directive on Remuneration Mechanisms for Water Ecosystem Services implemented by Sanitation Service Providers" - Board of Directors Resolution No. 039-2019-SUNASS-CD (Resolución de Consejo Directivo que aprueba la nueva “Directiva de Mecanismos de Retribución por Servicios Ecosistémicos Hídricos implementados por las Empresas Prestadoras de Servicios de Saneamiento” - Resolución de Consejo Directivo N° 039-2019-SUNASS-CD)

Family Summary: This resolution approves the National Contribution Objectives for the Implementation of the Paris Agreement. It also charges the Minister of Nature, Environment and Tourism  to approve the action plan for the implementation of the objectives, submit it to the Secretariat of the UN Framework Convention and provide integrated management and organisation for further implementation. Family Name: National Climate Change Response Strategy
Family Summary:
The National Climate Change Response Strategy (NCCRS) provides a framework for a comprehensive and strategic approach to climate change adaptation, mitigation, technology and finance. The objective of the Strategy is to 'mainstream climate change adaptation and mitigation strategies in economic and social development at national and sectoral levels through multi-stakeholder engagement'.
The Strategy mainly aims to help the country and its citizens to adapt to severe droughts, increasing temperatures, irregular rainfall patterns and food shortages, attributed in part to climate change effects.
The risks and impacts of climate change are analysed in the NCCRS, followed by sectoral strategies (agriculture, energy, water, etc.), with varying implementation timeframes. The seven pillars of climate change responses are:


  • adaptation and disaster risk management

  • mitigation and low carbon development strategies

  • capacity

  • governance framework

  • finance and investment

  • technology development and transfer, including infrastructure

  • communication and advocacy


The Plan also recommends establishing a National Climate Fund to tackle the impacts of climate change, with need for financing evaluated at more than USD 9.9 billion over the next 5 to 10 years
Document Title: National Climate Change Response Strategy

Family Name: National Forest Policy
Family Summary:
The National Forest Policy has four objectives:

  1. Provide forest areas respecting the balance of ecosystems and utilisation;
  2. Stop and prevent the destruction of forests and biodiversity;
  3. Ensure the conservation and utilisation of forest resources, wildlife and biodiversity;
  4. Efficient forest resource management system based on knowledge and innovation including participation of all sectors. 

The Policy sets the goal of designating an area for forests that accounts for at least 40% of the country's area. Furthermore, conserved forests should not be less than 25% of the country's area, and economic and community forests should not be less than 15% of the country's area.
Document Title: National Forest Policy

Family Name: Agreement on the Distribution of Research Reserves 2020
Family Summary: With this Agreement, the Government and a broad majority in Parliament decided to allocate DKK 700 million to establish four green research missions under the auspices of the Innovation Fund. This included a mission focusing on capture, storage and utilization of CO2 under the name “Inno-CCUS”.  The mission aims to develop cost-effective CO2 capture and storage solutions that can be used to reduce CO2 emissions and create negative emissions from large industrial emitters, waste incineration plants, biogas plants and biomass-based CHP installations.
Document Title: Agreement on the Distribution of Research Reserves 2020

Family Name: Woodland Carbon Guarantee - carbon capture
Family Summary:
The Woodland Carbon Guarantee is an incentive scheme to help accelerate woodland planting rates across England. These new woodlands will permanently remove CO2 from the atmosphere.

The guaranteed price for your CO2 is agreed with the government through an online reverse auction. In order to bid in the auction, the applicant need to calculate how much money will be needed(per tonne of CO2) to the planting project be viable and worthwhile. If the bid is successful in the auction, the government will buy the CO2 for the bid price.
Document Title: Getting Started with the Woodland Carbon Guarantee

Family Summary: This document was endorsed and adopted by the Nauruan Cabinet on 27 November 2019 as a guide to public infrastructure investment planning and budgeting. Document Title: Nauru Integrated Infrastructure Strategic Plan

Family Name: India's National Disaster Management Plan
Family Summary:
The National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) provides a framework and direction to government agencies for all phases of disaster management cycle. It notably covers disasters provoked by climate change effects.

The NDMP has five main pillars:
  1. Conforming to the naonal legal mandates—the DM Act 2005 and the NPDM 2009
  2. Participating proactively to realising the global goals as per agreements to which India is signatory—Sendai Framework for DRR, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) an Conference of Parties (COP21) Paris Agreement on Climate Change
  3. Prime Minister’s Ten Point Agenda for DRR arculang contemporary national priorities
  4. Social inclusion as a ubiquitous and cross-cutting principle
  5. Mainstreaming DRR as an integral feature
Document Title: India's National Disaster Management Plan

Family Name: Czechia National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary: The National Energy and Climate (ENCP) Plan is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets.   The main part of the National Plan is the setting of the Czech Republic’s contribution to the European climate and energy targets concerning the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, the increase in the share of renewable energy sources and increase of energy efficiency. Quantified objectives are provided for in the plan. There are three energy efficiency-related targets for the period 2021–2030: 1) an indicative target for the size of primary energy sources, final consumption and energy intensity; 2) a binding energy savings target for public sector building, 3) a binding year-on-year rate of final consumption savings.
Document Title: National Energy and Climate Plan of the Czech Republic

Family Name: Netherlands Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 2021-2030
Family Summary: The National Energy and Climate (NECP) Plan is a ten-year integrated document mandated by the European Union to each of its member states in order for the EU to meet its overall greenhouse gases emissions targets. The Energy and Climate Plan addresses all five dimensions of the EU Energy Union: decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security, internal energy markets and research, innovation and competitiveness. The plan establishes the following objectives : 1) reduction of greenhouse gas emissions with renewable energy and energy saving; 2) combating climate change with a climate-neutral electricity system. The limited availability of renewable sources in the Netherlands is an important point of concern. Since the Netherlands is located along the coast and the wind is relatively strong, this offers potential for wind energy on land and offshore; 3) a transition to an emission-free mobility system that involves sustainable energy carriers (electricity, biofuels and green hydrogen); 4) homes and other building will be made more energy-efficient in a sustainable transformation of the built-up environment; 5) to promote a robust and sustainable agriculture which adopts a more efficient approach to raw materials and the environment.
Document Title: Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan

Family Name: Australia's National Hydrogen Strategy
Family Summary:
This Strategy was first published in 2019 and then refreshed in 2024. It sets a vision for a clean, innovative, safe and competitive hydrogen industry and aims to position the country as a major player by 2030. New policies including the Hydrogen Production Tax Incentive and an expanded Hydrogen Headstart program, position Australia as one of the best places in the world to make green hydrogen.

Under the 2024 Strategy, the Australian Government is investing around $500 million to support the development of hydrogen hubs in regional Australia, where producers, users and exporters of hydrogen work side by side to share infrastructure and expertise and help the hydrogen industry springboard to scale.
Document Title: 2024 National Hydrogen Strategy

Family Name: Operational Programme Quality of Environment (2014-2020)
Family Summary: The Operational Programme Quality of Environment (OP QE) of the Slovak Republic for the 2014–2020 programming period focused on sustainable and efficient resource use, environmental protection, climate change adaptation, and the promotion of a low-carbon, energy-efficient economy. Aligned with the Europe 2020 strategy and the Slovak National Reform Programme, the OP QE addressed national and regional challenges through a targeted investment strategy. This strategy incorporated three thematic objectives: shifting to a low-carbon economy, promoting climate change adaptation and risk management, and preserving the environment while enhancing resource efficiency.

Family Summary:
The roadmap is meant to act as the guiding tool for implementation of the EEC Policy and enabling integration into the 12th Five Year Plan (July 2018- June 2023) and subsequent five-year plans. It will also form the basis for the national process to review progress in the implementation of EEC measures.

The roadmap includes the target of reducing 1.8 MtCO2e through energy efficiency measures over the course of 15 years.
Document Title: Energy Efficiency Roadmap

Family Summary: This policy aims to lower the energy intensity of Bhutan's economy through demand-side management measures. It estimates that planned measures could save up to 155 kWh annually.
Document Title: National Energy Efficiency and Conservation (EE&C) Policy

Family Name: National Guidelines for Preparation of Action Plan - Prevention and Management of Heat Wave
Family Summary: To respond to increasing frequency and intensity of heatwaves, these guidelines provide a framework to evaluate impacts of heat waves and plan adaptation and mitigation strategies for prevention and preparedness.
Document Title: National Guidelines for Preparation of Action Plan - Prevention and Management of Heat Wave

Family Name: Decree No. 2019-1931 The Regional Spatial Planning Scheme (SRAT)
Family Summary: Decree No. 2019-1931 relates to the appraisal, preparation, validation and implementation of the The Regional Spatial Planning Scheme (SRAT), to be drawn up or revised at the initiative of a region. It includes (Article 6) that the SRAT shall take into account measures for the protection against climate risks and disasters, and adaptation, as well as the specific needs of each sector of economic and strategic development. The SRAT includes a territorial analysis, a regional outlook, and a strategic plan. The process of creating the regional land-use plan (Article 7) shall take into account the obligation to refer to the specifications of the SRAT Guide, considering the issues of resilience and adaptation to climate change in spatial planning.
Document Title: Decree No. 2019-1931 The Regional Spatial Planning Scheme (SRAT)

Family Name: Concept of Environmental Protection in the Republic of Uzbekistan until 2030
Family Summary: The Concept of Environmental Protection in the Republic of Uzbekistan until 2030 sets an overarching long-term direction for sustainably managing the natural environment and its resources. Among eight core approaches, the Concept names international co-operation on climate change action as a priority area. It emphasises the need to combat land degradation and water scarcity, to alleviate domestic climate issues, and to reduce emissions, contributing to international mitigation efforts.
Document Title: Concept of Environmental Protection in the Republic of Uzbekistan until 2030

Family Summary: The resolution 103/2019 approves the National Strategy for Electric Mobility (ENME) and creates the Inter-institutional Commission for Electric Mobility (CIME). The Commission's goal is to implement ENME. The strategy sets a number of electrification targets for 2030 and aims at reaching them through improvements in governance, normative action, focusing on strategic sectors and raise knowledge and education.

Family Name: Disaster Ready Fund Act 2019
Family Summary:
This Act establishes the Disaster Ready Fund, which will enhance Australia's ability to make arrangements with persons or bodies in relation to natural disasters; and make grants to persons or bodies in relation to natural disasters.

The Disaster Ready Fund consists of the Disaster Ready Fund Special Account; and the investments of the Disaster Ready Fund. The Future Fund Board is responsible for deciding how to invest the Disaster Ready Fund. In doing so, the Future Fund Board is bound by the Disaster Ready Fund Investment Mandate given to it by the responsible Ministers.

The Emergency Management Minister may, on behalf of the Commonwealth: make an arrangement with a person or body in relation to a natural disaster; and make a grant to a person or body in relation to a natural disaster.

This Act establishes the Disaster Ready Fund Payments Special Account. Amounts will be transferred from the Disaster Ready Fund Special Account to the Disaster Ready Fund Payments Special Account. The purposes of the Disaster Ready Fund Payments Special Account are to pay amounts payable by the Commonwealth under arrangements relating to a natural disaster, and to make grants relating to a natural disaster. Amounts will be transferred from the Disaster Ready Fund Special Account to the Federation Reform Fund for the purposes of making grants to the States and Territories in relation to natural disasters.
Document Title: Disaster Ready Fund Investment Mandate Direction 2020

Family Name: National Strategy 2018-2037
Family Summary: This Strategy is developed in accordance with Section 65 of the Constitution of the Kingdom of Thailand, which stipulates that the State should develop a national strategy in accordance with the principle of goood governance. The National Strategy is (2018-2037) is the country’s first national long-term strategy to ensure that the country achieves its vision of becoming “a developed country with security, prosperity and sustainability in accordance with the Sufficiency Economy Philosophy” with the ultimate goal being all Thai people’s happiness and well-being. The Strategy considers Thailand's national development in the light of unpredictable and abrupt impacts of climate change. It includes solutions such as smart farming; increasing value of a maritime bioeconomy; and promoting climate-friendly growth and infrastructure development.

Family Summary: The overarching principle of this policy is to minimise the natural resources and toxic materials used, and the waste and pollutants generated, throughout the entire production and consumption process in all economic sectors. It notably aims to mainstream climate and disaster resilience into the management of water and sanitation, into the development of energy, industry and tourism sectors. It also seeks to promote disaster and climate resilient buildings and constructions.

Family Name: Executive Decree No. 19-280 establishing the Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Commission (20 October 2019)
Family Summary:
The Executive Decree No. 19-280 of 21 Safar 1441, corresponding to 20 October 2019, establishes the creation, organisation, and operation of the Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Commission. This Commission reports to the Prime Minister and is develops renewable energy and energy efficiency measures, to provide energy security in economic development, environmental preservation, and the fight against climate change.

The Commission is also responsible for ensuring, in liaison with the reelvant secotrs, the implementation, monitoring and evaluation of Algeria's commitments under international conventions and agreements in the areas of combatting the effects of climate change and achieving sustainable development goals.
Document Title: Executive Decree No. 19-280 establishing the Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Commission (20 October 2019)

Family Name: National Transport Policy 2019-2030
Family Summary:
The policy aims to develop a sustainable transport sector that accelerates economic growth while lowering carbon emissions. It promotes the adoption of energy-efficient and electric vehicles, as well as the necessary infrastructure, such as charging stations. The policy emphasises the development of public transportation systems as a primary feature in urban areas to reduce reliance on private, fossil-fuel-powered vehicles. Additionally, it encourages the use of cleaner fuels and electric vehicles. The policy also includes education and public engagement initiatives designed to shift user behaviour toward more sustainable transport modes and practices.

The policy seeks to achieve the following objectives:

1. Create a supportive ecosystem for the transport industry to enhance productivity and competitiveness.

2. Facilitate the seamless movement of goods to boost trading activities and improve the ease of doing business.

3. Provide mobility solutions that meet the expectations of the people and promote inclusivity.

4. Increase the modal share for public transport.

5. Deliver an intelligent, safe, and secure transport system.

6. Ensure the efficient and sustainable use of resources while minimising environmental pollution.
Document Title: National Transport Policy 2019-2030

Family Name: Integrated Resource Plan
Family Summary:
This plan was originally published in 2010 as a subset of the Integrated Energy Plan. A revised plan was published in October 2019. 

This document sets the government's strategy for its mining and energy sectors. It notably 1) acknowledges the pressure of coal mining on climate change and health, 2) envisions carbon capture and storage as a solution for reducing the sector's externalities, 3) examines a carbon budget approach to enable a low-carbon future, and 4) acknowledges that renewable energy sources are to be considered. The government also commits to a substantial increase in new capacity of wind and solar.
Document Title: Integrated Resource Plan

Family Name: Alternative and Renewable Energy Policy 2019
Family Summary: Pakistan's ARE 2019 sets several overall objectives and some specific targets for the energy sector in the country. The first objective of increasing the share of renewable energy is accompanied by a target of increasing renewable energy generation to 20% by 2025, and then 30% by 2030. Some other objectives of the policy include the indigenization of energy resources and enabling local manufacturing capacity and dispalcement of expensive energy with cheaper renewable sources. The scope of the policy covers almost all sources of renewable energy like biogas, biomass, energy from waste, geothermal, hydrogen, synthetic gas, solar, wind, ocean/tidal wave, storage technologies, and hybrids of any of these.
Document Title: Alternative and Renewable Energy Policy 2019

Family Name: Strategy for Sustainable Rural, Agricultural and Fisheries Development 2030
Family Summary: The Strategy for Sustainable Development of Rural Areas, Agriculture and Fisheries 2030 (SZRWRiR 2030) aims to ensure food security, increase the economic value added from agriculture, and sustainably raise incomes of rural residents while reducing economic, social and territorial disparities and improving the natural environment. The strategy pursues three complementary objectives: strengthening food security and resilience to crises, improving quality of life and environmental conditions, and developing entrepreneurship and non-agricultural employment. It sets out integrated directions of intervention and actions that are financed from national and EU funds, with a strong emphasis on modernisation, innovation, environmental sustainability and increasing sector resilience to climate change.The strategy was adopted by Resolution 123/2019 on 15 October 2019.
Document Title: Resolution 123/2019 adopting the Strategy for Sustainable Rural, Agricultural and Fisheries Development 2030

Family Name: National Disaster Risk Management Plan
Family Summary: The main purpose of Kiribati's National Disaster Risk Management Plan is to provide a framework for effective disaster planning and execution within a DRM structure, where the outcomes of planning are reflected in a sustainable development environment. The plan links together DRM, DRR, and climate change adaptation as part of what it envisions to be a holistic planning process, and explicitly recognizes climate change as a major factor in contributing to Kiribati's vulnerability to disasters. The principal function of the National Disaster Risk Management Plan is to define the phases of disaster risk management in Kiribati, which range from readiness to long-term recovery, as well as the roles and responsibilities of government agencies during each phase. It therefore defines general DRM responsibilities that apply to all government bodies, such as maintaining a log of disaster resources and conducting annual review of DRM arrangements, as well as specific responsibilities, such as requiring the Meteorological Office to monitor threats and advise the Office of Te Beretitenti accordingly.
Document Title: National Disaster Risk Management Plan

Family Name: Climate protection programme 2026 (Klimaschutzprogramm 2026)
Family Summary:
The Federal Government of Germany introduced the 2023 Climate Protection Programme to address a significant climate protection gap of 1.1 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalents by 2030, with a reduction target of 65% of all greenhouse gases compared to 1990 levels. The program encompasses various legislative amendments aimed at achieving these goals. These amendments collectively aimed to bridge the climate protection gap by up to 80%, aligning with Germany's climate targets and commitments under international agreements like the Paris Agreement. However, the German court upheld the lawsuit against the Federal Republic of Germany and determined that the Climate Protection Program must contain all measures necessary to achieve the 2030 climate protection target. The 2023 program does not meet these requirements because, firstly, the forecasts of the greenhouse gas reduction effect of the proposed measures are flawed, and secondly, there is a gap of 200 million tons of CO₂ equivalents that must be closed to achieve the 2030 target.

As a result, in March 2026, the Federal Government adopted the Climate Protection Programme 2026. The programme comprises 90 measures overall aimed at achieving climate neutrality in Germany, 67 of which are targeted at the energy, industry, buildings, transport, and agriculture sectors, with a further 23 measures addressing land use, land-use change, and forestry (LULUCF). Together these measures are projected to cut CO2 emissions by more than 25 million tonnes by 2030, intended to close the gap toward Germany's national 2030 climate target under the Bundes-Klimaschutzgesetz (KSG) and its longer-term 2045 climate-neutrality goal. Eight billion euros in additional funding is earmarked for implementation between 2027 and 2030.
Document Title: Climate protection programme 2030

Family Name: National Strategy for Adaptation to Climate Change of the Republic of Tajikistan for the period up to 2030 (NSACC 2030)
Family Summary: This strategy was approved by the governmental Order 482/2019. It lays out a risk assessment of the sudden and prolonged adverse effects of climate change in the country, with a particular focus on agriculture and land use. The document details sectoral adaptation actions to undertake.
Document Title: National Strategy for Adaptation to Climate Change of the Republic of Tajikistan for the period up to 2030 (NSACC 2030)

Family Name: Vanuatu National Energy Roadmap (2016-2030) implementation plan
Family Summary: Vanuatu's National Energy Roadmap (2016-2030) Implementation Plan aims to make energy accessible, secure, sustainable and affordable, promoting the green growth of the national economy. It primarily supports increased renewable energy installation and the improved electrification of currently off-grid rural areas. Other provisions include energy efficiency projects for transport, household appliances, biomass end-use and diesel electricity generation. The plan also emphasises improved data collection, aiming to build on the success of previous energy usage censuses.
Document Title: Vanuatu National Energy Roadmap (2016-2030) implementation plan

Family Name: 2nd Basic Plan for Climate Change Response
Family Summary:
This document is the overarching national plan for climate actions. It aims to limit the national GHG emissions to 536 MtCO2eq by 2030. To achieve these objectives, the Republic of Korea set out climate mitigation and adaptation measures by sector under its core strategies; transition to a low-carbon society, establishment of a robust adaptation system, and enhancement of a climate change response framework.

This document is mentioned in South Korea's 2nd NDC, but the whole text has not been identified.
Document Title: 2nd Basic Plan for Climate Change Response

Family Name: Burundi's REDD+ National Strategy and Action Plan
Family Summary:
The goal of the strategy is that by 2027, Burundi should be a country with a forest carbon stock, allowing to increase the national economy and improve the living environment of the populations.

Burundi's updated NDC mentions the approval of a revised National Forestry Strategy in 2021, but this document has not been found elsewhere.
Document Title: Burundi's REDD+ National Strategy and Action Plan

Family Name: Marine Strategy Part One: UK updated assessment and Good Environmental Status
Family Summary:
This strategy aims to achieve Good Environmental Status (GES). The 2019 updates of the Strategy's Part One highlights in part 2.3 the importance of blue carbon and nature based solutions for climate mitigation and adaptation efforts, as following:

"We recognise the crucial role of nature-based solutions for climate mitigation and adaptation, such as the protection and restoration of coastal habitats, including seagrass and saltmarsh. The primary purpose of MPAs is to protect biodiversity, protecting coastal and marine habitats. In addition they provide a number of climate related co-benefits for mitigation and adaptation, including improved ocean resilience to the accelerating impacts of climate change, providing coastal protection from erosion and storm surge, and the protection of blue carbon habitats and nursery grounds for species of commercial interest and marine conservation importance. We continue to work on developing methods to assess impacts of climate change on MPAs and with marine industries on environmental net gain."

Part Two of the UK Marine Strategy sets out how progress towards GES will be monitored. Part Three of the UK Marine Strategy outlines the measures that contribute to the achievement and maintenance of GES in UK seas.
Document Title: Marine Strategy Part One: UK updated assessment and Good Environmental Status

Family Name: Charging Infrastructure for Electric Vehicles - Revised Guidelines and Standards
Family Summary:
This policy regulates the construction and operation of EV charging stations to ensure quality standards and compatibility. The Guidelines and Standarrds were first issued on 14 December 2018, with a revision on 1 October 2019 and another revision on 14 January 2022. Minor changes to the guidelines on service charges were made on 7 November 2022.

The objectives are to enable the faster adoption of electric vehicles, amongst others. The 2022 revised consolidated guidelines have the added objective of promoting energy security and the reduction of emission intensity of the country by promoting the entire EV ecosystem. Of note is that individuals and entities are free to set up public charging stations provided that the stations meet the technical, safety and performance standards laid down by the authorities.the Ministry of Power, Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) and Central Electricity Authority (CEA).
Document Title: Charging Infrastructure for Electric Vehicles - Revised Guidelines and Standards (14 January 2022 along with 7 November 2022 amendment)

Family Name: Strategy for Sustainable Transport Development 2030
Family Summary:
The main goal of the national transport policy outlined in the strategy is to increase the country's transport accessibility, improve the safety of road users, and enhance the efficiency of the transport sector by creating a coherent, sustainable, innovative, and user-friendly transport system at the national, European, and global levels. Achieving this goal will foster favorable conditions for the country's stable economic development.

The document also indicates modern solutions that facilitate the functioning of the entire transport sector, reducing its negative impact on the environment and climate, so as to create a sustainable transport system for the country by 2030.The strategy was adopted by Resolution 105/2019 on 24 September 2019.
Document Title: Strategy for Sustainable Transport Development 2030

Family Name: Presidential Decree No. 357/2019 on Renewable Energy Sources
Family Summary: Presidential Decree No. 357/2019 establishes the legal basis for a renewable energy quota system, with energy quotas set by the Council of Ministers, for the enhanced planning and promotion of renewable energy generation. It is primarily targeted at new energy installations, and contains provisions for additional favourable pricing of excess energy when renewable quotas are exceeded by a generator.
Document Title: Presidential Decree No. 357/2019 on Renewable Energy Sources

Family Summary: The RES1 decree supports the production of energy from renewable sources in order to achieve the European targets by 2030 defined in the Integrated National Plan for Energy and Climate. It provides incentives for the diffusion of photovoltaic, wind, hydroelectric and purification gas plants.The aim is to promote the effectiveness, efficiency and sustainability of the sector, both in environmental and economic terms, by promoting the creation of thousands of new jobs through the implementation of a transition to low-carbon energy. It supersedes the Decree 23 June 2016 almost entirely. Article 21 brings the provisions of the mentioned decree that continue in force
Document Title: Ministerial Decree 04 July 2019 ( RES 1 Decree)

Family Name: National disaster risk management plan
Family Summary: This policy presents Botswana's disaster risks and natural hazards, such as flood, drought and wildfire, and discusses the country's institutional and legal framework for disaster reduction. It provides directives on the elaboration of effective national disaster management programme and outlines key definitions, measures and responsibilities for the preparation of disaster management plans at all levels.
Document Title: National disaster risk management plan

Family Name: National Air Pollution Control Programme 2020-2030
Family Summary:
The primary goal of the program is to ensure compliance with the emission reduction obligations for 2020 and 2030 for key air pollutants, including sulfur dioxide (SO₂), nitrogen oxides (NOₓ), non-methane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs), ammonia (NH₃), and fine particulate matter (PM2.5). The program outlines its objectives, the measures required to achieve emission reductions, implementation deadlines, the necessary funding, and the responsible institutions. It focuses on sectors that are major contributors to air pollution, such as agriculture, road transport, and residential heating.

The updated programme strengthens Bulgaria’s national framework for reducing air pollutant emissions in line with EU Directive (EU) 2016/2284 requirements.
Document Title: National Air Pollution Control Programme 2020-2030 (Updated 2025)

Family Name: The National Climate Plan
Family Summary: The National Climate Plan presents an agenda both in terms of mitigation and adaptation, aims to realize sustained economic growth and inclusive social development, while taking due account of climate change related challenges. It provides an overview of climate change vulnerabilities in Algeria and proposes over 70 action measures, including: - adoption of cleaner energy consumption model by substituting liquid fuels by natural gas and liquefied propane; - achieving 35,000 hectares of forests and developing another 175,000 hectares; -waste recovery (13.5 million tonnes / year), - electrification of railway transport and intensification of urban public transport (including constructing the Algiers metro and tramway infrastructure in several cities). The Plan further promotes uptake of renewable energies and sets a target of installing of 22,000 MW of renewable power capacity between 2011 and 2030, divided between 12, 000 MW to be dedicated to cover the national demand for electricity and 10,000 MW for export.
Document Title: The National Climate Plan

Integrating climate change into policies and strategies6. Education and communication7. reinforcing Guinea's meterological services8. Risk reduction and management, including immigration9. Promotion of access to climate financeThe strategy proposes numerous actions and measures to support its overall objectives.
Document Title: National Strategy on Climate Change of Guinea

Family Name: Ghana Infrastructure Plan 2018-2047
Family Summary:
This plan was prepared by the National Development Planning Commission. The extensive, wide-ranging document seeks to provide the country with reliable and robust national energy infrastructure stimulating economic growth, poverty alleviation and general wellbeing, as per the objectives set out in the Long-term National Development Plan (LTNDP). The plan notably aims to develop the production and use of energy from renewable and nuclear sources. It also aims to accommodate the use of electric vehicles and rail.

The document further contains non-mitigation measures, including on housing, food security and disaster risk management. it charges the government to improve drainage, and reduce the risks of flooding and coastal erosion on people, the economy, environment and society.

Family Summary: One of the plan's missions is titled "Meeting the Challenges of Climate Change", and includes plans to:1. Family Name: Climate Resilience Strategy and Action Plan
Family Summary: This plan aims introduces a climate resilience framework to project planning, design and establishment of institutional frameworks concerning road infrastructure in Montenegro. Its key objectives are to decrease the number of road accidents in non-climate resilient road sectors, ensure sustainable maintenance of road infrastructure in line with adaptation costs and other climate resilience measures and prepare in case of severe climate events such as flooding, landslides, rockslides and fires. The plan further identifies technical, regulatory, financial, institutional and social issues that might impede timely solutions to improving the climate resilience aspects of roads in the country.
Document Title: Climate Resilience Strategy and Action Plan

Family Name: Lesotho National Strategic Resilience Framework (2019-2030)
Family Summary:
This Framework guides, coordinate and leads the process of resilience building in the country to ensure that Lesotho finds a durable solution to address the multifaceted challenges posed by climate-induced shocks and stresses. Hazards that affect the country are snowfall, hailstorms, strong winds, localized floods, and early frost. This has resulted in Lesotho experiencing maintained high levels of vulnerability which have compromised food security situation of a majority of the population, especially the rural poor and very poor over the years. The triggers among others have been natural hazards with drought being the main contributor followed by heavy rains and extreme weather variability.

There are 11 pillars which are disaster and climate risk management, capacity development, social protection, access to basic services, sustainable livelihoods, sustainable management of natural resources, and access to economic/financial services, governance for resilience, mainstreaming resilience, research, innovation and development.
Document Title: Lesotho National Strategic Resilience Framework (2019-2030)

Family Name: National Regional Development Strategy
Family Summary: The National Regional Development Strategy (KSRR 2030 - in Polish) is Poland’s key strategic document guiding regional policy through 2030, built around a model of socially sensitive and territorially balanced development that responds to regional disparities and supports inclusive growth. It aims to increase national cohesion by leveraging internal territorial potentials, reducing socio‑economic inequalities between regions (including rural/urban divides), and strengthening the competitive advantages of all areas. To achieve this, the strategy sets three core objectives: reducing development disparities in social, economic, environmental and spatial dimensions; enhancing regional competitive strengths; and improving governance and implementation of territorially focused policies.
Document Title: National Regional Development Strategy

Family Name: Development Cooperation Policy
Family Summary:
This Policy concretises Zimbabwe's vision of inclusive partnerships to further its development agenda and provides a framework for management and coordination in development cooperation. It covers the government's working modalities with various stakeholders, including development partners and civil society.

This Policy states that the government will develop best practices for deploying blended finance in key economic systems and sectors, such as sustainable infrastructure, and address specific issues such as climate change. The government will also strive to form strong partnerships with civil society actors to develop and implement priorities and approaches that promote environmental sustainability for present and future generations, including urgent responses to climate crises, with specific attention to the socio-economic, cultural and indigenous conditions for ecological integrity and justice.
Document Title: Development Cooperation Policy

Family Name: Executive Decree No. 19-226 establishing the missions and organization of the wilaya environmental directorates (13 August 2019)
Family Summary:
Executive Decree No. 19-226 of 12 Dhou El Hidja 1440, corresponding to 13 August 2019, establishes the missions and organisation of the wilaya environmental directorates.

The wilaya environmental directorate is responsible for: designing and implementing, in conjunction with other external services, the wilaya, and the municipality, programs for environmental protection, the promotion, development, and exploitation of renewable energy, and energy management throughout the wilaya; ensuring the implementation of sectoral policies and action programs for environmental protection and the promotion, development, and exploitation of renewable energy; and ensuring the enforcement of current environmental and renewable energy legislation and regulations.

The directorate must participate in any action related to the fight against climate change, in particular, adaptation and mitigation, in relation to the services concerned and promote information, education and awareness-raising actions on the environment and renewable energy.
Document Title: Executive Decree No. 19-226 establishing the missions and organization of the wilaya environmental directorates (13 August 2019)

Family Name: Presidential Regulation 55/2019 on electric vehicles
Family Summary:
This document aims at enabling battery-powered electric vehicles to be made and deployed in Indonesia. It includes two, three and four wheelers. It sets up incentives for local manufacturers, with minimum rates of local components, and aims at expanding the charging infrastructure. The regulation defines and details a fiscal and non-fiscal scheme of incentives for the sector, and determines the electricity supply rates to be applied.

MEMR Regulation no 13/2020 on the Provision of Electric Charging Infrastructure for Battery Electric Vehicle was adopted to implement decision 55/2019.
Document Title: Presidential Regulation 55/2019 on electric vehicles

Family Name: National Energy Policy and Strategies 2019
Family Summary: Sri Lanka's National Energy Policy and Strategy aims to guide the medium to long term development of the energy sector, and notes climate change as a major national threat. The policy contains provisions to avoid emissions by deploying renewable energy, while partially carbon-offsetting existing fossil fuel power generation by planting plantation trees. On renewable energy, it aims to remove bureaucratic obstacles to project deployment, introduce competitive contractor bidding to reduce costs, optimise grid infrastructure for renewable connections, expand energy storage, enhance supply forecasting for intermittent sources, and develop innovative financing instruments.

Family Name: Agreement issuing the General Territorial Tourism Planning Program (Acuerdo que expide el Programa de Ordenamiento Turístico General del Territorio)
Family Summary: The General Tourism Planning Programme of the Territory, enacted by the Secretaría de Turismo (Secretary of Tourism) of Mexico, is a comprehensive policy framework designed to regulate and promote sustainable tourism development across the country. This policy aims to address the spatial distribution and management of tourism activities, ensuring that tourism growth is balanced, sustainable, and beneficial to both the environment and local communities. The program seeks to achieve a more equitable distribution of tourism infrastructure and services, reduce environmental impacts, and enhance resilience to climate change. This Plan incorporates considerations for climate change adaptation and mitigation, recognising the vulnerabilities of many tourist destinations to natural disasters and climate-related risks such as hurricanes, floods, earthquakes, droughts, and coastal erosion. The policy outlines specific actions to protect natural assets, such as beaches, forests, reefs, and biodiversity, and to reduce risks to populations and service providers. It also promotes the implementation of water sustainability projects, adaptation to climate change, and the development of sustainable urban mobility infrastructure. Additionally, the program includes guidelines for energy efficiency in hotels and restaurants and encourages the restoration of the water cycle balance in tourist destinations.
Document Title: Agreement issuing the General Territorial Tourism Planning Program (Acuerdo por el que se expide el Programa de Ordenamiento Turístico General del Territorio)

Family Summary:
This Policy provides overarching guidance for building resilience and mainstreaming climate change into the national development agenda for low-carbon and sustainable growth. This Plan was prepared by the Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines (GoSVG), Ministry of Finance, Economic Planning, Sustainable Development and Information Technology, with technical assistance from the Caribbean Natural Resources Institute (CANARI) under the Organisation for Eastern Caribbean States (OECS) Regional Disaster Vulnerability Reduction Project funded by the World Bank and the Climate Investment Fund’s Pilot Program for Climate Resilience.

This Policy includes an overview of the national circumstances and context, including observed and future climate change trends and impacts, and the policy framework for use in climate change planning and decision-making. It identifies priorities for action for the period 2018-2030 including specific objectives for adaptation, mitigation and cross-cutting areas. These cross-cutting areas include information management, research and monitoring, integration of disaster risk management and national security, inter-sectoral coordination, investment and economic planning and stakeholder capacity building and engagement. The Policy also outlines the institutional arrangements for coordination and implementation to address adaptation, mitigation and the cross-cutting areas as well as mechanisms for financing and monitoring and evaluation. The Policy is aligned with the National Economic and Social Development Plan (2013-2025), the National Adaptation Plan (2018-2030) and Nationally Determined Contribution (2015).
Document Title: National Climate Change Policy

Family Name: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP)
Family Summary:
This action plan outlines the current legal and institutional framework around renewable energy, as per the requirements of the EU's Renewable Energy Directive.This document aims to achieve the following:

  1. Assess the current legislative and institutional framework for renewable energy, specifically checking its compliance with the Renewable Energy Directive.
  2. Recommend policy and investment measures necessary to both meet the 2020 target of 30% renewable energy consumption and fully implement the Directive, along with an estimate of the associated costs.
Document Title: Georgia's National Renewable Energy Action Plan

Family Name: Renewable Energy Roadmap 2030 for the Electricity sector
Family Summary: This document sets Mauritius' government strategy for enhancing the role of renewable energy sources within the country's electricity sector. It defines capacity targets to reach by 2025 and 2030. The technologies include solutions generating current from tidal/wave, offshore wind, solar and hydro.
Document Title: Renewable Energy Roadmap 2030 for the Electricity sector

Family Name: Concept note for ensuring electricity supply in Uzbekistan 2020-2030
Family Summary: This document aims at ensuring that Uzbekistan electricity sector is able to power the country over the decade 2021-2030 in a sufficient, secure and sustainable way. It defines mid-term and long-term objectives and directions for the development of power sector in the country, priorities and benchmarks as well as arrangements aimed at ensuring the efficiency and effectiveness of the government’s energy policy at different stages of practical implementations guaranteeing achievement of planned goals.The main objectives of this document are 1) to find how to satisfy the country’s electrical power demand in full through domestic generation without dependence on energy imports and thus ensuring energy security; 2) improvement of national economy’s energy efficiency with parallel reductions in energy intensity achieved through, inter alia, creation of economic mechanisms to stimulate rational use of electrical power by consumers; 3) increasing energy efficiency of generation, transmission and distribution of electrical power to satisfy the growing demand; 4) reduction of power equipment wear through consistent renewal, increasing reserves in generation and transmission assets; 5) development and expansion of renewables use and their integration into the unified power system; and 6) development of efficient basic electricity market model.The note notably sets targets for electricity generation from wind and solar sources.
Document Title: Concept note for ensuring electricity supply in Uzbekistan 2020-2030

Family Name: National Electricity Master Plan (RUKN) for 2019-2038
Family Summary: The RUKN sets out the national electricity policy, development direction of electricity supply, the current condition of electricity supply, and the projection of electricity demand for the next 20 years. The national electricity policy consists of policy on electricity supply, engineering and environmental protection. Targets include a minimum of 23% renewable energy in 2025, utilisation of clean coal technology and utilisation of nuclear energy. Modelling was conducted to project the electricity demand for each of the 34 provinces in Indonesia.
Document Title: National Electricity Master Plan (RUKN) for 2019-2038

Family Name: Zero Waste Masterplan 2019
Family Summary: The Masterplan lays out Singapore's strategies to build climate, resource and economic resilience by moving away from the linear 'take-make-dispose model to a circular one that reuses resources endlessly. Climate resilience is explained as doing Singapore's part to mitigate climate change and protecting Singapore from its effects. In a resource- and carbon-constrained world, Singapore needs to adopt a circular economy approach, where scarce resources are valued and kept in use for as long as possible. By conserving resources, Singapore can also reduce greenhouse gas emissions from production and the incineration of waste, which will help to mitigate climate change.The Masterplan sets a target to reduce the amount of waste per capita sent to landfill by 30% by 2030, which is in addition to the existing target to achieve a 70% overall recycling rate by 2030. The strategies include reducing food waste; encouraging e-waste recycling among households; extending the mandatory waste reporting scheme; closing the waste loop with innovative solutions; exploring alternative uses for treated incineration bottom ash and waste treatment residues; turning waste into resources; and exploring the chemical recycling of plastic waste.
Document Title: Zero Waste Masterplan 2019

Family Name: National Program for Sustainable Urban Transport
Family Summary: This decree establishes the National Sustainable Urban Transport Program, PROMOBILITY, within the scope of the Ministry of Transport. The main objective of the Program is to promote sustainable transport within cities in a way that includes the promotion of both climate change mitigation and adpationa measures. Specific objectives of the measure include: a) Contribute to improving the institutional and technical capacities of local governments for the development and management of urban transport within their competence, through the formation of human capital in the corresponding municipalities. b) Support in the planning, the formulation of studies and technical files of investments and actions in transport and urban traffic under the approach and standards indicated in paragraph 2.1 of article 2, as well as carry out the monitoring and evaluation of their execution in the framework of its objectives and purpose. c) Promote the execution of actions and investments that result from urban transport planning in local governments through their management and co-financing, within the framework of budgetary capacity.
Document Title: Decree 27/2019 on the National Program for Sustainable Urban Transport

Family Name: Law No. 2019-675 of 23 July 2019 establishing the Forestry Code
Family Summary:
This Law provides for the classification of forests, including forests intended for the purposes of stablising the climate.

The objectives of this Law are:

• strengthening, for the benefit of present and future generations, the contribution of the forestry sector to sustainable development by promoting the environmental, socio-economic, and cultural functions of forest resources;

• preserving and enhancing biological diversity and contributing to the balance of forest ecosystems and other associated ecosystems;

• promoting the active participation of local populations, Non-Governmental Organizations, and associations in the sustainable management of forest resources to improve their income and living conditions, by taking into account, in forestry matters, their individual and collective rights derived from customs, the Rural Land Code, this law, and by disseminating information on forest policy;

• To promote the creation of community forests, forests belonging to local authorities, forests owned by individuals, and forests owned by private legal entities;

• To enhance the value of forest resources through more advanced wood processing and improved profitability of forest products;

• To encourage the establishment of a forest cover rate representing at least 20% of the national territory; and

• To promote an eco-citizen culture.
