Family Name: Fiji Low Emission Development Strategy 2018-2050
Family Summary: This document aims at defining pathways to achieve low emission development in Fiji until 2050. The strategy lays out sectoral targets for decarbonisation, determines the government's strategy for adaptation and resilience, examines opportunities for green jobs, aims to foster education and raise awareness, and determines how the implementation of this strategy will be ensured through governance, monitoring and evaluation.
Document Title: Fiji Low Emission Development Strategy 2018-2050

Collection Name: Law 7/2021 on climate change and energy transition [Spain]
Collection Summary:
Enacted in 2021, this law establishes Spain's legal framework for achieving climate neutrality by 2050, aligning with the Paris Agreement and Sustainable Development Goals. It mandates a 23% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 (compared to 1990 levels), alongside ambitious renewable energy targets, including 42% of final energy consumption from renewables and 74% renewable electricity generation by 2030. Energy efficiency measures aim for a 39.5% reduction in primary energy consumption within the same timeframe. The law also prohibits new hydrocarbon and radioactive mineral exploitation, requires emission-free transport systems in cities with populations exceeding 50,000, and emphasises sustainable urban mobility.

The legislation includes a national Just Transition Strategy to ensure equitable economic opportunities, particularly for vulnerable regions, while fostering adaptation and resilience to climate risks across critical sectors such as water, biodiversity, and health. It creates governance mechanisms like the Expert Committee on Climate Change and Energy Transition to monitor progress and updates to Spain's Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC). Projecting investments exceeding €200 billion by 2030, the law is expected to enhance Spain’s GDP by €16.5–25.7 billion annually and generate 250,000–350,000 new jobs. The focus on education, innovation, and public awareness underscores its commitment to a holistic and inclusive transition.

This collection represent a body of policies, strategies, and plans enacted under this law.
Family Name: Just transition strategy 2021
Family Summary: The Just Transition Strategy (ETJ), as part of Spain's Strategic Energy and Climate Framework, ensures a fair and inclusive ecological transition by creating quality jobs, supporting vulnerable communities, and promoting social and territorial cohesion. It focuses on gender equality, rural revitalization, stakeholder engagement, and sectoral planning while enhancing RD and innovation. Through "Just Transition Agreements", it aims to mitigate negative impacts on workers and regions, particularly coal-dependent areas, ensuring that the shift to a low-carbon economy drives economic growth and environmental sustainability without leaving anyone behind.
Document Title: Just transition strategy 2021

Family Name: Programme of the Government of Armenia 2019 - RA Government Decision No 65-A/2019
Family Summary: This programme lays the government's strategic plan for its mandate and was submitted to parliament. It notably promotes sustainable growth. Point 4.8 commits the government to environmental protection, and including sustainable forest management, climate change mitigation and adaptation. Point 6.2 stresses the need to foster the production and use of renewable energy sources. Point 6.5 encourages efficiency gains in the transport sector and improve railway tariffs as well as modernising the rolling stock.
Document Title: Programme of the Government of Armenia 2019 - RA Government Decision No 65-A/2019

Family Name: Energy Policy 2019-2050 (Política Energética 2019-2050)
Family Summary:
The Energy Policy 2019-2050 of Guatemala establishes long-term guidelines to ensure a sustainable, reliable, and competitively priced energy supply that supports economic growth and societal well-being. The policy emphasises efficient resource use and infrastructure modernisation while fulfilling national and international environmental commitments, particularly regarding greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction. It seeks to revise existing energy policy targets based on current needs and future scenarios, promote regulatory mechanisms to achieve these goals, foster sectoral participation through dialogue, and implement an integrated information system for monitoring and control.

Key strategic principles include diversification of energy supply to reduce dependency risks, enhancing system resilience through capacity reserves and contingency planning, and recognising the global integration of energy markets. The policy prioritises the transition towards renewable energy sources and the adoption of efficient technologies, particularly in the transport sector, where diversification of fuels (e.g., LPG, biocombustibles, natural gas) and mass transit systems are promoted to reduce fossil fuel dependence. It also addresses the need for regulatory updates aligned with international climate commitments. The policy incorporates a comprehensive greenhouse gas inventory system based on IPCC methodologies, highlighting the sector’s growing emissions due to increased energy demand. Operational actions focus on expanding renewable energy participation, improving emission measurement and verification, and supporting climate change mitigation efforts within the energy sector.
Document Title: Energy Policy 2019-2050 (Política Energética 2019-2050)

Family Name: Ghana Renewable Energy Master Plan
Family Summary: This plan aims to achieve the following by 2030: 1) increase the proportion of renewable energy1 in the national energy generation mix from 42.5 MW in 2015 to 1363.63 MW (with grid connected systems totalling 1094.63 MW) 2)educe the dependence on biomass as main fuel for thermal energy applications, 3) provide renewable energy-based decentralised electrification options in 1,000 off-grid communities, and 4) promote local content and local participation in the renewable energy industry.
Document Title: Ghana Renewable Energy Master Plan

Family Name: Greener Slovakia - Strategy of the Environmental Policy of the Slovak Republic until 2030 (Envirostrategy 2030)
Family Summary: This document defines a vision until 2030, which takes into account a possible, probable, and the desired future development, identifies the fundamental systemic problems, sets the objectives until 2030 and proposes a framework for measures to improve the current situation, and it also contains basic result indicators that will enable a verification of achieved results. The basic vision of Envirostrategy 2030 is to achieve better environmental quality and sustainable circulation of the economy, which is based on rigorous protection of environmental compartments and using as little non-renewable natural resources and hazardous substances as possible, which will lead to an improvement in health of the population. Environmental protection and sustainable consumption will be part of the general awareness of citizens and policy makers. Through the prevention and adaptation to climate change, the consequences will be as subdued as possible in Slovakia.
Document Title: Greener Slovakia - Strategy of the Environmental Policy of the Slovak Republic until 2030

Family Name: National Sustainable Development Strategy (NSDS) of Guinea
Family Summary:
This document sets out Guinea's development strategy. Axis five of the strategy is focused on the energy transition but it also contains a number of other climate related goals:

Objective 1.6 To develop sustainable finance
This includes a section on developing climate finance mechanisms

Objective 2.3 To make quality water available for all and promote its sustainable use
This includes a section on ensuring the water supply is adapted to the effects of climate change

Objective 3.6 To improve the resilience of the agricultural sector to climate change
By 2040 70% of farmers will have put in place adaptation actions

Objective 4.4 To combat the degradation of natural resources and restore degraded forests and vegetation cover
By 2040, 40% of the territory should be forested

Objective 5.1 To reduce greenhouse gas emissions and promote energy efficiency and domestic sustainable energy
By 2040, 70% of rural households use improved cook stoves

Objective 5.2 Promote renewable energy
By 2040 the level of renewable energy in the energy mix will pass between 22% and 44%

 Objective 5.3 Promote the electrification of rural areas and combat energy poverty

Family Name: National Programme on Climate Change & Human Health (NPCCHH)

  2. To strengthen capacity of healthcare system to reduce illnesses/ diseases due to variability in climate
  3. To strengthen health preparedness and response by performing situational analysis at national/ state/ district/ below district levels.
  4. To develop partnerships and create synchrony/ synergy with other missions and ensure that health is adequately represented in the climate change agenda in the country
  5. To strengthen research capacity to fill the evidence gap on climate change impact on human health

Family Name: Action plan for the development of electromobility in Slovakia
Family Summary: The aim of the increased use of electric vehicles in the transport system is to shift to low-emission and zero-emission forms of transport, which is a trend strategically defined also at the level of the European Commission and is part of the low-carbon economy. Transport is currently responsible for a quarter of greenhouse gas emissions and is the dominant polluter, especially in urban agglomerations. For the above reasons, the Action Plan proposes 15 measures to ensure that consumers perceive low-emission mobility as seamless, including by accelerating the implementation of the relevant infrastructure.

Family Summary: This document was approved by the Climate Change Commission's Resolution 2019-001 entitled “A Resolution adopting the National Climate Risk Management Framework (NCRMF) to address intensifying adverse impacts of climate change”. Family Name: Argentina National REDD+ Strategy
Family Summary: Argentina's REDD+ strategy aims to guide the long-term conservation, restoration and sustainable economic development of forest ecosystems. REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation) is a voluntary framework for climate change mitigation developed under the UNFCCC, with a focus on the challenges faced by developing countries. This strategy applies largely to native forests, and seeks a broad set of interventions including regularision of land tenure for indigenous groups, improved governance of fire prevention, awareness-raising about the value of natural assets, integrated watershed-level management and new protected areas.
Document Title: Argentina National REDD+ Strategy

Family Name: Policy for Designed Living Environment
Family Summary:
This document sets out an integrated approach to the work on the designed living environment and also provides a comprehensive national architecture policy. In doing so, it integrates climate-specific considerations.

For instances, it mentions the Climate Leap program which provides support for measures that reduce climate impact. It also highlights the importance of climate-smart cities within urban development. In addition, it encourages the use of sustainably-produced forest products within construction to increase climate benefits.
Document Title: Policy for Designed Living Environment

Family Name: Decree No. 2019-027/MESUDD implementing Law No. 2018-28, establishing the principles of Environmental Assessment
Family Summary: The Decree n° 2019-027/PRN/MESU/DD provides the detailed application principles for the Law 2018-28, establishing the fundamental principles of Environmental Assessment (EA) in Niger, designating the Bureau National d’Évaluations Environnementales (BNEE) as the primary responsible body. The decree specifies four assessment types, with the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (EIES) for projects and the Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment (EESS) for public policies, plans, and programs being the central tools for assessing climate change impacts. Through the EIES, the decree ensures that individual projects are evaluated for their vulnerability to climate risks (such as increased flooding or drought) and their contribution to environmental degradation or mitigation efforts. The EESS, on the other hand, guarantees that new government policies, plans, and programs integrate climate change adaptation and mitigation strategies at a high, strategic level.
Document Title: Decree No. 2019-027/MESUDD

Family Name: Regulation of Liquid Biofuels and their Mixtures
Family Summary:
The biofuel regulation aims to foster the development of the biofuel industry in Costa Rica. For this purpose, the decree regulates the production, transport, storage, and trade of biofuels. It designates the Ministry of Environment, Energy and Telecommunications (MINAET) and the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (MAG) as the institutions in charge of promoting, implementing and managing the development of the National Biofuels Programme.
 
 According to the decree, prices of raw materials employed in the production of biofuels as well as the sales of biofuels to consumers and to the national oil refinery (RECOPE) are to be determined by the market. However, the prices of fossil fuels mixed with biofuels are regulated by the competent national authority.
 
 The Decree further sets up the National Research and Development Bioenergy Policy to enhance the environmental sustainability of biofuel production, increase production, and support research in new sources of biomass.
Document Title: Regulation of Liquid Biofuels and their Mixtures

Family Name: Oman Vision 2040
Family Summary:
Oman's vision 2040 sets out the future vision in Oman. It takes a specific approach in promoting environmental sustainability in Oman. In doing so, it highlights ways to overcome the environmental challenges that have been encountered over the years in Oman, prioritizes an effective eco-system to be implemented in Oman to protect the environment and encourage new infrastructures towards green economy, green strategies and renewable energy production.

The following are a list of objectives of Oman's vision 2040 regarding the environment:

·       promoting environmental ecosystem that are of high quality and free from pollution;

·       Sustainable use of and investment in natural resources and wealth to deliver high added value;

·       Renewable energy, diversified sources of energy, and rationalized consumption to achieve energy security;

·       A green and circular economy that addresses national needs and moves consistently with the global trends; and

·       Environmental awareness coupled with the effective implementation of sustainable consumption and production rules.

The vision also sets objectives of reduction of the share of oil production in the total GDP by 2030 and 2040.
Document Title: Oman Vision 2040

Family Name: ES' National Plan for Adaptation to Climate Change (NAP)
Family Summary:
The key principles of this plan are:
• The national plan for adaptation to climate change is part of the fulfillment of the Sustainable Development Goals, the National Plan for Climate Change and the Nationally Determined Contributions.
• The formulation of the plan must consider different approaches: gender, multi-ethnic groups, generational.
• Establish and strengthen institutional, sectoral and local capacities to achieve adaptation to climate change.
• The plan must be approached from a sectoral and territorial perspective, since it is precisely in the territories where the impact of climate change is felt, with the effects on the populations and resources that cohabit there.
• Empowerment of the national adaptation plan and its sectoral plans involving the different sectors and the population in general, and especially vulnerable groups, for which a participatory approach is established, and with a “bottom-up” construction scheme. ”, through consultation and validation processes. This participation must involve municipalities, government institutions and agencies, non-governmental organizations, the private sector, academia, and other relevant sectors.
• The national plan and the sectoral and intersectoral plans must be constituted in an integrated set of measures that allow generating climate resilience in El Salvador.

Family Name: Federal Government Charging Infrastructure Master Plan I, II and III
Family Summary:
It is the Federal Government Charging Infrastructure Master Plan 2030, which is Germany’s national roadmap for expanding and improving EV charging infrastructure through 2030. It focues on shifting from simply increasing charger numbers to reliability, accessibility, affordability, transparency, and user experience. It contains 41 measures across five priorities:

  1. Increase EV charging demand and private investment.
  2. Accelerate charging infrastructure deployment and simplify permitting.
  3. Strengthen competition and improve charging-price transparency.
  4. Integrate charging infrastructure with the electricity grid and enable smart/bidirectional charging.
  5. Improve convenience, accessibility, cybersecurity, and overall user experience.

Its priority areas include (i) residential/apartment charging, workplaces, motorway fast charging, and charging for electric trucks and buses; (ii) grid capacity and faster grid connections; (iii) reduction of administrative barriers and make public land and suitable sites more readily available. The overall objective is to establish a reliable, competitive, user-friendly and scalable charging ecosystem capable of supporting widespread EV adoption by 2030.
Document Title: Federal Government Charging Infrastructure Master Plan III - 2030

Family Name: National Strategy REDD+ for Equatorial Guinea
Family Summary: EN-REDD+ has as a long-term objective "to contribute to the global fight against climate change and to the country's sectoral development to achieve the well-being of the Equatorial Guinean people through REDD+, with an approach based on competitiveness, sustainability, integrated land management, food security, and social and gender equity”. EN-REDD+ will contributefor the country to achieve the climate objectives stipulated in its planned contributions determined at the national level (CPDN) and the development objectives established in the National Economic and Social Development Plan (PNDES) Horizon 2020 (RGE, 2007).The EN-REDD+ sets ambitious goals to meet its objectives: 1) reduce GHG emissions linked to agriculture, forestry and other land uses (AFOLU) by 20% by 2030, and in 50% by the year 2050; 2) maintain the forest area around 93% of the national territory; 3) reduce the rate of forest degradation to 0.45% per year; 4) strengthen the National System of Protected Areas (SNAP); 5) increase the area of productive forests with sustainable management plans up to 80% by the year 2030; 6) achieve sustainability and improve the efficiency of the forestry and agricultural sectors; and 7) mitigate and compensate the possible negative consequences for forests of future productive activities.REDD+ is part of the national structure of fight against climate change, which includes both adaptation to climate change and mitigation of its effects. The implementation of the REDD+ process will be guided by the principles of good governance: accountability, effectiveness, efficiency, equity, participation and transparency, as well as the application of a multisectoral and territorial development approach.Said implementation will be the responsibility of a REDD+ Steering Committee (CP-REDD+) and a REDD+ National Coordination (CN-REDD+), which will act as the entity responsible for governance and as the technical executive body, respectively.To achieve its objectives, the country plans to develop policies and measures for REDD+ structured in eight strategic axes. Four of them are sectoral axes, whose objective is to achieve sustainable productive development, which in turn makes it possible to mitigate the direct causes of deforestation and forest degradation, and four are cross-cutting axes, which will address the underlying causes.
Document Title: National Strategy REDD+ for Equatorial Guinea

Family Name: Climate Change Strategy 2018-2030
Family Summary: The Myanmar Climate Change Strategy sets out the framework for climate change action in Myanmar, setting out Myanmar's vision to become a climate-resilient country and to contribute to efforts to curb greenhouse gas emissions. The strategy, which covers multiple sectors and aims to both reduce vulnerability to climate change and promote low-carbon growth rests on five implementation pillars including an overarching policy framework, a multi-stakeholder institutional mechanism, a financial mechanism, a capacity strengthening framework, and a monitoring and evaluations framework. The policy aims at the realisation of the following, sector-specific outcomes: (a) Climate-resilient productivity and climate-smart responses in the agriculture, fisheries and livestock sectors to support food security and livelihood strategies while also promoting resource-efficient and low-carbon practices. (b) Natural resource management that enhances the resilience of biodiversity and ecosystem services that support social and economic development and deliver carbon sequestration. (c) Climate-resilient and low-carbon energy, transport and industrial systems that support inclusive and sustainable development and economic growth. (d) All township and city dwellers, including the most vulnerable, are safe from increased risks of rapid- and slow-onset natural disasters and live in sustainable, inclusive, low-carbon, climate-resilient towns. (e) Communities and economic sectors are able to respond to and recover from climate-induced disasters, risks and health impacts and build a healthy society, and (f) Strengthened education, awareness and technological systems that foster a climate-responsive society and human capital to design and implement climate-resilient and low-carbon development solutions for inclusive and sustainable development.

Family Name: DK2020 Project
Family Summary:
The DK2020 project intends for every municipality to draw up a climate action plan to reduce emissions and help keep global heating at safe levels. The impact of this collective effort has huge potential – Danish municipalities aim to cut 76% of Denmark’s total emissions by 2030, compared to 1990.

DK2020 supports municipalities all over Denmark in developing, upgrading or adjusting their existing work on climate action to global best practice, and in ultimately developing climate action plans in line with the 1.5 degree goal in the Paris Agreement. The climate action plans must show the way towards local climate neutrality in 2050 – or sooner. 

The climate action plans will comply with the Climate Action Planning Framework developed by the C40 cities network. DK2020 marks the first time this international standard is adapted and applied for use in smaller cities and municipalities. Realdania, a private association in Denmark which supports projects in architecture and planning, formed a partnership with Local Government Denmark and the five Danish regions – ensuring DK2020 a total funding of DKK 45 mill (appr. €6 mio.) that made it possible to invite all Danish municipalities to join the project. Simultaneously, five geographical organizations with specialist competencies were established to provide advice and consultancy on a regional level. From the beginning in 2019, C40 and green think tank CONCITO have assisted as knowledge partners and project secretariat.
Document Title: Adaptation approaches in Danish municipalities' climate action plans (report on the DK2020 project)

For instance, the priority ‘E’ is to strengthen adaptive capacity and resilience to health risks associated with climate change, as well as supportive measures to mitigate climate change and achieve health equity in accordance with the Paris Agreement with one specific activity to raise awareness of the impact of climate change on human health.
Document Title: National Environmental and Health Action Plan of the Slovak Republic (NEHAP V)

Family Name: Master Plan for Urban Nature: Federal Government Action Programme for a Vibrant City
Family Summary:
The Masterplan Stadtnatur translates the strategic vision of the White Paper on Urban Green into a concrete programme of measures. While the White Paper defines the overall goals for greener, healthier, and more resilient cities, the Masterplan specifies 14 actions that the federal government will implement to increase biodiversity, strengthen urban green infrastructure, and support municipalities. It puts biodiversity, nature-based solutions and integrated planning at the core for climate adaptation.

The Masterplan adopts a broad definition of urban nature, including parks, gardens, urban forests, rivers, wetlands, street trees, green roofs and façades, brownfields, and habitats for wildlife within the built environment. Its objective is to strengthen these elements through coordinated planning, funding, research, education, and policy.
Document Title: Master Plan for Urban Nature: Federal Government Action Programme for a Vibrant City

Family Name: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan, 2019 - 2030
Family Summary:
This policy document contains a section on mainstreaming climate change adaptation and mitigation into biodiversity conservation. Climate-related strategies include the following:

  • Implement climate smart agriculture (CSA) strategy at the counties within the framework of agro-ecological practices;
  • Prioritize needs for research arising from the Kenya’s updated National Climate Change Action Plan related to biodiversity conservation objectives;
  • Implement actions from Kenya’s updated National Climate Change Action Plan related to biodiversity conservation and harnessing.
Document Title: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan, 2019 - 2030

Family Name: Energy Efficiency Label for Residential Buildings
Family Summary:
The key objective of the programme is to make a transparent instrument over the energy performance of a home which will gradually lead to an effective model taken into consideration while deciding over the home prices in future. The objective of the labeling program is to make an energy performance of a home an instrument of comparison while deciding over the home prices in the future. It also aims to provide a benchmark to compare one house over the other on the energy efficiency standards to create a consumer-driven market transformation solution for energy efficiency in the housing sector.

This program is another step towards realizing the vision of an energy surplus India with 24/7 power to all. Proposed Labelling program will cover all types of residential buildings in India. All the envisaged objectives can be achieved through the proposed labeling mechanism by making it as a mandatory information required in any real estate transaction/leasing.
Document Title: Energy Efficiency Label for Residential Buildings

Family Name: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
Family Summary:
Sets out targets for improved energy efficiency in 2020, 2025 and 2030, with concrete actions for energy transmission and demand sectors in the years 2019-2020.

The 2019-2020 NEEAP, which was officially adopted by the Government of Georgia in 2019, sets national energy-saving targets for the public and private sectors and proposes concrete measures and actions to meet these targets. It includes financial, regulatory and informational measures for energy efficiency in all key energy demand sectors, including transport, buildings, electricity transmission and industry, as well as cross-sector and institutional measures. An updated NEEAP is anticipated for 2021.
Document Title: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)

Family Name: Exemplary Administration Pact (Pacte de l'exemplarité de l'administration)
Family Summary: The objective of this pact is to boost energy efficiency and environmental concern in the Moroccan administration. It includes energy audits of territorial and central administrative buildings. The pact also plans to educate public actors on energy efficiency and to promote the use of electric vehicles as well as the recycling of waste. It was adopted as part of the 2019 Action Plan of the National Climate Change Strategy by the Strategic Committee for Sustainable Development.
Document Title: Exemplary Administration Pact (Pacte de l'exemplarité de l'administration)

Family Name: National Action Plan on Agriculture and Climate Change (Version 1 - 2019)
Family Summary: Sectoral plan to reduce emissions by 25.74 MtCO2e by 2030 through afforestation initiatives, smart agriculture and biomass energy use
Document Title: National Action Plan on Agriculture and Climate Change (Version 1 - 2019)

Family Name: 3rd Energy Master Plan
Family Summary:
This strategic policy document sets out a series of sectoral targets for 2040, as well as an economy-wide final energy consumption target. Main 2040 targets included are:

- 30-35% renewable electricity generation

- Final energy consumption target of 39.2 Mtoe reduction against BAU scenario

- Energy efficiency target in industrial sector 21% reduction and 38% in the building sector against 2017 baseline

- 11,420,000 Low emissions vehicles including electric and hydrogen

- 1.12 trillion won in clean energy RD
Document Title: 3rd Energy Master Plan

Family Name: Steel Scrap Recycling Policy
Family Summary: This Scrap Policy only furthers the role envisaged in the NSP-2017 to ensure scrap segregation (quality wise), collection, processing and recycling. The policy is to provide a framework for carrying out the activities in a scientific manner to have assured and regular supply of processed scrap for the downstream industry.
Document Title: Steel Scrap Recycling Policy

Family Name: Suriname national adaptation plan 2019-2029
Family Summary:
The Republic of Suriname is recognized as the most forested country in the world and contributes significantly to mitigating the adverse effects of climate change. Suriname, however, is forced to take urgent adaptive measures to cope with the impacts of global warming. Mindful of the Sustainable Development Goals, the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) for Suriname is a national initiative designed to effectively address climate-related challenges in the pursuit of sustainable development. The NAP received support from the United Nations Development Programme’s Japan-Caribbean Climate Change Partnership (J-CCCP).
The objective of the NAP is to enable Suriname to conduct comprehensive medium and long-term climate adaptation planning. It is a flexible approach that builds on the country’s existing adaptation activities and mainstreams climate change into national decision-making, development planning, policies and programs. The NAP will align the country's future efforts with the broad objectives of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and outline actionable groundwork for the integration of climate change considerations into national strategic and sectoral planning and budgeting processes.
Document Title: Suriname national adaptation plan 2019-2029

Family Name: National adaptation plan
Family Summary: Ethiopia's National Adaptation Plan (NAP-ETH) builds on ongoing efforts to address climate change in the country's development policy framework, including the Climate Resilient Green Economy (CRGE) strategy and the second Growth and Transformation Plan (GTP II), as well as sectoral climate resilience strategies and regional and municipal adaptation plans. Its goal is to reduce vulnerability to the impacts of climate change by building adaptive capacity and resilience.NAP-ETH aims to strengthen holistic integration of climate change adaptation in Ethiopia's long-term development pathway, supported by effective institutions and governance structures, finance for implementation and capacity development and strengthened systems for disaster risk management and integration among different sectors. The plan and its implementation are guided by the principles of participation, coherent interventions, stakeholder empowerment, gender sensitivity, equitable implementation and partnership.
Document Title: Ethiopia: Climate resilient green economy - National adaptation plan

Family Name: National Disaster Risk Management Plan 2019 - 2030
Family Summary:
The National Disaster Risk Management Plan 2019 - 2030 is divided into four strategic axes, which are aligned with the Sendai Framework, whose action priorities are (i) improving knowledge of disaster risks, (ii) strengthening disaster risk governance, (iii) developing and using financial mechanisms to build the resilience of communities, public and private structures and (iv) improving preparedness for an effective response and rapid recovery after a disaster.

This revised Haitian strategic framework for disaster risk management integrates the issue of climate change and human security. It emphasizes gender sensitivity, the inclusion of people living with disabilities and universal access during the intervention and reconstruction phases. Investment protection, risk transfer, public and community governance of disaster risks, the organization of volunteering and accountability are also integral parts of it. Furthermore, this plan is based on a common vision by focusing action on the role of individuals and communities in disaster risk management. It favours a participatory, inclusive approach and an integrated and holistic strategy.
Document Title: National Disaster Risk Management Plan 2019 - 2030 (Plan national de gestion des risques de désastre 2019 - 2030)

Family Name: National Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy (SN-RRC) 2020-2030
Family Summary:
The National Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy (SN-RRC) 2020-2030 of Côte d'Ivoire aims to strengthen the country's resilience in the face of hazards and disaster risks of natural, technological or anthropogenic origin by 2030. This vision is structured around several fundamental principles:

  • Centre disaster risk reduction (DRR) actions on communities: Involve local populations in risk prevention and management initiatives.
  • Adopt an all-risk, integrated, and holistic approach: Consider all types of risks and ensure cross-sector coordination for global and coherent management.
  • Target multidimensional vulnerability: Identify and address the different dimensions of vulnerability, whether social, economic, environmental or institutional.
  • Articulate the operational framework of the SN-RRC with the National Development Plan (PND), the national decentralization policy and other sectoral policies and plans: Ensure the coherence and integration of DRR actions into national development strategies.
  • Rely on regional and international cooperation: Strengthen partnerships with other countries and international organizations to benefit from exchanges of experiences, resources and technical support.
Document Title: National Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy (SN-RRC) 2020-2030 ( Stratégie Nationale de Réduction des Risques de Catastrophes (SN-RRC) 2020-2030)

Family Name: Decree 222/019 - Approval of the National Environmental Plan for Sustainable Development
Family Summary:
It regulates the Environmental Act (Law 17.283) through the approval of an environmental plan for sustainable development to guide its execution. The Plan has four (4) overarching objectives that guide the proposed actions:

  • Ensure national commitment to environmental protection and equitable access to environmental resources for current and future generations, prioritizing vulnerable populations.
  • Promote respect for nature, conserve biodiversity, and enhance the resilience of environmental systems.
  • Encourage sustainable production and consumption models, integrating environmental considerations into socio-economic activities.
  • Strengthen institutional and citizen capacities for environmental management, including mechanisms for joint Plan implementation and evaluation.
Document Title: National Environmental Plan For Sustainable Development

Family Name: Decree 222/019 - Approval of the National Environmental Plan for Sustainable Development
Family Summary:
It regulates the Environmental Act (Law 17.283) through the approval of an environmental plan for sustainable development to guide its execution. The Plan has four (4) overarching objectives that guide the proposed actions:

  • Ensure national commitment to environmental protection and equitable access to environmental resources for current and future generations, prioritizing vulnerable populations.
  • Promote respect for nature, conserve biodiversity, and enhance the resilience of environmental systems.
  • Encourage sustainable production and consumption models, integrating environmental considerations into socio-economic activities.
  • Strengthen institutional and citizen capacities for environmental management, including mechanisms for joint Plan implementation and evaluation.
Document Title: Decree 222/019

Family Name: National Policy on Competitiveness and Productivity (Política Nacional de Competitividad y Productividad)
Family Summary:
The Supreme Decree 345-2018 approved the National Policy on Competitiveness and Productivity . The overall objective of the policy is to create the conditions necessary to promote well-being for all Peruvians. For doing that, the Policy is organised in 9 priority goals:

  • Provide the country with high-quality economic and social infrastructure
  • Strengthen human capital
  • Foster capacity building for innovation, adoption, and transfer of technological improvements
  • Promote local and external financing mechanisms
  • Create the conditions for a dynamic and competitive labor market to generate decent employment
  • Create the conditions to develop a productive business environment
  • Facilitate conditions for foreign trade in goods and services
  • Strengthen the country’s institutional framework
  • Promote environmental sustainability in the operation of economic activities
Document Title: National Policy on Competitiveness and Productivity (Política Nacional de Competitividad y Productividad)

Family Name: Order no 602/2018 approving the national strategy of the Republic of Tajikistan on the decrease in risk of natural disasters for 2019-2030
Family Summary: The national strategy consists in building a national capacity to manage natural disasters. Several measures are proposed : 1) an evaluation of the risks, 2) a creation of national and local databases about natural disasters, 3) rethinking infrastructure construction.
Document Title: Order no 602/2018 approving the national strategy of the Republic of Tajikistan on the decrease in risk of natural disasters for 2019-2030

Family Name: Order no 602/2018 approving the national strategy of the Republic of Tajikistan on the decrease in risk of natural disasters for 2019-2030
Family Summary: The national strategy consists in building a national capacity to manage natural disasters. Several measures are proposed : 1) an evaluation of the risks, 2) a creation of national and local databases about natural disasters, 3) rethinking infrastructure construction.
Document Title: National strategy of the Republic of Tajikistan on the decrease in risk of natural disasters

Family Name: State Program on Road Safety 2019-2023
Family Summary: This program determines measures to reduce the number of road accidents as well as to mitigate the negative environmental impacts of the transport industry, through the improvement of fuel quality and the implementation of European emission standards.
Document Title: State Program on Road Safety 2019-2023

Family Name: GD no. 1277/2018 on the establishment and operation of the National Monitoring and Reporting System (NMRS)
Family Summary: Government Decision no. 1277/2018 approves the implementation of a National Monitoring and Reporting System (NMRS) for greenhouse gas emissions and other information relevant to climate change in Moldova, the execution of which is to be controlled by the Ministry of Agriculture. This system centralises and formalises national-level GHG emissions reporting, under a ministerial budget, and assigns responsibility for sectoral reporting to particular bodies within and outside the Ministry of Agriculture. The reporting system also includes statistics indirectly related to emissions, such as protein consumption per capita and measures of forestry extent.
Document Title: GD no. 1277/2018 on the establishment and operation of the National Monitoring and Reporting System (NMRS)

Family Name: Supreme Decree 3751, authorising a financing agreement for the programme MyWater (MiAgua)
Family Summary: This Supreme Decree, grounded in constitutional provisions for universal and equitable access to basic services, authorises the signing of a financing contract with the European Investment Bank for the programme MyWater (MiAgua). The programme, aligned with Bolivia's Economic and Social Development Plan 2016-2020 under the Framework for Integral Development for Living Well (Law N° 786), aims to expand sustainable water and sanitation services nationwide. MyWater's primary objectives include providing potable water and sewerage services whilst increasing local resilience to climate change, with the ultimate goals of poverty reduction, environmental pollution mitigation, and improvement of living conditions. The decree authorises resource transfers to the Ministry of Environment and Water as the Executing Entity and the National Fund for Productive and Social Investment (FPS) as Co-executor, emphasising principles of accessibility, quality, continuity, and equitable tariffs with social participation and control.
Document Title: Supreme Decree 3751, authorising a financing agreement for the programme MyWater (MiAgua)

Family Name: Ordinance (2017: 1319) on state support for measures that contribute to industry's climate change
Family Summary: This document charges the government to provide state support in the form of grants for measures that 1) contribute to reducing such greenhouse gas emissions from industry that have a direct or indirect connection with industry processes, 2)contribute to negative emissions through the capture, transport and geological storage of greenhouse gases of biogenic origin or taken out of the atmosphere, or 3) through the application of new technology or other innovative solutions in industry significantly contribute to achieving the environmental quality goal Limited climate impact and its milestones. The total amounts of the grants are specified in the 2021 regulation letter.
Document Title: Regulation (2017: 1319) on State Aid for Measures to Reduce Industrial Greenhouse Gas Emissions

Family Name: Ordinance (2017: 1319) on state support for measures that contribute to industry's climate change
Family Summary: This document charges the government to provide state support in the form of grants for measures that 1) contribute to reducing such greenhouse gas emissions from industry that have a direct or indirect connection with industry processes, 2)contribute to negative emissions through the capture, transport and geological storage of greenhouse gases of biogenic origin or taken out of the atmosphere, or 3) through the application of new technology or other innovative solutions in industry significantly contribute to achieving the environmental quality goal Limited climate impact and its milestones. Family Name: Ministerial Order No. 2018-1182 of December 18, 2018 relating to aid for the purchase of ecological vehicles
Family Summary: This order establishes and regulates a system for subsidising the purchase of low-emission vehicles, with subsidy per purchase capped at 10,000 euros for the lowest emitting and smaller amounts available for other vehicle classes.
Document Title: Ministerial Order No. 2018-1182 of December 18, 2018 relating to aid for the purchase of ecological vehicles

Family Name: 12th Five Year Plan (2018-2023)
Family Summary: This document was prepared by the Gross National Happiness Commission and aims at enabling a just, harmonious and sustainable society through enhanced decentralisation. It notably seeks to ensure adequate renewable energy supply, water, food and nutrition security, improved efficiency and effectiveness of public service delivery.
Document Title: 12th Five Year Plan (2018-2023)

Family Name: National Energy Policy 2018
Family Summary: The National Energy Policy 2018 aims to set overarching goals and priorities in the energy sector. It aims to achieve universal, affordable, secure, sustainable energy, while enhancing employment and economic growth. To achieve these goals and contribute to climate mitigation efforts, the policy promotes the expansion of on-grid solar energy, and greater exploration of other renewable generation sources such as wind and geothermal.
Document Title: National Energy Policy 2018

Family Name: Fundamental Plan for National Resilience
Family Summary: This plan defines four overarching principles governing resilience in Japan: preventing loss of life, maintaining state and society functions, minimizing property damage, and achieving swift recovery. The policies planned for by the Japanese government place special emphasis on combining "hard" and "soft" adaptation measures. Examples include developing disaster management facilities, resilient construction, emergency drills, and disaster management education. Additionally, this plan outlines procedures for conducting vulnerability assessments, different mechanisms for promoting resilience in different sectors and at different levels of government, and the process for reviewing national and subnational resilience plans.
Document Title: Fundamental Plan for National Resilience

Family Name: Mozambique NDC operationalization plan for 2020-2025
Family Summary: This plan was approved by the Council of Ministers at its 38th Session, held on 11 December 2018. It was identified in Mozambique's updated NDC, however no further documentation is available.
Document Title: Mozambique NDC operationalization plan for 2020-2025

Family Name: National Development Strategy "Moldova 2030"
Family Summary: The National Development Strategy "Moldova - 2030" is a strategic vision document that indicates the direction of development of the country and society in the next decade based on the principle of the human life cycle, his rights and quality of life, and which includes the following four pillars of sustainable development: a sustainable and inclusive economy, reliable human and social capital, respected and effective institutions, and a healthy environment. The plan identifies the fact that climate change poses risks and opportunities and that these need to be assessed as part of the development agenda.
Document Title: National Development Strategy "Moldova 2030"

Family Name: Climate Change Policy for the Public Works, Transport and Housing Sector 2018-2036
Family Summary:
This policy emanates from the Ministry for Public Works and Transport (MOPTVDU) and aims to prevent, care for and reduce the vulnerability of the population towards adverse effects of climate change, with a particular focus on the most affected. The document details key concepts and sets the ministry's strategy to design a multi-sectoral plan within its vested powers. The document also has a mitigation component, in particular with regard to urban and transport actions.

The strategy laid out in the policy focuses on updating the legal and regulatory framework; enhance knowledge creation and sharing; and promote institutional coordination at all levels while involving citizens. The strategy also discusses financial and budgetary matters (alternative financing mechanisms, MOPTVDU budget, taxes, project management involving international actors).
Document Title: Climate Change Policy for the Public Works, Transport and Housing Sector 2018-2036

Family Name: National Climate Learning Strategy (SNACC) 2016-2025
Family Summary: Burkina Faso's National Climate Learning Strategy (SNACC) for 2016-2025 aims to promote awareness-raising, education and training on climate change adaptation and mitigation, to help contribute to long-term sustainable development and global efforts to address climate change. It notes that the public sector lags behind the private sector on climate training/education, and that human resources for this type of training are scarce nationally. Specific interventions are not given, but the strategy underscores climate change learning as a basic requirement for the fulfilment of other existing and future climate policies/strategies.
Document Title: National Climate Learning Strategy (SNACC) 2016-2025

Family Name: National Green Growth Strategy to 2030
Family Summary: This document aims to enable mitigation and adaptation actions to be undertaken across socioeconomic sectors by 2030. It notably seeks to 1) enhance investment environment, 2) develop rural areas and alleviate poverty, 3) promote gender equality, and 4) improve the country's resilience to adverse effects of climate change.
Document Title: National Green Growth Strategy to 2030

Family Name: National Waste Policy 2018-2023
Family Summary: The goal of this policy is to manage waste sustainably in order to protect the integrity of the environment and improve quality of life. It charges the Ministry of Environment, Energy and Climate Change to encourage waste reduction and recovery strategies, strengthen its institutional and legal framework, and upgrade waste operations in line with international practices.
Document Title: National Waste Policy 2018-2023

Family Name: National Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2018-2022
Family Summary: The National Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2018-2022 (PNACC-2) is France's second adaptation Plan (PNACC-1 covered the period 2011-2015). Its general objective is to implement the necessary actions to adapt by 2050, the metropolitan and overseas French territories to expected regional climate change; this in line with the long-term objectives of the Paris Agreement and the relevant objectives of other international conventions. The plan has 6 axes that cover governance, prevention and resilience, nature and environment, economic sectors, knowledge and information and the international scene, each one with specific measures.
Document Title: The National Climate Change Adaptation Plan (PNACC 2)

Document Title: Understanding the National Climate Change Adaptation Plan (PNACC 2)

Family Name: National Circular Economy Strategy
Family Summary: This document seeks to implement the fundamentals of circular economy in the country. One of its goals is to reduce carbon emissions.
Document Title: National Circular Economy Strategy

Family Name: Trajectory for Low Energy Buildings
Family Summary:
The Trajectory is a national strategy for Commonwealth, State and Territory action across all buildings.

The Trajectory has been created by the Commonwealth, States and Territories under the leadership of the Energy and Climate Change Ministerial Council (ECMC).

The Trajectory provides an opportunity to work towards a net zero emissions building sector by 2050 while:

  • lowering costs for households and businesses
  • improving building comfort for all Australians.

The updated Trajectory replaces the 2019 Trajectory for Low Energy Buildings and its Addendum.

Building on the ambition of 2019, the updated Trajectory reflects the following current and emerging drivers of change:

  • net zero ambitions
  • energy efficiency
  • fuel switching and electrification
  • energy demand flexibility
  • embodied carbon emissions
  • resilience
  • green finance
  • refrigerant emissions.

The updated objectives of the Trajectory are to:

  • reduce energy costs for households and businesses
  • drive emissions towards net zero
  • reduce and manage demand on the electricity grid
  • keep people healthy, comfortable and safe from climate hazards
  • ensure equitable access to energy performance benefits.
Document Title: Addendum to 2019 Trajectory for Low Energy Buildings - Existing Buildings

Family Name: Navigating our Energy Future: Marshall Islands Electricity Roadmap
Family Summary:
This Roadmap presents costed, technically sound pathways for the electricity sector to help achieve the Marshall Islands' 2025 and 2030 NDC targets (reducing greenhouse gas emissions economy-wide by 32 percent below 2010 levels by 2025, with additional targets of 45 percent by 2030), and briefly outlines the longer-term pathways required to achieve total decarbonisation of the electricity sector by 2050. It covers the main grids of Majuro and Ebeye; mini-grids; and individual solar home systems or stand-alone power systems.

The electricity sector must reduce diesel use by at least 50 percent below 2010 levels by 2025, and 65 percent by 2030. Other objectives are affordability; improved energy efficiency and reduced losses; increased energy security; reliable power supply; 'diesel-off' capability by 2025 with use of wind and solar renewable energy; and improving the quality of life on the outer islands.

The technologies considered suitable for the Marshall Islands are: wind turbines; solar photovoltaics (PV); biodiesel; diesel generators; and enabling technologies such as battery energy storage and automatic control systems; and utility-scale controllable loads and thermal storage. The policy and institutional development and human resources strategies required to achieve the outcomes are outlined in the Roadmap.
Document Title: Navigating our Energy Future: Marshall Islands Electricity Roadmap

Family Name: Our Waste, Our Resources: A Strategy for England (2018)
Family Summary: Our Waste, Our Resources: A Strategy for England (2018) sets out England’s long-term approach to reducing the environmental and climate impacts of resource use and waste, with the objectives of doubling resource productivity and eliminating avoidable waste by 2050. From a climate perspective, the strategy aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions associated with the extraction, production, use and disposal of materials by moving towards a more circular economy, in which products and materials are kept in use for longer through waste prevention, reuse, repair, remanufacturing and recycling. It identifies resource efficiency and waste prevention as important tools for reducing carbon emissions and supports measures to increase recycling, reduce reliance on landfill, tackle food waste and improve the sustainability of key material-intensive sectors such as construction. The strategy also recognises the role of waste management in reducing methane and other emissions and sets out measures to increase the recovery of energy and resources from waste where prevention and recycling are not possible. Overall, it provides a high-level policy framework for reducing the carbon intensity of England’s resource and waste system and supporting the transition towards a low-carbon circular economy.
Document Title: Our Waste, Our Resources: A Strategy for England

Family Name: National Waste Policy (2018)
Family Summary: The 2018 National Waste Policy provides a framework for Australia's waste management until 2030, promoting collaboration across sectors and focusing on five principles: avoiding waste, improving resource recovery, increasing recycled material demand, managing material flows, and fostering innovation. In 2019, they also included targets such as banning certain waste exports, reducing waste generation by 10% per person, achieving an 80% recovery rate, increasing recycled content, and halving organic waste in landfills. In October 2022, Environment Ministers recognized progress and called for better product design and production processes, with updates in the National Waste Policy Action Plan Annexure 2022 to support 2030 targets.
Document Title: National Waste Policy (2018)

Family Name: National Family Farming Action Plan 2020-2024
Family Summary: This plan notably seeks to enhance small-scale agriculture's mitigation and adaptation capabilities.
Document Title: National Family Farming Action Plan 2020-2024

Family Name: National Policy on Seas and Coasts of Mexico (Política Nacional de Mares y Costas de México)
Family Summary: This policy, developed through the Interministerial Commission for the Sustainable Management of Seas and Coasts (CIMARES), provides a cross-sectoral framework for sustainable governance of Mexico’s marine and coastal regions. Anchored in the ecological, social, and economic significance of these territories, the policy aims to improve local livelihoods while conserving marine ecosystems and enhancing resilience. The document acknowledges the growing threats posed by climate change (especially sea-level rise, increased storm intensity, and coastal vulnerability) integrating these into its risk prevention and territorial planning strategies. Specific actions include promoting climate risk atlases at the municipal level, developing State Climate Change Programs in all 17 coastal states, and mainstreaming climate considerations into infrastructure planning, making the policy a vital instrument in Mexico’s broader climate adaptation agenda.
Document Title: Mexico's National Policy for Seas and Coasts. Comprehensive management of the most dynamic regions of the country (Política Nacional de Mares y Costas de México. Gestión integral de las regiones más dinámicas del territorio nacional)

Family Name: National Development Strategy with Low GHG Emissions
Family Summary: This document was prepared through a consultative process. It promotes the construction of tools for individual, sectoral and national application, oriented to development with low emissions, which strengthen the economy, improve efficiency and increase the profitability of small, medium and large-scale production, in addition to facilitating access to international markets and new sources and mechanisms of financing.
Document Title: National Development Strategy with Low GHG Emissions

Family Name: Regulations Limiting Carbon Dioxide Emissions from Natural Gas-fired Generation of Electricity (SOR/2018-261)
Family Summary: These Regulations establish a regime for limiting carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions that result from the generation of electricity by means of thermal energy from the combustion of natural gas, whether in conjunction with other fuels, except coal, or not.
Document Title: Regulations Limiting Carbon Dioxide Emissions from Natural Gas-fired Generation of Electricity (SOR/2018-261)

Document Title: Regulations Limiting Carbon Dioxide Emissions from Natural Gas-fired Generation of Electricity (SOR/2018-261)

Family Name: Planned Relocation Guidelines - A framework to undertake climate change related relocation
Family Summary: This document provides guidance for the Government of the Republic of Fiji and all other stakeholders present in Fiji to consider planned relocation solutions for the affected communities as part of their adaptation strategies in relation to environmental change, and disasters due to climate change related slow-onset events occurring on the territory of Fiji.
Document Title: Planned Relocation Guidelines - A framework to undertake climate change related relocation

Family Name: Order of 28 November 28, 2018 on "Low Carbon" label reference
Family Summary: This Order aims to promote the emergence of additional projects to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in France, by setting up a framework for monitoring, notifying and verifying GHG emissions, allowing the valorisation of additional emission reductions, carried out voluntarily by natural or legal persons in various sectors of activity. Project leaders (any natural or legal person) will be able to be paid by a voluntary partner (public or private actor), who will be able to have their contributions to additional emission reductions from these projects recognised. Emission reductions are neither transferable nor exchangeable either over the counter or on any voluntary or mandatory market. Emission reductions can only be used for the voluntary compensation of emissions from non-state actors.

Family Name: Namibian Transport Policy 2018-2035
Family Summary: The Namibian Transport Policy 2018-2035 serves as an overarching guiding document for development of the transport sector. The policy acknowledges climate change as one of the greatest threats globally, nationally and sectorally. In particular, it notes the threats from flooding to transport infrastructure, and eventual risks to low-lying coastal zones from sea level rise. It calls for increased drainage requirements in new and existing transport infrastructure. The policy also promotes further investigation into cleaner aviation fuels to mitigate emissions, and increased fuel efficiency in other forms of public transportation.

Family Name: National plan for civil protection, prevention and mitigation of disasters
Family Summary:
The Civil Protection, Prevention and Mitigation of Disasters Law, LPC, in article 20, defines that the Civil Protection, Prevention and Mitigation of Disasters Plan, PNPC, aims to define the actions of the State and civil society for the management of risks, the study of existing vulnerabilities and their mitigation, as well as preparations for care and recovery in the event of disasters.

The PNPC has planned results for the public administration period 2014-2019 based on the Five-Year Development Plan and expected results until 2030 based on the international commitments to implement the 2030 Agenda, The Paris Agreement, COP 21, and the Sendai Framework, these international commitments are country commitments and the following public administrations must take up their implementation in their five-year planning cycles.

The approach used in planning for the GIRRD is intersectoral, interinstitutional and multidisciplinary. It includes prevention, mitigation, response, and post-disaster recovery in its design, and its actions indicate that all public entities, the private sector, and civil society are involved in its execution. The premise of the planning is that to the extent that the risk is known, the person will be better prepared to prevent, mitigate and confront them in a timely and effective manner for recovery.

The PNPC is divided into five chapters: the first addresses the national and international regulatory legal framework that regulates the PNPC; the second the institutional framework that, due to its intersectoral nature, is needed to execute the PNPC; The third chapter interrelates the PNPC with the Sendai Framework, the SDGs and the Five-Year Development Plan 2014-2019 of El Salvador; The fourth articulates the conceptualization of the prevention, mitigation, response and post-disaster recovery components. The fifth chapter develops the strategic framework of planning, its philosophy and executive direction by establishing the mission, vision, objectives, priorities and strategic lines of action; finally, the sixth chapter defines the guidelines for post-disaster recovery.
Document Title: National plan for civil protection, prevention and mitigation of disasters (Plan nacional de protección civil, prevención y mitigación de desastres)

Family Name: Cambodian Sustainable Development Goals (CSDGs) Framework 2016-2030
Family Summary: The CSDGs Framework of 2016-2030 provides guidance for the formulation of national policy, and the monitoring of the implementation process. The framework is centred around the idea of not leaving anyone behind, and ensuring equity and prosperity for all Cambodians, whilst maintaining national economic growth. Moreover, it places emphasis on natural capital, and efforts for combating climate change. Family Name: Sustainable Development Strategy 2030
Family Summary:

HORIZON 2020

• Integrate measures to adapt to climate change into the strategies and sectoral development plans and pursue their intersectoral harmonisation.

• Raise awareness of the imminent threat of climate change both at the political level of institutions of state and among citizens, regardless of age.

2030 TARGETS

Family Name: Guidance for municipalities and landowners on coastal protection
Family Summary:
This guidance for municipalities and landowners on coastal protection methods was developed following the amendment to the Coastal Protection Act on 23 January 2018, which stated that citizens should have the opportunity to protect their properties to a greater extent than previously, and that individual landowners should have greater freedom to choose how they want to protect their property if there are technically more options that do not cause a nuisance to neighbours.

This guidance therefore focuses on common coastal protection methods, but also contains a short section on risk reduction through non-structural measures for coastal protection (Section 5.4). Risk is defined as the probability of flooding and/or erosion occurring multiplied by the consequences thereof. Risk reduction encompasses a broad spectrum of measures including prevention as well as protection and preparedness. Prevention can, for example, consist of avoiding any future flood damage by not building housing and industrial plants in areas prone to flooding.

Protection refers to the more traditional view of coastal protection, where measures are taken, both structural and otherwise, to reduce the risk of flooding and erosion. Preparedness in this context means that citizens are informed about the flood risk and how to behave in the event of flooding.

The guidance covers both solutions that require several landowners to come together to establish coastal protection, the so-called municipal joint projects, and solutions that are intended to be implemented by a single landowner.
Document Title: Guidance for municipalities and landowners on coastal protection

Family Name: National Adaptation Plan for the Agricultural Sector
Family Summary: Uganda's National Adaptation Plan for the Agricultural Sector aims to address growing threats of drought and extreme weather due to climate change, and ensure a sustainable and resilient agrifood system and economy over the long term. The plan seeks to promote a wide range of improvements including to public awareness (of resilient agricultural techniques), research and innovation, and improvements using existing technology, implemented across animal agriculture, crops and fisheries. More specific interventions include connecting weather early warning systems to farmers, introducing resilient crop varieties and field trials, training on rainwater harvesting technology, river basin level planning, among numerous others.
Document Title: National Adaptation Plan for the Agricultural Sector

Family Name: Multi Annual Energy Plan
Family Summary:
The Multi Annual Energy Plan (MAEP) is a tool to help France reach carbon neutrality by 2050. It was created through the implementation of the Law on Energy Transition for Green Growth (2015). The document focuses on 2 successive five-year plans (2019-2023; 2024-2028). It will be reviewed and updated before the second phase is implemented. The goals presented in the document are as follow:

By 2023: renovation of 2.5 million homes; replacement of fossil fuel heating systems by renewable ones or high performance gaz boilers; 1,2 million personal EVs; 20,000 gas-fueld lorries; 9,5 million homes heated with certified wood burners; 3,4 million homes connected to district heating systems.

By 2028: Reducing 14% of final energy consumption (all sectors, baseline 2012); reducing fossil fuel primary consumption by 35% (baseline 2012); doubling production of electricity through renewable energies; increasing the production of renewable heat by 40%.
Document Title: Multi Annual Energy Plan

Family Name: National Development Plan (PND) 2018-2025
Family Summary: The 2018-2025 PND is structured around the following major themes: (i) human capital and the well-being of populations; (ii) economic productivity and competitiveness; iii) environment, climate change and territorial development, and iv) governance. Through this architecture, it expresses the urgency of proceeding with an integrated approach to solutions to current development challenges and constitutes a favorable framework for the consolidation and sustainability of the achievements of the Government's Action Program ( PAG) 2016-2021.
Document Title: National Development Plan (PND) 2018-2025

Family Name: National climate change adaptation strategy (2018)
Family Summary: The National Climate Change Adaptation Strategy (NCCAS) of South Africa provides a common vision of climate change adaptation and climate resilience for the country and outlines priority areas for achieving this vision. The NCCAS is an important step forward for South Africa, as it:Acts as a common reference point for climate change adaptation efforts in South Africa in the short to medium-term2, providing guidance across all levels of government, sectors, and stakeholders affected by climate variability and change.Provides a policy instrument in which national climate change adaptation objectives for the country can be articulated to provide overarching guidance to all sectors of the economy.Facilitates the degree to which development initiatives at different levels of government and business integrate and reflect critical climate change adaptation priorities, and thus inform resource allocation by the various stakeholders towards climate change resilience.Guides stronger coherence and coordination on climate change adaptation activities between different institutions and levels of government.Supports South Africa in meeting its international obligations by defining the country’s vulnerabilities, plans to reduce such vulnerabilities and leverage opportunities, outlining the required resources for such action, whilst demonstrating progress on climate change adaptation.The NCCAS is divided into sets of strategic objectives, strategic interventions and strategic outcomes with associated actions. The document is directed not only at national government departments but speaks to South African society as a whole, including the key relevant sectoral institutions, provincial governments and municipalities, and non-governmental entities including the private sector, the research community and civil society.
Document Title: South Africa: National climate change adaptation strategy (2018)

Family Summary:
• The general objectives of the Strategy are set out in section 3(a).Make Vietnam a strong sea power;
  • Develop a sustainable sea-based economy;
  • Shape the marine ecosystem culture;
  • Adapt to climate change and sea rise level;
  • Prevent pollution and degradation of the sea environment, coastal landslides and coastal erosion; and

Family Name: Royal Decree-law 15/2018 on urgent measures for energy transition and consumer protection
Family Summary: This decree law aims to accelerate the transition to a decarbonised economy by increasing integration of renewable energies into the Spanish economy and promoting energy efficiency. It aims to use economic signals to incentivise consumers, companies and others to adopt renewable energy and energy efficient technologies. In order to accelerate Spain's transition to renewable energies, the law introduces a number of fiscal measures, including (1) a tax exemption for producers of energy incorporated into the electricity system for a period of six months, (2) a tax exemption for the use of energy products intended to produce electricity in power stations or the production of electricity or the co-generation of electricity and heat in combined heat and power stations, (3) a tax exemption for self-consumed energy of renewable origin, co-generation or waste.This document derives from Law 24/2013 on the energy sector.

Research and higher education is meant to develop a society that is environmentally, scoially, culturally, economically and politically sustainable, including fulfilling Norway's climate obligations.

The Norwegian government will invest in education, research and technology development that helps reach the climate and environmental targets and promotes the shift to a greener society. Specifically, it will:

  • strengthen research efforts for restructuring towards a low-emission society;
  • give priority to developing technology and solutions for the transition to a greener society;
  • strengthen research and higher education that can increase understanding of climate change and lay a foundation for successful climate change adaptation; and
  • strengthen research and higher education to further develop an integrated, knowledge-based public administration that safeguards considerations relating to climate and the environment.

The strategy operationalises the National Climate Change Policy and was developed using a participatory approach, gaining input and recommendations from diverse stakeholder groups through national consultations. The Strategy details specific adaptation objectives and measures across eight sectors.
Document Title: National Climate Change Adaptation Strategy, 2018

Family Name: Energy Master Plan 2034
Family Summary: This document builds on the 2003 National Energy Policy, notably to boost the production of energy from renewable sources. As stated in the document, the masterplan seeks to provide national decision makers with the quantitative basis for planning future energy sector development through identifying and addressing the country’s distinct barriers in the supply of energy. It uses modelling tools to build its recommendations that include the development of renewable energy options involving the private sector; the creation of a comprehensive distributed power generation plan; and the need to develop policies and regulations to facilitate private sector engagement in rural electrification. It also sets energy efficiency goals.
Document Title: Energy Master Plan 2034

Family Name: National strategy of energy access (SNAE)
Family Summary: This document notably seeks to attract funds to increase the supply of energy from renewable sources.Its overarching goal is to raise the national electricity access rate to at least 80% by 2035. It sets an interim target for 2025: increasing access from around 20–23% (national average in recent years) to about 34% by 2025.
Document Title: National strategy of energy access (SNAE)

Family Name: Intelligent Transport program (PTI)
Family Summary:
The Intelligent Transport program seeks to promote good practices and the implementation of technologies for efficient transportation in order to:
● Improve energy efficiency
● Increase competitiveness by reducing logistics costs.
● Reduce GHG (greenhouse gas) and local effect emissions
● Create a community of good practices and encourage their use in freight transport.
Document Title: Intelligent Transport program (PTI)

Family Name: National Adaptation Plan Framework
Family Summary:
Ghana's National Adaptation Plan Framework is led by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in partnership with the National Development Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance. It is intended to address climate change impacts in a more integrated, coordinated and sustainable manner. This Framework will guide and advance Ghana's National Adaptation Plan (NAP) process to address medium- and long-term adaptation needs.

This Framework covers the approach and structure for the NAP process going forward; the guiding principles; the alignment of this Fraemwork with existing national policies and planning processes, as well as regional and international frameworks; proposed institutional arrangements for Ghana's NAP process; monitoring, evaluation and learning; climate finance resource mobilisation; and next steps and milestones.
Document Title: Date issued

Family Name: National Forest Programme 2018
Family Summary:
Denmark's National Forest Program (2018) sets a course for sustainable forest management that ensures a good balance between use and protection, and supports the many different functions of the forest.

The forest program contains two long-term goals:

  • that forest landscapes cover 20-25 percent of Denmark's area by the end of the 21st century.
  • that 10 percent of the total forest area by 2040 has nature and biological diversity as the primary operational purpose.

The Danish Environmental Protection Agency follows up on the forest program and contributes to implementing the forest program's specific actions.
Document Title: National Forest Programme

Family Name: Standards to mainstream risk management in Ministries, State Secretariats and public institutions
Family Summary:
Establish general guidelines for mainstreaming Risk Management in Ministries, State Secretariats and Public Institutions, with respect to their competence in the national territory, through a Management Model that allows coordination with the actors of the National Decentralized Management System of Risks (SNDGR).

This document applies to Ministries, State Secretariats and Public Institutions at the national level and their respective deconcentrated levels.
