Family Name: 2050 Climate Strategy
Family Summary:
The Tile Til Eo 2050 Climate Strategy "Lighting the way" makes a number of recommendations to achieve the country's objectives of net zero emissions by 2050 and 100 % renewable energy. These include periodic revision of GHG emissions reductions, specific goals such as in the waste sector, and a planning of new climate policies to adopt, such as a National Adaptation Plan by the end of 2019. This Strategy shall be periodically reviewed by the authorities over the period.

The document further promotes 1) the use of public transport, 2) efforts to phase out the use of kerosene for lighting and strengthen existing institutional arrangements to reduce GHGs from cooking and lighting, 3) the establishment of a long-term finance strategy to implement this strategy, 4) the prioritisation of capacity-building in all sectors, and 5) the inclusion of health considerations in the National Adaptation Plan.
Document Title: 2050 Climate Strategy

Family Name: Ordinance 373/2018 on measuring deforestation in authorised areas
Family Summary: Establishes a procedure for systematising and measuring information on authorised areas of vegetative suppression in accordance with Brazil's Nationally Determined Contribution to the Paris Agreement.
Document Title: Ordinance 373/2018 on measuring deforestation in authorised areas

Family Name: 7th Energy Research Programme
Family Summary:
Through this programme, Germany's government aims to follow up on recent progresses in energy research, take new initiatives and define priorities for research funding and innovation policy in the energy sector. The programme is based on the following principles:

  •  technology and innovation transfers are deemed urgent because they are seen as a prerequisite for the efficient and intersectional implementation of the energy transition.
  • direct funding for limited-term projects with a defined topic will be augmented. The research spectrum will be broadened in order to also comprise systemic and inter-systemic issues of the energy transition.
  • institutional research funding for the Helmholtz Association of German Research Centres (HGF) is to be supported by the federal government.
  • National research work shall be more closely intertwined with international and European partners.
Document Title: 7th Energy Research Programme

Family Name: Action Plan for the development of Renewable Energies in Equatorial Guinea 2018 – 2025 (PAER)
Family Summary:
The National Action Plan for the Development of Renewable Energies in Equatorial Guinea establishes the following general objectives:
1. Promote the study, research, use and comprehensive development of electricity generation with renewable sources in the country, through a model of sustainable energy development, which ensures a positive contribution from the environment, and with significant impacts on the economy and the backbone social of the territories.
2. Reduce dependence on electricity generation through fossil fuels, implementing generation projects with renewable sources, achieving climate change mitigation, and also contributing a differential value to energy security and the sustainability of the country's electrical system.
Document Title: Action Plan for the development of Renewable Energies in Equatorial Guinea 2018 – 2025 (PAER)

Family Name: Bicycle and active mobilities plan 2022-2027 ("plan vélo et mobilité actives")
Family Summary:
The second version of the Plan Vélo was presented on September 20th, 2022. The core objectives of the plan are:1. making cycling and walking an attractive alternative to the individual car for proximity trips and combined with public transport for the displacements of longer distances.2. leverage economic benefits by accompanying the ecosystem of French bicycle actors.3. Make the bike accessible to everyone, from an early age and throughout life.The plan is organised around the following measures.Safety:

  • Develop cycle facilities and improve road safety.
  • The bicycle plan also plans to help communities to finance cycle infrastructure projects on their territory. The Active Mobility Fund (Fonds Mobilités actives) aims to support, accelerate and amplify projects to create cycle routes within communities.
  • AVELO program to help communities to engage in a cycle policy.
  • Development of temporary cycle paths.

Safety: Better fighting theft.

  • Cycles identification
  • Secure parking in train stations and other multimodal places
  • Secure parking lots of bikes in buildings

Create an incentive framework fully recognising the use of cycling as a virtuous mode of transport:

  • Bonuses to buy bicycle.
  • Tax incentives.
  • The durable mobility package.
  • Tax reductions for companies providing their employees with a fleet of bikes for their home-work trips.
  • Develop intermodality train-bike and bus-bike.

Develop a bicycle culture:

  • Knowing how to ride by bike
  • promoting May as a bicycle month.
Document Title: Information about the Bicycle and active mobilities plan 2022-2027 ("plan vélo et mobilité actives")

Family Name: Plan for cycling and active mobility
Family Summary:
This plan aims at strengthening the cycling culture and increase the mode share of cycling in the country. The plan notably defines measures to improve road safety and vows to switch the incentives dedicated to commuting towards cycling. In order to reach its objectives, the government notably creates through this document a National Active Mobility Fund to foster the building of dedicated cycle lanes, and improves the framework to allow local territories to reach their own targets. The plan also seeks to reduce theft.


In 2023, an amended plan was released for the period 2023-2027. The new plan pursues three main objectives:

  1. Make cycling accessible to everyone, from all stages of life.
  2. Make cycling and walking an attractive alternative to private cars for local trips, and combined with public transport over longer distances.
  3. Make cycling a lever for the economy by supporting French players in the sector.
Document Title: Plan for cycling and active mobility

Family Name: Iceland’s Climate Action Plan for 2018-2030 and 2020 update
Family Summary:
The Climate Action Plan aims to boost efforts in cutting net emissions in order to reach the government‘s aim to make Iceland carbon neutral before 2040. The plan consists of 34 government measures, ranging from an increase in reforestation to a ban on new registration of fossil fuel cars by 2030.

The main emphasis of the document is: 1) to phase out fossil fuels in transport, 2) to increase carbon sequestration in land use, by restoration of woodlands and wetlands, revegetation and afforestation. 

Climate mitigation measures will get an increase in funding of almost 7 billion Icelandic krónur in the period 2019-2023. A general carbon tax, already in place, will be gradually increased (it was increased by 50% in the beginning of 2018, and will be increased by 10% in 2019, and by 10% again in 2020).

The plan was thoroughly updated in 2020.
Document Title: Iceland’s Climate Action Plan for 2018-2030

Family Name: Cultural Heritage in a Changing Climate Action Plan for Climate Adaptation 2019–2023
Family Summary:
The National Antiquarian Board's action plan aims to increase understanding of and strengthen the conditions for preventive work on cultural heritage in a changing climate. The activities aim to implement the action plan for climate adaptation of cultural environment in the cultural environment work of relevant agencies, and to ensure that knowledge base on climate adaptation of cultural heritage is accessible, updated and relevant:

1. Organize Forums for Climate and Cultural Heritage – with different themes.

2. Collaborate on methodological and knowledge base for preventive climate adaptation work.

3. Compile and communicate knowledge base on cultural heritage in a changing climate to the action plan's target groups linked to the prioritized environmental objectives.

4. Highlight research needs on cultural heritage in a changing climate in the agency's RD program and interest other RD funders.

5. Develop relevant knowledge bases that are used to preserve, use and develop cultural heritage in a changing climate.

6. Participate in the work of developing and systematically reviewing relevant standards.

7. Monitor the world nationally and internationally, compile and disseminate interdisciplinary knowledge bases on cultural heritage in a changing climate where it is currently lacking.

8. Implement an internal knowledge upgrade at the National Heritage Board on cultural heritage in a changing climate and the action plan for climate adaptation.

9. Coordinate climate adaptation issues that affect the National Heritage Board.
Document Title: Cultural Heritage in a Changing Climate Action Plan for Climate Adaptation 2019–2023

Family Name: National Policy on Climate Change and Disaster-Induced Displacement
Family Summary:
This document sets Vanuatu's strategy regarding displacements of populations. These displacements occur, either temporarily or permanently, because the people are no longer able to reside on the land on which they live or lose access to land and natural resources upon which their livelihoods depend. A major cause for disasters causing displacement identified in the document is climate change. 

The policy seeks to minimise the drivers of displacement, better understand the population's needs and wishes and take it into account, and promote access to disaster-resilient housing. It further identifies current policy gaps, and aims to optimise displacements so they can be more durable, through 1) sustainable return and reintegration at the place of origin, 2) sustainable local integration in areas where displaced persons have taken refuge, and 3) sustainable integration in another part of the country.
Document Title: National Policy on Climate Change and Disaster-Induced Displacement

Family Name: The food sector in a changing climate — a plan for what the Swedish National Food Agency needs to do
Family Summary:
The Swedish National Food Agency believes that the goals in Agenda 2030 and Sweden's national environmental goals should be guiding for climate adaptation work in the food sector. Many of the goals in Agenda 2030 concern food consumption and food security. Goal 13 explicitly includes climate adaptation. Reduced food waste (Goal 12) contributes to reduced pressure on food production and thus indirectly contributes to the food sector's climate adaptation. The goal of sustainable consumption and production patterns (Goal 12), the goal of securing food supply and improved nutrition (Goal 2) and the goal of access to water (Goal 6) also have strong links to climate adaptation. The generation goal is a strategic goal that should permeate the entire national environmental goal work. The food sector is affected to a greater or lesser extent by all environmental quality goals. Eight of the sixteen goals have been identified by the Swedish National Food Agency as particularly relevant. These are:

  • Limited climate impact,
  • A non-toxic environment,
  • No eutrophication,
  • Living lakes and watercourses,
  • Good quality groundwater,
  • A balanced sea and a living coast and archipelago,
  • A rich agricultural landscape and
  • A rich flora and fauna.

The Swedish National Food Agency contributes to developing a long-term sustainable and robust food sector that actively addresses climate change through knowledge building, surveys, scientific risk assessments and the dissemination of knowledge to public and private activities.
Document Title: The food sector in a changing climate — a plan for what the Swedish National Food Agency needs to do

Family Name: National Policy and Response Strategy on Climate Change
Family Summary:
This document defines the overarching climate mitigation and adaptation strategy of Liberia, sectoral implications and cross-cutting issues. It notably assesses the country's vulnerabilities to climate change including regarding poverty and forest management. Identified pillars for the policy are improved governance, financing mechanisms, capacity building, technology innovation, infrastructure, integrated planning and data management. The Policy determines that adaptation and disaster risk management efforts should focus on forestry and wildlife, agriculture, coastal areas, water resources, fishery, energy, mining, industry, transport, tourism, infrastructure, urbanisation and settlement, and health. 

 Mitigation policies include 1) the enhancement of the country's potential for carbon sequestration by promoting conservation, sustainable forest management, community forestry and curbing key drivers of deforestation and forest degradation, which in turn will contribute to sustainable wildlife management, 2) encouraging lowland farming, investing in smallholder agriculture and allowing large-scale concessions on degraded land to avoid and reduce national emissions levels, 3) marching towards universal access to affordable, sustainable, and environmentally friendly low carbon energy services, 4) ensure that the mining sector develops by gradually mixing the use of low emission energy sources and technologies, 5) a low-carbon transport system, and 6) energy recovery from waste.  Crosscutting issues to mainstream in climate policies include communication, education and raising awareness, technology transfer, gender, HIV and AIDS.
Document Title: National Policy and Response Strategy on Climate Change

Family Name: Government Regulation No. 189/2018 Coll. on on Sustainability Criteria for Biofuels and Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions from Fuels, last amended by Government Regulation No. 108/2025 Coll
Family Summary:
The Czech Government Decree 189/2018 Coll main purpose is to define sustainability criteria for biofuels, to set rules for calculating greenhouse-gas emissions from fossil and renewable fuels (including electricity for transport), and to require documentation, certification and reporting for producers and suppliers. It defines, for example, which types of biomass (agricultural, forestry, waste, residues) are eligible under sustainability rules and prohibits biomass from land with high ecological value (e.g. natural forests, protected areas, high biodiversity sites) or formerly wetlands / peatlands.

The last amendment brought to the regulation a new list of feedstocks and raw materials for the production of advanced biofuels.
Document Title: Government Regulation No. 189/2018 Coll. on on Sustainability Criteria for Biofuels and Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions from Fuels, last amended by Government Regulation No. 108/2025 Coll

The strategy largely aims to extend and strengthen existing and recently successful funding and governance programmes in indigenous land rights, fire management, forest restoration and building incentive systems to direct economic activity towards sustainable activity.

Family Name: Emirates Youth Climate Strategy 2018-2021
Family Summary:
The Emirates Youth Climate Strategy provides an integrated framework to enhance the role of youth in meeting the challenges of climate change in accordance with the Government's approach to develop an empowered future generation to achieve the UAE vision 2021, the 2071 Plan, the 2050 Climate Change Plan, the National Youth Agenda and the Arab Youth Strategy.

The Strategy comprises three strategic objectives:

  • Raise awareness about the issue of climate change among international youth;
  • Develop the capacities of youth to meet the challenges of climate change; and
  • Promote youth participation in decision-making and climate action. 

To achieve these objectives, the Youth Council at the Ministry will:

  1. Engage youth with decision-makers in climate change policy and strategic development;
  2. Develop youth capacities in climate change;
  3. Engage youth in international and local forums/conferences on climate change;
  4. Provide opportunities for pilot projects and research on climate change;
  5. Enhance youth participation in climate change volunteering programs; and
  6. Establish a dedicated youth platform on climate change.

Family Name: National Flood Protection Plan (NFPP) IV
Family Summary: The National Flood Protection Plan IV (NFPP) was concived in the aftermath of the 2010 floods, the most devastating floods in Pakistan. The planning strategy is concious that flood management in the past has focused on structural measures (such as construction of dams) which have proven sufficient. Therefore, the NFPP IV implements integrated watershed management through structural and non-structural measures like flood forecasting and early warning, flood risk zoning, etc. The NFPP's flood protection investment plan envisions two phases of investment worth Rs.332.246 billion for a 10 year period until 2025.
Document Title: National Flood Protection Plan (NFPP) IV

Family Name: Agreement announcing the North Pacific Marine and Regional Ecological Management Program (Acuerdo que da a conocer el Programa de Ordenamiento Ecológico Marino y Regional del Pacífico Norte)
Family Summary: This policy establishes the Marine and Regional Ecological Zoning Programme for Mexico's Northern Pacific, mandating integrated spatial planning to align coastal and marine development with constitutional mandates for environmental protection and sustainable development. The programme employs systems dynamics modelling to forecast environmental conflicts across sectors (including tourism, fisheries, aquaculture, and agriculture) designating Environmental Management Units (UGAs) to regulate land and sea use. It prioritises biodiversity conservation (e.g., whale habitats, turtle nesting grounds) while promoting sustainable economic activities, emphasising intergovernmental coordination between federal agencies, state governments, and local authorities to balance ecological preservation with socioeconomic objectives.The policy addresses climate change through vulnerability assessments and adaptive spatial planning. It identifies low-lying sandy zones and coastal lagoons as highly exposed to sea-level rise, erosion, and extreme weather events, projecting impacts such as habitat loss and water scarcity. Key adaptation measures include restricting development below 5m elevation, protecting coastal ecosystems (mangroves, dunes, seagrasses) as natural buffers, mandating wastewater treatment to maintain water quality, and implementing sustainable water resource management to mitigate aquifer depletion.
Document Title: Agreement announcing the North Pacific Marine and Regional Ecological Management Program (Acuerdo por el que se da a conocer el Programa de Ordenamiento Ecológico Marino y Regional del Pacífico Norte)

Family Name: Decision 1604/QD-NHNN Approving Vietnam’s Scheme for Green Banking Growth in Vietnam (Vietnam’s Green Taxonomy)
Family Summary: This decision no. 1604/QD-NHNN by the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) approves the scheme for green banking growth in Vietnam (the Green Taxonomy) with the central objective of increasing awareness around the banking system’s social responsibility for environmental projection and preventing climate change, and directing financial flows towards eco-friendly and green manufacturing and services industries to contribute to sustainable development and green growth in Vietnam.
Document Title: Decision 1604/QD-NHNN

Family Name: National Development Plan - PND 2018-2022
Family Summary: In this document, the government states that it will aim to develop climate action and promote renewable energy sources.
Document Title: National Development Plan - PND 2018-2022

Family Name: Comprehensive management plan for climate change in the energy mining sector
Family Summary: This Plan was adopted by the ministerial Resolution no 4 0807. The Plan aims at reducing vulnerability to climate change and promoting low carbon development at sector level, strengthening and protecting the sustainability and competitiveness of the industry. The Plan seeks in particular at reducing GHG emissions in the sector, and sets specific targets in that direction, including regarding flaring emissions. It also analyses how to incorporate adaptation and disaster risk management within the mining decision-making structure. Improving governance is a key aspect of the plan, notably through monitoring, reporting, coordination, financing cooperation and knowledge management. The document also calls for low-carbon cooperation across with the transport sector, and for a compensation system to remunerate actors engaging in mitigation activities.
Document Title: Comprehensive management plan for climate change in the energy mining sector

Family Name: Master Plan for the Deployment of Renewable Energies in Chad
Family Summary: This document lays out the government's plan to develop renewable energy in Chad, based on a range of studies on their potential in the country. The document focuses on off-grid systems as well as on larger scale power plants, and hybrid systems coupled with batteries or diesel generators.
Document Title: Master Plan for the Deployment of Renewable Energies in Chad

Family Name: Myanmar Sustainable Development Plan (2018-2030)
Family Summary:
The Myanmar Sustainable Development Plan (MSDP) has been designed as a living document that presents practical and implementable pathways toward addressing development challenges. The plan provides a long-term vision founded upon the objective of giving coherence to the policies and institutions necessary to achieve inclusive and transformational economis growth. 

The plan is structured around three pillars ('A peaceful, Prosperous and Democratic Myanmar'), five goals (1) Peace, National reconciliation, Security and Good Governance; 2) Economic Stability and Strengthened, Macroeconomic Management; 3) Job Creation and Private Sector Led Growth; 4) Human resources and Social Development for a 21st Century Society; 5) Natural Resources and the Environment for Posterity of the Nation), 28 strategies and 251 action plans.
Document Title: Myanmar Sustainable Development Plan (2018-2030)

Family Name: Climate Compass: A climate risk management framework for Commonwealth agencies
Family Summary: This set of guidelines is designed to create a framework to help public servants in Australia identify and manage the risks from climate change. It builds on the best available climate change adaption research and science and reflects current leading practice for climate risk management and planning for long-term and uncertain outcomes.
Document Title: Framework document

Family Name: Preparing Israel to Adapt to Climate Change: implementing the recommendations to the government for a national strategy and action plan (Decree 4079)
Family Summary:
This Decree acknowledges the need to ensure Israel is prepared for climate change. It established the National adaptation Administration ("The Secretariat"), an entity overseen by the MoEP, with the aim of overseeing and executing the National Adaptation Plan.

The Decree also mandates the National Emergency Authority, to formulate national emergency plans in light of extreme weather events. It is also responsible for leading the Emergency Subcommittee, who in collaboration with meteorological services evaluate reference scenarios for fires, floods, and other extreme events.

In 2022, Decree 4079 was amended by Decree 1902 to set a final date for the preparation and submission of adaptation plans by ministries for the end of 2023.
Document Title: Amending Decree 1902

Family Name: Royal Decree 958/2018 establishing and regulating the Interministerial Commission on Climate Change and Energy Transition
Family Summary: The Real Decreto 958/2018 establishes the Interministerial Commission for Climate Change and the Energy Transition to better address Spain's ecological transition, enhancing the government's efforts in climate action and energy transition. This commission, which is led by the Minister for Ecological Transition, is tasked with coordinating and proposing public policies related to climate change and energy, from a participatory and multidisciplinary perspective. Its key functions include facilitating the drafting of Spain's Climate Change and Energy Transition Law, the National Integrated Energy and Climate Plan, and strategies for decarbonizing the economy by 2050. Additionally, the commission supports a just transition for affected communities and advises the Government’s Economic Affairs Commission on proposals with significant economic implications.
Document Title: Royal Decree 958/2018 establishing and regulating the Interministerial Commission on Climate Change and Energy Transition

Family Name: Decision No. 4079 - Israel's Preparedness to Adapt to Climate Change: Implementing Recommendations for a Strategy and a National Action Plan
Family Summary:
This decision instructs the Executive Committee chaired by the Ministry of Environmental Protection to prepare a national plan for preparing and adapting to climate change. 

The five following goals must be achieved by the plan and strategy: 
1. Reducing damage to life and property and building economic resilience.
2. Taking measures to increase the durability of natural systems.
3. Building and updating the scientific knowledge base for decision making.
4. Education, raising awareness and making knowledge accessible to decision makers and the public.
5. Israel's integration into the global effort in accordance with its commitments, and the promotion of regional and international cooperation.

The national plan must implement the recommendations and establish an administration to prepare the State of Israel for adaptation to climate change. It must also establish a governing body, to be called the Climate Change Preparedness Administration, which will be responsible for inter-ministerial coordination and monitoring the implementation of the national adaptation strategy and the implementation of the preparation plans in the outline of the adaptation plan and updated from time to time. The administration will be headed by the Ministry of Environmental Protection and will ensure a coordinated effort between government ministries and other public authorities.

The document further sets a monitoring, reporting and verification system.
Document Title: Decision No. 4079 - Israel's Preparedness to Adapt to Climate Change: Implementing Recommendations for a Strategy and a National Action Plan

Family Name: Presidential Decree 171/18 approving forestry regulations
Family Summary: This document approves the forestry regulations, namely, the "regulamento florestal", that aims at enabling a sustainable management of the country's forest. It notably seeks to increase the knowledge on the risks of climate change on the country's ecosystems, and reforest the country including for carbon sequestration purposes.
Document Title: Presidential Decree 171/18 approving forestry regulations

Family Name: Industrial Heat Recovery Support programme
Family Summary: The Industrial Heat Recovery Support (IHRS) programme was designed to encourage and support investment in heat recovery technologies. This means helping businesses identify and invest in opportunities for recovering and reusing heat that would otherwise be wasted.
Document Title: Industrial Heat Recovery Support programme

Family Name: National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction 2018-2030
Family Summary:
The National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction for the planned period from the year 2018 until the year 2030 outlines the vision for reducing the risk of disasters on the territory of the Republic of Bulgaria. The NSDR takes into account the international approach to ensuring policy coherence for disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation and sustainable development, under the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030, addressing natural hazards like floods, droughts, and extreme temperatures. Regional and municipal plans, such as the Integrated Territorial Strategies and Municipal Integrated Development Plans, incorporate climate adaptation and disaster risk reduction measures tailored to local vulnerabilities.

It sets the following strategic goals: 1. Achieving resilience of society in the face of disasters; 2. Capacity building for disaster risk management at all administrative levels of government; 3. Achieving coherence in the implementation of policies for sustainable development, adaptation to climate change and disaster risk reduction; 4. Achieving sustainability of disaster protection financing.
Document Title: National Strategy for Disaster Risk Reduction 2018-2030

Family Name: Decree on Environmental Levy for Air Pollution with Carbon Dioxide Emissions
Family Summary: The Slovenian Decree on the environmental tax on air pollution caused by carbon dioxide emissions (Uredba o okoljski dajatvi za onesnaževanje zraka z emisijo CO₂) establishes a fiscal instrument aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions by imposing a tax on CO₂ released primarily from the combustion of fuels. The decree defines the taxable activities, taxpayers (generally entities using fossil fuels), and the calculation of the tax based on the quantity of emissions, thereby internalising environmental costs and incentivising lower-carbon energy use. It forms part of a broader system of environmental taxes adopted under the Environmental Protection Act and complements other climate instruments such as excise duties and the EU emissions trading system. Subsequent developments and amendments have mainly adjusted the scope and application of the tax in response to economic and energy conditions. The Decision on the amount of the environmental tax for air pollution by carbon dioxide established that the value per unit is 30.85 euros.
Document Title: Decree on Environmental Levy for Air Pollution with Carbon Dioxide Emissions (Initial text)

Family Name: Green Growth Policy
Family Summary:
This policy document seeks to enable Colombia to benefit from the supply of natural capital for the production of environmental goods and services to generate a green, low-carbon growth. It establishes that in order to maintain and increase the rate of economic growth that the country needs, and thus address social problems, in terms of poverty, inequality and peace building, the search for new sources of information is required. This policy recognizes that current economic development will be unsustainable in the long term.

THE document contains the Green Growth Policy for the country, which consists of five strategic axes. One of its main objective is to boost to 2030 the increase of the productivity and the economic competitiveness of the country, while ensuring the sustainable use of natural capital and social inclusion, in a manner compatible with the climate.

The policy will be implemented during a time horizon of 13 years (2018-2030) and includes specific actions of intersectoral nature.
Document Title: Green Growth Policy

Family Name: The flare gas (prevention of waste and pollution) regulations 2018
Family Summary:
The flare gas regulations establish a legal framework to pursue the objectives of the Federal Government for the reductions of GHG emissions by the flaring and venting of natural gas.

The main objectives of the regulations are 1) to reduce the environemental and social impact caused by the flare of natural gas, 2) to prevent the waste of natural resources, 3) to create social and economic benefits from gas flare capture.

The document introduces several facts : 1) the legal basis for the implementation of the Nigerian Gas Flare Commercialisation Programme (NGFCP), 2) a new payment regime for gas flaring - "polluter pays" principle 3) obligations on producers and gas flare out projects for the reporting of data.
Document Title: The Flare Gas (prevention of waste and pollution) Regulations 2018

Family Summary: The 5th Strategic Energy Plan details the government's vision to 2030 and 2050 in order to enforce the Basic Act on Energy Policy. The Plan notably defines an increased role of renewables in the medium and long terms, and determines the nuclear policy post Fukushima. Family Summary: The goal of this policy is to increase access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, efficient and modern energy for every person in the country. Family Summary: This document aims to increase the agricultural sector's resilience by 2030 and adjust its production processes in order to reduce GHG emissions. It also seeks to adopt a participatory and inclusive approach.

Family Name: Road to Zero Strategy
Family Summary: This policy sets out a target of at least 50%, and as many as 70%, of new car sales and up to 40% of new van sales being ultra low emission by 2030.
Document Title: Road to Zero Strategy

Family Name: Ordinance (2016:837) on grants for renovation and energy-efficiency improvements in certain residential areas
Family Summary:
This Ordinance introduces a grant which, subject to the availability of funds, may be given to provide rented homes with discounted rent in residential areas with socio-economic challenges in renovated and energy-efficient apartment buildings.

The grants amounts to 20 per cent of the renovation costs and is paid to the tenant in the form of a rebate over the period of seven years.
Document Title: Ordinance (2016:837) on grants for renovation and energy-efficiency improvements in certain residential areas

Family Name: Energy Agreement (2018)
Family Summary:
The agreement aims to ensure a market-driven green transition. To ensure that renewable energy becomes our predominant source of electricity within the foreseeable future, as well as an increasingly utilised primary energy source for heating, technology-neutral energy tender processes involving solar PV, land-based wind, offshore wind near coasts and other technologies will be conducted in the coming years. The expansion of renewable energy capacity will need to contribute to the cheapest possible future production of green energy, thus benefitting Danish society as a whole. Funds will also be earmarked to ensure the continued expansion and improved efficiency of biogas and other green gasses in Denmark.

The agreement includes the following initiatives:

• World class offshore wind

• Renewable energy on market conditions

• Reduction of taxes on electricity and restructuring of surplus heat utilisation

• Targeted energy savings

• Modernisation of the heating sector and mitigating the impacts of eliminating the “base

subsidy”

• Strengthened energy and climate research

• Denmark leading the way in exports of green energy solutions

• A smart and flexible energy system

• Funding for green transport

• Reserve for additional investments in RE from 2025 onwards
Document Title: Energy Agreement (2018)

Family Name: Action Plan for the Implementation of the 2030 Agenda
Family Summary:
The Action Plan for the Implementation of the 2030 Agenda serves as a transitional framework to operationalise the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development in Spain, setting the groundwork for a long-term Sustainable Development Strategy (2020–2030). This comprehensive action plan seeks to align national policies with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), fostering collaboration across government levels, civil society, academia, and the private sector. It emphasises immediate measures to tackle pressing issues such as poverty, inequality, and environmental sustainability, while proposing governance reforms and accountability mechanisms to ensure effective implementation.
Climate change plays a pivotal role in this plan, notably through the Law 7/2021 on climate change and energy transition, which aims to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050 and build resilience to climate risks. Among others, the plan supports the integration of sustainable energy systems (SDG 7) and urgent climate action (SDG 13), alongside cross-cutting policies on circular economy, water management, and urban development. This holistic approach underscores a commitment to a just transition, ensuring social equity while advancing towards a low-carbon, climate-resilient economy. By embedding climate considerations within the broader sustainable development framework, the plan positions Spain as a proactive actor in addressing the global climate crisis.
Document Title: Action Plan for the Implementation of the 2030 Agenda

Family Name: Ordinance (2018:1428) on government climate adaptation work
Family Summary:
According to this Ordinance, 32 national authorities and all county administrative boards must conduct climate and vulnerability analyses, develop government targets for their work on climate adaptation and an action plan to achieve the targets. The latest versions of the action plans are shown below.

The Ordinance states that designated authorities must initiate, support and evaluate work on climate adaptation within their areas of responsibility and within the framework of their assignments. They must conduct climate and vulnerability analyses for their operations and develop current government targets for their work on climate adaptation. The targets must contribute to the government achieving its climate adaptation targets and be measurable to the extent that is practically possible.

The authorities must have an action plan for the work of achieving these government targets. Resources, approaches, timeframes and division of responsibilities that apply to the work shall be stated in the action plan. The work according to the action plan is followed up and evaluated with the aim of continuously improving the work. The action plan is updated in the event of significant changes in the operations or at least every five years.
Document Title: Ordinance (2018:1428) on government climate adaptation work

Family Name: Electrification strategy of Togo
Family Summary: This strategy aims for universal access by 2030, based in particular on renewable energies. The strategy will be carried out in three phases and extend over 12 years, will cost 1,000 billion CFA francs , 50% of which will come from private investment funds.
Document Title: Electrification strategy of Togo

Family Name: Ministerial Order No. 2018-613 of June 26, 2018 relating to the thermal characteristics of new buildings and renovations of existing buildings
Family Summary: The order regulates the energy performance of new buildings, renovations and extensions, applying minimum efficiency standards and requiring expert audits to ensure appropriate thermal insulation can be installed. Family Summary: This document approves the regulations for the infrastructure for charging electric vehicles

Family Name: Normative Resolution No. 819 of 19 June 2018
Family Summary:
This Resolution establishes the procedures and conditions for electricity distribution companies (concessionaries and public service permit holders) and other interested parties to carry out electric vehicle recharging activities. The installation of a charging station must generally be communicated to the distributor, which then consolidates information for the Brazilian Electricity Regulatory Agency (ANEEL). The distributor has the discretion to install charging stations in its area of operation and may establish specific electricity safety standards for installations. Charging equipment must comply with the protocols for communication and remote supervision and control.

The Resolution permits owners of the charging stations to set charges for charging at freely negotiated prices. The Resolution also provides for consequential amendments for revenue sharing and tariff regulations.
Document Title: Normative Resolution No. 819 of 19 June 2018

Family Name: National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2018
Family Summary: The vision of this Policy is to build a climate-adapted and climate-resilient nation safe from disaster risk. The goal of this policy is to reduce disaster mortality and number of affected people substantially, increase resiliency by reducing disaster damage to means of livelihoods as well as critical infrastructures and disruption of basic services such as agriculture, industry, roads, communication, water supply and sanitation, education and health facilities, and reduce direct disaster economic loss. It mainstreams diverse areas of disaster management, risk reduction, and efficient and effective response as well as adopting the approach of Build Back Better (BBB) for rehabilitation and reconstruction in the post-disaster period.

Family Name: Joint resolution 1/2018 creating the Environmental and Insurance Sustainability Program
Family Summary: This resolution creates the Environmental Sustainability and Insurance Program (PROSAS) and enables the creation of the reforestation initiative ForestAR 2030. It aims to promote investments in new forestry ventures and in the extensions of existing forests, and is based on Law 25.080. ForestAR is an inter-ministerial strategy that aims to consolidate the country as a sustainable forestry power by 2030, promoting the creation of a competitive and sustainable market, where reforestation promotes social, economic and environmental development. It entails the creation of an insurance programme to sustain forestry activities dedicated to reforestation and enrichment of primary forests.
Document Title: Joint resolution 1/2018 creating the Environmental and Insurance Sustainability Program

Family Name: National Wildlife Strategy 2030
Family Summary:
Kenya's National Wildlife Strategy 2030 is based on four pillars:
  1. Resilient Ecosystems
  2. Engagement by all Kenyans
  3. Evidence based Decision Making
  4. Sustainability and Governance
It recognises that climate change places Kenya's wildlife at risk, but also that ecosystem conservation and management can contribute to greater climate resilience by serving as a form of adaptation. It specifically calls for the creation of a National Wildlife Adaptation Strategy, which would determine complementarities between wildlife conservation and climate change adaptation.
Document Title: National Wildlife Strategy 2030

Family Name: National Climate Policy
Family Summary:
The National Climate Policy aims to enable Zimmbabwe to establish the legal structures toregulate businesses in climate-related matters, and enable them to reduce their greenhouse gasesemissions.

The Policy further focuses on adaptation with regard to rural communities and agriculture.
Document Title: National Climate Policy

Family Name: Climate Smart Agriculture Policy
Family Summary: The Climate Smart Agriculture Policy aims at ensuring that farmers and agricultural advisers adopt practices consistent with a changing climate. The Policy is based on the Climate-Smart Agricultural Manual for Agriculture Education in Zimbabwe that was released in 2017, and that discusses the necessary changes to the institutional framework and specific, sectoral agricultural practices.
Document Title: Climate Smart Agriculture Policy

Family Name: National Programme for the recovery of Degraded Ecosystems' Goods and Services
Family Summary: The programme was approved by the ministerial agreement 1030-2018. It is a strategic planning instrument to comply with the General Environmental Law, with the International Commitments of the Framework Convention on Climate Change and the 20/20 Initiative, basically encouraging the Recovery of Degraded Ecosystem Goods and Services in Honduras.
Document Title: National Programme for the recovery of Degraded Ecosystems' Goods and Services

Family Name: Somalia Recovery and Resilience Framework
Family Summary:
The guiding principles are:
- Promote the development of integrated and harmonized policies and strategies for recovery, resilience and disaster risk management, by supporting flexible and adaptive strate- gies to address national development prior- ities that are climate-smart, environmentally friendly, gender-sensitive and addressing the drivers of displacement;
- Strengthen coordination of interventions among stakeholders and aid harmonization, and setting uniform and consistent stan- dards for the implementation of the recov- ery program;
- Promote bottom-up needs based planning at the state and federal levels that support par- ticipatory inter-governmental planning pro- cesses and ownership by all affected groups;
- Establish robust monitoring and evaluation mechanisms for disaster recovery at the pro- grammatic and project levels; and
-  Ensure adequate sequencing, avoid critical gaps and maximise financing available for recovery and resilience building through developing interlinked projects for resilient recovery, and leveraging predictable investments, while ensuring inclusiveness.
Document Title: Somalia Recovery and Resilience Framework

Family Name: National Agriculture Policy Framework 2018-2030
Family Summary: This document aims to modernise the country's agricultural sector, enable investments and a switch to sustainable production. It seeks to improve farmer resilience and promote sustainable agricultural practices in response to climate change.
Document Title: National Agriculture Policy Framework 2018-2030

Family Name: National Plan for the Development of Burundi 2018-2027 (PND BURUNDI 2018-2027)
Family Summary: This document sets the government's development vision for the period 2018-2027. It focuses on five strategic goals: (1) develop growth-promoting sectors for the structural transformation of the economy; (2) develop human capital; (3) ensure sustainable management of the environment, mitigate climate change and improve land use planning (4) strengthen governance, security and the safeguard of national sovereignty and (5) mobilise resources, improve management public spending and develop regional and international cooperation.
Document Title: National Plan for the Development of Burundi 2018-2027 (PND BURUNDI 2018-2027)

Family Name: Climate Change Adaptation Strategy
Family Summary:
This Strategy sets out the impacts of climate change and the course of action in Liechtenstein for the following sectors: water management,  natural hazards, agriculture, forestry, energy, tourism, biodiversity, health, and urban planning.

The most pressing changes that are identified include increasing temperatures in the summer and winter, changes in seasonal precipitation, and an increase in extreme weather events as well as a shift in the snow line.

The Strategy outlines already existing and planned activities. It further sets out an implementation plan. Key areas are identified where further measures are needed. Those include, in particular, water resources management, flood protection, biodiversity protection and healthcare during heat waves.

Family Name: Kiribati Climate Change Policy
Family Summary:
The Kiribati Climate Change Policy is based on seven fundamental principles: 
  1. Safeguarding communities and the country as a whole from the adverse impacts of climate change and disasters and ensuring a safe and resilient Kiribati with a healthy environment for all
  2. Mainstreaming climate change and disaster risk reduction into development planning, policies, strategies, sector plans, and decision-making and budgeting processes at both national and local level
  3. Emphasizing that adaptation, mitigation and disaster risk management are shared responsibilities that require coordinated, integrated, multi-partner, multi-sectoral and whole-of-government or whole-of-island approaches
  4. Strengthening key institutions and capacities as a basis for enhanced action and measures to ensure implementation is conducted in an efficient manner
  5. Focusing on actions that will strengthen the long-term resilience of Kiribati communities through sustainable environmental, social and economic benefits that combine the use of modern technologies with the preservation of traditional knowledge
  6. Ensuring that adaptation, mitigation and disaster risk management are equitable, inclusive, gender-sensitive, community-driven and participatory, and reflect the commitments that Kiribati has agreed to under various multilateral frameworks
  7. Strengthening and maintaining strategic partnerships both internally and externally
It further establishes national priorities for climate change in ten specific sectors. Important objectives of the policy include integrated coastal zone management, natural resource management, food and water supply management, incentivizing renewable energy and energy efficiency, strengthening ecosystem conservation, improving public awareness of the health effects of climate change, implementing the government's national disaster risk management plan, and improving climate finance.
Document Title: Kiribati Climate Change Policy

Family Name: Strategy and action plan for adaptation to climate change in Luxembourg 2018-2023
Family Summary:
1. This document sets out the government's adaptation strategy for the period 2018-2023. A set of adaptation measures are proposed in the fields of energy, infrastructure, water management, urban environment management, agriculture, etc. The plan notably outlines strategies to: expand awareness on the object of energy savings and the expansion of decentralised solar energy;
  2. expand biomass power plants taking into account aspects of sustainability in the framework for the national review of the EU climate change agreement
  3. adjust building standards in extreme weather conditions
  4. develop infrastructure and initiative measures to reduce vulnerability.

These strategies will be implemented by each ministry within their existing means.
Document Title: Strategy and action plan for adaptation to climate change in Luxembourg 2018-2023

Family Name: National Climate Change Policy 2017-2027
Family Summary:
The National Climate Change Policy establishes 22 strategies in order to ensure that stakeholders address climate change impacts and their causes through the identification, mainstreaming and implementation of adaptation and mitigation measures, while promoting sustainable development.

Its main objectives are 1) promote climate-resilient, social, economic and environmental development, 2) explore low-carbon development opportunities, nationally and internationally, in order to promote the sustainable use of resources, 3) strengthen a framework that promotes climate change governance, international cooperation, capacity building, research and systematic observations, clean technology development, transfer and use, education, training and public awareness. 

The policy sets out  1) strategies that include legal and other institutional arrangements, 2) resources mobilization strategies and advocates for private sector investment, 3) recommends a Monitoring and Evaluation Framework. The objective of the document is to enhance effective policy implementation, ensuring appropriate utilization of resources, communication of results to decision makers and stakeholders for future action.

The implementation of this policy will undergo an independent external evaluation in five years time. The recommendations resulting from this evaluation will then feed into the revision process for the new policy.
Document Title: National Climate Change Policy 2017-2027

Family Name: National Policy for the Preservation, Rehabilitation, and Expansion of Forests (PNPREF)
Family Summary:

The three pillars of this Policy are:• The preservation of biodiversity;• The maintenance of favorable climate for the development of socio-economical activities and agricultural area; and• The respect of Côte d’Ivoire’s international commitments.
Document Title: National Policy for the Preservation, Rehabilitation, and Expansion of Forests (PNPREF)

Family Name: Ethiopia National REDD+ Strategy
Family Summary: Ethiopia's REDD+ strategy aims to guide the long-term conservation, restoration and sustainable economic development of forest ecosystems. REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation) is a voluntary framework for climate change mitigation developed under the UNFCCC, with a focus on the challenges faced by developing countries.
Document Title: Ethiopia National REDD+ Strategy

Family Name: National Electric System Development Program 2018-2032 (Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional 2018-2032)
Family Summary: Mexico’s energy transition strategy, outlined in the Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional 2018-2032, prioritises diversifying the electricity matrix through conventional and clean technologies while addressing climate commitments. Conventional technologies (such as combined cycle, coal, and internal combustion plants) currently supply most of the nation’s electricity but contribute significantly to greenhouse gas emissions (18% of national GHG output). To mitigate environmental impacts, the strategy emphasises phasing out high-pollution units, promoting dual-fuel conversions, and integrating carbon capture technologies. The document declares these measures align with national decarbonization targets, including the Contribución Prevista y Determinada a nivel Nacional (INDC), which aims to cap electricity-sector emissions at 139 million tons of CO2 equivalent by 2030.
Document Title: 2018-2032. Prodesen. National Electric System Development Program (2018-2032. Prodesen. Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional)

Family Name: Saint Lucia’s National Adaptation Plan 2018-2028
Family Summary:

Family Name: National Adaptation Policy 2018-2030 (PNACC) approved by decree 41091-MINAE
Family Summary:
This Policy is proposed as a guiding framework that will guide the country's actions in terms of adaptation. It establishes an overall and sectoral diagnostic about how climate change will impact Costa Rica, synthesises the global and national legal norms under which the government has to place its adaptation efforts, discusses the institutional framework under which these efforts must be undertaken, and develops a strategy. 

The general objective of the policy is to "move towards a model of resilient development of the Costa Rican society, which avoids human losses and moderate the material damages generated by the adverse effects of climate change, contributes to the quality of life of the most vulnerable populations and takes advantage of the opportunities to innovate and transform the productive sectors and ensure the continuity of public services." 

It seeks in particular to strengthen capacities and resilience conditions, reduce vulnerability / damages and losses, and take advantage of opportunities generated by adaptation measures. Human rights, gender equity, focus on indigenous people and integrated solutions are jointly pursued. 

The policy further aims to: 1) improve knowledge management on the effects of climate change, climate services and the development of local and institutional capacities 2) Promote conditions for the resilience of human and natural systems through territorial, marine and coastal planning 3) better manage biodiversity, ecosystems, watersheds and marine and coastal spaces for adaptation 4) adapt public services and make infrastructure resilient 5) adapt eco-competitive production systems 6) foster investment and financial security for climate action.
Document Title: National Adaptation Policy 2018-2030

Family Summary:
This Decree creates the National Climate Change Metric System (SINAMECC) which constitutes the official coordination platform, and institutional and sectoral linkage of the Costa Rican State to facilitate the management and distribution of climate change knowledge and information. SINAMECC will operate as a sub-module of the National Environmental Information System (SINIA) and will be linked to the National Statistics System (SEN). The coordination, operation and execution will be under the responsibility of the Directorate of Climate Change (DCC).

The SINAMECC will allow the compilation and management of the data and information produced by the State on climate change, and where appropriate, of the private sector, academia and civil society, and will guarantee its dissemination, respecting the confidentiality of information that possess that character, of compliance with current regulations.

Family Name: Sri Lanka's Coastal Zone and Coastal Resource Management Plan (CZ&CRMP) for 2024- 2029
Family Summary:
This plan plans to build on post-conflict opportunities to boost the wellbeing of coastal communities. It focuses on shoreline management, conserving coastal habitats, control coastal water pollution, deal with special management areas, and improve regulatory mechanisms. It notably devise strategic schemes to combat floods, sea-level rise and storms. It mandates the country to combat erosion notably by adopting climate compatible technologies and designs for fisheries, tourism and other economic activities located in coastal zones. It also calls for protecting mangroves in order to protect the coast from erosion and ensure carbon storing capabilities. The plan was updated for the 2024-2029 period, in broad alignment. The plan also aims to ensure the availability of contingency measures to mitigate impacts of climate change on coastal features, infrastructure and coastal communities and that systems for timely implementation of such contingency measures and plans are developed. It lists the following proposed actions:

  1. Collate data from all relevant authorities on climate change parameters such as wind patterns, rainfall, temperature, sea level rise, etc. to predict coastal impacts of sea level rise.
  2. establish a database on climate change features relevant to coastal zone management in collaboration with relevant state organisations.
  3. establish links with international agencies/global programmes to obtain data and information on climate change, related features and mitigatory actions.
  4. analyse impacts of climate change and establish systems for timely adaptive and mitigatory action.
  5. Develop an effective mechanism to collaborate with institutions dealing with the scientific and social aspects of natural hazards to minimise impacts and for efficient remedial action.
  6. Coordinate inter-agency action required to mitigate impacts of natural hazards in the Coastal Zone and for remedial measures.
  7. establish a mechanism through which realistic estimates of sea level rise and other climate change impacts are taken into account routinely in erosion management and development in the Coastal Zone.
Document Title: Sri Lanka's Coastal Zone and Coastal Resource Management Plan (CZ&CRMP) for 2024- 2029

Family Name: Organic Law for the comprehensive planning of the special territorial district of the Amazon
Family Summary: The Organic Law for the Comprehensive Planning of the Special Territorial District of the Amazon establishes a framework for integrated territorial planning that addresses social, economic, cultural, and environmental dimensions of the Amazon region. Guided by the principles of Sumak Kawsay (living well) and Ecuador's Constitution, the law prioritises sustainable development, the protection of ecosystems and biodiversity, and the rights of nature. It also emphasises equitable development, respect for cultural heritage, and the active participation of Indigenous communities, peoples, and nationalities in planning and decision-making.A focus on climate change is considered within the law, particularly in its mandates to incorporate climate criteria into local and national planning. Articles 23 and 55 require the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from deforestation and forest degradation, the promotion of sustainable forest and agroforestry management, and the implementation of adaptation and mitigation measures. Article 56 outlines priorities for climate action, including protecting vulnerable populations, biodiversity, and infrastructure, and aligning local efforts with the National Climate Change Strategy. The law underscores coordination among government levels and stakeholders to ensure a unified and effective response to climate challenges in the Amazon.
Document Title: Organic Law for the comprehensive planning of the special territorial district of the Amazon

Family Summary:
The vision of this policy is to include all persons with disabilities in all communities, provincial and national development efforts by 2025. All persons with disabilities shall have equal access to their rights. 

The goal of this policy is to guide action in priority areas to ensure that persons with disabilities enjoy their right to participate effectively in all areas of development in Vanuatu on an equal basis with others.

The Policy has five guiding principles:

  1. Respect;
  2. Shared responsibility;
  3. Autonomy;
  4. Equality of opportunity and non-discrimination;
  5. Melanesian and religious values.

As one of the priority sectors for mainstreaming the rights of persons with disabilities climate change is named. When planning for disaster risk reduction and climate change resilience, persons with disabilities must be included on all levels.

It promotes a "cross-border and integrated European approach covering the whole value chain of the batteries ecosystem, and focusing on sustainability". The plan targets the transport industry as a key sector in need of getting EU-produced batteries.

Family Summary:

1/ Improve forest governance;
2/ Strengthen the protection of residual forests, extend them and manage them sustainably in classified forests;
3/ Restore degraded forest areas in rural areas and build resilience to the effects of climate change.
Finally, this document:
defines the main strategic axes, the actions and activities to be carried out for the preservation and rehabilitation of forests in the protected domain and the classified domain of the State;
specifies the methods for implementing the Strategy and identifies the sources of financing to be mobilised.

Family Name: National Climate Change Action Plan 2018-2022 (NCCAP)
Family Summary:
This plan aims to strengthen the country's path towards sustainable, climate-resilient development while achieving low carbon climate resilient development. It builds on the previous Action Plan spanning the period 2013-2017. The NCCAP consists in three documents, including an Adaptation Technical Analysis Report (volume II), and a Mitigation Technical Analysis Report (volume III).

The Plan seeks in particular to: 1) reduce risks to communities and infrastructure resulting from climate-related disasters such as droughts and floods, 2) Increase food and nutrition security through enhanced productivity and resilience of the agricultural sector in as low- carbon manner as possible, 3) Enhance resilience of the Blue Economy and water sector by ensuring access to and efficient use of water for agriculture, manufacturing, domestic, wildlife and other uses, 4) Increase forest cover to 10% of total land area; rehabilitate degraded lands, including rangelands; increase resilience of the wildlife and tourism sector, 5) Mainstream climate change adaptation into the health sector; and increase the resilience of human settlements, including improved solid waste management in urban areas, 6) Improve energy and resource efficiency in the manufacturing sector, and 7) Climate-proof energy and transport infrastructure; encourage electricity supply based on renewable energy; encourage the transition to clean cooking; and develop sustainable transport systems.
Document Title: National Climate Change Action Plan (NCCAP) 2018-2022: Volume I

Family Name: Present Situation and Future Roadmap of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Sector (White Paper)
Family Summary:
This White Paper is authored by Honourable Barshaman Pun, the Minister of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation of Nepal at the time of publication on 8 May 2018. It outlines the current situation and problems in the field of energy, water resources and irrigation and formulates the future road map for this field according to the available resources, equipment and opportunity. The objectives of the White Paper include fulfilling the energy demand of Nepal by increasing access to renewable and alternative energy, to reduce water-induced disasters, and making weather and flood forecasts more effective.

The future roadmap section sets out that, for water, legal and structural arrangements will be made for the construction and implementation of the Integrated National Water Resources Policy; model action plan, rules and regulation will be prepared in province and local level for irrigation development; and the existing water-induced disaster management policy will be revised. For energy, the Electricity Act and Nepal Electricity Authority Act will be revised; the Renewable Energy Development Act will be formulated; and the Electricity Regulation Commmission will be completed.

The roadmap also sets out future hydropower projects; electricity transmission lines and trade; carbon trading plans; and irrigation construction projects.

Family Name: National Policy of Sustainable Production and Consumption 2018-2030
Family Summary:
This policy aims at strenghtening the maximum number of initiatives that allow Costa Rica to confidently switch to a socio-productivist structure that is socially, environmentally and economically sustainable. These initiatives are notably meant to respond to the objectives set in the Agenda 2030. The Policy was officially approved by Decree no 41032.

According to this document, the mid-term developement of the country must be sustainable, ensure the protection of human rights and be inclusive. The Policy sets seven strategic areas where to seek sustainability: 1) production, 2) agricultural systems, 3) tourism, 4) lifestyle, 5) construction, 6) public purchases, and 7) ensure a reinforcement of institutions. "Green jobs" in particular are deemed essential to contribute to climate change adaptation efforts.
Document Title: Officialization of the National Production and Sustainable Consumption Policy

Family Name: National Policy of Sustainable Production and Consumption 2018-2030
Family Summary:
This policy aims at strenghtening the maximum number of initiatives that allow Costa Rica to confidently switch to a socio-productivist structure that is socially, environmentally and economically sustainable. These initiatives are notably meant to respond to the objectives set in the Agenda 2030. The Policy was officially approved by Decree no 41032.

The Policy sets seven strategic areas where to seek sustainability: 1) production, 2) agricultural systems, 3) tourism, 4) lifestyle, 5) construction, 6) public purchases, and 7) ensure a reinforcement of institutions. Document Title: National Sustainable Production and Consumption Policy 2018-2030

Family Name: Resolution 153/2018 on Losses and Damages in Disasters
Family Summary:
This Resolution provides for the procedure for the evaluation, certification, pricing, accounting, financing, taxation and control of loss and damage occurring in the case of disasters.

The objective of this procedure is to regulate, in the event of a disaster, the evaluation and certification of damages, the accounting of losses and damages, the prices of goods and services offered to victims to compensate for the damages, the provision of financial resources to compensate for the corresponding expenses for the losses and damages caused, as well as the adjustments for the payment of taxes that apply under these circumstances. This includes losses and damages caused by the impact of disaster hazards during the response and recovery stages of disaster situations.

Resolution 159/2019 amended this Resolution to include details relating to transportation budgets.
Document Title: Resolution 153/2018 on Losses and Damages in Disasters

Family Name: National REDD+ Strategy 2017-2027 (NEC decision 126/2017)
Family Summary: The strategy is a key part of the country's response to climate change and of the Green Growth Development agenda as per the National Strategy for Responsible and Sustainable Development. The NRS aims to strengthen sustainability of Papua New Guinea's forest while helping to improve land use planning and management to ensure forests and environments are protected. The ultimate aim is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and reduce the vulnerability of communities to climate change.
Document Title: National REDD+ Strategy 2017-2027 (NEC decision 126/2017)

Family Name: Action Plan to Accelerate Renewables Projects in Tunisia
Family Summary: The Action Plan to Accelerate Renewables Projects in Tunisia is a subsidiary of the 2015 Solar Plan, and aims to facilitate its implementation, reaffirming its goals for 2020 and 2030, and extending ambitions further towards 2050. The action plan sets out goals for government wind and solar energy supply concessions, acquisition of public and private finance, review and revision of authorisation requirements, fast-tracked access for small renewable projects, revision of metering/billing systems, identification of land constraints, creation of an independent regulator and help-desk, and better research systems to forecast supply and demand.
Document Title: Action Plan to Accelerate Renewables Projects in Tunisia

Family Name: Climate Investment Programme  - Operational Framework for Managing and Accessing Climate Finance in the Kyrgyz Republic
Family Summary:
This document was prepared in cooperation with a range of international finance institutions. It aims to finance a range of climate resilient projects that are aligned with climate-related national policies. The programme identifies the following key actions to enable:

  • Improving the quality of climate services;
  • Improving food security from agriculture, through improved water resources, land management and agricultural practices;
  • Making energy supply infrastructure climate resilient;
  • Making transport infrastructure climate resilient;
  • Making municipal water supply climate resilient;
  • Making buildings climate resilient;
  • Increasing the climate resilience of healthcare;
  • Increasing the climate resilience of mining;
  • Enhancing private sector participation in climate resilience;
  • Enhancing the climate resilience of forestry and biodiversity;
  • Enhancing the climate resilience of emergency situations.
Document Title: Climate Investment Programme  - Operational Framework for Managing and Accessing Climate Finance in the Kyrgyz Republic

Family Name: National REDD+ Strategy INDIA
Family Summary: The overarching objective of National REDD+ Strategy (NRPS) of India is to facilitate implementation of REDD+ programme in the country in conformity with relevant international decisions, as well as the national legislative and policy framework for conservation and improvement of forests and the environment.
Document Title: National REDD+ Strategy INDIA

Family Name: Energy Route 2018-2022
Family Summary: The Energy route 2018-2020 presents a strategic and long-term perspective, with a country vision of where the country's energy policy should head. It was developed trough a participatory and decentralised work with a multidimensional approach, taking into account different stakeholders throughout Chile. The plan presents 7 lines of actions which include energy efficiency and low emissions energy generation.
Document Title: Energy Route 2018-2022

Family Name: Sectoral Planning Guidelines for Climate Change Adaptation
Family Summary:
To support these key national sectors in planning for climate change adaptation and achieving resilience by 2050, sectoral adaptation guidelines published by the Department of the Environment, Climate and Communications (DECC) in 2018 have been updated to account for national adaptation progress and to reflect the evolving landscape of international policy and best practice. These guidelines aim to ensure that a coherent and consistent approach to adaptation planning is adopted at national and sectoral levels. The new guidelines draw on the most up-to-date national approaches to change risk assessment (such as the National Climate Change Risk Assessment (NCCRA)) and sources of climate and adaptation information (such as the Irish Climate Change Assessment Report (ICCA), the National Framework for Climate Services (NFCS), and Climate Ireland).

Sectors preparing sectoral adaptation plans under the NAF are required to prepare their plans in line with the process described within these guidelines, while also being aware of the overall requirements regarding the development of sectoral adaptation plans in Sections 5 and 6 of the Climate Action and Low Carbon Development Acts 2015 to 2021 (Climate Act) and the NAF (particularly Chapters 2 and 3). In addition, when preparing sectoral adaptation plans, sectors should consult and take account of the recommendations of the NCCRA Technical Guidance for Sectoral Risk Assessments (EPA, 2024c), and the national and sectoral priorities and targets (such as those related to emissions reductions). The Technical Guidance will ensure that all sectors plan for common and well-accepted climate scenarios, as well as a common understanding of the future climate.
Document Title: Sectoral Planning Guidelines for Climate Change Adaptation

Family Name: National Wetlands Policy (PNZH)
Family Summary:
The National Policy on Wetland Management (PNZH) in Niger aims primarily to improve food security and population well-being through the sustainable management and enhancement of wetland resources. The Policy's vision is that by 2030, wetland ecosystems will be conserved, viable, and sustainably managed to provide essential goods and services, ultimately reducing poverty and contributing to global biodiversity conservation.

The PNZH is built upon four priority strategic axes, including Knowledge and Degradation Control and the Rational Use of wetlands. Critically, the Policy's strategic actions include a focus on climate change and disaster risk management (item 8.2). Specifically, the PNZH aims to leverage wetlands' natural function to mitigate the effects of climate change and reduce disaster risks, such as severe flooding and droughts, thereby reinforcing the overall resilience of local populations and ecosystems. Implementation relies on core guiding principles, requiring the participation of all stakeholders in securing sites, developing management plans, and integrating wetland issues into national and local development policies.
Document Title: National Wetlands Policy (PNZH)

Family Name: National Housing Co-Investment Fund
Family Summary:
The National Housing Co-Investment Fund can provide low-cost repayable loans and/or forgivable loans to build new affordable housing and repair/renew existing affordable and community housing. The Fund is designed to attract partnerships and investments, and to incentivize new construction, repair and renewal that meets or exceeds ambitious mandatory minimum standards for energy efficiency, accessibility and universal design, and proximity to transit.

For new construction, projects must demonstrate that they will either achieve a 25% decrease inenergy consumption and Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions relative to the 2015 National EnergyCode for Buildings or the 2015 National Building Code; OR a 15% decrease relative to the 2017National Energy Code for Buildings.

For repair (renewal), projects must demonstrate that they will achieve a 25% reduction in energy useand Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions relative to past performance.
Document Title: National Housing Co-Investment Fund - Minimum Requirements
