Family Name: Executive Decree N°41095-MP-MTSS
Family Summary:
This decree establishes a series of standards for the inclusion, attention and protection of disabled people in cases of emergency and disaster. The decree explored:

  • The structure and implementation of the standards.
  • The scope of application.
  • Celebrating appropriate consultations and promoting the participation of people with disabilities and their organizations in inclusive management of the economy and the implementation of standards.
  • Information and communication technologies are used for inclusive management and the implementation of standards.
  • National and international cooperation and technical assistance for the implementation of standards.
  • Programmatic planning and assumption for implementing standards and inclusive management of the economy.
Document Title: Executive Decree N°41095-MP-MTSS (Decreto ejecutivo N°41095-MP-MTSS)

Family Name: Strategy for the development of the automotive industry
Family Summary: Order from 28 April 2018
Document Title: Strategy for the development of the automotive industry

Family Name: Guyana's National Forest Plan
Family Summary: The National Forest Plan provides a set of actions and interventions to effectively and sustainably manage Guyana's forest resources, accompanying the National Forest Policy Statement (2018). The plan is driven by four 'specific objectives': deriving sustainable economic benefits; enhancing conservation; enhancing governance to promote sustainable management; and building human and institutional capacity to achieve the above goals. Its interventions for economic benefits are primarily aimed at forestry efficiency improvements and job/revenue growth while reducing deforestation. Its conservation interventions aim to reduce forest fires and pest/disease outbreaks, and improve forest quality monitoring, all while maintaining the share of forest goods and services in GDP. Its governance interventions aim to generally streamline forestry-related proceedings and reduce costs, while maintaining strong and transparent stakeholder contact. Its capacity building interventions aim to enhance research outputs and public engagement, promoting efficiency gains downstream of this.
Document Title: Guyana's National Forest Plan

Family Name: Energy Renovation in Buildings Plan
Family Summary: The fifth-year Energy Renovation in Buildings Plan, released in April 2018, is the government's strategy to meet the challenge of carbon neutrality and improve the purchasing power. The plan offers tools suitable for housing, tertiary and public buildings.The Plan aims at: 1) creating a guarantee fund of more than 50 million euros to help 35,000 low-income households a year; 2) simplifying support for all by transforming the tax credit into a premium and adapting existing loans; 3) enhancing the reliability of the energy label of homes through diagnosis of energy performance (DPE); 4) better training professionals and better controlling the quality of work by reforming the label RGE (recognized guarantor of the environment), investing 30 million euros in the training of professionals and 40 million euros in innovation; 5) encouraging a massive renovation of public buildings of the State and communities by mobilizing 4.8 billion euros; and 6) missioning a start-up to support the renovation of public buildings of local authorities by pooling resources to consolidate contracts, reduce costs and remove contractual, legal and institutional obstacles.
Document Title: Energy Renovation in Buildings Plan

Family Name: Energy Methanisation for Nitrogen Autonomy Plan
Family Summary:
The Energy Methanisation Nitrogen Autonomy (EMAA) Plan was launched by the Ministry of Agriculture and Food and the Ministry of Ecological and Inclusive Transition. The reduction of nitrogen emissions is meant to contribute towards climate change mitigation.

The EMAA plan aims to:

  • manage nitrogen across the territories, by promoting organic nitrogen, in particular that from livestock effluents, and by reducing the dependence of French agriculture on mineral nitrogen. This logic is based on greater autonomy for farms, whether in terms of animal feed or in terms of the use of synthetic fertilisers. The EMAA plan therefore reduces total nitrogen inputs in territories where they are in excess and, to a certain extent, to substitute mineral nitrogen with organic nitrogen, on site and elsewhere. This plan is part of an agronomic approach based on respect for the balance of fertilisation and the overall reduction of the use of inputs ;
  • develop a "French model of agricultural methanisation" to make intermediate-sized collective agricultural methanisation a source of additional income for farms, by using nitrogen and promoting the development of more renewable energy anchored in the territories, with a view to sustainable agriculture and energy and ecological transition. The objective is to develop 1,000 on-farm methanisers in France by 2020, compared to 90 at the end of 2012.
Document Title: Energy Methanisation Nitrogen Autonomy Plan

Family Name: Government Decision no. 373/2018 on the National Pollutant Release and Transfer Register
Family Summary: Government Decision no. 373/2018 establishes a National Pollutant Release and Transfer Register, an automated and centralised system operated by the Ministry of Environment. This system records air, soil and water pollutants, as well as off-site transfers of polluting material. The decision stipulates that this registry must be made available to the public through sharing the UNFCCC and a range of other means, with a separate procedure for exceptions.
Document Title: Government Decision no. 373/2018 on the National Pollutant Release and Transfer Register

Family Name: Development Programme of the Kyrgyz Republic for the period 2018-2022
Family Summary:
This document was approved by decree no. 2377-VI of 2018. It seeks to enhance the country's mitigation, adaptation and disaster risk management actions.
It notably states that the government will propose mechanisms for the creation of new investment funds (venture, green climate, trust, sovereign funds and development funds).
Document Title: Development Programme of the Kyrgyz Republic for the period 2018-2022

Family Name: National Disaster Response Plan (RESPONDE Ec)
Family Summary: The National Disaster Response Plan (RESPONDE Ec) establishes a comprehensive framework for addressing natural and anthropogenic emergencies, guided by constitutional provisions such as Articles 261 and 389, which emphasise state responsibility for disaster management and risk reduction. The plan outlines an organisational, technical, and operational structure for interinstitutional coordination under the National Decentralized Risk Management System (SNDGR). It prioritises timely and efficient resource utilisation, protecting lives and property, maintaining governance during crises, and fostering community resilience through early recovery initiatives.Aligned with Ecuador's climate commitments, the plan integrates climate change considerations into disaster response and risk management strategies. It acknowledges the impact of climate-driven phenomena like forest fires, emphasising their links to changing atmospheric conditions and highlighting the need for preparedness to reduce vulnerabilities. Specific measures include strengthening the capacity of emergency operations committees, improving response times, and ensuring comprehensive recovery efforts that align with sustainable development goals.
Document Title: National Disaster Response Plan (RESPONDE Ec)

Family Name: REDD+ National Strategy
Family Summary:
The objectives include the following:

1. To reduce carbon emission, enhance carbon sequestration and enhance climate resilience through both mitigation and adaptation approaches by minimizing the causes and effects of drivers of deforestation and forest degradation, and intensifying sustainable management of forest resources and across the ecological regions.

2. To ensure fair and equitable sharing of carbon and non-carbon benefits of forests among right holders with effective implementation of safeguard measures.

3. To increase livelihood assets and diversify employment opportunities of forest dependent communities, particularly poor, women, IPs and Dalits.

4. To improve and harmonize policy and legal framework to harness carbon and non-carbon benefits; strengthen institutional capability and improve governance of forest agencies and sector

5. To establish and maintain a robust National Forest Monitoring System with strong monitoring, reporting and verification mechanisms.
Document Title: REDD+ National Strategy

Family Name: Basic Environment Plan
Family Summary:
Japan's Basic Environmental Plan defines the principles that govern the implementation of environmental policies in Japan, especially with respect to climate change policies. It also outlines the current policy frameworks in place for government environment- and climate change-related policy matters and proposes new areas of priority for the government. The policy priorities related to climate change the plan lists include:
  • Promoting research and development of emissions reduction technologies
  • Promoting energy conservation
  • Promoting adaptation measures in regional agriculture and disaster prevention sectors
  • Implementing national policy frameworks, such as the Plan for Global Warming Countermeasures.
Document Title: Basic Environment Plan

Family Name: The Swedish Marine and Water Authority's work on the action plan for climate adaptation
Family Summary:
This action plan aims to adapt operations to a changing climate so that the resilience of ecosystems is strengthened rather than weakened. Other climate adaptation measures will be worked into the action plan gradually.

Measures that contribute to increased resilience to climate change include:

- Effective cooperation between the working areas, marine area protection, green infrastructure, maritime planning, water environment and marine environment management. G

- Green infrastructure: Promoting natural climate adaptation solutions such as restoration of wetlands and floodplains.

- Taking increased action against other environmental pressures such as eutrophication and toxicants to increase the resilience of ecosystems to the effects of a changing climate and ocean acidification. The authority's action work takes into account the effects of a changing climate and links to climate adaptation and limited climate impact.

- Promoting adaptation in collaborations: Working actively for climate adaptation within the framework of the authority's national, European and global collaborations.
Document Title: The Swedish Marine and Water Authority's work on the action plan for climate adaptation

Family Name: Agro-Sylvo-Pastoral Sector Policy (2018-2027)
Family Summary: Burkina Faso's Agro-Sylvo-Pastoral Sector Policy (2018-2027) aims to promote the sustainable development and management of the agricultural sector. It aims to increase productivity while combating land degradation and increasing the resilience of agricultural systems to climate change, emphasising water storage and distribution as a key factor in climate adaptation. Alongside proposing improvements in governance, subsidy access and market efficiency, the policy aims to increase the number of protected forest areas, and put more existing protected areas under management, contributing to land-based climate mitigation efforts.
Document Title: Agro-Sylvo-Pastoral Sector Policy (2018-2027)

Family Name: National REDD+ Strategy of Congo
Family Summary: This strategy seeks to combat the direct and underlying causes of deforestation and forest degradation in the country. It covers the period 2018-2030.
Document Title: National REDD+ Strategy of Congo

Family Name: Marine and Water Authority's climate strategy 2018-2020
Family Summary:
Based on the Marine and Water Authority's mission and vision of living oceans, lakes and watercourses, and the environmental analysis in the appendix, the Authority's objectives are:

- Contribute to reduced greenhouse gas emissions and the energy transition by creating the conditions for sustainable renewable energy.

- Work both nationally and internationally for the restoration and protection of natural environments that can function as natural carbon sinks, such as eelgrass meadows, salt marshes and mangrove forests.

- Intensify internal environmental work to reduce the authority's own climate impact.

The Authority works with climate adaptation in the following ways:

- Promote measures that contribute to climate adaptation by increasing the resilience of ecosystems.

- Integrate climate adaptation into work processes such as action programs, guidelines, environmental assessments and statements.

- Promote climate adaptation in the authority's collaborations, networks and stakeholder dialogues.
Document Title: Marine and Water Authority's climate strategy 2018-2020

Family Name: Regulations Respecting Reduction in the Release of Methane and Certain Volatile Organic Compounds (Upstream Oil and Gas Sector) (SOR/2018-66)
Family Summary: These regulations impose requirements on the oil and gas sector in order to reduce emissions of methane and certain volatile organic compounds, and designate the contravention of certain of its provisions as serious offences by adding them to the schedule to the Regulations Designating Regulatory Provisions for Purposes of Enforcement (Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999).
Document Title: Regulations Respecting Reduction in the Release of Methane and Certain Volatile Organic Compounds (Upstream Oil and Gas Sector) (SOR/2018-66)

Family Name: Regulations Respecting Reduction in the Release of Methane and Certain Volatile Organic Compounds (Upstream Oil and Gas Sector) (SOR/2018-66)
Family Summary: These regulations impose requirements on the oil and gas sector in order to reduce emissions of methane and certain volatile organic compounds, and designate the contravention of certain of its provisions as serious offences by adding them to the schedule to the Regulations Designating Regulatory Provisions for Purposes of Enforcement (Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999).
Document Title: Regulations Respecting Reduction in the Release of Methane and Certain Volatile Organic Compounds (Upstream Oil and Gas Sector) (SOR/2018-66)

Family Name: Enhanced Methane Regulations
Family Summary: In December 2025, the Minister of the Environment, Climate Change and Nature, announced final regulations to reduce methane emissions from the oil and gas sector and landfills across Canada. The regulations form a key pillar of the new Climate Competitiveness Strategy. The new regulations apply to onshore oil and gas production, gas processing plants, LNG, and transmission facilities. They build on Canada's 2018 methane regulations by establishing stronger requirements to reduce methane emissions. The regulations come into force in 2028 for the oil and gas sector. They expand on the regulations introduced in 2018.
Document Title: Regulations Respecting Reduction in the Release of Methane and Certain Volatile Organic Compounds (SOR/2018-66)

Family Name: The National Plan for Disaster Response
Family Summary: The objective of the National Plan for Disaster Response is to guarantee attention to the population affected by dangerous, natural or anthropogenic events, with the establishment of procedures and protocols, generating adequate coordination and inter-institutional coordination. The plan notably focuses on natural disasters as flood and drought. Specific objectives are 1) to provide to the institutions of the National DGR System a tool that guides the fulfillment of the functions, procedures and actions that they must develop during the response to emergencies and disasters, 2) protect life and assets of the affected population, 3)maintain governance and governability during the response, 4) guarantee the planned and orderly intervention of the authorities and institutions through the Emergency Operations Committees, 4)optimize time and available resources during response operation,5) generate the foundations for the recovery process.
Document Title: The National Plan for Disaster Response

Family Name: National Action Plan for Electric Mobility
Family Summary:
"The objectives of this Action Plan include:

- Undertake a comprehensive review of current gaps, barriers and challenges to the implementation and/or advancement of the NDC’s transport provisions;

- Identify and conceptualize clear and concrete action to support implementation of the transport provisions of the NDC;

- Engage a comprehensive range of stakeholders, including public and private sectors and consumers, in participatory dialogue, prioritization and action planning for electric mobility;

- Build the capacity of government partners, civil society and transport operators to support and advance the transport provisions of the NDC."
Document Title: National Action Plan for Electric Mobility

Family Name: Water and Environment Strategic Investment Plan 2018-2030
Family Summary: The plan, developed in partnership between the Ministry of Water and Environment (MWE) and a US team at Industrial Economics (IEc), establishes long term investment priorities in the water and environment sectors, aiming to facilitate sustainable socioeconomic development while adapting to climate change and maintaining ecosystems valuable to emissions mitigation. A key focus is physical and human capital investment, such as enhancing water storage, wastewater disposal, community training. It also provides for improved weather stations, for weather information distribution, and significant funding for the rehabilitation of wetlands and forests.
Document Title: Water and Environment Strategic Investment Plan 2018-2030

Family Name: Offshore Wind Energy Roadmap 2030
Family Summary: This roadmap is set out by the Dutch Ministry for the Economy and Climate to foster new offshore wind generation in the country by 2030. The plan sets out a target of additional capacity of 4.5 GW to be added by 2023 and 7 GW between 2024 and 2030. The document also deals with grid connection for specific wind farms.
Document Title: Offshore Wind Energy Roadmap 2030

Family Name: Ordinance MMA No. 76/2018 on the National Programme for the Conservation of the Coastline
Family Summary: The National Programme for the Conservation of the Coastline aims to promote the integrated management of the coastline, its technical and scientific knowledge, its variations according to extreme events and climate change, multiple uses and the protection of marine and coastal ecosystems.
Document Title: Ordinance MMA No. 76/2018

Family Name: CONPES 3919/2018 - National Policy of Sustainable Building
Family Summary: This policy aims to integrate sustainability into the life cycle of buildings by using transition tools, monitoring, control mechanisms, and financial incentives, targeting sustainable construction initiatives through 2025. The policy complies with the stipulations of the National Development Plan 2014-2018 "All for a New Country," deepening the vision of the National Green Growth Strategy and the sectoral mitigation action plan for housing and territorial development (2014), as part of the Colombian Low Carbon Development Strategy. Moreover, the policy supports international commitments like the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), focusing on sustainable cities (Goal 11), sustainable consumption and production (Goal 12), reducing GHG emissions (Paris Agreement), and following the New Urban Agenda set at Habitat III.
Document Title: CONPES 3919/2018 - National Policy of Sustainable Building

Family Name: National REDD+ Strategy of Côte d'Ivoire
Family Summary:
This Strategy includes climate change-related measures, including strengthening the resilience of agricultural production systems to climate change through the restoration of forest cover in production areas. Other objectives include reducing poverty by increasing the productivity of village plantations of cocoa, rubber, oil palm, and cashew nuts in order to increase producers' incomes and livelihoods; and improving food security by promoting food crops in conjunction with reforestation and perennial crops.

There will be the creation of a working group on the theme of climate change within the Public-Private Partnership platform
Document Title: National REDD+ Strategy of Côte d'Ivoire

Family Name: Clean Air programme (Czyste Powietrze)
Family Summary:
The "Clean Air" is the first nationwide program of subsidies for replacing old furnaces and insulating single-family houses. It is established by the National Fund for Environmental Protection and Water Management, and the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The overall aim of the program is fighting smog. It follows the idea that the lower the income, the higher the subsidy. You can receive financial support for projects that are completed (except pre-financed grants), in progress or have not yet started.

Financial support can be received by the following:

  • an energy audit that will allow you to obtain complete information such as:
    • insulate the building most effectively,
    • choose the best heat source for your home,
    • get the maximum subsidy and then pay lower heating bills,
    • insulation of walls, ceiling, floor,
    • replacement of windows, doors, garage gate,
    • replacing an old furnace – a solid fuel boiler (coal, wood) – with a modern heat source,
    • central heating (central heating) and domestic hot water (hot water) installation,
    • mechanical ventilation with heat recovery,
    • photovoltaic micro-installation.

You can receive

  • Up to PLN 135,000 in the case of the highest level of funding with comprehensive thermal modernization.
  • Up to PLN 99,000 in the increased and up to PLN 66,000 in the basic level of funding.
  • Additionally, energy audit: up to PLN 1,200.
Document Title: Information page „Czyste Powietrze”

Family Name: Decree No. 2018-191/PRN/ME/DD determining the terms and conditions for implementing Law No. 2004-040 on forestry
Family Summary:
The Decree n. 2018-191/PRN/ME/DD provides the application rules for Niger's Forestry Law (Law 2004-040), structured across seven titles. Title 1 (General Provisions) establishes the administrative framework, defines the national forest domain, and mandates the National Forestry Inventory and National Forestry Plan.

A key climate-related element is found in Article 10 within Title 1, which explicitly requires the National Forestry Inventory to track the stocks of sequestered carbon, directly linking the decree to national climate mitigation efforts.
Document Title: Decree No. 2018-191/PRN/ME/DD

Family Name: Government Decree No. 2018-263 to operationalise the implementation of the Paris Agreement
Family Summary: This decree establishes a management unit to monitor and coordinate activities relating to the implementation of the Paris Agreement. It defines its missions, its organisation and the modalities of its functioning.
Document Title: Government Decree No. 2018-263 to operationalise the implementation of the Paris Agreement

Family Name: Action Plan: Financing Sustainable Growth
Family Summary: This action plan specifically aims to 1) reorient capital flows towards sustainable investment in order to achieve sustainable and inclusive growth, 2) manage financial risks stemming from climate change, resource depletion, environmental degradation and social issues, and 3) foster transparency and long-termism in financial and economic activity.The renewed strategy is intended to implement the aims of the Action Plan on Financing Sustainable Growth.
Document Title: Renewed sustainable finance strategy and implementation of the action plan on financing sustainable growth

Family Name: Action Plan: Financing Sustainable Growth
Family Summary: This action plan specifically aims to 1) reorient capital flows towards sustainable investment in order to achieve sustainable and inclusive growth, 2) manage financial risks stemming from climate change, resource depletion, environmental degradation and social issues, and 3) foster transparency and long-termism in financial and economic activity.The renewed strategy is intended to implement the aims of the Action Plan on Financing Sustainable Growth.
Document Title: Action Plan: Financing Sustainable Growth

Family Name: Sweden: National strategy for climate change adaptation 2018
Family Summary: The National Climate Strategy concerns municipal land and water use, municipal development and preservation of the built environment.
Document Title: Sweden: National strategy for climate change adaptation 2018

Family Name: Ministerial Decree of March 2, 2018, promoting the use of biomethane in the transport sector
Family Summary: This Decree aims at valuing agricultural waste and raise the share of renewable energy in the transport sector.The document defines the connection conditions of biomethane production plants to the natueral gas network, discusses the quality and sustainability of biomethane, and examines means of promoting biomethane in transport. The inisterial Decree of 5 August 2022 specifies the conditions upon which biomethane production plants have access to the incentives provided for by Ministerial Decree of March 2, 2018
Document Title: Ministerial Decree of 5 August 2022, interpreting the Ministerial Decree of 2 March 2018 on incentives for the production of biomethane

Family Name: National Water Policy, 2018
Family Summary: Pakistan's first National Water Policy emerges from a threat of imminent water crises in the country, and sets policy objectives and strategic priorities for 2018-2030. Among other things, the NWP envisions policies and practical efforts in the area of irrigated agriculture, drinking water and sanitation, urban water management and sustainable infrastructure. Many important goals also depend on cooperation with neighbouring countries for transboundary rivers.The federal government budget crucially sees an increase in the percentage investment in the water sector from 10% in 2018 to 20% by 2030. Further, the NWP is a national level policy offering guidelines to achieve targets. More detailed regulations for local water resources is entrusted to provincial governments.
Document Title: National Water Policy, 2018

Family Name: Ministerial Decree concerning the issuance by the Belgian government of a bond series - Green bonds (“Green OLO”)
Family Summary:
The first edition of green bonds, issued by the Belgian state was in February 2018. The second issue of green government bonds was issued on 14 September 2022, and raised EUR 4.5 Billion.

The “Green OLO” is used as a tool to channel investments into green assets at the national, regional, and international level, through this contributing to the transition of the economy towards a lob-carbon, more resilient, and more environmentally friendly society.

The new green bonds are in the running for almost 17 years, ending on 22 April 2039. The issues have gone through a selection process, in which their environmental and climate impact is evaluated by the Climate Change Department, in which the results will be reported. For the second issue the following sectors were selected:

  • Clean transport
  • Energy efficiency (including green buildings)
  • Renewable energy
  • Circular economy (including waste and water management)
  • Living resources and land use
Document Title: Ministerial Decree concerning the issuance by the Belgian government of a bond series (Green bonds (“Green OLO”) 2022)

Family Name: Action plan to address the impacts of drought and water scarcity
Family Summary:
The aim of the Action Plan to Address the Impacts of Drought and Water Scarcity (Action Plan) is to prevent drought through preventive measures, to eliminate the negative impacts of climate change. Drought is a natural phenomenon, while water scarcity is strongly influenced by anthropogenic activity

The Action Plan provides a set of options for natural and socio-economic systems to adapt to ongoing or expected climate change, with the aim of reducing potential negative impacts and benefiting from the positive effects of climate change.
Document Title: Action plan to address the impacts of drought and water scarcity

Family Name: National strategy on Community Forestry
Family Summary:
This National Strategy for Community Forestry aims to strengthen the capacity of provincial authorities and ensure that the country’s community forestry laws do in fact include and benefit communities. The plan calls for an “experimental phase” over the next five years to gradually provide access to areas of the roughly 700,000 square kilometres of available forest through community management permits and to test different approaches to community forestry through a number of officially recognised pilot projects.

The implementation of the National Strategy should be ensured on four axes:

1. the establishment of a steering committee (national and provincial);

2. the regular convening of the Roundtable on Community Forestry (at both national and provincial levels) to intensify the dialogue between stakeholders involved;

3. establishing a database of local community forest concessions;

4. ongoing monitoring of these concessions to assess the impact on forest protection, as well as drivers of deforestation and degradation.

In French: Stratégie Nationale pour la Foresterie Communautaire.
Document Title: National strategy on Community Forestry

Family Name: National Strategy for the Mobilisation of Biomass (Stratégie Nationale de Mobilisation de la Biomasse)
Family Summary:
Strategic planning regarding the development and use of biomass in France. It highlights the different categories that might be mobilised; sustainability criteria and good practice; an estimation of the amount of biomass that would be necessary to satisfy energy needs; the current legislative framework (national and European) regulating biomass energy; production and mobilisation targets; complementary measures necessary to reach the targets; an evaluation of import needs; modalities of monitoring and evaluation.

Un récapitulatif des politiques et mesures sectorielles nationales ou communautaires ayant un impact sur l'évolution des ressources de biomasse non alimentaire, sur leur mobilisation et sur la demande en biomasse non alimentaire

Une évaluation quantitative de toutes les ressources de biomasse-énergie mobilisables aux échéances mentionnées à l'article D. 211-1 » 20, « compte tenu des leviers et contraintes technico-économiques, sociales et environnementales ; les ressources prises en compte pour cette évaluation comprennent l'ensemble des catégories de biomasse susceptible d'avoir un usage énergétique

Des objectifs de production et de mobilisation des ressources de biomasse susceptible d'avoir un usage énergétique, aux échéances considérées, assortis de trajectoires de développement et déclinés par région.

Pour le secteur forestier, aux échéances considérées par le programme national de la forêt et du bois mentionné à l'article L. 121-2-2 du code forestier, les objectifs mentionnés au précédent alinéa sont ceux fixés par ce programme ; pour la filière biomasse issue des déchets, aux échéances considérées par le plan national de prévention et de gestion des déchets mentionné à l'article L. 541-11 du code de l'environnement, ils sont ceux fixés par ce plan 17 ;

Les mesures complémentaires nécessaires pour atteindre les objectifs définis au 6° 17 ;

Une évaluation des importations de biomasse nécessaires pour satisfaire les besoins mentionnés au 3°, compte tenu des objectifs définis au 6° 17 ;

Les modalités d'évaluation et de suivi de sa mise en œuvre, comprenant la mise en place d'indicateurs, ainsi que les dispositions permettant de garantir l'atteinte des objectifs fixés, notamment les conditions de mise en œuvre des mesures mentionnées au 7°
Document Title: National Strategy for the Mobilisation of Biomass (Stratégie Nationale de Mobilisation de la Biomasse)

Family Name: Decree No. 2.19.452 on the National Committee for Sustainable Development
Family Summary:
The decree no 2.17.655 creates the Strategic Committee for Sustainable Development, which will also oversee climate change matters. The decree comes as an application of framework law no 99.12, art. 15, on the establishment of an evaluation and monitoring system to achieve its objectives and to control and rectify, if necessary, the actions taken on this subject. The Committee will also be responsible for monitoring the National Strategy for Sustainable Development presented on June 25, 2017, and to ensure that sectoral policies comply with the Strategy's overall goals.

The decree no 2.19.452 relating to the organisation of the National Committee for Sustainable Development was published on June 29, 2019, replaces the former decree to put Morocco better in line with its 2030 sustainable objectives. This document notably states that he High Commission for Planning is a member of this committee, responsible for preparing reports on the SDGs.
Document Title: Decree No. 2.19.452 organized by the National Committee for Sustainable Development

Family Name: Programme for the Promotion of the Green Economy in the Republic of Moldova 2018-2020
Family Summary: Moldova's Programme for the Promotion of the Green Economy (2018-2020) is a broad economy-wide programme and action plan for mainstreaming environmental sustainability. It contains a key aim to promote the inclusion of climate adaptation and mitigation considerations in new legislation and government documentation across sectors. Carbon dioxide emissions and economic carbon intensity are given as major progress indicators for the success of the programme to be evaluated against. The programme aims for a 17% renewable share of gross final energy consumption and an 8.2% increase in energy efficiency (baseline 2018) by 2020.
Document Title: Programme for the Promotion of the Green Economy in the Republic of Moldova 2018-2020

Family Name: Strategic Development Plan of the Republic of Kazakhstan until 2025
Family Summary: The priorities of this plan are to accelerate national economic growth and improve people’s quality of life. It seeks to promote the development of climate suitable and green technologies to improve energy efficiency in the country. It further revises the national environmental regulations to incorporate the ‘polluter pays’ principle, aimed at incentivising polluting enterprises to reduce their emissions.
Document Title: Presidential Decree No. 636 validating the Strategic Development Plan of the Republic of Kazakhstan until 2025

Family Name: Presidential Decree No. 45/18 approving the Statute of the Ministry of Environment (MINAMB)
Family Summary: This Presidential Decree modifies the structure and functions of the Ministry of Environment (MINAMB) in order to respond to the new challenges the Executive faces in this area. It consists of 33 articles divided into four Chapters and three Annexes, and it establishes the composition, duties and responsibilities of MINAMB. As part of the modifications it creates a Climate Change Cabinet, in charge of promoting and coordinating climate change adaptation and mitigation projects/programs. It also establishes a National Environment Fund. This document replaces Presidential Decree 85/14
Document Title: Presidential Decree No. 45/18 approving the Statute of the Ministry of Environment (MINAMB)

Family Name: Minimum Energy Performance Standards for air conditioners
Family Summary: Airconditioners cannot be sold by the manufacturer and/or importers in the Chilean market if they have a energy rating inferior to A, meaning that only air conditioners with an energy efficiency index (índice de eficiencia energética - IEE) superior to 3.20 will be allowed on the market. Concerning compact air conditioners, only those with an IEE is above 3.00 will be permitted to be sold.
Document Title: Minimum Energy Performance Standards for air conditioners

Family Name: Decree-Law no. 4/2018 on incentives to electric mobility
Family Summary: This Decree-Law creates an incentive to promote the replacement of fossil fuels with electricity for the supply of municipal public passenger transport vehicles. The regime provided for in this decree-law expires on December 31, 2025.The price of electric energy used in the supply of electric vehicles for the municipal and intermunicipal public passenger transport service and for the activity of collecting undifferentiated waste and recyclable materials is subject to a discount. This discount will be revised every couple of years.
Document Title: Decree-Law no. 4/2018 on incentives to electric mobility

Family Name: Updated National Strategy for Sustainable Tourism Development (2014-2030)
Family Summary: The updated National Strategy for Sustainable Tourism Development 2014–2030 aims to foster a tourism sector in Bulgaria that balances economic growth, social well-being, and environmental and cultural preservation. Strategic objectives focus on creating a favorable business and natural environment for sustainable tourism, with measures including institutional capacity building, regulatory framework development, quality management systems, infrastructure improvement, climate change adaptation, human resource development among others. Key actions include integrating sustainability and climate adaptation into tourism education, promoting responsible use of protected areas.
Document Title: Updated National Strategy for Sustainable Tourism Development (2014-2030)

Family Name: Rwanda's National Forest Policy
Family Summary: The National Forest Policy aims to guide the long-term management, conservation and development of Rwanda's forest resources. It notes the importance of forest carbon sequestration for climate mitigation, and the need to ensure that forests and the resources they provide are also resilient to the effects of climate change. The policy aims to ensure sustainable forestry management at all levels, securing biomass supply for rural communities while preventing ecosystem degradation. It supports additional climate-resilient actions such as agroforestry development, and promotes seeking national and international climate finance to support climate-safe forest usage and recovery.
Document Title: Rwanda's National Forest Policy

Family Name: Maldives’ nationally determined contribution (NDC) implementation plan
Family Summary: Maldvies' NDC Implementation Plan is being developed to monitor and evaluate the implementation of the actions proposed in the NDC to ensure that Maldives meet the commitments to the implementation of the Paris Agreement.
Document Title: Maldives’ nationally determined contribution (NDC) implementation plan

Family Name: Seychelles Blue Economy Strategic Policy Framework and Roadmap
Family Summary: This document was prepared for the Seychelles and approved by the cabinet. It notably examines how to enhance resilience and adaptation to climate change.
Document Title: Seychelles Blue Economy Strategic Policy Framework and Roadmap

Family Name: National Action Plan for Forest Biomass Energy 2018-2027
Family Summary: The National Action Plan for Energy from Forest Biomass 2018–2027 sets out a strategic framework to promote the sustainable use of forest biomass for energy across Bulgaria. It focuses on assessing and mobilising the potential of forest biomass while ensuring that harvesting respects forest sustainability and biodiversity. The plan aims to increase the use of biomass for district heating, electricity, and combined heat and power, supporting local communities and small to medium-sized enterprises in the energy sector.
Document Title: National Action Plan for Forest Biomass Energy 2018-2027

Family Name: National Adaptation Plan 2018
Family Summary: This National Adaptation Plan has been endorsed by the Fijian government and has been prepared by national policymakers in coordination with a group of international actors. It contains 160 adaptation measures to be prioritised over five years.
Document Title: National Adaptation Plan 2018

Family Name: National Green Economy Strategy 2018-2027
Family Summary: Burkina Faso's National Green Economy Strategy for 2018-2027 aims to promote sustainable economic growth while contributing to international efforts to mitigate climate change. With a focus on synergising green development with increased employment opportunities, it promotes public transport, increased recycling and waste management, and an expansion of activity in the water management sector. It also contains broad objectives to improve long-term governance, climate-sustainable production/consumption, green entrepreneurship, and the general administration of this strategy (including the formation of action plans).
Document Title: National Green Economy Strategy 2018-2027

Family Name: Regulation on the establishment of the inter-sector co-ordination Commission for policy and mitigation and adaptation measures for climate change
Family Summary: This decision establishes a commission to provide recommendations to the Croatian government on overarching climate policy, and the mitigation and adaptation measures it contains. This commission will recommend, monitor and evaluate climate policy, and will appoint technical working groups on low-carbon development and mitigation, drawn from a range of expert sources inside and outside the state. The decision places administrative and technical responsibilities for this commission onto the Ministry of Environment and Energy.
Document Title: Regulation on the establishment of the inter-sector co-ordination Commission for policy and mitigation and adaptation measures for climate change

Family Name: National Forest Policy Statement (2018-2028)
Family Summary: The National Forest Policy Statement (2018) promotes and establishes a shared vision for Guyana's forests and their use, covering the period 2018 to 2028. Its four overarching objectives are: to derive economic benefits from the forestry sector; forest conservation; forest social governance; and building capacity for more effective delivery of the above aims. The policy aims to value the country's forests for more than timber, while also promoting the efficiency of the timber sector and better integrating wood into the construction sector as a sustainable low-carbon resource. It notes the key role of Guyanese forests in global and national carbon sequestration, preserving them as a net carbon sink.
Document Title: National Forest Policy Statement (2018)

Family Name: Royal Decree No. 6/2018 - Creates the Interministerial Commission for the incorporation of ecological criteria in public procurement
Family Summary:
This Royal Decree creates the Inter-ministerial Commission for the incorporation of ecological criteria in public procurement, in order to achieve environmental policies related to climate change, the use of resources and sustainable production and consumption.

The Commission is attached as a collegiate body to the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Food and Environment, and aims to guarantee the coordination of the General State Administration (AGE), its Public Organizations and the common services and the Social Security Management Entities, in the incorporation and use of ecological criteria in public procurement.
Document Title: Royal Decree No. 6/2018 - Creates the Interministerial Commission for the incorporation of ecological criteria in public procurement

Family Name: NAMA for a Low Carbon and Climate Resilient Livestock Sector in Honduras
Family Summary: This NAMA (Nationally Appropriate Mitigation Actions) sets out a long-term agenda for the sustainable and climate-resilient management of the livestock sector in Honduras. It promotes rotational silvopastoral systems for land resilience and carbon sequestration, as well as significant capacity building measures to provide farmers with better knowledge and access to financing systems. The NAMA also promotes technological solutions such as nutritional blocks to reduce livestock digestive emissions, and biodigesters to turn animal dung into biogas which displaces wood fuel.
Document Title: NAMA for a Low Carbon and Climate Resilient Livestock Sector in Honduras

Family Name: National Adaptation Framework
Family Summary:
Ireland's first statutory National Adaptation Framework (NAF) was released on January 19th, 2018. The NAF sets out the national strategy to reduce the vulnerability of the country to the negative effects of climate change and to avail of positive impacts. The NAF was developed under the Climate Action and Low Carbon Development Act 2015 and succeeds to the NCCAF previously released in 2012.

Ireland's second statutory National Adaptation Framework (NAF) was published by Minister Eamon Ryan TD on 5 June 2024. This latest NAF replaces the first iteration of the framework published in 2018, which was reviewed in 2022 in line with the five-year requirement of the 2015 Climate and Low Carbon Development Act (the Climate Act).

Ireland’s first Statutory National Adaptation Framework (NAF) was published in 2018 and sets out the national strategy to reduce the vulnerability of the country to the negative effects of climate change and to avail of any positive impacts. Twelve key sectors were identified and are required to prepare sectoral adaptation plans.
Document Title: Second National Adaptation Framework

Family Summary: Decision 84 sets out objectives of creating and developing urban green growth areas in Vietnam to promote the transformation of the urban economic growth model towards green growth, improve competitiveness, and ensure economic development in urban areas that is rapid, effective, sustainable, contributing to job creation, hunger eradication, poverty reduction, improving people's material and spiritual lives, and enhancing the urban system's ability to respond to climate change, contributing to the national commitment to reduce GHG emissions.

Family Name: Decree 51/2018
Family Summary: This Decree introduces measures that allow for the use and manufacture of electric buses, by reducing the tariffs for 36 months, for up to 350 electric buses with each company limited to a quota of 60 electric buses. This Decree also allows applicants to present a Local Production Plan for electric buses, with the percentage of national integration of locally produced units to reach at least 10% within two years and at least 25% from the third year of production. Import operations will accordingly have tariffs reduced to zero.
Document Title: Decree 51/2018

Family Name: A European Strategy for Plastics in a Circular Economy
Family Summary: The strategy incites a sustainable plastics industry, where design and production fully respects the needs of reuse, repair, and recycling, brings growth and jobs to Europe and helps cut EU's greenhouse gas emissions and dependence on imported fossil fuels. By 2030, all plastics packaging placed on the EU market is either reusable or can be recycled in a cost-effective manner, and by 2030, more than half of plastics waste generated in Europe is recycled. More plastic recycling helps reduce Europe’s dependence on imported fossil fuel and cut CO2 emissions, in line with commitments under the Paris Agreement.
Document Title: A European Strategy for Plastics in a Circular Economy

Family Name: Concept of Urban Development of the Slovak until 2030
Family Summary:
The concept states:

An adaptation process is significantly facilitated by the establishment of a local adaptation strategy or adaptation action plan and the systematic inclusion of the topic of climate change and mitigation in the strategic documents and development plans of the local government, in particular in spatial plans and programmes for economic and social. Preparedness will enable the local government and the whole community to respond in a targeted manner to the expected impacts of climate change on their territory, to respond to emerging risks and, where appropriate, to take advantage of the opportunities presented by climate change.

Cities need to take a systems approach to change adaptation. To ensure a systemic approach to adaptation, its requirements should be taken into account during spatial planning. It is crucial to assess the vulnerability of the territory and the potential risks and impacts of climate change in all key areas, without which it is not possible to design adaptation measures at the local level. Preparedness and adequate adaptation of cities to the adverse effects of climate change is a contribution to reducing or at least partially eliminating the risk of deterioration in the health status of the population, which is one of the potential consequences of climate change.

The concept promotes a city-led approach towards adaptation to the adverse impacts of climate change and supports the mainstreaming of adaptation measures into the spatial planning documentation.
Document Title: Concept of Urban Development of the Slovak unti 2030

Family Name: Rectangular strategy (RS) IV 2018
Family Summary: "This document aims to accelerate the governance reform in Cambodia by developing 1) human resources, 2) the private sector and jobs, 3) inclusivity and sustainability, and 4) economic diversification. The strategy states that 1. the government must give priority to the National Strategic Plan on Green Growth 2013-2030”, “Cambodia Climate Change Strategic Plan 2014-2023”, “National Environment Strategy and Action Plan 2016-2023”, “National REDD+ Strategy, and use social and environmental fund effectively to ensure economic development with low-carbon emission and resilience to climate change. 2. Further strengthening the management of protected areas, biodiversity conservation, natural resource conservation, especially the ecosystems of Tonle Sap lake, Mekong river and the coastline areas. 3. Further strengthening the management of solid waste, waste water, gas and lethal substance by implementing principles of reduction, reuse, recycling and non-use as well as strengthening pollution monitoring and control mechanism and control. 4. Promoting resource efficiency and sustainability by implementing the principle of sustainable consumption and production. 5. Increasing the usage of environmental-friendly and climate-friendly technologies in physical infrastructure and socio-economic development. 6. Continuing to promote the implementation of carbon trading mechanisms and related regulatory frameworks, strengthen the capabilities to develop and implement climate change adaptation and resiliency measures as well as explore the possibility of studying financial resiliency to respond to disasters caused by climate change. 7. Further promoting the development and implementation of integrated water resource management plan in order to expand water supply in response to demand, minimize the risks caused by flood and drought, as well as to ensure long-term water security. 8. Continuing to encourage and increase investment in clean energy and renewable energy, especially solar power while reducing the production of energy from unclean sources to ensure long-term energy security. 9. Continuing to strengthen regulatory framework, research, as well as development of skill and capacity for national and sub-national official in terms of environment, green development, climate change, integrated water resource management, and the usage of natural resources in a sustainable manner."
Document Title: Rectangular strategy (RS) IV 2018

Document Title: Decree No. 52 creating the Permanent Presidential Advisory Committee on Climate Change

Family Name: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan 2017-2023 (High Planning Council decision number 2017/22)
Family Summary: The National Energy Efficiency Action Plan for the 2017-2023 is a broad document released in Official Gazette 30289 and targeting energy savings in buildings and services, energy, transport, industry and technology and agriculture. The Action Plan aims to save 23.9 Million-Ton Equivalent of Petroleum from Turkey's primary energy consumption, via a strategy which includes $10.9 billion of planned investment. Cogeneration and district heating/cooling systems are planned to become compulsory in new community buildings. To support renewable energy use, related administrative processes will be expedited for existing buildings.Disincentives will be introduced to limit cars in city centers, including increased parking fees and installing automated parking alarm systems. National and international financial support will be sought to promote use of shared vehicles, as well encourage employees to use public transport.

Family Name: Switzerland’s climate policy, 2018
Family Summary: This policy details how Switzerland aims to meet its commitments made under the Paris Agreement. It is a multi-sectoral document that primarily focuses on reducing GHG emissions from fossil thermal and motor fuels. It urges action at national and local levels, by public and private actors.

Family Name: National Resilience Strategy 2018-2030
Family Summary:
This strategy aims to create a country free of chronic vulnerability and nutrition insecurity, where sustainable economic development creates opportunities for everyone, and where people are resilient to economic and environmental shocks that affect their lives and livelihoods.

The following "pillar impacts" are listed:

1. Transformed agricultural sector into an engine for shared economic prosperity, food security and poverty reduction;2. Scaled-up climate-resilient infrastructure, and enhanced climate-adaptation capacity of all stakeholders, through better access to climate information and early warning and response mechanisms that safeguard lives and livelihoods from shocks;

3. Sustained reduction in the number of chronically food insecure households by scaling up access to predictable social support services, complementary livelihood packages, nutrition services, and expanded access to national programmes;

4. Reduction in stunting of children <5 years of age through well-coordinated and high-impact multi- sectoral investments in nutrition-specific and nutrition-sensitive interventions;

5. Expanded public, private and community partnerships to safeguard Malawi’s natural resource endowments and ecosystems that contribute to social and economic prosperity;

6. Strengthened national and devolved government institutions, civil society, and private sector actors to adopt effective and accountable practices that prevent, mitigate, and respond to disasters, and promote long-term development;

7. Strengthened women’s empowerment through cross-cutting strategies and measurable outcomes.
Document Title: National Resilience Strategy 2018-2030

Family Name: National Plan for Adaptation to Climate Change 2018-2030
Family Summary:
• The objective of this document is to guide adaptation actions focused on the integration of sustainable development strategies in order to reduce the adverse impacts of climate change and variability in the country. It sets the following principles and policy actions:Adoption of precautionary measures for the benefit of the environment even in the face of scientific uncertainty
  • Inter-institutional and intersectoral coordination.
  • Integrality and coherence between adaptation and mitigation for the generation of co-benefits.
  • Education, research and transfer of knowledge and technologies based on the scientific and traditional knowledge of indigenous and Afro-Honduran communities and peoples.
  • Recognition of the value of ecosystems and biodiversity in reducing the adverse effects of climate change on human communities and on infrastructure.
  • Mainstreaming the issue of adaptation to climate change in the framework of public policy and sustainable development planning under a human rights approach.

Family Name: Ministerial Resolution 98/2019 regarding the use of alternative fuels resulting from waste treatment processes in cement factories
Family Summary:
This resolution aims to: 1) Use alternative fuels resulting from municipal solid waste treatment processes as an alternative for energy production, 2)Supporting industries and initiatives aimed at treating municipal solid waste generated in the country and exploiting it to obtain products that are a tributary to the national economy, 3) Environmental protection, human health and sustainable development.

The document further states the following:

  • The provisions of this resolution apply to all cement factories that use coal in their energy production operations.
  • All cement factories that use coal in their energy production operations must commit to using at least 10% (if available in the country) of their total energy needs from alternative fuels generated from municipal solid waste treatment plants in the country, starting from 2020. And monitor the air quality around.
  • The competent authority in each emirate shall determine the requirements for the transfer of alternative fuels.
  • It is prohibited to import all types of alternative fuels resulting from waste treatment operations.

Family Name: Accelerated Growth and Sustainable Development Strategy (SCA2D) 2018-2021
Family Summary:

  •  Improve the quality of life of the population and guarantee equitable access to basic social services,
  •  Ensure rational exploitation of natural resources, in accordance with the principles of sustainable development, while taking into account climate change,
  •  Strengthen good governance and resilience in the face of political and institutional fragility, and promote the rule of law and social cohesion.


The document calls for more production from renewable energy sources, and protecting its carbon sinks.

Family Summary: The PNRBN constitutes a support and guidance instrument for decision-making in national and provincial jurisdictions and forest development processes, within the framework of the National Strategy for mitigation and adaptation to Climate Change. The Plan proposes to develop a program for a first period of six years (2018-2023) in order to reach the goal of 18,000 hectares of native forest restored by 2023. The promotion of ecological restoration, recovery and restoration is defined as a general objective. rehabilitation of the native forest of Argentina with different degrees of degradation in the provision of ecosystem goods and services, which lead to the recovery and conservation of biological diversity and forest biomass, within a framework of mitigation and adaptation policies to environmental changes global current and development established. The following are established as specific objectives: a) restore the functional processes of native forests and their biodiversity; b) identify priority regions; c) promote the necessary alliances for the implementation of the national restoration strategy; d) recover the productive value of the native forest; e) promote the reduction of forest degradation factors, coordinating with Local Authorities; f) promote the reduction and compensation of GHG emissions from deforestation and degradation; g) generate environmental awareness about the importance of the native forest in the different social actors that act on them directly or indirectly; h) link restoration to socio-economic processes established for development, promoting the generation of benefits and ensuring the participation of all actors and sectors of society, cultural and multi-ethnic diversity throughout the implementation of restoration processes; i) and identify and add all existing or potential restoration initiatives in order to enhance the impacts, creating a National Native Forest Restoration Database.
Document Title: Resolution 267/2019 approving the National Plan for the Restoration of Native Forests (PNRBN)

Family Name: National Development Plan 2018-2027
Family Summary: The National Development Plan is a broad document setting the Government's policy vision over the period 2018-2027. It includes a chapter on the transition to a low carbon and climate resilient society. The Government pledges to invest 22 billion euros in order to reach an almost zero emissions economy by 2050. The funds are to be primarily deployed to reduce carbon emissions from transport, housing, agriculture and the energy sector, along with flood defenses.
Document Title: National Development Plan 2018-2027

Family Name: Tanzania Health National Adaptation Plan 2018-2023
Family Summary:
This Plan aims at making the Tanzanian health system resilient to climate change, by mainstreaming adaptation efforts into health policies. It focuses on vector-borne diseases, nutrition, water-related diseases and disasters (flood and drought frequency). The Plan sets a long-term target and a five-year implementation strategy.

The Plan also seeks to 1) guide health practitioners on the need to develop and operationalise a climate sensitive early warning system for diseases outbreaks, 2) advocate for the mobilisation and allocation of resources for adaptation to climate change in health sector, and 3) facilitate the integration of health priorities into the National Adaptation Plan and support the NDC implementation process.
Document Title: Tanzania Health National Adaptation Plan 2018-2023

Family Name: Strategic Investment Framework for Environment and Natural Resources Management (CSIGERN)
Family Summary:
The Strategic Investment Framework for Environment and Natural Resources Management (CSIGERN) replaces the National Program of Investment for the Environment and Natural Resources. It is a programmatic framework defining interventions related to the environment and natural resource management. It constitutes the reference document for the Ministry of the Environment and Forestry Resources interventions over the period 2018-2022, and serves as a basis for drawing up sectoral development projects and investment projects.

The framework seeks an inclusion of environmental concerns, including climate change mitigation and adaptation aspects, into sectoral policies, and sets a budget to finance actions in forestry and other environments.
Document Title: Strategic Investment Framework for Environment and Natural Resources Management (CSIGERN)

Family Name: Angola Energy 2025
Family Summary:
The Strategy Angola Energia 2025 assesses the main long-term options and establishes the Government's atlas and vision for development of the electricity sector in the 2018-2025 horizon, identifying priority investments in generation, transmission and interconnection, as well as the distribution and network expansion model up until 2025.

The document analyses both the supply and demand sides of the energy sector, proposing a 2025 vision and atlas. Annexes include a list a list of priority investments over the 2018-2025 horizon and a list of grid connected municipality capitals by 2025.
Document Title: Angola Energy 2025

Family Name: Decarbonisation plan
Family Summary:
This plan sets out the government's strategy to decarbonise Costa Rica's economy until 2050. It differentiates between the initial phase (2018-2022), the inflection period (2022-2030), and the "massive deployment" (2031-2050).

The Plan is organised around ten focus areas:
1) Development of a mobility system base on safe, efficient and renewable public transport, and active and shared mobility schemes.
2) Transformation of the light duty vehicle fleet to a zero emissions one, nourished by energy that is renewable and not of fossil origin.
3) Promotion of a freight transport that adopts modalities, technologies and energy sources that emit zero or the lowest possible emissions.
4) Consolidation of the national electric system with the capacity, flexibility, intelligence, and resilience necessary to supply and manage renewable energy at competitive cost.
5) Development of buildings of different uses (commercial, residential, institutional) under high efficiency standards and low emission processes.
6) Modernization of the industrial sector through the application of electrical, efficient, and sustainable processes and technologies of low and zero emissions.
7) Development of an integrated waste management system based on the separation, reuse, revaluation, and final disposal of maximum efficiency and low greenhouse gas emissions.
8) Promotion of highly efficient agricultural food systems that generate low-carbon local consumption and export goods
9) Consolidation of an eco- competitive livestock model based on productive efficiency and reduction of greenhouse gases.
10) Consolidation of a model of management of rural, urban, and coastal territories that facilitates the protection of biodiversity, the increase and maintenance of forest cover and ecosystem services based on nature-based solutions.
Document Title: National Decarbonization Plan 2018-2050

Family Name: Output-Based Pricing System Regulations (SOR/2019-266)
Family Summary:
This document implement an output-based pricing system for industrial GHG emissions with respect to covered facilities where industrial activities are engaged in. These Regulations set out 1) the manner in which a person responsible for a covered facility must, under Part 2 of the Act, provide a report that sets out the information with respect to the GHG emissions limit and cause the report to be verified; 2) the methods to quantify the GHGs from a covered facility and the production from each specified industrial activity engaged in at the covered facility; 3) the manner of determining the covered facility’s GHG emissions limit based on the facility’s production from each specified industrial activity and the applicable output-based standard; and 4) the manner in which compensation is provided for excess emissions and surplus credits are issued.On 15 March 2025, the Regulations Amending the Output-Based Pricing System Regulations: SOR/2025-108 were issued to ensure that the on-site transportation emissions of covered facilities remain subject to carbon pollution pricing, and, in circumstances where the Minister cancels the designation of a voluntary facility in 2025, to align the compliance period for these facilities to end when the fuel charge rate is set to 0$.

The Proceeds from this system fund the Output-Based Pricing System Proceeds Fund, which has two streams: the Decarbonization Incentive Program (DIP) and the Future Electricity Fund (FEF).
Document Title: Regulations Amending the Output-Based Pricing System Regulations: SOR/2025-108
