Family Name: Myanmar Agriculture Development Strategy and Investment Plan (2018-19/ 2022-23)
Family Summary:
The Agriculture Development Strategy (ADS) and Investment Plan (IP) responds to the need: 
1) for the consolidation and integration of various plans, strategies, roadmaps, and approaches developed by various stakeholders; 
2) for a systematic approach to operationalize agricultural policy implementation and link it to the IP; 
3) to coordinate activities, projects, programs, and policies; 
4) to build a dialogue with domestic and foreign investors and harmonise foreign aid to the sector.

The document notably sets a yearly budget to support farmers in order to increase their resilience to climate change and disasters
Document Title: Myanmar Agriculture Development Strategy and Investment Plan (2018-19/ 2022-23)

Family Name: Bangladesh National Action Plan (NAP) for Reducing Short Lived Climate Pollutants (SLCPs)
Family Summary: This document aims at reducing the adverse impacts of short-lived climate pollutants (SLCP) such as black carbon, methane, tropospheric ozone on health, agriculture and the climate. This 2018 document builds on a previous version released in 2014. The action plan aims at identifying the most cost-effective pathways for large scale implementation of SLCP mitigation measures.
Document Title: Bangladesh National Action Plan (NAP) for Reducing Short Lived Climate Pollutants (SLCPs)

Family Name: National Climate Finance Strategy
Family Summary: The National Climate Finance Strategy (ENFC in Spanish) is a key tool to ensure Colombia has the necessary financial resources to tackle climate change and achieve its long-term sustainability goals. It aims to address the financial challenges related to climate change in Colombia and has as its main goal to mobilise financial resources for climate change adaptation and mitigation efforts, supporting Colombia's transition to a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy.
Document Title: National Climate Finance Strategy

Family Name: National Employment Policy
Family Summary: The National Employment Policy aims to improve the employment opportunities in Fiji to cope with socio-economic developments as well as climate change and natural disasters. The policy places emphasis on a just transition for the work force in the context of climate change by identifying and promoting green jobs and new green skill sets.
Document Title: National Employment Policy

Family Name: Master Plan on Electricity
Family Summary: This Plan seeks to promote he use of non-conventional renewable energy sources in Ecuador to increase energy efficency and attract domestic and foreign investors. It particularly promotes the development of projects that seek to replace fossil fuel use with clean energy.
Document Title: Master Plan for Electricity

Family Name: Plan of Action to Implement Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030
Family Summary: The Bangladesh Plan of Action for Implementing the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction outlines the country's strategy to minimise disaster risks and strengthen resilience. It acknowledges that climate change increases the frequency and severity of disasters, threatening the livelihoods and assets of millions. The plan stresses the importance of integrating disaster risk reduction with climate change adaptation strategies to improve resilience and reduce vulnerabilities.
Document Title: Plan of Action to Implement Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030

Family Name: National Agricultural Policy for the Maltese Islands
Family Summary: The National Agricultural Policy for the Maltese Islands is a 10-year plan aimed at making agriculture more sustainable, economically viable, and socially inclusive. It outlines six strategic objectives, including improving food traceability, supporting resource management, and promoting research and development, with a total of 70 measures across economic, social, resource, and governance objectives. The policy also includes an Action Plan detailing timelines and responsible entities for implementation. It emphasises adaptation, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and enhancing the resilience of agricultural systems to environmental risks.
Document Title: National Agricultural Policy for the Maltese Islands

Family Name: Green Public Procurement National Action Plan
Family Summary: Malta Green Public Procurement National Action Plan 2019-2025 is a national sectoral action plan that aims to reduce the environmental impact of procurement (goods and services it purchases). Specific criteria focus on waste reduction, water and energy efficiency as well as climate change adaptation.
Document Title: Green Public Procurement National Action Plan

Family Name: The Swedish Energy Agency's work on climate adaptation - Action Plan No. 2018–926
Family Summary: The overall objective (society's capacity) for the work on climate adaptation in the energy sector is to prevent and mitigate negative consequences for society and energy users due to disruptions and interruptions in energy supply caused by a changing climate. The work is based on an all-risk perspective and is integrated where possible into other processes for robust supply chains and a well-planned and practised crisis management capability. The objective of this action plan is for the Energy Agency to support the energy sector's climate adaptation by strengthening the Energy Agency's internal work on climate adaptation, primarily through an all-risk perspective within existing responsibilities and processes.
Document Title: The Swedish Energy Agency's work on climate adaptation - Action Plan No. 2018–926

Family Name: Investing for Food and Jobs (IFJ): An Agenda For Transforming Ghana's Agriculture (2018-2021)
Family Summary:
The agricultural sector, a key to the national development agenda, is expected to lead the growth and structural transformation of the economy and maximise the benefits of accelerated growth.

This Plan is developed to provide structured public investment and leverage private investments under three main categories: (i) developing critical infrastructure to modernise the agri-food system; (ii) building both public and private sector systems to generate the enabling results and the outcome results respectively; and (iii) direct transfer to farmers, agri-food enterprises and other value chain actors.

This Plan seeks to address cross cutting issues including biodiversity, climate change and environmental management. Actions include Support the development and introduction of climate resilient, high-yielding, disease and pest-resistant, short duration crop varieties taking into account consumer health and safety; promoting agricultural insurance instruments
Document Title: Investing for Food and Jobs (IFJ): An Agenda For Transforming Ghana's Agriculture (2018-2021)

Family Name: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP) 2018/2019 - 2021/2022
Family Summary:
The 2nd NEEAP replaced the first plan (2012-2015). The 2nd plan is in line with the Egypt's Vision 2030 and Egypt’s Integrated and Sustainable Energy Strategy (ISES) 2035 and had the mission of:

  • Achieving energy efficiency improvement without affecting growth or production rates in the sectors of industry, trade, services and agriculture, or affecting the wellbeing of consumers, whether in terms of residential or public uses.
  • Raising the competitiveness of energy consuming sectors by improving the efficiency of energy use.

The plan is divided in:

• General framework: national rationalization goals.• Energy efficiency measures in different sectors.• Complementary energy efficiency measures.• Common measures among the sectors.• Evaluation of the development of energy efficiency policies.
Document Title: Second National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)

Family Name: National Strategic Development Plan II 2018/19 to 2022/23
Family Summary:
This Plan has the theme "In pursuit of economic and institutional transformation for private sector-led job creation and inclusive growth" to promote investment facilitation and thereby accelerate economic growth. The Plan mainstreams climate change and the environment, youth, children and disability, gender, and social protection across all chapters.

Interventions include promoting climate-smart and resource-efficient infrastructure; incorporating climate change education in school curricula at tertiary institutions; constructing new infrastructure to climate-proof standards, etc.
Document Title: National Strategic Development Plan II 2018/19 to 2022/23

Family Name: Climate Change Communications Strategy
Family Summary: This Strategy provides a blueprint to guide communications planning. It is organised around five key components: setting objectives and organising internally (i.e. getting different government entities involved and coordinated); identifying key audiences, both internally and externally; developing key messages; selecting the most effective modes, methods and channels for communication of messages; and establishing ways to evaluate the impacts of the communications campaign. There are sector-specific messaging examples for various sectors and examples of climate messages targeted at different audiences.
Document Title: Climate Change Communications Strategy

Family Name: National Adaptation Plan Roadmap and Capacity Development Plan 2018‐2028
Family Summary:
The Roadmap details the sequence of activities that create and organise Saint Lucia's National Adaptation Plan (NAP) process.

The Capacity Development Plan measures the skills deemed weakest at each government level (policy, organisational and operational) and the capacity-building activities suggested to strengthen these weak skills. It also presents a tentative framework for implementation and potential funding sources.
Document Title: National Adaptation Plan Roadmap and Capacity Development Plan 2018‐2028

Family Name: Monitoring and Evaluation Plan of Saint Lucia’s National Adaptation Planning Process
Family Summary: This Plan focuses on tracking the implementation of the cross-sectoral and sectoral measures included in the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) and Sectoral Adaptation Strategies and Action Plans (SASAPs). The monitoring and evaluation system will also track progress on the implementation of: 1. the NAP process (by following the formulation, review and update of SASAPs and the review and update of the NAP itself); and 2. the CCAP core elements (facilitation, implementation and finance).
Document Title: Monitoring and Evaluation Plan of Saint Lucia’s National Adaptation Planning Process

Family Name: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2018-2030
Family Summary: Vanuatu's National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2018-2030 acknowledges climate change as a significant threat to the nation's biodiversity and ecosystem services, and emphasises the importance of ecosystems such as mangroves in climate mitigation via carbon sequestration. It contains measures for monitoring biodiversity changes, and enhancing funding to nature recovery projects which include nature-based solutions expected to feed into carbon credit markets. Organic carbon stock is given as a factor for the prioritisation of habitats for restoration and protection efforts.
Document Title: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2018-2030

Family Name: Disaster Risk Reduction National Strategic Action Plan 2018-2030
Family Summary: The Disaster Risk Reduction National Strategic Action Plan 2018-2030 was developed by the Nepalese Government following the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2017. This document outlines strategic actions and activities for the short, medium, and long term. This Plan aims to significantly mitigate and prevent new natural and non-natural disaster risks and losses in life, property, health, livelihood, means of production, infrastructure, and cultural and environmental heritage. This is achieved through the identification of strategic activities and the formulation and implementation of periodic and annual plans that enhance preparedness, response, rehabilitation, reconstruction, and overall resilience.
Document Title: Disaster Risk Reduction National Strategic Action Plan 2018-2030

Family Name: Gender and Climate Change Action Plan
Family Summary:
This Plan promotes gender equality by including it in the decisions of climate change summits, and in national climate change policies, in order to better address the extreme weather events that are increasingly affecting our country and the planet. It is a public policy management tool that guides and promotes government action so that the various entities responsible for climate change mitigation and adaptation design and implement actions that help women and men have equal opportunities to address this phenomenon and move toward sustainable development. The PAGCC-RD links national policy with international agreements on gender and climate change and proposes comprehensive, cross-cutting, and multisectoral solutions that enable concrete and synergistic action toward a common goal.

The National Council for Climate Change and Clean Development Mechanism (CNCCMDL), and the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources requested technical assistance from the Global Gender Office (GGO) of the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), with support from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), to prepare this Plan.

This Plan covers the priority sectors of energy, transport and infrastructure; agriculture and food security; waste; forestry; water; health; coastal marine; tourism; and risk management.
Document Title: Gender and Climate Change Action Plan

Family Name: National Disaster Risk Reduction Framework
Family Summary:
The National Disaster Risk Reduction Framework is a multisector collaboration led by the National Resilience Taskforcewithin the Australian Government Department of Home Affairs. The National Disaster Risk Reduction Framework outlines a national, comprehensive approach to proactively reducing disaster risk, now and into the future.

The 2030 Vision for Disaster Risk Reduction in Australia is to actively reduce disaster risk and limit the impacts of disasters oncommunities and economies. All sectors of society understand and respond to social, environmental, technological and demographic changes which have the potential to prevent, create or exacerbate disaster risks.All sectors of society:– make disaster risk-informed decisions,– are accountable for reducing risks within their control, and– invest in reducing disaster risk in order to limit the cost of disasters when they occur.
Document Title: National Disaster Risk Reduction Framework

Family Name: National Drought Agreement
Family Summary:
The National Drought Agreement (NDA) is an agreement between the Commonwealth of Australia and New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland, Western Australia, South Australia, Tasmania, the Australian Capital Territory, and the Northern Territory.

Parties acknowledge that drought is one of a number of business risks that farmers and other businesses should actively prepare for and adapt to. Promoting and enabling a culture of self-responsibility is a shared goal, and drought policy and programs should support the agricultural sector and rural communities to prepare for drought and climate variability to enhance their long-term sustainability and resilience. Climate science states Australia can expect increased and more extreme climate variability.
Document Title: First National Drought Agreement 2018-2024

Family Name: Clean Energy for Rural and Remote Communities Program
Family Summary:
The Clean Energy for Rural and Remote Communities (CERRC) program provides funding for renewable energy and capacity building projects to reduce the reliance on fossil fuels for heating and electricity in Indigenous, rural and remote communities across Canada. In support of the clean energy transition, the program’s objective is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and fossil fuel use by increasing the use of local renewable energy sources and related energy efficiency measures. This creates environmental, social and economic benefits to support healthier and more sustainable communities.

Investing in clean energy solutions in Indigenous communities improves energy security, reconciliation, self-determination and economic development for Indigenous Peoples.

Launched in 2018, the CERRC program was allocated $220 million over 8 years to reduce diesel reliance for heat and power in Indigenous and remote communities. CERRC received an additional $233 million over 5 years through Budget 2021.
Document Title: Clean Energy for Rural and Remote Communities Program

Family Name: Disaster Mitigation and Adaptation Fund
Family Summary:
In 2018, the Government of Canada launched the Disaster Mitigation and Adaptation Fund (DMAF), committing $2 billion over 10 years to invest in structural and natural infrastructure projects to increase the resilience of communities that are impacted by natural disasters triggered by climate change.

As announced in Budget 2021, an additional $1.375 billion in federal funding over 12 years was provided to renew the DMAF. A minimum of $138 million of this funding is allocated to Indigenous Recipients.

As outlined in the Government of Canada Adaptation Action Plan (GOCAAP), the federal plan to implement the National Adaptation Strategy’s goals, objectives and proposed targets, the Government of Canada will invest up to an additional $489.1 million over 10 years through the DMAF to help communities increase their resiliency against the effects of climate change.

To be considered eligible, projects must be aimed at reducing the socio-economic, environmental and cultural impacts triggered by natural hazards and extreme weather events taking into consideration current and potential future impacts of climate change in communities and infrastructure at high risk.

Natural hazard and extreme weather events include but are not limited to:

  • Avalanche
  • Drought
  • Earthquake
  • Erosion
  • Extreme Temperature
  • Flood
  • Hurricane
  • Landslides
  • Permafrost thaw
  • Sea Level Rise
  • Storm
  • Tsunami
  • Wildland Fire
  • Other (If Other, specification required)
Document Title: Disaster Mitigation and Adaptation Fund

This Framework outlines government coordination; research funding; adaptive technologies; mitigation actions.

Family Name: Emissions Trading Scheme Pilot Project
Family Summary:
In 2012, Mexico enacted the General Law on Climate Change (GCCL), which required the creation of a national registry for greenhouse gases and provided orientation to federal, state and municipal authorities toward the authority to establish a voluntary emissions trading scheme (ETS). (https://carbon-pulse.com/44724/) Mexico will launch a pilot national emissions trading scheme in Aug. 2018 with a three-year pilot phase. The pilot is scheduled to last 36 months, between 1 January 2020 and 31 December 2022. "The pilot will cover the energy and industry sectors. Energy encompasses both electricity generation and fossil-fuel extraction and production. Industry includes, among others, the automotive, cement, chemicals, glass, steel, metallurgical, mining, and petrochemicals subsectors, as well as the pulp and paper subsector. Only direct CO2 emissions will be regulated through the pilot, and participation is limited to entities with annual emissions greater than 100,000tCO2. The system is expected to cover around 300 entities in this phase, corresponding to approximately 45% of national emissions." (ICAP 2019)

New Developments: In 2017, Mexico began a simulation of a voluntary Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS) and the General Climate Change Law makes the scheme mandatory as soon as its three-year pilot phase concludes. The pilot phase—originally planned to start in August 2018—started operation in January 2020. The ETS will not replace the existing carbon tax.
Document Title: Emissions Trading Scheme Pilot Project

Family Name: Saint Lucia’s sectoral adaptation strategy and action plan for the fisheries sector (Fisheries SASAP) 2018-2028
Family Summary:
The Sectoral Adaptation Strategy and Action Plan for the Fisheries Sector (Fisheries SASAP) 2018-2028 seeks to strengthen the sustainability of Saint Lucia’s fisheries and fishery-dependent businesses and the security of fisheries-dependent livelihoods under a changing climate. The Fisheries SASAP, funded with the support of the United States In-Country NAP Support Programme (NAP-SP), implemented by the International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD), builds on previous efforts and projects, and is the product of an in-depth contextual analysis.
The plan consists of 31 adaptation measures that are endorsed by relevant stakeholders and offer solutions to information, technical, institutional, financial, regulatory and policy limitations hampering adaptation in the sector. In the Fisheries SASAP, the adaptation measures are grouped under eight strategic objectives and contribute to these four major expected outcomes:

- Enhanced enabling environment for climate adaptation action in the fisheries sector
- Enhanced nutrition, food availability, quality and security through adaptation in the fisheries sector
- Strengthened partnerships for building sustainable and resilient fisheries in a changing climate 
- Strengthened preparedness to climate variability and extremes in the fisheries sector
Document Title: Saint Lucia’s sectoral adaptation strategy and action plan for the fisheries sector (Fisheries SASAP) 2018-2028

Family Name: Saint Lucia’s sectoral adaptation strategy and action plan for the agriculture sector (Agriculture SASAP) 2018-2028
Family Summary: The Sectoral Adaptation Strategy and Action Plan for the Agriculture Sector (Agriculture SASAP) 2018-2028 aims to facilitate the adoption and scaling up of climate-resilient agriculture in Saint Lucia. The Agriculture SASAP, funded with the support of the United States In-Country NAP Support Program, through the NAP Global Network, builds on previous efforts and projects, and is the product of an in-depth contextual analysis and search for potential effective solutions to the country’s agriculture-related climate challenges.The Agriculture SASAP consists of 45 adaptation measures deemed critical for building climate-resilient agriculture systems in the country. The measures, endorsed by relevant stakeholders, offer solutions to information, technical, institutional, financial, regulatory and policy limitations hampering adaptation in the sector. In the SASAP, the adaptation measures are grouped under 14 strategic objectives and contribute to these four major expected outcomes:- Enhanced enabling environment for climate adaptation action in the agriculture sector - Enhanced nutrition, food availability, quality and security through adaptation in the agriculture sector- Strengthened partnerships for scaling up climate-resilient agriculture- Built adaptive capacity to climate variability and extremes in the agriculture sector
Document Title: Saint Lucia’s sectoral adaptation strategy and action plan for the agriculture sector (Agriculture SASAP) 2018-2028

Family Name: Saint Lucia’s sectoral adaptation strategy and action plan for the water sector (Water SASAP) 2018-2028
Family Summary:
Saint Lucia’s Sectoral Adaptation Strategy and Action Plan for the Water Sector (Water SASAP) 2018-2028 seeks to reduce water-related risks induced by climate change and climate variability. The plan also aims to build the capacities of relevant actors for ensuring the sustainable management of water resources and services under current and future climatic conditions. The Water SASAP, funded with the support of the United Nations Development Programme’s (UNDP) Japan-Caribbean Climate Change Partnership (J-CCCP), builds on previous efforts and projects, and is the product of an in-depth contextual analysis and search for potential effective solutions to the country’s water-related challenges under a changing climate.
The plan consists of 70 adaptation measures deemed critical for improving water resource and service management, and for reducing water-mediated climate change impacts in the country. The measures, endorsed by relevant stakeholders, offer solutions to information, technical, institutional, financial, regulatory and policy limitations hampering adaptation in the water sector. In the Water SASAP, the adaptation measures are grouped under 13 strategic objectives and contribute to these four major expected outcomes:

- An enhanced enabling environment and improved behaviour for water-related climate adaptation action
- Increased water access, availability and quality 
- Increased water efficiency and conservation
- Strengthened preparedness to climate variability and extremes
Document Title: Saint Lucia’s sectoral adaptation strategy and action plan for the water sector (Water SASAP) 2018-2028

Family Name: Climate-resilient green economy strategy - Sector-wise GTP II implementation monitoring checklist
Family Summary: This document provides detailed sector-wise checklists of climate change mitigation and adaptation activities in Ethiopia to support the implementation of Ethiopia's Growth and Transformation Plan (GTP II) for the period 2016-2020 and the Climate-Resilient Green Economy Strategy (CRGE).Poverty eradication through broad-based accelerated and sustained growth is outlined in the GTP. Through Agricultural Development-Led Industrialization (ADLI), the country aims to build an economy with a modern and productive agricultural sector and a strong industrial sector, ultimately increasing per capita income to the level of middle-income countries by 2025.Achieving these ambitious objectives is challenging, but vital for the future of Ethiopia and its citizens. Climate change is one of the major current challenges and adds considerable stress to the societies and environment. From shifting weather patterns that threaten food production to rising sea levels that increase the risk of catastrophic flooding, the impacts of climate change are global in scope and unprecedented in scale. Ethiopia has historically suffered from climatic variability. Repeated rain failures, famines and chronic food crisis resulting from frequent droughts, environmental degradation, and decline in food production have rocked the country many times and remain a major challenge. The country’s economic output growth is closely linked to fluctuations in precipitation levels, as its agriculture is highly rain-fed, with only 2% of total arable land covered by irrigated and permanent crops. This strong association between rainfall and the economy is largely due to the nature of the country’s most dominant sector, agriculture and weak capacity of the rural population to adapt to climate variations.
Document Title: Ethiopia: Climate-resilient green economy strategy - Sector-wise GTP II implementation monitoring checklist

Family Name: National Disaster Risk Management and Reduction Policy: 2018 Update
Family Summary:
The updated National Policy for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management of Paraguay becomes the main umbrella for the National Emergency Secretariat, as well as for government institutions, subnational governments, civil society, academia and the private sector, to generate policies, plans, programmes, projects and strategies in accordance with their own realities, which together lead Paraguay to sustainable, safe and resilient development.

The guidelines updated in this document respond to new global commitments, national regulatory frameworks and the national reality, based on the national interest materialised through the inclusion of disaster risk reduction and management in the political agenda as an indispensable component of the country's strategic sustainable development and under the premises of participation without exclusion, social empowerment, intersectoral action and interculturality.

The broad debate generated 4 strategic pillars that include the guidelines for actions to be achieved by the Policy. All strategic pillars are fundamental and equal in importance, and must be addressed and considered simultaneously:

Strategic Pillar 1: Institutional Capacity Building

Strategic Pillar 2: Financial

Strategic Pillar 3: Education, Communication and Citizen Participation

Strategic Pillar 4: Knowledge Management and Technology.
Document Title: National Disaster Risk Management and Reduction Policy: 2018 Update (Política Nacional de Gestión y Reducción de Riesgos de Desastres Actualización 2018)

Family Name: National Protocol for Action on Social Protection in the Face of Climate Shocks
Family Summary:
This action protocol for social protection against climate shocks is a planning and procedural tool for the actions of the Social Policy Coordination Office (GCPS), including special actions of the Progressing with Solidarity (PROSOLI) program, the Single Beneficiary System (SIUBEN), the Community Technology Centers (CTC), and the Social Subsidy Administrator (ADESS), in response to critical events associated with emergencies or socio-natural disasters, with an emphasis on extreme weather events, more specifically storms, hurricanes, and floods.

This protocol establishes the GCPS coordination framework in emergency situations and recovery processes with two basic purposes:

Respond to the challenges of ensuring achievements in poverty reduction in the face of climate and disaster shocks through the coordinated action of the Social Cabinet, with an emphasis on Progressing with Solidarity initiatives before and during emergencies and disasters, and in recovery processes.

Generate synergies between social protection and disaster risk management policies in the country.

This action guide seeks to ensure the timely, integrated, sustainable, and efficient coordination and action of the main public institutions responsible for social policies and programs in their efforts to support populations affected by disasters. It is timely because it seeks to respond proactively in risk reduction and response preparation, as well as offering a range of easily accessible social services to meet the needs of the affected population.

This protocol is primarily intended for severe and escalating events, with an emphasis on floods and tropical storms, which offer warning and preparation times. For events with different characteristics, such as sudden events (earthquakes, tsunamis, etc.), adaptations to the standardized procedures proposed here are necessary.
Document Title: National Protocol for Action on Social Protection in the Face of Climate Shocks

Family Name: National Implementation Plan of the Sendai Framework 2018-2022

It is a short-, medium-, and long-term multisectoral planning tool for achieving the objective and seven targets of the Sendai Framework, which allows progress toward strengthening resilience in Paraguay. Family Name: 8th Basic Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand 2017-2031
Family Summary: The Eighth long-term plan for electricity supply and demand is an extensive document setting targets of increased production from renewable energy sources and natural gas, while reducing the country's reliance on coal and nuclear sources. The document adopts policy changes and seek an amendment of the Electricity Business Act accordingly. It charges the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Energy to establish a plan for electricity supply in accordance with the present targets and Implementation Plan, taking into account economic efficiency, the environment and general safety.  The Plan sets an objective of 20 % share of electricity production obtained from renewables by 2030, while natural gas would reach 18.8 %, and both coal and nuclear decreasing to 36.1 % and 23.9 % respectively. This corresponds to an installed capacity of renewable energy, with solar and wind especially favoured, going from from 11.3 GW to 23.3 GW in 2022 and 58.5 GW in 2030. The Plan further details a roadmap to phase-out eleven nuclear power plants, and five new projected plants. These targets are also expressed in objectives of GHG emissions reductions to 2030.  The Plan is expected to be translated into law in the coming year.
Document Title: 8th Basic Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand 2017-2031

Family Name: Energy Conservation (Regulated Goods and Registered Suppliers) Regulations (S 748/2017), last amended in 2025
Family Summary: The energy conservation (Regulated Goods and Registered Suppliers) Regulations was enacted under the Energy Conservation Act (Chapter 92C) and sets out the energy efficiency standards and compliance requirements .This regulation was amended several times since then, the last amendment was in 2025. It is he primary legal instrument that details the implementation of the Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS) and the Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme (MELS) for various regulated goods, including lamps.Energy efficiency requirements is brought in the Part 2, regulation 5 and energy label requirements in regulation 6 and 7. MEPS are minimum energy efficiency requirements that regulated appliances must meet to be supplied in Singapore. Their purpose is to (i) Remove the most inefficient appliances from the market, (ii) raise the average energy efficiency of households and industries, (iii) prevent consumers from being locked into high energy consumption and costs associated with inefficient appliances and (iv) drive manufacturers and suppliers to introduce more energy-efficient models into the market. MELS requires specific household appliances, designated as "regulated goods," to carry an energy label. This label provides consumers with information about the appliance's energy consumption and costs, as well as a "tick rating" that indicates its relative energy efficiency (more ticks mean higher efficiency) The 2019 amendments strengthened Singapore's commitment to energy efficiency in lighting by both removing inefficient products from the market through stricter MEPS and by empowering consumers to make better choices through a broader and more visible MELS.

Family Name: National Carbon Emission Trading Market Power Construction Plan (2017)
Family Summary: In December 2017, China issued an emissions trading scheme plan to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions. In its initial phase, the participants in the trading scheme are limited to enterprises or other other entities in the power generation industry with annual emissions of 26,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide or more. The document sets forth a three phase plan for the implementation of the trading scheme: In the first phase, taking approximately one year, the construction of a unified national data reporting system, registration system and trading system should be completed. An administrative management system for the carbon market should also be established. In the second phase, also taking approximately one year, a simulation of the scheme's operation should take place that "comprehensively tests the effectiveness and reliability of the various elements of the market, strengthens mechanisms for early warning and control of market risks, and improves the administrative management and support system for the carbon market". In the third phase, spot marketing trading for quotas between participants in the power generation industry should be carried out. Rather than a cap and trade system, allocations are made on an output-based allowance basis.The trading scheme completed its first full compliance cycle in December 2021.
Document Title: National Carbon Emission Trading Market Power Construction Plan (2017)

The specific objectives of the agreement are as following: 1) to regulate the generation of electrical energy destined exclusively for self-consumption, as well as the surpluses generated as a by-product of self-consumption; 2) to regulate the adoption of clean technologies (renewable sources) for the generation of electrical energy by Clients of Distribution Companies with generation facilities up to a maximum of five megawatts, 3) to ensure the safety of people and property associated with the generation connected in the electrical distribution system, 4) to establish mechanisms that offset the costs incurred in the distribution network. and. Guarantee the quality and continuity of supply for users connected to the distribution network, 5) to establish a mechanism that rewards the surplus energy injected into the network of each distributed generation unit, and 6) Define technical installation criteria for distributed generators.

The agreement has to be understood within the context of the enactment of law no. 1011/2019, which amends art. 32 of law no 272/1998 on the electricity industry.

Under the Land Use and Building Act, it guides regional and municipal land-use planning and state authorities, ensuring nationally significant issues and international commitments are reflected in planning. It responds to climate change, urbanization, demographic change, and biodiversity loss, and explicitly frames land use as key to meeting Finland's Paris Agreement targets.

It sets five thematic objective groups:

  • functional communities and sustainable mobility
  • efficient transport system
  • healthy and safe living environment and climate adaptation
  • Environment and natural resources
  • Renewable energy supply (bioenergy, centralized large-scale wind power)

The National Land Use Objectives (VAT) are currently under review.

Family Name: Regulation No.70/2017 Implementing REDD+ and Sustainable Management of Forests

Family Name: Common Action Framework for Deforestation-Free Cocoa Value Chain (Cocoa and Forests Initiative)
Family Summary:
This Framework sets out the actions for building a deforestation-free cocoa value chain, underlining the crucial role of forests, biodiversity, and conservation in combating climate change, regulating local and regional climate, and providing other essential ecosystem services that support the resilience of the cocoa sector and local livelihoods.

It promotes community-based models for forest protection and restoration, including among other things, the engagement of local communities and producers in awareness campaigns on the status of National Parks and Reserves and Classified Forests and on the critical role played by forests in climate regulation, soil fertility and the water cycle.

The Cocoa and Forests Initiative (ICF) is a joint partnership of the governments of Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana, and 35 companies in the cocoa and chocolate sector representing 85% of the world's cocoa trade, aimed at eliminating deforestation from the cocoa supply chain. The ICF complies with the Preservation, Rehabilitation and Extension Strategy of the Government of Côte d'Ivoire. It is an essential component. The purpose of this strategy is to ensure that the Swedish Transport Administration's work on climate adaptation is carried out efficiently and in a coordinated manner, and that the work is followed up and evaluated.

Family Name: Regulation No. 46/2017 concerning Environmental Economic Instruments
Family Summary:
In order to implement the provisions of Article 43 paragraph (4) and Article 55 paragraph 14) of Law 32/3009 on the Protection and Management of the Environment, Regulation No. 46/2017 concerning Environmental Economic Instruments sets out a framework for the introduction of both economic incentives and disincentives to protect the environment and reduce pollution greenhouse gas emissions.

The Regulation provides for inter-regional environmental compensation (or remuneration) for activities such as water system protection, the protection of biodiversity, carbon sequestration and storage, and the preservation of natural beauty, amongst other activities. Such compensation may be carried about by the central government to local governments; local governments with regional governments; and governments with any legal person (as defined in the Regulation). This compensation must be used for restoring the environment; conservation purposes; biodiversity enrichment; community capacity building in preserving environmental functions; the development of renewable energy; sustainable economic development; and the development of supporting infrastructure for any of the above mentioned purposes, amongst others.

The regulation further establishes an Environmentally Friendly Label system that may be applied to goods produced within Indonesia as well as those imported from other countries.

Article 31. e) of the Regulation introduces the development of Waste and/or Emission Discharge Permit Trading System as a possible economic instrument to incentivise environmental and climate protection, to be carried out by the central and regional governments. Article 43. 2) stipulates that the development of this trading system will be used to reduce environmental pollution and regulate the allocation of waste discharge and emissions permits in a “fair and proportional manner”. The Regulation goes on to outline the requirements for the Trading System and Article 52. 2) stipulates that the Waster Discharge and/or Emission Trading system must be implemented no later than seven years from the enactment of the Regulation.
Document Title: Regulation No. 46/2017

Family Name: Green Finance Action Plan
Family Summary:
This plan notably aims to enable the country to switch to clean energy and reduce its carbon emissions. The specific goals are as stated:◆ Encourage banks in Taiwan to extend credit to startups in such important fields as green technology.◆ Persuade banks to voluntarily adopt international Equator Principles, which dictate that impacts to society, the environment and other areas be considered in credit risk assessment and decision-making.◆ Relax rules and regulations governing lending and raising capital; for example, allowing branches of foreign banks in Taiwan to issue New Taiwan dollar-denominated bonds and other such financial instruments.◆ Develop Taiwan's green bond market.◆ Utilize corporate governance assessment mechanisms to induce listed companies to issue green bonds.◆ Encourage the insurance industry to invest capital in green energy companies.◆ Loosen rules and regulations governing indirect investment in green energy by insurers.◆ Open more channels for investment in public works and green energy projects by such entities as private equity funds, venture capitalists and venture fund management firms.

In August 2020, the Taiwanese government announced the Green Finance Action Plan 2.0, which puts further measures in place to enhance the transparency and quality of disclosures by listed companies, and establish taxonomy regulations for sustainable finance in Taiwan.

In September 2022, the Green Finance Action Plan 3.0 was released, covering the following key implementation measures: GHG inventory and climate risk management of financial institutions; promoting and developing Taiwanese sustainable taxonomy; integrating ESG and climate-related information; enhancing sustainable finance training; and establishing cooperation mechanisms.
Document Title: Green Finance Action Plan 3.0

Family Name: National disaster risk reduction framework 2017-2030
Family Summary: The Papua New Guinea National Disaster Risk Reduction Framework (NDRRF) 2017-2030 represents international best practices in DRR stemming from the Sendai Framework. It aligns with the Framework for Resilient Development in the Pacific (2017-2030) and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Disaster Risk Reduction Plan. The NDRRF aims to raise understanding and awareness about the goals of the Sendai Framework, which seeks to prevent new and existing disaster risks through a comprehensive approach that reduces vulnerability and increases resilience. This framework provides a common DRR vision and mutual understanding for different government departments and agencies. The NDRRF also promotes improved communication, coordination and cooperation on DRR.

Family Name: National Climate Change Policy for Grenada, Carriacou and Petite Martinique (2017-2021)
Family Summary:
The policy objectives for 2017 – 2021 are to;
1) Strengthen institutional structure to support coordination, mainstreaming and implementation of climate change adaptation and mitigation action, along with the systematic integration of climate change adaptation into development policies, plans, programmes, projects, budgets and processes.
2) Build climate resilience in the following priority thematic areas: water supply and sewage management; ‘agriculture, agri-business and food security’39; biodiversity and ecosystems; human health and coastal zone management.
3) Facilitate climate smart (low carbon, climate resilient) infrastructure location, planning, design and maintenance, sustainable land management and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in the electricity, transport, waste and forestry sectors.
4) Integrate disaster risk management and climate change adaptation, and support funding applications for disaster risk management activities.
5) Strengthen institutional arrangements for the collection, storage, analysis, sharing and use of climate, GHG emission and pollutant/chemical data and information to inform evidence-based decision making.
6) Improve citizens’ awareness of the causes, impacts and appropriate responses to climate change, so that they are in a better position to take independent action and support relevant public policies, and state and non-state activities.
7) Access climate technologies for mitigation and adaption along with capacity building. Increase external climate finance support to Grenada’s adaptation and mitigation process.
8) Advocate for international action on climate change through foreign policy.
Document Title: National Climate Change Policy for Grenada, Carriacou and Petite Martinique (2017-2021)

Family Name: National Food Waste Strategy
Family Summary: The National Food Waste Strategy leverages existing local, regional and national efforts to target food waste, outlining example solutions, and identifies four priority areas where improvements can be made—policy support, business improvements, market development, and behaviour change. An initial funding commitment of over $1.3 million over 24 months supports an independent organisation that will develop an implementation plan and a monitoring and evaluation framework for the strategy, and coordinate priority areas of work; a voluntary commitment program that will initially engage businesses and industries to commit to actions that reduce food waste; and a National Food Waste Baseline to monitor and track progress towards Australia's goal to halve its food waste by 2030.
Document Title: National Food Waste Strategy

Family Name: Second National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP) 2018‑2020
Family Summary: Jordan's Second National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP) for 2018‑2020 is a national document summarising and promoting the nation's roadmap for achieving its energy efficiency goals. The action plan sets an overarching target for a 20% energy efficiency improvement by 2020 from a 2006-2010 average baseline, and states sectoral recommendations and progress. Climate change mitigation through lowered emissions is a key motivating factor for this action plan. Specific costed measures in the action plan include: the replacement of existing street lamp bulbs by LED alternatives; more efficient technology at pumping stations; enhanced energy efficiency audits by experts across industrial sectors; enhancing the enforcement of thermal insulation codes in residential and commercial construction projects.

The goals of the NAP for 2017-2021 are: (i) strengthened institutional structure; (ii) climate-responsive water management; (iii) integration of climate change adaptation into national sustainable development plans and projects; (iv) food security; (v) ecosystem preservation and improved management and conservation of protected areas; (vi) integrated coastal zone management; (vii) sustainable land management; (viii) fund allocation for disaster risk reduction; (ix) public health; (x) collection, analysis and provision of climate related data; and (xi) public awareness-raising.Climate-smart practices will be integrated into food, agriculture, and fisheries sectors to support food security in times of climate change induced stress on the food production sector. Family Name: National Strategy for Disaster Risk Prevention and Reduction (SNPRRC) of the Republic of Congo
Family Summary: This strategy aims to address the current situation and optimize the implementation of disaster risk management in the Republic of Congo. The strategy constitutes the main instrument for implementing the country's vision and priorities for disaster risk management within the framework of a comprehensive and comprehensive approach, covering all its components, which are simultaneously objectives, modalities, and components or phases of disaster risk management. This document contains seven strategic areas of intervention, comprising several fields of intervention, namely: Promoting the effectiveness of disaster risk management at the decentralized and local community levels (populations). Building institutional (technical and material) capacities at all levels and among the public for disaster risk management. Strengthening national coordination of disaster risk management and its key mechanisms. Optimizing preparedness and strengthening disaster response capacity at all levels. Strengthening risk assessment and monitoring, as well as early warning and risk information systems, at the national level. Optimizing the implementation and practice of risk prevention and reduction of all origins, at all levels. Strengthening regional, subregional, and international cooperation. For each area, this policy discloses expected results and key performance indicators. In addition, the document contains an implementation and monitoring framework.

Establishes the National Emissions Registration System - Sirene, provides for the instruments of the National Policy on Climate Change referred to in item XIII of the caput of art. 6 of Law No. 12,187, of December 29, 2009, and amends Decree No. 7,390, of December 9, 2010, which regulates said Policy.

Related to this, normative instruction 12/2010 stipulates in art 2 that the IBAMA Licensing Board evaluates, in the process of licensing activities capable of emitting greenhouse gases, the measures proposed by the entrepreneur with the objective of mitigating these environmental impacts, in compliance with the commitments assumed by Brazil in the Convention- United Nations Framework on Climate Change. Art 3 states that the Terms of Reference, prepared by IBAMA, to guide the Environmental Impact Studies for the licensing of projects capable of emitting greenhouse gases, include measures to mitigate or compensate for these environmental impacts in line with the National Plan on Climate Change.

Family Name: Master Plan for Disaster Risk Reduction 2017-2030
Family Summary:
The overarching goal of this document is that “the population, their livelihoods and health and public and private infrastructure resilient to extreme events and the effects of climate change and with a consolidated culture of prevention, preparedness, response and recovery”.

The Strategic Lines associated with this vision are:
> Consolidation of acquired experience, in order to guarantee continuity, learning and development;
> Prospective action on the generating processes risk and protection of public and private investments, as a way of adapting prospective risk management;
> Strengthening of territorial planning, paying attention to the growing urban risk and climate change, as a way of containing and controlling trends of increased risk generated by urbanisation processes, recognised as the main source of risk;
>Capacity development, as a way of raising awareness of the entire Mozambican society, to ensure effective actions for preparedness and response to emergencies and disasters, as well as to strengthen community resilience, with special attention to inclusion criteria and the gender balance;
> Involvement of local communities, promoting good practices and the use of local knowledge to complement scientific knowledge in the implementation of specific sectoral policies, strategies, plans and programmes, with an intersectoral approach adapted to the context;
> Corrective intervention to lay the groundwork for rapid recovery and resilient reconstruction after extreme events; and
> Promotion of regulatory and institutional reform processes to improve public policies and institutional management, through a legal, normative and innovative framework.
Document Title: Master Plan for Disaster Risk Reduction 2017-2030

Family Name: Clean Growth Strategy
Family Summary:
The Clean Growth Strategy exposes how the Government intends to foster national income while reducing greenhouse gases emissions, and do so at the least possible cost for taxpayers while maximising the social and economic benefits. The Strategy comes in line with the commitment made under the 2008 Climate Change Act that requires the country to reduce its emissions "by at least 80% by 2050". The Strategy acknowledges that efforts to reduce emissions will have to significantly ramp up in order to meet the fourth and fifth carbon budgets (covering the periods 2023-2027 and 2028-2032). Beyond setting up the strategy to 2032, the document explores electrification, hydrogen and emissions removal as three pathways to 2050.
 
 The Strategy firstly highlights the image of leadership and situation of progress that the country has made in the last two decades. It details the economic opportunities brought by the Paris Agreement for its low-carbon industries, notably thanks to its academic strength, expertise in high-value service and financial industries and stable regulatory framework. According to the document, the low carbon sector could grow by around 11% a year on the period 2015-2030, or four times faster than the overall economy, and "could deliver between £60 billion and £170 billion of export sales of goods and services by 2030". The document also mentions the co-benefits of actions to reduce greenhouse gases emissions on local air quality, public health, the economy and the environment. The Strategy also recalls the objective of energy affordability and the fact that leaving the EU represents an opportunity as "domestic binding emissions targets are more ambitious than those set by EU legislation".
 
 A number of more precise objectives are detailed as following: 1) develop green finance capabilities, including by setting up a green finance taskforce and providing up to £20 million to support a new clean technology early stage investment fund,- 2) develop a package of measures to support businesses to improve their energy productivity, by at least 20% by 2030,- 3) improving energy efficiency and aiming at reducing emissions from homes by 19% and energy use by 9%,- 4) rolling out low carbon heating,- 5) accelerate the shift to low carbon transport and reduce emissions by 29% by relying mostly on electric vehicles,- 6) deliver clean, smart, flexible power,- 7)enhance the benefits and value of domestic natural resources,- 8) and lead in the public sector. The government also commits £2.5 billion of investment in transport (33% of the total), power, cross-sector, smart systems, homes, business and industry, land use and waste.
Document Title: Clean Growth Strategy

Family Name: Better growth, lower emissions Strategy
Family Summary: This strategy aims at enabling Norway' private sector to be competitive and environmentally friendly, and enable the country to enjoy full employment, high income and low greenhouse gases emissions. The strategy focuses on green markets (including emissions trading and taxation), green and innovative procurement, research, energy infrastructure, climate risk, circular economy and exports of green solutions.
Document Title: Better growth, lower emissions Strategy

Family Name: Green Construction through Wood Program
Family Summary:
The Green Construction through Wood (GCWood) program encourages the use of innovative wood-based building technologies in construction projects. This program supports Canada’s commitment to reach 2030 and 2050 emissions reduction targets under the Paris Agreement and advance long-term priorities regarding greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction.

GCWood invests in wood construction projects that generate many benefits, including:

  • reduced GHG emissions from renewable and sustainable resources that help decarbonize the built environment
  • accelerated adoption of innovative building technologies and systems
  • updated building codes that allow for taller and larger wood buildings
  • affordable housing and community infrastructure

Since its launch in 2017, the GCWood program has supported 16 demonstration projects aimed at reducing risks and promoting the broader use of wood-based products in construction. As of March 2023, it has funded 4 tall wood buildings, 10 low-rise non-residential buildings, and 2 timber bridge projects. The program also developed the 2021 State of Mass Timber in Canada report and an interactive map to track and analyse mass timber construction progress. These resources help applicants understand Canada’s advancements in the field.

Upon renewal, the program broadened its scope to include support for schematic designs, innovative wood construction systems, and the use of advanced bio-based building materials in both new and existing low GHG emission buildings. It offers non-repayable funding of up to $1.4 million for eligible project costs.

Future funding will prioritise projects in areas such as prefabrication, modular construction, retrofitting, and adaptable or disassemblable design.
Document Title: Green Construction through Wood (GCWood) Program

Family Name: Romania's strategy for mobilising investments in the renovation of residential and commercial buildings existing at national level, both public and private
Family Summary: This Strategy, published by the Ministry of Regional Development, Public Administration and European Funds in 2017, sets out plans to improve the energy efficiency of the buildings sector. The strategy notes that increasing energy efficiency is essential for Romania to meet its medium to long term climate change objectives of moving to a competitive low carbon economy by 2050. The Strategy was designed to align with the EU Energy Efficiency Directive (2012/27/EC).The strategy plans to mobilise investment and technology for both energy efficiency measures and the introduction of onsite renewables generation. It is structured in three phases:Phase I: Establishing foundations so that deep renovations can become a goal within 5 yearsPhase II: Supporting technological developmentPhase III: Deep renovation of Buildings within 15 years.
Document Title: Strategy for mobilising investments in the renovation of residential and commercial buildings existing at national level, both public and private

Family Name: The Austrian Strategy for Adaptation to Climate Change (NAS)
Family Summary: Austria's climate change adaptation strategy identifies 14 key sectors: agriculture, forestry, water resources, tourism, energy, construction and housing, protection from natural hazards, disaster risk management, health, ecosystems/biodiversity, transport infrastructure, spatial planning, business/industry/trade, and cities. It defines principles to support the planning and implementation of adaptation measures and develops a plan of action.
Document Title: The Austrian Strategy for Adaptation to Climate Change Part 1 - Strategy

Family Name: Uganda National REDD+ Strategy
Family Summary:
Uganda's REDD+ strategy from 2017 supports and guides the sustainable development of the agricultural and forestry sectors with a view to enhancing carbon storage and landscape-level climate resilience. Actions it promotes include climate smart agriculture, sustainable fuel-wood production, energy-efficient cooking stoves, and further strengthening the national policy framework around forest protection.

The strategy was updated in 2021.
Document Title: Uganda National REDD+ Strategy

Family Name: National Mitigation Plan for Transport Sector
Family Summary: Intregated national sectoral plan for transport aiming to guide the development of the sector to satisfy present and future mobility needs of citizens in a sustainable way. It includes an investment plan aiming to prioritize railway transport, low-emissions mobility, alternative transport such as cycling, public transport, as well as modernization of air transport and freight transport systems. These measures aim to reduce GHG emissions from the transport sector by 5.91 MtCO2e by 2030 against a BAU scenario, or accumulated savings of 46.95 MtCO2e for the period 2011-2030. Total emissions from transport by 2030 are estimated to be 82.5 MtCO2e under the BAU scenario, and 76.6 MtCO2e (7.2% lower than BAU) on the additional measures scenario.
Document Title: National Mitigation Plan for Transport Sector

Family Name: Climate-smart agriculture, fisheries and livestock for food security: Policy guidance brief
Family Summary: This plan seeks to achieve climate-resilient productivity and promote climate-smart responses to support food security and livelihood strategies in Myanmar. To accomplish this, the plan establishes that Myanmar must: - Integrate climate change into relevant policies, planning and budgeting procedures, and put these into practice, taking into account gender considerations.- Adopt climate-resilient and environmentally sound adaptation technologies and climate-smart management practices, supported by international and domestic finance.- Establish institutional coordination and a multistakeholder engagement framework.Climate change has already challenged the agriculture sector in Myanmar by affecting rice yields and livestock production, while disasters such as foods and cyclones have caused massive destruction in rural areas. This plan will help enhance the sector's resilience while ensuring sustainable development.
Document Title: Myanmar: Climate-smart agriculture, fisheries and livestock for food security: Policy guidance brief 1

Family Name: National adaptation plan framework
Family Summary: This framework sets out the approaches and principles which will underpin how Fiji's National Adaptation Plan (NAP) is implemented. It also sets out the institutional arrangements which will guide the formulation and coordination of efforts to implement the NAP and thus steer the national process over the long term. It also proposes some initial efforts to progress the NAP process. However, it does not itself constitute an action plan which would require more activities and wider consultation.
Document Title: Fiji: National adaptation plan framework

Family Name: UAE Water Security Strategy 2036
Family Summary:
The UAE Water Security Strategy 2036 aims to ensure sustainable access to water during both normal and emergency conditions in line with local regulations, standards of the World Health Organisation, and the UAE's vision to achieve prosperity and sustainability. 

The overall objectives of the strategy are to reduce total demand for water resources, increase water productivity, reduce water scarcity, increase the reuse of treated water and increase national water storage capacity.

The strategy also includes the establishment of 6 connecting networks between water and electricity entities across the UAE. Water networks will be able to provide 91 litres of water per person per day in cases of emergency, or 30 litres per person per day in cases of extreme emergencies. Once implemented, the Water Security Strategy 2036 will achieve savings of AED 74 billion and reduce the emissions of carbon dioxide (CO2), associated with water desalination process, by 100 million metric tons.
Document Title: UAE Water Security Strategy 2036

Family Name: Ministerial Decree no. 40616 creating the Citizen Advisory Council on Climate Change
Family Summary: This decree creates the Citizen Advisory Council on Climate Change as a platform for citizen participation that is part of the national policy of open government, which seeks to strengthen the mechanisms of accountability, availability and access to information.The Council will have the following functions: 1) Deliberate independently about the design, application and evaluation of climate change policies proposed and operated by the government, through its different institutions, 2) Respond to the questions submitted by MINAE or other public bodies about the design, application and evaluation of their climate policies, programs and metrics. 3) Generate the activities that are considered necessary to increase the level of information and awareness of citizens in relation to Climate Change. 4) Improve the levels of coordination and communication between public administration and citizens. 5) Serve as a citizen audit space in charge of analyzing, discussing and supporting the implementation of the Predicted and Determined Contribution at the National Level presented by Costa Rica before the Conference of the Parties 21 held in Paris in December 2015. 6) Interact with the governance bodies established for the Sustainable Development Goals of the United Nations (Decree No. 40203-PLAN-REMINAE), generating inputs on the progress made in meeting Objective 13 (on combating climate change and its effects), of the Sustainable Development Goals within the framework of the 2030 Agenda, providing feedback to the corresponding institutions.
Document Title: Ministerial Decree no. 40616 creating the Citizen Advisory Council on Climate Change

Family Name: Har Ghar Bijli  programme ("Saubhagya")
Family Summary: This scheme aims at granting energy access to all. It involves performing last mile connectivity for un-electrified households in rural and urban settings. The plan notably involves installing solar and battery capacities.
Document Title: Har ghar bijli program ("saubhagya")

Family Name: Malawi Growth and Development Strategy (MGDS III)
Family Summary: This medium-term strategy covers the period 2017-2022. It aims to move the country to a productive, competitive and resilient nation through sustainable agriculture and economic growth, energy, industrial and infrastructure development while addressing water, climate change, environmental management and population challenges. The strategy set five key priority areas: 1) agriculture, water development and Climate Change Management, 2) Education and Skills Development, 3) transport and ICT infrastructure, 4) energy, Industry and Tourism Development, and 5) Health and Population.
Document Title: Malawi Growth and Development Strategy (MGDS III)

Family Name: Decree creating national DRR platform
Family Summary:
This involves the creation by decree of the Platform and the interministerial committee for crisis and disaster management.

Mali is located in West Africa, the eighth largest in the country. As a landlocked state, Mali faces various risks, including droughts that affect a significant portion of the population. Conflict complicates risk management in the country.
Document Title: Decree creating national DRR platform (Décret création plateforme nationale RRC)

Family Name: Decree on green public procurement
Family Summary: The purpose of this regulation is to reduce the negative impact on the environment through the public procurement of environmentally less burdensome goods, services and works and to promote the development of environmental innovation and the circular economy, and to set an example for the private sector and consumers. Article 4 brings a series of items which it is mandatory to take into account sustainable or environmental aspects or aspects of the circular economy. Article 6 obliges that when awarding public contracts, the contracting authority shall take into account, among others, energy efficiency, the use of renewable or other alternative energy sources. Annex 1 brings the full list. Also, annex 2 brings the definition of objectives and conditions in the field of public procurement of clean and zero-emission vehicles for road transport.
Document Title: Decree on green public procurement (Consolidated version)

Family Name: Plan for Expanding Biofuel Ethanol Production and Promoting Ethanol Usage in Motor Vehicles
Family Summary: In September 2017, China announced a nationwide ethanol mandate to expand E10 fuel use across the country by 2020. The plan also targets demonstrating a 50,000-ton cellulosic ethanol plant by 2020, with large-scale production by 2025. Building a biofuel ethanol industrial base promotes China's alternative fossil energy, reduces greenhouse gas emissions, and cultivates new momentum for agricultural and rural development.
Document Title: Plan for Expanding Biofuel Ethanol Production and Promoting Ethanol Usage in Motor Vehicles

Family Name: Comprehensive Plan for Reconstruction with Changes (Plan Integral para la Reconstrucción con Cambios)
Family Summary: The Comprehensive Plan for Reconstruction with Changes (Plan Integral de Reconstrucción con Cambios "PIRCC") addresses the aftermath of El Niño Costero, a climatic phenomenon that caused widespread damage to infrastructure, livelihoods, and communities in Peru. Its primary objective is to rehabilitate and reconstruct public infrastructure—such as roads, schools, health facilities, and water systems—while prioritizing the recovery of vulnerable populations displaced by floods, landslides, and other disasters. The plan emphasizes climate-resilient reconstruction and disaster risk reduction, integrating adaptive measures to prevent future vulnerabilities. The PIRCC outlines two core intervention types: (1) rehabilitation and replacement of damaged infrastructure to restore essential services, and (2) preventive measures such as river desilting, flood barriers, and urban planning reforms to reduce exposure to climate-related hazards. It incorporates sustainable construction standards, including climate-resilient materials, energy-efficient systems, and disaster-safe housing, ensuring long-term resilience. The plan also prioritizes territorial ordering and sustainable land use, addressing the root causes of vulnerability linked to unregulated urban growth.
Document Title: Reconstruction with Changes - Comprehensive Reconstruction with Changes Plan (Reconstrucción con Cambios - Plan Integral de Reconstrucción con Cambios)

Family Name: National Agricultural Planning 2017-2030 (Planeación agrícola nacional 2017-2030)
Family Summary: The National Agricultural Planning 2017-2030 was designed to align stakeholders in the agri-food sector towards shared objectives. It focuses on 38 strategic crops, outlining market strategies, optimal production regions based on agroclimatic and logistical factors, and measures to enhance productivity while reducing costs. The policy emphasises climate-smart agriculture and sustainable practices to address stagnating productivity, alongside strategies to mitigate cross-border pests and diseases exacerbated by climate change threatening food security. It also highlights the need for risk-responsive approaches to natural disasters and conflicts, which disproportionately affect food-insecure regions due to climate-agriculture interdependencies. The framework promotes a regionally tailored development model, prioritising agroclimatic suitability, innovation, and infrastructure investment. It encourages public-private collaboration, capacity-building, and resource efficiency to strengthen resilience and market competitiveness.
Document Title: National Agricultural Planning 2017-2029 (Planeación agrícola nacional 2017-2029)

Family Name: National Renewable Energy Policy
Family Summary:
This policy seeks to provide access to modern, clean, environmentally sustainable, and affordable energy services for all Namibians. It aims to boost public and private investments in renewable energy projects, create an enabling regulatory and economic environment for the sector, promote connected and off-grid schemes, pursue climate resilience in the energy sector, and accelerate the development of energy storage facilities.

The policy recommends the government to consider a subsidy framework. Solar, wind, or invader- bush based bioenergy are sources primarily favoured, since the hydropower sector is subjected to high climate change uncertainty.
Document Title: National Renewable Energy Policy

Family Name: Decree No. 079/CAB/PM
Family Summary: According to Cameroun's second NDC, art. 2 of this document states that the mission of the interministerial committee is to “coordinate and monitor sectoral diligence relating to the implementation of the recommendations of the Paris Agreement on global warming".
Document Title: Decree No. 079/CAB/PM

Family Name: Long-term National Development Plan of Ghana (2018-2057)
Family Summary: This document was prepared by the National Development Planning Commission (NDPC) and sets the long-term development strategy of the country. It contains a number of climate-related clauses, including regarding agricultural practices, coastal and marine areas management, and the protection of the natural environment, notably of wetlands.
Document Title: Long-term National Development Plan of Ghana (2018-2057)

Family Name: National plan for drinking water and sanitation
Family Summary: This document defines the needs for drinking water and sanitation capacities in each area of the country. It takes into account the impacts of climate change on water access.
Document Title: National plan for drinking water and sanitation

Family Name: National Disaster Recovery Framework (Volume II: Drought)
Family Summary:
This policy was updated in response to the 2015-2016 drought. It aims to sustainably improve the resilience of communities affected by floods and drought, support prolonged food security of vulnerable populations, and restore the livelihoods of disaster-affected communities.

The Framework should serve as a guide for government and other implementing stakeholders in prioritising the implementation of PDNA findings and guide recovery investment and resource allocations across short-term humanitarian needs and medium- to long-term reconstruction.
Document Title: National Disaster Recovery Framework (Volume II: Drought)

Family Name: Government Action Plan for the Implementation of the President's Programme
Family Summary:
This Plan contains five chapters on: rule of law and governance; economic recovery and renewal; strengthening human development and social cohesion; a dynamic and proactive foreign policy; and strengthening national security and defence. Economic recovery is focused on the energy and mining sectors.

The Plan expresses the intention of the government to develop a national plan and local plans to adapt to the risks of climate change and strengthen resilience to its effects, including optimising the use of water and improving health coverage for its population. The government will also promote nature and biodiversity, green technologies, and accelerate the implementation of the ciruclar economy.
Document Title: Government Action Plan for the Implementation of the President's Programme
